    local now = GetGameTimer()                                     -- a rate limit, and a table
    if lastBuy[source] and now - lastBuy[source] < 500 then return end  -- to clean up when they leave
    lastBuy[source] = now

    if type(itemKey) ~= 'string' or not itemKey:match('^[%w_]+$') then return end
    amount = tonumber(amount)
    if not amount or amount ~= math.floor(amount) or amount < 1 or amount > 100 then return end

    local pos = GetEntityCoords(GetPlayerPed(source))              -- at the counter
    if #(pos - COUNTER) > 5.0 then return end

    -- At last, the purchase. Every return above was silent:
    -- nobody can see what was refused, or why.
    buy(source, player, itemKey, amount)
end)

The same purchase as a SecureEvent:

exports.whip_core:SecureEvent('myshop:buy', {
    rateLimit = 500,
    params = {
        {'itemKey', 'key', 60},       -- letters, digits, _ and -
        {'amount',  'amount', 100},   -- a whole number from 1 to 100
    },
    near = { at = COUNTER, range = 5.0 },
}, function(source, player, itemKey, amount)
    buy(source, player, itemKey, amount)   -- loaded, alive, checked, at the counter
end)

The rules run before your handler, and every refusal is recorded with its reason. The biggest saving is the check people forget: whether the slot, stash or car a client names is really theirs. The slot, addr and vehicle types make that check for you (below).

What whip checks for you

CheckWhat it stopsYou write
A loaded characterCalls from someone on character select, or already logging outNothing: on by default
AliveA dead player buying, looting or using itemsNothing: on by default
How oftenA call fired hundreds of times a secondNothing (10 in a row, then one every 100 ms), or rateLimit
Every valueThe wrong type, a negative amount, text where a number goesparams
Where they areBuying from across the mapnear
What they ownNaming somebody else's slot, stash or carThe slot, addr and vehicle types
Who they areAdmin and staff actions from everyone elseace or permission

And with every one, for nothing:

  • It saves as one. Everything whip saves while your handler runs (the cash taken, the item given, the log rows) is written together, in one transaction, so a crash never leaves half a purchase in the database (one player action saves as one). Saving is not undoing: a return false or an error does not take back what your handler already did, so put it right yourself, as a refund does.
  • Errors are caught. An error in your handler is printed in the console and recorded against the event.
  • Every call is in the Monitor, accepted or refused, with who sent it and why.
What it does not do. near trusts the position the player's own game reports, so a cheat that teleports can still pass it; an anticheat is still the answer to teleporting, god mode and aimbots. A valid call at the allowed rate is allowed: how much a player may earn is your game's rule. And a cheat can fire your client events on its own game, so never let a client handler decide anything that matters.

Writing one

Call SecureEvent from your server code with three things: the event's name, its rules (the schema) and your handler. Here is a tip jar for the coffee stand from Your First Resource:

-- server.lua
Whip.register(function()
    exports.whip_core:SecureEvent('mycafe:tip', {
        rateLimit = 2000,                                   -- one tip every 2 seconds
        params    = { {'amount', 'amount', 500} },          -- $1 to $500, or refused
        near      = { at = Config.Counter, range = 3.0 },   -- at the counter
    }, function(source, player, amount)
        local receipt, err = exports.whip_core:ChargePlayer(source, amount, { reason = 'Tip' })
        if not receipt then return false, err end          -- refused: they are shown why
        exports.whip_core:NotifyPlayer(source, ('Thanks for the tip, %s'):format(player.firstName), 'success')
    end)
end)

-- client.lua: sent like any other event
TriggerServerEvent('mycafe:tip', 20)
  • It goes inside Whip.register, with everything else your resource gives whip. whip_core keeps your event in its memory, so a whip_core restart forgets it; Whip.register declares it again as soon as whip_core is back (Your First Resource, step 3). The shorter examples below say so in their first line.
  • The name is yours. Start it with your resource's name ('mycafe:tip') and no other resource can take it.
  • The handler gets source, player, then your values, in the order params lists them. Use this source, not the global one: whip_core receives the event and calls your function, so FiveM never sets the global for your resource. player is a copy of the player's data sheet (charId, firstName, isDead …): read it, and change the player through whip's exports.
  • The client does not change. It sends the event with TriggerServerEvent, as it always has.

Try it: the Monitor

Open /whip → System → Monitor (an admin's tool: the whip.devtools ACE, with developer mode on in /w). Every call to a SecureEvent or SecureCallback is there, accepted or refused, with who sent it, the reason, and how long your handler took. To see a refusal, send the tip jar a bad value from a throwaway command in client.lua:

RegisterCommand('tiptest', function()
    TriggerServerEvent('mycafe:tip', -50)   -- refused: amount: Amount must be a whole number of 1 or more
end)

The history is kept whether or not anyone has the Monitor open, until whip_core restarts. Accepted calls never push refusals out: the last 500 of each are kept. Refusals are printed in the server console too, one line per player and event every 5 seconds with a count of the rest (Config.LogSecureRejections = false turns that off). The screen itself is described under Dev Tools.

Checking the values: params

One line for each value the client sends, in the order it sends them: a name, a type, then that type's limits. The name is what a refusal mentions (amount: Amount must be a whole number of 1 or more). Only the values you list reach your handler; anything more the client sends is dropped.

The value isTypeFor example
How many of something, or moneyamount{'count', 'amount', 50}: 1 to 50
A thing named by a number: a door, a player, a recordid{'doorId', 'id'}
A thing named by a word: an item, a shopkey{'itemKey', 'key', 60}
One of a few choicesenum{'mode', 'enum', {'buy', 'sell'}}
Yes or nobool{'locked', 'bool'}
Text the player typedstring{'note', 'string', 200}
A measurement or a setting: a speed, a volumenumber{'volume', 'number', 0, 1}
A slot in their pockets, a car they own, a store they have openslot, vehicle, addrBelow
A list of any of theselist{'items', 'list', {'itemKey', 'key', 60}}
Another player, near them: the one they cuff, search, heal or give toplayer{'target', 'player', { range = 3 }}
One table of named fields: a formrecord{'form', 'record', { {'accountId', 'id'}, {'note', 'string', 200} }}

A value that names a thing or costs money is refused, never corrected (amount, id, key, and the three below), so your handler never runs on a guess. The softer types are for settings: number pulls a value into range, which suits a slider, and enum, bool and string fall back to a default when you give one. Numbers sent as text ("5", as a NUI page often sends them) count as numbers, except in an enum, which matches exactly.

id and key check the form of a value, not that the thing exists: whether door 12 is real is your handler's question (or near's, below). Every type's exact rules, with what comes after it, are in the types table on the SecureEvent card.

Checking what they own: slot, vehicle, addr

These three types do more than check a number. They look the thing up, check that this player may use it, and hand your handler the thing itself. The ownership check you would have written is already done, the same way in every resource.

slot: a slot in the caller's own pockets. The client sends a slot number, or { sub = 'accessory', slot = 3 }. It is refused if the slot is empty or, with item, holds something else; allowEmpty = true accepts an empty slot. Those two are refusals a player meets when the item moved after they pressed, so they are told ("That item is not there any more", "That slot holds something else now"): a callback answers false and those words, an event shows them. A pocket that is not one of theirs or a slot number out of range is a forged request and stays silent. Your handler gets { addr, item, amount, metadata }: the slot's address, which every slot export takes, and a copy of what is in it.

-- server.lua, inside Whip.register: "the magazine the player right-clicked", checked before you see it
exports.whip_core:SecureEvent('myguns:unload', {
    params = { {'mag', 'slot', { item = { 'myguns_mag_pistol', 'myguns_mag_rifle' } }} },
}, function(source, player, mag)
    -- mag.item is one of the two, mag.addr is where it is, mag.metadata a copy of its data
    exports.whip_core:SetItemMetadata(mag.addr, { rounds = 0 })
end)

vehicle: a car this player owns. Your handler gets the same snapshot GetVehicle answers (v.vehicleId, v.plate, v.model, v.owner, v.stats …). It is a copy: changing it changes nothing. Add near = { at = 'vehicle' } and they must be standing at the car too.

-- server.lua, inside Whip.register
exports.whip_core:SecureEvent('mykit:install', {
    params = {
        {'kit', 'slot', { item = 'mykit_turbo' }},   -- the kit, in their own pockets
        {'vehicle', 'vehicle'},                -- their car, as a GetVehicle snapshot
    },
    near = { at = 'vehicle', range = 5.0 },      -- and they are standing at it
}, function(source, player, kit, v)
    -- No ownership check to write: a client naming somebody else's car never gets here,
    -- and kit.addr is a slot of theirs that really holds the kit.
    local taken, why = exports.whip_core:StoreTake(kit.addr, 1, { reason = 'fitted to ' .. v.plate })
    if not taken then return false, why end
    exports.whip_core:SetVehicleData(v.vehicleId, 'mykit_turbo', { fittedAt = os.time() })
end)

The client sends the car's vehicleId, whip's own number for it (not the entity or the netId; see Vehicle references). Options go third, as in {'vehicle', 'vehicle', { anyOwner = true }}: anyOwner accepts anybody's owned car, for something anyone at a car may do, like refuelling it (pair it with near), and session = true also accepts a car nobody owns, such as a street car. A car that is not theirs, or is not there any more, is refused with a message for the player (shown for an event, the reason for a callback); a value that is not a vehicle id at all is refused silently, since only a modified client sends one.

addr: a slot in a store the caller may reach, such as a stash they have open or a boot they hold. Every item move in whip passes this one gate. Your handler gets { addr, item, amount, metadata }, as for slot. See Addresses.

Checking where they are: near

Most calls that act on the world only make sense from beside the thing: the counter, the door, the car. near refuses a call unless the player is within range metres (5 if left out) of at, which is one of three things:

at =Means
vector3(…) or { x, y, z }A fixed spot: your one counter, bench or NPC
function(source, player, …values)A spot worked out from the call: answer x, y, z, a vector3 or { x, y, z }
'vehicle'The car in this schema's vehicle value. Sitting in it counts as near
-- server.lua, inside Whip.register
exports.whip_core:SecureEvent('myshop:browse', {
    params = { {'shopId', 'id'} },
    near = {
        range   = 15.0,
        at      = function(source, player, shopId)   -- given the checked values
            local shop = exports.whip_core:GetShop(shopId)
            if not shop then return nil end               -- no such shop: refused
            return shop.x, shop.y, shop.z
        end,
        message = 'You are too far from the shop',
    },
}, function(source, player, shopId) --[[ ... ]] end)

A player who is too far is shown your message (Too far away if you give none). Write message = false for a call sent on a timer rather than by a press. When at finds no position, the call is refused as too far; allowUnknown = true lets it through instead, for a handler that explains a bad id better itself. range can also be a function, to follow a setting.

How often: rateLimit and burst

Every event is rate limited for each player, whether you say so or not:

You writeA player may send
nothing10 in a row, then one every 100 ms. Nobody clicking a button reaches that.
rateLimit = 2000One, then one every 2 seconds: a cooldown.
rateLimit = 2000, burst = 55 in a row, then one every 2 seconds.
rateLimit = falseAny number. For something that must never be refused.

A player who pauses earns calls back, one per interval, up to the burst. Give a burst to anything a player does quickly by hand, like dragging items, and to anything that closes or lets go of something: a refused close leaves the thing open.

Who may send it: the living, ace and permission

Dead players are refused. A dead player cannot use items, move items or act on the world, and each new event you write is covered without a line of code. whileDead = true lets them through, for what a dead player still needs: closing a screen, chat, the respawn.

Admins. ace = 'myresource.admin' lets through only players with that ACE, FiveM's own permission, given in server.cfg. An ace event is an admin tool, so a dead admin may still use it. For whip's own admin ACE, whip.devtools, the admin also needs developer mode on: a switch in /w, so an admin who is just playing does not act as one by accident. They are told if it is off.

Staff. permission = 'mygarage.manage' lets through only players given that whip permission: a role you give and take away while the server runs. Permissions compares the two.

Before a character loads. requirePlayer = false accepts calls from players with no character loaded yet, for character select and other screens before the game. Your handler's player is then nil.

Saying no

Your handler refuses a request by returning false:

Your handler returnsThe player seesThe Monitor records
false, 'You need a wrench'The message, as an errorRefused, with the message
falseNothingRefused
anything else, or nothingOnly what your handler sends themAccepted
-- server.lua, inside Whip.register
exports.whip_core:SecureEvent('mymech:fitTurbo', {
    params = { {'vehicle', 'vehicle'} },
    near   = { at = 'vehicle', range = 5.0 },
}, function(source, player, v)
    if not exports.whip_core:HasItem(source, 'mymech_wrench', 1) then
        return false, 'You need a wrench'   -- shown to them, and recorded as refused
    end
    -- ... fit it
    exports.whip_core:NotifyPlayer(source, 'Turbo bolted on', 'success')
end)

To record a reason in the Monitor without showing the player one (your own screen already told them), call RecordEventRejection, then return.

Asking the server: SecureCallback

When the client needs an answer (a price, a list of cars, "may I?"), register a SecureCallback on the server and ask with Callback on the client. It takes the same schema and makes the same checks; your handler returns the answer.

local PRICES = { mycafe_coffee = 15, mycafe_muffin = 8 }   -- the server's prices, never the client's

-- server.lua, inside Whip.register
exports.whip_core:SecureCallback('mycafe:getPrice', {
    rateLimit = 500,
    params    = { {'itemKey', 'key', 60} },
}, function(source, player, itemKey)
    local price = PRICES[itemKey]
    if not price then return false, 'Not sold here' end   -- false and why: a nil would lose the why
    return price
end)

-- client.lua, in a command or event handler (Callback waits for the answer)
local price, why = exports.whip_core:Callback('mycafe:getPrice', 'mycafe_coffee')
if not price then return exports.whip_core:Notify(why, 'error') end

The answer arrives up to its first nil (that is FiveM's rule for anything crossing between resources), which is why a refusal is false, why. When there is no answer to give, the client gets false and a reason:

The reasonWhen
'Rate limited', 'Player is dead', 'No player session', 'Too far away', 'itemKey: invalid key' …whip's checks refused the call
YoursYour handler returned false, 'Not sold here'
'Server error'Your handler errored (the error itself is in the server console)
'Unknown callback'No callback has that name
'That is no longer available'The resource that registered it has stopped
'No answer from the server'Nothing came back within 10 seconds

if not price then catches every one, and the reason is what to tell the player. So answer a yes-or-no question with something other than false for "no": a word, or a table. And because a callback's return values are its answer, the Monitor records them as accepted, false included; to record a refusal, call RecordEventRejection before you return.

Less common options

OptionFor
ownerOfOnly the game that runs an entity (its network owner) may send this, for reports about an NPC or object only that game simulates. Name one of your id values holding a netId: params = { {'npcNet', 'id'} }, ownerOf = 'npcNet'. A refusal is quiet: ownership moves between games all the time.
onRejectfunction(source, reason, rawArgs), run when whip refuses the call before your handler, for a client waiting on an answer (an inventory drag). rawArgs are exactly what the client sent, unchecked. SecureEvent only.
sheet = 'light'Hands your handler a smaller player: who they are, and whether they are dead. For an event sent many times a second, like a shot fired.

And one helper: if your handler takes a lock (a machine one player uses at a time), TrackInvocationLock releases it if the handler errors before it can.

Common mistakes

  • Registering outside Whip.register. At the top of a file it runs the moment your resource starts, which on a cold start can be before whip_core is ready to take it. Without dependency 'whip_core', a whip_core restart also forgets it while your resource keeps running. Inside Whip.register neither can happen.
  • Using the global source in a handler, or a helper it calls. Pass along the source you were handed.
  • int or number for money or a count. They pull -50 into range instead of refusing it. Use amount, and give it a max: without one there is no upper limit.
  • Forgetting a value in params. Only listed values reach your handler; one you left out arrives as nil.
  • A callback answering nil to refuse. The client cannot tell why. Answer false, 'why'.

Coming from ESX, QBCore or ox_lib

Events and callbacks only; everything else is on Coming from QBCore, ESX or ox.

You use todayIn whip
RegisterNetEvent + AddEventHandlerSecureEvent
ESX.RegisterServerCallback, QBCore.Functions.CreateCallback, lib.callback.registerSecureCallback: return the answer, no cb
ESX.TriggerServerCallback, QBCore.Functions.TriggerCallback, lib.callback.awaitCallback: waits, and answers in place

To move an event over: swap the call, list every value the client sends in params, delete the checks you wrote by hand, put it inside Whip.register, and use the source you are handed. Then look at your returns: return false now means "refused". The client side does not change. Plain RegisterNetEvent keeps working beside it, so a resource can move over one event at a time; until it does, whip does not check those events and the Monitor does not show them.

SecureEvent & SecureCallback

The server exports. Secure Events, above, explains each rule with an example; these cards are the reference.

SecureEvent(eventName, schema, handler)SERVER

Registers a net event whose every call is checked against schema before handler runs.

ParamTypeDescription
eventNamestringThe event's name, starting with your resource's ('myshop:buy'), up to 128 characters
schematableThe rules, below. {} takes every default, and hands the handler no values
handlerfunctionfunction(source, player, ...values). player is the caller's data sheet (no metadata: GetPlayer(source).metadata has it); the values come in params order. return false, 'why' refuses (Saying no)
Schema fieldDefaultDescription
params{}One definition per value: {name, type, …} (the types). Only these reach the handler
rateLimit10 in a row, then one per 100 msLeast time between calls, in ms, per player. false: no limit. Set on its own, it is a cooldown (burst 1). 0 is refused (rate limits)
burst1 with a rateLimit, else 10Calls allowed back to back before rateLimit applies. A whole number, 1 or more
nearnone{ at, range = 5.0, message?, allowUnknown? }: the player must be within range of at (near)
acenoneAn ACE the player must have. A dead player with it is let through
permissionnoneA whip permission the player must have, or a list of them (any one)
whileDeadfalsetrue lets a dead player send it
requirePlayertruefalse accepts players with no character loaded
ownerOfnoneThe name of an id value holding a netId: only that entity's network owner may send it
onRejectnonefunction(source, reason, rawArgs), run when whip refuses the call before the handler. rawArgs are unchecked
sheet'full''light': the handler's player holds only source, session, userId, charId, firstName, lastName, fullName, dateOfBirth, gender, isDead, for an event sent many times a second
Value typeWrittenAccepts
amount{name, 'amount', max?}A whole number of 1 or more, at most max (no upper limit if left out: give one for money). Anything else is refused: the rule every item, cash and bank call uses
id{name, 'id', min?, max?}A whole number from min (1 if left out) to max. Anything else is refused, never clamped: clamping a 0 up to 1 would hand the player thing number 1. The form only: whether the thing exists is the handler's question
key{name, 'key', maxLen?}Letters, digits, _ and -, at most maxLen long (60 if left out). Anything else is refused, never cleaned up: 'legion.sq' is refused, not turned into 'legionsq'
enum{name, 'enum', {values}, default?}One of the values, matched exactly ("1" is not 1). Anything else becomes default, or is refused when there is none
bool{name, 'bool', default?}true, 1, "true" and "1" are true; false, 0, "false", "0" and "" are false. Nothing sent counts as default (or false). Anything else becomes default, or is refused when there is none
string{name, 'string', maxLen, default?}Text, cut to maxLen, with control characters other than tab and newline removed. Empty, or not text, becomes default, or is refused when there is none
number{name, 'number', min, max, default?}Any number, pulled into min to max. A value that is not a number becomes default, or is refused when there is none
int{name, 'int', min, max, default?}As number, rounded down to a whole number. For a setting; never for a count, money or an id
slot{name, 'slot', opts?}A slot in the caller's own pockets, as { addr, item, amount, metadata }. opts: item (a key or a list), allowEmpty (slot)
vehicle{name, 'vehicle', opts?}A car the caller owns, as a GetVehicle snapshot. opts: anyOwner, session (vehicle)
addr{name, 'addr', opts?}A store address the caller may name, as { addr, item, amount, metadata }. opts: slotOptional, to accept a whole store with no slot (Addresses)
list{name, 'list', entry, max?}A list of at most max entries (50 if left out), each checked against entry: one definition, such as {'itemKey', 'key', 60}, or a list of them for entries that are tables, such as { {'slot', 'id', 1, 50}, {'index', 'int', -1, 99} }. A refusal names the entry: basket[2].slot: invalid id. An addr cannot go inside a list: send a list of slots and one addr beside it
player{name, 'player', { range?, notSelf? }}Another player by server id: online with a character loaded, not in the character creator, in the caller's routing bucket, within range metres (3 if left out), and not the caller (notSelf = false allows it). The handler gets their light sheet: { source, charId, firstName, lastName, fullName, isDead, … }. "They are not here" and "They are too far away" are shown to the player
record{name, 'record', fields}One table, each field checked as a list entry's: { {'accountId', 'id'}, {'note', 'string', 200} }. The handler gets only those fields. For a form or an app request that sends one table
any{name, 'any'}Anything, unchecked: yours to check in the handler. Reach for record, list or slot first
-- server.lua: a mechanic signs off any owned car, with a sticker from their pockets
Whip.register(function()
    exports.whip_core:SecureEvent('mygarage:inspect', {
        rateLimit  = 5000,                                       -- one every 5 seconds
        permission = 'mygarage.mechanic',                        -- staff only
        params     = {
            {'vehicle', 'vehicle', { anyOwner = true }},          -- anybody's owned car
            {'sticker', 'slot', { item = 'mygarage_sticker' }},   -- one in their pockets
        },
        near       = { at = 'vehicle', range = 4.0, message = 'Stand at the car' },
    }, function(source, player, v, sticker)
        local taken, why = exports.whip_core:StoreTake(sticker.addr, 1, { reason = 'inspected ' .. v.plate })
        if not taken then return false, why end
        exports.whip_core:SetVehicleData(v.vehicleId, 'mygarage_inspected', { at = os.time(), by = player.charId })
        exports.whip_core:NotifyPlayer(source, v.plate .. ' passed inspection', 'success')
    end)
end)
Returns: true, or false, reason (also printed in the console): the name is another resource's, starts whip_core: or cb:, or is a server lifecycle event such as playerDropped; or the schema is wrong (a rateLimit of 0, an unknown type, an enum with no values)
SecureCallback(name, schema, handler)SERVER

Registers a callback the client asks with Callback. The same checks as SecureEvent; the handler's return values are the answer.

ParamTypeDescription
namestringThe callback's name, starting with your resource's
schematableAs SecureEvent's, without onReject: a callback's refusal is its answer
handlerfunctionfunction(source, player, ...values), returning the answer. Its values reach the client up to the first nil; refuse with return false, 'why'
-- server.lua
Whip.register(function()
    exports.whip_core:SecureCallback('mygarage:getVehicles', { rateLimit = 1000 }, function(source, player)
        return exports.whip_core:GetVehiclesOf(source)
    end)
end)

-- client.lua, in a command or event handler
local vehicles, why = exports.whip_core:Callback('mygarage:getVehicles')
Returns: true, or false, reason, as SecureEvent. The client receives the handler's answer, or false, reason (the reasons)
RecordEventRejection(eventName, src, reason)SERVER

Records a refusal in the Monitor, from inside your handler, for the two cases whip cannot see by itself: a SecureCallback saying no (its false is an answer, recorded as accepted), and a SecureEvent saying no with a reason in the Monitor but nothing on the player's screen. That call is then recorded as refused, not accepted.

ParamTypeDescription
eventNamestringThe event or callback your handler is answering, named as you registered it
srcnumberThe player whose request was refused
reasonstring|nilWhy, as the Monitor shows it
local PRICES = { mycafe_coffee = 15, mycafe_muffin = 8 }

Whip.register(function()
    exports.whip_core:SecureCallback('mycafe:getPrice', {
        params = { {'itemKey', 'key', 60} },
    }, function(source, player, itemKey)
        local price = PRICES[itemKey]
        if not price then
            exports.whip_core:RecordEventRejection('mycafe:getPrice', source, 'Not sold here')
            return false, 'Not sold here'
        end
        return price
    end)
end)
Returns: nothing
TrackInvocationLock(releaseFn, eventName?, src?)SERVER

Releases a lock your handler took if the handler errors before it can. A lock is anything one player uses at a time: a machine, a safe, a stash. Without this, an error between taking it and releasing it leaves the thing locked until a restart. A handler that returns normally keeps its locks, so release them yourself on every path; this is only the net for an error.

ParamTypeDescription
releaseFnfunctionReleases the lock. Called if the handler errors
eventNamestring|nilThe event or callback your handler is answering
srcnumber|nilThe source your handler was given
Whip.register(function()
    exports.whip_core:SecureEvent('myheist:crackSafe', {
        rateLimit = 2000,                      -- burst 1: see below
        params    = { {'safeId', 'id'} },
    }, function(source, player, safeId)
        local release = acquireSafeLock(safeId)   -- your own: a release function, or nil if taken
        if not release then return false, 'Someone is already at that safe' end
        exports.whip_core:TrackInvocationLock(release, 'myheist:crackSafe', source)
        crackSafe(safeId, source)   -- may wait, may error: if it errors, whip calls release
        release()                   -- the normal path releases it itself
    end)
end)
Pass the event name and the source, so the lock lands on this call. And keep burst at 1 on an event whose handler takes locks (declare a rateLimit): two overlapping calls from one player cannot be told apart. Outside a SecureEvent or SecureCallback handler it attaches nothing and answers false, reason.
Returns: true, or false, reason

Callback

The client half of a SecureCallback: ask the server a question, and wait for its answer.

Callback(name, ...)CLIENT

Asks a server SecureCallback and waits for the answer. Commands and event handlers can wait already; anywhere else, call it inside CreateThread.

ParamTypeDescription
namestringThe callback's name, as the server registered it
...anyThe values, in the order its params lists them
-- client.lua
local stock, why = exports.whip_core:Callback('myshop:getStock', 'corner')
if not stock then
    exports.whip_core:Notify(why, 'error')
    return
end
-- show the shop with its stock

-- From your NUI page: it asks your client, your client asks the server
RegisterNUICallback('getStock', function(data, cb)
    CreateThread(function()
        local stock, why = exports.whip_core:Callback('myshop:getStock', data.shopKey)
        cb({ stock = stock, why = why })
    end)
end)
Returns: whatever the server's handler returned; or false, reason: refused by whip's checks ('Rate limited', 'Player is dead', 'No player session', 'Too far away', a bad value), the handler's own refusal, 'Server error', 'Unknown callback', 'That is no longer available' (its resource stopped), or 'No answer from the server' after 10 seconds

Sentinel: Tamper Guard

whip shares a few facts with every player's game, so each one can draw the world right: who is dead, who is on duty and for which job, who is being escorted, how much damage a player takes, a car's stats. FiveM carries these in statebags, and it lets a player's own game change the statebags about them and about the car they drive. A cheat menu can use that: lower its own damage modifier, and every other player's game believes it and their shots barely hurt.

The Sentinel watches every statebag key whip writes. When a player's game changes one, the Sentinel puts the right value back at once, for everyone, and gives that player a strike. An honest game never writes these keys, so a detection is not a guess: it is a modified client caught in the act. It is on out of the box, and there is nothing to write.

FiveM has a setting that stops games writing statebags at all, sv_stateBagStrictMode. Leave it off if your voice resource needs it off; whip is safe either way, and with it on the Sentinel simply has nothing to catch.

When it catches oneServer owners

  • The true value goes back on the next server tick, for every player.
  • The Monitor shows it: a red Tampered with <key> row in its feed and a red Sentinel tile. Watched keys opens the Sentinel's page: each key with its count, then Detections, what the player wrote beside what the server had. The console (and txAdmin's live console) prints a TAMPER line.
  • The player gets a strike. At 3 strikes they are kicked ("Kicked: statebag tampering detected"), and a note signed Sentinel on their account in the Player Manager records the evidence. That note is the lasting record: the Monitor keeps its history in memory, until whip_core restarts. Strikes wear off after an hour without a new one, and start again if the player rejoins.
  • A kick is not a ban. Once you are sure, ban them from the Player Manager.

A cheat, or a resource? A resource that writes one of whip's keys directly looks exactly like a cheat. One player, struck on a key that helps them, is a cheat. Several players struck on the same key at once, or right after something like an admin menu's revive, is a resource: turn kicking off and find it. After installing a resource you have not checked, leave kicking off for a while and watch the Monitor.

enabled, autoKick and strikesForgetMinutes can also be changed while the server runs, in /whip → Settings → Config → Server (changing a setting in game); a value saved there wins over config.lua. Kicking off is an empty Kick after box there, false here.

Config.SentinelDefaultWhat it does
enabledtruefalse turns the Sentinel off
autoKick3Strikes before a kick. false records them and kicks nobody
strikesForgetMinutes60Minutes without a new strike before the count starts again. false: never
logDebounceMs1000Repeats of one key by one player within this many ms count as one
bootSweeptrueStatebags outlive a restart: at start, any value left wrong is put back, with no strikes
damageModifierClamp{ min = 0.05, max = 4.0 }The range damage and melee modifiers are held to (0.05: take 5% of the damage). Also the most a forged one can do before it is put back

What it watches

Every key whip writes starts with whip, so another resource's own keys never look like tampering. On players: whipDead, whipJob, whipEscorted, whipEscortedBy, whipDamageMod, whipMeleeMod, whipMood. On cars: whipVehicleId, whipVehicleSession, whipStats, whipLive, whipAppearance, whipVehData, whipVehDoors, whipEngineHold. On anything an admin holds with the object viewer: whipOvHold.

For resource developers

  • On the server, ask whip, not the statebag. A statebag is for drawing things on players' screens. A server check reads what the server wrote: the player sheet (isDead), or SentinelGetTruth. The same goes for anything a client hands you that came from a statebag. A player's character name and charId are never in one, since every game can read it: ask for a name with GetPlayerFullName.
  • Never write whip's keys. Change them through whip (its revive, for whipDead). The Sentinel sees a value change, not who changed it, so a bare Player(src).state:set on one looks exactly like a cheat: it is put back, and the player is struck for it.
  • Keep your own facts off statebags where you can. An event sent from the server to the players who need it cannot be forged. If other players' games must read a fact of yours from a statebag, and it matters, the Sentinel can guard it too: the cards below are how.
RegisterSentinelKey(def)SERVER

Puts one of your own statebag keys under the Sentinel, so a player's game changing it is put back and struck like a change to whip's own. For a player key, the truth is whatever you last wrote with SentinelSetPlayerKey. For an entity key, you give a truth function, because entities come and go (a stored car comes back as a new one) and only your resource knows what each should hold: handed the entity, it answers that, or nil when the entity should not have the key (it is then removed).

FieldTypeDescription
def.keystringThe key to watch. One another resource watches is refused
def.familystring'player' or 'entity'
def.truthfunction|nilEntity keys only, and required there: function(entity) → value|nil. It runs only when the key changes. A key at its default should be absent, so answer nil, not an empty table
Whip.register(function()
    local ok, err = exports.whip_core:RegisterSentinelKey({ key = 'mygang_tag', family = 'player' })
    if not ok then print('mygang_tag watch refused: ' .. err) end
end)
Entity keys: change your own table first, then write the key with SentinelSetEntityKey. The Sentinel compares the key with your truth function the moment it is written. The other way round, the console warns that the two disagree and the key is set back to your truth's answer. A bare Entity(e).state:set is worse: it strikes whoever runs the entity, for a car its driver.
Returns: true, or false, reason. Your watches go when your resource stops
SentinelSetPlayerKey(src, key, value) / SentinelGetTruth(src, key)SERVER

Write a player key, and read back what the server wrote. SentinelSetPlayerKey notes the value in the server's own record, then writes the statebag; SentinelGetTruth reads that record, never the statebag, which the player can change. Gate server checks on SentinelGetTruth. It reads whip's own keys too (whipDead, whipJob …), but only whip writes those: change them through whip's own systems.

ParamTypeDescription
srcnumberThe player's server id. To set, they must be connected
keystringTo set: your own keys only. A key another resource watches is refused, and so are whip's; a key nobody watches is accepted
valueanySet only. nil when the fact is "off", not false: an absent key costs nothing to share
-- write the fact
exports.whip_core:SentinelSetPlayerKey(src, 'mygang_tag', 'ballas')

-- check it on the server: the record, never the statebag
if exports.whip_core:SentinelGetTruth(targetId, 'mygang_tag') == 'ballas' then
    -- ...
end
Returns: set: true, or false, reason ('no such player', 'key "whipDead" is owned by whip_core') · truth: the value the server wrote (false and nil are different answers here)
SentinelSetEntityKey(entity, key, value)SERVER

Writes one of your entity keys. Change your own table (the one your truth function reads) first, then write through this: if the two disagree, the console says so and nobody is struck. A bare Entity(e).state:set strikes the car's driver instead.

ParamTypeDescription
entitynumberThe entity (it must exist)
keystringYour own keys only: another resource's, and whip's, are refused. A key nobody watches is accepted
valueanyWhat the key should hold; nil removes it
tunes[plate] = t                                                   -- your table, first
exports.whip_core:SentinelSetEntityKey(veh, 'mytune_data', t)     -- then the key
Returns: true, or false, reason ('no such entity', 'key "x" is owned by …')

Permissions

For roles between "everyone" and your full admins: a builder, a moderator, a garage manager. Your resource declares a permission, it is given to a player, and your events ask for it with permission = 'name'. Nobody edits server.cfg and nobody restarts: a grant works the moment it is given.

A permission is given to an account, so every character on it has it. That makes it a staff role, not a job: for "police only", check the job in your handler (Jobs & Business). Full admins hold every permission: the whip.devtools ACE with developer mode on, and staff given dev tools in the Player Manager until the restart.

Permission or ACE?

ace = '…'permission = '…'
What it isFiveM's own permission systemwhip's
GivenIn server.cfg, with add_aceFrom your code, with GrantPermission, or by an admin in /whip → Players → Player Manager → the player → Permissions (Give / Take), with no code at all
Best forYour full admins, and anything only they should doStaff roles you hand out and take back while the server runs
A dead playerLet through: it is an admin toolRefused, as for any event (whileDead = true lets them)

Using one

Whip.register(function()
    -- 1. Declare it
    exports.whip_core:RegisterPermission('mygarage.manage', {
        label       = 'Garage manager',
        description = 'Add and remove garages',
    })

    -- 2. Ask for it
    exports.whip_core:SecureEvent('mygarage:remove', {
        permission = 'mygarage.manage',
        params     = { {'garageId', 'id'} },
    }, function(source, player, garageId)
        -- only a garage manager, or a full admin, gets here
    end)
end)

-- 3. Give it: here, from the server console, by the player's server id
RegisterCommand('makegaragemanager', function(source, args)
    if source ~= 0 then return end                    -- the console only
    local target = exports.whip_core:GetPlayer(tonumber(args[1]))
    if not target then return print('No player on a character with that id') end
    local ok, why = exports.whip_core:GrantPermission(tonumber(args[1]), 'mygarage.manage')
    print(ok and (target.fullName .. ' is a garage manager') or why)
end)

A list asks for any one of them: permission = { 'mygarage.manage', 'mygarage.admin' }. A refused player shows in the Monitor with the permission they lacked.

Giving oneServer owners

whip's own permissions, the Director's builders and admins, are given in /whip → Director → Access. Any other permission is given the way the resource that declared it says: usually a command or a screen of its own, like step 3 above. whip has no general screen for them.

RegisterPermission(name, def?)SERVER

Declares a permission. The name is your resource's; another resource cannot take it. The declaration goes when your resource stops, but its grants stay on record and in force.

FieldTypeDescription
namestring3 to 64 letters, digits, ., _ and -. Start it with your resource's name
def.labelstring?The name the Monitor shows when someone is refused for lacking it
def.descriptionstring?A sentence about it, for your own screens
def.impliesstring[]?Other permissions this one includes: a Director admin is a builder too
def.devtoolsboolean?false: full admins do not hold it automatically (they do if left out)
def.grantedBystring?A permission whose holders may give and take this one, in the Player Manager and on the Director's Access page. A full admin always may; an admin given dev tools only until the restart needs this permission to
Whip.register(function()
    exports.whip_core:RegisterPermission('mygarage.manage', {
        label       = 'Garage manager',
        description = 'Add and remove garages',
        implies     = { 'mygarage.view' },   -- a manager can view, too
    })
end)
Returns: true, or false, reason
HasPermission(source, name)SERVER

Does this player have it: a grant on their account, one that includes it, or full admin. It costs nothing to ask (held in memory). For an event, permission = 'name' in its schema asks for you.

ParamTypeDescription
sourcenumberThe player's server id
namestringThe permission
if not exports.whip_core:HasPermission(source, 'mygarage.manage') then
    return false, 'You cannot manage garages'
end
Returns: boolean
GrantPermission(who, name) · RevokePermission(who, name)SERVER

Gives a person's account a permission, or takes it away. It is saved, then in force at once. whip_core:permission:changed fires on the server, and on the game of every online player on the account the local whip_core:permission:changed fires (Client Events; whip shows them nothing: handle it to tell them), and the activity log records it, with your resource as the giver.

ParamTypeDescription
whonumber|tableA person: an online player's server id, or { charId = n } (online or not); or the account itself, { userId = n }. The same player as HasPermission(source, …)
namestringThe permission
local ok, why = exports.whip_core:GrantPermission(targetSource, 'mygarage.manage')
if not ok then return false, why end
Returns: true, or false, reason
GetPermissionHolders(name)SERVER

Everyone given it directly, each named by their online character, else their latest one. Full admins hold every permission without being listed.

ParamTypeDescription
namestringThe permission
Returns: { { userId, name, account, grantedBy, grantedAt, online }, … }, or false, reason

Character Lifecycle

A player connects, picks a character, plays, and logs out or leaves. What your resource can rely on at each step:

Connecting

A player needs a FiveM licence to join; without one they are turned away. Anyone on the ban list (by any of their identifiers) is turned away with the reason and when the ban ends. Everyone else gets an account, their userId, made the first time they connect, and is then connected with no character yet.

Character Selection

The character screen shows up to Config.MaxCharacters (default 4) characters, where the player picks one, makes one or deletes one.

Load Flow

When a character is picked, whip_core loads its row, pockets and stats, puts the player in the shared world (routing bucket 0), sends the character to their game (which spawns the ped and applies the appearance) and syncs what is around them: ground items, stashes, vehicles and keys, shops, zones, time and weather, jobs. The server's whip_core:player:loaded fires last: your "player ready" hook. The client's own whip_core:player:loaded fires once the ped is in the world and the screen is back.

Save System

Memory is the truth; the database catches up. A change takes effect at once, in whip's memory, and is written to the database within about a second (Config.FlushInterval, 1000 ms), so a busy server doesn't spend its time waiting on the database.

One player action saves as one: you write no saving code. Every SecureEvent and SecureCallback handler is an action. Whatever whip saves while it runs: the item a use handler took, the nitro it put on the car, the cash, the bank deposit, the activity log rows, lands in ONE transaction: when the handler ends, or with a bank or car data write made inside it. That includes what your resource does through whip's exports while its handler runs, and while whip runs your use handler, item action, onComplete, panel hook or AddAction callback.

Moving an item from one player to another? Do it in ONE call: StoreMove(fromAddr, toAddr), not RemoveItem then AddItem. One call always saves as one; two calls can save as two.

Your resource's OWN database writes join in when you hand them to whip. If you change an inventory and then write a row to a table of yours, a sales ledger after a RemoveItem, write it with CommitWithAction: the row and the item land in one transaction, or neither does. (A write you make yourself through oxmysql is not tied: call exports.whip_core:SavePlayer(source) first, so a crash between them cannot leave the item in both places.)
WhatWhenHow
Pockets, stashes, boots, health and armour, activity logWithin Config.FlushInterval (1s), or when the action that changed them endsOnly what changed since the last write, everything owed in ONE transaction. Both halves of a move always land together
Player position, hunger, thirst and your own saved statsEvery Config.PlayerPositionSaveInterval (30s): the position if they moved, a stat if it changedWith the player's pockets and row. A stat that drops every few seconds would otherwise be a write every few seconds for every player
Car stats (fuel, nitro…) and car positionEvery Config.VehicleStatsSaveInterval (15s), or with the action that changed themOne statement per car
Car data, the bank, ground itemsImmediatelyCar data and bank writes carry the running action's other saves in the same transaction
Disconnect and logoutAt onceThe player's unit is written before the session goes; their next login waits for anything still owed
restart whip_coreWhen it stopsEvery owed write is sent (a stopping resource cannot wait for answers)
txAdmin restart or shutdownOn txAdmin's warningThe final save writes everything, most important first, waiting for each; the console says if anything did not fit. Give it room: set txAdmin's Shutdown Notice Delay to 15 seconds

When a write fails

A failed write is not a failed action. The change stands in memory, and whip keeps trying to write it, waiting longer each time, up to a minute. It never gives up: after five failures the save is listed as stuck (/whipsaves in the console shows it, and admins are told every minute), and it is still written the moment the database takes it. A character whose save is still waiting cannot be loaded again until it lands.

If the database goes away (connection errors, not slowness), whip locks players' items: the inventory will not open and item actions are refused, so nobody changes what cannot be saved. When it is back, everything owed is written first, then items unlock and the console prints BACK TO NORMAL with what was saved.

Stats are saved from the server's own values. Health, armour, hunger and thirst live on the server, and a save never asks the player's game. Combat damage reaches the server from the hurt player's game as it happens.
Health and armour are what the player's game last reported, up or down. A player's character belongs to their own game in FiveM (it is the same on QBCore and ESX), so the server takes the health and armour it reports: a modified game can report full armour it never bought. Only a report of 0 health is checked against the character itself. So don't treat "is at full health" or "has armour" as proof on the server. To sell armour, give it with SetStat after the payment, and keep your own record of what you sold. Hunger, thirst and your own stats are the server's alone.

Logging out and leaving

Logout takes the player back to the character screen; they stay connected. Disconnect is leaving the server. Both do the same for your resource:

  • The character and their pockets are saved, along with any stash or boot they had open.
  • Panels they had open close. A panel your resource opened gets its onClose if they were its last viewer, which is where you save it.
  • They are clocked off every job, and any escort (escorting or being escorted) ends.
  • whip_core:player:logout fires, and its why says which happened ('logout' or 'disconnect').

New Characters

A new character starts with each stat at its own starting value (hunger and thirst full), a bank account holding Config.StartingBalance ($1000), and is loaded straight away, with the appearance creator open.

That first load carries isNewCharacter = true in the player data whip_core:player:loaded hands you (e.newCharacter on the server and the client alike, and e.player.isNewCharacter). It is the hook for a starter car or a welcome pack. Every later load of that character has it false, including the loads that open the creator again because the player left it unfinished.

Deleting a Character

Only from the character screen. What the character held goes back to stock, and nothing inside it is thrown away:

WhatAfter the delete
Homes they ownedNo owner: up for sale again. Every key to them is gone; the furniture and everything stored inside stay, for whoever gets the home next
Keys they heldRemoved
JobsThey leave every job. A business they owned has no owner and keeps running: staff, shop and business account stay; give it a new owner in /whip → Economy → Jobs
Stashes locked to themThe contents stay; the owner and one-person lock are cleared
Cars and bank accountsStay exactly as they are (for systems such as shared accounts and shared garages); an admin can reassign them

A resource that keeps its own per-character things listens for whip_core:character:deleted (below) and does the same.

Any server resource can fire that event. It is news, not proof. Before your handler removes anything for good, check that the character really is deleted: if not exports.whip_core:IsCharacterDeleted(e.charId) then return end. It answers true for a deleted character (or one that never existed), and false for a live one, or when it cannot tell, so a doubt never removes anything.
New character is not new player. A player can delete a character and make another (deleting frees the slot), and every one of them arrives with isNewCharacter = true. A starter gift that can be sold or handed on is a gift that can be farmed. Tie it to the account (e.player.userId) if it must be once per person, or make the gift something that cannot leave the character.

Server Events

EventWhenPayload (one table)
whip_core:player:loadedCharacter fully loaded and ready. newCharacter is true on a brand-new character's first load{ source, charId, name, newCharacter, player }: the same table on the client
whip_core:player:logoutLogout or disconnect (after save){ source, charId, player, why }
whip_core:character:createdNew character created{ source, charId }
whip_core:character:deletedCharacter deleted{ source, charId }
whip_core:character:renamedAn admin renamed a character (Player Manager). The name only: the charId and everything kept by it stay. Online or not; source is nil when they are not in. A name you keep to show, update it here; never key anything by name{ charId, source, firstName, lastName, name, oldName, by }

On the renamed player's own game, whip_core:player:renamed fires with { charId, firstName, lastName, name }, after their sheet's names have changed.

Restarting your resource mid-session? whip_core:player:loaded is not sent again for players who are already in. If you set something up per player in that handler, also do it for everyone already loaded, from Whip.register: 
local function setUp(source, player) --[[ your per-player setup ]] end

AddEventHandler('whip_core:player:loaded', function(e) setUp(e.source, e.player) end)

Whip.register(function()
    for source, player in pairs(exports.whip_core:GetPlayers()) do setUp(source, player) end
end)
GetPlayers answers every loaded player, keyed by server id. Make setUp safe to run twice for one player: Whip.register runs again whenever whip_core restarts.

Player

IsReady() SERVER

Has whip_core finished starting? For code that has to ask: a command that should refuse while whip_core is down. Registration does not need it: Whip.register runs your function at the right times on its own (and Whip.isReady() asks this for you, safely, from the helper).

if not exports.whip_core:IsReady() then return end
See Your First Resource, step 3 for how registration works and why it is safe to run twice.
Returns: boolean
IsSessionCurrent(source, session)SERVER

Is this still the same character session: loaded, not logging out, and not replaced by the next character on the same source? Every sheet carries a session number, new for each character load. Ask this in a handler that waited (a database await, a Wait, a progress bar) before it gives or takes something: a player who logs out and picks another character inside that wait is on the same source, and without the check the goods land on the second character while the charge stays on the first.

exports.whip_core:SecureEvent('myshop:buy', {
    params = { {'item', 'enum', { 'lockpick' }} },
}, function(source, player, item)
    local receipt, err = exports.whip_core:ChargePlayer(source, 500)
    if not receipt then return false, err end
    Wait(4000)   -- the hand-over animation
    if not exports.whip_core:IsSessionCurrent(source, player.session) then
        exports.whip_core:RefundPlayer(receipt)
        return false, 'You left before the sale went through'
    end
    local given, why = exports.whip_core:AddItem(source, item, 1)
    if not given then exports.whip_core:RefundPlayer(receipt) return false, why end
end)
Logout waits up to two seconds for a player's running handlers before its final save (and ends their progress bars and skill checks first), so a short wait is covered without this. The check is for the long one.
Returns: boolean
GetPlayer(source) SERVER

Get a connected player's data as a plain table. Returns nil until their character is fully loaded, which makes it a readiness check as well as a getter.

ParamTypeDescription
sourcenumberServer player ID
local player = exports.whip_core:GetPlayer(source)
if not player then return false, 'Still loading' end   -- nil until the character is in
print(player.fullName, player.charId, player.cash)       -- a copy: read it, call exports to change things
Returns: table|nil: see WhipPlayer Object. nil until the character has finished loading
It copies the whole sheet, appearance included. For one number use GetCharId; to ask "are they in?" use IsPlayerLoaded. Neither copies anything.
GetCharId(source) · IsPlayerLoaded(source) · IsPlayerDead(source)SERVER

GetCharId: their charId, or nil while no character is loaded. IsPlayerLoaded: true once a character is loaded. IsPlayerDead: true while they are down, the server's own reading (what a SecureEvent's whileDead asks). All read memory and copy nothing, so they are the calls for a hot path.

local charId = exports.whip_core:GetCharId(source)
if not charId then return false, 'Still loading' end
Returns: integer|nil · boolean
GetPlayers(opts?) SERVER

Get all connected players with loaded characters. GetPlayers({ light = true }) gives each one's light sheet: source, session, userId, charId, names, date of birth, gender, isDead, without the position, cash, health and appearance that each full sheet reads: much cheaper when you only want to know who is on.

for source, p in pairs(exports.whip_core:GetPlayers({ light = true })) do
    print(source, p.fullName)
end
Returns: table<number, table>: each player's sheet, keyed by server id
GetPlayerFromUserId(userId) SERVER

Find a player by their persistent user ID.

ParamTypeDescription
userIdnumberDatabase user ID
Returns: table|nil: the player sheet, or nil when that account has no character in
GetPlayerFromCharId(charId) SERVER

Find a player by their active character ID.

ParamTypeDescription
charIdnumberCharacter ID
local owner = exports.whip_core:GetPlayerFromCharId(ownerCharId)
if owner then exports.whip_core:NotifyPlayer(owner.source, 'Your car is being towed', 'warning') end
Returns: table|nil: the player sheet, or nil when that character is not online
GetPlayersInRange(coords, range?) SERVER

The players within network range of a point: Config.NetworkRange, 424 m by default. Send a message about a place to these instead of -1, which reaches every player on the server.

ParamTypeDescription
coordsvector3 | tableThe point (x, y; height is ignored)
rangenumber?Metres; default Config.NetworkRange
Returns: number[] server ids: empty for bad input
IsCharacterDeleted(charId) SERVER

Is this character gone: deleted, or never there? Ask it before your resource removes anything for good on whip_core:character:deleted, which any server resource can fire.

AddEventHandler('whip_core:character:deleted', function(e)
    if not exports.whip_core:IsCharacterDeleted(e.charId) then return end   -- a fired copy, or a doubt
    removeLicences(e.charId)   -- your own per-character data
end)
Returns: true, 'deleted' or true, 'no such character'; false for a live character, and false, why when it cannot tell (a bad id, the database not answering), so a doubt never removes anything
GetPlayerFromIdentifier(idType, identifier) SERVER

Find a player by a platform identifier.

ParamTypeDescription
idTypestring'license', 'steam', 'discord', or 'fivem'
identifierstringThe identifier value
Returns: table|nil: the player sheet, not the live object
GetPlayerIdentifiers(source) SERVER

The four platform identifiers, which GetPlayer deliberately leaves off the player sheet.

ParamTypeDescription
sourcenumberServer player ID
Returns: table|nil: { discord, fivem, license, steam }

Acting on a player

Each takes a source and finds the player itself, so there is no player object to go stale between fetching and using it.

GetPlayerCash(source)SERVER

Total cash items across every container the character carries.

Returns: number: 0, 'Player not loaded' if the player is not loaded
AddPlayerCash(source, amount, reason)SERVER

The low-level call: banknotes into the player's pockets, or nothing. To pay a player, use PayPlayer: it puts what does not fit at their feet (or pays their bank) and says where it went. Use this one only when notes in the pockets are the whole point and a payment on the ground would be wrong (change from a till the player must be able to put back).

ParamTypeDescription
amountnumberPositive integer
reasonstring?Optional. Written in the activity log beside your resource's name, e.g. 'rental refund · by my_rentals', so an admin can tell a wage from a refund. Leave it out and the row just says which resource it was.
local paid, why = exports.whip_core:AddPlayerCash(source, 20, 'change')
if not paid then return false, why end   -- no room for the notes: nothing was paid
Returns: true, or false, reason: no room, no such player, or not a whole number of dollars
Cash never drops. Unlike AddItem, banknotes that will not fit are refused, not put on the floor: a payout that "succeeded" onto the pavement is money you think you paid. If this answers false, nothing was paid: pay into their bank instead, or tell them. The amount must be a whole number of dollars: 12.5 is refused and pays nothing, so round it yourself first (math.floor(hours * 12.5)).
RemovePlayerCash(source, amount, reason)SERVER

Remove cash items. Returns false without taking anything if they do not have enough.

Check the return value. This is the difference between charging someone and believing you charged them.
ParamTypeDescription
amountnumberPositive integer
reasonstring?Optional, for the activity log (see AddPlayerCash)
local ok, why = exports.whip_core:RemovePlayerCash(source, 50, 'parking fine')
if not ok then return false, why end   -- 'Not enough cash': nothing was taken
Returns: true, or false, reason ('Not enough cash' when they do not have it)
NotifyPlayer(source, text, kind, duration)SERVER

Show a player one of whip's toasts, of any kind, from the server. -1 as the source shows it to everyone.

exports.whip_core:NotifyPlayer(source, 'Your rental ends in 5 minutes', 'warning')
ParamTypeDescription
textstringUp to 300 characters
kindstring?'info' (default), 'success', 'warning' or 'error'
durationnumber?Milliseconds. Leave it out for the usual short toast.
Returns: boolean: false for a player who is not on the server, or no text
ShowPlayerText(source, text, opts) · HidePlayerText(source)SERVER

The instruction band (the client's ShowText) from the server: a step of a job, a prompt. One band per player, and a new one takes it over; HidePlayerText takes down only yours. Gone when your resource stops, your run's tag is released (opts.tag), or they log out. Colour codes are removed; at most 200 characters. (The Director's own objectives are not on the band: each run has a card of its own at the top right, which the band never takes.)

exports.whip_core:ShowPlayerText(source, 'Take the package to the docks')
exports.whip_core:ShowPlayerText(source, 'Get out before the alarm', { countdown = 90 })   -- 'Get out before the alarm · 1:30'
exports.whip_core:HidePlayerText(source)
ParamTypeDescription
textstringWhat it says
opts.positionstring?'bottom' (default) or 'top'
opts.progressnumber?0–100: fills the band, as a progress bar does
opts.countdownnumber?Seconds: a clock after the text, counted down by the player's own game a second at a time (sent once, never every second), the band's fill draining with it. At 0:00 it stops and stays until the text changes. While another resource has the band the clock goes on unseen, and comes back when the band is free
opts.countdownTotalnumber?Seconds: the clock's full length, for the fill, when it started before now (default: countdown)
opts.tagstring?Your run tag (see ReleaseTag)
Returns: true, or false, reason
ShowBlip(audience, id, spec) · RemoveBlip(id) · SetPlayerWaypoint(source, coords)SERVER

A blip on some players' maps, from the server. audience is 'everyone', { people = { serverId | { charId = n } } }, or a job's people, { job = 'police', onDuty = true }; a character named by charId sees it whenever they are on, and a job's people as they clock on and off. The same id again moves or changes that blip; ids are your resource's own. Gone when your resource stops or your run's tag is released. SetPlayerWaypoint sets GTA's own waypoint for one player. No frame loop on either side.

exports.whip_core:ShowBlip({ people = { source } }, 'dropoff', {
    coords = vector3(215.0, -810.0, 30.7), label = 'Drop-off', color = 5, route = true,
})
exports.whip_core:RemoveBlip('dropoff')
exports.whip_core:SetPlayerWaypoint(source, vector3(215.0, -810.0, 30.7))
specTypeDescription
coordsvector3Where (or { x, y, z })
labelstring?Its name in the map's legend (40 characters)
spriteinteger?GTA's blip icon number: 1 (the dot, default). An area with no label and no route gets none (the circle alone); 0 asks for none. A name and a route live on the dot.
colorinteger?GTA's blip colour number: 5 yellow (default), 1 red, 2 green, 3 blue, 0 white
routeboolean?The GPS route to it
radiusnumber?Metres: an area (a translucent circle) instead of a point
shortRangeboolean?Only on the radar when near, like a shop (default: always shown)
scale · flashnumber? · boolean?Its size (0.3–2, default 0.9) · it flashes
tagstring?Your run tag (see ReleaseTag)
Returns: true, or false, reason
ShowPropSet(id, spec) · HidePropSet(id)SERVER

Props put up from the server and made by each player's own game as they come near (and removed as they leave): crates in a warehouse, barriers across a road, cash on a table. They are not networked, so they cost the server nothing and never migrate; they are scenery: solid unless you say not, frozen exactly where you put them (no snap to the ground), and nobody can pick them up. Inside an MLO, interior = true makes each game wait for the interior before making the prop and files it in its room (a lamp, light = true, in the interior's limbo so it lights the room). The same id again replaces the set; ids are your resource's own; yours go when your resource stops or your run's tag is released.

exports.whip_core:ShowPropSet('roadblock', {
    props = {
        { model = 'prop_barrier_work05', coords = vector3(215.0, -810.0, 30.7), heading = 90.0 },
        { model = 'prop_mp_cone_01', coords = vector3(217.0, -810.0, 30.4) },
        { model = 'prop_worklight_03a', coords = vector3(219.0, -811.0, 30.7), light = true },
    },
})
exports.whip_core:HidePropSet('roadblock')
specTypeDescription
propstable1 to Config.PropSetMaxProps props (256 unless changed): { model, coords, rot?, heading?, interior?, light?, collision?, weapon?, attach?, attachOffset?, attachRot? }. rot is vector3(tiltForward, tiltSideways, heading) in degrees (GTA's rotation order 2, as furniture is saved); heading alone turns it. collision = false: players walk through it
props[n].weaponstring?A firearm with a world model, GTA's ('WEAPON_RPG') or one a running resource adds (Whip.weapons): each game makes that gun's world model (the Director's Fixed Weapon)
props[n].attachtable?What it rides on: { net = netId } (a networked car or NPC), { set = id, index = n } (a prop of another of your sets that is up), or { index = n } (a prop of this same set). attachOffset is { x, y, z } in metres from it, attachRot { x, y, z } in degrees. Each game attaches its own copy once it has both, and puts it back where it was placed when the parent goes
audience'everyone' | table?Who sees them (default everyone): { people = { serverId | { charId = n } } }
tagstring?Your run tag (see ReleaseTag)
Returns: true, or false, reason. A model a player's game does not have is left out on that game (and said in its console).
GetPlayerMetadata(source, key)SERVER

Read one metadata key, or the whole table when key is omitted. The player's own game holds the same table, so nothing in it is secret (see SetPlayerMetadata).

Returns: any
SetPlayerMetadata(source, key, value)SERVER

Write one metadata key. Persists with the character on the next save.

exports.whip_core:SetPlayerMetadata(source, 'licences', { driving = true })
local licences = exports.whip_core:GetPlayerMetadata(source, 'licences') or {}
The player's own game gets every value. Each change is sent to their client (their GetPlayerData), so a player with a mod menu can read it. Keep a secret (a code, an answer, a cheat flag) in your own server-side table or database row instead. whip's own keys are refused: appearance, outfits, creatorPending, walk, mood, whipFlags, moneyHeldOwed, pourRefundOwed, lastSeat. Each has its own call, and one shared name would overwrite the other. Name yours after your resource ('myjob_licences'), as the keys are one table shared by every resource.
Returns: true, or false, reason: one of whip's own keys, the player is not loaded, or the value cannot be saved (a function, NaN, …)
GetPlayerCoords(source)SERVER

Where the player is now: their ped's position and heading, read on the server (the saved position until the character has spawned).

Returns: vector4|nil
GetPlayerFullName(source)SERVER

The character's full name: just the name, where GetPlayer copies the whole sheet. For something that runs often, like naming the author of every chat message. Not FiveM's GetPlayerName, which is the account's name.

Returns: string|nil: nil for a player not in a character yet
GetCharacterNames(charIds)SERVER

Characters' names by charId, online or not: for a list of people who are not all on, like a job's staff or a shared account's users. Up to 200 at a time. It answers anyone's name; before showing a player someone they don't already know (a list of who is nearby, the name behind a typed ID), ask CanSeePlayerName.

ParamTypeDescription
charIdsnumber[]The characters
local staff = exports.whip_core:GetJobEmployees('burgershot') or {}
local ids = {}
for charId in pairs(staff) do ids[#ids + 1] = charId end
local names = exports.whip_core:GetCharacterNames(ids)
for charId, emp in pairs(staff) do print(names[charId] or '?', emp.roleName) end
Returns: table: { [charId] = 'First Last' }; a charId that names no character is left out
CanSeePlayerName(viewer, target)SERVER

May this player be shown that one's character name? whip's one name rule, Config.ShowPlayerNames: with 'nearby', only someone within PlayerNameRange, in the same world and not in the character creator (an offline character is never nearby); 'always' anyone; 'never' only yourself. The client's GetPlayerFullName, the phone's lists of people nearby and the Director's Pick Team all follow it. Use it wherever your resource shows a player someone's name.

ParamTypeDescription
viewerpersonThe player who would see it: source, or { charId = n } (online)
targetpersonWhose name: source, or { charId = n }
-- A "who's here" list: only the people this player may see by name
local list = {}
for _, target in ipairs(nearbySources) do
    if exports.whip_core:CanSeePlayerName(source, target) then
        list[#list + 1] = exports.whip_core:GetPlayerFullName(target)
    end
end
Returns: true, or false, why ('Too far away', 'Names are hidden on this server', 'Player not loaded')
SavePlayer(source)SERVER

Write this character's inventory, then their row, now, rather than waiting for the next flush.

You rarely need this. Writes are batched every second and forced on disconnect, logout and resource stop. Reach for it when your own write has to follow an inventory change you made (a ledger row after a RemoveItem) so a crash between the two cannot leave the item in both places; or when something outside whip is about to read the rows directly.
Returns: boolean ok, string|nil err
KickPlayer(source, reason)SERVER

Save the character and drop the player, showing them the reason.

Returns: boolean ok, string|nil err
LogoutPlayer(source)SERVER

Save the character, tear down its server-side state, and return the player to character select.

A teardown, not a screen change. The player's entry is dropped from the live table, and the same character can then be loaded again into a fresh inventory. Unless you are building your own character-select flow, you want KickPlayer.
Returns: boolean ok, string|nil err: false, 'Already leaving' while they are already logging out or disconnecting
SanitizeAppearance(appearance)SERVER

Run an appearance table through whip's own validator (the same one the character creator's save path uses) and get back either the cleaned version or the reason it was refused. Every drawable, texture and prop index is clamped to a legal range.

Tattoos are an optional list, tattoos = { { collection = 'mpBiker_overlays', overlay = 'MP_MP_Biker_Tat_000_M' }, ... }, in the order they were put on. A tattoo is kept only if whip's list (shared/tattoo_list.lua) names it for that body (written back in the list's spelling, once each, at most 40) and anything else is dropped, never refused. No tattoos: no tattoos key at all.

The hair fade (the shaved stubble drawn on the scalp under a short hairstyle, picked on the character editor's Hair tab, Fade) is optional too: hairFade = { collection = 'multiplayer_overlays', overlay = 'NG_M_Hair_001' }, one at most. It is kept only if whip's list (shared/hair_fades.lua) names it for that body, written back in the list's spelling; anything else is dropped. No fade: no hairFade key.

ParamTypeDescription
appearancetableAppearance data to validate
local ok, result = exports.whip_core:SanitizeAppearance(appearance)
if not ok then return false, result end   -- result is the reason
outfits[charId] = result                  -- result is the cleaned table
Returns: boolean ok, table|string result: the sanitized appearance, or the reason it was refused

WhipPlayer Object

Returned by GetPlayer(source): a plain, copyable table of player data. There are no methods: see the export list below for those.

Fields

local player = exports.whip_core:GetPlayer(source)   -- nil until the character is loaded
if not player then return end

-- player.source       number  the server id
-- player.session      number  this character load (for IsSessionCurrent)
-- player.userId       number  the account
-- player.charId       number  the character
-- player.firstName, player.lastName, player.fullName  ("First Last")
-- player.dateOfBirth  string  "YYYY-MM-DD"
-- player.gender       string
-- player.cash         number  cash on hand
-- player.position     table   { x, y, z, w }
-- player.health       number  0-200 (200 full)
-- player.armour       number
-- player.isDead       boolean
-- player.metadata     table   (left out of the sheet a SecureEvent handler is given)
The player's identifiers are not on the sheet. license, steam, discord and fivem stay off it because whip sends the same sheet to the client. Ask for them with exports.whip_core:GetPlayerIdentifiers(source), which returns { discord, fivem, license, steam }.
There is no player.inventory on the sheet. Read pockets with GetInventory(source).
From a satellite, the readiness check is simply whether GetPlayer returned anything. A player is added to whip_core's registry only after their inventory has come back from the database, so GetPlayer(source) answers nil right up until the character is completely loaded, and whip_core:player:loaded fires at the same moment. Either is a correct gate; the event is better, because waiting beats asking repeatedly.
There is no player.statuses field. Hunger, thirst and every other stat live in the Stats system, not on the player object: read them with GetAllStats(source) or GetStat(source, name).

Acting on a player

The sheet has no methods. To act on a player, call the export with their source (each has its card under Player):

ToExport
Read their cashGetPlayerCash(source)
Give or take cashAddPlayerCash(source, n), RemovePlayerCash(source, n)
Read or write metadataGetPlayerMetadata(source, key), SetPlayerMetadata(source, key, value)
Where they are nowGetPlayerCoords(source)
Save nowSavePlayer(source)
Kick them, or send them to character selectKickPlayer(source, reason), LogoutPlayer(source)

Player & Status (Client)

IsReady()CLIENT

Have whip_core's client files all loaded? For code that has to ask. Registration does not: Whip.register in a client script runs your function when whip_core's client is ready, and again if it restarts.

This is not "has the player loaded a character": that is IsPlayerLoaded(). This one is about whip_core itself being ready to receive registrations. See Your First Resource, step 3.
Returns: boolean
GetPlayerData()CLIENT

The local player's sheet, kept current: the login data, with cash and metadata updated as they change on the server, and isDead, health and armour read live at the moment you call. A copy: changing it changes nothing.

local me = exports.whip_core:GetPlayerData()
if me.charId then print(me.fullName, me.cash) end   -- {} before a character is loaded
Returns: table: { source, userId, charId, firstName, lastName, fullName, dateOfBirth, gender, cash, position, health, armour, isDead, metadata }; {} before a character is loaded
position is where the character was when they loaded; use GetEntityCoords(PlayerPedId()) for where they are now.
IsPlayerLoaded()CLIENT

Check if a character is loaded and ready.

Returns: bool
EnterCharacter(opts?)CLIENT

Into a character with nobody at the game, for tools and tests (a test tool uses it after a whip_core restart): past the welcome screen as a press would, the character's card chosen, and Play as the button does, without the map, so they arrive where they left. Waits until the character is loaded (up to 90 s).

local ok, why = exports.whip_core:EnterCharacter({ slot = 1 })
optsTypeWhat it does
charIdnumberThe character, by id
slotnumberOr its card's place on the character screen. The first card when neither is given
Returns: ok, why (false, 'already in a character' when one is loaded)
GetCharId()CLIENT

Get the local player's character ID.

Returns: number|nil
GetPlayerFullName(serverId, wait)CLIENT

Another player's character name, by server id: asked of the server, which answers under Config.ShowPlayerNames: 'nearby' (the default, within Config.PlayerNameRange metres, in the same instance), 'always' or 'never'. The same name as the server export. Names are not on the shared player data (every client receives that, so any cheat menu could list every character); this is how you get one.

ParamTypeDescription
serverIdnumberThe player's server id: ctx.player.serverId when aiming at them
waitboolean|niltrue waits for the server's answer (up to a few seconds). Left out, it answers from what it already knows: the first ask for someone answers nil and fetches, and the next one has the name: right for a label, which is asked every frame
Returns: string|nil: nil while fetching, for someone too far away (or when names are 'never'), or for nobody at that id
label = function(ctx)
    local name = exports.whip_core:GetPlayerFullName(ctx.player.serverId)
    return name and ('Search ' .. name) or 'Search'
end,
GetStat(name)CLIENT

Read one stat from the local cache. Any stat registered with RegisterStat, not just hunger and thirst.

ParamTypeDescription
namestringStat name, e.g. 'hunger'
Returns: number|nil: nil if that stat has never been set for this player
GetAllStats()CLIENT

Every stat the client currently knows about, as a copy.

Needs count down. hunger and thirst start at 100, decay towards 0, and start costing health once they are at 10 or below. So AddStat(source, 'hunger', 25) feeds the player.
Returns: table: { [name] = number }
HasEffect(name)CLIENT

Is a named effect currently active on the local player?

ParamTypeDescription
namestringEffect name
Returns: boolean
GetEffects()CLIENT

Every active effect on the local player, as a copy: the same plain data as the server's GetEffects.

Returns: table: { [name] = { duration, remaining, magnitude, tickRate, damageModifier, meleeModifier, resource } }
OnStatChange(name, callback, id, opts)CLIENT

Run a function whenever a stat changes, instead of polling it every frame. The server has the same export, for every player (Stats guide).

ParamTypeDescription
namestringStat to watch, or '*' for every stat
callbackfunction(newValue, oldValue), or (name, newValue, oldValue) for '*'
idany|nilOnly to hold two listeners on one stat (the options may go here instead)
