optstable|niltable = true: one table { key, value, old } instead · now = true: also called once straight away with the current value (old = nil)
Returns: boolean ok, string|nil err
-- Warn once, as hunger falls into the danger zone. Needs count DOWN: 100 is full.
Whip.register(function()
    exports.whip_core:OnStatChange('hunger', function(new, old)
        if new <= 20 and (old or 100) > 20 then   -- old is nil the first time
            exports.whip_core:Notify('You are starving.', 'error')
        end
    end)
end)
Stats are written on the server, never on the client. There is no client-side setter, and that is on purpose: a value the client can write is a value the client can invent. Change a stat with the server exports SetStat(source, name, value, reason) and AddStat(source, name, delta, reason); the new value is pushed down to the client automatically, where GetStat and OnStatChange pick it up.
IsPlayerDead()CLIENT

Check if the local player is in the death state. See Death guide.

Returns: boolean
GetBodyState()CLIENT

Is the player doing something with their body that work in the hands cannot be done in? Under water (swimming under, or sitting in a car that has sunk), swimming, or falling (a fall, a skydive): the first that applies, and the words to show them. For something instant your resource does; a progress bar takes the same states as notWhile and checks them itself, at the start and while it runs.

local state, words = exports.whip_core:GetBodyState()
if state then exports.whip_core:Notify(words, 'error') return end   -- 'You cannot do that while swimming'
Returns: 'underwater', 'swimming' or 'falling' and the words, or false
GetVoiceLevel() / GetVoiceName()CLIENT

The player's current voice range setting: the value as a number (20, 50 or 100) and its name ('Whisper', 'Normal', 'Shout'). The player cycles it with Z (the whip_cyclevoice key mapping, rebindable in GTA settings), and the HUD bar reads GetVoiceLevel directly.

Returns: number (20 / 50 / 100) / string ('Whisper' / 'Normal' / 'Shout')
Client-owned on purpose. Voice range is the one gauge the player changes locally and instantly; as a server stat it would snap back after every keypress. A voice resource reads it here and listens for whip_core:voice:rangeChanged to tell its own server, as whip_voice does.
local range = exports.whip_core:GetVoiceLevel()   -- 20, 50 or 100
local label = exports.whip_core:GetVoiceName()    -- 'Whisper', 'Normal', 'Shout'
SetVoiceTalking(talking, mode?)CLIENT

For a voice resource: lights the HUD's voice gauge while the player transmits: blue for normal talk, or orange with a walkie-talkie in place of the mic when mode is 'radio'. Call it as push-to-talk goes down and up; switching between the two while still held is fine. The light belongs to the resource that set it and goes out if that resource stops.

Returns: nothing
exports.whip_core:SetVoiceTalking(true)            -- blue: talking
exports.whip_core:SetVoiceTalking(true, 'radio')   -- orange, radio icon: talking on the radio
exports.whip_core:SetVoiceTalking(false)           -- off
PlayEmote(cmd)CLIENT

Play an emote on the player by its /e name, as if they typed it: its animation and its props, under whip's own cancel (X), the F3 menu and the logout cleanup. Use it for anything held in the hand (a phone, a clipboard, a tablet) instead of your own TaskPlayAnim and props, which would fight the emote system. The list of emotes is shared/emote_list.lua. It answers at once; the emote starts a moment later, once its animation has loaded.

ParamTypeDescription
cmdstringThe emote's /e name, e.g. 'drink' or 'phone'
local ok, why = exports.whip_core:PlayEmote('phone')
if not ok then print(why) end   -- no such emote, dead, in a vehicle, a bar running, a weapon out...
Returns: boolean ok, string? why: false, why when it cannot play now
CancelEmote()CLIENT

Stop the emote the player is doing and put away its props. Stop only the one you started: ask IsEmoting first, so you do not end an emote the player chose themselves.

if exports.whip_core:IsEmoting() == 'phone' then exports.whip_core:CancelEmote() end
Returns: boolean: whether there was an emote to stop
IsEmoting()CLIENT

The emote the player is doing now. It answers the emote's /e name, not true, so you can tell your own emote from one the player chose.

Returns: string|false: the /e name, or false when the player is not emoting
SetWalkOverride(clipset)CLIENT

Take over the player's walk for a while (a drunk stagger, an injury limp), or give it back with nil. While several resources hold one, the newest wins; when the last is cleared, the walk the player chose with /walk comes back, not the game's default. Kept per resource, and cleared when that resource stops.

ParamTypeDescription
clipsetstring|nilA GTA movement clipset, e.g. 'MOVE_M@DRUNK@VERYDRUNK'; nil gives the walk back
exports.whip_core:SetWalkOverride('MOVE_M@DRUNK@VERYDRUNK')   -- stagger
exports.whip_core:SetWalkOverride(nil)                        -- sober: the player's own walk again
Returns: boolean: true

Player flags

A flag is a named fact about one character that outlives a job and a restart: "met the fence", "jobs done: 3", "betrayed Lester". Director scenarios set and read them (Set Player Flag, If Player Flag, a Dialog Line answer's Only if), and so can any resource. Kept in the character's metadata, so a flag is saved with the character the way whip saves everything, and reading one costs nothing. Only an online character's flags can be read or set. The player's own game can see their flags (their metadata); nobody else's can.

SetPlayerFlag(who, name, value) · GetPlayerFlag(who, name) · GetPlayerFlags(who)SERVER

Set, read or list a character's flags. The character must be online.

exports.whip_core:SetPlayerFlag(source, 'met_fence', true)
local jobs = exports.whip_core:GetPlayerFlag(source, 'jobs_done') or 0
exports.whip_core:SetPlayerFlag(source, 'jobs_done', jobs + 1)
exports.whip_core:SetPlayerFlag(source, 'met_fence', nil)     -- cleared (false clears too)
ParamTypeDescription
whonumber | { charId }A server id, or a character (who must be online)
namestringLetters, digits and _ . - : (at most 64), starting with a letter. Names starting with _ are whip's own
valuetrue | number | string | nilText at most 100 characters; nil or false clears it. At most 256 flags a character
Returns: Set: true, or false, reason. Get: the value, or nil. GetPlayerFlags: { [name] = value }, or nil when they are not on. whip_core:flag:changed { source, charId, name, value, was } fires on each change.

Stats & Effects

Where stats live

Every stat's value lives on the server, and each player's game follows it. The one exception is combat damage: a hit is seen first by the hurt player's own game, which reports it to the server, so a shot lands without waiting for the server.

Built-in Stats

StatTypeRangeDecayThreshold
healthvital0–200——
armourvital0–100——
hungerneed0–100empty in Config.HungerMinutes (120)≤10 → health -1
thirstneed0–100empty in Config.ThirstMinutes (90)≤10 → health -1
oxygencustom0–100drains under water, refills above0 → drowns

Out of the box hunger and thirst are on: each drains, is saved and has a gauge, and at 10 or below costs 1 health per decay tick. Turn one off with Config.Hunger / Config.Thirst (or /whip → Settings → Config → Hunger, thirst and breath, at once). Then it has no gauge, no drain and is not saved, and it reads 100 to anything that asks, so food and drink are still eaten. 100 = full, 0 = starving. The gauges' order is Config.StatOrder.

Stat Types

  • vital: health and armour. Synced to the GTA ped. Combat damage is reported by the client; framework changes (healing, effects) are pushed by the server.
  • need: hunger, thirst. Server-driven decay with configurable thresholds that can damage other stats.
  • custom: developer-defined stats (stress, tiredness, etc). Registered via export, can have decay and thresholds.

Registering Custom Stats

The hud field is optional. Include it to show a ring on the HUD. Omit it for server-only stats with no visual: useful for backend logic like reputation, kill counts, or internal tracking.

-- WITH HUD ring — players see a stress gauge on screen
exports.whip_core:RegisterStat('stress', {
    type    = 'custom',
    default = 0,
    min     = 0,
    max     = 100,
    persist = true,
    decay   = -0.5,
    decayInterval = 15,
    hud = {
        icon  = 'M12 2C6.48 2 2 6.48 2 12s4.48 10 10 10...',
        color = '#e879f9',
        order = 5,
    },
})

-- WITHOUT HUD ring — server-only stat, no visual
-- Still works with GetStat, SetStat, AddStat, OnStatChange, decay, thresholds
exports.whip_core:RegisterStat('reputation', {
    type    = 'custom',
    default = 0,
    min     = 0,
    max     = 1000,
    persist = true,
    -- no hud field = invisible stat, backend only
})

Example: Reputation System (No HUD)

A server-only stat with no visual: persists across sessions, supports thresholds, and can be read from client for gating.

-- server.lua
local DROP_OFFS = {                      -- where each route ends
    [1] = vector3(-47.2, -1757.5, 29.4),
    [2] = vector3(374.1, 327.8, 103.6),
}
local onRoute = {}                       -- [source] = the route the SERVER gave them

-- Stats and events live in whip_core's memory, so both go in Whip.register
Whip.register(function()
    exports.whip_core:RegisterStat('reputation', {
        type    = 'custom',
        default = 0,
        min     = 0,
        max     = 1000,
        persist = true,
        -- no hud, no decay — purely event-driven
    })

    -- Starting a route: the server remembers which one, so it can check the finish later
    exports.whip_core:SecureEvent('delivery:start', {
        rateLimit = 5000,
        params = { {'routeId', 'id', 1, #DROP_OFFS} },   -- 'id': names a thing, refused if out of range
    }, function(source, player, routeId)
        onRoute[source] = routeId
    end)

    -- Finishing: only for a route the server started, and only AT its drop-off.
    -- Never trust "I finished" from the client on its own — anyone can fire an event.
    exports.whip_core:SecureEvent('delivery:complete', {
        rateLimit = 5000,
        near = {
            at = function(source) return DROP_OFFS[onRoute[source] or 0] end,
            range = 10.0,
            allowUnknown = true,          -- no route: the handler says so, not "Too far away"
        },
    }, function(source, player)
        if not onRoute[source] then return false, 'You are not on a delivery' end
        onRoute[source] = nil             -- one reward per route
        exports.whip_core:AddStat(source, 'reputation', 10, 'delivery')
    end)
end)

AddEventHandler('playerDropped', function() onRoute[source] = nil end)

-- client.lua — react to a milestone. A listener is a registration too: Whip.register.
Whip.register(function()
    exports.whip_core:OnStatChange('reputation', function(value, old)
        if not old then return end   -- the first value after login is not a milestone
        if value >= 500 and old < 500 then
            exports.whip_core:Notify('Reputation: Respected! Premium access granted.', 'success')
        elseif value >= 100 and old < 100 then
            exports.whip_core:Notify('Reputation: Trusted! New routes unlocked.', 'success')
        end
    end)
end)

You write no database table, save/load logic or HUD code: the stat persists in the character's save data, syncs to the client automatically, and survives disconnects and restarts.

Reading & Writing Stats

-- Server: read/write stats
local hunger = exports.whip_core:GetStat(source, 'hunger')
exports.whip_core:SetStat(source, 'hunger', 100)  -- full
exports.whip_core:AddStat(source, 'hunger', 25)   -- restore 25
local all = exports.whip_core:GetAllStats(source)

-- Client: read-only access
local hunger = exports.whip_core:GetStat('hunger')
local all = exports.whip_core:GetAllStats()

The setters answer true, or false and a reason: 'no stat named "x" (RegisterStat it first)', 'value must be a number', 'Player not loaded'. A name nobody registered is refused rather than quietly kept for one session and never saved. Both take an optional last reason ('quest reward'), shown in the Player Stats Debug change log (/w, the debug panel) and handed to OnStatChange.

Making Consumable Items

-- A sandwich restores 25 hunger. (whip_core's own 'food' item is the same thing, in server/items/food.lua.)
Whip.register(function()
    exports.whip_core:RegisterItem('mycafe_sandwich', {
        name = 'Sandwich', weight = 0.3, type = 'consumable',
        stack = true, maxStack = 10, usable = true, cooldown = 3,
    })
    exports.whip_core:RegisterUseHandler('mycafe_sandwich', function(source, player, slotData)
        local ok, why = exports.whip_core:AddStat(source, 'hunger', 25, 'item:sandwich')
        if not ok then return false, why end   -- refused: they keep it
        return true  -- consume one
    end)
end)

All stat mutations are server-side. No client events are needed: the Stats system automatically syncs to the client.

Listening to Stat Changes

The same export on both sides. The server's hears every player and gets the player's source first, and the reason last. Every change is heard: decay ticks, items, effects, combat damage, other resources' SetStat.

-- server.lua
exports.whip_core:OnStatChange('hunger', function(source, value, old, reason)
    if value <= 0 then --[[ starving ]] end
end)

-- client.lua — React to a specific stat changing
exports.whip_core:OnStatChange('hunger', function(newValue, oldValue)
    -- Update your custom HUD, trigger effects, etc.
end)

-- Wildcard: listen to ALL stat changes (the stat's name comes first)
exports.whip_core:OnStatChange('*', function(statName, newValue, oldValue)
    -- fires for every stat change
end)

-- Options (either side): one table instead, and a first call with what is there now
exports.whip_core:OnStatChange('hunger', function(change)
    -- change.key, change.value, change.old (+ change.source, change.reason on the server)
end, { table = true, now = true })

Register from Whip.register: listeners are keyed by your resource (and an optional id, before the options), so running it again replaces instead of doubling. They are removed when your resource stops.

Spawn Guard

After respawn or revive, players have 10 seconds of immunity from threshold damage and effects. This prevents instant death from low hunger/thirst when reviving. Decay still runs (hunger/thirst continue to tick) but threshold damage (hunger ≤10 → health damage) is paused.

Effect System

Effects are temporary stat modifiers with timed duration, tick callbacks, and automatic cleanup. They're the building block for buffs, debuffs, poisons, healing-over-time, and damage modifiers.

-- Heal 5 HP every second for 10 seconds (bandage)
exports.whip_core:ApplyEffect(source, 'healing', {
    duration  = 10,         -- seconds (nil = permanent until removed)
    magnitude = 5,          -- arbitrary value your onTick can read
    tickRate  = 1,          -- onTick fires every 1 second
    onTick = function(src, player, effect)
        exports.whip_core:AddStat(src, 'health', effect.magnitude)
    end,
    onApply = function(src)
        exports.whip_core:NotifyPlayer(src, 'Healing...', 'success')
    end,
    onRemove = function(src)
        exports.whip_core:NotifyPlayer(src, 'Healed!', 'success')
    end,
})

Effect Fields

FieldTypeDefaultDescription
durationnumber|nilnilSeconds until auto-remove. nil = permanent until RemoveEffect.
magnitudenumber1Arbitrary value for your callbacks to use (damage amount, heal rate, etc).
tickRatenumber1Seconds between onTick calls.
onTickfunctionnilfunction(source, player, effect): called every tickRate seconds.
onApplyfunctionnilfunction(source, player, effect): called when effect is first applied.
onRemovefunctionnilfunction(source, player, effect): called when effect expires or is removed, and when the player logs out or disconnects with it still on (effect.reason is then 'logout' or 'disconnect'). It is not called when your own resource stops: the callback lives in it.
damageModifiernumber|nilnilWeapon damage multiplier. 0.5 = take half damage. See Damage Modifiers below.
meleeModifiernumber|nilnilMelee damage multiplier. Same scale as damageModifier.
replaceSilentlybooleanfalseNothing stacks: applying an effect under a name that is already active replaces it. By default the old one's onRemove runs first; true skips it. stackable is refused.

The effect belongs to the resource that applied it, and is removed (without its onRemove) when that resource stops.

Effect Examples

-- Poison: drain 5 HP every 2 seconds for 20 seconds
exports.whip_core:ApplyEffect(source, 'poison', {
    duration  = 20,
    magnitude = 5,
    tickRate  = 2,
    onTick = function(src, p, effect)
        exports.whip_core:AddStat(src, 'health', -effect.magnitude)
    end,
})

-- Remove an effect early (antidote)
exports.whip_core:RemoveEffect(source, 'poison')

-- Check if a player has an effect
if exports.whip_core:HasEffect(source, 'poison') then --[[ ... ]] end

-- Get all active effects, as plain data
local effects = exports.whip_core:GetEffects(source)
-- { poison = { remaining = 14, duration = 20, magnitude = 5, tickRate = 2, resource = 'my_res' } }

Damage Modifiers

Damage modifiers let you make players take more or less weapon/melee damage via effects. Add damageModifier and/or meleeModifier to any ApplyEffect call: no extra exports, no client code.

-- 50% weapon damage reduction for 30 seconds
exports.whip_core:ApplyEffect(source, 'armour_buff', {
    duration       = 30,
    damageModifier = 0.5,  -- 0.5 = take 50% damage
})

-- Take double damage for 20 seconds (cursed debuff)
exports.whip_core:ApplyEffect(source, 'cursed', {
    duration       = 20,
    damageModifier = 2.0,  -- 2.0 = take 200% damage
})

-- Melee immunity for 15 seconds
exports.whip_core:ApplyEffect(source, 'iron_skin', {
    duration      = 15,
    meleeModifier = 0.1,  -- take 10% melee damage
})

-- Combine with other effect features
exports.whip_core:ApplyEffect(source, 'combat_stim', {
    duration       = 60,
    damageModifier = 0.5,
    magnitude      = 2,
    tickRate       = 5,
    onTick = function(src, p, effect)
        exports.whip_core:AddStat(src, 'health', effect.magnitude) -- slow heal too
    end,
})

Who the modifier applies to

Each attacker's game scales its own damage when it aims at or punches that player, so a hit lands right the first time. Shots fired from the hip without aiming do full damage.

Modifier Stacking

Multiple effects with damageModifier stack multiplicatively, and the result is kept between 0.05 and 4.0 (Config.Sentinel.damageModifierClamp). GetDamageModifier answers the kept value:

Effect AEffect BCombinedDamage Taken
0.5—0.550%
0.50.50.2525%
0.52.01.0100% (cancel out)
2.02.04.0400%
0.050.50.05 (kept at the floor)5%

Reading Modifiers (Server)

-- Get the combined weapon modifier for a player
local mod = exports.whip_core:GetDamageModifier(source)  -- 1.0 = normal

-- Get the combined melee modifier
local melee = exports.whip_core:GetMeleeModifier(source)

Complete Item Example

-- server.lua — the whole item: definition, use and effect, in Whip.register.
-- (whip_core's own damage_reducer, server/items/damage_reducer.lua, is the same shape.)
Whip.register(function()
    exports.whip_core:RegisterItem('mydoc_iron_tonic', {
        name     = 'Iron Tonic',
        desc     = 'Halves incoming weapon damage for 20 seconds.',
        weight   = 0.2,
        type     = 'consumable',
        stack    = true,
        maxStack = 5,
        usable   = true,
        cooldown = 25,
        prop     = 'prop_cs_pills',
    })

    exports.whip_core:RegisterUseHandler('mydoc_iron_tonic', function(source, player, slotData)
        local ok, why = exports.whip_core:ApplyEffect(source, 'mydoc_iron_tonic', {
            duration       = 20,
            damageModifier = 0.5,
            onApply  = function(src) exports.whip_core:NotifyPlayer(src, '50% damage reduction for 20 seconds', 'success') end,
            onRemove = function(src) exports.whip_core:NotifyPlayer(src, 'Damage reduction wore off', 'warning') end,
        })
        if not ok then return false, why end
        return true
    end)
end)

That's everything: the item, the use handler and the effect, all on the server. whip sends it to every player's game and removes it when it runs out.

Combat Damage Tracking

The debug panel's Player Stats Debug (/w) shows what caused each hit:

ScenarioDebug Label
Shot by a playercombat (reported): Carbine Rifle by John Smith (#3)
Shot by NPCcombat (reported): Pistol (NPC)
Run over by playercombat (reported): vehicle hit by Jane Doe (#5)
Explosioncombat (reported): Explosion
Drowningcombat (reported): Drowning
Killing blowkilled (reported): Advanced Rifle by John Smith (#3)

"Reported" because the text comes from the hurt player's own game. It is a good description for an honest player, and anything a modified game wants it to say for a cheat, so do not decide anything from it. For who the server saw kill a player, use killer on the server's whip_core:player:died event.

Server Exports

ExportReturnsDescription
GetStat(source, name)number|nilRead a stat value
SetStat(source, name, value, reason?)ok, errSet a stat (clamped to min/max)
AddStat(source, name, delta, reason?)ok, errAdd/subtract from a stat
GetAllStats(source)tableGet all stats as {name = value}
OnStatChange(name, fn, id?, opts?)ok, errBe told when a player's stat changes ('*' for all)
RegisterStat(name, config)ok, errRegister a new stat type
ApplyEffect(source, name, config)ok, errApply a timed effect
RemoveEffect(source, name)ok, errRemove an active effect
HasEffect(source, name)booleanCheck if effect is active
GetEffects(source)tableGet all active effects, as plain data
GetDamageModifier(source)numberCombined weapon modifier (1.0 = normal)
GetMeleeModifier(source)numberCombined melee modifier (1.0 = normal)

Client Exports

ExportReturnsDescription
GetStat(name)number|nilRead a stat from the local cache
GetAllStats()tableGet all stats as {name = value}
HasEffect(name)booleanCheck if effect is active locally
GetEffects()tableGet all active effects
OnStatChange(name, fn, id?, opts?)ok, errRegister a callback for stat changes ('*' for all)
Debug overlay: turn on Player Stats Debug in /w (the debug panel) to see real-time stat values, active effects, decay rates, change log with damage sources, and ped health/armour comparison.
RegisterStat(name, config)SERVER

Register a stat type from your own resource. The config is validated and copied (whip never keeps a reference to your table), and if it carries a hud block, the gauge appears on every connected player's HUD the moment the call returns. Decay, thresholds, persistence and client sync all come with the registration; there is nothing else to wire.

FieldTypeDescription
typestring'need' or 'custom' (default 'custom'). Vitals are whip's own. Anything else is refused
defaultnumberWhat a character starts on (default 0)
min / maxnumberThe range writes are clamped to (default 0–100)
persistbooleanSave with the character (default true)
decaynumber|nilPoints added every decayInterval seconds; negative drains. Omit for none: 0 is treated as no decay
decayIntervalnumberSeconds between decay ticks (default 10)
thresholdstable|nilArray of { stat, delta, value, below }: while this stat is past value (below = true for ≤, otherwise ≥), add delta to stat on each decay tick. Only fires on stats that decay
hudtable|nil{ color, icon, iconCritical, order, heartbeat, hideWhenEmpty, noCritical, showAboveZero, showBelowFull, glide }: draws a HUD ring. Omit for a server-only stat
Returns: boolean ok, string|nil err: check it; a refusal is a reason, not an error
Names are owned (the registration rule). health, armour and oxygen belong to whip_core and cannot be taken, and a stat another resource registered cannot be re-registered by yours: both refuse with the reason in err. Registering your own stat again is always fine: the same definition changes nothing (and redraws no HUD), a changed one replaces it.
persist = false means neither saved nor loaded. A non-persisting stat starts from default on every login. A value that is not written must not be read back either: otherwise "not persisted" quietly means "frozen at the last value that was".
The registration is dropped when your resource stops: the gauge comes off every HUD and the decay stops ticking. In-memory values are left alone, so a satellite restart that re-registers on start loses nothing. Stats live in whip_core's memory too: register them in Whip.register, which runs again when whip_core comes back.
Whip.register(function()
    local ok, err = exports.whip_core:RegisterStat('stress', {
        type    = 'custom',
        default = 0, min = 0, max = 100,
        persist = true,
        decay   = -0.5,        -- eases off half a point...
        decayInterval = 15,    -- ...every 15 seconds
        hud = { icon = 'M12 2C6.48 2 2 6.48 2 12...', color = '#e879f9', order = 5 },
    })
    if not ok then print(('stress refused: %s'):format(err)) end
end)
GetStat(source, name) / GetAllStats(source)SERVER

Read one stat from the server cache, or every stat as a copy. The cache is the single source of truth: combat damage the client reports lands here too, so health is current without touching the ped.

ParamTypeDescription
sourcenumberPlayer server ID
namestringStat name (GetStat only)
Returns: number|nil / table: for a player with no character loaded, GetStat answers nil (one value) and GetAllStats answers {}, 'Player not loaded' (a list)
local hunger = exports.whip_core:GetStat(source, 'hunger')
local all = exports.whip_core:GetAllStats(source)  -- { health = 200, hunger = 74, ... }
SetStat(source, name, value, reason)SERVER

Set a stat to an exact value. Clamped to the stat's registered min/max, cached, synced to the client immediately, and queued for the character's next save when the stat persists.

ParamTypeDescription
sourcenumberPlayer server ID
namestringStat name: a registered one
valuenumberWhat to set it to
reasonstring|nilOptional: what caused it ('quest reward'). Shown in the Player Stats Debug change log and handed to OnStatChange; defaults to 'by <your resource>'
Returns: boolean ok, string|nil err: 'Player not loaded', 'no stat named "x" (RegisterStat it first)', 'value must be a number'
The stat must be registered. An unknown name is refused: a typo like 'hungr' answers false instead of looking like it worked.
exports.whip_core:SetStat(source, 'thirst', 100, 'fountain')  -- fully hydrated
AddStat(source, name, delta, reason)SERVER

Add to a stat: the convenience wrapper around SetStat. Reads the current value (or the registered default when unset), adds delta, and sets the result, clamped to the stat's range. Negative deltas subtract.

ParamTypeDescription
sourcenumberPlayer server ID
namestringStat name: a registered one
deltanumberAmount to add; negative subtracts
reasonstring|nilOptional, as for SetStat ('item:food')
Returns: boolean ok, string|nil err: as SetStat, or 'amount must be a number'
exports.whip_core:AddStat(source, 'hunger', 25, 'item:food')   -- ate something
exports.whip_core:AddStat(source, 'health', -10)  -- took a hit
OnStatChange(name, callback, id, opts)SERVER

Be told when a player's stat changes, on the server: the same export as the client's, with the player's source first and the reason last. Every path is heard: decay ticks, items, effects, combat damage, and other resources' SetStat/AddStat. Keyed by name, so a stat nobody listens to costs nothing.

ParamTypeDescription
namestringA stat name, or '*' for every stat
callbackfunction(source, value, old, reason), or (source, name, value, old, reason) for '*'. reason is what caused it: 'decay', 'item:food', 'combat (reported): Pistol', 'by my_resource'
idany|nilOnly to hold two listeners on one stat (the options may go here instead)
optstable|niltable = true: one table { source, key, value, old, reason } instead · now = true: also called once straight away for every loaded player who has the stat (old = nil, reason = 'now')
Returns: boolean ok, string|nil err
Register from Whip.register: the listener is keyed by your resource and the id, so running it again replaces rather than doubles, and it is removed when your resource stops. A listener that sets the stat it is listening to is not called again for that change (the value still lands), so clamping a value from inside its own listener cannot loop.
Whip.register(function()
    exports.whip_core:OnStatChange('hunger', function(source, value, old, reason)
        if value <= 0 and (old or 1) > 0 then
            exports.whip_core:NotifyPlayer(source, 'You are starving', 'error')
        end
    end)
end)
ApplyEffect(source, name, config)SERVER

Apply a timed effect to a player: the building block for buffs, debuffs, poisons and healing-over-time. The framework runs your callbacks on its own tick thread, counts down the duration, removes the effect when it expires, and syncs the whole thing to the client.

FieldTypeDescription
durationnumber|nilSeconds until auto-remove. nil = until RemoveEffect
magnitudenumberArbitrary value your callbacks read (default 1)
tickRatenumberSeconds between onTick calls (default 1)
onTick / onApply / onRemovefunction|nil(source, player, effect)
damageModifier / meleeModifiernumber|nilIncoming damage multiplier: 0.5 = take half. See Damage Modifiers above
replaceSilentlybooleanWhen an effect of this name is already active, skip its onRemove as this one replaces it (default: it runs first)
sheet'light'?Your callbacks get the light player sheet (who, and whether dead) instead of the full one, which reads the ped, the pockets and two stats on every tick
Returns: boolean ok, string|nil err: why the config was refused ('duration must be a positive number of seconds, or nil', 'Player not loaded'...)
Nothing stacks. A second apply under the same name always replaces the effect: magnitude, remaining duration, everything. replaceSilently decides one thing: whether the replaced instance's onRemove fires first (default) or is skipped. If you want stacking magnitude, read the old effect with GetEffects and apply the sum yourself. stackable is refused.
The effect is yours. It is recorded against the resource that applied it: shown in Player Stats Debug and GetEffects, and removed (without its onRemove) when your resource stops. There is no way to apply one in another resource's name: a resource field in the config is ignored.
ApplyEffect moves no stat by itself. Apart from the damage modifiers, which the framework applies for you, an effect only does what its callbacks do: the drain or the heal is your onTick calling AddStat. To change a number once, call SetStat/AddStat directly; reach for an effect when the change has a lifetime that must expire and clean up on its own.
Effect ticks pause while the player is dead and for the 10-second spawn guard after a respawn or revive, so a poison cannot finish someone off the moment they are revived.
-- Poison: drain 5 HP every 2 seconds for 20 seconds
exports.whip_core:ApplyEffect(source, 'poison', {
    duration  = 20,
    magnitude = 5,
    tickRate  = 2,
    onTick = function(src, p, effect)
        exports.whip_core:AddStat(src, 'health', -effect.magnitude)
    end,
})
RemoveEffect(source, name)SERVER

Remove an active effect before it expires. Fires the effect's onRemove, recalculates the damage-modifier statebag if it carried one, and tells the client. Any resource may remove any effect: an antidote from one resource curing a poison from another is the point.

ParamTypeDescription
sourcenumberPlayer server ID
namestringThe name the effect was applied under
Returns: boolean ok, string|nil err: 'no effect named "x" on this player' when there was nothing to remove
exports.whip_core:RemoveEffect(source, 'poison')  -- antidote
HasEffect(source, name) / GetEffects(source)SERVER

Is an effect active on a player, and what is active. GetEffects returns plain data keyed by effect name: duration, remaining, magnitude, tickRate, damageModifier, meleeModifier and the resource that applied it. The callbacks are never included.

ParamTypeDescription
sourcenumberPlayer server ID
namestringEffect name (HasEffect only)
Returns: boolean / table: { [name] = effect }, empty when none
if exports.whip_core:HasEffect(source, 'poison') then
    -- refuse the sprint, tint the screen, etc.
end
GetDamageModifier(source) / GetMeleeModifier(source)SERVER

The combined incoming weapon (or melee) damage multiplier from every active effect, multiplied together. 1.0 means no active modifier. Use it when your own server-side damage math should respect the same buffs the framework applies to combat.

ParamTypeDescription
sourcenumberPlayer server ID
Returns: number: 1.0 when no effect carries a modifier
-- A custom trap respecting armour buffs
local mod = exports.whip_core:GetDamageModifier(source)
exports.whip_core:AddStat(source, 'health', -25 * mod)

HUD Framework

Overview

The status HUD is data-driven: every ring on screen is generated from the stat's hud config. To add a ring, give the stat a hud field when you register it; no HTML, CSS or JS changes are needed.

How It Works

Register a stat with a hud block and every player's HUD gains its ring at once, players already in included. The ring follows the stat's value as it changes, and comes off when your resource stops.

HUD Config Fields

FieldTypeRequiredDescription
iconstringYesSVG path d attribute (24x24 viewBox). The icon shown inside the ring.
colorstringYesHex color for the arc and glow (e.g. '#34d399'). Auto-generates glow/haze variants.
ordernumberNoPosition in the bar, after every stat the server has placed (Config.StatOrder, dragged on the Hunger, thirst and breath settings page, which wins once your stat is placed there). Lower = further left. Default: 99.
heartbeatbooleanNoEnable heartbeat icon animation when critical (<20%). Used by health.
iconCriticalstringNoAlternate SVG paths (pipe-delimited) shown when critical. First path = fill, rest = stroke lines. Used by armour for crack effect.
hideWhenEmptybooleanNoFade to 25% opacity at 0% instead of showing empty ring. Used by armour.
noCriticalbooleanNoDisable the red critical warning below 20%. For stats where low isn't urgent (drunk, stress).
showAboveZerobooleanNoCompletely hidden at 0%. Slides in when stat goes above 0, slides out when it returns to 0. For situational stats (drunk).
showBelowFullbooleanNoThe other way round: completely hidden while the stat is full. Slides in as it drops below full, slides out once it is full again. For a reserve that is usually full: whip's own oxygen, under water.
glidebooleanNoMoves between readings at a steady speed instead of step by step: the gauge goes to each new value over the time the values have been arriving apart, so a stat your server moves once a tick drains as one continuous motion. For a stat that moves steadily: whip's own oxygen. Leave it off for one that should snap to a hit (health).
showWhenPresentbooleanNoVehicle stats only. Drawn when the vehicle actually carries the stat, whatever its value. For fittings whose resting value is not zero: a turbo idling at 1. See below.
showAboveZero and showWhenPresent answer different questions, and only agree when the stat's default is zero. A car without the stat reads as its default, so showAboveZero on a stat that rests at 1 draws a gauge on every car on the server, including the ones with nothing fitted. Use showAboveZero for a quantity that runs out, and showWhenPresent for a part that is either bolted on or is not.

Built-in HUD Behavior

StatColorBehavior
HealthGreen #34d399Heartbeat animation below 20%. Red arc + icon when critical.
ArmourPurple #818cf8Cracked shield icon below 20%. Fades out at 0% (hideWhenEmpty).
HungerOrange #fb923cRed arc + icon below 20%.
ThirstBlue #38bdf8Red arc + icon below 20%.

All stats: below 20% the arc turns red and the icon turns red (unless noCritical is set). At 0% the ring ghosts out (faded track, dim icon).

Adding a HUD Ring from an External Resource

-- server.lua — a "stress" stat with a HUD ring: one call, in Whip.register
Whip.register(function()
    exports.whip_core:RegisterStat('stress', {
        type    = 'custom',
        default = 0,
        min     = 0,
        max     = 100,
        persist = true,
        decay   = -0.5,
        decayInterval = 15,
        hud = {
            icon  = 'M12 2C6.48 2 2 6.48 2 12s4.48 10 10 10 10-4.48 10-10S17.52 2 12 2zm0 18c-4.42 0-8-3.58-8-8s3.58-8 8-8 8 3.58 8 8-3.58 8-8 8zm-1-13h2v6h-2zm0 8h2v2h-2z',
            color = '#e879f9',
            order = 5,
        },
    })
end)

The ring then appears on every player's HUD automatically, with no HTML, CSS or JS to write. When the stat changes (via SetStat/AddStat), the ring updates. When it hits 0, it ghosts out. When it goes below 20%, it turns red (unless noCritical).

Situational Stats (show/hide)

A ring that only matters some of the time (drunk) sets showAboveZero = true (and usually noCritical = true): hidden at 0, slides in above it. The drunk effect below is the worked example. A reserve that is usually full sets showBelowFull = true instead: hidden while full, as whip's own oxygen is on dry land.

Complete Example: a drunk effect

A whole drunk effect in one small resource, using a stat, a HUD ring and an item. Both of its files are below in full; put them in a folder with an fxmanifest.lua that loads @whip_core/lib/satellite.lua as a shared script and they run as they are.

What it does: Beer item → 5-second drinking animation with beer prop in hand (the player can walk) → drunk stat +20 → walk animations change by tier → ragdolling at 80%+ → decays 1 per 2 seconds → HUD ring appears when drunk > 0, disappears when sober → ring stays its normal color at low levels (no red warning).

-- server.lua — the complete server file

-- Declared whenever whip_core becomes ready, and again if it restarts (Whip.register comes from
-- shared_script '@whip_core/lib/satellite.lua' in fxmanifest.lua).
Whip.register(function()
    -- 1. Register the stat with HUD ring
    exports.whip_core:RegisterStat('drunk', {
        type          = 'custom',
        default       = 0,
        min           = 0,
        max           = 100,
        persist       = false,          -- resets on restart
        decay         = -1,             -- sobers up: -1 per interval
        decayInterval = 2,              -- every 2 seconds
        hud = {
            icon          = 'M10 1h4v1.5h-1v3h.5c1.5 0 2.5 1.5 2.5 3V21a1 1 0 0 1-1 1H9a1 1 0 0 1-1-1V8.5c0-1.5 1-3 2.5-3h.5v-3H10V1z',
            color         = '#b8860b',  -- beer brown
            order         = 5,
            noCritical    = true,       -- low drunk isn't urgent — no red warning
            showAboveZero = true,       -- hidden when sober (0), slides in when > 0
        },
    })

    -- 2. Register the item
    exports.whip_core:RegisterItem('alcohol', {
        name     = 'Beer',
        desc     = 'A cold beer. Drink responsibly... or don\'t.',
        weight   = 0.5,
        type     = 'consumable',
        stack    = true,
        maxStack = 12,
        usable   = true,
        cooldown = 6,
        prop     = 'prop_amb_beer_bottle',
    })

    -- 3. Drinking it: a TABLE, not a function — a declared timed use (see RegisterUseHandler).
    -- whip runs the bar with the animation and the bottle, times it on the server, checks the
    -- beer is still there, takes it, and only then calls onComplete.
    exports.whip_core:RegisterUseHandler('alcohol', {
        label    = 'Drinking...',
        duration = 5000,
        anim     = { dict = 'mp_player_intdrink', clip = 'loop_bottle', flag = 49 },   -- upper body
        prop     = { model = 'prop_amb_beer_bottle', bone = 18905 },                  -- left hand
        disable  = { move = false },   -- they can walk while they drink
        reason   = 'drunk',            -- what the item log says it was used for

        canUse = function(source)
            if GetVehiclePedIsIn(GetPlayerPed(source), false) ~= 0 then
                return false, 'Not while you are in a vehicle'   -- shown to the player
            end
            return true
        end,

        onComplete = function(source)
            -- AddStat's answer is onComplete's: false, 'why' gives the beer back
            return exports.whip_core:AddStat(source, 'drunk', 20, 'item:alcohol')
        end,
    })
end)
-- client.lua — walk anims and ragdoll. (No drinking code: the bar is whip_core's.)

local CLIPSETS = {
    { min = 20, max = 40,  clipset = 'MOVE_M@DRUNK@SLIGHTLYDRUNK' },   -- tipsy
    { min = 40, max = 60,  clipset = 'MOVE_M@DRUNK@MODERATEDRUNK' },   -- drunk
    { min = 60, max = 101, clipset = 'MOVE_M@DRUNK@VERYDRUNK' },      -- very drunk
}
local RAGDOLL_AT = 80

local level, walk, stumbling = 0, nil, false

-- Random falls every 3-8 s at RAGDOLL_AT or more; the thread ends once they sober up below it
local function startStumbling()
    if stumbling then return end
    stumbling = true
    CreateThread(function()
        while level >= RAGDOLL_AT do
            Wait(math.random(3000, 8000))
            local ped = PlayerPedId()
            if level >= RAGDOLL_AT and not IsEntityDead(ped) and not IsPedRagdoll(ped)
                and not IsPedInAnyVehicle(ped, false) then
                SetPedToRagdoll(ped, 2000, 2000, 0, false, false, false)
            end
        end
        stumbling = false
    end)
end

local function onDrunkChanged(value)
    level = math.floor(value or 0)
    local clipset = nil
    for _, tier in ipairs(CLIPSETS) do
        if level >= tier.min and level < tier.max then clipset = tier.clipset break end
    end
    if clipset ~= walk then
        exports.whip_core:SetWalkOverride(clipset)   -- on top of their own /walk; nil gives it back
        walk = clipset
    end
    if level >= RAGDOLL_AT then startStumbling() end
end

-- A listener is a registration: Whip.register, so a whip_core restart does not drop it.
-- now = true calls it straight away with the current value.
Whip.register(function()
    exports.whip_core:OnStatChange('drunk', onDrunkChanged, nil, { now = true })
end)

-- Logging out ends the night
AddEventHandler('whip_core:player:logout', function() onDrunkChanged(0) end)

Key HUD features demonstrated:

  • showAboveZero = true: ring is completely invisible when sober. First sip → ring slides in. Back to 0 → ring slides out and disappears.
  • noCritical = true: ring stays beer-brown at all levels. Low drunk doesn't trigger the red warning.
  • decay = -1, decayInterval = 2: stat decreases by 1 every 2 seconds automatically. No client code is needed for decay.
Finding SVG icons: search for Material Design Icons, Lucide Icons, or Heroicons. Copy the SVG path d="" attribute. All use 24x24 viewBox which matches the HUD ring icon size.

Death & Revive

When a player dies

whip puts them in the death state by itself, and the server fires whip_core:player:died (Events, below). What killed them is printed in the server console and in the Stats change log, marked "reported" because it is the dying player's own game that says so:

ScenarioConsole OutputStats Debug Log
Shot by player[whip_core] John [3] has died — reported: Carbine Rifle by Jane (#5) (charId: 12)killed (reported): Carbine Rifle by Jane (#5)
Shot by NPC[whip_core] John [3] has died — reported: Pistol (NPC) (charId: 12)killed (reported): Pistol (NPC)
Run over[whip_core] John [3] has died — reported: vehicle hit by Jane (#5) (charId: 12)killed (reported): vehicle hit by Jane (#5)
Explosion[whip_core] John [3] has died — reported: Explosion (charId: 12)killed (reported): Explosion
Unknown/threshold[whip_core] John [3] has died (charId: 12)death

Death State

While dead:

  • They lie where they fell, and take no more damage.
  • Every control is off except the camera (V, and looking around), chat (T), push-to-talk (N) and E to respawn.
  • The death screen shows (below).
  • Other players can still escort (drag) them.
  • Hunger and thirst stop draining, low ones cost no health, and effects stop ticking.

Dead in a vehicle. Someone who dies in a seat stays in it, slumped the way GTA leaves them, and the car can be driven with them in it. The other rules above are for a body on the ground. While the death lasts, whip follows the body: taken out of a seat (pulled out, the car gone), it falls, settles and is laid down as on the ground; put into a seat, it is dead in that one instead. That can happen any number of times in one death. A revive in a seat keeps them in it; a respawn takes them out.

Respawn System

After death, the death screen shows You are dead and "You can respawn in 10 seconds" (Config.RespawnTime, in /whip → Settings → Config → Hunger, thirst and breath). When the timer expires, it changes to "Hold E to respawn" (A on a controller), with a bar that fills while it is held. Holding it for 1.5 seconds triggers respawn. The server refuses a respawn sooner than the wait.

Holding a respawn. An EMS resource with a medic on the way keeps the player where they lie with HoldRespawn: their screen shows the hold's words instead of "Hold E to respawn", and the server refuses a respawn until every hold goes (released, a revive, a logout, or the resource that held it stopping).

A death screen of your own. Config.DeathScreen = false turns whip's off; a resource draws its own from the client event whip_core:death:screenChanged, which carries the same fields whip's page gets (state 'count', 'ready', 'held' or 'off', the seconds left, how far E is held, a hold's words). whip still counts down and reads E held to respawn.

Hiding the death screen. A key hides the screen so the player can watch the world: H on a keyboard, Y on a controller. The key's hint stays on screen while it is hidden, saying Show, and the same key brings the screen back. Respawning needs the screen showing. Every new death shows it again. A theme can change the screen's red with --ui-death-curtain.

Respawning fades the screen out and brings the player back at a random hospital, with full health (200), no armour, and damage modifiers back to normal. For the next 10 seconds (the spawn guard), low hunger and thirst cost no health, so a starving player is not killed again at once. The hospitals are Config.RespawnLocations in config.lua: a list of vector4(x, y, z, heading), one picked at random.

HoldRespawn(source, key, label?) · ReleaseRespawn(source, key?) · GetRespawnHold(source)SERVER

Keep a dead player from respawning at a hospital while your resource means to come for them: a medic on the way. Their death screen shows label (80 letters; default "Help is on the way") instead of "Hold E to respawn", and the server refuses a respawn. A hold is for this death: it goes when you release it, the player is revived, they log out, or your resource stops. key names your hold; the same key again changes its words. GetRespawnHold answers the words their screen shows, or nil.

-- An EMS call is taken: the patient waits for the medic, not the hospital
local ok, why = exports.whip_core:HoldRespawn(patient, 'call', 'A medic is on the way')

-- The call is dropped: they can respawn again (once the usual wait is over)
exports.whip_core:ReleaseRespawn(patient, 'call')
Returns: HoldRespawn: true, or false, 'no such player' | 'they are not dead'. ReleaseRespawn: true when a hold went

Revive Methods

MethodHowDetails
Admin revive/whip_revive <charId>Console, or in-game with whip.devtools. No item required.
Self revive/whip_revivemeIn-game only, with whip.devtools. No item required.
Hospital respawnHold E (A on a controller) after countdownTeleports to random hospital. No item required.

Every revive and respawn sets health to 200 and armour to 0, and starts the 10-second spawn guard. While a player is dead, their health stat reads 100 (GTA's dead value) and their armour 0.

Checking Death State

-- Client: check if local player is dead
if exports.whip_core:IsPlayerDead() then
    -- player is in death state
end

-- Server: check via player object
local player = exports.whip_core:GetPlayer(source)
if player and player.isDead then --[[ ... ]] end

-- Any client: check another player's death state via statebag
local isDead = Player(serverId).state.whipDead

Leaving while dead

A player who leaves while dead is still dead when they come back: leaving is not a way out of a death.

Events

EventSidePayload
whip_core:player:diedServer{ source, charId, killer, reported }: killer is the server id the server saw do it (a car's driver counts), or nil; reported is the victim's own game's description, for display only
whip_core:player:revivedServer{ source, charId, how, reason }: how is 'revived' or 'respawned'
whip_core:player:diedClient{ reconnected, respawnRefused }
whip_core:player:revivedClient{ how }
whip_core:death:screenChangedClientWhat the death screen shows now, for a screen of your own: { state = 'count', left, total }, { state = 'ready', progress, key }, { state = 'held', label }, { state = 'off' } or { hidden }

Any server resource can fire the server events: never pay out on one alone.

Escort System

Overview

Grab another player and move them around. Dead players can be escorted too.

Controls

ActionMethodWhen
EscortLeft Arrow keyTarget not in vehicle, not already escorted
ReleaseRight Arrow keyCurrently escorting someone

Escorted Player

The escorted player is attached beside the holder. Only movement is disabled: they can still look around, open their inventory and chat.

Escort Breaks

The escort automatically breaks if:

  • Either player ragdolls (hit by car, fall, etc.)
  • The escort holder dies
  • The two end up more than 10 m apart
  • Either player disconnects

State

-- Client: check escort state
local escorting = exports.whip_core:IsEscorting()          -- am I holding someone?
local escorted = exports.whip_core:IsBeingEscorted()     -- am I being held?
local target  = exports.whip_core:GetEscortTarget()      -- serverId of who I'm escorting

-- Other client: check via statebag
local isEscorted = Player(serverId).state.whipEscorted     -- boolean
local escortedBy = Player(serverId).state.whipEscortedBy   -- serverId of holder

The controls above run through whip's own network messages; they are not an API. To know escort state, use the client exports below or the whipEscorted / whipEscortedBy statebags.

Client Exports

Three read-only checks, for scripts that need to know whether the local player is tied up in an escort: blocking a job action while restrained, hiding a menu, refusing to let someone drive.

IsEscorting()CLIENT

Is the local player currently escorting someone else?

Returns: boolean
IsBeingEscorted()CLIENT

Is the local player currently being escorted by someone else? This is the one to check before letting the player do anything that being dragged along should prevent.

Returns: boolean
GetEscortTarget()CLIENT

Who the local player is escorting, or nil if nobody.

Returns: number|nil: the escorted player's server ID

Bank System

Account Types

Accounts have a type field: 'personal', 'savings', 'business', 'shared'. On character creation, one personal account is created with Config.StartingBalance ($1000) and isDefault = 1.

Access Roles

view (1) < deposit (2) < withdraw (3) < manager (4) < owner (5)

Roles are hierarchical: a withdraw role can also view and deposit. A granter can only give roles below their own level. Owner access cannot be revoked.

Transaction Behavior

  • Amounts must be whole numbers of 1 or more: anything else (a fraction, zero, a string, NaN) is refused with 'Amount must be a whole number of 1 or more', never rounded
  • Frozen accounts block all operations
  • Same-account transfers are rejected
  • With Config.BlockOwnCharacterTransfers on (the default), a character cannot transfer to, pay into or take from an account another character of the same player owns, nor share an account with one: "That is another character of the same player: money cannot pass between them". Every way in obeys it (BankTransfer, BankDeposit, BankWithdraw, ChargePlayer, GrantBankAccess, ATMs, the phone). System moves (BankSystem*) are not affected
  • Every transaction fires whip_core:bank:balanceChanged
  • Every bank read (GetDefaultBankAccount, GetBankAccount, GetCharacterBankAccounts…) is a database read and waits for it: their cards say WAITS. Read when the player asks (opening an app, pressing an ATM), not every frame or on a timer. To show a balance, GetBalance answers from memory after its first read, kept true by every bank write; or follow whip_core:bank:balanceChanged

Two kinds of money movement

Who decidesExports
A player'sTheir role on the account (deposit to pay in, withdraw to take out or transfer)BankDeposit, BankWithdraw, BankTransfer; pass the player: their source, or { charId = n } (a bare number is a server id, never a charId). These move bank money only: no cash is taken or given (see each card)
The system'sYour resource: no permission checkBankSystemDeposit (wages, takings), BankSystemWithdraw (fines, fees), BankSystemTransfer (payroll). Written to the activity log with your resource's name.

Ask first with CanUseBankAccount(accountId, who, role) (who is a person) when you need to decide what to offer, e.g. list only the accounts a player can actually pay from. To charge a player for something, use ChargePlayer, below; to pay one, PayPlayer.

-- A wage into a character's bank, online or not (the system pays: no permission asked)
local ok, err = exports.whip_core:PayPlayer({ charId = charId }, 500, { method = 'bank', reason = 'Weekly paycheck' })

-- A fine out of a player's default account
local account = exports.whip_core:GetDefaultBankAccount(source)
if account then
    local taken, why = exports.whip_core:BankSystemWithdraw(account.accountId, 250, 'Speeding fine')
end

Account Numbers

Format: WB-XXXXXX, six random digits.

Charging a Player

One call takes a payment (cash or bank) and hands you a receipt. If the thing being paid for then fails, give the receipt to RefundPlayer and the money goes back exactly where it came from. whip's own fuel pumps, shops, ATMs and whip_autos all pay this way.

local receipt, err = exports.whip_core:ChargePlayer(source, 500, {
    method = 'auto',          -- 'cash' | 'bank' | 'auto': cash if they carry enough, else the bank
    reason = 'Car wash',      -- on their bank statement and the activity log
})
if not receipt then
    return exports.whip_core:NotifyPlayer(source, err, 'error')   -- 'Not enough cash (have $20, need $500)'
end

if not washTheCar() then
    exports.whip_core:RefundPlayer(receipt)   -- all of it; or RefundPlayer(receipt, 200) for part
end
OptionDefaultWhat it does
method'auto''cash', 'bank', or 'auto' (cash if they have enough, otherwise the bank)
accountIdtheir default accountBank: which account. The player's own withdraw permission on it is what's checked, so a job account they can only view cannot pay.
currency'cash'Cash: the item that counts as money here. A black market trading in gold charges gold bars, and refunds gold bars, the very ones it took, with whatever they carry (a paid gun keeps its serial)
reason'Payment'What it was for
The receipt remembers how they paid. A refund goes back the same way with no permission check (it is your resource undoing its own charge); a bank refund that is refused comes back as cash, and cash for a player who has since left goes to their bank. A refund that cannot be delivered answers false and is printed as CRITICAL.
The receipt is checked against whip's own record. Only the resource that charged may refund, only up to what is left of the payment, and only within 30 minutes. Editing the receipt table changes nothing: a forged one is refused.
The money lands with what it pays for. Inside your SecureEvent the payment is taken at once (the player cannot spend it twice) but it is written in the same transaction as your next whip write: the car CreateOwnedVehicle makes, the data SetVehicleData sets, the parts SetVehicleAppearance fits, or the end of your handler if you write nothing. A crash or a whip_core restart between paying and delivering keeps neither. If that write fails, nothing was taken, and the RefundPlayer you call then simply lets it go. Called from a thread of yours, outside any SecureEvent, the payment is written at once.

An amount of 0 takes nothing and still answers a receipt, so a free item needs no special case. To pay a player instead (a wage, a sale), use PayPlayer.

Bank

GetBankAccount(accountId)SERVER

Get a bank account by its ID.

ParamTypeDescription

Returns: table|nil: { accountId, accountNumber, label, type, ownerCharId, jobId, balance, isDefault, frozen, createdAt }. type is 'personal', 'savings', 'business' or 'shared'; times are epoch seconds (the same for every bank read)

Find a bank account by its WB-XXXXXX number.

ParamTypeDescription

Get all bank accounts a character has access to.

ParamTypeDescription
charIdnumberCharacter ID
local canPay = {}
for _, acct in ipairs(exports.whip_core:GetCharacterBankAccounts(charId)) do
    if acct.role == 'withdraw' or acct.role == 'manager' or acct.role == 'owner' then
        canPay[#canPay + 1] = acct
    end

Returns: table[]: array of accounts, each includes role field
Offering accounts to pay from? Keep the ones whose role is withdraw, manager or owner: the others will be refused at the till. (Or ask per account with CanUseBankAccount.)
GetDefaultBankAccount(who)SERVER

Get a person's default bank account.

ParamTypeDescription
whonumber|tableA person: their server id, or { charId = n }
local acct = exports.whip_core:GetDefaultBankAccount(source)
if acct then print(acct.accountNumber, acct.balance) end
Returns: table|nil. A database read every call: to show a balance, use GetBalance
GetBalance(who)SERVER

A balance without the database. The first read of an account goes to the database (and waits); after that whip keeps it in memory, kept true by every deposit, withdrawal, transfer and payment, so a HUD, a phone app or an ATM prompt can ask as often as it shows it.

ParamTypeDescription
whonumber|tableA person (their server id, or { charId = n }) for their main account, or { accountId = n } for one account
local balance, why = exports.whip_core:GetBalance(source)
if balance then print(('$%d in the bank'):format(balance)) end
Returns: integer, or false, why: no such person or account, they have no bank account, or it is closed
CanUseBankAccount(accountId, who, role)SERVER

May this person do role's worth of things on this account? The same rule the bank itself applies, asked before you act, so a shop can offer only accounts that can pay, and a menu can hide what a rank cannot touch.

ParamTypeDescription
accountIdnumberBank account ID
whonumber|tableA person: their server id, or { charId = n }
rolestring'view', 'deposit', 'withdraw', 'manager' or 'owner': each includes those before it
local ok, why = exports.whip_core:CanUseBankAccount(accountId, source, 'withdraw')
if not ok then return false, why end   -- 'Needs withdraw access to this account'
Returns: bool, string|nil: false, 'Needs withdraw access to this account', 'Account not found'
BankDeposit(accountId, amount, actor, reason)SERVER

A player deposits into a bank account: their own deposit permission on it is checked. For the system paying in (a wage, a sale's takings), use BankSystemDeposit.

It moves bank money only: no cash is taken from them. For a cash deposit (a teller, an ATM), take the notes first with ChargePlayer(source, n, { method = 'cash' }), deposit only when that answers a receipt, and hand the notes back with RefundPlayer if the deposit is refused. Without the first step, a deposit makes money from nothing.

ParamTypeDescription
accountIdnumberBank account ID
amountnumberA whole number, 1 or more
actornumber|tableThe person depositing: required; must have deposit (or higher) on the account
reasonstring?Shown on the statement
Returns: bool, string|nil: fires whip_core:bank:balanceChanged
BankWithdraw(accountId, amount, actor, reason)SERVER

A player withdraws from a bank account: their own withdraw permission is checked. To charge a player for something, use ChargePlayer: it handles cash too and hands back a receipt you can refund.

It moves bank money only: no cash is given to them. For a cash withdrawal (a teller, an ATM), give the notes with AddPlayerCash once this answers true. Without that, the money simply leaves the account.

ParamTypeDescription
accountIdnumberBank account ID
amountnumberA whole number, 1 or more
actornumber|tableThe person withdrawing: required; must have withdraw (or higher) on the account
reasonstring?Shown on the statement
Returns: bool, string|nil
BankTransfer(fromId, toId, amount, actor, reason)SERVER

A player transfers between accounts: their withdraw permission on the source is checked. For the system moving money (payroll), use BankSystemTransfer.

ParamTypeDescription
fromIdnumberSource account
toIdnumberDestination account
amountnumberA whole number, 1 or more
actornumber|tableThe person transferring: required
reasonstring?Shown on the statement
-- The player sends rent from their account to the landlord's
local ok, err = exports.whip_core:BankTransfer(fromId, toId, 500, source, 'Rent')
if not ok then return false, err end   -- 'Insufficient funds', 'No withdraw permission on source account'...
Returns: bool, string|nil

Create a new non-default bank account for a character. Starts with $0 balance (only the auto-created default account gets Config.StartingBalance). A character may own at most Config.MaxExtraAccounts savings and shared accounts (default 5); one more is refused. Their personal account and job accounts don't count.

ParamTypeDescription

Grant a character access to a bank account (shared accounts). The granter can only give roles below their own, and only to someone below them; the owner cannot be changed this way.

Would GrantBankAccess with these arguments be allowed? Every one of its rules is asked and nothing is written. For a step that waits on someone before it grants: the phone's Bank app asks it before it sends an invite, then grants when the invite is accepted (and the rules are asked again then).

whonumber|tableThe person who would get it
rolestringThe role they would get
grantedBynumber|tableThe person who would grant it
local ok, why = exports.whip_core:CanGrantBankAccess(accountId, { charId = typedId }, 'view', source)
if not ok then return false, why end   -- say why now, before asking them
Returns: bool, string|nil

The money and the access list stay as they are. Trusted: your code decides who may; the activity log records which resource did it.

What your resource charges for vehicles. The Banks page values an owned car at this price; when several resources sell the same model, it takes the average. The system moves money between two accounts: payroll out of a business account. No permission check; the same refusals as a transfer otherwise. Written to the activity log with your resource's name.

ChargePlayer(source, amount, opts)SERVER

Take a payment from a player (cash or bank) and get a receipt RefundPlayer can undo. The one way whip charges anyone. See Charging a Player.

ParamTypeDescription
sourcenumberPlayer server ID
amountnumberA whole number, 0 or more (0 takes nothing and still answers a receipt)
opts.methodstring?'cash', 'bank' or 'auto' (default: cash if they carry enough, else the bank)
opts.accountIdnumber?Bank: which account (default their default one); their withdraw permission is checked
opts.currencystring?Cash: the item that counts as money (default 'cash')
opts.reasonstring?What it was for: on the statement and the activity log
local receipt, err = exports.whip_core:ChargePlayer(source, 75, { reason = 'Car wash' })
if not receipt then return false, err end   -- a sentence the player can read
Returns: receipt|false, string|nil: receipt { id, amount, method, accountId, currency, refunded }
RefundPlayer(receipt, amount)SERVER

Give back a payment ChargePlayer took: all of it, or amount. It goes back where it came from with no permission check; a bank refund that is refused comes back as cash, and cash for a player who has left goes to their bank. Only the resource that charged may refund, only up to what is left, and only within 30 minutes.

ParamTypeDescription
receipttable|numberThe receipt, or its id
amountnumber?How much to give back (default: everything not yet refunded)
local done, why = washTheCar(source)   -- your own step, after ChargePlayer
if not done then
    exports.whip_core:RefundPlayer(receipt)   -- the whole charge back
    return false, why
end
-- Part of it instead: RefundPlayer(receipt, 25) gives back $25 of what is left
Returns: bool, string|nil: false when it could not be delivered (also printed as CRITICAL)

Money held: pay now, settle for what was used

For a service that is metered: the fuel a pump pours, a taxi's fare, a charging point's minutes, a car wash's cycles. ChargePlayer then RefundPlayer loses the change if your resource or the server stops in between; a hold cannot. Take the most it could cost with HoldMoney, say how much is used as it runs (SpendMoneyHold), and SettleMoneyHold when it ends: the rest comes back. Nothing is lost either way. The refund owed for all of it is noted on the payer's character in the same write as the charge, so a crash before the settle is paid back at their next login. The payer leaving, your resource stopping, or whip_core stopping settles it there and then for what was used. Cash change goes to the pockets (the bank when it does not fit); a bank refund that cannot be made now is paid at the next login. A hold is your resource's own: only you spend or settle it. whip_fuel's pumps work this way.
HoldMoney(source, amount, opts)SERVER

Take amount from the player now, cash or bank, for a metered service. opts = { method = 'cash' | 'bank', reason, vehicle? }: vehicle (a vehicleId) keeps that car's row unwritten until the settle, so fuel it was given and not yet paid for is never saved.

local holdId, why = exports.whip_core:HoldMoney(source, 100, { method = 'cash', reason = 'Car wash' })
if not holdId then return false, why end
-- each cycle: SpendMoneyHold(holdId, usedSoFar); at the end: SettleMoneyHold(holdId)
Returns: the hold's id, or false, why (not enough money, no bank account)
SpendMoneyHold(id, spent)SERVER

How much of your hold is used so far: money, from 0 to what was held. Say it as the service runs; it is what a settle keeps if your resource or the server stops first.

Returns: true, or false, why when the hold is gone (whip_core settled it: the payer left) or is not yours. Stop giving the service then
SettleMoneyHold(id, spent?)SERVER

End your hold: spent (or what SpendMoneyHold last said) is kept, the rest goes back, the note is cleared and a held vehicle's row is written, all together.

Returns: { spent, refunded, paidNow } (paidNow false: the change is owed, paid at the next login), or false, why when it was settled already or is not yours
GetMoneyHold(id)SERVER

One of your holds as it is now. Ask it before you give more of the service: nil means it is over.

Returns: { source, amount, spent, method }, or nil (not yours, or settled)
PayPlayer(who, amount, opts)SERVER

The call for paying a player (a wage, a reward, a sale): the other way from ChargePlayer. who is a server id, or { charId = n } for a character who may be away (paid into the bank). Cash that does not fit their pockets lands at their feet, never lost; every payment is on the activity log with your resource's name.

exports.whip_core:PayPlayer(source, 250, { reason = 'Courier job' })
exports.whip_core:PayPlayer({ charId = 12 }, 250, { method = 'bank', reason = 'Wages' })
ParamTypeDescription
whonumber|tableA server id (online), or { charId = n }
amountnumberA whole number, 0 or more (0 pays nothing)
opts.methodstring?'cash', 'bank' or 'auto' (default: cash while they are online, else their bank)
opts.accountIdnumber?Bank: which account (default their default one)
opts.currencystring?Cash: the item paid (default 'cash')
opts.reasonstring?What it was for: on the statement and the activity log
Returns: true, { method, amount, currency?, placement?, accountId? }: placement is 'inventory' or 'ground', or false, reason

Inventory System

Player Containers

Each player has two containers:

ContainerSlotsMax WeightPurpose
player3080 kgPrimary inventory: items go here first
accessory510 kgQuick-access items (keys, phone, etc.)

Sizes come from Config.ContainerSlots and Config.MaxWeight. Config.AccessoryStrip = false takes the strip away: player is then the only pocket, and whatever a character had in the strip moves into it when they log in. Read the list at runtime with GetPockets() rather than typing it out.

More room is an item, not a pocket. A duffle bag holds 25 slots, and players find, drop, steal and lose it like anything else. See RegisterPanelItem for how a container-item is declared.

The Four Verbs

Everything you do to a player's inventory is one of four calls, and each works across everything the character is carrying:

ExportWhat it does
AddItemPuts an item on the player, wherever it fits
RemoveItemTakes an item from wherever it is
HasItemDo they have at least this many, anywhere on them?
GetItemCountHow many are they carrying in total?

To act on one specific slot, name it with an address ({ kind = 'player', id = source, sub = 'player', slot = 3 }) and use GetItemAt, SetItemMetadata, StoreGive or StoreTake. You rarely type one out: a use handler and FindItem both hand you the address of the item they are about.

Weight Is Nested

An item's weight in Config.Items is what it weighs empty. If it holds anything, the contents are added on top: recursively, at every level.

A wallet is 0.2 kg. Put 5,000 cash in it and the wallet weighs 0.2 kg plus the cash. Put that wallet in a duffle bag, and the bag carries the lot. A magazine in a rifle in a duffle bag in a car boot is counted at all four levels.

-- duffle_bag   1.5kg   (empty)
--  └─ wallet   0.2kg   (empty)
--      └─ 5,000 cash @ 0.0001kg = 0.5kg
--
-- The bag reports 2.2kg, and every container above it agrees.
You do not declare any of this. A bag registered with RegisterPanelItem is weighed with what is in it from the start, and there is nothing to keep in step when you add a new one.

Consequences worth knowing:

  • A bag is not a hole to pour weight into. Filling one makes the carrier heavier, so capacity is real.
  • The weight a tooltip shows includes everything inside the item.
  • Bags inside bags are counted 4 levels deep at most.
  • A read hook that throws falls back to the item's base weight rather than failing the move.
  • An item with no definition weighs 0: see the note on unregistered items under Panels.

What Happens When an Inventory Is Full

It depends on which of two things you are doing:

OperationMeaningWhen it will not fit
GiveThe item is entering the world from outside it: a reward, a purchase, a refund, an admin spawnDropped at the player's feet. Failing would destroy it; it exists nowhere else
MoveThe item already exists somewhere: a ground pickup, a stash transfer, a slot drag, a tradeLeft where it is. Nothing is lost, and creating a copy at the player's feet would duplicate it

AddItem is a give: it drops what doesn't fit rather than lose it, and tells you which happened. It answers 'inventory' or 'ground', and both count as given.

Item Definitions

Items are defined in Config.Items (for built-in items) or registered at runtime via RegisterItem (for external resources). An item is a table of fields; name and weight are required. Every field is listed under Item Definition.

Item icons

An item registered by your resource shows a picture from your resource, not from whip_core, so it survives a whip_core update. Two things make it work:

  1. A picture named after the item key, WebP or PNG: html/img/items/lockpick_gold.webp (or any path, named by the item's image field). WebP is smaller for the same picture, and every player downloads every icon, so prefer it. When both exist, the WebP is used.
  2. The matching line in your fxmanifest.lua, so FiveM serves the pictures: files { 'html/img/items/*.webp', 'html/img/items/*.png' } (just the one you use is fine).

Without the files line the inventory shows the "missing" picture. whip_autos does this and is worth copying. whip_core finds each item's picture once and remembers it; a new picture shows after its resource restarts.

Registering Items at Runtime

-- server.lua — Register a new item from your resource
-- (fxmanifest.lua: shared_script '@whip_core/lib/satellite.lua')
Whip.register(function()
    exports.whip_core:RegisterItem('mycrime_lockpick_gold', {
        name     = 'Gold Lockpick',
        desc     = 'A premium lockpick that never breaks.',
        weight   = 0.3,
        type     = 'tool',
        stack    = false,
        maxStack = 1,
        usable   = false,
    })
end)

Registered items work everywhere immediately: inventory, ground drops, containers, shops, NUI tooltips. The Items section of the Admin Panel (/whip) shows which resource registered each item.

Stacking

Items with stack = true and maxStack > 1 stack in a single slot. When adding: existing stacks are topped up first (lowest slot number), then remainder fills empty slots. When removing: highest slots are depleted first (preserves lower slots). Cash has maxStack = 999999 and near-zero weight (0.0001 kg per note).

Item Use System

When a player right-clicks an item marked usable = true:

  1. Server validates the item exists, is usable, and is off cooldown
  2. Calls the registered UseHandler for that item key
  3. Handler returns true → consume 1 unit (food, bandage, potion)
  4. Handler returns false → keep the item (equippable tools, toggle items)
  5. Handler returns false, 'why' → refused: nothing happened (no cooldown, no event, nothing taken) and the player is shown why
  6. Inventory syncs to client, whip_core:item:used event fires
-- UseHandler: true = consume it, false = keep it, false, 'why' = refused (nothing happens)
-- 'myems_medkit' is an item your resource registered ('bandage' is whip_core's own)
Whip.register(function()
    exports.whip_core:RegisterUseHandler('myems_medkit', function(source, player, slotData, addr)
        local ok, why = exports.whip_core:ApplyEffect(source, 'medkit_heal', {
            duration = 10, magnitude = 5, tickRate = 1,
            onTick = function(src, p, effect) exports.whip_core:AddStat(src, 'health', effect.magnitude) end,
        })
        if not ok then return false, why end   -- refused: they keep the medkit and see why
        return true  -- consume the medkit
    end)
end)

The handler is given (source, player, slotData, addr). slotData is the item that was used, { item, amount, metadata }. addr is where it is, as an address: { kind = 'player', id = source, sub = 'player', slot = 4 }. Hand addr to GetItemAt, StoreTake or SetItemMetadata to act on that exact item.

An item used up at the end of a progress bar (a drink, a bandage, a part fitted to a car) passes a table instead of a function, and whip runs the bar, times it on the server, takes the item and then calls your onComplete: see a use with a progress bar. Something that cannot be done in the water or while falling says so in that table (notWhile = { 'swimming', 'falling' }): whip refuses the bar there, and stops it if either begins.

Context Actions

Items with defaultAction and contextOptions get right-click menu options beyond "Use". Register a handler for the action key: it is given the same four arguments as a use handler. Start the key with your resource's name: action names are shared by every resource on the server.

An item's own options go at the top of its menu, under Use, and Give, Place, Split and Destroy go below them. Give each option an order to set where it sits: lowest first. Options without one keep the order you list them in, after those with one. whip_gunny's are Equip (1), Load Bullets (2), Unload (3), then Open.

Whip.register(function()
    exports.whip_core:RegisterContextAction('my_resource:inspect_serial', function(source, player, slotData, addr)
        local serial = slotData.metadata and slotData.metadata.serial or 'none'
        exports.whip_core:NotifyPlayer(source, 'Serial: ' .. serial)
    end)
end)

Options that come and go

An option can show only some of the time. when asks the item (its metadata): Unload only while a magazine has rounds in it. require asks the player, with the same words as an interaction's require (job, onDuty, jobPermission, item, zone, charId, ace, vehicle, alive). An option that fails either is left off the menu, and the server asks both again before it runs, so a player who clicks anyway is told no.

contextOptions = {
    { action = 'my_guns:unload', label = 'Unload', when = { ammo = { above = 0 } } },
    { action = 'my_cops:prints', label = 'Check for prints', require = { job = 'police', onDuty = true } },
}

A when has one test per metadata field, and every one must pass: ammo = 0 (equal to), model = { 'adder', 't20' } (one of), ammo = { above = 0 } (also below, atLeast, atMost), slots = { empty = false } (has something in it; empty is nothing, false, '', 0 or a table with nothing in it). Put default beside a test for an item that has no such field: ammo = { below = 12, default = 0 } is "not full", and a magazine with no ammo field counts as empty. A word whip does not know is refused when the item registers, with what to write instead.

The menu just leaves an option out when its when fails, but a double-click or a hotbar key that runs it is told why. Say it in the item's own words with whyNot: whyNot = 'Magazine is full'. Without one the player hears "Load Bullets isn't possible right now".

Options outside the pockets

An item's options show only while the player carries it. Add anywhere = true to an option to offer it in a boot, a glovebox, a stash, a bag or wallet, or a resource's panel too (not on the ground, in an ignition or on a shop's shelf). Its handler is then handed that store's address as addr ({ kind = 'vehicle', id, sub = 'trunk', slot }, say), so write it for any address, not only kind = 'player'. The player must have that store open, and when and require are checked as usual.

-- An evidence bag's tag, read in an evidence locker as well as in the pockets
{ action = 'mypd_read_tag', label = 'Read the tag', anywhere = true }

Options on the ground

A pile of an item on the ground has a 3D prompt: Pick up. An item can add up to three more with groundOptions, each naming one of the item's own options (a contextOptions action, or its defaultAction). The player scrolls to one and presses E. The item is picked up exactly as Pick up does, and only once it is in their pockets does that option run on the slot it landed in, as if they had chosen it in the inventory, with the same checks (when, require). It is checked before anything moves, so a refusal leaves the item where it lies. whip_gunny's weapons offer Equip: picked up, then drawn.

groundOptions = {
    { action = 'whip_gunny:equip_weapon', label = 'Equip', icon = 'target' },   -- the prompt says "Equip Pump Shotgun"
}

label is what the prompt says, before the item's name (24 letters at most). icon is a glyph's name from html/js/glyphs.js; without one it wears Pick up's arrow.

An option on someone else's item
