Your resource can add an option to an item it does not own: a police resource's "Check for prints" on whip_gunny's guns. It is the same shape as a contextOptions entry, its action is yours (register it with RegisterContextAction), and it goes when your resource stops.

Whip.register(function()
    exports.whip_core:RegisterContextAction('my_cops:prints', function(source, player, slotData, addr) ... end)
    exports.whip_core:AddItemOption('gunny_pistol', {
        action = 'my_cops:prints', label = 'Check for prints', order = 10,
        require = { job = 'police', onDuty = true },
    })
end)

Pictures that change with the item

An item's images list gives it other pictures for other states. The first one whose when passes is drawn; none passes, and it is the item's own picture. A path is inside your resource, as image is, and a {field} in it is filled from the item's metadata. {make} is the maker of the car the item's model names (a vehicle key's), which the game knows. A picture whose file is not there yet shows the item's own instead, so you can add the rule before the art.

images = {
    { when = { slots = { empty = false } }, image = 'html/img/items/duffle_bag_full.webp' },   -- zipped and full
}
images = {
    { image = 'html/img/items/keys/{make}.webp' },   -- keys/pegassi.webp for a Pegassi's key
}
images = {   -- by how many are in the slot, as whip's cash is
    { amount = { below = 100 },  image = 'html/img/items/coins_few.webp' },
    { amount = { atLeast = 100 }, image = 'html/img/items/coins_heap.webp' },
}

amount tests the slot's count with above, below, atLeast and atMost, and can sit beside a when. Where there is no slot to count, as in a shop's list or /whip → Economy → Items, no amount picture fits and the item's own picture is drawn, so give the item an image that stands for any amount.

An admin can change these on the Items page: what shows each picture, their order, and new pictures added by link (In game: /whip → Economy → Items). What a picture can be shown by there is the count (an item that stacks), the item's card rows (metaFields), any field its own pictures test, and the fields you list in pictureFields, so list the metadata a picture might be picked by, with words an admin reads:

pictureFields = {
    { key = 'mustard', label = 'Mustard', type = 'bool' },     -- a burger with mustard: its own picture
    { key = 'bites',   label = 'Bites taken', type = 'number' },
}

type is 'bool' (shown by yes or no), 'number' (at least, at most, over, under or exactly) or 'text' (is, is set, is not set), 'text' when left out.

Item settings

An admin can change any item's name, description and weight on the Items page, and Reset puts the item's own back. Your item has these without doing anything: the defaults are what your definition says, so rewording your item moves the default with it, and an admin's change stays until they reset it.

Settings of its own. An item can opt in to more, declared with the item: a magazine's size, a gun's reload time, a radio's range. Each is a setting of that one item, not of your resource, so it sits on the item's page rather than in Settings. Add a settings list to the definition. An entry is a RegisterSettings entry: a key, a type ('int', 'number', 'bool', 'string' or 'enum': a value or an on/off), a default, a label, and the min, max, step, unit, maxLen, nullable, options or help its type takes. Twenty at most; name, desc and weight are taken. A mistake (a default outside its own range, a type it cannot be) refuses the item, with why.

Whip.register(function()
    exports.whip_core:RegisterItem('my_guns_mag', {
        name = 'Pistol Magazine', weight = 0.2, stack = false,
        settings = {
            { key = 'capacity', type = 'int', min = 1, max = 100, default = 12,
              label = 'Rounds it holds', help = 'How many rounds fit in one.' },
            { key = 'quickLoad', type = 'bool', default = false, label = 'Loads in one go' },
        },
    })
end)

-- Server or client: the value in force (the admin's, or the default)
local capacity = exports.whip_core:GetItemSetting('my_guns_mag', 'capacity')
-- ...and every change after, Reset included. Inside Whip.register, like any registration.
exports.whip_core:OnItemSettingChanged('my_guns_mag', 'capacity', function(value, old)
    MyMags.capacity = value
end)

A change takes effect at once, on the server and every player's game. The simplest way to use one is whip_gunny's: write the value into your own config table as it arrives (Config.Magazines[item].capacity = value), and everything that reads that table needs no change. Keep your config's own value for the default before you write over it, or the next registration declares the admin's value as the default. A player's game has the values once whip_core has sent them as it joins: until then GetItemSetting answers nil there, and your hook runs when they arrive. Saved like every setting: in whip_settings, with who changed it and when, and every change in whip_settings_log.

In game: /whip → Economy → ItemsServer owners

Every item the server knows, from every resource, with its picture. Search by name, key or resource, or pick a resource. With no item picked, the page says how many there are, which ones an admin has changed (each opens from there), and how many come from each resource.

An item's page has, top to bottom:

  • What it is, beside its picture: its key and resource, its weight, and whether it stacks and how many to a slot. Give to me puts some in your pockets. Edit hand position sets how it sits in the hand when it is held out to give or throw: the panel steps aside and a copy of you holds it, still, in one of give mode's poses, a free camera beside it (hold the right mouse button to look round); the furnisher's arrows and rings move and turn it (R swaps between them). H goes to the next pose: aiming, in a car at the left window, at the right window, then walking and jogging on the spot to see it carried (the left window is the left hand, the others share the right; the item can't be moved while it walks). It keeps what you set in the hand you leave, Confirm & Exit saves every hand you set, and Esc leaves it as it was. Every item is listed down the left, found by name, resource or whether its hand position is set; picking one goes straight to it, and with changes not saved you are asked first (Cancel, Save & swap, Disregard & swap). Over the list, two switches. Allow player walk animation: off (the default), a player holding the item out walks with the give walk (Config.GiveModeStyle, the trash-bag walk); on, they keep their own walk, and the walking poses show it. Picked up with both hands: off (the default), a player picks one up off the ground with the hand on its side; on, with both, for something big. Both are saved with the hands. Saved on the item for everyone (a permanent admin's); a thrown one leaves the hand turned that way.
  • Its settings, side by side: its name, description and weight (for config.lua's own items also whether it stacks, how many to a slot, its cooldown and its kind; whether it is used and its prop stay in config.lua), then its own settings, made by its resource for that item: whip_gunny's magazines have their size, its guns their reload time. Each shows the item's own value, Reset when it differs, and who changed it last. Change what you need and press Apply: it is checked as you type, saved for everyone at once, and works as Config does (changing a setting in game). Only a permanent admin can change them; dev tools given in the Player Manager can look.
  • What players see: its pictures, Default (its own) first, then each picture it changes to, named by what shows it (Quantity under 100, Mustard). The first from the left that fits is drawn, Default when none does. Click one to change what shows it (Always, the quantity, or one of the item's fields: pictures that change), move it earlier or later, or remove it. Add picture takes a link from a site in Picture links accepted (Fivemanage unless the server changed it). Reset pictures puts its resource's back. Saved with Apply, like the settings. A picture named after a car's maker (a vehicle key's) lists which of the game's makers have one and which are not made yet.

Metadata

Items can carry arbitrary JSON metadata (vehicle plate on a key, fuel level on a jerry can, nested inventory on a wallet). It is saved with the item and travels with it everywhere: drops, trades, containers.

-- Give an item with metadata
exports.whip_core:AddItem(source, 'id_card', 1, {
    name   = 'John Smith',
    number = 'A-10294',
})

-- Every new radio (your own item) starts with this metadata. A registration, so in Whip.register:
Whip.register(function()
    exports.whip_core:RegisterItemDefaultMeta('radio', function(itemKey)
        return { frequency = 100.0, battery = 100 }
    end)
end)

Finding Items

-- Find the first stack of an item (searches every pocket)
local found = exports.whip_core:FindItem(source, 'jerry_can')
-- found = { item = 'jerry_can', amount = 1, metadata = { fuel = 100 },
--           addr = { kind = 'player', id = source, sub = 'player', slot = 3 } }

-- Find ALL stacks
local allCans = exports.whip_core:FindAllItems(source, 'jerry_can')

if found then
    -- Read the slot it is in
    local can = exports.whip_core:GetItemAt(found.addr)

    -- Change the metadata on that slot, leaving every other key alone
    exports.whip_core:SetItemMetadata(found.addr, { fuel = 50 })
end

Persistence

Inventories save write-behind: a change is in memory at once and written within about a second (Config.FlushInterval), only the rows that changed (the first save after a load writes nothing), with both halves of a move in one transaction. A true from a change means "in memory and owed to disk", not "on disk", so a hard crash can lose up to one flush interval; data that cannot afford that belongs on a store kind that writes through. When everything else saves, and what happens when a write fails, is under Character Lifecycle → Save System.

Durability is per store kind, declared on the kind itself. Player inventories, containers and vehicle storage defer. Ground items and shop stock write through, and the bank writes immediately: carrying whatever the running action has saved, so an ATM's cash and its bank write are one transaction. If a move touches any write-through store, the whole move commits immediately.

Server Exports (Quick Reference)

ExportDescription
AddItemGive a player an item: answers 'inventory', or 'ground' when it would not fit and was dropped at their feet
RemoveItemTake an item from a player, from wherever it is on them
HasItemCheck if a player has at least N of an item
GetItemCountCount an item across a player's pockets
CanFitItemPre-check if an item fits on a player (weight + slots)
FindItem / FindAllItemsSearch a player for items by key: each answer carries the item's address
GetItemAt / SetItemMetadataRead one slot, or change its metadata, in any store, by address
StoreRead / StoreCountWhat is in any store: a stash, a boot, a panel, a player
StoreGive / StoreTakeCreate or destroy items in any store
StoreMoveMove a stack between any two stores, in one committed step
FindItemByUid / FindItemByMetaWhere one specific item is: by its uid, or by a metadata value (a gun's serial)
GetOpenStoresEvery store a player has open, as addresses
OpenStore / CloseStorePut a stash, a car boot or your own store kind on a player's screen, and take it away again
GetInventoryDeep copy of a player's whole inventory
GetPockets / GetPocketSlots / GetPocketMaxWeightWhich pockets a player has, and each one's slots and weight limit
RegisterItemRegister a new item definition at runtime
RetireItem / UnretireItemTake one of your items out of the game for good: RetireItem('mycafe_bagel', 'Bagels are off the menu'). Its definition goes, nothing can make a new one, and every one out there is taken away, logged as lost with your reason, not refunded: at once from online players, open stashes, boots and the ground; the rest as each loads (a character at login, a stash or car when opened), inside duffle bags and wallets too. Only your own items: one another resource holds is refused. Not inside a panel that keeps its own shape (a magazine), nor your own store kinds: those are yours to clear
RegisterUseHandlerRegister what happens when an item is used
RegisterContextActionRegister a right-click menu action
AddItemOptionAdd a right-click option to an item, yours or another resource's
RemoveItemOptionTake back an option you added
RegisterItemDefaultMetaAuto-generate metadata for new items

Stores: one move for every kind of storage

A player's pockets, an accessory slot, a world container, a vehicle boot, a shop, and an item's own panel (a duffle bag) are all the same thing to whip_core: a store. (Items lying on the ground are not a store: they are ground items, with their own exports.) Each kind says how it is read, how it is written, how quickly it is saved, and what happens before and after a move; whip does the rest (weight and slot checks, stacking, saving, updating players' screens) the same way for all of them.

So a move between any two kinds (pockets to a boot, a stash to a bag) is a single step: there is no moment where a stack has left one side and not arrived at the other.

From server code, every store is reached by address. A player's pockets: AddItem, RemoveItem, HasItem. Any store at all, pockets included: StoreGive, StoreTake, StoreRead, StoreMove, GetItemAt, SetItemMetadata with an address. None of them need the player to have anything open.

A kind may also declare beforeMove and afterMove. beforeMove runs before anything is mutated and can refuse with a reason; afterMove runs only once the move has committed. They are what a panel's onValidate and onChange hooks are built on (Panels), and a kind of your own declares them with RegisterStoreKind.

A hook that errors refuses the move. An error in beforeMove never counts as a yes. The refusal is logged, with the error in your resource's console.

Addresses: naming a store (and a slot)

Every store is named the same way: a small table, { kind, id, sub, slot }. Hand one to StoreRead, StoreCount, StoreGive, StoreTake, StoreMove, GetItemAt, SetItemMetadata, OpenStore or CloseStore. The slot is left out when a call can choose one itself (or, for OpenStore, has no use for one).

KindAddressWhat it is
player{ kind = 'player', id = source, sub = 'player' }A player's pockets. The accessory strip is { kind = 'player', id = source, sub = 'accessory' }. sub defaults to 'player'
container{ kind = 'container', id = containerId }A world stash. Loaded if nobody has opened it since the restart
vehicle{ kind = 'vehicle', id = vehicleId, sub = 'trunk' }A car's 'trunk', 'glovebox' or 'key' (ignition). id may also be a vehicle reference such as { plate = 'ABC 123' }. Loaded the same way
panel{ kind = 'panel', id = panelId }A panel that is open right now (owner = source to name whose)
your own{ kind = 'mykind', id = ..., sub = ... }A kind a resource registered with RegisterStoreKind

shop and basket exist only while a player has one open, so they have no server-side address. GetOpenStores(source) lists what a player has open, already as addresses.

StoreMove(fromAddr, toAddr, opts)SERVER

Move a stack from one store to another, or within one store. Both sides are opened, both ends' hooks are asked, the move is validated, it is persisted, and open viewers are told, the same sequence a player's own drag takes.

It takes two addresses, whip's standard { kind, id, sub, slot } shape. sub names a player's pocket or a vehicle's storage type.

-- Take whatever is in slot 3 of container 12 and put it in the player's slot 1
local ok, err = exports.whip_core:StoreMove(
    { kind = 'container', id = 12, slot = 3 },
    { kind = 'player', id = source, sub = 'player', slot = 1 }
)
if not ok then print(err) end

-- Move just two of them, rather than the whole stack
exports.whip_core:StoreMove(from, to, { amount = 2 })
ParamTypeDescription
fromAddrtable{ kind, id?, sub?, slot }: source (the slot is required)
toAddrtable{ kind, id?, sub?, slot? }: destination. Leave the slot out and it goes wherever it fits
optstable?{ amount?, mode?, reason? }. amount 0 or omitted moves the whole slot; mode is 'move', 'one' or 'split'; reason goes in the activity log
It is on the record. A move made through this writes a "moved" row on the timeline of each character it touched, saying which resource asked (and your reason). Players whose pockets changed are sent their inventory, and it fires whip_core:item:added / item:removed for them.
Prefer this to a remove-then-add pair. Removing from one store and adding to another is two independent operations, and the second one can fail, leaving the item deleted. StoreMove cannot end that way.
shop and basket have no server-side address. Both exist only relative to a player who has one open, so there is no server-wide "the shop" to name and StoreMove refuses them rather than guessing which session you meant.
Returns: boolean, string|nil: false plus a reason
StoreRead(addr)SERVER

What is in any store, as plain data: { kind, id, sub, label, slots, maxWeight, weight, items = { [slot] = { item, amount, metadata } } }, keyed by slot number. It is a copy, so changing it changes nothing. A slot in the address is ignored.

local stash = exports.whip_core:StoreRead({ kind = 'container', id = 12 })
if not stash then return end
for slot, it in pairs(stash.items) do
    print(slot, it.item, it.amount)
end

-- A car's boot. The id may be a vehicleId or a vehicle reference
local boot = exports.whip_core:StoreRead({ kind = 'vehicle', id = { plate = 'ABC 123' }, sub = 'trunk' })

-- A panel you opened, by the id you gave OpenPanel
local bench = exports.whip_core:StoreRead({ kind = 'panel', id = 'bench_' .. source })
A stash or a boot nobody has open is loaded for you, so this works on any stash that exists. A panel only exists while somebody has it open: once the last viewer has gone the answer is false, 'that panel is not open'. An open panel that is empty answers with items = {}.
Returns: table, or false, reason: 'No such container', 'Vehicle not found', 'that panel is not open', ...
StoreCount(addr, item)SERVER

How many of one item a store holds.

local n = exports.whip_core:StoreCount({ kind = 'vehicle', id = vehicleId, sub = 'trunk' }, 'delivery_package')
Returns: number, or false, reason
Check it before you compare it. A store that cannot be reached answers false, not 0, unlike GetItemCount, which counts a player's pockets and answers 0, reason. StoreCount(addr, 'x') >= 5 throws on false; write local n = StoreCount(addr, 'x') and then if n and n >= 5 then.
StoreGive(addr, item, amount, metadata, reason)SERVER

Create an item in any store: a reward into a stash, stock into a boot, a part into a panel. With a slot in the address it goes into exactly that slot (onto the same item if it can stack) or is refused; without one it goes wherever it fits, across several slots if it has to, all of it or none of it.

-- 20 packages into a job van's boot, wherever they fit
local slot, err = exports.whip_core:StoreGive(
    { kind = 'vehicle', id = vanId, sub = 'trunk' }, 'delivery_package', 20, nil, 'delivery shift')
if not slot then print(err) end
ParamTypeDescription
addrtableAn address; slot optional
itemstringA registered item
amountnumber?A whole number, 1 or more (default 1)
metadatatable?Leave it out and an item with a default generator (a gun's serial) gets fresh metadata in each slot
reasonstring|table?For the activity log, or { reason = '...' }
Returns: number: the (first) slot it landed in, or false, reason
For a player, AddItem is still the call for a reward. StoreGive with a player address refuses when the pockets are full; AddItem drops the item at their feet instead, so nothing is lost.
StoreTake(addr, amount, opts)SERVER

Take items out of any store, destroying them: materials used up, evidence confiscated. With a slot in the address, from that slot (amount nil = the whole stack). Without one, name the item in opts.item and it is taken from wherever it is in the store, all of it or none.

-- From one slot
local taken = exports.whip_core:StoreTake({ kind = 'container', id = 12, slot = 3 }, 2)

-- 5 water bottles ('drink') from wherever they are in the stash
local taken, err = exports.whip_core:StoreTake({ kind = 'container', id = 12 }, 5, { item = 'drink' })
ParamTypeDescription
addrtableAn address, with or without a slot
amountnumber?How many
optstable|string?{ item = 'drink' } when the address has no slot; reason for the log. A plain string is the reason
Returns: { item, amount, metadata }: what was taken (metadata only from a single slot), or false, reason ('Empty slot', 'Not enough items', ...). All or nothing: asking one slot for more than it holds takes nothing
Taking is not moving. What you take is gone. To put it somewhere else, use StoreMove, which cannot lose it halfway.
GetItemAt(addr)SERVER

What is in one slot of any store, such as a player's pockets, a stash, a boot or a panel: { item, amount, metadata }, as a copy. nil when the slot is empty; false, reason when the address is wrong (no such store, a slot past the end).

-- The item a use handler was given: is it still there?
local item = exports.whip_core:GetItemAt(addr)
if not item or item.item ~= 'alcohol' then return end

-- Slot 4 of a player's pockets
local it = exports.whip_core:GetItemAt({ kind = 'player', id = source, sub = 'player', slot = 4 })
ParamTypeDescription
addrtableAn address with a slot
Returns: { item, amount, metadata }; nil for an empty slot; false, reason for a wrong address
Empty is nil, wrong is false, and both are falsy, so if not item then covers both. Read the second value when you need to tell "nothing there" from "that is not a slot".
SetHeldItem(source, addr)SERVER

Say which of a player's items is in their hand: the slot of the item your resource just drew (a weapon, a tool), or nil when it is put away. Others act on the item in hand where it matters (GetHeldItem): whip_fuel's "Fill Jerry Can" at a pump and "Refuel (jerry can)" at a car door use the fuel can the player holds, never another one in their pockets. whip_gunny sets it for every weapon it draws.

The record is your resource's: another resource cannot change it while yours runs, and it goes when your resource stops, at logout and when the player leaves. It names the item and its serial, so an item dragged out of the slot, dropped, or swapped for another of the same kind no longer counts as held.

The player's own game is told each change: the client's GetHeldItem() reads it, and an action's require = { held = ... } is checked against it there, before any canInteract of yours is asked.

-- your tool, drawn from the slot the player clicked
exports.whip_core:SetHeldItem(source, addr)
-- ...and put away
exports.whip_core:SetHeldItem(source, nil)
ParamTypeDescription
sourcenumberThe player
addrtable|nilOne of that player's pocket slots: { kind = 'player', id = source, sub = 'player'|'accessory', slot = n }; nil to clear
Returns: true, or false, reason (an empty slot, not their own pockets, another resource's record)
GetHeldItem(source)SERVER

What the player holds, as GetItemAt answers it plus its addr: { addr, item, amount, metadata }. nil when nothing is held, or the held item has left its slot.

local held = exports.whip_core:GetHeldItem(source)
if held and held.item == 'jerry_can' then print('fuel:', held.metadata.fuel) end
Returns: { addr, item, amount, metadata } or nil
GetHeldItem()CLIENT

What this player holds, as the server last told this game: { item, pocket, slot } (a copy), or nil when the hand is empty. No metadata: for that, the server's GetHeldItem(source). For a prompt that is only for one held thing, require = { held = 'jerry_can' } is the cheaper way: whip checks it itself, so your canInteract is not asked while the hand holds anything else.

local held = exports.whip_core:GetHeldItem()
if held and held.item == 'jerry_can' then print('a jerry can, in slot', held.slot) end
Returns: { item, pocket, slot } or nil
SetItemMetadata(addr, metadata, opts)SERVER

Change the metadata of the item at an address: in a player's pockets, a stash, a boot or a panel. Only the keys you pass change; everything else on the item stays. { replace = true } makes the table the whole metadata instead, and { remove = { 'key' } } takes keys away. The change is saved and shown to whoever has that store open. Item metadata goes whole to the game of whoever sees the item, so keep a secret (a safe's code, a winning ticket number) server-side and put only an id on the item.

ParamTypeDescription
addrtableAn address with a slot: a use handler's addr, found.addr from FindItem, or one you build
metadatatable|nilThe keys to change. nil only with replace (clears it all) or remove; a bare nil is refused, so a variable that happened to be empty cannot wipe an item
optstable|nilreplace = true: the table becomes the whole metadata. remove = { 'key', ... }: take those keys away. quiet = true (a player's pockets only): save without sending their inventory to their screen, for a value that changes many times a second and reaches the player another way, such as a round count while firing
-- Note who a weapon was issued to, leaving its serial and everything else alone
local found = exports.whip_core:FindItem(source, 'gunny_pistol')
if found then
    exports.whip_core:SetItemMetadata(found.addr, { issuedTo = 'LSPD' })
end

-- A gun lying in stash 12, slot 3: mark it as evidence, and drop its custom label
local at = { kind = 'container', id = 12, slot = 3 }
exports.whip_core:SetItemMetadata(at, { evidence = true }, { remove = { 'label' } })
Returns: true once the slot has changed, even if the save has to be retried, or false, reason ('Empty slot', a wrong address, metadata that cannot be saved)
The item's uid is kept either way. It is the item's identity in the activity log, and a replace that dropped it would cut the item's history in two. Pass uid = false if you really mean to clear it.
Only plain data. Strings, numbers, booleans and tables of them. A function, a NaN, or anything else json.encode cannot write is refused (false, 'metadata cannot be saved: ...') before anything changes.
FindItemByUid(uid)SERVER

Where one specific item is: its address with a slot, or { kind = 'ground', id }, or nil. Every item that has been logged carries a uid in its metadata.

-- Where is the pistol with this uid now? (uid from its metadata or the activity log)
local at = exports.whip_core:FindItemByUid(uid)
if at and at.kind == 'player' then
    exports.whip_core:NotifyPlayer(at.id, 'The police want a word about your pistol', 'warning')
end
It searches what is loaded: online players, stashes, boots and panels in memory, and the ground. An item in a stash nobody has touched since the restart, or inside a bag, is not found.
Returns: table|nil
FindItemByMeta(key, value)SERVER

Where an item whose metadata key holds value is: its address, or nil. The first one found, so it is for a value one item carries, such as a gun's serial. It searches the same loaded places as FindItemByUid.

-- Run the serial: who has this gun?
local at = exports.whip_core:FindItemByMeta('serial', 'AB12CD34EF56')
if at and at.kind == 'player' then
    exports.whip_core:NotifyPlayer(officer, ('Registered to player %d'):format(at.id), 'info')
end
Returns: table|nil. GetItemAt(addr) reads the item
GetOpenStores(source)SERVER

Every store this player has open right now, as addresses, in a stable order: { { kind = 'container', id = 12 }, { kind = 'vehicle', id = 40, sub = 'trunk' }, ... }. Their own pockets are not "opened" and never listed; a shop they are browsing is { kind = 'shop' }. A panel is listed with its label too: { kind = 'panel', id = 'wallet_...', owner = source, label = 'Wallet' }, which is how you learn the id of a panel an item opened.

-- Is this player looking into stash 12?
for _, open in ipairs(exports.whip_core:GetOpenStores(source)) do
    if open.kind == 'container' and open.id == 12 then
        -- ...
    end
end
Returns: table[]: empty when nothing is open
OpenStore(source, addr, opts)SERVER

Put a store on a player's screen, beside their pockets: a world stash, a car's boot, or a store kind your resource registered (shown in the same right-hand grid). It runs the same checks as a player opening it themselves: a stash's access, distance and lock, a boot's distance and lock, unless opts says your resource has already decided. While it is open, the player's drags in it count.

-- A stash, after your own keycard check
local ok, reason = exports.whip_core:OpenStore(source, { kind = 'container', id = containerId }, {
    skipAccess = true,   -- my resource owns this box and has already decided
})
if not ok then
    exports.whip_core:NotifyPlayer(source, reason, 'error')
end

-- A car's boot, even though the car is locked (a warrant, a spare key)
exports.whip_core:OpenStore(source, { kind = 'vehicle', id = vehicleId, sub = 'trunk' }, { skipAccess = true })

-- Your own store kind, usable while they stay within 2 m of the safe
exports.whip_core:OpenStore(source, { kind = 'my_safe', id = 3 }, { coords = safeCoords, range = 2.0 })
ParamTypeDescription
sourcenumberServer player ID
addrtable{ kind = 'container', id }, { kind = 'vehicle', id, sub = 'trunk' } (the id may be a vehicle reference), or { kind = 'mykind', id, sub }
optstable?Any of the options below
OptionForDescription
skipDistancea stashDo not require the player to be standing at it. (A boot always does: it is where they must stay for their moves to count.)
skipAccessa stash, a bootIgnore a stash's lock and owner, or a boot's lock, for when your resource has already decided
coords, rangeyour own kindThe player must stay within range (default 3 m) of coords for their moves to count, as they must at a stash
readOnlyyour own kindThey can look, and every move is refused
Not everything opens this way. OpenStore refuses, with a reason:
• a player's pockets: use OpenPlayerInventory;
• a panel: use OpenPanel;
• a car's glovebox or ignition: those open from the car's seat, so only sub = 'trunk' is accepted;
• a player who already has a screen open: whip declines the open and releases it again.
A successful open makes that player a viewer until something closes it. Being a viewer is what lets their drags in that store count, so if you open a store for someone, close it with CloseStore when you are done, or they can keep moving items in it. Inside a SecureEvent handler the framework releases the view if your handler errors; anywhere else that is yours to do.
Several players can have one stash open at once. They share one copy of its contents, so two people reaching into the same stash resolve correctly: the loser of a race is simply told the slot is empty.
Returns: true, or false, reason
CloseStore(source, addr)SERVER

Take a store off a player's screen and away from them: the other half of OpenStore, for a stash, a boot or your own kind. Once closed they can move nothing in it, wherever they are standing. A stash or boot is saved first, and unloaded if nobody else is using it. Other players with the same store open are untouched.

exports.whip_core:CloseStore(source, { kind = 'container', id = containerId })
ParamTypeDescription
sourcenumberServer player ID
addrtableThe same address you opened it with
Returns: true, or false, reason: 'That is not open' when that player did not have it open
Works even if that player has since disconnected: a view held by somebody who has gone is the one most worth releasing. A panel closes with ClosePanel.

Inventory

Four verbs, each operating on every container the character carries. See what happens when an inventory is full.

To target one specific slot, name it with an address, such as { kind = 'player', id = source, sub = 'player', slot = 4 }, and use GetItemAt, SetItemMetadata, StoreGive or StoreTake. Those work on any store, not only a player's pockets. A use handler and FindItem hand you the address of the item they are about.
GetInventory(source)SERVER

Get a safe deep copy of a player's inventory.

ParamTypeDescription
sourcenumberServer player ID
local inv = exports.whip_core:GetInventory(source)
for pocket, slots in pairs(inv) do
    for slot, it in pairs(slots) do print(pocket, slot, it.item, it.amount) end
end
Returns: table: { player = { [slot] = { item, amount, metadata } }, accessory = { ... } }, or {}, 'Player not loaded'
This is safe: it returns a deep copy. Mutating the returned table will NOT affect the player's real inventory.
RegisterUseHandler(itemKey, handler)SERVER

Register a use handler for an item. Called when a player uses the item via hotbar (keys 1-5) or context menu "Use" option. The item must have usable = true in its definition. The handler receives (source, player, slotData, addr): player is the player's data sheet (the table GetPlayer gives you, less metadata), not whip's live object; slotData is the item used, { item, amount, metadata }; addr is where it is, as an address: { kind = 'player', id = source, sub = 'player', slot = 4 }.

Return Values

ReturnBehaviorUse Case
trueItem used successfully: consume one from the stackFood, drink, bandage, single-use items
falseItem used successfully: do NOT consume, keep the itemReusable tools, toggles

Only false keeps the item: returning nothing uses one up, the same as true. A bare false is still a use (the cooldown starts and whip_core:item:used fires), so "not now" is false, 'why'. false, 'why' refuses: nothing happened. The item is kept, no cooldown starts, no whip_core:item:used fires, nothing is logged as a use, and the player sees why. (The table form below reads a bare false from onComplete differently. See its card.)

ParamTypeDescription
itemKeystringItem key
handlerfunction | tablefunction(source, player, slotData, addr) → boolean, or a table for a use with a progress bar (below)
-- Consumable: heals and gets used up
exports.whip_core:RegisterUseHandler('myems_medkit', function(source, player, slotData, addr)
    local ok, why = exports.whip_core:SetStat(source, 'health', 200, 'item:medkit')
    if not ok then return false, why end
    return true  -- consume one medkit
end)

-- Reusable: equips a tool, item stays in inventory
exports.whip_core:RegisterUseHandler('flashlight', function(source, player, slotData, addr)
    TriggerClientEvent('myresource:toggleFlashlight', source)
    return false  -- keep the flashlight
end)

-- Wears out: keep the pick, and take a point of durability off THIS one
exports.whip_core:RegisterUseHandler('pickaxe', function(source, player, slotData, addr)
    local left = (slotData.metadata and slotData.metadata.durability or 100) - 1
    exports.whip_core:SetItemMetadata(addr, { durability = left })
    return false
end)

A use with a progress bar: pass a table

Pass a table instead of a function and whip does the whole timed use: canUse → the bar, timed by the server (a modified client cannot skip it) → the same item still where the use started (they had the whole bar to move or drop it) → the item is taken → onComplete. Taking before onComplete means the effect only ever happens with the item gone; onComplete answering false, 'why' (or erroring) puts it back, and the player is shown the why (an error shows "That did not work"). One timed use at a time per player.

exports.whip_core:RegisterUseHandler('field_dressing', {   -- your own item ('bandage' is whip_core's)
    label    = 'Bandaging...',
    duration = 4000,
    anim     = { dict = 'missheistdockssetup1clipboard@idle_a', clip = 'idle_a' },

    -- Optional: checked before the bar. false, 'why' refuses and shows 'why'.
    -- whip's health is GTA's scale: 200 is full, 100 is down.
    canUse = function(source)
        if exports.whip_core:GetStat(source, 'health') >= 200 then
            return false, 'You are not hurt'
        end
        return true
    end,

    -- The bar finished and the bandage is gone. false, 'why' gives it back — so RETURN the
    -- effect's answer: a heal that failed then costs the player nothing.
    onComplete = function(source)
        return exports.whip_core:AddStat(source, 'health', 25)
    end,
})
FieldTypeDescription
durationnumberRequired. The bar's length in milliseconds
labelstring?Text above the bar. Default 'Using <item name>...'
anim, prop, disable, cancelOnDeath, cancelOnExit, notWhiletable / booleanWhat the bar does to the player: the same options as the client Progress. cancelOnExit = true for a use done from a seat (whip_autos' nitrous bottle): getting out stops it and they keep the item. notWhile = { 'swimming' } for a use that cannot be done in the water: it does not start there, and stops if they go in; they keep the item. A state misspelt there is refused when you register
iconstring?The bar's disc shows the item's own picture; this icon is for an item with none, as the client Progress takes it ('eat', 'fuel'…)
canCancelboolean?Default true: the player may press X to stop, and keeps the item
consumeboolean?Default true. false keeps the item: a timed use of a tool
reasonstring?What the item log says it was used for. Default 'used'
canUsefunction?function(source, player, slotData, addr) → true, or false, 'why' to refuse before the bar
onCompletefunction?function(source, player, item, addr) after the item is taken. false, 'why' gives it back and shows why. A bare false also gives it back (a refusal with no message, no cooldown), not "keep it" as in the function form. To keep a tool, set consume = false

Worked examples: the drunk effect's server.lua in HUD Framework (a beer: walking allowed, refused in a car), whip_core/server/items/armour.lua, and whip_autos/server/power/nitrous.lua (an install that finds the car the server sees the player in, so the client never names one).

Not an item? A bar started from a prompt or a command uses the server Progress(source, opts) directly inside your SecureEvent: the same server-timed bar, without the item steps.
Returns: true, or false, reason (a missing key or handler, a table without a positive duration, or an item another resource already handles, the registration rule). The item needs usable = true in its definition: whip says so in the console if it is registered without it, because otherwise players only ever see "Item not usable".
AddItem(source, item, amount, metadata, opts)SERVER

Add an item, trying the player's pockets first, then the accessory slot. If it fits nowhere, the item is dropped at the player's feet rather than lost, and the answer says which happened: 'inventory' or 'ground'. With Config.DropOnFullInventory = false (or opts.noDrop) it answers false, reason instead and gives nothing, so anything that charged for the item checks the answer.

ParamTypeDescription
sourcenumberServer player ID
itemstringItem key: must be registered
amountnumber?A whole number, 1 or more (default 1)
metadatatable?Custom metadata (pass nil to skip it and still give options)
optsstring|table?A reason for the activity log ('quest reward', written beside your resource's name), or a table:
reason: the same;
noDrop = true: refuse instead of dropping at their feet;
pocket = 'player'|'accessory': only that pocket;
coords: where to drop it instead of at their feet.
RemoveItem takes a reason as its last argument too.
local where, err = exports.whip_core:AddItem(source, 'drink', 2, nil, 'quest reward')
if not where then
    print('nothing was given: ' .. err)
elseif where == 'ground' then
    -- their pockets were full, so it is at their feet (they are told automatically)
end

-- Refuse rather than drop, and only into the accessory strip
local where, err = exports.whip_core:AddItem(source, 'id_card', 1, nil, { pocket = 'accessory', noDrop = true })
A mistyped item name or a bad amount is refused, not dropped. AddItem(src, 'drnk') answers false, 'Unknown item "drnk"'; 0.5, -3 or 'lots' answer false, 'Amount must be a whole number of 1 or more'.
Returns: 'inventory' | 'ground': where it went, or false, reason
ReturnsMeaning
'inventory'Landed in a pocket
'ground'Dropped at their feet because it would not fit. The player is notified automatically
false, reasonNowhere at all. Nothing was created: a refusal (an unknown item, a bad amount, noDrop with no room), or rarely no ped or a failed drop
A ground drop counts as given, on purpose. Almost every caller writes if not where then and undoes something. If a successful drop reported failure, those handlers would refund a payment that was already made, or drop a second copy beside the one whip just created.

If you need to know it went to the floor, check for 'ground'. If you would rather the give simply fail, pass { noDrop = true }, or set Config.DropOnFullInventory = false for the whole server.
The tradeoff. A ground item is public: anyone standing nearby can pick it up. The default trades silent loss (which players cannot react to) for visible loss (which they can). Nothing whip does destroys the item either way. Pass { noDrop = true } when your code would rather the give simply fail.

Note that whip_core:item:added does not fire for a ground drop, because nothing entered the inventory.
RemoveItem(source, item, amount, reason)SERVER

Remove an item across both containers (player first, then accessory).

ParamTypeDescription
sourcenumberServer player ID
itemstringItem key
amountnumber?A whole number, 1 or more (default 1)
reasonstring|table?For the activity log (see AddItem), or { reason = '...' }
local ok, err = exports.whip_core:RemoveItem(source, 'lockpick', 1, 'snapped')
if not ok then return false, err end   -- 'Not enough items (have 0, need 1)': nothing was taken
Returns: bool, string|nil: nothing is taken unless they have the full amount
A test's items. What a Director test or a Systems test hands out is marked as the test's (director or systest in its metadata). When the test ends it is taken back from its players' pockets and the ground, or at the next login for a player who was gone. While it lasts it may stay only where that end looks (the players' pockets, the test's own cars and containers): a move anywhere else is refused. Otherwise it is an item like any other, and your resource counts, takes and uses it as usual. A live Director run marks nothing: its items are real (what a run hands out).
HasItem(source, item, amount)SERVER

Check if a player has at least amount across both containers.

ParamTypeDescription
sourcenumberServer player ID
itemstringItem key
amountnumber?Minimum (default 1)
if not exports.whip_core:HasItem(source, 'lockpick') then return false, 'You need a lockpick' end
Returns: bool, string|nil
GetItemCount(source, item)SERVER

Count total of an item across both containers.

ParamTypeDescription
sourcenumberServer player ID
itemstringItem key
Returns: number, string|nil
CanFitItem(source, item, amount, metadata)SERVER

Check if a player's inventory can fit an item (checks slots and weight). Pass metadata when the item carries contents, or it is weighed empty.

ParamTypeDescription
sourcenumberServer player ID
itemstringItem key
amountnumber?Quantity (default 1)
metadatatableOptional. The specific instance's metadata, so its contents are weighed too
local fits, why = exports.whip_core:CanFitItem(source, 'drink', 10)
if not fits then
    exports.whip_core:NotifyPlayer(source, why, 'error')   -- e.g. 'Only 3 fit'
    return
end
Returns: true, or false, reason, the reason is a sentence: 'Only 3 fit', 'No room', 'Unknown item "x"', 'Amount must be a whole number of 1 or more', 'Player not loaded'
FindItem(source, item, pocket)SERVER

The first stack of an item the player carries, with its address: { item, amount, metadata, addr }, a copy. Searches every pocket by default, or just one; within a pocket the lowest slot comes first (FindAllItems answers in the same order).

ParamTypeDescription
sourcenumberServer player ID
itemstringItem key
pocketstring|nilOnly this pocket ('player' or 'accessory'): nil searches them all. A pocket that does not exist finds nothing
local found = exports.whip_core:FindItem(source, 'lockpick')
if found then
    -- found.item, found.amount, found.metadata
    -- found.addr = { kind = 'player', id = source, sub = 'player', slot = 7 }
    exports.whip_core:StoreTake(found.addr, 1, { reason = 'lockpick snapped' })
end
Returns: table|nil: { item, amount, metadata, addr }
FindAllItems(source, item, pocket)SERVER

Every stack of an item the player carries, each as a FindItem entry: { item, amount, metadata, addr }. Searches every pocket by default, or just one.

ParamTypeDescription
sourcenumberServer player ID
itemstringItem key
pocketstring|nilOnly this pocket, or nil for all
for _, key in ipairs(exports.whip_core:FindAllItems(source, 'vehicle_key')) do
    print(key.metadata.plate, key.addr.sub, key.addr.slot)
end
Returns: table: array of { item, amount, metadata, addr } (empty array if none; {}, 'Player not loaded' before they load)
RegisterContextAction(actionKey, handler)SERVER

Register a custom context menu action for inventory items. The handler fires when a player selects this action from an item's right-click menu.

ParamTypeDescription
actionKeystringUnique action identifier: named by the item's defaultAction or one of its contextOptions, or no player can reach it. Start it with your resource's name ('my_bows:equip', not 'equip'): it is one name for the whole server, and a bare name another resource took first sends your items to its handler. At most 32 characters
handlerfunctionfunction(source, player, slotData, addr, how), the same four arguments as a use handler, and a fifth: player is the data sheet, not whip's live object; addr is where the item is; how is { from = 'ground' } when it runs straight after a ground option's pick-up (the player grabbed it off the floor: skip your own draw or take-out animation), else nil. Return false, 'why' to refuse, the player sees why
Whip.register(function()
    exports.whip_core:RegisterContextAction('my_bows:string', function(source, player, slotData, addr)
        if slotData.metadata and slotData.metadata.strung then return false, 'Already strung' end
        return exports.whip_core:SetItemMetadata(addr, { strung = true })
    end)
end)
Returns: true, or false, reason. The name is yours once registered (the registration rule): an action name another resource holds (including the ones whip uses for its own panel items, a wallet's or a bag's) is refused with the owner named, never silently taken over.
AddItemOption(itemKey, option)SERVER

Add a right-click option to an item, yours or another resource's. It shows on that item's menu with its own, and goes when your resource stops.

ParamTypeDescription
itemKeystringThe item it goes on. It need not be registered yet
optiontableA contextOptions entry: { action, label, order?, when?, require? }. The action is yours, registered with RegisterContextAction
exports.whip_core:AddItemOption('gunny_pistol', {
    action = 'my_cops:prints', label = 'Check for prints',
    require = { job = 'police', onDuty = true },
})
Returns: true, or false, reason: an option that is not one is refused saying why, and so is an action the item already has of its own, or the same item and action another resource added.
RemoveItemOption(itemKey, action)SERVER

Take back an option AddItemOption added. Only your own; they all go anyway when your resource stops.

Returns: true, or false, reason.
RegisterItemDefaultMeta(itemKey, generator, opts?)SERVER

Register a metadata generator function for an item. Called automatically when the item is created without explicit metadata: given with AddItem or StoreGive, picked up off the ground, shown on an infinite shop's shelf, or bought.

ParamTypeDescription
itemKeystringItem key
generatorfunctionfunction(itemKey, ctx) → table. It gets the item's key and who the item is for, and returns the metadata table. ctx.source and ctx.charId are the player receiving it, or nil into a stash or a boot. ctx.reason is 'given', 'pickup', 'shelf' (on an infinite shop's shelf, before anyone buys it) or 'bought'. ctx itself can be nil (the Director's item rewards), so cope without it
optstable?{ forBuyer = true }: bought off an infinite shop's shelf, the item is made again for the buyer (reason 'bought'). The shelf's copy was made for nobody. Stocked shops sell real items, which keep their metadata
exports.whip_core:RegisterItemDefaultMeta('radio', function(itemKey)
    return { frequency = 100.0, battery = 100 }
end)

-- A SIM card with its buyer's new number (whip_phone)
exports.whip_core:RegisterItemDefaultMeta('sim_card', function(itemKey, ctx)
    if not (ctx and ctx.charId) then return {} end   -- for nobody yet: blank
    return { phoneNumber = NewNumber(), owner = ctx.charId }
end, { forBuyer = true })
Returns: true, or false, reason: refused when another resource registered a generator for that item
RegisterItem(key, definition)SERVER

Register a new item definition at runtime. Adds to Config.Items. The key belongs to your resource: another running resource cannot redefine it (false, reason). Returns true or false, reason.

Items are NOT removed when your resource stops, on purpose: players are still carrying them, and an inventory full of items whip no longer recognises would be worse than a definition left behind. Once your resource has stopped, though, the keys are no longer yours, and another resource may take them over. Register them in Whip.register; the same definition again changes nothing.
ParamTypeDescription
keystringUnique item key: letters, digits, _ and - only, 50 characters at most (the database column's width). No colon, unlike container, door and event names, an item key is not res:name; prefix it with an underscore instead ('mypd_evidence')
definitiontableItem definition: see schema
Whip.register(function()
    exports.whip_core:RegisterItem('mypd_evidence_bag', {
        name   = 'Evidence Bag',
        desc   = 'Sealed forensic evidence',
        weight = 0.2,
        type   = 'police',
    })
end)
-- Its icon: html/img/items/mypd_evidence_bag.png (named after the key) in YOUR resource, plus
-- files { 'html/img/items/*.png' } in your fxmanifest (see Item icons)
GetItemSetting(item, key) · OnItemSettingChanged(item, key, fn)SERVER CLIENT

One of an item's own settings (its definition's settings) as it is in force: what an admin saved on the Items page, or its default. On the server, 'name', 'desc' and 'weight' answer the item's own too. nil for an item or key it does not have, and on a player's game until whip_core has sent the values.

OnItemSettingChanged runs fn(value, old, item, key) after one changes on that side, Reset included (on a player's game, also when the values first arrive). One per resource for each setting: calling it again replaces it, so a Whip.register that runs again does not stack them. It goes when your resource stops. Answers true, or false, reason.

ParamTypeDescription
itemstringThe item's key
keystringThe setting's key
fnfunctionfunction(value, old, item, key)

See Item settings.

GetPockets()SERVER

The pockets a character carries on their person, in fallback order: currently { 'player', 'accessory' }. Returns a copy, so mutating it changes nothing.

Returns: string[]

Read it inside Whip.register, so it is read again each time whip_core starts: it does not change while whip_core runs, but Config.AccessoryStrip adds or takes away the accessory pocket at whip_core's next start. A list kept from your resource's own start goes stale then (whip_gunny refills its list in place in its first Whip.register, before its callbacks register again). Its use is anything that lists or walks the pockets. To take one slot of them from a client, use the 'slot' param type instead: it checks the pocket, the range and what is in the slot before your handler runs.

-- Ask, don't type. Read once, reuse everywhere.
local POCKETS = exports.whip_core:GetPockets()
for _, pocket in ipairs(POCKETS) do
    -- ... StoreRead({ kind = 'player', id = source, sub = pocket })
end

-- A slot the client names: not a hand-built address — the 'slot' type (inside Whip.register)
exports.whip_core:SecureEvent('my_resource:server:stash', {
    params = { {'what', 'slot'} },   -- { sub = 'accessory', slot = 3 } or a bare slot number
}, function(source, player, what)
    -- what.addr is a slot in their own pockets that holds something; what.item says what
end)
GetPocketSlots(pocket)SERVER

How many slots one of the player's pockets has: 'player' or 'accessory'. Called with no argument, returns the whole table.

ParamTypeDescription
pocketstring|nil'player', 'accessory', or omit for all
Returns: number | table
GetPocketMaxWeight(pocket)SERVER

The weight limit of one of the player's pockets. Same contract as GetPocketSlots: omit the argument to get the whole table. The pockets are one weight: 'player''s limit is everything carried, the strip included, and 'accessory''s is the strip on its own, inside it.

ParamTypeDescription
pocketstring|nil'player', 'accessory', or omit for all
Returns: number | table
RegisterAccessorySlot(def)SERVER

Reshape one slot of the inventory's accessory strip from a satellite: label, icon, and what it accepts. The registration broadcasts to every connected client, rides the login sync for late joiners, and unwinds automatically when your resource stops (config-seeded slots re-seed). The accepts rule is enforced server-side in the move validator, not just drawn in the UI.

Who may reshape a slot. whip's own five slots (AccessoryStripSlots in shared/inventory_shape.lua) are defaults: any resource may replace one, and it comes back when that resource stops. A slot another resource has registered is theirs: yours is refused with their name. On a server with Config.AccessoryStrip off there is no strip, and every registration is refused.

FieldTypeDescription
def.slotnumberRequired. Whole number, 1..Config.ContainerSlots.accessory
def.acceptsstring|nilItem key this slot is restricted to (nil = anything)
def.labelstring|nilShown under the slot: default 'Accessory'
def.iconstring|nilA built-in icon: 'accessory' (a pouch), 'plus', 'phone', 'vehicle_key' or 'cash'. Left out, the slot shows what it takes: the built-in icon of that name, or the item's own picture greyed, and a slot that takes anything shows the pouch. whip's own five slots show the pouch and take any item; while whip_phone runs it gives slot 1 the phone icon, since that is where it looks for a phone first, and slot 1 still takes anything.
def.iconSvgstring|nilInline SVG markup: wins over icon. Developer-authored, so it passes the decode boundary; never build it from player input.
def.tagstring|nilA run tag ('run:42'): ReleaseTag(tag) puts whip's own slot back, for a slot that should last only as long as one run of something. A released tag stays closed, so use a new one each run.
Returns: bool ok, string|nil err
-- In Whip.register, NOT file scope: it runs again after a core restart, which is
-- exactly when the registry's state has died.
Whip.register(function()
    local ok, err = exports.whip_core:RegisterAccessorySlot({
        slot = 4, accepts = 'bandage', label = 'Medkit',
    })
    if not ok then print('medkit slot refused: ' .. err) end
end)
Check the return value. A bad slot number, or a slot another resource holds, is refused with (false, reason), not an error: a silent fire-and-forget call that was refused just leaves the strip unchanged and you hunting a ghost.
GetAccessorySlots()SERVER

What the accessory strip looks like right now, keyed by slot number: the read side of RegisterAccessorySlot.

-- Which accessory slots take anything, rather than one item?
for slot, def in pairs(exports.whip_core:GetAccessorySlots()) do
    if def.accepts == nil then print(('slot %d (%s) takes anything'):format(slot, def.label)) end
end
Returns: table: { [slot] = { slot, accepts, label, icon } }. A copy; assigning into it changes nothing
RegisterIgnitionKey(itemName)SERVER

Declare an item as an ignition key. The ignition slot's acceptance, the "has a key in the ignition" checks, and the key sweeps all consume this one registry: server-enforced, broadcast live, unwound on your resource's stop. A registered key still follows the vehicle-key rule: its metadata.vehicleId must match the vehicle.

ParamTypeDescription
itemNamestringRegistered item key
Returns: bool ok, string|nil err
Shared by everyone who registers it. Two resources can both declare the same item a key; it stays a key until the last of them stops.
Whip.register(function()
    exports.whip_core:RegisterIgnitionKey('skeleton_key')
end)
BlockHands(source, id, opts) / UnblockHands(source, id)SERVER

The client's BlockHands, set from the server for one player: jail, an arrest, a mission. It is sent to their game, which empties the hands and refuses there, and kept here, so a server check can ask AreHandsBlocked(source, what) (whip_gunny refuses a draw). Gone at their logout or a drop, or when your resource stops.

ParamTypeDescription
sourcenumber | { charId }The player, online
idstringYour name for this block
optstable?As the client's: label, only = 'weapons'
exports.whip_core:BlockHands(target, 'cuffed', { label = 'You are handcuffed' })
-- ... and when the cuffs come off
exports.whip_core:UnblockHands(target, 'cuffed')
Returns: true, or false, reason (no such player online, a bad id or opts)
AreHandsBlocked(source, what) / FreeHands(source)SERVER

AreHandsBlocked: are this player's hands blocked by the server ('weapon', or nothing for anything in them)? A block their game set for itself is that game's to keep. FreeHands: have their game empty the hands now, the client's FreeHands moment (a gun holstered, a nozzle dropped), without blocking them.

local blocked, why = exports.whip_core:AreHandsBlocked(source, 'weapon')
if blocked then return false, why end

exports.whip_core:FreeHands(source)   -- the guard took their gun off them
Returns: AreHandsBlocked: true, words or false. FreeHands: true once asked, or false, reason (not online)
Building a whole custom inventory UI? The renderer seam (Config.InventoryRenderer) lets a resource replace the entire inventory drawing layer while whip keeps running the state machine: your UI needs one function, render(), and every move is one call. Build it in Chrome with sample items and no game (node whip_core/dev/inventory-preview/preview.js my_inventory_ui, which reloads when you save), then try it in game with /whip_inventory_ui my_inventory_ui (developer mode). The contract lives in whip_core/docs/nui-inventory.md.

Inventory (Client)

IsInventoryOpen()CLIENT

Check if the inventory UI is currently open.

Returns: bool
Is the player busy? IsInventoryOpen answers only about the plain inventory. For "may the player start something else", ask IsAnyUIOpen; for a hotkey, IsGameInputFree. Both are under Screens, input and controls.
RegisterClientHook(hookName, handler)CLIENT

Run your own code at a named moment inside whip_core's client inventory flow. A handler may return a delay in milliseconds; whip_core waits for the longest delay any handler asked for before carrying on.

ParamTypeDescription
hookNamestring'beforeGiveMode' (the player starts give mode), 'beforePlaceMode' (they start placing an item or an emote) or 'freeHands' (something is about to use the player's hands, the phone coming out, any resource's FreeHands: put away what you hold, as whip_gunny holsters)
handlerfunctionMay return a delay in ms
idstring?Only to hold two handlers on one hook; the same id again replaces
Whip.register(function()
    exports.whip_core:RegisterClientHook('beforeGiveMode', function()
        if MyWeaponEquipped() then   -- your own state
            Holster()                -- your own animation
            return 200               -- whip waits 200 ms for it
        end
    end)
end)
Returns: true, or false, reason: no handler, or a hook name that is not one of the three (also said in F8, with the three)
SetGiveModeStyle(style)CLIENT

How a player moves while they hold an item out to give it (give mode): their walk, and how fast they may go. Applied when give mode starts and taken off when it ends, and the player's own walk comes back. The server's own is Config.GiveModeStyle (the Trash walk, no faster than a jog); a resource's wins while it runs. An item with playerWalk on keeps the player's own walk, at the same speed.

ParamTypeDescription
styletable|nilwalk: a /walk name ('trash') or a clipset; speed: 'jog' (no sprint) or 'walk' (no running). nil clears yours
Whip.register(function()
    exports.whip_core:SetGiveModeStyle({ walk = 'trash', speed = 'jog' })
end)
Returns: true, or false, reason. Keyed by your resource: the latest a resource set wins, and yours goes when your resource stops
FreeHands()CLIENT

Your resource is about to put something in the player's hands: a phone, a tool, a box. Whatever holds them puts it away first: whip runs the 'freeHands' moment (RegisterClientHook), whip_gunny holsters the gun with its animation, and whip waits for it. whip_phone asks this as the phone comes out. It waits: call it from a thread, through Whip.call. While the hands are blocked (BlockHands, below) it answers false and the block's words.

local free, why = Whip.call('FreeHands')
if not free then return end   -- still armed, or the hands are blocked (why says by what)
Whip.call('PlayEmote', 'clipboard')
Returns: true when the hands are free after it (no weapon in them), false when a weapon still is, or false, words while they are blocked
BlockHands(id, opts) / UnblockHands(id)CLIENT

The player's hands may not be used for now, with the words they are shown: everything (tied up, a cutscene), or weapons only (a hospital, a police station). A block of everything empties the hands at once (the 'freeHands' moment), and FreeHands answers false and its words while it lasts, so the phone, a tool or give mode will not start. Every block puts a drawn gun away and stops a draw: whip_gunny asks AreHandsBlocked('weapon'). Keyed by your resource; yours go when it stops. A block the server set for this player is BlockHands(source, id, opts) on the server.

ParamTypeDescription
idstringYour name for this block; the same id again replaces it
optstable?label: the words the player is shown; only = 'weapons': weapons only. None: everything
AddEventHandler('whip_core:zone:entered', function(e)
    if e.key == 'pillbox' then
        exports.whip_core:BlockHands('pillbox', { only = 'weapons', label = 'No weapons in the hospital' })
    end
end)
AddEventHandler('whip_core:zone:exited', function(e)
    if e.key == 'pillbox' then exports.whip_core:UnblockHands('pillbox') end
end)
Returns: true, or false, reason (no id, only not 'weapons', a label that is not text; UnblockHands: none of yours by that id)
AreHandsBlocked(what)CLIENT

Are the player's hands blocked, this game's blocks and the server's? 'weapon' asks about drawing one (every block stops that); nothing asks about anything in the hands (only a block of everything). Ask it before your resource puts something in the hands without FreeHands; listen for whip_core:hands:blocked to put away what you already hold.

local blocked, why = exports.whip_core:AreHandsBlocked('weapon')
if blocked then exports.whip_core:Notify(why, 'error') return end
Returns: true, words, or false
CloseInventory() CLIENT

Force-close the inventory UI, including any open containers, vehicle storage, or external panels.

-- Force close everything
exports.whip_core:CloseInventory()
HasItem(itemKey, [filter])CLIENT

Check if the player has an item in their inventory. Scans player and accessory containers. No registration needed: just call it.

-- Simple check
if exports.whip_core:HasItem('lockpick') then
    print('Player has a lockpick')
end

-- With metadata filter
local hasGoldPick = exports.whip_core:HasItem('lockpick', function(meta)
    return meta and meta.tier == 'gold'
end)
ParamTypeDescription
itemKeystringThe item key to search for
filterfunction | number | nilOptional: function(metadata) → bool, or a number: at least that many (HasItem('bandage', 3))
Returns: bool
GetItemCount(itemKey, [filter])CLIENT

Count how many of an item the player has across all containers. Returns total amount (respects stack sizes).

local cashAmount = exports.whip_core:GetItemCount('cash')
print('Player has $' .. cashAmount)

-- With filter: only the keys for one car
local keys = exports.whip_core:GetItemCount('vehicle_key', function(meta)
    return meta and meta.vehicleId == vehicleId
end)
ParamTypeDescription
itemKeystringThe item key to count
filterfunction | nilOptional: function(metadata) → bool. A number here is ignored: counting has no minimum; HasItem(item, 5) is the "at least 5" question
Returns: number: total amount (0 if none found)
GetInventory()CLIENT

The player's whole inventory, client-side, for drawing your own UI. Returns a deep copy: { [container] = { [slot] = { item, amount, metadata } } }, or {}, 'Player not loaded' before the first sync (the server export's answer).

-- Empty before the first sync, so the loop simply draws nothing
for container, slots in pairs(exports.whip_core:GetInventory()) do
    for slot, data in pairs(slots) do
        print(container, slot, data.item, data.amount)
    end
end
Returns: table: a deep copy; {}, 'Player not loaded' before the first sync

Replacing the inventory UI

A different look or a whole different screen is the renderer seat (Config.InventoryRenderer, contract in whip_core/docs/nui-inventory.md): your resource draws the inventory, whip keeps running it, and every move goes through the same checks as whip's own screen. Nothing in whip_core needs editing, so it survives every update.

Config.EnableInventoryUI = false is only for a server that wants no inventory screen at all. This export is read-only: the table you get back is a copy, and editing it changes nothing.

Item Flags (Client)

Flags that say whether the player carries particular items, kept up to date on every inventory change. Use them in an action's canInteract to gate options by item ownership, without editing whip_core. (For a plain "carries one", require = { item = ... } on the action does it for you.)

RegisterItemFlag(flagName, [itemOrFilter], [filter])CLIENT

Register a flag that tracks whether the player has a specific item. Scans player and accessory containers. Supports optional metadata filters.

Simple: track any item by name

-- Does the player have a crowbar anywhere in their inventory?
exports.whip_core:RegisterItemFlag('crowbar')

With metadata filter: only count items that match

-- Does the player have a crowbar with durability > 0?
exports.whip_core:RegisterItemFlag('crowbar', function(meta)
    return not meta or (meta.durability or 100) > 0
end)

Named flag: different flag name than item key

-- "my_valet_key" flag, but it actually checks for a vehicle_key
-- with a specific plate in its metadata
exports.whip_core:RegisterItemFlag('my_valet_key', 'vehicle_key', function(meta)
    return meta and meta.plate == 'ABC123'
end)
ParamTypeDescription
flagNamestringUnique name for this flag (often same as the item key)
itemOrFilterstring | function | nilItem key if different from flagName, OR a metadata filter function
filterfunction | nilMetadata filter: function(metadata) → bool. Only used when itemOrFilter is a string.
Returns: true, or false, reason: a name that is not a string, or a flag name another resource holds (whip_core's own lockpick included). Flags are named per resource, so pick one that is yours.
Your flags are yours. They go when your resource stops, and a filter that errors counts as "no" for that item and is reported once in the F8 console. Register them in Whip.register; the same flag again changes nothing.
HasItemFlag(flagName)CLIENT

Instant boolean check: does the player currently have the registered item? Updated automatically on every inventory change.

if exports.whip_core:HasItemFlag('lockpick') then
    print('Player has a lockpick!')
end
ParamTypeDescription
flagNamestringThe flag name you registered
Returns: bool

Full Example: an option only for players carrying something

For a plain "has at least one", require = { item = 'crowbar' } on the action is enough. An item flag earns its keep when the rule is about metadata (a charged battery, a key for this car): it is checked from a cache, not a scan of the inventory each frame.

-- client.lua in your resource (fxmanifest.lua includes '@whip_core/lib/satellite.lua')

Whip.register(function()
    -- 1. Register YOUR flag. (Not 'lockpick': that one is whip_core's, and a flag
    --    another resource holds is refused.)
    exports.whip_core:RegisterItemFlag('my_crowbar', 'crowbar')

    -- 2. A choice on a locked car's driver door, for people with one
    exports.whip_core:AddAction({
        id          = 'crowbar',   -- an id, so a re-run replaces instead of adding a second
        at          = { vehiclePart = 'door_dside_f' },
        label       = 'Pry Open',
        canInteract = function(ctx)
            return exports.whip_core:HasItemFlag('my_crowbar')
                and GetVehicleDoorLockStatus(ctx.entity) == 2
        end,
        onSelect    = function(ctx)
            TriggerServerEvent('my_resource:pry', VehToNet(ctx.entity))
        end,
    })
end)

-- 3. Nothing to clean up: whip removes your flag and your action when your resource stops.

Item Definition Schema

Used with RegisterItem(key, definition), and for the built-in items in Config.Items. name and weight are required; everything else is optional.

FieldTypeRequiredDescription
namestringYesDisplay name shown in NUI
descstringNoTooltip description
weightnumberYesWeight per unit in kg
typestringNoCategory label for tooltip ('consumable', 'weapon', 'tool', etc.)
stackbooleanNoWhether the item can stack in one slot
maxStacknumberNoMaximum units per stack. Not stackable: always 1 (RegisterItem refuses stack = false with a larger one). Stackable with none given: 100
usablebooleanNoCan be used via hotbar / right-click
cooldownnumberNoSeconds between uses (0 = no cooldown)
propstringNoGTA prop model for ground drops
grabstringNoHow it is picked up off the ground: '1h' (the default, one hand) or '2h' (both hands: a rifle, a duffel bag). Also in /whip → Economy → Items → Edit hand position ("Picked up with both hands")
playerWalkbooleanNoHeld out to give or throw, the player keeps their own walk instead of the give walk (Config.GiveModeStyle, the trash-bag walk). Default false. Also in /whip → Economy → Items → Edit hand position ("Allow player walk animation")
metaFieldstable[]NoRows on the item's card, read from its metadata: { { key='plate', label='Plate' } }. A field with a value shows that text when the item has no key of its own: { key='caliber', label='Ammo Type', value='5.56x45' }
fuelCapacitynumberNoMakes the item a fuel can: how much of a car's tank a full one holds, in the tank's units (a tank is 100, so 30 is 30%). Its metadata fuel is how full the can is, 0-100. Read by whip_fuel: with one in hand (as GTA's petrol can) a pump offers "Fill Jerry Can", priced per unit like a car, and a car's doors offer "Refuel (jerry can)". Both act on the can the player holds (SetHeldItem), never another in their pockets. whip_gunny's jerry_can is one
defaultActionstringNoContext menu action key (for items that open panels, etc.)
contextOptionstable[]NoAdditional right-click options: { { action='open', label='Open', order=1 } }. They go at the top of the menu, under Use, lowest order first (without one, as listed, after those with one); Give, Place, Split and Destroy go below. when (the item's metadata) and require (the player) make one show only some of the time: see options that come and go. An icon field is ignored: the menu shows words only. Options show only while the player carries the item, unless one has anywhere = true (options outside the pockets).
groundOptionstable[]NoUp to three more choices on a pile's 3D prompt, after Pick up: { { action='my_guns:equip', label='Equip', icon? } }, each naming one of the item's own options (a contextOptions action or its defaultAction). Chosen, the item is picked up as Pick up does, then that option runs on the slot it landed in. See options on the ground
imagestable[]NoOther pictures for other states, the first match wins: { { when = { slots = { empty = false } }, image = 'html/img/items/bag_full.webp' } }. {field} in a path is filled from metadata, {make} is a car's maker. An admin can change them on /whip → Economy → Items. See pictures that change.
pictureFieldstable[]NoMetadata an admin can show a picture by on /whip → Economy → Items: { { key='mustard', label='Mustard', type='bool' } }, type 'bool', 'number' or 'text' (the default). See pictures that change.
imagestringNoThe icon, as a path inside YOUR resource, when it is not html/img/items/<key>.webp or .png, e.g. 'html/img/items/wrench.webp'. An item you register for another resource takes its icon from that one with '@resource/path' (whip_gunny does this for a weapon pack's guns). See Item icons
settingstable[]NoSettings of this item's own that an admin can change on the Items page, each a RegisterSettings entry (int, number, bool, string or enum): { { key='capacity', type='int', min=1, max=100, default=12, label='Rounds it holds' } }. Read with GetItemSetting. See Item settings
Whip.register(function()
    exports.whip_core:RegisterItem('myems_medkit', {
        name     = 'Medical Kit',        -- Display name in tooltip
        desc     = 'Heals injuries',     -- Tooltip description
        weight   = 0.5,                  -- Weight in kg per unit
        type     = 'medical',            -- Category label
        stack    = true,                 -- Can this item stack?
        maxStack = 5,                    -- Max per slot
        usable   = true,                 -- Appears in hotbar / Use option
        cooldown = 10,                   -- Seconds between uses
        prop     = 'prop_ld_health_pack',          -- (optional) World prop model
        image    = 'html/img/items/medkit.png',    -- (optional) icon path in YOUR resource; left out: html/img/items/myems_medkit.png
    })
end)

Item lookups

Read item definitions, on the server and the client.

GetItemDef(key)SERVER CLIENT

Get an item's definition by key.

ParamTypeDescription
keystringItem key (e.g. 'food')
local def = exports.whip_core:GetItemDef('lockpick')
if def then print(def.name, def.weight) end
Returns: table|nil: see Item Definition
GetAllItemDefs()SERVER CLIENT

Get all item definitions.

Returns: table: { [key] = definition }

Player Inventory Inspection (Server)

Open another player's inventory as a secondary panel. Full read/write access: drag items between your inventory and theirs. Works with online players (live cache) and offline players (loaded from database). Designed as the foundation for admin tools and robbery systems.

OpenPlayerInventory(source, target, opts)SERVER

Open a target player's inventory alongside your own. The target's inventory appears as a secondary panel with their player and accessory slots. Items can be dragged between both inventories. If the target is online, their inventory is locked while you're viewing it. If offline, inventory is loaded from the database and saved on close.

ParamTypeDescription
sourcenumberServer player ID (the viewer)
targetnumber|tableWhose pockets: a person, either their server id or { charId = n } (offline too)
optstable|nil{ range? }: how many metres the viewer must stay within of an online target (default 5). range = false is no limit, for an admin tool.
Returns: true, or false, reason (the viewer is not loaded, no such character, someone else already has it open, they are too far away, …)
Held to where it was opened. With a range (the default), every move is refused once the viewer is out of it, and the session closes itself when they walk away, when the target leaves, or after five minutes. Without one, only the viewer closing it (or ClosePlayerInventory) ends it, and the target cannot open their own inventory until then.
-- Admin inspect, from anywhere
exports.whip_core:OpenPlayerInventory(adminSource, { charId = targetCharId }, { range = false })

-- Robbery system: the victim is a player standing there, so their server id
exports.whip_core:OpenPlayerInventory(robberSource, victimSource)
ClosePlayerInventory(source)SERVER

Close a player inventory inspection session. Unlocks the target's inventory (if online), saves both inventories.

ParamTypeDescription
sourcenumberServer player ID (the viewer)
-- The robbery was interrupted: shut the robber's view of the victim's pockets
exports.whip_core:ClosePlayerInventory(robberSource)
Returns: true, or false, reason (not loaded, or no player inventory open)
IsCharacterBeingInspected(charId)SERVER

Check if a character's inventory is currently being inspected by another player (an admin, a robbery). It does not answer whether the player has their own inventory screen open.

ParamTypeDescription
charIdnumberCharacter ID to check
if exports.whip_core:IsCharacterBeingInspected(player.charId) then
    return false, 'Not while someone is going through your pockets'
end
Returns: boolean

Ground Items

Drop & Throw

Drop: drag from the inventory to the Ground panel: the item leaves the pockets and lands in front of the player. Throw: in give mode, aim and release: the item becomes a ground item the moment it leaves the hand, anyone in reach can grab it out of the air, and it settles where it comes to rest. Either way the pockets lose the item only as the ground item is made, so nothing is lost or copied.

Pickup

Two methods: E-key quick pickup (via Interactions system, auto-places in best slot) or drag from Ground panel to inventory slot. If two players grab the same item at once, one gets it.

Proximity Sync

Ground items reach only the players near them: the world is cut into Config.GroundItemCellSize (50 m) cells, and each player is sent the items in the cells around them as they move: creations, changes and pickups alike.

Client Streaming

Each player's game draws the props for items within Config.GroundItemStreamRange and removes them as they leave it.

From your resource

-- Server: leave loot on the ground
local pile, err = exports.whip_core:CreateGroundItem({
    item   = 'drink',
    amount = 2,
    coords = vector3(200.0, -900.0, 30.0),
})
if not pile then print('drop failed: ' .. err) end

Ground Items

CreateGroundItem({ item, amount, coords, metadata, heading })SERVER

Spawn a ground item in the world. Automatically syncs to nearby clients.

local row, err = exports.whip_core:CreateGroundItem({
    item   = 'drink',
    amount = 2,
    coords = vector3(x, y, z),
})
if not row then return false, err end
print('dropped as ground item', row.id)
FieldTypeDescription
itemstringA registered item key
amountnumber?A whole number, 1 or more (default 1)
coordsvector3|vector4World position (a vector4's w is the heading)
metadatatable?Custom metadata
headingnumber?Rotation in degrees
reasonstring?For the activity log, beside your resource's name
Returns: table: { id, item, amount, metadata, x, y, z, heading, createdAt }, or false, reason (not a table, an unknown item, a bad amount, no coordinates)
DeleteGroundItem(id)SERVER

Remove a ground item from the world.

ParamTypeDescription
idnumberGround item ID
local ok, err = exports.whip_core:DeleteGroundItem(row.id)   -- the id CreateGroundItem answered
if not ok then print(err) end
Returns: bool, string|nil
GetGroundItemsNearby(x, y, z, range)SERVER

Find all ground items within a 3D radius.

ParamTypeDescription
x, y, znumberCenter position, or pass a vector3 as the first argument and the range second
rangenumber?Radius in metres (default 10)
