-- A street sweeper: clear everything within 5 m of a spot
for _, row in ipairs(exports.whip_core:GetGroundItemsNearby(vector3(x, y, z), 5.0)) do
    exports.whip_core:DeleteGroundItem(row.id)
end
Returns: table[]: { id, item, amount, metadata, x, y, z, heading, ... } rows
GetGroundItem(id)SERVER

One ground item by its id: { id, item, amount, metadata, x, y, z, heading, ... }, or nil once it is gone (picked up or deleted).

Returns: table|nil

Containers

Opening one

A stash's prop appears when a player is within 100 m, with an E prompt. The server checks the stash isn't locked, that this player may open it (Access Control, below), and that they stand within 4.5 m. It opens beside their inventory, in place of the Ground panel. Several players can have one stash open at once, and they all see the same contents.

From your own resource, the same open is OpenStore(source, { kind = 'container', id = containerId }, opts), and CloseStore takes it away again. What a stash holds is StoreRead({ kind = 'container', id = containerId }): nobody needs to have it open.

-- Server, in Whip.register: a stash your resource always has, found again on every start.
-- Staff only, and only while on duty — leave requirements out and ANYONE can open it.
local locker, why = exports.whip_core:EnsureContainer('myjob:locker', {
    name = 'Staff Locker', slots = 30, maxWeight = 150.0,
    x = 452.0, y = -980.0, z = 30.7, heading = 90.0,
    requirements = { jobs = 'myjob', onDuty = true },
})
if not locker then print('locker: ' .. why) end

Access Control

FieldEffect
locked = trueNobody can open (except admin override)
accessCharId = charIdOnly that character can open
requirements = { jobs = 'police', onDuty = true }Who may open it: any one of jobs (with onDuty, on duty there), charIds, items (carrying a keycard), ace, or property (the owner and keyholders of that property, by id or key) lets them in. A required item can never be put into the container it opens, so nobody locks their own key inside. Held on every move, so going off duty, losing the key to the property, or the stash being locked stops the looting there. A shape it would not take is refused with the reason
none of the abovePublic: anyone can open
allowedItems = { 'item1', 'item2' }Only these items can be placed in
allowedItems = nilAll items allowed

Close & Save

On close: what changed is saved, the player leaves the viewers, and the inventory is unloaded from memory once the last viewer has gone. On disconnect: any open container is auto-saved and released.

Memory efficient: container inventories are only loaded into memory while a player has them open. Thousands of containers can exist with minimal memory cost.

Containers

A stash your resource always has? EnsureContainer, not CreateContainer. CreateContainer makes a new one every time it is called: put it in your resource's start and you get a twin (with its own, separate contents) on every restart. EnsureContainer is keyed: the first call makes it, every later call finds it.
EnsureContainer(key, data)SERVER

A container declared in code, by key: the same rule as EnsureShop and EnsureZone. A new key makes the container. Called again with the same declaration, nothing changes, so edits an admin made since then stand. Called with a changed declaration, every field you declare is applied; an allowedItems or requirements you stop declaring is cleared; and fewer slots are refused while an item sits above the new count. A key another running resource declared is refused. The job/duty rule (requirements) is declared with it; the one character it belongs to (ownerCharId, accessCharId) is not: change that with UpdateContainer.

ParamTypeDescription
keystringStable identifier: letters, digits, _ - . :, at most 100. Prefix it with your resource, e.g. 'pd:weapon_locker'
datatable{ x, y, z, heading?, name?, type?, slots?, maxWeight?, prop?, locked?, allowedItems?, requirements? }, where requirements is who may open it: { jobs?, onDuty?, charIds?, items?, ace?, property? }, any one of which lets a player in (with onDuty, on duty at that job; items = an item they carry, like a keycard, never one that can be put inside it; property = a propertyId or property key, for its owner and keyholders). Checked when they open it and on every move after. lockpick is a door's and is refused. An action's require is taken in its place when it names one rule (require = { job = 'police', onDuty = true }), and refused when it names more, as the two read several rules differently (doors: any one, against an action's all). A field a container does not read is said in the server console
-- The police armoury: officers on duty only. Without `requirements` anyone could loot it.
Whip.register(function()
    local locker, why = exports.whip_core:EnsureContainer('pd:weapon_locker', {
        name         = 'Weapon Locker',
        slots        = 30,
        maxWeight    = 200.0,
        x = 441.5, y = -982.3, z = 30.7, heading = 90.0,
        allowedItems = { gunny_pistol = true, gunny_mag_pistol = true },
        requirements = { jobs = 'police', onDuty = true },
    })
    if not locker then print('weapon locker: ' .. why) end
end)
Returns: table: the container, with containerId and key, or false, reason. The declaration is kept in its declared field. Called while whip_core is still starting, it waits for it (up to 60 s), and after that answers false, 'whip_core has not finished starting …', the same for EnsureZone, EnsureDoors and EnsureJob.
GetContainerBy(kind, value)SERVER

One container, found by what you have: 'key' (the key it was declared by) or 'id'. The same pair shops and vehicles have (GetShopBy, GetVehicleBy).

local locker = exports.whip_core:GetContainerBy('key', 'pd:weapon_locker')
if locker then
    exports.whip_core:OpenStore(source, { kind = 'container', id = locker.containerId })
end
Returns: table|nil
CreateContainer(data)SERVER

Create a persistent container in the world: a new one on every call. For one your resource always has, use EnsureContainer.

-- A stash only one character can open, made when they buy it
exports.whip_core:CreateContainer({
    name         = 'Rented Locker',
    slots        = 30,
    maxWeight    = 200.0,
    accessCharId = player.charId,   -- only this character; leave it out for a public stash
    x = 441.5, y = -982.3, z = 30.7,
    heading      = 90.0,
    prop         = 'prop_cs_cardbox_01',
    allowedItems = { gunny_pistol = true, gunny_mag_pistol = true },
})
A job stash takes requirements: requirements = { jobs = 'police', onDuty = true }; a house stash, requirements = { property = 'pinklady_flat' }; a keycard locker, requirements = { items = 'locker_card' }. See EnsureContainer.

One that is never saved, for a job or a heist: persist = false. It is your resource's, has no row, and goes when your resource stops or when its tag is released (ReleaseTag): the screens it is open on shut, and what was left in it is written down as lost. It takes items (what it holds from the start, all or nothing), prop = false (no prop: only its prompt, for a room with its own safe) and placed = true with rx/ry (exactly there, no snap to the ground). Only you can change or delete it.

-- The vault's safe: never saved, gone with the job, the money already inside
local safe = exports.whip_core:CreateContainer({
    persist = false, tag = 'heist:' .. jobId, name = 'Safe',
    x = 255.1, y = 225.4, z = 101.9, prop = false,
    items = { { item = 'cash', amount = 5000 } },
    requirements = { charIds = crewCharIds },   -- only the crew
})
Returns: table: container def with containerId, or false, reason (no x/y/z, a key already taken, a requirements shape it would not take (a lockpick rule, a property that does not exist), an item that cannot go in, a run whose tag has ended, a database error)
DeleteContainer(containerId)SERVER

Delete a container and its inventory. Refused while a shop sells from it.

ParamTypeDescription
containerIdnumberContainer ID
local ok, err = exports.whip_core:DeleteContainer(containerId)
if not ok then print(err) end
Returns: true, or false, reason
GetContainerDef(containerId)SERVER

What a container is: its name, size, position and owner, from cache. What it holds is StoreRead({ kind = 'container', id = containerId }).

ParamTypeDescription
containerIdnumberContainer ID
Returns: table|nil
A stash is a store. What is in it, putting items in and taking them out, and opening it on a player's screen all go through the store calls with the address { kind = 'container', id = containerId }:
• what it holds: StoreRead (.items, keyed by slot number), StoreCount;
• put in or take out: StoreGive, StoreTake, StoreMove;
• open it for a player, or take it away: OpenStore, CloseStore.
None of them need anyone to have it open: a stash nobody has touched since the restart is loaded for you.
UpdateContainer(containerId, data)SERVER

Change a container's definition after it has been created. Only the fields present in data are touched; everything else is left alone. Writes through to the database and re-syncs the definition to clients.

ParamTypeDescription
containerIdnumberContainer ID
datatableAny of name, type, slots, maxWeight, ownerCharId, accessCharId, locked, x, y, z, heading, prop, allowedItems, requirements, key. Fewer slots are refused while an item sits above the new count. key gives an existing container a key (so EnsureContainer finds it); false takes it away. requirements is who may open it ({ jobs, onDuty, charIds, items, ace, property }, see EnsureContainer); false clears it
Players who already have it open are held to the change. Lock it, hand it to someone else or give it a job requirement, and anyone looting it at that moment is refused on their next move, not only on their next open.
-- Hand a stash over to whoever just used the key
exports.whip_core:UpdateContainer(containerId, {
    accessCharId = player.charId,
    locked       = false,
})
accessCharId is the interesting one. It is what makes a container private to a single character, and this export is the only way to change it after creation: which is what a tradeable key, a transferred stash or a job handover needs. Pass 0 to clear it and make the container public again. (Leaving it out, or nil, which in a Lua table is the same thing, leaves it as it is.)
Returns: true, or false, reason: the container does not exist, a slot above a smaller slots still holds something, the key is another container's, or the write failed

Store Kinds

A store is anything items can sit in: pockets, an accessory slot, a stash, a car boot, a crafting panel. Each kind declares how it is read, written, how durable it is, and what happens around a move. Everything else (weight, stacking, metadata merging, the transaction, the client sync) is one shared implementation you inherit by declaring a kind.

RegisterStoreKind(kindId, kindDef)SERVER

Declare a new kind of store from your own resource. Call once per kind, never per instance. The kind name is yours once registered (the registration rule): whip's own kind names are reserved, another resource's kind is refused, and registering yours again swaps the definition in quietly.

Your handle must carry an ID, never a live table. resolve runs in your resource and its return value crosses the export boundary back into whip_core, so FiveM copies it. A handle built as { id = id, rows = myStorage[id] } hands whip_core a copy of rows; when whip_core later calls set(handle, …) the handle is copied again on the way in, and your write lands in a copy of a copy.

It fails silently, and it loses items: the move reports success, the item leaves the player, and nothing ever arrives in your storage.

Return { id = id } and have get, set and clear look your own storage up from that id. Those three run inside your resource, where your tables are real: 
resolve = function(key) return myStorage[key.id] and { id = key.id } or nil end,
get     = function(h, slot) return myStorage[h.id].slots[slot] end,
set     = function(h, slot, item, amount, metadata)
    myStorage[h.id].slots[slot] = { item = item, amount = amount, metadata = metadata }
    return true
end,
local lockers = { [3] = { slots = {} } }   -- yours, in memory; save it from persist

Whip.register(function()
    exports.whip_core:RegisterStoreKind('my_locker', {
        resolve    = function(key) return lockers[key.id] and { id = key.id } or nil end,
        instanceId = function(key, h) return 'my_locker:' .. h.id end,
        slots      = function(h) return 20 end,
        maxWeight  = function(h) return 100.0 end,
        get        = function(h, slot) return lockers[h.id].slots[slot] end,
        set        = function(h, slot, item, amount, metadata)
            lockers[h.id].slots[slot] = { item = item, amount = amount, metadata = metadata }
            return true
        end,
        clear      = function(h, slot) lockers[h.id].slots[slot] = nil; return true end,
    })
end)

-- Show locker 3 beside a player's pockets
exports.whip_core:OpenStore(source, { kind = 'my_locker', id = 3 })
FunctionSignaturePurpose
resolve(key) → handle|nilRequired. Turn an instance key into something to operate on. nil means "cannot proceed", never "empty".
instanceId(key, handle) → stringRequired. Stable identity of this exact store. It must start with your kind's name and a colon ('my_safe:3' for kind my_safe) or OpenStore refuses it.
unitKey(key, handle) → stringWhat persists together. Optional: leave it out and it is the same as instanceId, which is right for almost every kind.
slots / maxWeight(handle) → numberRequired. Capacity.
get(handle, slot) → slotData|nilRequired. { item, amount, metadata }
set / clear(handle, slot, …)Required. Write and empty a slot.
authorize(src, addr) → booleanOptional. The other way to let players drag in your store, for a kind that decides "has it open" itself. Not needed while you have it open on their screen with OpenStore.
allows(handle, itemKey, metadata) → booleanOptional item filter, for the whole store.
allowsAt(handle, slot, itemKey, metadata) → boolean, reason?Optional per-slot filter: when each slot takes something different (a tool rack, a magazine slot). Checked everywhere an item lands in a slot.
persist(handle) → queries[]|nilOptional. nil means "cannot persist right now".
durability'writeThrough' | 'writeBehind'Defaults to write-through.
beforeMove / afterMove(handle, ctx)Optional veto/interception and post-commit side effect. ctx has direction, slot, otherSlot, item, amount, metadata, swap, and other, the store at the far end, as an address ({ kind, id, sub, slot, label }). A player destroying an item asks too: direction = 'out', destroyed = true, and no other.
Returns: boolean ok, string|nil err: never throws, so a malformed definition cannot kill your resource at load
Once registered, your kind works with every store call. StoreRead, StoreCount, StoreGive, StoreTake, StoreMove, GetItemAt and SetItemMetadata all take { kind = 'mykind', id = ..., sub = ... }, which is resolved with resolve({ id, sub }): always that shape, whichever path opens it.
When a player drags, id and sub come from their client. They are whatever the client sent, not sanitised for you: resolve must look them up in your own storage and answer nil for anything it does not know. And resolve, get, set and clear must not yield: no Wait, no database await. The mover relies on nothing else running between its steps: its undo after a refused write is a plain set back, which is only safe if nobody could have moved anything in the meantime. Keep your storage in memory and save it from persist.
Show it to a player with OpenStore. OpenStore(source, { kind = 'mykind', id = 3 }) puts your store in the inventory screen's right-hand grid, beside their pockets. While it is open there, that player can drag items in and out of it: held to opts.coords / opts.range if you gave them, and refused entirely if you opened it readOnly. CloseStore takes it away again.
Players cannot touch your store until you let them. Your resource can always move items in and out. A player can drag in it only while you have it open on their screen with OpenStore, or, for a kind that decides "has that vault open" itself, when your authorize function says so. whip takes only a literal true from authorize, and one that errors is treated as a refusal.
Reserved names. whip's own kinds (player, rawInventory, container, vehicle, panel) plus every client-addressable name such as target and each pocket name (player, accessory), are refused. Two resources cannot claim the same kind either; the first wins and the second gets a clear error. Your kinds are dropped automatically when your resource stops.

Is a store kind what you want?

You wantUse
A slot grid open for one session, contents owned by your resourceOpenPanel: simpler, no persistence to write
An item that contains other itemsRegisterPanelItem
Storage that persists, authorises itself and behaves like a first-class containerRegisterStoreKind

Panels (OpenPanel)

Overview

The Panel system lets external resources create custom inventory-like UI panels without building their own NUI. Panels appear alongside the player's inventory with drag-and-drop support. The server manages all state: items, weight, allowed items, and move validation. Panels are the building block for crafting stations, storage, input/output interfaces, and item-as-container patterns (wallets, toolboxes).

Two APIs

APIUse CasePersistence
OpenPanelStandalone panels (crafting stations, refineries, evidence lockers)You manage persistence: save what is left in the panel in your own state/DB from its onClose hook
RegisterPanelItemItems that contain other items (wallet, toolbox)Automatic: items are folded into the parent item's metadata as they change

OpenPanel: Standalone Panels

Open a panel for a player with full control over slots, allowed items, weight limits, and move validation. Everything (including the hooks that react to moves) goes in the one config table.

-- Open a 6-slot input panel that only accepts specific items
local ok, err = exports.whip_core:OpenPanel(source, {
    id           = 'crusher_input',     -- unique ID — its address is { kind = 'panel', id = 'crusher_input' }
    label        = 'Crusher — Input',    -- header text
    slots        = 6,                     -- number of slots
    items        = savedItems,             -- pre-populate with existing items (optional)
    allowedItems = {'old_radio', 'broken_phone'},  -- whitelist (optional)
    maxWeight    = 50,                    -- weight limit in kg (optional)
    readOnly     = false,                 -- if true, they can look but every move is refused

    -- What happens when the last person walks away (see "The three hooks" below)
    onClose = function(ctx)
        myState.savedItems = ctx.items   -- { [slot] = { item, amount, metadata } }
    end,
})
if not ok then print(err) end

Every config field is on the OpenPanel card. The three hooks are the part to understand:

The Three Hooks

A panel has three hooks, all optional, all passed in the OpenPanel config, and each is handed one table, ctx:

HookWhen it runsWhat it can do
onValidate(ctx)Before a player's move into, out of or within the panel, or a Split or Destroy on one of its slots. Nothing has changed yetReturn false, 'reason' to refuse: the player sees the reason. Anything else allows the move. A hook that errors refuses it
onChange(ctx)After a player's move (or Split, or Destroy) has landedReact to it: pay for what was put in, start a machine, update your own state. ctx.items is what the panel holds now
onClose(ctx)Once, when the last viewer leavesSave what was left. ctx is { panel, source, items }. Optional: with none, players get back what they put in, and your stock goes

ctx for onValidate and onChange:

FieldWhat it is
sourceThe player moving the item
panelThe panel's id
direction'in' (into the panel), 'out' (out of it) or 'within' (from one panel slot to another: a Split is one of these)
slotThe panel's slot
otherSlotThe slot at the other end (for 'within', the other panel slot)
otherThe store at the other end, as an address, e.g. { kind = 'player', id = source, sub = 'player', slot = 4 }. nil when the item is being destroyed
destroyedtrue when the player is destroying the item (the context menu's Destroy, offered only to a developer with developer mode on): direction is 'out' and there is no other
item, amount, metadataWhat is moving
swaponValidate only: true when this is the returning half of a swap (the item already in the slot going back the other way). Asked for a swap inside one panel too
replacingonValidate only: on the forward half of a swap, { item, amount, metadata } of what is in the slot now and will go back the other way: so a rule like "one magazine at a time" can allow a new one dropped onto the fitted one. nil when nothing is displaced
itemsonChange only: what the panel holds now, a copy keyed by slot
hostA RegisterPanelItem panel only: the item the panel belongs to (see below)
-- An output tray: the player can take things out, but not put anything in
exports.whip_core:OpenPanel(source, {
    id    = 'crusher_output',
    label = 'Crusher — Output',
    slots = 12,
    onValidate = function(ctx)
        if ctx.direction == 'in' then return false, 'This tray is output only' end
    end,
})

-- A pawn counter: whatever is dragged in is bought on the spot
local PRICES = { gold_ring = 150, old_watch = 80 }

exports.whip_core:OpenPanel(source, {
    id           = 'pawn_' .. source,
    label        = 'Sell to the pawn shop',
    slots        = 1,
    allowedItems = { 'gold_ring', 'old_watch' },
    onChange = function(ctx)
        if ctx.direction ~= 'in' then return end
        -- The item has landed in the panel. Take it out (destroying it), then pay for what was taken.
        local taken = exports.whip_core:StoreTake({ kind = 'panel', id = ctx.panel, slot = ctx.slot })
        if taken then
            -- PayPlayer: cash that will not fit their pockets lands at their feet, so the sale is never unpaid
            exports.whip_core:PayPlayer(ctx.source, PRICES[taken.item] * taken.amount, { method = 'cash', reason = 'pawn shop' })
        end
    end,
})
The hooks belong to the panel, not to one player. Several players can have the same panel id open at once (all opened by one resource), and they share one set of contents. The first OpenPanel for that id that brings any hooks sets them, and they are asked for every viewer's moves. Hooks passed by a later opener are ignored while the panel stays open. onClose runs once, when the last viewer leaves, whoever that is.
To act on an item a player drags in, do it in onChange. By then the move has really happened and is on the record, so taking the item and paying for it (as the pawn counter does) cannot pay for something that never arrived. onValidate only decides whether the move may happen.

Server-Initiated Updates

A panel is a store like any other, so your resource fills it, empties it and reads it with the ordinary store calls and its address, { kind = 'panel', id = id, slot = n }:

-- Place an item in a panel slot from the server (e.g., crafting output)
exports.whip_core:StoreGive({ kind = 'panel', id = 'crusher_output', slot = 1 }, 'steel_ingot', 4)

-- Clear a slot
exports.whip_core:StoreTake({ kind = 'panel', id = 'crusher_output', slot = 1 })

-- Read current panel contents
local panel = exports.whip_core:StoreRead({ kind = 'panel', id = 'crusher_output' })
if panel then
    for slot, it in pairs(panel.items) do print(slot, it.item, it.amount) end
end

-- Force-close a panel for this player
exports.whip_core:ClosePanel(source, 'crusher_output')
Your own writes are not asked. StoreGive and StoreTake into a panel do not call its onValidate or onChange: your resource is the one deciding. The panel's own rules still apply to them: its slot count, maxWeight, allowedItems, and one slot holding no more than the item's stack size. Every player looking at the panel sees the change.

RegisterPanelItem: Items as Containers

For items that store other items inside their metadata (wallets, toolboxes), RegisterPanelItem handles everything automatically: context action registration, metadata generation, and folding the contents back into the parent item.

Contents are saved as they change, not when the panel closes. Each change is folded into the parent item's metadata as it happens, so a wallet's contents are exactly as durable as the wallet itself: leaving the panel open indefinitely is safe.

How It Works

  1. The panel hangs off a context action: either the item's defaultAction, or one named explicitly with action in the config (below). One of the two is required.
  2. RegisterPanelItem registers for you: a metadata generator (empty storage on each new item) and the context action that opens the panel. Each change is folded back into the item's metadata as it happens
  3. Items stored inside the panel live in the parent item's metadata.slots (or a custom key): they travel with the parent item through drops, trades, containers, and storage automatically
-- server.lua (your resource). The item first: a panel registration naming an item
-- whip_core has never heard of is refused — so declare both in the same function.
Whip.register(function()
    exports.whip_core:RegisterItem('mymech_toolbox', {
        name          = 'Toolbox',
        weight        = 2.0,
        stack         = false,
        defaultAction = 'mytools:open_toolbox',   -- or name one with `action` in the registration
        contextOptions = {
            { action = 'mytools:open_toolbox', label = 'Open' },
        },
    })

    local ok, err = exports.whip_core:RegisterPanelItem('mymech_toolbox', {
        slots        = 6,
        label        = 'Toolbox',
        allowedItems = { 'wrench', 'screwdriver' },   -- a list of names; { wrench = true } works too
    })
    if not ok then print('toolbox panel: ' .. err) end
end)

That's it. Right-click the toolbox → "Open" → a 6-slot panel appears → drag tools in. Each change is written into the toolbox's metadata as it happens. Drop it, pick it up, open it: the tools are still there. whip_core's own wallet is this same declaration (server/items/wallet.lua: 3 slots, allowedItems = { 'cash', 'id_card' }).

Custom Storage Shapes: canOpen / read / onValidate / write / onChange

The toolbox above stores a plain list of slots, which is all most items need. Some items don't: a weapon's magazine is a single record {item, ammo, serial}, and a revolver's chamber is just a number. Neither is a slot array, and neither can be expressed with storageKey alone.

Five optional hooks close that gap. Leave them all out and you get the plain slot list above, so nothing you have already written changes.

HookSignatureAnswers
canOpen(host) → ok, reasonMay this open at all?
read(host) → itemsWhat does the panel show?
onValidate(ctx) → ok, reasonMay this move happen? The item is ctx.host
write(host, items) → metadataHow does a change fold back? Only build and return the metadata: whip calls it on a copy first to check each move, and refuses a move your write errors on (or returns no table for), so a bug in it blocks the move instead of losing or copying items
onChange(ctx)What else should happen? (post-commit) The item is ctx.host, the contents ctx.items

onValidate and onChange are the same two hooks an OpenPanel panel has, handed the same ctx (see The Three Hooks above), with ctx.host filled in. For onChange, ctx.host is read after the change was folded into the item.

canOpen runs before read, so an item that must stay shut never shows what is inside. Use it for anything whose answer is simply no: a locked box, a sealed crate, a case that needs a tool. A canOpen that errors keeps the item shut.

host is the item the panel belongs to: { source, container, slot, addr, item, amount, metadata }, read fresh from the inventory each time, so it stays correct even if the player moves the item while its own panel is open. addr is the item's address, ready for GetItemAt, SetItemMetadata and StoreTake.

The panel is a view, not a second place the items live. read projects the host's own metadata into slots; write folds slots back into that metadata. That is what lets a count on one side be an item stack on the other, and it is why these panels need no persistence of their own, because the host item's own storage already has it.

Worked Example: whip_gunny's magazine slot

Condensed from whip_gunny/server/magpanel.lua: the whole magazine slot, for every weapon in the resource, in one declaration.

Written inline here so it reads top to bottom. The real file also covers guns with no magazine (revolvers, pump shotguns): there read shows a plain round count, and write saves it back as a number.
exports.whip_core:RegisterPanelItem(weaponItem, {
    action = 'whip_gunny:open_weapon',   -- a named context option, not the item's use action
    slots  = 1,
    label  = weaponCfg.label .. ' Mag',

    -- What the panel shows: the weapon's magazine, rendered as one slot. The gun keeps the
    -- magazine's WHOLE metadata (its uid and the rest), so it comes out as it went in.
    read = function(host)
        local mag = host.metadata.magazine
        if not mag then return {} end
        local item, metadata = GunnyMagazineOut(mag)   -- the record without its item name
        return { [1] = { item = item, amount = 1, metadata = metadata } }
    end,

    -- The rule allowedItems cannot express: it depends on WHICH weapon, and what
    -- is already in it. The weapon is ctx.host. The reason is shown to the player.
    onValidate = function(ctx)
        local host = ctx.host
        -- Either way, not while the gun is loaded a shell at a time: the client is counting the shells.
        if GunnyLoopedReloadOpen(host.source, host.slot, host.addr.sub) then
            return false, 'Finish reloading first'
        end
        if ctx.direction ~= 'in' then return true end
        if not Config.IsMagCompatible(host.item, ctx.item) then
            return false, 'That magazine does not fit this weapon'
        end
        -- On a swap the fitted magazine is the one leaving (ctx.replacing dropping a new one onto it,
        -- ctx.swap dragging it out onto a new one), so only a SECOND one is refused.
        if host.metadata.magazine and not ctx.swap and not ctx.replacing then
            return false, 'Remove the current magazine first'
        end
        return true
    end,

    -- Fold the slot back into the weapon's own shape.
    write = function(host, items)
        local held = items[1]
        -- The magazine's whole metadata, plus its item name (server/main.lua)
        host.metadata.magazine = held and GunnyMagazineIn(held.item, held.metadata) or nil
        return host.metadata
    end,

    -- Post-commit only. Never runs speculatively, which is what makes it the right
    -- place to touch the ped: swapping the visible magazine for a move that then
    -- failed would leave the model disagreeing with the inventory.
    onChange = function(ctx)
        local mag = ctx.host.metadata.magazine
        -- The rounds changed here, not by a shot: gunny numbers the change, and a count the game sent
        -- for the old magazine is then ignored (GunnyCountChanged, server/weapons.lua).
        -- Nil when this is not the gun in the hand: then there is nothing on the ped to change.
        local version = GunnyCountChanged(ctx.host.source, ctx.host.addr, ctx.host.metadata.serial)
        if not version then return end
        if mag then
            TriggerClientEvent('whip_gunny:client:magazineInserted', ctx.host.source, ctx.host.slot, mag.ammo, version, mag.item)
        else
            TriggerClientEvent('whip_gunny:client:magazineRemoved', ctx.host.source, ctx.host.slot, version)
        end
    end,
})
Many items can share one action. whip_gunny registers every one of its guns against a single whip_gunny:open_weapon action, and whip hands the handler whichever gun was used. You do not need a separate action per item.

Full Example: Item Refinery

A complete crafting system using two panels: an input panel with item whitelist, and an output-only panel.

-- server.lua — Refinery with input + processing timer + output

local REFINERIES = { vector3(1087.2, -2002.1, 30.9) }    -- where each one stands
local RECIPES = {
    old_radio    = { output = 'copper_wire',   amount = 3 },
    broken_phone = { output = 'circuit_board', amount = 2 },
}
local state = {}                                         -- [refineryId] = { input, output, busy }

local function refinery(id)
    state[id] = state[id] or { input = {}, output = {}, busy = false }
    return state[id]
end

-- Only a refinery that exists, and only standing at it
local function at(_, _, id) return REFINERIES[id] end

Whip.register(function()
    -- INPUT: load items into the crusher
    exports.whip_core:SecureEvent('refine:openInput', {
        params = { {'refineryId', 'id', 1, #REFINERIES} },
        near   = { at = at, range = 3.0 },
    }, function(source, player, refineryId)
        local r = refinery(refineryId)
        if r.busy then return false, 'Still crushing' end

        exports.whip_core:OpenPanel(source, {
            id           = 'refine:input_' .. refineryId,
            label        = 'Crusher — Input',
            slots        = 6,
            items        = r.input,
            allowedItems = { 'old_radio', 'broken_phone' },

            -- Once, when the LAST person at the crusher walks away
            onClose = function(ctx)
                r.input = ctx.items
                if r.busy or next(ctx.items) == nil then return end
                r.busy = true
                exports.whip_core:NotifyPlayer(ctx.source, 'Crushing... 15 seconds', 'success')
                SetTimeout(15000, function()
                    for _, it in pairs(r.input) do
                        local recipe = RECIPES[it.item]
                        if recipe then
                            local slot = 1
                            while r.output[slot] do slot = slot + 1 end   -- after anything not yet collected
                            r.output[slot] = { item = recipe.output, amount = recipe.amount * it.amount }
                        end
                    end
                    r.input, r.busy = {}, false
                end)
            end,
        })
    end)

    -- OUTPUT: collect what was made (take only)
    exports.whip_core:SecureEvent('refine:openOutput', {
        params = { {'refineryId', 'id', 1, #REFINERIES} },
        near   = { at = at, range = 3.0 },
    }, function(source, player, refineryId)
        local r = refinery(refineryId)
        exports.whip_core:OpenPanel(source, {
            id    = 'refine:output_' .. refineryId,
            label = 'Crusher — Output',
            slots = 12,
            items = r.output,
            onValidate = function(ctx)
                if ctx.direction == 'in' then return false, 'This tray is output only' end
            end,
            onClose = function(ctx) r.output = ctx.items end,
        })
    end)
end)

Cleanup

Panel sessions are automatically cleaned up when a player disconnects or the resource stops. When the player who disconnects was the panel's last viewer, its onClose hook runs during that cleanup, so items are saved even on an unexpected disconnection. A panel whose hooks belong to a resource that stops loses those hooks. When nothing is left to keep what is in the panel (no onClose, your resource stopped, or whip_core stopped), each character gets back what they put in and did not take out, and your own stock goes, logged.

The exports, OpenPanel, ClosePanel and RegisterPanelItem, are under Panels (Server), below. A player can have several panels open at once, so name the one you mean when you close it.

Panels (Server)

The panel exports. How panels work, the three hooks and worked examples are in the Panels guide above.

OpenPanel(source, config)SERVER

Open a panel for a player. Auto-opens their inventory alongside the panel. The server keeps the panel's contents, checks every player move against its rules (slots, weight, allowed items, read-only), and calls the panel's hooks: onValidate before a player's move, onChange after one lands, onClose when the last viewer leaves.

ParamTypeDescription
sourcenumberServer player ID
configtablePanel configuration (see fields below)
Config FieldTypeRequiredDescription
idstring|numberYesUnique panel identifier. Its address is { kind = 'panel', id = id }. The same id opened twice by one player does nothing the second time. Ids are shared across resources, so start yours with your resource's name ('myres:bench_' .. src): while one resource has an id open, another resource opening it is refused, false, 'Panel id "…" is already open by …'
labelstringNoHeader text (default: 'Panel')
slotsnumberNoNumber of slots (default: 10, max 5 per row)
itemstableNoInitial items: { [slot] = { item, amount, metadata } }. Used only when the panel is not already open
maxWeightnumberNoWeight limit in kg (nil = unlimited)
allowedItemstableNoOnly these items: a list of names {'food','drink'} or a keyed table {food=true} (nil = any item)
readOnlybooleanNoIf true, the player can look, and every move they try is refused: rearranging included
onValidatefunctionNo(ctx) → ok, reason: before a player's move. Return false, 'reason' to refuse; anything else allows. An error refuses
onChangefunctionNo(ctx): after a player's move has landed. ctx.items is what the panel holds now
onClosefunctionNo: see the note(ctx): once, when the last viewer has left. ctx is { panel, source, items }. Give it one when the panel should keep its contents. Without one (or if it errors), each player gets back what they put in and did not take out (in their pockets, or at their feet when those are full, unless the server has turned dropping off); what your resource stocked it with, anything of a player who has left, and anything that could not be given back goes with the panel (logged as lost). A readOnly panel without one gives nothing back: what is in it just goes
A panel's contents live in memory until you take them. whip does not save an OpenPanel: when a player drags an item in, their pocket's side of the move is saved, and the panel's side exists only in the server's memory until onChange or onClose hands it to you. A crash in between loses whatever was in the panel. For anything that must survive a crash, save it in onChange, or keep it in a store that persists (RegisterStoreKind with a persist, shown with OpenStore).

ctx for onValidate and onChange holds source, panel, direction ('in' | 'out' | 'within'), slot (the panel's), otherSlot, other (the other end, as an address), item, amount, metadata, destroyed (true when the player is destroying the item, then there is no other), plus swap in onValidate and items in onChange. The Panels guide has the full table.

Returns: true, or false, reason
local ok, err = exports.whip_core:OpenPanel(source, {
    id           = 'evidence_locker',
    label        = 'Evidence Locker #7',
    slots        = 12,
    maxWeight    = 50,
    allowedItems = {'mypd_evidence_bag', 'mypd_weapon_case'},
    items        = {
        [1] = { item = 'mypd_evidence_bag', amount = 3 },
    },

    -- Before a player's move: refuse with a reason they see
    onValidate = function(ctx)
        if ctx.direction == 'in' and not IsSealed(ctx.metadata) then
            return false, 'Evidence must be bagged and sealed'
        end
    end,

    -- The last person has left: persist what is in the locker
    onClose = function(ctx)
        SaveLocker(7, ctx.items)
    end,
})
if not ok then print(err) end
The hooks belong to the panel, not to the player you opened it for. The first OpenPanel for an id that brings hooks sets them, and they are asked for every viewer's moves. Hooks passed by later openers are ignored while the panel stays open.
Your own writes are not asked. StoreGive / StoreTake into the panel ({ kind = 'panel', id = id, slot = n }) skip onValidate and onChange, your resource is the one deciding, but the panel's slots, maxWeight and allowedItems still apply. Read it with StoreRead({ kind = 'panel', id = id }).
ClosePanel(source, panelId?)SERVER

Close a panel for one player. If that player was its last viewer, the panel's onClose hook runs with what was left in it, and the panel is gone; otherwise the other viewers carry on.

ParamTypeDescription
sourcenumberServer player ID
panelIdstring|number?Which panel. Omitting it closes every panel this player has open
exports.whip_core:ClosePanel(source, 'evidence_locker')   -- its onClose runs if they were the last viewer
Returns: true, or false, 'No such panel open'
Learning a panel's id. A panel you opened yourself has the id you chose. A panel opened by a RegisterPanelItem context action does not: whip makes that id up, and its format is internal. Find it with GetOpenStores(source), which lists each open panel as { kind = 'panel', id, owner, label }, instead of rebuilding it: 
for _, open in ipairs(exports.whip_core:GetOpenStores(source)) do
    if open.kind == 'panel' and open.label == 'Wallet' then
        local wallet = exports.whip_core:StoreRead(open)   -- what is in it right now
    end
end
RegisterPanelItem(itemKey, config)SERVER

Register an item that opens a panel when used via its context action. Automatically registers the context action, metadata generator, and close handler that saves panel items back into the item's metadata. This is how wallets, toolboxes, and containers-as-items work.

Answers true or false, reason, and refuses before changing anything when: the item is not registered or has no action; another resource has already registered a panel for this item; or the action name is a context action another resource holds. The empty-slots metadata default is only added when the item has none of its own.

ParamTypeDescription
itemKeystringItem key. Must already be registered, and must have a defaultAction unless the config names an action.
configtablePanel configuration
Config FieldTypeRequiredDescription
slotsnumberNoNumber of slots (default: 3)
labelstring | functionNoPanel header text. May be (host) → string when the title depends on the item's own state: a magazine showing its round count, a case showing whose it is.
storageKeystringNoMetadata key to store items in (default: 'slots')
allowedItemstableNoOnly these items: a list of names { 'cash', 'id_card' } or a keyed table { cash = true, id_card = true }. Fixed at registration: for anything that depends on the amount or on the host item's state, use onValidate.
actionstringNoContext action that opens the panel. Defaults to the item's defaultAction. Several items may share one action.
canOpenfunctionNo(host) → ok, reason: refuse to open at all, with a reason the player sees. Runs before read, so a refused item never has its contents projected. Fails closed.
readfunctionNo(host) → items: project the host's own metadata into slots. Absent: reads metadata[storageKey].
onValidatefunctionNo(ctx) → ok, reason: veto a player's move, with a reason they see. Runs before anything is changed. The same hook OpenPanel has: ctx has source, panel, direction, slot, otherSlot, other (the far end, as an address), item, amount, metadata, swap, destroyed, and host, the item the panel belongs to
writefunctionNo(host, items) → metadata: fold the panel back into the host's own shape. Absent: writes metadata[storageKey]. It must only build and return metadata (no side effects): whip also calls it on a copy to check a move before it happens, and refuses the move if it errors or returns no table.
onChangefunctionNo(ctx): after a player's move landed. ctx.host is the item (read after the change was folded into it), ctx.items the panel's contents. Never runs speculatively.

host is { source, container, slot, addr, item, amount, metadata }, where container is the pocket the item is in and addr its address (for GetItemAt and friends).

Two things RegisterPanelItem does not take, despite OpenPanel taking them: maxWeight and readOnly. They are ignored without complaint, so a panel item declaring them behaves as though they were never written. An item panel's capacity is its slot count; for a read-only view of an item, refuse the moves in onValidate.
allowedItems is a plain list of names: a per-item maxPerSlot is not honoured. In the keyed form only the keys count, here and in OpenPanel alike. If you need a cap, enforce it in onValidate, where you can see the amount and refuse with a reason.
-- A money clip: 1 slot that holds cash, stored in the clip's own metadata
Whip.register(function()
    exports.whip_core:RegisterItem('myshop_money_clip', {
        name = 'Money Clip', weight = 0.05, stack = false,
        defaultAction  = 'myshop_open_clip',
        contextOptions = { { action = 'myshop_open_clip', label = 'Open' } },
    })

    exports.whip_core:RegisterPanelItem('myshop_money_clip', {
        slots        = 1,
        label        = 'Money Clip',
        allowedItems = { 'cash' },

        -- A cap belongs here, where the amount is visible and the refusal has a reason.
        onValidate = function(ctx)
            if ctx.direction == 'in' and ctx.amount > 5000 then
                return false, 'That will not fit in the clip.'
            end
            return true
        end,
    })
end)
Returns: true, or false, reason. See the Panels guide for the hooks and a worked example.

Vehicles & Keys

Vehicle States

StateMeaningEntity Exists?
'out'In the world, position trackedYes
'garaged'Stored in a garageNo
'impounded'Seized (admin), retrievableNo

Key & Ignition System

Vehicle keys are inventory items (vehicle_key) with metadata { vehicleId, plate, model }. Non-stackable, weight 0.1 kg.

  1. Player receives a key via GiveVehicleKey, CreateOwnedVehicle with { giveKey = true }, or SpawnTempVehicle with forSource (it gives that player a key unless giveKey = false). CreateOwnedVehicle without giveKey hands out no key. SpawnTempVehicle with keyInIgnition = true puts a key straight into the ignition instead
  2. Player takes the driver's seat → the server checks the car's 1-slot ignition storage for a key
  3. No key in ignition: engine forced off, vehicle undriveable, scroll-up shows "No key in ignition!"
  4. Key in ignition: scroll-up starts engine, scroll-down stops it
  5. Key is inserted by dragging vehicle_key from inventory to the ignition slot in the NUI
  6. Only a key whose metadata.vehicleId matches the vehicle is accepted
To stop a car's engine (an overheat, a breakdown), hold it with HoldVehicleEngine: a running engine stops, it will not start again, and the driver sees your reason until ReleaseVehicleEngine. whip otherwise keeps a running engine on while its key is in the ignition.

Locking

Toggle with the L key, or Lock / Unlock on a door's prompt. The lock is saved with the car.

ContextKey Required In
Inside vehicle (driver)Ignition OR inventory
On footInventory only

Lock range on foot: Config.VehicleLockRange (8m). Players nearby see two flashes for lock, one for unlock.

NPC Vehicle Locks

Every vehicle whip does not own stays locked, so a player has to lockpick a random NPC car rather than climbing straight in. Once lockpicked, a car becomes a whip vehicle and stays unlocked. A car only one player's game has (a resource's local car, not networked) is left as its resource made it: its door, bonnet and boot-lid prompts work on that game alone, and it has no boot storage.

Range is Config.NpcVehicleLockRange (10m); set it to 0 to switch the rule off and let anyone enter any NPC car.

Seats

Passengers stay in their seat. GTA no longer slides a passenger into an empty driver's seat, getting in at the passenger door gives the passenger seat (walking away, or F / Y again, still stops it until the player climbs in, as GTA's own does), and GTA's own shuffle button (H, D-pad right) does nothing. Config.Seats.NoAutoShuffle = false brings back GTA's own way.

Players change seat with Seats on the F1 wheel (or /seats). The wheel stays open and turns into the vehicle's seats, each Free, Occupied or You, for however many seats it has. Picking a free seat (A or a click) moves them there, sliding across to the seat beside them and straight to any other; B or a right-click goes back to the wheel. It works in any vehicle, moving or locked. The server holds a picked seat for a moment, so two players picking the same one cannot both get it.

To ask which seat a player is in, use GetPlayerSeat. To hear about changes, listen to whip_core:vehicle:entered: it fires again with the new seat when someone moves seat without getting out.

Vehicle Persistence

whip's cars stay in the world when the player near them leaves the server or drives away. After a restart, every car that was out in the world comes back where it stood; garaged cars stay in their garage.

Vehicle Storage

Each vehicle has trunk, glovebox, and ignition storage. Capacity resolves in priority order:

  1. Per-vehicle column override (if set): given when the car was made (the new-vehicle wizard's Extras, or a script)
  2. The model's (vehicle_meta): /whip → Vehicles → Vehicle Adjustments, a vehicle picked: every car of one model, unless it has its own
  3. The category's (vehicle_class_meta): Vehicle Adjustments, a category picked: every model of one GTA vehicle class (Motorcycles, SUVs, Industrial and so on), unless the model has its own
  4. Config globals (VehicleTrunkSlots, etc.)

A category or a model can also turn its trunk or its glovebox off: the vehicle then offers no View Trunk Inventory (its lid still opens), and F2 in it is the plain inventory. A model's on or off is over its category's, so one emergency truck can keep a trunk while the rest of Emergency has none.

Fewer slots, or turning one off, are refused while a car that uses them still has something in the slots that would go: empty those first.

Vehicle Registration: How It Works

whip_core tracks two kinds of vehicles:

TypeSourcePersists?vehicleId
OwnedCreated with CreateOwnedVehicle (a dealership, an admin spawn), or a street car made owned with ClaimVehicleYes (DB)DB auto-increment (1, 2, 3...)
SessionNPC/AI vehicles, registered on first interactionNo (memory only)Synthetic (1,000,000,000 and up, far above any owned car's id)

Session vehicles are registered automatically when a player interacts with any NPC vehicle: entering the driver seat, lockpicking, opening the trunk, refueling, or calling ResolveVehicle. Once registered, they get a vehicleId and all framework features work on them (trunk, glovebox, ignition, lock/unlock, fuel).

If the NPC vehicle had its engine running, a key is auto-generated in the ignition so the player can drive it immediately.

You never need to check "is this a framework vehicle?": GetVehicleId answers instantly for a car whip already knows, and ResolveVehicle registers any other car on the spot.

Vehicle Resolution: The Developer Pattern

Every vehicle interaction in whip follows one pattern. Your scripts should too:

-- Step 1: Try instant cache lookup (free, no server call)
local vehicleId = exports.whip_core:GetVehicleId(entity)

-- Step 2: If nil (NPC vehicle not yet registered), resolve it
-- This is BLOCKING — only use in an action's onSelect, never in canInteract or a label!
local why
if not vehicleId then
    vehicleId, why = exports.whip_core:ResolveVehicle(entity)   -- false, why when it cannot
end

-- Step 3: Now you have a vehicleId — use it everywhere
if vehicleId then
    -- Send to server events, read vehicle info, check keys, etc.
    TriggerServerEvent('myresource:doSomething', vehicleId)
end

Client Vehicle Exports

ExportBlocking?ReturnsUse In
GetVehicleId(entity)Nonumber|nilConditions, frequent calls, anywhere
GetVehicleBy('entity', entity)NoThe full GetVehicle snapshotConditions, UI, anywhere
HasVehicleKey(vehicleId)NoboolConditions, anywhere
HasKeyForPlate(plate)NoboolConditions, anywhere
ResolveVehicle(entity)Yesnumber, or false, why (not near you, an owned car's plate, too many street cars held)Callbacks ONLY (one-time actions)
GetNearbyVehicles(radius)Notable[] sorted by distanceMenus, scans
Never call ResolveVehicle in canInteract, a label function, loops, or per-frame code! It does a server round-trip. Use GetVehicleId or GetVehicleBy('entity', entity) for instant checks. Only call ResolveVehicle in an action's onSelect (runs once on click), one-time actions, or command handlers.

The Correct Pattern for Vehicle Scripts

Here's how to build a vehicle interaction that works on any vehicle, owned or NPC:

-- client.lua — Tow truck: hook up any vehicle. Registrations go in Whip.register.
Whip.register(function()
    exports.whip_core:RegisterItemFlag('tow_hook')

    exports.whip_core:AddAction({
        id    = 'hook',
        at    = { vehiclePart = 'trunk' },   -- a choice on any car's boot prompt
        label = 'Hook Vehicle',

        -- canInteract: instant check, asked while you stand at a car's boot and again at the click
        canInteract = function(ctx)
            return exports.whip_core:HasItemFlag('tow_hook')
        end,

        -- onSelect: runs once on click, in its own thread — safe to use ResolveVehicle here
        onSelect = function(ctx)
            local vehicleId, why = exports.whip_core:GetVehicleId(ctx.entity), nil
            if not vehicleId then
                vehicleId, why = exports.whip_core:ResolveVehicle(ctx.entity)   -- registers a street car
            end
            if not vehicleId then return ctx.refuse(why) end
            TriggerServerEvent('tow:hookVehicle', vehicleId)
        end,
    })
end)

-- server.lua — inside Whip.register too
exports.whip_core:SecureEvent('tow:hookVehicle', {
    rateLimit = 2000,
    -- 'vehicle' resolves the id before the handler runs (a bad one is refused, never turned into
    -- car #1). anyOwner: a tow truck hooks anybody's car. session: street cars get towed too.
    params = { {'vehicle', 'vehicle', { anyOwner = true, session = true }} },
    near   = { at = 'vehicle', range = 8.0 },   -- where the car IS now, not where it was saved
}, function(source, player, v)
    print(('Towing %s (%s)'):format(v.model, v.plate))
end)

Server Vehicle Exports

On the server, a car is named by its vehicleId or by a vehicle reference:

-- If you have a vehicleId (from client event):
local v = exports.whip_core:GetVehicle(vehicleId)

-- If you have something else — a plate, a netId, an entity:
local v = exports.whip_core:GetVehicleBy('plate', plate)
-- 'plate' answers for vehicles whip already knows. To adopt an unknown NPC car
-- standing in the world, AdoptVehicle({ entity = veh }) registers it and returns its id
-- (a plate works too, when that is all you have) — only when you are about to work on
-- it: adopting pins the car wherever it is.

-- Or name the car with a vehicle reference — every vehicle export takes one:
local v = exports.whip_core:GetVehicle({ plate = plate })

-- Other useful exports:
exports.whip_core:GetVehiclesOf(source)           -- array of snapshots (or { charId = n })
exports.whip_core:SetVehicleLocked(vehicleId, true) -- lock/unlock
exports.whip_core:SetVehicleStat(vehicleId, 'fuel', 100) -- fuel is a stat
exports.whip_core:GiveVehicleKey(source, vehicleId) -- give key item

-- Everything the old one-answer exports told you is a field on the snapshot:
--   v.owner  v.session  v.locked  v.state  v.netId  v.coords  v.stats  v.storage

Damage a car keeps

An owned car keeps its engine and body health, the doors torn off it and its burst tyres. They are saved with the car and put back on when it comes out of a garage or after a restart. Dents are not kept: the car looks clean and keeps its numbers. Config.VehicleDamage.remember = false turns it off.

  • Saved when the driver gets out, every VehiclePositionSaveInterval, and when the car is stored or leaves the world.
  • Put back when the car comes out of a garage. A car brought back after a restart is put right when a player comes near. It only ever adds damage, so a car hit since it spawned keeps those hits too.
  • A wreck comes back with its engine at Config.VehicleDamage.engineFloor (100): smoking and barely driving, never on fire.

The damage is five vehicle stats whip owns, read with GetVehicleStat: engineHealth and bodyHealth (0 to 1000, GTA's scale: below 400 the engine smokes), doorsOff (bit n is door n: 0 front left, 1 front right, 2 rear left, 3 rear right, 4 bonnet, 5 boot), and tyresFlat and tyresRim (bits over GTA's tyre numbers 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 45, 47). A repair must clear them, or the next spawn puts the damage back: whip's own repairs do, and a script's calls ClearVehicleDamage as it fixes the car.

-- Server: a mechanic's quote from what the car has kept
local engine = exports.whip_core:GetVehicleStat(vehicleId, 'engineHealth')
local price = math.floor((1000 - engine) * 2)

Vehicle Data: everything that is not a gauge

SetVehicleData attaches anything that should stick to a car and is not a gauge, a GTA mod or an item: a fitted part's grade, an install setting, a finance flag. Values are opaque to whip: anything json-encodable, keyed by name, never clamped, drawn, decayed or consumed.

-- Server: attach it
exports.whip_core:SetVehicleData(vehicleId, 'turbo', {
    grade = 'A', fitter = player.charId, at = os.time(),
})

-- Client: read it, anywhere, any player — the same vehicleId (or { entity = veh })
local turbo = exports.whip_core:GetVehicleData(vehicleId, 'turbo')
if turbo and turbo.grade == 'A' then --[[ ... ]] end

-- Client: be told when it changes
exports.whip_core:OnVehicleDataChange('turbo', function(vehicleId, value, old, entity)
    -- ...
end)

Which one do I want?

If it is…Use
a number with a range that a player should watch movea vehicle stat
items in slotsa store
a GTA mod: colour, extra, wheelproperties
anything else that should stick to the carvehicle data

Three properties worth knowing

A key belongs to the resource that wrote it. Every resource can read every key, but only the one that wrote a key can change or clear it, and ClearAllVehicleData takes away only your own. So two scripts that both pick a name like level cannot trample each other, and uninstalling one kit cannot wipe another off the same car. Who owns what is saved with the data.

It follows the car, not the entity. Store a vehicle in a garage and take it out again and that is a new entity with a new handle: a statebag you wrote yourself dies there. Vehicle data is kept by vehicleId and sent again each time the car spawns, so it survives garaging, despawning, streaming out and a server restart.

It goes with the car. It is saved with the car itself, so deleting the car takes it too: there is no cleanup to write.

Everyone who can see the car can read it. Every player's game near the car gets the same data, so it is the wrong place for a secret: a hidden tracker would be readable by the driver.
It is not a database. Bounded at 32 keys per resource per car, of 40 characters, not indexed, and written through on every change. If you need to query it ("every financed car"), keep history, or store something that is not per-vehicle, build a table, and still use this for the slice that has to be on the car and on every client.

Ownership: transfer and delete

A vehicle's owner is one field, ownerCharId. Two exports move it and remove it, and both keep every affected client's list in step.

-- Sell a car. Takes the buyer's SOURCE, not a charId.
local ok, err = exports.whip_core:TransferVehicle(vehicleId, buyerSource)
if not ok then return exports.whip_core:NotifyPlayer(source, err, 'error') end

-- Chop shop, repossession, insurance write-off.
exports.whip_core:DeleteVehicle(vehicleId)

The new owner is a source, as for CreateOwnedVehicle, so they must be online. For a sale, they already are.

TransferVehicle takes an optional third argument, { giveKey, revokeOldKeys }. Both default to true: the buyer gets a key, and the keys in the seller's pockets are taken. Pass false to skip either.

Old keys are not all taken back. A vehicle key is an item carrying a vehicleId, so revokeOldKeys can only take the keys in the previous owner's pockets while they are online. A key that is offline, in a stash, in another car's boot, on the ground or left in the ignition still works. Empty the ignition yourself before a sale if it matters.
DeleteVehicle removes an owned car for good: the car, its boot, glovebox and ignition, in one step, with every item in them logged as lost. Any resource may call it (a chop shop is not an admin), so check who may before you do. A street car is only forgotten, not removed from the world. See the DeleteVehicle card.

Vehicle events

Listen for vehicle state changes with AddEventHandler (all server-side; a client cannot send them):

EventPayloadFires when
whip_core:vehicle:created{ vehicleId, ownerCharId }Any path mints a vehicle, including CreateOwnedVehicle
whip_core:vehicle:ownerChanged{ vehicleId, from, to }A vehicle moves between characters
whip_core:vehicle:deleted{ vehicleId, ownerCharId, wasOut }A vehicle stops existing
whip_core:vehicle:dataChanged{ vehicleId, key, value, old, cleared, resource }Vehicle data is attached or removed. resource is who did it
whip_core:vehicle:lockChanged{ vehicleId, plate, locked, source }A car is locked or unlocked, by anything. source is the player, when a player did it
whip_core:vehicle:spawned{ vehicleId, entity, netId, plate, model, session, temp? }whip puts a car into the world: an owned car coming out, or a SpawnTempVehicle car (temp = true)
whip_core:vehicle:despawned{ vehicleId, netId }An owned car leaves the world (garaged, despawned). The record is still there. A new spawn gets a new netId, so anything holding the old one should let it go
whip_core:vehicle:released{ vehicleId, reason, temp }whip lets go of a car nobody owns: a street car handed back to GTA, or a temp car removed. reason is 'expired', 'idle', 'gone', 'stopped', 'despawned', 'deleted', 'released' (its tag was released: ReleaseTag) or 'failed'. After this the vehicleId means nothing: drop anything you kept for it
whip_core:vehicle:registered{ vehicleId, plate, model, session, source }whip takes on a street car that is already in the world (a player drove it, a lockpick, a pump, AdoptVehicle). session is always true; source is the player who reported it, when one did
whip_core:vehicle:claimed{ vehicleId, from, ownerCharId }A street car became an owned car (ClaimVehicle); from is the session id it had
whip_core:vehicle:plateChanged{ vehicleId, from, to }A car's plate changed
whip_core:vehicle:lockpicked{ vehicleId, plate, source }A player lockpicked a car open

These are for listening. Firing one yourself (TriggerEvent('whip_core:vehicle:despawned', …)) tells every other listener something that did not happen, and changes nothing inside whip.

Keep anything of your own per car? Listen for deleted, and remove it there: nothing else tells you a car is gone. Vehicle data goes with the car by itself.

Hearing a stat change: OnVehicleStatChange

A vehicle stat changing has no event. A server script names the stat it cares about with OnVehicleStatChange and is called only when that stat moves, on any car, whoever registered the stat. A resource can react to another resource's stat this way without either one changing the other's code:

-- A coolant add-on reacting to whip_autos' boost: neither resource knows the other's code
exports.whip_core:OnVehicleStatChange('boost', function(vehicleId, value, previous)
    if value >= 20 then -- flat out: start this resource's own clock
    end
end)

-- Every stat, with its name second. Called the most of anything here: name the stats when you know them.
exports.whip_core:OnVehicleStatChange('*', function(vehicleId, name, value, previous, cleared)
    print(name, previous, '->', value, cleared and '(retired)' or '')
end)
Called on a change, not on a clock. A stat that sits still calls nobody, so "held at full for ten seconds" is the listener's own timer. Several stats written together (a burn report) are told once the whole write is done, in the same server frame, one call per stat.

Lockpicks and seats

-- Server-side: react to lockpick (e.g. police dispatch)
AddEventHandler('whip_core:vehicle:lockpicked', function(data)
    local coords = GetEntityCoords(GetPlayerPed(data.source))
    TriggerClientEvent('dispatch:alert', -1, 'Vehicle Break-In', coords)
end)

-- Client-side: react to entering a vehicle
AddEventHandler('whip_core:vehicle:entered', function(data)
    print(('Entered vehicle: %s (%s)'):format(data.plate, tostring(data.vehicleId)))
end)

See Server Events and Client Events for the full list.

Vehicles

Three calls read a vehicle. GetVehicle when you have an id, GetVehicleBy when you have a plate, a netId or an entity, and GetVehiclesOf for everything a character owns. All three answer with the same snapshot, so owner, lock, state, netId, stats and storage are fields on it rather than separate calls.
One way to name a car, on both sides: a vehicle reference. Every vehicle, stat and data export takes one as its first argument: 
{ id = vehicleId }   { entity = entity }   { plate = 'ABC123' }   { netId = netId }
A bare number is always a vehicleId, on the server and on the client, for every vehicle export. The car in the game world (an entity handle from a native) goes in as { entity = veh }. The only exceptions are the converters whose job is the entity: GetVehicleId(entity) and ResolveVehicle(entity). The vehicle table GetVehicle answers is a reference too: its vehicleId names it, so a snapshot can be handed straight back. On the server, a reference that names no car answers 'Vehicle not found'; a table that names nothing answers 'Invalid vehicle reference'. A client only knows the cars streamed in around it, so a reference to a car far away answers nil there.
GetVehicle(vehicleId, opts)SERVER

Everything the server knows about a vehicle, as a copy, or nil when whip does not know the car. A client has its own GetVehicle (the CLIENT card below), which answers what that client can see.

ParamTypeDescription
vehicleIdnumber|tableVehicle ID, or a vehicle reference
optstable|nil{ occupants = true } to include who is sitting in it. Off by default because finding out walks every player on the server.
Returns: table|nil
local v = exports.whip_core:GetVehicle(vehicleId)
if not v then return false, 'No such vehicle' end

print(v.plate, v.model, v.owner.charId, v.state, v.locked)

-- Also on it: displayName, class, vehType, owner.name, owner.online, garage, coords, heading,
-- session, temp, secure, spawned, entity, netId, stats (v.stats.fuel), data (your keys),
-- properties, and occupants when you pass { occupants = true }.
-- storage is only there when the car's storage is already loaded:
-- v.storage.trunk = { slots, maxWeight, used }
It is always a copy. Editing what this returns changes nothing: not the vehicle, not whip. A read cannot become a write by accident, which is why every read goes through here and nothing hands out the framework's own table.
Street car or rental? Read temp, not just session. session = true means nobody owns the car, and that covers both street traffic whip picked up and a SpawnTempVehicle car (a rental, a job van). temp = true is only the second kind. A tow job that treats every session car as abandoned traffic will tow away somebody's rental.

displayName and class come from the vehicle catalog, so they are nil for a model the catalog does not have. Check before you compare.
GetVehicleBy(kind, value, opts)SERVERCLIENT

The same snapshot, found by something other than an id.

ParamTypeDescription
kindstring'plate', 'netId' or 'entity': on both sides
valueanyThe plate text, net id, or entity handle
optstable|nilPassed through to GetVehicle (server)
Returns: table|nil
exports.whip_core:GetVehicleBy('plate', 'ABC123')
exports.whip_core:GetVehicleBy('netId', netId)
exports.whip_core:GetVehicleBy('entity', entity)
The same as GetVehicle with a reference. GetVehicleBy('plate', 'ABC123') and GetVehicle({ plate = 'ABC123' }) are one call. On the client it only finds cars streamed in near that player.
You say which kind, on purpose. vehicleIds and entity handles are both plain integers, so a lookup that guessed which one it had been given could answer with a different vehicle, silently.
GetVehiclesOf(who)SERVER

Every vehicle a person owns, as full snapshots. who is a person: a server id, or { charId = n } for a character online or not.

ParamTypeDescription
whonumber|tableA server id, or { charId = n }
-- Every car this player's character owns
for _, v in ipairs(exports.whip_core:GetVehiclesOf(source)) do
    print(v.vehicleId, v.plate, v.state, v.garage)
end

-- A character who may be offline
local cars = exports.whip_core:GetVehiclesOf({ charId = 42 })
Returns: table[]: {}, why when who names nobody
IsPlayerDrivingVehicle / IsPlayerInVehicleSERVER

Is this player in the driver's seat of this vehicle, or in it at all? Three natives, no allocation, no scan.

ParamTypeDescription
sourcenumberPlayer server id
vehicleIdnumberVehicle ID
-- In a fuel-burn report: only the driver may send one
if not exports.whip_core:IsPlayerDrivingVehicle(source, vehicleId) then
    return false, 'You need to be driving'
end

-- In a glovebox open: anyone sitting in the car
if not exports.whip_core:IsPlayerInVehicle(source, vehicleId) then
    return false, 'You need to be in the car'
end
Returns: boolean
Reach for these rather than GetVehicle when the answer is a yes or a no. The snapshot answers the same question, but it copies the whole vehicle to do it: a lot of work, on something running twice a second per player, to find out whether somebody is in seat -1.
GetVehicleDriver(vehicle)SERVER

Whose game drives this car now: the player in its driver's seat, or the player whose game plays a Director take (a recorded drive) on it. Ask it before you take a car to another game to pull or carry it. A take's game takes its car back every two seconds, and the two would fight.

ParamTypeDescription
vehiclenumber | tableA vehicleId, or { netId } / { entity } (any networked car, whip's or not) / { plate }
-- whip_rope: a car someone (or a take) drives pulls; it is never taken to the hand that holds the rope
local source, how = exports.whip_core:GetVehicleDriver({ netId = netId })
if source then
    -- how: 'seat' (they sit at the wheel) or 'take' (their game plays its recorded drive)
end
Returns: source, 'seat' | 'take', or nil for a car nobody drives (parked, an NPC at the wheel)
GetPlayerVehicle(source, opts)SERVER

Which whip car is this player sitting in? Asked of the server's view of the player, never the client's word: the call an in-car item (nitrous, a part fitted from inside) starts with.

ParamTypeDescription
sourcenumberPlayer server id
optstable?{ driver = true }: only the driver's seat counts. Without it, any seat
Returns: vehicleId, or false, why: a sentence you can show the player: not in a vehicle, not driving, or a car whip does not look after (an NPC's car nobody has taken).
local vehicleId, why = exports.whip_core:GetPlayerVehicle(source, { driver = true })
if not vehicleId then return false, why end
GetPlayerSeat(source)SERVER

Which seat is this player in, as the server sees them? Any vehicle, street cars included. Seat -1 is the driver's, 0 the front passenger's, then the rear seats.

ParamTypeDescription
sourcenumberPlayer server id
local at, why = exports.whip_core:GetPlayerSeat(source)
if not at then return false, why end
if at.driver then
    -- at.vehicleId is whip's id for the car (nil for a street car); at.netId always works
end
Returns: { seat, driver, vehicleId, netId }, or false, why: not in a vehicle, or not in a seat yet (still getting in).
A car's boot, glovebox and ignition are stores. Read, fill and empty them with the store calls and the address { kind = 'vehicle', id = vehicleId, sub = 'trunk' } ('glovebox', 'key'), the id may be a vehicle reference such as { plate = 'ABC 123' }:
• what is in it: StoreRead, StoreCount, GetItemAt;
• put in or take out: StoreGive, StoreTake, StoreMove;
• open the boot on a player's screen: OpenStore, CloseStore.
SetVehicleLocked(vehicleId, locked)SERVER

Lock or unlock a vehicle. Persists to DB and applies via OneSync. A car comes back after a restart locked or unlocked as it was left, except one locked with its own key in the ignition, which is unlocked; a car taken out of a garage is locked unless its own key is in the ignition.

ParamTypeDescription
vehicleIdnumber|tableVehicle ID, or a vehicle reference
lockedbooltrue = locked
local ok, err = exports.whip_core:SetVehicleLocked(vehicleId, true)
if not ok then print(err) end
Returns: bool, string|nil
Every lock change is announced, whoever made it. whip_core:vehicle:lockChanged fires when the state actually changes (through this export, the key fob, a lockpick or the admin tool) with { vehicleId, plate, locked, source }.
GiveVehicleKey(who, vehicleId)SERVER

Give a vehicle key item to a player. Adds a vehicle_key with metadata to their inventory, so they must be online.

ParamTypeDescription
whonumber|tableA person who is playing: their server id, or { charId = n }
vehicleIdnumberVehicle ID
local ok, err = exports.whip_core:GiveVehicleKey(source, vehicleId)
if not ok then return false, err end
Returns: true, or false, reason ('Already has a key for this vehicle', no room, not online)
HasVehicleKey(source, vehicleId)SERVER

Check if a player has a key for a specific vehicle in their inventory.

ParamTypeDescription
sourcenumberServer player ID
vehicleIdnumberVehicle ID
if not exports.whip_core:HasVehicleKey(source, vehicleId) then
    return false, 'You have no key for this car'
end
Returns: bool, string?: false, 'Player not loaded' for someone not in a character
GetPlayerVehicleKeys(source)SERVER

Get all vehicle keys a player has in their inventory.

ParamTypeDescription
sourcenumberServer player ID
for vehicleId, plate in pairs(exports.whip_core:GetPlayerVehicleKeys(source)) do
    print(vehicleId, plate)
end
Returns: table: { [vehicleId] = plateText }; {}, 'Player not loaded' before they load
CreateOwnedVehicle(source, data, opts)SERVER

Create a vehicle owned by a player's character. A dealership sale, a heist reward, a job vehicle: this is the only way a satellite mints one. With opts it does the whole sale: it also brings the car out where you say and hands over the key, and if either of those fails the car is removed again and you get (false, reason): there is never a half-made car to clean up.

ParamTypeDescription
sourcenumberThe receiving player
datatable{ model, plate?, garage?, stats?, properties?, vehType? } (stats: what it starts with, by stat name: { fuel = 100 }; one left out reads its registered default) (and the trunk/glovebox sizes: trunkSlots?, trunkMaxWeight?, gloveboxSlots?, gloveboxMaxWeight?), garage must name a garage that exists (GetNearestGarage, GetGarage); left out, the car goes in the default garage
optstable|nil{ giveKey?, spawnAt? }: spawnAt is a vector4 (heading in w), a vector3, or { x, y, z, heading }; it makes the car out there. Without it the car starts in its garage. A spot with a vehicle on it (or another player in it) is refused before any car is made: false, 'Something is already parked in that spot'. So is a builder in the Director's Isolate world, since cars come out in the shared world: false, 'Leave Isolate world first: cars come out in the shared world' (ask CanBringOutVehicleFor before charging)
Out in the world means spawnAt. data.state = 'out' without a spawnAt is refused, and data.x/y/z are not read: a car is placed by spawnAt or not at all.
Returns: number|false vehicleId, string|nil err, boolean|nil saved. saved comes only after a database fault: the car was saved, with the payment that rode it, but could not be read back yet. It is theirs and arrives in their garage with its key once it reads back, so do not refund on false, err, true; refund only on a plain false.
The owner is taken from the player record, not from data. A satellite passing a charId would be asserting who owns the vehicle, and nothing downstream would question it.
The second return is the error, always. The plate and netId are fields of the vehicle: GetVehicle(vehicleId).plate, .netId.
A bike is built as a bike. Leave out vehType and whip reads the model's class from the vehicle catalog, so a motorbike, boat, helicopter or plane is the right kind of entity on its very first spawn.
-- A whole sale: payment, car, spawn and key, or nothing at all
local canOut, outWhy = exports.whip_core:CanBringOutVehicleFor(source)
if not canOut then return false, outWhy end

local receipt, err = exports.whip_core:ChargePlayer(source, 250000, { reason = 'Adder' })
if not receipt then return false, err end

local vehicleId, why = exports.whip_core:CreateOwnedVehicle(source, { model = 'adder' }, {
    giveKey = true,
    spawnAt = vector4(-56.7, -1097.2, 26.4, 160.0),
})
if not vehicleId then
    exports.whip_core:RefundPlayer(receipt)
    return false, why
end

local plate = exports.whip_core:GetVehicle(vehicleId).plate
CanBringOutVehicleFor(source)SERVER

Whether a car can be brought out for this player now. Ask it before charging for a car that comes out into the world (CreateOwnedVehicle with spawnAt), so the sale is refused before any money moves. A builder in the Director's Isolate world is refused: whip's cars come out in the shared world, where they would not see it. CreateOwnedVehicle still asks the same question itself.

ParamTypeDescription
sourcenumberThe player the car is for
local ok, why = exports.whip_core:CanBringOutVehicleFor(source)
if not ok then return false, why end   -- 'Leave Isolate world first: ...'
Returns: boolean ok, string|nil why
VehicleModelExists(model)SERVER

Whether this game has a vehicle called model. The server cannot read game files, so each player's game sends its list of vehicles (add-on cars included) as they join, at the character screen, and the server keeps every name any of them reported. The list is saved, per platform and game build, so after a restart the server knows the cars before anyone joins; a name no game has reported for 14 days is dropped (an add-on car you took out). CreateOwnedVehicle, SpawnTempVehicle and the garages refuse a model the game does not have, with 'There is no vehicle called "x" in this game'. Ask this to leave such cars out of what you sell; GetVehicleCatalog's rows carry the same answer as inGame.

ParamTypeDescription
modelstringThe model name, like 'sultan'
if exports.whip_core:VehicleModelExists(model) == false then
    return false, 'That car is not in this game'
end
Returns: boolean|nil: nil while no player's game has reported yet (a new server, or a new game build), or for a model not on the list once it is full (20,000 names); nothing is refused then
SpawnTempVehicle(model, coords, opts)SERVER

Put a temporary car in the world: a rental, a job van, a test drive. Nobody owns it and it is never saved, but it has a vehicleId, stats, data, a trunk and keys like any other car. It belongs to your resource and is removed when your resource stops, when despawnAfter runs out, after ten minutes with nobody near it (unless idleDespawn = false), or by DespawnVehicle. Its key is taken back from the player it was given to when it goes, and whip_core:vehicle:released fires with the reason.

ParamTypeDescription
modelstringVehicle model name
coordsvector4|vector3|tableWhere. { x, y, z, heading } works too
optstable|nilAll optional:
forSource: the player it is for; they get a key unless giveKey = false
despawnAfter: seconds until it is removed
locked: it spawns locked; false for one that stands open
