keyInIgnition: true puts a key in its ignition, so whoever sits in the driver's seat can start it (a van the whole crew drives). Works with or without the pocket key.
idleDespawn: false and it is never removed just for sitting with nobody near it
tag: one of your tags (see ReleaseTag): releasing the tag removes the car, and once a tag is released nothing more spawns under it
secure: true and its lock cannot be picked nor its ignition hacked: only its key works, and only a key cut for this car, not one kept from an earlier one (GetVehicle shows secure = true)
force: true and it is made even when another car or a player is on the spot (GTA pushes them aside). Without it, a spot that is not clear is refused
plate, vehType: normally left out
Returns: number|false vehicleId, string|nil err
despawnAfter removes the car even if somebody is driving it. Warn them before the time runs out.
Knowing why it went. Listen for whip_core:vehicle:released on the server and read reason: 'expired' (your despawnAfter), 'idle' (nobody near it for ten minutes), 'despawned', 'stopped' (your resource stopped), 'released' (you released its tag) or 'gone' (the car had already left the world). GetVehicle shows a temp car as temp = true.
-- A rental: locked, the renter holds the key, gone in half an hour
local vehicleId, err = exports.whip_core:SpawnTempVehicle('blista', vector4(x, y, z, h), {
    forSource    = source,
    despawnAfter = 1800,
})

-- A job van: key in the ignition, nobody's pocket
local vanId = exports.whip_core:SpawnTempVehicle('speedo', vector4(x, y, z, h), {
    keyInIgnition = true,
})
ClaimVehicle(vehicle, who, opts) · SetVehiclePlate(vehicle, plate)SERVER

Make a car nobody owns (a temporary car or a street car whip picked up) into an owned car, saved like any other: the end of a boosting job, a race won for pink slips. who is a person: a server id, or { charId = n }. The owned car is a new vehicle (a new vehicleId, and a new plate unless opts.plate names one) with the same model, look and fuel and the same trunk and glovebox contents; it takes the old car's place, with the driver still behind the wheel, and points made on the old car move to it. If anything fails before the old car goes, nothing changes. A model whip's vehicle catalog does not know (an add-on car not in it) is refused.

SetVehiclePlate changes any car's plate: saved for an owned car, and for a car nobody owns until it goes. Keys cut before the change still fit.

local vehicleId, note = exports.whip_core:ClaimVehicle(runCarId, source, { plate = 'BOOST01' })
exports.whip_core:SetVehiclePlate(vehicleId, 'NEWPLT')
optsTypeDescription
platestring?Its new plate (8 characters at most, not one another car wears); default a new one
hereboolean?false: put away in their garage instead of standing where it stood
garagestring?Which garage it belongs to (default the default garage)
keyboolean?false: no key for them (default: they get one)
reasonstring?For their activity log
leavefunction?function(metadata, item) answering true for a stack to leave behind: it stays in the old car and goes with it (a job's own things: the Director's Claim Car leaves its run's)
Returns: ClaimVehicle: the new vehicleId (and a note when it could not come out and waits in its garage), or false, reason. SetVehiclePlate: true, or false, reason. whip_core:vehicle:claimed { vehicleId, from, ownerCharId } and whip_core:vehicle:plateChanged { vehicleId, from, to } fire.
AdoptVehicle(plate | { entity } | { netId })SERVER

Take on a car that is already in the world. Hand it the car ({ entity = veh } or { netId = id }) and that exact car is registered as a session vehicle; hand it a plate and it takes whichever car on the map wears that plate first. A car whip already knows answers with its vehicleId. It never creates a car.

ParamTypeDescription
refstring | tableA licence plate, or { entity = vehicle } / { netId = networkId }. Prefer the car: a plate is text a driver can change, so the plate form can land on a different car wearing the same text. Add player = source to the car form when a player's action brings it in (filling it at a pump): a car whip has never seen then counts against that player's street-car limit (20, as their own path), and past it the answer is false, reason
local vehicleId, err = exports.whip_core:AdoptVehicle({ netId = netId })
if not vehicleId then return false, err end
Returns: number|false vehicleId, string|nil err
For a client holding an entity rather than a plate, ResolveVehicle is the same idea from the other side and needs no plate at all.
Not a lookup. To find out about a car by its plate, use GetVehicleBy('plate', plate): that only reads. AdoptVehicle searches every car in the world, and the one it finds is registered and pinned (GTA can no longer clear it away) wherever it is on the map, with none of the limits the player path has (20 m and 20 cars per player). Use it when you are about to work on that car, not to answer a question.
HoldVehicleEngine(vehicleId, key, reason)SERVER

Keep a car's engine from running, saying reason to its driver (80 letters): out of fuel, a flat battery, an immobiliser. While any hold is on it the engine will not start however the driver asks (their game refuses at once: the reason rides on the car), and a running one stops; the car still rolls. key names your hold (a resource may hold one car for two reasons); the same key again replaces its reason. Yours alone: it goes when you release it, when your resource stops, or when the car's id goes for good.

exports.whip_core:HoldVehicleEngine(vehicleId, 'battery', 'The battery is flat')
exports.whip_core:ReleaseVehicleEngine(vehicleId, 'battery')
Returns: true, or false, why (no such vehicle)
ReleaseVehicleEngine(vehicleId, key?)SERVER

Let go of your hold key on the car; with no key, every hold of yours on it.

Returns: true when one went, false, why when you had none
GetVehicleEngineHold(vehicleId)SERVER

Is anything holding the car's engine off, whoever's hold it is?

Returns: the reason shown, or nil
GetVehiclePoint(vehicle, action)CLIENT

Where a named point is on this vehicle now, on the side nearest the player: whip's own ('fuel' its filler, 'engine', 'storage' its boot, 'mount' how you get on a bike, 'board' a boat's) or one of yours (SetVehiclePointRules). For whatever you put there: a nozzle, a cable, a hose. vehicle is a vehicle reference, as every vehicle export takes: a vehicleId, or the entity as { entity = veh }.

A car's 'fuel' is its petrol cap where the model has one, else above a rear wheel at the height of its door handles, on one side of the car: the side set for its model (Config.VehicleFillers), else its one side tank's, else a side picked once per model.

Returns: { x, y, z, heading, side, fixed } (heading: a sign facing out of its side; side: 'left', 'right', 'front', 'rear'; fixed: true when the point is on that side wherever the player stands, as a car's filler is, false when it is on the side they are on), or nil when the model has nowhere for it
SetVehiclePointRules(action, rules)CLIENT

Name a point of your own (a charging port, a wash bay's spot). rules = { default = { place, … }, bike = { … }, boat = { … } }: for each kind of vehicle, the places to try in order. A place is a bone name ('petrolcap'), a list of bone names, 'entry' (a door's way in), 'box', 'box:rear' or 'box:front' (on its bounding box), or 'filler' (a car's filler, as whip's 'fuel' finds it). whip's own points cannot be taken, nor another resource's; yours go when your resource stops. Every kind's list is checked: one that is not a list of places is refused.

exports.whip_core:SetVehiclePointRules('charge', { default = { 'petrolcap', 'box:front' }, bike = { 'box:rear' } })
local p = exports.whip_core:GetVehiclePoint({ entity = veh }, 'charge')
Returns: true, or false, why
StoreVehicle(vehicleId, garageKey)SERVER

Put a vehicle away: out of the world, position cleared, state garaged.

ParamTypeDescription
vehicleIdnumberVehicle ID
garageKeystring|nilDefaults to the garage it is already assigned to, or the default garage when it has none. A key that names no garage is refused: false, 'No such garage: …'
-- Impound: off the street and into your own garage
local ok, err = exports.whip_core:StoreVehicle(vehicleId, 'impound')   -- a garage your resource made
if not ok then return false, err end
Returns: boolean ok, string|nil err. A street car or a temporary car has no garage to go to: false, 'A street car cannot be put in a garage', or for a temporary car false, 'A temporary car cannot be put in a garage'.
DespawnVehicle puts a car away too, into the garage it is filed under. This is the one that takes a garage key, and it refuses a car with somebody inside it; DespawnVehicle does not.
RetrieveVehicle(vehicleId, garageKey)SERVER

Take a vehicle out of a garage. Marks it out and locked; it still has to be spawned.

ParamTypeDescription
vehicleIdnumberVehicle ID
garageKeystring|nilDefaults to the garage it is assigned to
local ok, err = exports.whip_core:RetrieveVehicle(vehicleId)
if not ok then return false, err end

local netId, spawnErr = exports.whip_core:SpawnVehicle(vehicleId, x, y, z, heading)
if not netId then return false, spawnErr end
Returns: boolean ok, string|nil err
Two calls, on purpose. Retrieving decides the car may come out; spawning decides where. A garage uses its own spawn point; a satellite may want it somewhere else.
TransferVehicle(vehicleId, newOwner, opts)SERVER

Hand a vehicle to another player. Writes the owner, re-syncs both players' vehicle lists, and fires whip_core:vehicle:ownerChanged.

ParamTypeDescription
vehicleIdnumberVehicle ID
newOwnernumber|tableThe receiving player, who must be online: their server id, or { charId = n }
optstable|nil{ giveKey, revokeOldKeys }: both default true; pass false to skip either
Returns: boolean, string|nil: ok, and why not ('The new owner must be online', 'Session vehicles have no owner' (for a car nobody owns, use ClaimVehicle), or 'Already owned by that character')
The new owner must be online, the same rule CreateOwnedVehicle follows: read off a live player record, the owner can only be a character that exists.
The seller can keep a working key. A key is an inventory item carrying a vehicleId, tied to no owner. What this does and does not reach:
• revokeOldKeys takes every key from the previous owner's own pockets, and only while they are online. A key in a stash, a boot or on the ground survives.
• A key left in the ignition stays there, and anyone sitting in the car can still drive it.
• giveKey is best effort: if the buyer's pockets are full they get no key, and this still returns true. Check with HasVehicleKey, or hand one over with GiveVehicleKey, which says when it fails.
local ok, err = exports.whip_core:TransferVehicle(vehicleId, buyerSource)
if not ok then notify(err) end
DeleteVehicle(vehicleId)SERVER

Destroy an owned vehicle and everything in it, permanently. The row, the trunk, the glovebox, the ignition contents, the entity, any queued writes and anybody's open view of its storage: all in one transaction. Every item in it is written to the activity log as lost. Fires whip_core:vehicle:deleted.

ParamTypeDescription
vehicleIdnumberVehicle ID
-- A chop shop: the car and everything in it, gone for good
local ok, err = exports.whip_core:DeleteVehicle(vehicleId)
if not ok then return false, err end
Returns: boolean, string|nil: ok, and why not
The most destructive call in the vehicle API, and deliberately ungated like every other satellite export: a chop shop, a repossession job or an insurance write-off all need it and none of them is an admin.
A street car is not removed from the world. It has no row, so "deleting" one means whip forgets it and hands it back to GTA as ordinary traffic: the car stays where it is (DespawnVehicle does the same to a street car). A SpawnTempVehicle car is different: whip built it, so it is removed. If your job really must make a street car vanish, call DeleteVehicle first and then DeleteEntity on the entity you read from GetVehicle beforehand.
Two words, two meanings, and the difference is real.
properties: the raw GTA block, applied to an entity. Client-side only, because paint and mods are client natives. GetVehicleProperties / SetVehicleProperties.
appearance: what whip has stored for a vehicle, keyed by vehicleId. Server-side authority. SetVehicleAppearance, RestoreVehicleAppearance, HoldVehicleAppearance.
A shop changes the appearance. The entity's properties are how that becomes visible.
SetVehicleAppearance(vehicleId, props, opts?)SERVER

Change how a vehicle looks and store it, in one call. This is the call a customisation shop makes. The props are merged over what the car already carries, so changing the colour does not restate every mod, and the merge goes one level deeper into mods so setting mod 11 does not drop mod 23.

ParamTypeDescription
vehicleIdnumberVehicle ID
propstableAppearance fields to apply over the current ones ({} for none)
optstable?data = { key = value } and clearData = { 'key' }: your resource's vehicle data, set and removed in the same write as the look, checked as SetVehicleDataMany checks it
Returns: true once applied (and saved, for a car that has a row); false, why when it did not save, and then none of it, look or data, changed. A car that is not saved anywhere (GetVehicle(id).session is true: a street car, a rental) wears the look for as long as the car exists, so tell a buyer.
-- One wheel and one colour. Everything else on the car is untouched.
exports.whip_core:SetVehicleAppearance(vehicleId, {
    mods = { ['23'] = 4 },
    color1 = 27,
})

-- New wheels and the tuning that goes with them, in one write: both land with the payment, or neither does.
exports.whip_core:SetVehicleAppearance(vehicleId, { mods = { ['23'] = 4 } }, {
    data      = { myStance = { height = -0.05 } },
    clearData = { 'myOldKit' },
})
An instruction, not a report. A client saying what a car looks like is believed about paint and bodywork only, because a client can lie. This is server-side, from code you wrote, so it is trusted for performance mods too. plate and model can never be written this way, whatever is passed.
RestoreVehicleAppearance(vehicleId)SERVER

Push the stored appearance back onto the car for every player who can see it. The undo for anything a client applied locally.

ParamTypeDescription
vehicleIdnumber|tableVehicle ID, or a vehicle reference
-- The customer left without paying: strip the parts they were trying on
exports.whip_core:RestoreVehicleAppearance(vehicleId)
Returns: boolean, string|nil
Vehicle mods replicate. A client with network control that calls SetVehicleMod changes the car for everyone who can see it, and none of that touches the server. That is what makes a live preview look right to bystanders, and it is why an abandoned preview leaves a car wearing parts nobody paid for until this is called.
HoldVehicleAppearance(vehicleId, held)CLIENT

Mark this vehicle as being previewed. The stored look only ever changes through SetVehicleAppearance (a client's report of how a car looks changes nothing but its dirt), so the hold does two things: whip does not report the preview (or log it as a mismatch) while it is on, and if your resource stops or crashes while holding it, whip puts the car's stored look back, so unpaid preview parts come off. Releasing reports the car immediately.

ParamTypeDescription
vehicleIdnumberVehicle ID
heldbooleantrue to hold, false to release
Returns: true, or false, reason: another resource holds the car, or you are releasing a hold that is not yours. Releasing a car nobody holds is true.
exports.whip_core:HoldVehicleAppearance(vehicleId, true)   -- before the first preview
-- ... player tries parts on, buys some, leaves ...
exports.whip_core:HoldVehicleAppearance(vehicleId, false)  -- once the car is real again
Always release it. A hold left set means this client never reports that car again (its dirt stops following it). Release it on close and on death. If your resource stops or crashes while holding one, whip releases it for you and puts the car's stored look back.
The full shop pattern. Hold → let the player preview locally → SetVehicleAppearance for what they paid for → RestoreVehicleAppearance to strip what they did not → release the hold.
SetVehicleData / GetVehicleData / GetAllVehicleData / ClearVehicleDataSERVERCLIENT

Attach arbitrary data to a vehicle: anything json-encodable, keyed by name. Persisted in the vehicle's own row and replicated to every client with the car in scope. Never clamped, drawn, decayed or consumed: whip stores it and hands it back.

ParamTypeDescription
vehicleIdnumber|tableVehicle ID, or a vehicle reference ({ entity = veh } for a handle). Set and Clear are server-only; Get and GetAll work on both sides
keystring1–40 characters of [A-Za-z0-9_]
valueanyAnything json-encodable, false included. nil removes it.
Returns: boolean, string|nil for writes; the value (a stored false reads back as false, on both sides), or a copy of the block, for reads
Server writes, client reads. The same trust model stats follow. SetVehicleDataMany writes several keys in one replication and one database write; ClearAllVehicleData removes all of your keys, for uninstalling a whole kit.
A key belongs to the resource that wrote it first. Any resource can read it; writing or clearing another resource's key is refused, with a reason naming the owner. So two scripts that both happen to use level cannot overwrite each other, and one script's ClearAllVehicleData cannot wipe another's data off the same car. Who owns which key is saved with the data, so it survives a restart.
Bounded at 32 keys per resource per car, of 40 characters, and not indexed. It is storage attached to a car, not a database. See the Vehicle Data guide for when to build a table instead.
-- server
exports.whip_core:SetVehicleData(vehicleId, 'turbo', { grade = 'A' })

-- client (the same vehicleId — or the entity, as { entity = veh })
local turbo = exports.whip_core:GetVehicleData(vehicleId, 'turbo')
exports.whip_core:OnVehicleDataChange('turbo', function(vehicleId, value, old, entity) --[[...]] end)
SetVehicleDataMany(vehicleId, values)SERVER

Attach several data values in one replication and one database write. The batch edition of SetVehicleData, for installing a whole kit: each key still fires its own whip_core:vehicle:dataChanged event after the commit, but the block crosses the wire and reaches the row once.

ParamTypeDescription
vehicleIdnumber|tableVehicle ID, or a vehicle reference
valuestable{ [key] = value }: keys are 1–40 characters of [A-Za-z0-9_], values anything json-encodable
Returns: number written, or false, reason when nothing was written (the whole batch refused, or no key fit)
A batch cannot remove keys. nil cannot sit in a Lua table, so there is no way to express "delete this" here: use ClearVehicleData (or ClearAllVehicleData) for removal. And the ceilings still apply: keys past your resource's 32-key limit on that car are skipped and logged, while a batch that would push the serialized block past 8KB is rolled back whole: "some of your keys landed" is a worse answer than "none did". A batch that touches a key another resource owns is refused whole, naming the key.
-- Fitting a kit: one replication, one write
local written = exports.whip_core:SetVehicleDataMany(vehicleId, {
    kit       = 'stage2',
    fittedBy  = player.charId,
    distances = { 250, 777, 1400 },
})
ClearAllVehicleData(vehicleId)SERVER

Remove every data value your resource put on a vehicle, in one call: the uninstall that takes a whole kit off. Other resources' keys on the same car are left alone. Replicates, writes through to the row, and fires one whip_core:vehicle:dataChanged per key removed, so a listener on someone else's key is never told it was cleared.

ParamTypeDescription
vehicleIdnumber|tableVehicle ID, or a vehicle reference
Returns: boolean, string|nil: ok, and why not (no such vehicle, or the write failed)
This clears data, not stats. A car's fuel, nitrous and every other registered stat are untouched: for taking one of those off, see ClearVehicleStat.
OnVehicleDataChange(key, callback, id, opts)SERVER

Be told when one piece of vehicle data changes, on any vehicle: the server half of the client export of the same name, and the targeted alternative to the whip_core:vehicle:dataChanged broadcast, which enters every resource with a handler on every data change anywhere. Subscribing by key is entered only when that key moved.

ParamTypeDescription
keystringThe data key to watch
callbackfunction(vehicleId, value, cleared, old), or one table, with table = true
idstring|nilOnly for two listeners on one key; registering again under the same id replaces
optstable|nil{ table = true, now = true }: may also go third, in place of id
Returns: boolean registered
Two options make it the same on both sides. table = true hands the callback one table ({ vehicleId, key, value, old, cleared, resource } here, with entity on the client), so you never have to remember which side puts what third. now = true also calls it once straight away for every car that already carries the key, so there is no separate "read what is there first" step. Without options the positional arguments differ by side: the server passes cleared third and old fourth, the client passes old third and the entity fourth. They differ between listeners too: OnVehicleStatChange passes (vehicleId, value, previous, cleared, source), so a callback copied from a stat listener gets the old value where it expects cleared. Use table = true for every listener and the question never comes up.
Whip.register(function()
    exports.whip_core:OnVehicleDataChange('kit', function(change)
        if change.cleared then
            -- the kit came off: change.old is what it was
        end
    end, { table = true, now = true })
end)
Register it inside Whip.register. The subscription lives in whip_core, so it is lost when whip_core restarts; Whip.register runs your function again when it comes back. It is dropped automatically when your own resource stops.
WatchVehicleData(key, data)CLIENT

Run code while a vehicle in scope carries a piece of data: the data twin of WatchVehicleStat. For the things every client has to do to a car itself, because GTA replicates none of them: an engine sound, wheel stance, handling. Returns a watcher id for UnwatchVehicleData, or false, why.

exports.whip_core:WatchVehicleData('engine', {
    onGained  = function(entity, value) ForceUseAudioGameObject(entity, value.audio) end,  -- every car in scope
    onLost    = function(entity, value) --[[ put it back ]] end,
    onStart   = function(entity, value) --[[ apply handling ]] end,     -- you got in and drive it
    onStop    = function(entity, value) --[[ restore handling ]] end,   -- you got out
    driverOnly = true,
})
FieldTypeDescription
onGainedfunction|nil(entity, value, vehicleId): a car in scope has the key: it arrived, streamed in, or was given it. Cars already in scope are announced at registration
onChangedfunction|nil(entity, value, old, vehicleId): a new value on a car that still has the key. Without it, a change fires onLost(old) then onGained(new)
onLostfunction|nil(entity, value, vehicleId): the key was removed, or the car left scope; value is what it was
onStartfunction|nil(entity, value, vehicleId): this watcher starts for the car (with driverOnly: you are now driving it)
onStopfunction|nil(entity, value, vehicleId), and stops (you got out, the key went, the car went). A new value while started fires onStop(old) then onStart(new)
driverOnlybool|nilNarrow onStart/onStop to the car this player drives: for handling, which only the driver owns. Default false
idstring|nilOnly for two watchers on one key; registering again under the same id replaces (with onStop)
Returns: string|false, string|nil: watcher id, or false and why not
Compared by content. A car whose other data changed does not re-fire your callbacks: worth knowing when re-applying costs something (setting an engine sound resets the radio).
One end never reaches onStop: your own resource stopping. Put things back in your own onResourceStop too, as with WatchVehicleStat. whip_core stopping stops your resource first (dependency 'whip_core'), so that is the same end; a resource without the dependency puts things back in Whip.onCoreLost as well.
SetVehicleHandlingLayer(vehicle, name, spec) · ClearVehicleHandlingLayer(name) · GetVehicleHandlingBase(vehicle, field)CLIENT

Never write handling yourself: declare a layer. whip_core is the one owner of handling on the car this player drives: it captures each field's stock value before the first write, applies every resource's layers, and puts the car back on every way out (your layer cleared, a different car, the car gone, your resource or whip_core stopping). Two features writing the same field directly undo each other: a turbo would wipe an engine swap the moment it let go.

-- an engine swap: absolute values
exports.whip_core:SetVehicleHandlingLayer({ entity = veh }, 'engine', {
    set = { fInitialDriveForce = 0.34, nInitialDriveGears = 6 },
})
-- a suspension tune: multipliers, applied after every set — so it tunes the swapped car
exports.whip_core:SetVehicleHandlingLayer({ entity = veh }, 'tune', {
    scale = { fSuspensionForce = 1.2, fSuspensionCompDamp = 1.1 },
})
-- longer gearing on whatever engine is in: an amount added after the sets (whip_autos' top speed)
exports.whip_core:SetVehicleHandlingLayer({ entity = veh }, 'topSpeed', {
    add = { fInitialDriveMaxFlatVel = 42.2 },
})
exports.whip_core:ClearVehicleHandlingLayer('tune')
More power is SetVehiclePower, not a layer. fInitialDriveMaxFlatVel is the gearing (the speed at redline in top gear), so scaling it with a turbo stretches every gear as the boost builds.
ParamTypeDescription
vehicletable|numberA vehicle reference: { entity = veh } for a handle
namestringYour layer's name, one per feature. Setting it again replaces it
spec.settable|nil{ field = value }: absolute values, in handling.meta units. Fields are CHandlingData floats (f…) and whole numbers (n…); gears are kept to 1–7
spec.addtable|nil{ field = amount }: amounts added (−1000 to 1000) after every layer's set, so they follow an engine swap; several layers' add up
spec.scaletable|nil{ field = factor }: multipliers (0.01–100), applied after every layer's set and add
spec.ordernumber|nilWhen two layers set one field, the higher order wins. Default 0
Returns: SetVehicleHandlingLayer → boolean, string|nil (ok, why not) · ClearVehicleHandlingLayer → boolean removed · GetVehicleHandlingBase → a field's value after every set and add and before any scale: what a multiplier multiplies
Only the driver. Physics belongs to whoever drives the car, so set layers from a driverOnly watcher's onStart (WatchVehicleStat or WatchVehicleData) and clear them in its onStop. One car at a time: a layer on a different car puts the previous one back first. Drivetrain changes are committed for you (the transmission rebuild, the high gear).
SetVehiclePower(vehicle, name, multiplier) · ClearVehiclePower(name)CLIENT

Ask for more (or less) engine torque on the car this player drives: a turbo's boost, a shot of nitrous. The gearing is left alone, so top speed comes out of the physics: more torque is more speed where drag held the car back, and none past the rev limiter in top gear. Ask again whenever the amount changes; the car gets the product of every resource's ask, written every frame, and is back to normal the frame nothing is asked.

ParamTypeDescription
vehicletable|numberA vehicle reference: { entity = veh } for a handle
namestringYour ask's name, one per feature. Asking again replaces it
multipliernumber0 to 10: 1.25 is a quarter more torque, 1.0 the engine as it is
-- boost from 0 to 1: up to a quarter more torque
exports.whip_core:SetVehiclePower({ entity = veh }, 'turbo', 1.0 + 0.25 * boost)
exports.whip_core:ClearVehiclePower('turbo')
Returns: SetVehiclePower → boolean, string|nil (ok, why not) · ClearVehiclePower → boolean removed
Only the driver, one car at a time, as with layers: ask from a driverOnly watcher and clear in its onStop. Asking for a different car drops what was asked for the last one. Don't call SetVehicleCheatPowerIncrease yourself: the last write in a frame wins, so a second writer undoes whip's.
SetVehicleRevRange(vehicle, engine)CLIENT

Say which engine a vehicle's rev dial follows, on this player's game. The dial goes by the engine: its model in Config.VehicleHud.rpmByModel, else rpmElectric for an electric motor, else its kind in rpmByClass. A vehicle's engine is its own model until you say otherwise, so an engine swap tells whip the donor: a dump truck with an F1 engine then revs to 15k like an F1. whip_autos does this for every car in view with a swap, and for the shop's previews.

-- this car carries a Formula engine
exports.whip_core:SetVehicleRevRange({ entity = veh }, 'formula')
-- or a range outright, in thousands of rpm
exports.whip_core:SetVehicleRevRange({ entity = veh }, { max = 11, idle = 1.2 })
-- back to its own engine
exports.whip_core:SetVehicleRevRange({ entity = veh }, nil)
ParamTypeDescription
vehicletable|numberA vehicle reference: { entity = veh } for a handle
enginestring|table|nilA vehicle model's spawn name (its engine), { max, idle? } in thousands of rpm (max 2–20, idle 0 or more and under max), or nil for the vehicle's own engine
Returns: boolean, string|nil: ok, or why not (no such vehicle, not a vehicle model, a range out of bounds, or another running resource already set it)
Every player's game, like the swap itself. It changes only this player's dial, so set it where you apply the engine on every client (a WatchVehicleData watcher on every car in view) and clear it in onLost. The car this player is sitting in gets its new dial at once. A resource's settings are dropped when it stops.
IsVehicleElectric(vehicle)CLIENT

Is this vehicle's engine electric? GTA's own flag on its engine's model: its own, or the one SetVehicleRevRange says it carries (an engine swap). whip_fuel gives electric cars no fuel; a charging resource would look here too.

ParamTypeDescription
vehicletable|numberA vehicle reference: { entity = veh } for a handle
Returns: boolean: false for a vehicle that is not here, or on a game build without the flag
SetVehicleDialGear(vehicle, gear)CLIENT

Say which forward gear the rev dial shows for a vehicle, when your resource drives the gears itself. whip_autos' gearbox computer does: it gives GTA one gear and changes that gear's ratio, so GTA's own gear number stays 1 while the car is really in 3rd. Reverse and N stay the game's.

Or 'speed', when your resource moves the car itself rather than its gearbox, as a recorded drive does by setting its speed every frame. GTA's gear then stays where it was, often 0, which the dial reads as R. With 'speed' the dial works the gear out from how fast the car goes and its gear ratios, and shows R when it goes backwards. Clear it when the car is handed back, and GTA's gearbox is put in the gear the dial was showing, so whoever drives on carries on in it.

exports.whip_core:SetVehicleDialGear({ entity = veh }, 3)
-- you move it, not its gearbox: worked out from its speed
exports.whip_core:SetVehicleDialGear({ entity = veh }, 'speed')
-- back to the game's gear
exports.whip_core:SetVehicleDialGear({ entity = veh }, nil)
ParamTypeDescription
vehicletable|numberA vehicle reference: { entity = veh } for a handle
gearnumber|string|nilA whole number, 1 to 20; 'speed' to work it out from the car's speed; or nil for the game's gear again
Returns: boolean, string|nil: ok, or why not (no such vehicle, a gear out of bounds, or another running resource already set it)
This player's dial only. Set it on the driver's game and clear it when you hand the gears back. A resource's settings are dropped when it stops.
UnwatchVehicleData(watcherId)CLIENT

Stop one of your data watchers. Fires onStop for anything it had started, not onLost: nothing about the world changed. Watchers are dropped automatically when their resource stops.

ParamTypeDescription
watcherIdstringThe id WatchVehicleData returned
Returns: boolean removed
RegisterVehicleStat(name, config)SERVER

Register a stat that every vehicle carries: nitrous, engine wear, a tuning chip, anything with a number. It is saved with the vehicle and replicated to every client sitting in it, so a passenger sees it change live. Give it a hud block and it becomes one of the small gauges orbiting the rev dial, with no further wiring (five at most are shown, by order).

The name is letters, digits and _, not starting with a digit, up to 32 characters: 'nitro', 'turbo_boost'. Anything else ('turbo-boost', '2step') is refused with a reason.
FieldTypeDescription
defaultnumberWhat a vehicle starts on
min / maxnumberThe range it lives in
persistboolean|stringtrue (default), false, or 'presence': see below
decaynumber|nilPoints changed every decayInterval seconds; negative drains it
decayIntervalnumber|nilSeconds between decay steps. Default 10
hudtable|nil{ label, icon, color, order, iconOnly, showAboveZero, showWhenPresent, hideWhenEmpty, noCritical }: draws a gauge around the rev dial. icon is an SVG path in a 24x24 box; order its place (lower first; fuel is 1); below 20% it flashes red unless noCritical. The dial draws gauges in white, so color is not used there, and an iconOnly stat (an on/off light) gets no gauge
consumetable|nil{ maxRate, driverOnly, clearAtMin, interval, slack }: the whole burn-down protocol, for values that fall. See below.
livetable|nil{ maxRate, driverOnly, interval, slack }: the same protocol for values the client drives up and down. See below.
displaytable|nilHow the value reads on its gauge and the /whip Vehicles page, instead of a percentage. { unit = 'psi', range = { -3, 30 } }: what the bottom and top of the stat's range read. { unit = '°C', points = { { 0, 20 }, { 50, 90 }, { 100, 130 } } }: a curve, percent of the range to reading, straight lines between. { ends = { 'E', 'F' } }: the gauge shows these at its empty and full ends and no number. decimals 0-2. The stat's own min..max is unchanged: this only says how it reads.
Leave decay out to disable it: do not set it to 0. Zero is a real value in Lua, so a decay of 0 ticks every interval and changes nothing: a stat that looks configured and does nothing.
clearAtMin requires default == min, and registration is refused otherwise. Clearing a stat makes it read as its default. So a stat registered with default = 100, min = 0, clearAtMin = true would drain to empty, be removed, and immediately read as full again: a stat that refills itself by running out, with every individual piece doing exactly what it was told. Use clearAtMin for installables (default 0, where absent and empty mean the same thing) and leave it off for anything a vehicle always has, the way fuel does.
The registration belongs to your resource and is dropped when your resource stops, so a restart never leaves a stat behind with no code to mean anything by it. Names whip owns, engine and the damage stats, cannot be taken (fuel is whip_fuel's).
Register a stat before you write it. SetVehicleStat, SetVehicleStats and AddVehicleStat refuse a name nobody registered, with 'unknown vehicle stat "x" — RegisterVehicleStat it first', so a typo such as 'feul' never lands on a car.
Registering a stat does not put it on every car. A vehicle's replicated block carries only what it actually has; an absent key means "at its registered default", and every reader resolves that for you. So ten registered stats cost nothing on the cars that never carry them.

persist: the stat, or the stat's value

Three settings, because "remember this stat" and "remember this number" are different questions:

ValueWhat survives a restartUse for
trueThe value, exactlyFuel, nitrous: the number is the point
falseNothingAnything derived or momentary
'presence'That the car has it, at the value it was given when fittedFittings with a live value: a turbo, a temperature sensor

'presence' writes when the stat appears on a car and when it is taken off, and leaves it alone in between. A value moving five times a second costs nothing on disk, and what comes back after a restart is the resting value the part was fitted at: which for anything live is the right place to start.

Returns: boolean, string|nil: ok, and why not
Whip.register(function()
    exports.whip_core:RegisterVehicleStat('nos', {
        default = 0, min = 0, max = 100,
        hud = { label = 'NOS', icon = 'M6 2h6v20H6z', color = '#60a5fa', order = 2 },
    })
end)

-- later, once a car has a bottle fitted
exports.whip_core:AddVehicleStat(vehicleId, 'nos', -10, 'mynos:boost')

consume and live: stats the client drives

Some vehicle values can only be known by the client. How much nitrous was actually burned, how far the throttle is open, what the engine is revving at: the server has none of it, and asking for it would cost more than being told. But a client that tells the server a number is a client that can lie about it.

whip owns that whole problem, in two shapes. You declare which one a stat is; you never write the event, the driver check or the rate cap.

consumelive
The valueonly fallsrises and falls
Client reportshow much was used, as a running totalwhat it is worth now
Client callsConsumeVehicleStat({ entity = veh }, name, delta)
ConsumeVehicleStats({ entity = veh }, deltas) for several at once		ReportVehicleStat({ entity = veh }, name, value)
Server capshow fast it can drainhow fast it can rise
Forfuel, nitrous, tyre wearturbo boost, engine heat, charge

What both give you

  • The event. There is none to write, name or secure: the framework owns it and batches every stat on one vehicle into a single message.
  • The driver check. driverOnly defaults to true. A passenger reporting on the car they are sitting in is how somebody drains a stranger's tank from the back seat.
  • The wall clock. Whatever the client claims, the server refuses anything that moved further than maxRate could carry it since the last accepted report. A modified client sending 100 every frame gets the same ramp an honest one does.
  • Recovery. A report lost to the rate limiter costs nothing: the next one carries the current picture and the server works out the difference.
Draining more than one stat? Use ConsumeVehicleStats({ entity = veh }, deltas). It takes a table of [name] = amount and does exactly what the single version does for each one (same accumulator, same per-stat cadence, same server cap) in one call. Every call into whip_core has a fixed cost, so ten stats in one call is far cheaper than ten calls. 
-- Build what moved, hand it over once.
local used = {}
for i = 1, 10 do used['part' .. i] = FULL * moved / distance[i] end
exports.whip_core:ConsumeVehicleStats({ entity = veh }, used)
The same rule applies reading: one GetAllVehicleStats beats ten GetVehicleStat calls, for the same reason.

The fields

FieldDefaultMeaning
maxRaterequiredUnits per second, flat out. The ceiling the server believes.
driverOnlytrueOnly the driver may report
interval1.0 / 0.5 sHow often the client sends (consume / live). Both floor at 0.25 s.
slack1.25Headroom over maxRate for network jitter
clearAtMinfalseconsume only: take the stat off the car when it bottoms out
A stat may declare one or the other, never both. They are two answers to "who owns this number and how does it change", and a stat with both would have the client subtracting through one path and asserting through the other, with whichever arrived last winning. Registration refuses it.

A live stat, end to end

-- Server: declare it. Nothing else here handles the reporting.
exports.whip_core:RegisterVehicleStat('boost', {
    default = 1, min = 1, max = 100,
    persist = 'presence',      -- the turbo is fitted; the number is momentary

    live = {
        maxRate  = 33.3,        -- nothing to full in three seconds, flat out
        interval = 0.25,        -- how often other people's gauges update
    },

    hud = {
        label = 'Boost', color = '#facc15', order = 6,
        showWhenPresent = true,
    },
})
-- Client: work out the value however you like, and say what it is.
exports.whip_core:ReportVehicleStat({ entity = veh }, 'boost', level)
interval is about other people, not about you. It governs how often the value reaches the server and therefore everyone else's gauges. Whatever the value drives locally (engine power, a sound, an effect) is yours to apply every frame and is not waiting on it.

Your own gauge need not wait on it either: register a SetVehicleStatDisplay provider and the local dial reads your simulation directly. Once you have, interval only serves passengers and the server's record, and a slower one is the cheapest performance win available, because reporting is the most expensive thing whip does on the server.
Reporting will not create a stat. A report for a stat the vehicle does not carry is refused. That is deliberate: without it, reporting boost on a stock car would fit a turbo to it.
Live values ride their own statebag key. Ordinary stats live in one block on the vehicle; anything registered live has its current value on a second, smaller key, so a number changing several times a second does not re-send every other stat on the car with it.

This is invisible if you read stats through GetVehicleStat, GetAllVehicleStats, OnVehicleStatChange or WatchVehicleStat: they all know about both. It only matters if you read the vehicle's statebag directly, which you should not: presence is recorded in the main block and the current value of a live stat is in the other, so a raw read of one key answers half the question.

Reacting to a stat: WatchVehicleStat

Registering a stat is one call. Putting it on a car is one call. Reacting to one is WatchVehicleStat: you say what should happen, and the framework decides when.

whip_core is already told when a stat appears or disappears on any vehicle in scope: the server writes the block once and every client that can see the car receives it. The watcher hands that over directly, so nothing you write ever polls a statebag, caches an answer, or invalidates a cache.

Two pairs of callbacks

Picking the right pair is the only thing to get right here.

onGained / onLostonStart / onStop
Answer towhat is true in the worldwhat this watcher is doing
Fires forevery vehicle in scope, alwaysonly what whileHeld runs for
Respects driverOnlynoyes
Getting out of the carnothing: the car still has itonStop
Use fora badge, a sound, an effect on any car nearbysetting up and tearing down your own work
If you modify a vehicle and must put it back, you want onStart/onStop. Getting out of a car is not a stat change, so onLost will not fire, and being scope-wide, it fires for cars you never touched. onStop covers getting out, losing the stat, the car despawning and somebody else pulling the part.
One way a watch ends WITHOUT onStop: your own resource stopping. When your resource stops, the functions onStop would call are going away too, so put the car back yourself in your own onResourceStop, as the example below does. whip_core stopping is the same case: with dependency 'whip_core' it stops your resource first. A resource without the dependency keeps running, and its watcher dies with whip_core, so it puts the car back in Whip.onCoreLost too.
-- A turbo satellite, in full. There is no loop and no cache anywhere in it.
exports.whip_core:WatchVehicleStat('boost', {
    onStart   = function(entity)             captureHandling(entity)  end,
    whileHeld = function(entity, value, dt) simulate(entity, dt)     end,
    onStop    = function()                   restoreHandling()        end,

    interval   = 50,      -- ms between whileHeld calls. 0 means every frame.
    driverOnly = true,    -- only the car this player is driving
})

-- The end onStop never hears about (whip_core stopping stops this resource first). restoreHandling must be
-- safe to call twice.
AddEventHandler('onResourceStop', function(res)          -- this resource is stopping
    if res == GetCurrentResourceName() then restoreHandling() end
end)
Scope is not configurable, and that is the point. onGained and onLost always fire for every vehicle in scope, exactly as the server replicated them. You cannot accidentally build the version where one player can see a car has something and another cannot.
interval is yours. Set it to 0 and whileHeld runs every frame: nothing stops you. Worth knowing what you are buying: a full frame of work at 120fps is 120 calls a second, and most things driven by a stat change far more slowly than that. The turbo example above settled on 50ms and a full three-second spool still gets sixty samples. When in doubt, start at 50 and lower it if you can feel the difference.

driverOnly narrows whileHeld to the car this player is driving. Anything that writes handling or physics wants it, because you only own the car you are in, and handling in particular is attached to a vehicle's handling class, so modifying a car you do not own affects every car sharing it.

WatchVehicleStat(name, data)CLIENT

Run code while a vehicle in scope carries a stat. name can be one stat or a list of them. Returns a watcher id for UnwatchVehicleStat and SetVehicleStatWatchInterval, or false and why if the stat name or the table was malformed (as WatchVehicleData does).

Several stats, one call. Pass a list and every callback gets the stat's name second, so one set of callbacks serves a whole kit: onGained(entity, name, value), onStart(entity, name, value), onStop(entity, name). The one id you get back covers the whole list. 
-- Which gauges does the car I am driving carry? Told, never polled.
exports.whip_core:WatchVehicleStat({ 'part1', 'part2', 'part3' }, {
    onStart = function(entity, name) fitted[name] = true  end,
    onStop  = function(entity, name) fitted[name] = nil   end,
    driverOnly = true,
})
With a list, whileHeld runs once per stat. Every call is a crossing into your resource, so ten stats with a whileHeld at 100ms is a hundred crossings a second. If the work is one job per car (draining ten gauges from one distance, say), use onStart/onStop to know what is fitted and run the job in a loop of your own that exists only while something is.
FieldTypeDescription
onGainedfunction|nil(entity, value): any vehicle in scope gained the stat
onLostfunction|nil(entity): any vehicle in scope lost it
onStartfunction|nil(entity, value): whileHeld is about to start running for this vehicle
onStopfunction|nil(entity): whileHeld has stopped running for this vehicle
whileHeldfunction|nil(entity, value, dt): repeatedly, while held. dt is real elapsed seconds; only a stall is clamped (to 0.25 s, or twice your interval if that is longer), so a slow interval integrates at the right speed. May return a number: this client's own reading of the stat on that car, which its gauge around the rev dial shows instead of the replicated value until onStop (return nothing to show the replicated one)
intervalnumber|nilms between whileHeld calls. Default 0 (every frame)
driverOnlybool|nilNarrow whileHeld, onStart and onStop to the car this player drives. Default false
Returns: string|false, string|nil watcher id, or false and why
Already-present cars are announced on registration. A watcher registered at resource start is immediately told about every vehicle already in scope carrying the stat, so onGained is the only place you ever have to write your setup.
UnwatchVehicleStat(watcherId)CLIENT

Stop a watcher. Fires onStop for anything it was still running for, so a satellite that unwatches mid-drive still gets to put the vehicle back. Does not fire onLost: nothing about the world changed.

ParamTypeDescription
watcherIdstringThe id returned by WatchVehicleStat: a list registration's id stops every stat in it
Returns: boolean removed
Watchers are owned by the resource that registered them and are dropped automatically when it stops, so this is only needed to stop watching while still running. It only stops your watchers (and SetVehicleStatWatchInterval only retunes yours).
SetVehicleStatDisplay(name, fn)CLIENT

Draw a local reading for a stat on this client's vehicle gauges (around the rev dial), instead of the replicated one. For a value this client is already calculating in real time.

Already running a WatchVehicleStat watcher for it? Return the reading from whileHeld instead. The gauges call a provider on every repaint, each call a crossing into your resource; a number returned from whileHeld is already in whip_core's hands. whip_autos' turbo does this. A reading from a watcher wins over a provider for the same stat.

A stat's value normally makes a round trip: the client reports it, the server validates and clamps it, the statebag replicates it back. That is right for anything the server owns, and it is a strange thing to do to a number this client just computed: a turbo satellite simulating boost every 50ms would leave the driver's own needle waiting a quarter of a second for its own arithmetic to come home.

exports.whip_core:SetVehicleStatDisplay('boost', function(entity, replicated)
    -- Only the car this client is simulating; nil defers to the replicated value
    if entity ~= myTunedVehicle then return nil end
    return liveBoost
end)
ParamTypeDescription
namestringRegistered stat name
fnfunction(entity, replicated) → a number, or nil to use the replicated value
Returns: true, or false, reason: refused when another resource already provides this stat's reading
It changes the number, never whether there is one. Presence stays the replicated answer, so a provider cannot draw a gauge for a part the car has not got, and it does not write the stat, does not reach the server, and does not change what anyone else sees. A passenger reads the validated value.

Which means your provider must decide whether this client is the one computing it. A passenger in the same car reaches the provider too, and handing them a value only the driver maintains replaces a live number with a stale one.
Repaints follow your whileHeld tick. If the stat has a WatchVehicleStat watcher running for the car you are driving, the gauges are repainted after each tick, at your cadence, with no export crossing, and with no NUI message when nothing moved. Without a watcher, the gauges still pick your reading up on their own repaints, whenever a stat on the car changes and at least once a second while you are in it, so the needle moves about once a second. Run a watcher when it has to move smoothly.
ClearVehicleStatDisplay(name)CLIENT

ClearVehicleStatDisplay stops drawing your local reading; the gauge returns to the replicated value. Providers are owned by the resource that registered them and are dropped automatically when it stops, so this is only needed to stop early. The gauges repaint by themselves when a reading changes: there is nothing to refresh by hand.

Returns: true or false, reason (not set, or set by another resource)
SetVehicleStatShown(name, fn) · ClearVehicleStatShown(name)CLIENT

Whether a stat's gauge is drawn on a car at all. fn(entity) answers false to hide it on that car: whip_fuel hides the fuel gauge on an electric car. Asked once for each car this player sits in, and the answer kept for that car, so answer from what the car is, not from something that changes while they sit in it. The stat itself is untouched; only this player's dial. One rule a stat, the setter's; dropped when that resource stops, or cleared with ClearVehicleStatShown.

exports.whip_core:SetVehicleStatShown('fuel', function(entity)
    return not exports.whip_core:IsVehicleElectric({ entity = entity })
end)
Returns: true or false, reason (no name or rule, or another resource's rule on that stat)
SetVehicleStatIcon(name, fn) · ClearVehicleStatIcon(name)CLIENT

A stat's gauge icon by the car. fn(entity) answers the icon to draw on that car, or nil for the stat's own: whip_fuel's pump points to the side the car's filler is on. An icon is one of the dial's own ('fuel', 'fuel_left', 'fuel_right', 'turbo', 'nitro', 'coolant', 'hack', 'weapon') or an SVG path in a 24x24 viewBox. Asked once for each car this player sits in, as the shown rule above is. One rule a stat, the setter's; dropped when that resource stops, or cleared with ClearVehicleStatIcon.

exports.whip_core:SetVehicleStatIcon('fuel', function(entity)
    local p = exports.whip_core:GetVehiclePoint({ entity = entity }, 'fuel')
    if p and p.fixed and p.side == 'left' then return 'fuel_left' end
end)
Returns: true or false, reason (no name or rule, or another resource's rule on that stat)
OnVehicleStatChange(name, callback, id, opts)CLIENT

Be told every time a stat's value changes, on any vehicle in scope. The callback receives (vehicleId, value, old, entity), or one table, with { table = true }. Use this when you care about the number changing; use WatchVehicleStat when you care about a car having the stat.

The same two options as the server's. table = true: one table, { vehicleId, key, value, old, cleared, entity }, with the field names the server uses. now = true: also called once straight away for every car in range that carries the stat. The options can go third or, after an id, fourth.
exports.whip_core:OnVehicleStatChange('fuel', function(vehicleId, value, old, entity)
    if value < 10 and (old or 100) >= 10 then
        exports.whip_core:Notify('Running low on fuel', 'warning')
    end
end)
ParamTypeDescription
namestringRegistered stat name
callbackfunction(vehicleId, value, old, entity)
Returns: boolean registered
OnVehicleStatChange(name, callback, id, opts)SERVER

Be told when one stat changes, on any vehicle, without being woken for the rest. The server-side counterpart to the client's OnVehicleStatChange.

exports.whip_core:OnVehicleStatChange('fuel', function(vehicleId, value, previous, cleared, source)
    if cleared then -- the stat came off the car entirely
    end
end)

-- Or: one table, and the current value of every car that carries it, straight away
exports.whip_core:OnVehicleStatChange('fuel', function(change)
    -- change.vehicleId, change.key, change.value, change.old, change.cleared, change.source
end, { table = true, now = true })
ParamTypeDescription
namestringA stat's name (yours or another resource's), or '*' for every stat
callbackfunction(vehicleId, value, previous, cleared, source); for '*', (vehicleId, name, value, previous, cleared, source). Or one table, with table = true (change.key is the stat)
idany|nilOnly for two listeners on one stat; registering again under the same id replaces
optstable|nil{ table = true, now = true }: may also go third, in place of id. now reports with source = 'now', for every car that already carries the stat. now = 'all' (a named stat): every car whip has instead, each with the value it reads as, its default included (a car on the default does not carry the stat, so now = true misses it). Use it when you decide something from the value (an engine hold, a warning light); registering again with it after the stat's default changed visits them all again
Returns: boolean registered
Name the stats you want; '*' is the costly one. A named listener is entered only when that stat moves. '*' is entered for every stat change on every car, every fuel report and boost step included. '*' is server only.
The callback must not wait. It runs inside whip's stat write: slow work (a database write, a wait) goes in a CreateThread.
Register it inside Whip.register, with your stats. The subscription lives in whip_core, so it is lost when whip_core restarts; Whip.register runs your function again when it comes back. Put it in the same function that calls RegisterVehicleStat. It is dropped automatically when your own resource stops.
HasVehicleStat(vehicle, name)CLIENTSERVER

Does this vehicle actually carry this stat, as opposed to reading as its registered default? The question GetVehicleStat cannot answer. Same call on both sides: a bare number is a vehicleId, and an entity handle is { entity = veh } (a vehicle reference).

ParamTypeDescription
vehiclenumber|tableThe vehicle ID, or a vehicle reference: an entity is { entity = veh }
namestringRegistered stat name
if exports.whip_core:HasVehicleStat(vehicleId, 'nos') then
    return false, 'This car already has a bottle fitted'
end
Returns: boolean
GetVehicleStat(veh, name) > 0 is not the same question. Reads resolve an absent stat to its registered default, so a stat that rests at any non-zero value reports true for every car on the server, including ones that have never carried it. Use this whenever you mean "is one fitted".
In a loop, prefer WatchVehicleStat: it is told the answer rather than asking for it.
GetVehicleStat / SetVehicleStat / AddVehicleStat / GetAllVehicleStatsSERVER

Read and write registered vehicle stats. Writes are clamped to the range the stat was registered with, saved, and replicated to everyone in the vehicle. GetAllVehicleStats returns every registered stat with defaults filled in.

ParamTypeDescription
vehicleIdnumber|tableVehicle ID, or a vehicle reference
namestringThe registered stat name: an unregistered one is refused
value / deltanumberWhat to set it to, or add to it
changeSourcestring|nilA label for the change event, e.g. 'refuel:pump'
local fuel = exports.whip_core:GetVehicleStat(vehicleId, 'fuel')
exports.whip_core:SetVehicleStat(vehicleId, 'fuel', 100.0, 'refuel:pump')

local ok, err = exports.whip_core:AddVehicleStat(vehicleId, 'nos', -10, 'mynos:boost')
if not ok then print(err) end
Returns: GetVehicleStat → number|nil; GetAllVehicleStats → { [name] = value }; writes → boolean, string|nil: every refusal says why (no such car, not a number, a stat nobody registered). GetVehicleStat and GetAllVehicleStats also work on the client, for a car streamed in near the player.
GetStoredVehicleStats answers a different question. GetAllVehicleStats fills in defaults, so it cannot tell you whether a car has a stat. GetStoredVehicleStats returns only what the vehicle actually carries, which is how "is a nitrous bottle fitted?" is answerable at all.
SetVehicleStats(vehicleId, values, changeSource)SERVER

Write several stats to one vehicle in a single replication. Every stat write re-sends the vehicle's whole block, so setting ten of them one at a time puts the same table on the wire ten times: nine of those describing a state already superseded by the time they arrive.

ParamTypeDescription
vehicleIdnumber|tableVehicle ID, or a vehicle reference
valuestable{ [statName] = value }: names nobody registered, and values that are not numbers, are skipped (and logged)
changeSourcestring|nilA label for the change events
Returns: number written: how many writes took, or false, reason when none did.
Worth reaching for whenever more than two stats move together: fitting a kit, applying a tune, resetting a car. One at a time needs nothing.
exports.whip_core:SetVehicleStats(vehicleId, {
    nitro = 100, boost = 100, coolant = 80,
}, 'mykit:install')
ClearVehicleStat(vehicleId, name)SERVER

Take a stat off one vehicle. The key leaves the stored block, the removal replicates and persists, and reads fall back to the registered default: the stat is still defined for every vehicle, this one simply has no value of its own any more. Announced through the ordinary stat-change event with cleared = true, so a listener can tell "gone" from "zero".

ParamTypeDescription
vehicleIdnumber|tableVehicle ID, or a vehicle reference
namestringRegistered stat name
Returns: boolean, string|nil: true includes "already absent"; false comes with the reason (no such vehicle, a bad name)
Setting a stat to zero is not the same thing. Zero leaves the key on the car (a bottle fitted and empty) and the row grows a field that means nothing. For anything installable, "present" is the key existing in the stored block, and this is the only call that removes it. It also resets the stat's rate-check cursor, so refitting a live stat is measured from idle rather than from wherever the value was when the part came off.
One car, not every car: to delete a stat's values everywhere, that is PurgeVehicleStat.
-- The bottle comes off with the part
exports.whip_core:ClearVehicleStat(vehicleId, 'nos')
ClearVehicleDamage(vehicle)SERVER

Forget the damage whip keeps on a car (see Damage a car keeps), so its next spawn comes out like new. Call it with a repair: it does not fix the car in the world, which only the game running it can do.

ParamTypeDescription
vehiclenumber|tableVehicle ID, or a vehicle reference
Returns: boolean, string|nil: false comes with the reason (no such vehicle)
-- Server, once the repair is paid for
local ok, err = exports.whip_core:ClearVehicleDamage(vehicleId)
if not ok then return false, err end
TriggerClientEvent('mymechanic:client:fix', source, vehicleId)   -- SetVehicleFixed on the driver's game
IsVehicleWrecked(vehicle)SERVER

Is this car wrecked: blown up, or sunk? No server native shows a sunk car, so the game running the car says it sank. A job's "car lost" check asks this.

ParamTypeDescription
vehiclenumber|tableVehicle ID, or a vehicle reference
Returns: boolean: false for a car that is not out in the world
if exports.whip_core:IsVehicleWrecked(vehicleId) then return 'lost' end
PurgeVehicleStat(name)SERVER

Delete a stat's values from every vehicle, permanently: cache, statebag and database. Each removal goes through the same path as ClearVehicleStat, so it replicates, persists and announces itself like any other. For a stat that is genuinely being retired.

ParamTypeDescription
namestringThe stat to retire
Returns: number: how many vehicles carried a value; or false, reason when another running resource has the stat registered (only it can purge it). A stat with no running owner can be purged by anyone.
This is not what a restart does, on purpose. Stopping a satellite unregisters its stats but leaves every stored value alone, so a restart never wipes a fitted part. Values are inert without a registration and come back to life when their owner does. Deleting them is something you ask for, by name, with this call, and there is no undo.
GetStoredVehicleStats(vehicleId)SERVER

Everything a vehicle actually has a stored value for, as a plain copy, with no defaults filled in. nil for a stat means no stored value, which for an installable stat is how "not fitted" is expressed. This is what the vehicle-list payloads send, so a garage card can tell a car with a spent bottle from a car that never had one.

ParamTypeDescription
vehicleIdnumberVehicle ID
Returns: table: { [name] = value }, only the stats actually stored; empty for an unknown vehicle
GetAllVehicleStats answers the other question (every registered stat with defaults filled in) and so cannot tell you whether a car has one. For a single name, HasVehicleStat is the direct test.
local stored = exports.whip_core:GetStoredVehicleStats(vehicleId)
if stored.nos ~= nil then
    -- a bottle is fitted, possibly empty; stored.nos == nil would mean none at all
end
RemoveVehicleKey(who, vehicleId)SERVER

Remove a vehicle's keys from a player's inventory. Scans all player containers, removes every key that fits this car (the same fit rule the ignition uses), syncs inventory + key cache to client.

ParamTypeDescription
whonumber|tableA person who is playing: their server id, or { charId = n }
vehicleIdnumberVehicle ID
Returns: bool, string?: true if at least one key was found and removed; otherwise false and why ('They have no key for that vehicle', 'Player not loaded', ...)
-- Impound system: confiscate keys and lock the car
exports.whip_core:RemoveVehicleKey(source, vehicleId)
exports.whip_core:SetVehicleLocked(vehicleId, true)
SpawnVehicle(vehicleId, x, y, z, heading)SERVER

Put a vehicle into the world. The server creates the entity, so there is no client hand-off and no window in which the vehicle is "out" but does not exist. Idempotent: calling it on a vehicle that is already out moves it rather than cloning it. Omit the position to use the vehicle's own saved one.

ParamTypeDescription
vehicleIdnumberThe vehicle to place
x, y, z, headingnumber|nilWhere to put it. Leave out to use its saved position. A spot with another vehicle on it, or a player in it, is refused ('Something is already parked in that spot', 'Someone is standing in that spot'), because GTA would throw one of them
local netId, err = exports.whip_core:SpawnVehicle(vehicleId, 215.8, -810.1, 30.7, 157.0)
if not netId then return false, err end
Returns: number|false: the network ID, or false plus an error message
DespawnVehicle(vehicleId)SERVER

Take a vehicle out of the world and put it away in the garage it is filed under (state garaged, no position, its record and storage contents intact) even with somebody inside. Storage is flushed before the entity goes. It does not come back at the next restart; SpawnVehicle brings it out again. For a temporary car (SpawnTempVehicle) this is the end of it: the car is removed, forgotten, and its key taken back.

ParamTypeDescription
vehicleIdnumber|tableVehicle ID, or a vehicle reference
local ok, err = exports.whip_core:DespawnVehicle(vehicleId)
if not ok then print(err) end   -- 'Vehicle is busy': try again in a moment
Returns: boolean ok, string|nil err
A car that was already out of the world is in the state you asked for, so that reports success. An unknown vehicleId is a failure, and so is a car that is in the middle of being spawned, stored or deleted: false, 'Vehicle is busy'; try again in a moment.
A street car stays in the world, and whip lets go of it. Street traffic whip picked up is handed back to GTA, not removed (it is not whip's car to delete), and whip forgets it: its vehicleId stops meaning anything, anything in its boot or glovebox is logged as lost, and whip_core:vehicle:released fires once.
GetVehiclePosition(vehicleId)SERVER

Where a vehicle is in the world right now, as three numbers. Only a car that is actually in the world answers: a garaged, despawned or lost car answers nil, so a near check against it fails rather than passing for whoever stands where it was last seen.

Returns: number, number, number: x, y, z, or nil if the car is not in the world
This is the one to reach for in a near schema, a distance check or a blip. GetVehicle also carries a position, but it copies the whole record to answer: fine once, wasteful on a tick. For where a car was last seen (a lost car's last spot), read GetVehicle(id).coords.
local x, y, z = exports.whip_core:GetVehiclePosition(vehicleId)
if not x then return false, 'That car is not out' end

local here = GetEntityCoords(GetPlayerPed(source))
if #(here - vector3(x, y, z)) > 5.0 then return false, 'Too far away' end

-- In a SecureEvent with a 'vehicle' param, near = { at = 'vehicle' } does this for you.
ReportVehicleStat(vehicle, name, value)CLIENT

Tell whip what a live stat is worth right now. The newest value supersedes any earlier one, and the framework sends it on at the cadence the stat was registered with. The server caps how fast it may rise and refuses it entirely unless the vehicle already carries the stat.

ParamTypeDescription
vehiclenumber|tableThe vehicle ID, or a vehicle reference: an entity is { entity = veh }
namestringA stat registered with a live block
valuenumberWhat it is worth now
exports.whip_core:ReportVehicleStat({ entity = veh }, 'boost', boost)
Returns: boolean: whether the value was taken
Do not call this every frame. Nothing breaks if you do (the newest value simply wins), but every call crosses into whip_core, which costs about 20µs. Feeding a sender that fires a few times a second from a loop running at the frame rate is a hundred-odd crossings a second buying nothing. Call it when your value has actually moved, and no more often than the stat's registered interval.
Pair the test with a short throttle and compare on difference rather than on change, so a refused send is retried by the next tick and a value that settles still gets its final number across.
ConsumeVehicleStat(vehicle, name, delta)CLIENT

Report that this client used some of a consume stat on a vehicle. The delta lands in a local accumulator and the framework reports the running total on the cadence the stat was registered with; the server measures whatever arrives against the wall clock and its maxRate, so a modified client claiming more gets the same ramp an honest one does.

ParamTypeDescription
vehiclenumber|tableThe vehicle ID, or, holding the car's entity handle, { entity = veh } (a vehicle reference)
namestringA stat registered with a consume block
deltanumberAmount used since the last call. Must be positive
Returns: boolean: false when the vehicle could not be resolved or the delta was not a positive number
This reports usage; it does not check the tank. There is no "only if enough is left" on this side: the server clamps the stat at its registered minimum and, with clearAtMin, takes it off the car when it bottoms out. If your simulation needs to know whether anything is left, read GetVehicleStat and stop consuming at zero yourself.
Safe to call every frame: accumulating locally is a table lookup and an addition. But each call still crosses an export boundary, so a loop draining several stats should use ConsumeVehicleStats below.
-- Each tick of a nitrous purge
exports.whip_core:ConsumeVehicleStat({ entity = veh }, 'nos', dt * BURN_PER_SECOND)
ConsumeVehicleStats(vehicle, deltas)CLIENT

Report several stats used on one vehicle, in a single call. Same accumulator, same per-stat cadence, same server cap: what changes is how many times your resource crosses into whip_core to say it. Every call has a fixed cost, so draining several stats in one call is far cheaper than one call each.

ParamTypeDescription
vehiclenumber|tableThe vehicle ID, or a vehicle reference: an entity is { entity = veh }
deltastable{ [statName] = amountUsed }: amounts since the last call, positive
Returns: boolean ok, number accepted: how many deltas were valid and applied
(true, 0) is a real answer. The vehicle resolved and nothing in the table was usable; a different fix from (false, 0), where the vehicle itself could not be resolved. Check ok before reading the count; a bare count would read as success at a call site, because 0 is truthy in Lua.
-- Build what moved, hand it over once
local used = {}
for i = 1, 10 do used['part' .. i] = FULL * moved / distance[i] end
exports.whip_core:ConsumeVehicleStats({ entity = veh }, used)
GetVehicle(vehicleId)CLIENT

Everything this client knows about a vehicle, in one call, or nil when it is not streamed in here. The same name as the server export, answered from what this client can see: a field this side cannot know is absent rather than guessed.

local v = exports.whip_core:GetVehicle({ entity = GetVehiclePedIsIn(PlayerPedId(), false) })
if not v then return end

print(v.vehicleId, v.plate, v.mine, v.hasKey, v.engineHealth)
-- Also: entity, netId, model, modelHash, class (GTA's class number), vehType, session,
-- keyInIgnition (only for the car you are in), coords, heading, locked, engineOn, bodyHealth,
-- colorPrimary, colorSecondary, occupants ({ seat, ped, isPlayer, serverId }), stats, data
SideSeesCannot see
ServerOwner, garage, state, saved position, stats, storage, players in itLive damage, colours, ambient peds
ClientLive damage, colours, lock and engine state, every occupant including pedsOwnership, garage, and anything not streamed in here
For a caller holding an entity handle, GetVehicleBy('entity', entity), or GetVehicle({ entity = entity }), a vehicle reference. whip never guesses: vehicleIds and entity handles are both plain integers in overlapping ranges, so any rule for telling them apart has a collision case whose failure mode is answering about a different car. You say which.
Stats come back with defaults filled in, and as a copy. The block on the wire holds only what the car actually carries, so a full tank would read as nil on a vehicle whose fuel has never been written.
Returns: table|nil: nil if the vehicle is unknown or not streamed in here
GetVehicleCatalog()SERVER

The whole vehicle catalog, keyed by model. Each row carries the model's display name, its vehicle class, and whether it has a picture. The cars come from server/vehicle_catalog_list.lua (930 of them, each a model, a class and a name): each start adds the ones the database does not have yet. A car has a picture when its img/vehicles/<model>.webp is in a media pack. A car pack adds its own with RegisterVehicles, with no edit to whip.

Returns: table: { [model] = { model, displayName, class, hasImage, image, inGame } }, a copy; hasImage is true/false and image is the picture's URL for your NUI (false when there is none), so there is no path to build yourself; inGame is VehicleModelExists' answer (leave inGame == false out of anything you sell)
local catalog = exports.whip_core:GetVehicleCatalog()
local row = catalog['sultan']
if row then print(row.displayName) end  -- 'Sultan', not 'SULTAN'
RegisterVehicles(list)SERVER

A car pack's cars in the catalog while the pack runs: named, classed and pictured everywhere the catalog is read (the dealership sells them, the vehicle wizard offers them, garages name them), with no edit to whip_core or the media packs. The list is the pack's whole list: a car left out of a later call goes, and all of them go when the pack stops. A model whip already lists keeps its name and class and takes your picture. Put the pictures in your resource and list them in its files { }, or the page cannot load them.

Whip.register(function()
    exports.whip_core:RegisterVehicles({
        { model = 'mypack_gt',   name = 'Velo GT',   class = 'sports', image = 'img/mypack_gt.webp' },
        { model = 'mypack_van',  name = 'Hauler Van', class = 'vans',   image = 'img/mypack_van.webp' },
    })
end)
Returns: true, or false, why (a model missing, a class whip does not know, a picture not in your resource, a model another pack registered); nothing is added when any entry is refused. class is a name (compacts, sedans, suvs, coupes, muscle, sportsclassics, sports, super, motorcycles, offroad, industrial, utility, vans, cycles, boats, helicopters, planes, service, emergency, military, commercial, trains, openwheel) or GetVehicleClass's number
GetVehicleImage(model)SERVER

The URL for a vehicle's picture, usable from any resource's NUI: the pictures live on disk in a media pack (whip_media_previews) and are served over cfx-nui, so the browser caches them like any other asset. nil when the model has no picture, like every lookup.

ParamTypeDescription
modelstringModel name; matched case-insensitively
Returns: string|nil: e.g. https://cfx-nui-whip_media_previews/img/vehicles/sultan.webp (vehicle pictures live in a media pack)
local url = exports.whip_core:GetVehicleImage('sultan')
if url then
    -- hand it to your NUI: { image = url }
end
HasVehicleImage(model)SERVER

Whether a model has a picture: the cheap check when you only need to decide between showing a picture and showing a placeholder.

ParamTypeDescription
modelstringModel name; matched case-insensitively
Returns: boolean

Vehicles (Client)

Client-side vehicle exports. Instant exports use local cache: safe for an action's canInteract and frequent calls. ResolveVehicle is blocking (server round-trip): use it in onSelect only.

GetVehicleId(entity)CLIENT

Quick cache lookup for a vehicle's framework ID. Returns nil for unregistered vehicles (use ResolveVehicle to register them).

ParamTypeDescription
entitynumber|tableVehicle entity handle (or { entity = veh })
local veh = GetVehiclePedIsIn(PlayerPedId(), false)
local vehicleId = exports.whip_core:GetVehicleId(veh)   -- nil: whip has never seen this car
Returns: number|nil: vehicleId
GetVehicleEntity(vehicleId)CLIENT

The other direction: the entity handle for a framework vehicle ID, or nil when that car is not streamed in around this player. For GTA natives: every whip vehicle export takes the vehicle ID itself.

ParamTypeDescription
vehicleIdnumber|tableFramework vehicle ID, or a vehicle reference ({ plate = }, { netId = }…)
Returns: number|nil: entity handle
A bare number is a vehicle ID, never an entity. Vehicle IDs and entity handles are both plain numbers and their ranges overlap, so guessing would let a car that had just despawned be mistaken for a different car. whip never guesses: a number is a vehicle ID on every vehicle export, on both sides, and an entity goes in as { entity = veh }.
-- whip's own calls take the ID
local fuel = exports.whip_core:GetVehicleStat(vehicleId, 'fuel')

-- GTA's natives need the entity
local veh = exports.whip_core:GetVehicleEntity(vehicleId)
if veh then SetVehicleEngineOn(veh, true, true, false) end

-- holding the entity (the car you are sitting in)? say so
local mine = exports.whip_core:GetVehicleStat({ entity = GetVehiclePedIsIn(PlayerPedId(), false) }, 'fuel')
HasVehicleKey(vehicleId)CLIENT

Check if the local player has a key for a vehicle (client-side cache).

ParamTypeDescription
vehicleIdnumber|tableVehicle ID, or a vehicle reference
if exports.whip_core:HasVehicleKey({ entity = veh }) then
    -- offer "Lock" / "Unlock"
end
Returns: bool
HasKeyForPlate(plate)CLIENT

Check if the local player has a key for a vehicle by plate (client-side cache).

ParamTypeDescription
platestringLicense plate text
Returns: bool
ResolveVehicle(entity)CLIENT

Ensure a vehicle is registered in the framework, returning its vehicleId. If already registered, returns instantly from cache. If not, performs a blocking server round-trip to register it as a session vehicle. Do NOT use in conditions or loops.

ParamTypeDescription
entitynumber|tableVehicle entity handle (or { entity = veh })
Returns: number: the vehicleId; or false, why, a sentence you can show the player as it is: the car is not there or not a vehicle, it has no plate, its plate belongs to an owned car somewhere else, or the player already holds too many street cars.
-- Example: an action's onSelect — resolve the vehicle, then act on it
onSelect = function(ctx)
    local vehicleId, why = exports.whip_core:ResolveVehicle(ctx.entity)
    if not vehicleId then return ctx.refuse(why) end   -- tells the player why
    TriggerServerEvent('vandalism:slashTires', vehicleId)
end,
Blocking! This export does a server round-trip via Callback. Never use it in canInteract, a label function, a loop, or any code that runs frequently. Use it in onSelect.
GetNearbyVehicles(radius)CLIENT

Get all vehicles within a radius of the local player, sorted by distance (closest first). Uses GetGamePool('CVehicle'). Max radius: 100m.

ParamTypeDescription
radiusnumber?Search radius in metres (default 25, max 100)
Returns: table[]: { entity, plate, vehicleId, distance, model } sorted by distance
-- Tow truck: list nearby vehicles
local nearby = exports.whip_core:GetNearbyVehicles(30.0)
for _, v in ipairs(nearby) do
    print(('%s — %.1fm away'):format(v.plate, v.distance))
end
GetVehicleProperties(vehicle)CLIENT

Read everything about how a vehicle currently looks, as a plain table: the same shape SetVehicleProperties takes, so capture-then-restore round-trips. A leaf: natives in, a table out, no whip state and no server involvement.

ParamTypeDescription
vehiclenumber|tableA vehicle ID, or a vehicle reference: the entity as { entity = veh }
Returns: table: { model, plate, plateIndex, color1, color2, customColor1, customColor2, pearlescent, wheelColor, mods, wheelType, turbo, smokeEnabled, xenon, tyreSmoke, neonColor, neonEnabled, windowTint, livery, extras, dirtLevel, headlightColor, interiorColor, dashboardColor }; empty for an invalid handle
