The three toggle mods live as booleans, not mod slots. mods covers slots 0–49 except 18, 20 and 22 (turbo, tyre smoke and xenons), which GetVehicleMod reports as -1 whether they are on or off. They come back as turbo, smokeEnabled and xenon instead, described once rather than twice.
Use it to remember, not to store. A satellite that wants an appearance to persist must hand it to the server (SetVehicleAppearance) because only the server writes the database, and a client saying what a car looks like is a client that can say anything.
SetVehicleProperties(vehicle, props)CLIENT

Apply an appearance to a vehicle, here and now. Local and unsaved, but not unseen: vehicle mods are part of GTA's networked state, so the change shows for every player who can see the car, provided this client holds network control of the entity. Nothing is stored, and the car reverts to what the server has the next time its appearance is pushed, which is exactly what makes it safe for previewing something a player has not bought yet.

ParamTypeDescription
vehiclenumber|tableA vehicle ID, or a vehicle reference: the entity as { entity = veh }
propstableThe shape GetVehicleProperties returns; absent fields are left alone
Returns: true, or false, why: no such car here, or a bare entity handle. QBCore's and ox_lib's call takes the entity first; in whip a bare number is a vehicleId, so pass { entity = veh } (F8 says so once)
Take network control first with TakeVehicleControl (below). Without it the natives silently do nothing: no error, no change.
-- Preview a livery in the tuning shop, then restore
local car = { entity = veh }
local before = exports.whip_core:GetVehicleProperties(car)
exports.whip_core:SetVehicleProperties(car, { livery = 3 })
-- ...player decides against it...
exports.whip_core:SetVehicleProperties(car, before)
SetVehicleExtras(vehicle, extras)CLIENT

Switch a vehicle's extras (the parts GTA turns on and off on some cars: light bars, roof racks, covers) and keep its damage. Only the extras not already as asked are switched. Local and unsaved, like SetVehicleProperties; to keep them, the server stores them with SetVehicleAppearance's extras, which merges one extra at a time.

ParamTypeDescription
vehiclenumber|tableA vehicle ID, or a vehicle reference: the entity as { entity = veh }
extrastable{ [n] = true } on, false off, for extras 1 to 14. One the model does not have is left alone
Returns: how many were switched
Use this, not SetVehicleExtra. GTA's own switch repairs the car: its health, doors, tyres, fuel and dirt. This reads them first and puts them back, so switching a part is never a free repair. Dents cannot be put back. Take network control first.
-- Light bar on, roof rack off
if Whip.call('TakeVehicleControl', { entity = veh }) then
    Whip.call('SetVehicleExtras', { entity = veh }, { [1] = true, [2] = false })
end
TakeVehicleControl(vehicle, opts)CLIENT

Take network control of a vehicle: ask, wait, check, retry. Mod, paint and repair natives (and SetVehicleProperties) only work for the client that controls the car, and silently do nothing for anyone else. Answers at once when you already have control.

ParamTypeDescription
vehiclenumber|tableA vehicle ID, or a vehicle reference: the entity as { entity = veh }
optstable|nil{ attempts = 3, wait = 500 }: tries, and milliseconds per try
Returns: true, or false, why: 'no such vehicle', 'another player is driving it', 'control was not granted'
Never from another player at the wheel. Taking control of a car someone is driving makes it rubber-band under them, so this refuses. Their own client owns the car: do the change there (a mechanic job asks the driver's client to apply it).
It waits (up to attempts × wait), so call it from a thread or a handler, through Whip.call.
local car = { entity = veh }
if Whip.call('TakeVehicleControl', car) then
    SetVehicleFixed(veh)
end

Adding options to a vehicle part

whip draws an interaction prompt on parts of a vehicle: the bonnet, the boot, the doors. Your resource adds its own choice to one of those stacks with AddAction and at = { vehiclePart = 'door_dside_f' }; that is how whip_fuel puts "Refuel (jerry can)" on a car's doors without owning the prompt (whip_fuel/client/car.lua). ctx.entity is the car.

Whip.register(function()
    for _, door in ipairs({ 'door_dside_f', 'door_pside_f', 'door_dside_r', 'door_pside_r' }) do
        exports.whip_core:AddAction({
            id          = 'jerrycan:' .. door,    -- one action per part, each with its own id
            at          = { vehiclePart = door },
            icon        = 'fuel',
            label       = 'Refuel (jerry can)',
            canInteract = function(ctx) return JerryCanInHand() and not TankFull(ctx.entity) end,   -- your own functions
            onSelect    = function(ctx)
                -- Its own thread already: it may wait. The server checks the can, the car and the distance.
                TriggerServerEvent('myfuel:pourCan', NetworkGetNetworkIdFromEntity(ctx.entity))
            end,
        })
    end
end)
Engine work goes on 'hood'. An option there only shows while the bonnet is open or torn off, so the player has to open the bonnet first. The parts are 'hood', 'trunk', 'door_dside_f', 'door_pside_f', 'door_dside_r' and 'door_pside_r', and the one prompt of a 'bike', 'bicycle' or 'boat'.
SetVehicleStatWatchInterval(watcherId, ms)CLIENT

Change how often an existing watcher's whileHeld runs, using the id WatchVehicleStat returned.

0 means every frame, and that is allowed. A watcher that genuinely needs a frame gets one. Most do not: a value in the tens of milliseconds is plenty for anything a driver can perceive.
ParamTypeDescription
watcherIdstringThe id from WatchVehicleStat: a list registration's id sets every stat in it
msnumberMilliseconds between runs
-- Fast only while the bottle burns, slow the rest of the time
exports.whip_core:SetVehicleStatWatchInterval(watcherId, burning and 50 or 500)
Returns: boolean changed, false when nothing changed: the same interval again, or an id that is not one of your watchers

Garages

The bay you are standing in is the interface. A garage has any number of parking bays, and the prompt on an empty bay expands into the list of cars parked there.

Retrieve Flow

  1. Collapsed: an empty bay carries one prompt option: the garage's name.
  2. Expanded: press E, and that option is replaced by one per car garaged there.
  3. Pick: E on a car brings it out into this bay, not at a fixed spawn point, with its colours and parts.
  4. Collapse: look away or walk off and the list folds back up.

Store Flow

  1. A bay with a car in it has no prompt of its own.
  2. Instead, the car's own doors get a Store option. It shows on any car sitting in a bay; the server then checks the player may store it, and says why when they can't.
  3. The server checks the car is really in that bay (within Config.GarageSpotRadius + 2 m) and stores it. The car leaves the world, and the bay's own prompt comes back.

Position Helper: the outline a driver sees

Prompts are off while you drive, so a driver sees bays marked on the ground instead.

Approaching a bay in a car, the bay is markedon the ground, and the mark changes once you are parked in it. On foot, the bays of garages you may use show too, but only within onFootRange (10 m), so a garage is easy to find walking up to it; 0 keeps the outline for drivers only.

  • It is a hint, not a control: nothing is pressable, and it fires no events
  • From a car, only free bays draw (and the one you are in). On foot, every bay draws, a car in it or not: it says where the garage is, and a bay with a car in it simply has no prompt, since that car is stored through its own Store option
  • In a vehicle, only for the driver, never for a passenger. Any car they drive gets it; Config.GaragePositionHelper.requireStorable = true limits it to cars this player owns
  • A car parked on the bay hides the outline, rather than the outline drawing over its roof

The outline's size is Config.GaragePositionHelper. Note that length and width share a ratio with the texture (2:1); change one without the other and the ring and the icon's disc go oval.

Setting a garage up, and changing one: the wizardServer owners

/whip → Vehicles → Garages → + New Garage (or Set up a new garage, with no garage picked). Four steps, nothing made until the last:

  1. Name: what players see on the map and over its bays. Its key is made from the name as you type (or type your own): every car parked there is filed under it, so it cannot change once the garage exists
  2. Bays: Set out bays in the world opens the bay tool. The step lists every bay, each with Teleport and Remove, and going out again adds to them (or moves or takes any away). Up to 40
  3. Map: the blip's place (the middle of the bays, or where you stand) and its icon and colour
  4. Create: a summary with a Change on each part. Create makes the garage and every bay at once
Create it at the car park. The wizard sends the bays it set out, so the server checks them against where you are when you press Create: any bay, or the map marker, further than Config.GarageWizardReach (250 m) from you is refused. A garage is made from where it is, never from across the map. Needs the whip.devtools ACE.

Changing a garage. Pick it in the list: its page says what it is: Name, Bays, Map, each with Change, which opens the same wizard filled in with the garage, on that part (every step is open from the rail). Change everything starts at Name. The key stays as it is; its bays come in with their numbers, so a bay you move stays that bay. The last step is Save: it marks what changed and Save changes writes only that, all at once. A new name or icon saves from anywhere; a moved marker or bay must be within Config.GarageWizardReach of you, and a garage keeps at least one bay. ESC goes back to the summary, then out (nothing saved). The page also has Teleport there and Delete, and lists its bays (Teleport To each) and the cars in it. A private garage (a property's) is shown with no Change: it is changed in Properties.

Setting bays out: the bay toolServer owners

One tool for every garage's bays. Wherever a garage's bays are changed, the same tool opens: the panel steps aside, the house card in the corner says what it is doing and which keys do what (a controller's buttons when you hold one), and each bay is drawn with the outline a driver sees.

WhereWhat it changesSaved when
/whip → Vehicles → Garages → + New Garage → BaysA new public garage's bays (up to 40)The wizard's Create
/whip → Vehicles → Garages → a garage → Change on Bays → Place & Edit Garage LocationsA saved public garage's bays: add, move, take away (up to 40; it keeps at least one)The wizard's Save changes: all at once
/whip → World → Properties → a property's Garage (or a new property's Garage step) → Place & Edit Garage Locations (Set out bays in the world on a new property with none yet)A property's private garage (up to 8)The property's Save
In the worldKeyboardController
Put a bay down where you aim (flat ground only)ENTERA
Aim at a bay already there and it lights up: pick it up, then put it down where it goes (it keeps its number)ENTER, then ENTERA, then A
Turn it: the heading a car comes out facing, unless it was parked backed inQ / E (ALT for slowly)LT / RT
Raise or lower it (up to 5 m either way; the height is kept as you re-aim, for a level that the aim cannot reach)↑ / ↓ (ALT for slowly)D-pad up / down
Take away the bay you aim at, or the one you carryXX
DoneESCMenu
Put a carried bay back where it was; with none carried, undo everything this visit didCB
Saved from where they are. Nothing is written while the tool is up. A saved garage's Save changes sends every bay at once, and the server adds, moves and takes away to match, refusing the lot if any new or moved bay is further than Config.GarageWizardReach (250 m) from you, so bays are never set out from across the map. A private garage's bays are only changed in Properties. Needs the whip.devtools ACE.
Cross-garage visibility: a bay's list shows vehicles garaged at THAT garage. A vehicle garaged at a different location won't appear.

Garages

A garage is a place on the map and its parking bays. What is in it is not stored on the garage: a vehicle's own garage field is the only record of that, so there is one answer to "where is this car" and nothing to keep in step.
GetGarage(key) / GetGarages()SERVER

One garage by key, or every garage keyed the same way. Both hand back copies.

ParamTypeDescription
keystringThe garage's key (GetGarage only)
for key, garage in pairs(exports.whip_core:GetGarages()) do
    print(key, garage.name)
end

local garage = exports.whip_core:GetGarage('legion_square')
Returns: GetGarage → table|nil: { garageId, key, resource, name, x, y, z, heading, spawnX, spawnY, spawnZ, spawnHeading, blipSprite, blipColor }, plus private = true and managedBy for a property's garage. GetGarages → { [key] = garage }
This is where a garage key comes from. StoreVehicle and SetVehicleGarage both take one, and hardcoding a string out of config.lua is how a satellite ends up failing with "Wrong garage" the first time somebody renames one.
GetNearestGarage(x, y, z, maxRange)SERVER

The garage closest to a point, and how far away it is. A garage's distance is to the nearest of its marker or its parking bays, so a player in a far bay of a big car park is still at that garage. With maxRange, nothing further away counts.

ParamTypeDescription
x, y, znumberThe point
maxRangenumber|nilOnly a garage within this many metres
Returns: string|nil key, number|nil distance
local ped = GetPlayerPed(source)
local c = GetEntityCoords(ped)
local key = exports.whip_core:GetNearestGarage(c.x, c.y, c.z, 15.0)
if key then
    exports.whip_core:StoreVehicle(vehicleId, key)
end
GetGarageVehicles(key)SERVER

The vehicles currently stored in one garage, as full GetVehicle snapshots: the same shape GetVehicle and GetVehiclesOf answer with, so there is one vehicle shape to learn.

for _, v in ipairs(exports.whip_core:GetGarageVehicles('legion_square')) do
    print(v.plate, v.owner.charId)
end
Returns: table[]: GetVehicle snapshots (vehicleId, plate, model, owner, state, garage, stats, …); {} for a key that names no garage
CreateGarage / UpdateGarage / DeleteGarageSERVER

Make, change and remove garages at runtime. Changes replicate to every client immediately: blips and markers update without a restart.

FieldTypeDescription
keystringUnique identity. Set at creation, never changed
namestringShown on the blip
x, y, z, headingnumberWhere the garage marker is
spawnX, spawnY, spawnZ, spawnHeadingnumberWhere the new garage's first parking bay goes (the marker, when left out)
blipSprite, blipColornumberMap blip style
local garage, err = exports.whip_core:CreateGarage({
    key  = 'impound',
    name = 'Impound Lot',
    x = 409.3, y = -1623.1, z = 29.3, heading = 230.0,
})
if not garage then print(err) end

exports.whip_core:UpdateGarage('impound', { name = 'City Impound' })   -- only what changes
exports.whip_core:DeleteGarage('impound')                              -- its cars move, they are not deleted
Returns: CreateGarage(data) → table|false, string|nil; UpdateGarage(key, data) and DeleteGarage(key) → boolean, string|nil, refused for a garage another running resource made: only it can change or delete it (one made in /whip or by a property, or whose resource is not running, is open to any)
A new garage comes with one parking bay. Bays are the only way into a garage, so create gives it one at the spawn point. Add more, or move it, in /whip → Vehicles → Garages. A garage whose last bay an admin deletes keeps none.
Update leaves absent fields alone. Send only what you are changing: you do not have to restate the whole garage to move its blip.
Deleting a garage does not delete the cars in it. From DeleteGarage they move to the nearest other garage (or the default one), and their owners who are online are told where. Nobody loses a vehicle because an admin tidied up a location. In /whip → Vehicles → Garages, a garage with cars in it cannot be deleted until the admin chooses the one public garage they all move to; the server refuses the delete without it.
SetVehicleGarage(vehicleId, garageKey)SERVER

Move a vehicle to a different garage without taking it out of storage.

ParamTypeDescription
vehicleIdnumber|tableVehicle ID, or a vehicle reference
garageKeystringThe garage it now belongs to
-- The impound releases the car to the owner's chosen garage
local ok, err = exports.whip_core:SetVehicleGarage(vehicleId, garageKey)
if not ok then return false, err end
Returns: boolean ok, string|nil err
Not the same as StoreVehicle. Store refuses anything that is not currently out in the world: a car that is already put away returns "Vehicle is already stored". This is the one that moves it: an impound releasing a car to its home garage, or a dealership delivering to the buyer's garage of choice.
CanUseGarage(key, who)SERVER

May this person use this garage? Always true for a public garage. A private garage (a property's, keyed property:<id>) is for its owner and keyholders only: its bays are hidden from everyone else, it has no blip, the bay events refuse anyone else, and GetNearestGarage never answers it. GetGarage marks one with private = true and managedBy.

ParamTypeDescription
keystringThe garage
whonumber|tableA person: their server id, or { charId = n }
local ok, why = exports.whip_core:CanUseGarage(garageKey, source)
if not ok then return false, why end
exports.whip_core:SetVehicleGarage(vehicleId, garageKey)
Returns: true, or false, why ('No such garage', 'That garage belongs to …')
SetVehicleGarage does not ask. It is the trusted path (an impound, an admin tool), so a satellite moving a player's car into a property garage should check this first. If the player cannot use it, whip moves the car back out to a public garage the next time access changes.
GetGarageSpot(spotId)SERVER

One parking spot within a garage, by id.

Returns: table|nil: { spotId, garageKey, x, y, z, heading, label }
GetGarageSpots()SERVER

Every parking spot the server knows about.

Returns: table[]: spots, in the shape GetGarageSpot answers

Jobs & Business

Concepts

A Job is a business entity (Police, Hospital, Burger Shot), named in code by its key ('police'). Each job has Roles (Cadet, Officer, Sergeant) with a level and permissions. Employees are characters hired into a job at a role. A job may have an owner, who holds its top role and its business bank account. Players clock on/off at runtime (not persisted, resets on logout and server restart).

Every job export names things the same way: a job by jobId or key, a person by source or { charId = n } (online or not), a role by roleId or name. Every export answers a value, or false and a reason. See the exports.

In game: /whip → Economy → JobsServer owners

Open /whip → Economy → Jobs. + New Job sets one up step by step:

  1. Name: what it is called. Its key (what doors, shops and scripts know it by) is made from the name; change it only if a script wants a particular one. It is fixed once the job exists.
  2. Ranks: start from Owner, Manager, Employee (Config.JobDefaultRoles), Emergency service or Owner and staff, then change any rank: its name, its level (who outranks who), what it may do (Hire, Fire, Promote, Demote, Manage, and any permission the job's own resource adds) and its access to the business account. The top rank is level 100: the owner holds it, with full control of the account.
  3. Owner: found by name or character id. The owner holds the top rank and gets the business bank account. Without an owner the job has no account.
  4. Staff: people found by name, each given a rank.
  5. Create: everything checked; Create makes the job, its ranks and account, and hires its staff.

Pick a job in the list for its page: its name, ranks, owner and staff, each with Change, then everyone who works there (with who is on duty), its business account and the shops it runs. Change opens the same wizard filled in with the job as it is, every step open from the rail: rename a rank, give it a permission, move someone to another rank, let someone go, hire someone. Its last step, Save, lists what changed, naming anyone being let go; nothing is written before Save changes. A rank people hold can be removed in the same Save that moves them to another.

Creating Jobs: EnsureJob

Your job resource declares its job with EnsureJob(key, data), from Whip.register so it runs again if whip_core restarts. The first call makes the job: with your roles, or Config.JobDefaultRoles without them. Later calls keep it in step with your code: the name, icon, your permissions and selfClockOn follow what you declare, and roles you add to the list are added. A role that already exists is never changed (a server owner may have edited it in /whip → Economy → Jobs), and neither is the owner.

Whip.register(function()
    local pd, why = exports.whip_core:EnsureJob('police', {
        name  = 'Police Department',
        icon  = 'shield',
        roles = {
            { name = 'Chief',   level = 100 },
            { name = 'Sergeant', level = 50, permissions = { canHire = true, canFire = true, cuff = true } },
            { name = 'Officer',  level = 20, permissions = { cuff = true } },
            { name = 'Cadet',    level = 1 },
        },
        permissions = { cuff = 'Cuff suspects' },   -- the job's own, beside the built-ins
    })
    if not pd then print('police job: ' .. why) end
end)

Roles & Permissions

Each role has a level (1–100) and a permissions table. A role can only hire, fire or promote someone below its own level. Level 100 has every permission regardless of its table. whip checks this for you when you pass { by = source } to HirePlayer, FirePlayer, SetPlayerRole or the role exports (CreateJobRole, UpdateJobRole, DeleteJobRole). The player must outrank both the person's role and the role given, and hold the matching permission. And nobody gives more than they have: below level 100, a player can't hand out (or put into a role) a permission their own role lacks, or more business-account access than their own. Leave by out only when your own code or an admin decides; then nothing is checked. The built-in permissions:

  • canHire: hire new employees
  • canFire: fire employees
  • canPromote / canDemote: change employees' roles
  • canManage: manage the business: its roles, and its shop's stock and prices

A job's own permissions (EnsureJob's permissions) work the same way: they show as toggles on each role on the Jobs page, and HasJobPermission answers them. A role's bankAccess ('none', 'view', 'deposit', 'withdraw', 'manager') is its access to the job's business bank account, kept in step as people are hired, promoted and fired.

Permissions hold on duty or off. Add { onDuty = true } when an action should need both.

-- A boss menu: `by = source` makes whip check the boss's rank and canHire / canPromote
local ok, why = exports.whip_core:HirePlayer(target, 'police', 'Cadet', { by = source })
if not ok then return false, why end   -- 'Your role is not allowed to do that', 'They (or that role) outrank you'...

local ok2, why2 = exports.whip_core:SetPlayerRole(target, 'police', 'Sergeant', { by = source })

Clock On / Off

Clock state is runtime-only: it is NOT saved to the database. Logging out takes a player off duty, and after a server restart everyone must clock on again. This is intentional (players should actively report for duty).

A player can be on duty at several jobs at once; their current job is the one they clocked on at most recently: what GetPlayerJob (on either side) and the whipJob statebag name. Set Config.JobDutyOneAtATime = true to make clocking on at a job clock them off every other one.

Clocking on. Players clock themselves on and off in the phone's Business app. A job resource can give them its own way in too: a command, or a prompt at the station. On the client, ClockOn answers whether it worked. To keep duty at the station only, give the job selfClockOn = false (the Business app's clock-on is then refused) and call ClockOn from your own server code. A resource that only needs "works here" can skip clocking entirely and check GetPlayerRole(source, 'police') ~= nil.
-- Server: clock player on (a prompt at the station fired this)
local ok, why = exports.whip_core:ClockOn(source, 'police')

-- Server: check if on duty
if exports.whip_core:IsPlayerClockedOn(source, 'police') then
    -- player is on duty
end

-- Client: clock on/off (from a thread: they wait for the server)
local ok, why = exports.whip_core:ClockOn('burgershot')
exports.whip_core:ClockOff()   -- every job

Events

Server, one table each: { jobId, key }, and for a person { charId, source } (source only while online):

EventExtra fields
whip_core:job:createdname
whip_core:job:updatedname, icon, ownerCharId, oldOwnerCharId
whip_core:job:deleted—
whip_core:job:hiredcharId, source, roleId, role, by
whip_core:job:firedcharId, source
whip_core:job:roleChangedcharId, source, roleId, role, oldRoleId
whip_core:job:clockedOn / clockedOffcharId, source

Client, for the local player: whip_core:job:clockedOn / clockedOff { jobId, key }, and whip_core:job:listChanged { jobs } when their job list changes.

Data Structures

Job object:

{
    jobId       = 1,
    key         = 'police',
    name        = 'Police Department',
    icon        = 'shield',
    ownerCharId = nil,
    settings    = {},
}

Role object:

{
    roleId      = 3,
    jobId       = 1,
    name        = 'Sergeant',
    level       = 50,
    permissions = { canHire = true, canFire = true, canManage = true },
}

Employee object:

{
    jobId   = 1,
    charId  = 42,
    roleId  = 3,
    hiredAt = 1710000000,
    hiredBy = 1,
}

Job list entry (from GetPlayerJobs, both sides):

{
    jobId       = 1,
    key         = 'police',
    name        = 'Police Department',
    icon        = 'shield',
    roleId      = 3,
    roleName    = 'Sergeant',
    roleLevel   = 50,
    clockedOn   = false,
    permissions = { canHire = true, cuff = true },   -- what they may do here
}

Jobs

Job/business management exports. Create jobs, manage employees, check duty status, control permissions.

Every job export names things the same way.
  • A job: its jobId (a number) or its key ('police').
  • A person: a source (a player who is online), or { charId = 42 } for any character, online or offline.
  • A role: its roleId or its name ('Manager', any capitals).
Every export answers a value, or false and a reason: a sentence a player can read ('No such job', 'They do not work there', 'They (or that role) outrank you'…), so a handler can pass it straight on with return false, why.
GetJob(job)SERVER

Get a job by jobId or key.

ParamTypeDescription
jobnumber|stringjobId, or key ('police')
local job = exports.whip_core:GetJob('police')
if job then print(job.jobId, job.name) end
Returns: table|nil: { jobId, key, name, icon, ownerCharId, settings }
GetJobs()SERVER

Every job, in jobId order.

Returns: table[]: job objects
GetJobRoles(job)SERVER

A job's roles, highest level first.

ParamTypeDescription
jobnumber|stringjobId or key
local roles, why = exports.whip_core:GetJobRoles('police')
if not roles then return false, why end
for _, role in ipairs(roles) do print(role.level, role.name) end
Returns: table[]: { roleId, name, level, permissions }, or false, 'No such job'
EnsureJob(key, data)SERVER

Idempotent find-or-create. A job resource calls it from Whip.register to declare its job: its name, its ranks, and any permissions of its own. A key another running resource declared is refused, as with EnsureZone and EnsureContainer. Called while whip_core is still starting, it waits for it (up to 60 seconds).

ParamTypeDescription
keystringStable identifier: letters, numbers and _ (e.g. 'police')
data.namestringDisplay name
data.iconstring?Icon
data.rolestable?The ranks: { { name, level, permissions } }, level 1–100. Without it the job gets Config.JobDefaultRoles.
data.permissionstable?The job's own permissions, beside the built-in five: { cuff = 'Cuff suspects' }. They show as toggles on each role on the Jobs page.
data.ownerperson?The owner: only when the job is made. They hold the top role and the business bank account.
data.selfClockOnboolean?false: players cannot clock themselves on with the client's ClockOn; your server code puts them on duty (at the station, say). Going off duty always works.
Returns: table|false, string: the job, or false and why (a bad key, 'roles[2] (Cadet): level must be...'). A new owned job whose business account could not be opened still comes back, and the server console says so.

On a job that already exists, what your code declares follows your code: the name, icon, permissions and selfClockOn are updated, and roles you list that the job doesn't have are added. Nothing else changes: not the owner (UpdateJob does that), not a role that exists (a server owner may have edited it on the Jobs page).

Whip.register(function()
    local pd, why = exports.whip_core:EnsureJob('police', {
        name = 'Police Department',
        icon = 'shield',
        roles = {
            { name = 'Chief',   level = 100 },
            { name = 'Officer', level = 20, permissions = { cuff = true, bankAccess = 'view' } },
            { name = 'Cadet',   level = 1 },
        },
        permissions = { cuff = 'Cuff suspects' },
        selfClockOn = false,   -- duty at the station only
    })
    if not pd then print('police job: ' .. why) end
end)
UpdateJob(job, patch)SERVER

Change a job's name, icon or owner. The business bank account follows a new owner; the old owner's access follows their job (their role if they still work there, none if not).

ParamTypeDescription
jobnumber|stringjobId or key
patchtable{ name?, icon?, owner? }: owner = false removes the owner (refused while the job has a business account)
-- Sell the business: the business account goes with it
local ok, why = exports.whip_core:UpdateJob('burgershot', { owner = buyerSource })
if not ok then return false, why end
Returns: true, or false, why. If the job changed but its business account could not follow a new owner, it still answers true (the job did change) and the server console says so. Refused for a job another running resource declares with EnsureJob: only it can change or delete it (one made on the Jobs page, or whose resource is not running, is open to any)
DeleteJob(job)SERVER

Delete a job, its roles and its staff list. Its business accounts close with it, and the delete is refused while one still holds money ('Empty the job's business account first').

ParamTypeDescription
jobnumber|stringjobId or key
local ok, why = exports.whip_core:DeleteJob('burgershot')
if not ok then print(why) end   -- 'Empty the job's business account first'
Returns: true, or false, why. Refused for a job another running resource declares, as UpdateJob
GetPlayerJob(who)SERVER

The job they are on duty at: the one they clocked on at most recently. The same job the whipJob statebag and the client's GetPlayerJob name. nil when off duty.

ParamTypeDescription
whopersonsource, or { charId = n }
local job = exports.whip_core:GetPlayerJob(source)
if not job or job.key ~= 'police' then
    return false, 'You need to be on duty as police'
end
Returns: table|nil: { jobId, key, name, icon, roleId, roleName, roleLevel }
GetPlayerJobs(who)SERVER

Every job they have a role at (employed, or the owner), on duty or not.

ParamTypeDescription
whopersonsource, or { charId = n }
for jobId, job in pairs(exports.whip_core:GetPlayerJobs(source)) do
    print(job.name, job.roleName, job.clockedOn)
end
Returns: table: by jobId: { jobId, key, name, icon, roleId, roleName, roleLevel, clockedOn, permissions }; {}, why for nobody
IsPlayerClockedOn(who, job?)SERVER

On duty at this job, or, with no job, at any.

ParamTypeDescription
whopersonsource, or { charId = n }
jobnumber|string?jobId or key
if not exports.whip_core:IsPlayerClockedOn(source, 'ambulance') then
    return false, 'Clock on at the hospital first'
end
Returns: boolean: and a reason with false when the question is wrong (no such player or job), so "off duty" and "asked about nobody" can be told apart
GetPlayerRole(who, job)SERVER

Their role at a job. The job's owner holds its top role, whether or not they are also hired.

ParamTypeDescription
whopersonsource, or { charId = n }
jobnumber|stringjobId or key
local role = exports.whip_core:GetPlayerRole(source, 'police')
if not role or role.level < 50 then
    return false, 'Sergeants and above only'
end
Returns: table|nil: { roleId, name, level, permissions }
HasJobPermission(who, job, permission, opts?)SERVER

May they do this at this job? The built-in permissions are canHire, canFire, canPromote, canDemote and canManage (the business: roles, shop stock and prices); a job's own come from its EnsureJob. Level 100 holds them all. Permissions hold on duty or off: pass { onDuty = true } to also require being on duty there.

ParamTypeDescription
whopersonsource, or { charId = n }
jobnumber|stringjobId or key
permissionstringA built-in or the job's own
optstable?{ onDuty = true }
Returns: true, or false, why ('Not on duty at Police', 'Not allowed at Police', no such player or job), an access check, answering like the others
if not exports.whip_core:HasJobPermission(source, 'police', 'cuff', { onDuty = true }) then
    return false, 'Only an officer on duty can do that'
end
GetJobEmployees(job)SERVER

Everyone on the payroll, online or not, by charId. The owner is listed only if also hired.

ParamTypeDescription
jobnumber|stringjobId or key
local staff, why = exports.whip_core:GetJobEmployees('police')
if not staff then return false, why end
for charId, emp in pairs(staff) do
    print(charId, emp.roleName, emp.onDuty)
end
Returns: table: by charId: { charId, roleId, roleName, roleLevel, hiredAt, hiredBy, onDuty, source } (hiredAt in epoch seconds; source only while online), or false, 'No such job'
GetClockedOnEmployees(job)SERVER

Everyone on duty at a job, the owner included. Duty ends at logout, so each has a source.

ParamTypeDescription
jobnumber|stringjobId or key
Returns: table[]: { charId, source }, or false, reason when there is no such job (hence the or {} below)
for _, cop in ipairs(exports.whip_core:GetClockedOnEmployees('police') or {}) do
    exports.whip_core:NotifyPlayer(cop.source, '10-31 in progress at the bank')
end
HirePlayer(who, job, role?, opts?)SERVER

Hire someone. Their business-account access follows the role; their client's job list updates by itself.

With Config.JobOneCharacterPerAccount on (the default), it is refused when another character of the same player account already works there, the job's owner included: "That is another character of someone who already works there, so they cannot be hired". So an alt cannot keep a fired character's access. Every way of hiring obeys it, trusted code included; set it to false to allow it.

ParamTypeDescription
whopersonsource, or { charId = n } (offline too)
jobnumber|stringjobId or key
rolenumber|string?roleId or name: default the lowest role
optstable?{ by = person }: the player hiring them. Recorded, and checked: they must outrank the role, hold canHire, and hold everything the role can do (its permissions, and at least its business-account access). Leave it out when your code or an admin decides.
Returns: true, or false, why ('They already work there', 'No such role at that job', 'No such character', 'Your role is not allowed to do that', 'They (or that role) outrank you'...)
local ok, why = exports.whip_core:HirePlayer(target, 'burgershot', 'Cook', { by = source })
CanHirePlayer(who, job, role?, opts?)SERVER

Would HirePlayer with these arguments be allowed? Every one of its rules is asked and nothing is written. For a step that waits on someone before it hires: the phone's Business app asks it before it sends a job offer, then hires when the offer is accepted (and the rules are asked again then).

local ok, why = exports.whip_core:CanHirePlayer({ charId = typedId }, jobId, roleId, { by = source })
if not ok then return false, why end   -- say why now, before asking them
Returns: true, or false, why (as HirePlayer)
FirePlayer(who, job, opts?)SERVER

Fire someone. They go off duty and lose their business-account access.

ParamTypeDescription
whopersonsource, or { charId = n }
jobnumber|stringjobId or key
optstable?{ by = person }: the player firing them, checked: they must outrank the person and hold canFire. Leave it out when your code or an admin decides.
-- A manager firing someone from the business app: their rank is checked
local ok, why = exports.whip_core:FirePlayer({ charId = targetCharId }, 'burgershot', { by = source })
if not ok then return false, why end
Returns: true, or false, why ('They do not work there'...)
SetPlayerRole(who, job, role, opts?)SERVER

Change someone's role. Their business-account access follows it.

ParamTypeDescription
whopersonsource, or { charId = n }
jobnumber|stringjobId or key
rolenumber|stringroleId or name
optstable?{ by = person }: the player making the change, checked: they must outrank the person's role now and the new role, and hold canPromote (up) or canDemote (down). The new role may give the person nothing the player's own role can't do. Nobody promotes themselves. Leave it out when your code or an admin decides.
local ok, why = exports.whip_core:SetPlayerRole(target, 'police', 'Sergeant', { by = source })
if not ok then return false, why end
Returns: true, or false, why
CreateJobRole(job, data, opts?)SERVER

Add a role to a job. Role names are unique within a job (case does not count).

ParamTypeDescription
jobnumber|stringjobId or key
datatable{ name, level, permissions? }: level 1–100; permissions like { canHire = true, cuff = true, bankAccess = 'view' } (built-ins, the job's own, and a bank access level). A permission the job does not have is refused.
optstable?{ by = person }: the player making it, checked: they need canManage, and below level 100 the new role must be below their own level and can do no more than theirs (no permission they lack, no more business-account access). Leave it out when your code or an admin decides.
local role, why = exports.whip_core:CreateJobRole('burgershot', {
    name = 'Shift Lead', level = 30,
    permissions = { canHire = true, bankAccess = 'deposit' },
}, { by = source })
if not role then return false, why end
Returns: table: { roleId, name, level, permissions }, or false, why ('There is already a role called Shift Lead', 'They (or that role) outrank you', 'That rank can do more than yours: you cannot give more than you have'...)
UpdateJobRole(job, role, patch, opts?)SERVER

Change a role's name, level or permissions. Permissions you don't name keep their value, and false takes one away. The business-account access of everyone holding the role follows it.

ParamTypeDescription
jobnumber|stringjobId or key
rolenumber|stringroleId or name
patchtable{ name?, level?, permissions? }
optstable?{ by = person }: the player changing it, checked: they need canManage; below level 100 the role and its new level must be below their own, and they can add nothing their own role can't do (what the role already has stays). Nobody may leave the job without a level 100 role (the owner's). Leave it out when your code or an admin decides.
local ok, why = exports.whip_core:UpdateJobRole('burgershot', 'Shift Lead', {
    permissions = { canFire = true, bankAccess = 'none' },
}, { by = source })
if not ok then return false, why end
Returns: true, or false, why
DeleteJobRole(job, role, opts?)SERVER

Delete a role. Refused while anyone holds it: move them to another role first.

ParamTypeDescription
jobnumber|stringjobId or key
rolenumber|stringroleId or name
optstable?{ by = person }: the player deleting it, checked as for UpdateJobRole.
local ok, why = exports.whip_core:DeleteJobRole('burgershot', 'Shift Lead', { by = source })
if not ok then return false, why end   -- 'Move the people in that role to another role first'
Returns: true, or false, why
ClockOn(who, job, opts?)SERVER

Put an online player on duty. With Config.JobDutyOneAtATime, every other job clocks off first. Runtime only: duty ends at logout and at a restart.

ParamTypeDescription
whopersonsource, or { charId = n }: they must be online
jobnumber|stringjobId or key
optstable?{ by = person }: the player doing it, checked like the client's ClockOn: they clock only themselves on, and only at a job that lets them (selfClockOn). Leave it out when your code decides.
-- A job with selfClockOn = false: on duty when they collect the uniform at the station
local ok, why = exports.whip_core:ClockOn(source, 'police')
if not ok then return false, why end
Returns: true, or false, why ('They do not work there', 'They are not online'...)
ClockOff(who, job?)SERVER

Take someone off duty at a job, or, with no job, at every job.

ParamTypeDescription
whopersonsource, or { charId = n }
jobnumber|string?jobId or key
Returns: true, or false, why ('They are not on duty'...)

Jobs (Client)

Client-side job state. Cached locally: no server round-trip, except ClockOn / ClockOff. Local events: whip_core:job:clockedOn / clockedOff { jobId, key } and whip_core:job:listChanged { jobs }. See also server job exports.

GetPlayerJobs()CLIENT

Get all jobs the local player is employed in. Returns a table keyed by jobId.

Returns: table: { [jobId] = { jobId, key, name, icon, roleId, roleName, roleLevel, clockedOn, permissions } }
local jobs = exports.whip_core:GetPlayerJobs()
for jobId, job in pairs(jobs) do
    print(job.name .. ' — ' .. job.roleName)
end
IsPlayerClockedOn(job?)CLIENT

Is the local player on duty at this job (jobId or key), or, with no job, at any?

ParamTypeDescription
jobnumber|string?jobId or key, or nil for any
if not exports.whip_core:IsPlayerClockedOn('police') then return end   -- no MDT off duty
Returns: boolean
HasJobPermission(job, permission)CLIENT

What the server's job list says the player may do at a job. A hint for what to OFFER (show a "Manage Stock" option); the server checks again when they use it.

ParamTypeDescription
jobnumber|stringjobId or key
permissionstringA built-in or the job's own
-- Show "Manage Stock" only to those who may; the server checks again when it is used
local showManage = exports.whip_core:HasJobPermission('burgershot', 'canManage')
Returns: boolean
GetPlayerJob()CLIENT

The job the player is on duty at: the most recent clock-on, the same one the server's GetPlayerJob names. nil off duty.

local job = exports.whip_core:GetPlayerJob()
print(job and ('On duty: ' .. job.name) or 'Off duty')
Returns: table|nil: an entry of GetPlayerJobs
ClockOn(job)CLIENT

Go on duty at a job (jobId or key). Waits for the server and answers: call it from a thread (a command, a key binding, an interaction callback). Refused ('This job puts people on duty itself') for a job whose resource set selfClockOn = false: that job puts people on duty from its own server code.

ParamTypeDescription
jobnumber|stringjobId or key
Returns: true, or false, why
RegisterCommand('duty', function()
    local ok, why = exports.whip_core:ClockOn('burgershot')
    if not ok then exports.whip_core:Notify('Not on duty: ' .. tostring(why), 'error') end
end)
ClockOff(job?)CLIENT

Go off duty at a job, or, with none, at every job. Always allowed, even while dead. Waits for the server and answers.

ParamTypeDescription
jobnumber|string?jobId or key
Returns: true, or false, why

Shop System

Overview

Built-in shop system with three modes: infinite (unlimited stock, business-owned), stocked (player-managed inventory with per-item pricing), and npc (server economy, money sink). Shops are placed in the world as NPCs or objects, used through a prompt on the shopkeeper (or over the shop's object), and integrate with the jobs, bank, inventory, and container systems.

Three Modes

ModeStockPricingRevenue
infiniteUnlimited: items never run outDefined in catalog JSON on the shopDeposited to linked business bank account
stockedBacked by a real container: employees stock items manuallyOne price per item: employees set prices and mark items for sale, whichever shelf slots hold themDeposited to linked business bank account. A shop priced in an item puts that payment into its own container (its stock room)
npcUnlimited: same as infiniteDefined in catalog JSONMoney sink: no business link

Business Integration

Modes infinite and stocked link to a job via jobId. The job system creates a business bank account for the job once the job has an owner: set one in /whip → Economy → Jobs. A job with no owner has no account yet, so GetJobBankAccounts returns nothing for it; a resource paying a job should have a fallback. When a customer purchases items, the revenue is paid into the business bank account as a system deposit (BankSystemDeposit is the export), with the buyer's charId recorded in the transaction log. The customer pays through ChargePlayer, and any line that cannot be handed over is refunded in the currency it was paid in.

Stocked Mode: Employee Workflow

  1. Create a container (stash) in the world to hold shop stock
  2. Create a shop with mode = 'stocked' and containerId pointing to that container
  3. Employees walk up to the shopkeeper (or the shop's object) → "Manage Stock" on its prompt (requires canManage job permission)
  4. The linked container opens: employees drag items in from their inventory
  5. Right-click items in the container → "Set Price" and "Mark For Sale"
  6. Items marked for sale with a price appear in the shop for customers
  7. When customers buy, the exact item (with all its metadata, such as its serial number) transfers from the container to the buyer

Customer Flow

  1. Walk up to the shopkeeper (or the shop's object) → press E on the prompt, which carries the shop's name
  2. The shop's goods take the inventory's place: cards with their prices, the shop's tabs, a sort and a search. The basket is on the right
  3. Click a card (or A on a pad) to add one. The card's − and + change what is in the basket
  4. Type the number: click the count on a card or a basket line, type how many, press Enter (Esc puts it back). More than the shelf has becomes what it has
  5. Hold to go faster: hold a card, its + or −, or a line's + or − (the mouse button, or A on a pad) and it keeps going, quicker the longer it is held, then in fives and tens
  6. The numbers change the moment you click; the server catches up a moment later and has the last word (a shelf that ran out, a full basket). Buy waits until it has
  7. Select payment: Cash or Bank (with an account selector; a shop priced in an item takes only that item)
  8. Click Buy: the goods go into your pockets and the payment is taken. The basket shows beforehand whether it all fits. For a moment Buy says how it went: Purchase Successful!, Not enough cash! (or why it was refused), You can't carry all of this!

Shop talk

Everyone nearby sees the shopping happen. The shopper's character says each step in a /me bubble, and the shopkeeper answers a moment later:

  • Opening the shop: "What do you got?" … "Welcome in."
  • Adding to the basket: "I'll take x3 Water" … "Coming right up."
  • Changing how many of something already in it, the new amount: "Actually, I want x5 Water instead" … "No problem, changed."
  • Taking it out altogether: "I changed my mind on x3 Water" … "No worries."
  • Paying: said as a sale, what was paid and what for: "Paid $1,170 for x10 Burger and x1 Phone" … "$1,170 received. Enjoy your x10 Burger and x1 Phone!"
  • Not enough money: "Uh... can I owe you?" … and the shopkeeper makes fun of them: "Come back when you can afford it, cheapskate." Said once in 8 seconds however often Buy is pressed
  • Closing without buying: "Nevermind, I'll shop elsewhere" … "Suit yourself."

The basket's + and − go one at a time, so nothing is said until the basket has been left alone for a second (each click waits again), then each item is said once. Going up and back down to where it was says nothing. A shop with an object instead of a shopkeeper has nobody to answer. Nothing is said by someone who is down. Nothing is said either when the shop is shut by a death, a logout or walking away, and opening the same shop again within 15 seconds is quiet. The lines and the timings are Config.ShopTalk (Configuration).

On the shop screen too. The screen covers the world and its bubbles, so the conversation also shows in the shop's header, with each speaker's face. A shop with no shopkeeper shows only the shopper's lines, and with shop talk switched off neither is shown.

Config Seeds

whip ships with no shops placed: they are set up in game with /whip → Economy → Shops. A shop can also be listed in config.lua's Config.Shops (same pattern as garages). It is made at start-up whenever no shop has its key, then managed in /whip like any other, so one deleted there comes back at the next restart while it is still listed:

Config.Shops = {
    convenience_1 = {
        name       = '24/7 Store',
        mode       = 'npc',
        npcModel   = 'mp_m_shopkeep_01',
        pos        = vector4(25.7, -1347.3, 29.5, 271.0),
        blipSprite = 52,
        blipColor  = 2,
        catalog    = {
            food    = 50,
            drink   = 30,
            bandage = 100,
        },
    },
}

From your resource

-- Server, in Whip.register: a shop your resource always has (made once, found on every start)
local shop, why = exports.whip_core:EnsureShop('my_gunshop', {
    name     = 'Gun Store',
    mode     = 'npc',
    npcModel = 's_m_m_ammucountry',
    x = 100.0, y = 200.0, z = 30.0, heading = 180.0,
    catalog  = { gunny_pistol = 2500, gunny_mag_pistol = 150 },
})
if not shop then print('gun store: ' .. why) end

-- Hear every sale
AddEventHandler('whip_core:shop:purchased', function(e)
    print(('charId %s bought %d line(s) for $%d'):format(e.charId, #e.items, e.total))
end)

In game: /whip → Economy → ShopsServer owners

Open /whip → Economy → Shops. + New Shop sets one up step by step, like the property Configurator:

  1. Kind: its name, and which kind: open to everyone (npc), a business that never runs out (infinite) or a business with real stock (stocked). A business picks the job that runs it.
  2. Where: Go and stand there hides the panel: walk to where the shopkeeper will stand, face the customers, press E.
  3. Shopkeeper: a person from the world builder's NPC list (pictures, categories, search; "Shop staff" first), a prop, or nobody. See them in the world stands them on the spot and looks at them through a camera: ←/→ for the next one in the list, the mouse to turn round them, E to choose.
  4. Stock room (stocked only): the container its staff stock, nearest first.
  5. Goods: the Items page's list beside the shelf being made: click an item to add it, give each a price. A stocked shop's step is Prices: it sells what its staff stock, and these price it.
  6. Map: a blip icon and colour, or none.
  7. Create: everything checked; Create makes it, keeper and all.

Pick a shop in the list for its page: the same summary as the wizard's last step, with its shopkeeper's picture, and Change on each part. Change opens the wizard filled in with the shop as it is, on that part, with every step open from the rail: pick another person, add or remove goods, move it, recolour its blip. Its last step, Save, marks what changed; Save changes writes it, and Esc goes back to that summary, then out without saving. For a stocked shop, removing an item from Prices takes it off sale in its stock room. The page also has Teleport there and Delete. Its shelf order and tabs are arranged in game with Edit Shelf.

Shops

Shop management exports. Create shops, manage pricing, query shop state. See the Shop System guide for concepts and modes.

GetShop(shopId)SERVER

Get a shop definition by ID. To find one by anything else (its key, its stock container, its job), use GetShopBy.

ParamTypeDescription
shopIdnumberShop ID
Returns: table|nil: { shopId, key, name, mode, jobId, containerId, npcModel, prop, x, y, z, heading, blipSprite, blipColor, catalog, settings }
GetShopBy(kind, value)SERVER

One shop, found by what you have: the same shape as GetVehicleBy. kind is 'id', 'key' (the stable key string you gave it, e.g. 'convenience_1'), 'containerId' (the shop that uses that container as its stock) or 'job'. 'job' answers with a list, since a job can own several shops.

exports.whip_core:GetShopBy('key', 'burgershot')
exports.whip_core:GetShopBy('containerId', 12)   -- the shop whose stock that is
exports.whip_core:GetShopBy('id', 4)
exports.whip_core:GetShopBy('job', 'police')     -- a list; the job by key or jobId
Returns: table|nil, or a list for 'job' ({}, 'No such job' for a job that does not exist)
EnsureShop(key, data)SERVER

A shop declared in code, by key: the same rule as EnsureZone. A new key makes the shop. Called again with the same declaration, nothing changes, so edits an admin made in the Shops panel since then stand. Called with a changed declaration (you edited the catalog or moved the shop in your resource), every field you declare is applied, and a link you stop declaring (jobId, containerId, npcModel, prop, blipSprite) is cleared. A key another running resource declared is refused. Safe to call every resource start.

ParamTypeDescription
keystringStable shop identifier
datatable{ name, mode, npcModel?, prop?, x, y, z, heading, catalog?, jobId?, containerId?, blipSprite?, blipColor?, settings? }: jobId takes a jobId or a job key
Returns: table: the shop, or false, reason (a bad catalog, no x/y/z, no such job or container, a key another resource owns, a database error). The declaration is kept in the shop's settings.ensured.
Whip.register(function()
    local shop, why = exports.whip_core:EnsureShop('my_gunshop', {
        name       = 'Ammu-Nation',
        mode       = 'npc',
        npcModel   = 's_m_m_ammucountry',
        x = -330.2, y = 6084.3, z = 31.5, heading = 228.0,
        blipSprite = 110,
        catalog    = { gunny_pistol = 2500 },
    })
    if not shop then print('gun shop: ' .. why) end
end)
CreateShop(data)SERVER

Create a new shop. Unlike EnsureShop, this does not check for existing keys: always creates. Fires whip_core:shop:created with { shopId, shop }.

ParamTypeDescription
datatableShop definition (same fields as EnsureShop)
-- A pop-up stall for one event; EnsureShop is for a shop your resource always has
local stall, err = exports.whip_core:CreateShop({
    name = 'Festival Stall', mode = 'npc', npcModel = 's_m_y_shop_mask',
    x = 190.2, y = -930.5, z = 30.7, heading = 145.0,
    catalog = { food = 12, drink = 5 },
})
if not stall then return false, err end
Returns: table: the shop, with shopId, or false, reason.
DeleteShop(shopId)SERVER

Delete a shop. Closes it for any player who has it open, despawns the entity. Fires whip_core:shop:deleted with { shopId }.

ParamTypeDescription
shopIdnumberShop ID
local ok, err = exports.whip_core:DeleteShop(stall.shopId)
if not ok then print(err) end
Returns: boolean, string|nil: false, 'Shop not found' for an unknown id. Refused for a shop another running resource made or declares: only it can change or delete it (one made in /whip, or whose resource is not running, is open to any)
UpdateShop(shopId, data)SERVER

Update shop fields. Only include the fields you want to change; pass false for jobId, containerId, npcModel, prop, blipSprite or key to clear it. Fires whip_core:shop:updated with { shopId, shop }.

ParamTypeDescription
shopIdnumberShop ID
datatableFields to update (same keys as shop definition). catalog: { [itemKey] = price, ... }, replaces an infinite/npc shop's whole catalog
Returns: boolean, string|nil: false, 'Shop not found' for an unknown id. Refused for a shop another running resource made or declares, as DeleteShop
-- Replace the catalog: add a new item and change a price
exports.whip_core:UpdateShop(shopId, {
    catalog = {
        food     = 50,
        drink    = 25,   -- was 30, now 25
        bandage  = 100,
        lockpick = 500,  -- new item
    },
})
To change one item's price, AddCatalogItem(shopId, itemKey, price) is simpler: it leaves the rest of the catalog alone.
SetShopItemPrice(containerId, itemKey, price, forSale)SERVER

Price an item on a stocked shop's shelf, or take it off sale. A stocked shop has one price per item: every shelf slot holding it sells at that price. Customers at the shop see the new price at once. Fires whip_core:shop:priceChanged with { containerId, item, price, forSale }.

ParamTypeDescription
containerIdnumber|tableThe shop's stock container ID, or { shopId = n }, like every other shop export
itemKeystringThe item (it must be registered)
pricenumberPrice in dollars (0 = free)
forSalebooleantrue = on the shopfront. false keeps the price but hides the item from customers
-- Water at $5 in this shop
local ok, err = exports.whip_core:SetShopItemPrice({ shopId = shopId }, 'drink', 5, true)
if not ok then return false, err end
Returns: boolean, string|nil. False with 'Unknown container', 'Unknown item' or 'Invalid price' (not a number). A negative price is set to 0.
SetShopLayout(shopId, { categories, layout })SERVER

Set a shop's tabs and where its goods sit: what the shop screen's Edit Shelf does (open to the shop's managers and whip's admins). categories is the tabs in order. Each layout entry puts an item in a tab and gives it a place; lower order comes first, and goods without a place follow, A to Z. Customers at the shop see the change at once.

ParamTypeDescription
shopIdnumberShop ID (any mode)
categoriesstring[]?The tabs, 1–24 letters each, at most 12. Leave it out to keep the shop's
layouttable?{ [itemKey] = { category, order } }. Each entry replaces that item's place; an entry with neither takes it away; an item not mentioned keeps its own
exports.whip_core:SetShopLayout(shopId, {
    categories = { 'Food', 'Drinks' },
    layout = {
        food  = { category = 'Food', order = 1 },
        drink = { category = 'Drinks', order = 2 },
    },
})
Returns: boolean, string|nil. False with the reason: an unknown item, a tab the shop does not have, a tab name too long, too many tabs.
The same two fields can sit in a shop's settings in config.lua or EnsureShop: see config.lua §9.
SetShopSlotPrice(containerId, slot, price, forSale)SERVER

Deprecated — use SetShopItemPrice. It prices whatever item a shelf slot of a stocked shop holds, and every slot holding that item takes the price.

ParamTypeDescription
containerIdnumber|tableThe shop's stock container ID, or { shopId = n }
slotnumberA shelf slot holding the item to price
pricenumberPrice in dollars (0 = free)
forSalebooleantrue = listed for sale
Returns: boolean, string|nil. False with 'Unknown container', 'Invalid slot' (not a slot that container has), 'Invalid price' or 'That shelf slot is empty'.
GetShopViewers(shopId)SERVER

Get all player source IDs currently browsing a specific shop.

ParamTypeDescription
shopIdnumberShop ID
for _, src in ipairs(exports.whip_core:GetShopViewers(shopId)) do
    exports.whip_core:NotifyPlayer(src, 'Prices just changed')
end
Returns: number[]: array of source IDs
GetAllShops()SERVER

Get all shop definitions sorted by shopId.

Returns: table[]: array of shop definitions
GetShopCatalog(shopId)SERVER

Get the catalog for an infinite/npc shop. Returns a table mapping item keys to prices.

ParamTypeDescription
shopIdnumberShop ID
local catalog = exports.whip_core:GetShopCatalog(shopId) or {}
print('lockpicks cost', catalog.lockpick)
Returns: table|nil: { [itemKey] = price } or nil if shop not found
AddCatalogItem(shopId, itemKey, price)SERVER

Add or update a single item in an infinite/npc shop's catalog, and save it. The item must be registered.

ParamTypeDescription
shopIdnumberShop ID
itemKeystringItem key to add
pricenumberPrice (≥ 0)
Returns: boolean, string|nil: success and error message
exports.whip_core:AddCatalogItem(shopId, 'lockpick', 500)
RemoveCatalogItem(shopId, itemKey)SERVER

Remove a single item from an infinite/npc shop's catalog, and save it.

exports.whip_core:RemoveCatalogItem(shopId, 'lockpick')
ParamTypeDescription
shopIdnumberShop ID
itemKeystringItem key to remove
Returns: boolean, string|nil: success and error message
GetShopStock(shopId)SERVER

Get the full stock view for a stocked shop: each shelf slot with the price of the item on it. Loads from database if not cached.

ParamTypeDescription
shopIdnumberShop ID (must be stocked mode)
local stock, err = exports.whip_core:GetShopStock(shopId)
if not stock then return false, err end
for slot, s in pairs(stock) do
    if s.forSale then print(slot, s.item, s.amount, s.price) end
end
Returns: table: { [slot] = { item, amount, metadata, price, forSale } }, or false, reason (not a stocked shop, no such shop)
GetShopPrices(shopId)SERVER

Get every item price a stocked shop has, for sale or not, keyed by item.

ParamTypeDescription
shopIdnumberShop ID (must be stocked mode)
local prices = exports.whip_core:GetShopPrices(shopId) or {}
if prices.drink and prices.drink.forSale then print('a drink costs', prices.drink.price) end
Returns: table: { [itemKey] = { price, forSale } }, or false, reason (not a stocked shop, no such shop)

Shops (Client)

IsShopOpen()CLIENT

Check if the shop UI is currently open.

Returns: boolean
GetActiveShopId()CLIENT

Get the shop ID the player is currently browsing. Returns nil if no shop is open.

Returns: number|nil

Properties & Homes

A property is a home a player can own: a house, a flat, a studio. It is built from three pieces, and knowing them explains everything else on this page.

PieceWhat it isExample
TemplateOne per interior (MLO archetype)A half-floor of Mega Tower B
UnitOne home inside that interior (its space, doors, signs, garage), measured from the interior's own originFlat 5 of the four on that half-floor
PropertyOne unit at one place the interior stands in the worldB805
Set one up once, and every copy has it. A unit is described in the interior's own space, so every placement of that interior shares it: set up one Mega floor's four flats and the other 35 floors are a button each. Fix a unit (move its sign, redraw its space) and you choose "all N properties on this unit" or "only this one".

Setting one up: /whip → World → Properties → New propertyServer owners

Stand inside the MLO and follow the steps. Nothing is written until Save, and nothing needs typing but the name.

  1. Interior: Read the interior you are standing in (or No interior, for a plain house on the map).
  2. Space: the whole interior, some of its rooms, or drawn in the world: a rectangle square to the interior, a rectangle along a wall (two corners, then how deep), or an outline. The wheel sets the height; other properties show in grey.
  3. Doors: Scan finds the doorways and door-shaped objects at the edge of the space. Give each a role: entrance and garage doors lock to the owner and keyholders; an inner door locks only if you say so. Double doors are paired.
  4. Signs: the outside sign (while it is for sale) and the manager inside (once owned). A suggested spot beside the front door, or aimed at a wall. Until a manager is placed, the owner's Keys stand at the outside sign's spot; Furnish never does: place the manager inside, or the owner types /furnish in the home.
  5. Garage: optional bays for a private garage (below).
  6. Name & settings: name, unit label, building, price, furniture limit, door auto-lock, owner.
  7. Review: then Save.

On an existing property, Edit on its Space, Doors or Garage row opens that one step, and Re-bind on its Interior row moves it onto the interior as it stands now (an MLO moved or re-exported).

Buying one. A property with a price is for sale at its outside sign: the sign lists its name, its garage bays, its rooms (when its space is the interior's rooms and they have been read) and its price. Selecting the price turns it into Purchase? (on a sign post the listing is printed on the board instead, with Purchase? as the one control under it), and selecting that asks how to pay: cash, or any bank account the player can pay from (theirs, or a shared or job account where they have withdraw access). With the money there, it is theirs at once: the sign becomes their manager, the doors lock to them, and the garage is theirs. Without it, the sale is refused and nothing changes. A price of 0 means not for sale: the sign only names it, and only an admin can hand it over (the panel, or SetPropertyOwner).

A whole building: Register here and Stamp modeServer owners

Register here: stand in another copy of an interior that has a template. Each of its units shows as already a property, overlapping one, or free. Name them from a pattern and press Register:

In a nameBecomes
{b}the building
{u} / {k}the unit's label / key
{f}the floor
{n} / {nn}a number counting up through the units from the start number / the same with two digits

B{f}{nn} on floor 8 starting at 5 names a half-floor's four flats B805 to B808.

Stamp mode (from Register here) flies you through the building. Every copy of a known interior lights up as you enter it:

KeyDoes
ERegister this copy with the current names
PgUp / PgDnFloor up / down
Tab / QNext / previous block of numbers. After each E they move on by themselves, so a row of one-flat studios needs nothing but E
EscDone

Export puts every interior an MLO has into one pack: open Export on one template, then Add the others.

Checking them: Verify and Quick checkServer owners

Verify now (one property) or Verify… (everything the list is showing) takes you to each one, waits for its interior to load and checks that it is the same interior, standing where the property says, with the same rooms and doorways, and every managed door where it should be. Space pauses, → skips one, Esc stops; you are brought back where you started. Quick check is the server's instant re-check of the list, without going anywhere.

StatusMeans
okVerify stood in it and found nothing wrong
unverifiedNever checked, or its placement or parts changed since it was
attentionSomething needs an admin; the reason says what (the list's "Needs attention" filter)

Owning one

  • Doors are managed doors: the owner and keyholders are written onto them, and the door system does the rest. Unowned, they open for nobody.
  • Keys are given face to face at the manager sign (within Config.PropertyKeyGrantRange). A key cannot outlive the owner who gave it: a change of owner takes every key back.
  • Furniture: the owner furnishes from the manager sign, up to the property's furniture limit.
  • Stashes: some furniture holds things (below). Only the owner and keyholders can open it.
  • Theme: when the resource that built the interior offers looks (below), the people who can furnish the home pick one from the same sign: Theme turns its prompt into the list of looks, each circle a swatch of that look's walls, trim and floor. A sale keeps it.
  • Private garage: a unit with bays gives each of its properties a garage of its own. Only the owner and keyholders see its bays; it has no blip, and GetNearestGarage never answers it. Lose access (a key taken back, the home sold) and any car of yours inside moves to the nearest public garage, with a message saying where.

Stashes

Furniture listed in Config.PropertyStashProps becomes a stash of the property it is placed in. Its open prompt sits on the piece of furniture, and only the owner and keyholders see it or can open it. In the furnisher it stays in its own category, and also shows under Containers.

  • It stays with its furniture. Move the piece and save: the stash moves with it, contents and all.
  • Nothing in a stash is thrown away. A save that would take away a stash with anything in it is refused, naming the stash to empty first. The admin's Clear is refused the same way. An admin can open any stash from /whip → Economy → Containers.
  • A new owner gets the stashes and what is in them, as they get the furniture.
  • Deleting the property deletes its stashes; what they held is written to the item log as lost.
  • A property has at most Config.PropertyStashLimit stashes. Lowering the limit takes none away.
-- config.lua: the model (from the furnisher's catalog), what players see, its slots and the most kg
Config.PropertyStashProps = {
    ['v_res_tre_wardrobe'] = { label = 'Wardrobe', slots = 40, weight = 150.0 },
    ['prop_ld_int_safe_01'] = { label = 'Safe', slots = 10, weight = 40.0 },
}

Interior themes

A resource that builds interiors can give its homes several looks (walls, trim and floor, one MLO entity set each), and whip finds it on its own. It needs one line in its fxmanifest.lua, whip_interior_themes 'v1', and four server exports. whip reads them when whip_core starts and whenever that resource starts. A whip property is one of its homes when the interior and origin it was set up on match a home's, within 2 m. Nothing has to be set up. The property's admin page, and the wizard when it is set up there, then show the looks. Its sign gets a Theme option beside Furnish for the owner (and admins).

Export (server)What whip expects
GetThemes(){ { id = 0, name = 'Original', walls = '#rrggbb', trim = '#rrggbb', floor = '#rrggbb' }, ... }: ids 0 to 255; 0 is a home's look until somebody picks another. The colours are the swatch players see
GetHomes(){ { key, archetype, designArchetype?, position }, ... }: archetype is the MLO's archetype name and position its instance origin, the two things whip stores for a property. designArchetype, when a home's interior was replaced, is the one it used to place, so a property set up before still matches
SetAllThemes(map){ [key] = themeId }: every home's look, whole (a home left out is 0). Sent when whip starts and when your resource starts
SetHomeTheme(key, themeId)One home changed. Answer true, or false, why

Your client draws the look. On an interior that loads fresh, switch the entity set before it is ready, with no RefreshInterior. When a change lands on an interior that is already showing, refresh it, then fire TriggerEvent('whip_core:interiorRefreshed', interiorId) so whip makes that home's furniture again: furniture left on a refreshed interior keeps lamps that light nothing.

-- fxmanifest.lua
whip_interior_themes 'v1'

-- client: a theme changed on a home that is showing
ActivateInteriorEntitySet(interiorId, 'wh_theme_2')
RefreshInterior(interiorId)
TriggerEvent('whip_core:interiorRefreshed', interiorId)

Shipping it with an MLOServer owners

Templates & packs → Export writes an interior (and where each copy stands) as a plain-data whip_properties.lua. Put it in the MLO's resource with one manifest line (whip_property_pack 'whip_properties.lua') and every server that ensures the MLO gets its homes with no admin steps. The file format is in whip_core/docs/properties.md.

ConfigDefaultWhat it does
PropertyMaxObjects150The furniture limit, unless a property's own settings say otherwise
PropertyKeyGrantRange5.0How close someone must stand to be handed a key
PropertyStreamRange60.0How close a property's sign appears from
PropertyFurnitureDistance20.0How close to a property's walls you must be for its furniture to appear (inside counts); it goes again 2 m further out. 0 = only while inside. Close enough that an MLO's interior is there and settled before anything is made in it
PropertyFurnitureRooms4How many properties show their furniture at once: the one you are in, then the nearest. Keeps an apartment tower from furnishing every flat that close
PropertySignPlaceRange12.0How far away an admin can aim a sign from
PropertyStashProps4 piecesThe furniture that is a stash once placed: ['model'] = { label, slots, weight }. See Stashes
PropertyStashLimit6The most stashes one property may have

Properties & Props

Houses and apartments (a property is one unit of an interior at one placement), the furniture inside them, and the catalogue of props that may be placed. Properties are set up in /whip → World → Properties; these exports read them, and set owners and keys. A property's doors are managed doors: its owner and keyholders are written onto them, and the door system does the rest.

GetProperty(propertyId)SERVER

One property: its name, owner, placement, space and signs, plus its keyholders (keys), its doors (doorIds), settings, its private garage (garageKey, when its unit has bays), and how it stands (status 'ok' | 'unverified' | 'attention', with statusReason). WhipProperty in types/server.lua lists every field.

local home = exports.whip_core:GetProperty(propertyId)
if not home then return false, 'No such property' end
print(home.name, home.ownerCharId, #home.keys)
Returns: table|nil
GetProperties()SERVER

Every property, as clients see them (no keyholders, doors or settings).

Returns: table[]
GetPropertyAt(x, y, z)SERVER

The property whose space holds this point, or nil. Takes a vector3 too.

local home = exports.whip_core:GetPropertyAt(GetEntityCoords(GetPlayerPed(source)))
if home then print('inside', home.name) end
Returns: table|nil
GetCharacterProperties(charId)SERVER

The property ids a character owns and holds keys to: { owned = {...}, keys = {...} }.

Returns: table
HasPropertyAccess(propertyId, who)SERVER

Is this person (a server id, or { charId = n }) the property's owner or a keyholder?

local ok, why = exports.whip_core:HasPropertyAccess(propertyId, source)
if not ok then return false, why end
Returns: true, or false, why ('No key to that property', 'No such property')
SetPropertyOwner(propertyId, who)SERVER

Give a property to a person (a server id, or { charId = n }), or pass nil or false to make it unowned. A change of owner takes back every key and locks the doors.

-- A real-estate sale: the money first, then the house, or the money back
local receipt, err = exports.whip_core:ChargePlayer(buyerSource, price, { method = 'bank', reason = 'House' })
if not receipt then return false, err end

local ok, why = exports.whip_core:SetPropertyOwner(propertyId, buyerSource)
if not ok then
    exports.whip_core:RefundPlayer(receipt)
    return false, why
end
Returns: boolean, string|nil
GivePropertyKey / RemovePropertyKey(propertyId, who)SERVER

Give a person (a server id, or { charId = n }) a key, or take it back. In game, keys are handed over face to face from the property's sign; these skip that rule.

local ok, err = exports.whip_core:GivePropertyKey(propertyId, { charId = roommateCharId })
if not ok then print(err) end   -- 'They already have a key'

exports.whip_core:RemovePropertyKey(propertyId, { charId = roommateCharId })
Returns: boolean, string|nil
GetPropertyObjectCount(propertyId)SERVER

How many pieces of furniture a property holds. Config.PropertyMaxObjects is the default limit.

Returns: number
GetPropertyObjectVersion(propertyId)SERVER

The version of a property's furniture. It goes up with every save and clear. A furniture save names the version it was made over and is refused over any other, so an editor opened on an old or empty copy of the room can never overwrite the real one.

Returns: number: 0 for a room never furnished this session
GetPropertyStashes(propertyId)SERVER

A property's stashes, in the order they were made: { containerId, name, slots, maxWeight, x, y, z } each. The containerId works with the container calls.

-- A police raid: which stashes the home has
for _, stash in ipairs(exports.whip_core:GetPropertyStashes(propertyId)) do
    print(stash.containerId, stash.name, stash.slots)
end
Returns: table[]: empty for a property with none
GetPropertyThemes(propertyId)SERVER

A property's looks: { label, current, themes = { { id, name, walls, trim, floor }, ... } }, or nil when its interior has none. label names the resource they come from.

local looks = exports.whip_core:GetPropertyThemes(propertyId)
if looks then print('in use:', looks.current, 'of', #looks.themes) end
Returns: table|nil
SetPropertyTheme(propertyId, themeId)SERVER

Give a property one of its looks, as its owner would from the sign, with no check on who asks. It is saved, then the interior's resource redraws the home.

local ok, err = exports.whip_core:SetPropertyTheme(propertyId, 3)
if not ok then print(err) end   -- 'That is not one of its themes'
Returns: boolean, string|nil
RegisterPropertyPack(pack)SERVER

Register an MLO's homes from a script: the same table a whip_property_pack file returns (whip_core/docs/properties.md has the format). Most MLOs need neither: the manifest line whip_property_pack 'whip_properties.lua' is found on its own. The pack belongs to the calling resource, and is checked whole first: the first mistake refuses it, saying where.

Returns: boolean ok, string: 'applied', 'unchanged' (nothing written) or 'queued' (before whip finished starting), or 'path: why' when refused
Applying it again is free. A pack identical to the last one applied writes nothing. A changed one only moves what the pack itself set: an admin's changes, owners, keys and furniture are never touched, and a home an admin deleted is not made again.
GetPropertyPacks()SERVER

The packs whip knows (id, resource, version, label, running) and the pack files it refused (file, error): what the Templates & packs tab shows.

Returns: { packs = {...}, problems = {...} }
GetCurrentProperty()CLIENT

The property the local player is standing in, or nil: { id, name, label, building, ownerCharId, mine, key } (key: this character holds a key). whip_core:property:entered and :exited fire as it changes.

local home = exports.whip_core:GetCurrentProperty()
if home and (home.mine or home.key) then
    -- the player is inside a home they may use
end
Returns: table|nil
GetInteriorFurnishState(interiorId)CLIENT

How far along whip's furniture is for the property an interior belongs to, for an interior resource that keeps its windows covered until the room behind them is finished. The interior is matched to the property whose placement it stands on.

AnswerMeans
'pending'whip will make it, or make it again, and it is not up yet: waiting for the interior to be ready and settle, the rows, the floor, or a remake after whip_core:interiorRefreshed
'done'It is up (or the furnisher has the room open: its editing copies stand in for it)
'none'Nothing to wait for: the property has no saved furniture, or the interior is not a property's
'idle'It has furniture, but whip is not making it now: further than PropertyFurnitureDistance from its walls, or not among the PropertyFurnitureRooms nearest

Cheap (a table lookup), but each call crosses into whip_core: ask a few times a second rather than every frame, or listen for whip_core:property:furnishStateChanged.

-- Keep the cover up until whip says there is nothing left to make
local ok, state = pcall(function() return exports.whip_core:GetInteriorFurnishState(interiorId) end)
if not ok or state == 'done' or state == 'none' then
    -- reveal the room
end
Returns: 'pending' | 'done' | 'none' | 'idle'
GetPropCatalog()SERVER

The placeable-prop catalogue, in the shape the client is sent.

Returns: table[]
RegisterProps(list)SERVER

A prop or MLO pack's props in the furnisher while the pack runs, under one of its categories, with your own pictures: no edit to config.lua or the media packs. The list is the pack's whole list (one left out of a later call goes), and all go when the pack stops. A model whip already lists keeps its row and an admin's choices on it, and takes your picture. List the pictures in your resource's files { }.

exports.whip_core:RegisterProps({
    { model = 'mypack_armchair', name = 'Velvet armchair', category = 'seating', image = 'img/armchair.webp' },
})
