Returns: true, or false, why (a category that is not one of Config.PropCategories, a picture not in your resource, a model another pack registered)
HasPropImage(model)SERVER

Does this prop model have a preview image on disk?

ParamTypeDescription
modelstringProp model name. Case-insensitive
Returns: boolean
IsPlaceableProp(model)SERVER

May this prop model be placed? false for an unknown model, and for one the catalogue marks unavailable. Ask it before placing a model a client named.

if not exports.whip_core:IsPlaceableProp(model) then
    return false, 'That cannot be placed'
end
ParamTypeDescription
modelstringProp model name. Case-insensitive
Returns: boolean

Door System

Overview

Take control of any door in the game world. Walk up to it, save it, lock/unlock it, set who may open it. The server decides every lock and unlock.

How It Works

  1. Doors are saved via the in-game Door Editor or CreateDoor() export
  2. Saved doors stay saved across restarts
  3. Each saved door carries an E prompt on each handle (the interaction system), usable within Config.DoorInteractRange (3 m)
  4. Player presses E → server checks requirements → allows or denies

Requirements

Meeting any one of them lets a player in. All are optional.

RequirementTypeCheck
jobsstring[]Player has a role at one of these jobs (employed, or the owner), on duty or not
onDutyboolWith jobs: only while on duty at that job (the Doors page's "On duty only")
charIdsnumber[]Character ID is in the list
itemstable[]Player carries one of these items
acestringPlayer has ACE permission
lockpickboolAllow lockpick skill check as fallback

Double Doors

Two physical doors can be linked: lock one, the other locks too. Use LinkDoors(id1, id2) or link them in the Door Editor; UnlinkDoors(id) or the Doors page's Unlink button separates them.

Shipping a map's doors

A map or MLO resource declares its doors with EnsureDoors (one list, each door named by a key) instead of running a door script of its own. Every start it brings the doors in line with the list: new keys are made, changed ones updated, dropped ones released. The doors are managed, so their access stays what the list says.

Quick Example

-- Server: the police station's doors, declared (inside Whip.register)
exports.whip_core:EnsureDoors({
    { key = 'front', label = 'PD Front Door', folder = 'Mission Row PD',
      model = 631614199, coords = vector4(434.7, -980.6, 30.7, 180.0),
      requirements = { jobs = {'police', 'ems'}, lockpick = true } },
}, { label = 'Mission Row PD' })

-- Or one door, saved and then left to admins:
local door, why = exports.whip_core:CreateDoor({
    label = 'Back Door', model = 631614199, x = 468.5, y = -1014.4, z = 26.4, heading = 0.0,
})

In game: the Door EditorServer owners

/whip → World → Doors opens the Doors page (every saved door, grouped by folder). Open the editor lets you fly around in noclip with the door lighting of the property door picker: every saved door near you is lit on its leaf: green, or grey when a system manages it (a property's door, changed in Properties), with a white line between linked leaves. The one you look at is brighter, outlined white and named over its top (#12 · Front · locked); an object that is not a door yet lights amber. Walls stop your aim, and a saved door near your line of sight is taken even when it stands open edge-on. Press G to save it, and whip controls it from then on; E links two saved doors, R deletes one.

Setting a door up properly: the wizard. + New Door (or Set up a new door with none picked). Five steps, nothing saved until the last:

  1. Door: Pick it in the world opens the editor to pick: G (A on a pad) takes the door you aim at, or lets a taken one go; for a double door take its other leaf too (they are linked, and open and lock together). Enter (☰) comes back with them, Esc (B) without. A door that is saved already cannot be taken
  2. Name: what the list calls it, and its folder: one it has (a chip), a new one typed, or none
  3. Locking: starts locked or unlocked; Locks itself after 1–300 seconds; Can be picked
  4. Access: Anyone, or Only some people: jobs, on duty only, an ACE, characters (any one of them will do). A door that can be picked with nobody named opens for nobody but a lockpick, and the step says so
  5. Create: a summary with a Change on each part. Create saves the door (both leaves, linked, or neither), and its page opens

Doors (Server)

EnsureDoors(list, opts)SERVER

Declare your resource's doors: the way a map pack or MLO brings its door locks to whip, instead of shipping a door script of its own that fights whip's locks. The list is your whole set, each door named by a key that stays the same between runs:

  • a new key makes its door, or adopts the door already on that spot;
  • a key you had before: its label, folder, requirements, auto-lock and link follow the list;
  • a key that left the list: its door is released: deleted if the list made it, put back as it was if it was adopted (prune = false keeps them).
Whip.register(function()
    local res, why = exports.whip_core:EnsureDoors({
        { key = 'lobby_l', model = 'v_ilev_ph_gendoor004', coords = vector4(-868.84, -1275.53, 5.10, 110.0), link = 'lobby_r' },
        { key = 'lobby_r', model = 'v_ilev_ph_gendoor004', coords = vector4(-867.60, -1273.20, 5.10, 110.0) },
        { key = 'office',  model = 'v_ilev_ph_gendoor', coords = vector3(-870.1, -1280.4, 5.1),
          requirements = { jobs = { 'realestate' }, onDuty = true }, autolock = true },
    }, { label = 'Pink Lady' })
    if not res then print('doors: ' .. why) return end
    for key, reason in pairs(res.failed) do print('door ' .. key .. ': ' .. reason) end
end)
Name your doors by key afterwards too. Every door export that takes a door takes its id or { key = 'office' } for a door your resource declared (add set = '…' if you declare more than one set). A key reaches only your own doors. exports.whip_core:SetDoorLocked({ key = 'office' }, false)

What changes by key, and what changes in the list. By key: locking (SetDoorLocked, UpdateDoor's locked), reading (IsDoorLocked, IsAuthorizedForDoor, GetDoor), and UpdateDoor's label and folder. The list owns the rest: requirements, autolock, the link, and whether the door exists at all: change the entry in your EnsureDoors list (or take it off to remove the door). UpdateDoor, DeleteDoor, ReleaseDoor, LinkDoors and UnlinkDoors refuse those on a declared door and say so, because the next EnsureDoors would put them back.
FieldTypeDescription
keystringRequired. Yours: letters, digits, _ - . :, at most 60
modelstring | numberRequired. A name, or a hash (signed or not)
coordsvector3 | vector4 | tableRequired. A vector4's w is the heading (or give x, y, z, heading)
label, folderstring?What the Doors page shows. The label defaults to the key
requirementstable?Who may open it; see IsAuthorizedForDoor. Left out: anyone
autolock, autolockDelayboolean?, number?Lock itself again this many seconds after an unlock (default 10): a player's press, SetDoorLocked, UpdateDoor's locked or the Doors page. A picked lock stays open.
linkstring?The key of the other half of a double door

opts: id (several sets per resource, default 'doors'), label (the Doors page's name for them), prune (default true).

The list wins. Your declared doors are managed: the Doors page can rename them but not change who opens them, and a rename is put back the next time your resource starts. Change the list. They stay when your resource stops; an admin can release them from the Doors page once it is gone for good. The whole list is checked before anything is written: one bad entry and nothing changes; a door that cannot be placed (another door on its spot) is reported in failed and the rest go ahead.
Returns: { doors = { [key] = doorId }, failed = { [key] = why }, released = n }, or false, reason
EnsureDoor(key, data, opts)SERVER

One declared door, by key: EnsureDoors for a single door. Never releases any. It is kept in its own set ('door:<key>'), so an EnsureDoors call in the same resource neither prunes it nor is undone by it. A pair of doors is declared with EnsureDoors, where link names the other key in the same list: a single door has nothing to link to. opts.id puts it in a set you name instead. data takes the fields of an EnsureDoors entry, without key and link.

Whip.register(function()
    local door, why = exports.whip_core:EnsureDoor('back_office', {
        model = 'v_ilev_ph_gendoor', coords = vector3(-870.1, -1280.4, 5.1),
        requirements = { jobs = { 'realestate' } },
    })
    if not door then print('back office door: ' .. why) end
end)
Returns: door, or false, reason
CreateDoor(data)SERVER

Save a door to the database and begin managing it. Always created locked. For doors your resource should own and keep in step with its code, use EnsureDoors. Waits for whip_core to finish starting (up to 60 s, then false and why), so it sees the doors already saved.

ParamTypeDescription
datatable{ label, folder, model, x, y, z, heading, requirements, metadata }
local door, err, existingId = exports.whip_core:CreateDoor({
    label = 'Storage Room', model = 'v_ilev_ph_gendoor', x = -870.1, y = -1280.4, z = 5.1, heading = 110.0,
})
if not door then print(err, existingId) end
Returns: the door, or false, reason — and, when another door is already within half a metre, its id as a third value
SetDoorLocked(doorId, locked)SERVER

Lock or unlock a door, and its linked door with it. The players near it are told. UpdateDoor(id, { locked = ... }) does the same.

ParamTypeDescription
doorIdnumber|tableDoor ID, or { key = … } for a door you declared
lockedbooleantrue = lock, false = unlock
local ok, err = exports.whip_core:SetDoorLocked({ key = 'office' }, false)
if not ok then print(err) end
Returns: true, or false, reason
IsAuthorizedForDoor(source, doorId)SERVER

May this player open this door, and if not, the reason they are shown. Requirements are any-of: one match opens it.

RequirementOpens for
jobs = { 'police' }anyone with a role at one of these jobs (employed or the owner), on duty or not…
onDuty = true…with it: only while on duty at that job
charIds = { 12 }these characters
items = { { key = 'keycard' } }anyone carrying one of these ({ key = 'lockpick', count = 2 }: at least that many)
ace = 'whip.admin'anyone holding this ACE
lockpick = true(a locked door offers a lockpick attempt)
Not the same as an action's require. AddAction and AddPoint use the same words the other way round: there, every requirement listed must pass. So { job = 'police', item = 'pd_keycard' } on an action means "a police officer holding the keycard", and on a door it means "any police officer, or anyone holding the keycard". A door or stash given require instead of requirements takes it when it names one rule (require = { job = 'police', onDuty = true } means the same either way) and refuses it, saying why, when it names more. A field a door or stash does not read is said in the server console.
ParamTypeDescription
sourcenumberPlayer server ID
doorIdnumber|tableDoor ID, or { key = … }
local ok, why = exports.whip_core:IsAuthorizedForDoor(source, { key = 'office' })
if not ok then return false, why end
Returns: true, or false, reason — e.g. 'Requires job: police (on duty)', 'Door not found'
LinkDoors(doorId1, doorId2, manager?)SERVER

Link two doors together. Locking/unlocking one automatically does the same to the other. Both halves are written at once; a door's old partner is unlinked.

ParamTypeDescription
doorId1numberFirst door ID
doorId2numberSecond door ID
managertable?The manager that holds them, as for UpdateDoor
local ok, err = exports.whip_core:LinkDoors(leftDoorId, rightDoorId)
if not ok then print(err) end
Returns: true, or false, reason
UnlinkDoors(doorId, manager?)SERVER

Undo a door's link: both halves, at once. true for a door that was not linked. (Setting linkedDoorId = nil in UpdateDoor cannot do it: a nil is no key at all in a Lua table.) The Doors page has an Unlink button too. A door someone manages needs that manager; a door you declared with EnsureDoors is unlinked by taking link off its entry.

ParamTypeDescription
doorIdnumber|tableEither door of the pair (its id, or { key = … })
managertable?The manager that holds it, as for UpdateDoor
Returns: true, or false, reason
GetDoorsNearby(x, y, z, range) · GetDoorsNearby(coords, range)SERVER

Find all saved doors within a range of a point. The same shapes on the client (which can also take just a range, measured from the player).

ParamTypeDescription
x, y, z / coordsnumber / vector3Center position
rangenumberSearch radius in metres (default 25)
-- Lock down every door around the bank
for _, door in ipairs(exports.whip_core:GetDoorsNearby(vector3(255.0, 225.0, 101.9), 30.0)) do
    exports.whip_core:SetDoorLocked(door.doorId, true)
end
Returns: table[]
GetDoor(doorId) SERVER

Get a door's full data from the server cache.

local door = exports.whip_core:GetDoor(17)
if door then
    print(door.label, door.locked)
end
ParamTypeDescription
doorIdnumberDoor database ID
Returns: table|nil
GetAllDoors() SERVER

Every door on the server. This is the complete set: the client's GetLoadedDoors returns only what that player has streamed in.

Returns: table[]: array of all door data
UpdateDoor(doorId, updates, manager) SERVER

Update a door's properties: label, folder, locked, requirements, autolock, autolockDelay, linkedDoorId (as LinkDoors does) and metadata (with its managedBy part unchanged). locked moves the linked door too, like SetDoorLocked. Every door starts locked whenever the server starts, so a lock change lasts until the next restart. Any other field is refused (a door's position and model are fixed). To clear requirements pass {}, not nil.

exports.whip_core:UpdateDoor(17, {
    label       = 'Back Door',
    folder      = 'Police Station',
    autolock    = true,
    autolockDelay = 10,
    requirements = { jobs = {'police'} },
})
ParamTypeDescription
doorIdnumberDoor database ID
updatestableFields to update
managertable|nilFor a door your resource manages (see AdoptOrCreateDoor): the same { id, key?, label? } you manage it as. A managed door refuses changes from anyone else
Returns: true, or false, reason ('Door not found', a managed door that is not yours, bad fields)
DeleteDoor(doorId, manager) SERVER

Delete a saved door from the database and cache.

ParamTypeDescription
doorIdnumberDoor database ID
managertable|nilAs for UpdateDoor: needed to delete a door your resource manages
Returns: true, or false, reason ('Door not found', a managed door that is not yours)
AdoptOrCreateDoor(data, manager) SERVER

Take charge of the door at a spot, making it if there is none. A managed door's requirements, link and auto-lock are yours alone: the Doors page and other resources are refused, because you set them. Your resource is always the manager, whatever you pass. Answers 'created', 'adopted' (a door that was already there, which ReleaseDoor gives back as it was) or 'already'; false, a reason and the id of the door in the way when another manager holds it or a different model is there. Your doors stay yours while your resource is stopped. Waits for whip_core to finish starting (up to 60 s), so a call at your resource's start finds the door already there instead of making a second.

local door, how = exports.whip_core:AdoptOrCreateDoor({
    model = 'v_ilev_gc_door01', x = -1200.4, y = -890.1, z = 13.9, heading = 35.0,
    label = 'Bean Machine', requirements = { jobs = {'beanmachine'} },
}, { id = 4, key = 'front', label = 'Business #4 · Bean Machine' })
ParamTypeDescription
datatable{ model, x, y, z, heading, label, folder, requirements }
managertable{ id, key?, label? }: which of your things holds the door
Returns: table|false, string, number|nil
ReleaseDoor(doorId, manager) SERVER

Give a managed door back. A door made for you is deleted; an adopted one gets back its old requirements, name, folder and auto-lock. true for a door nobody manages; refused for another manager's. UpdateDoor, DeleteDoor and LinkDoors take the same manager as a last argument for doors you hold.

ParamTypeDescription
doorIdnumberDoor database ID
managertable{ id }: the one holding it
-- The business closed: give its front door back
local ok, err = exports.whip_core:ReleaseDoor(doorId, { id = 4 })
if not ok then print(err) end
Returns: boolean, string|nil
HoldDoor(data, opts) SERVER

Hold a door for as long as you need it: a heist's vault, a job's back door. The door at that spot (model, x, y, z as the Door Editor reads them, within half a metre), saved or not: where whip has no door there, a temporary one is made, for every player, and never saved. A hold lives in memory only, so nothing is written to the door's row and a restart leaves no trace. While you hold it, nobody may press it until you say who (SetHeldDoorAccess, or opts.requirements), and it never relocks by itself; lock and unlock it with SetDoorLocked. Both leaves of a linked pair are held. When the hold ends (ReleaseHeldDoor, its tag released with ReleaseTag, or your resource stopping) the door goes back to the lock it had, and a temporary one is gone. Lockpicking stays as the door's own row says. A property's door, another resource's managed door, and a door another hold has are refused.

ParamTypeDescription
datatable{ model, x, y, z, heading?, label? }
optstable?{ tag?, requirements? }: tag releases it with the rest of your job; requirements (a door's shape) is who may press it, nobody when left out
-- vaultModel / vaultPos: what the Door Editor (or GetEntityModel / GetEntityCoords) reads off the door
local vault = exports.whip_core:HoldDoor({ model = vaultModel, x = vaultPos.x, y = vaultPos.y, z = vaultPos.z },
    { tag = 'heist:' .. jobId })
-- the hack passed: open it, and let the crew use it
exports.whip_core:SetDoorLocked(vault, false)
exports.whip_core:SetHeldDoorAccess(vault, { charIds = crewCharIds })
Returns: doorId, how ('held', 'made' for a temporary door, 'already'), or false, reason. Also SetHeldDoorAccess(doorId, requirements) (nil = nobody, {} = anyone), ReleaseHeldDoor(doorId), and GetDoorHold(doorId) → { owner, tag, doorId, made } or nil.
GetManagedDoors(id) SERVER

The doors your resource manages: all of them, or one manager id's. What to reconcile against when your resource starts.

ParamTypeDescription
idany?A manager id, or nil for all
for _, door in ipairs(exports.whip_core:GetManagedDoors(4)) do
    print(door.doorId, door.label)
end
Returns: table[]
IsDoorLocked(doorId) SERVER

Check if a door is currently locked (server-side).

ParamTypeDescription
doorIdnumberDoor database ID
if exports.whip_core:IsDoorLocked({ key = 'vault' }) then
    return false, 'The vault is shut'
end
Returns: true / false, or nil for a door that does not exist
GetDoorByPosition(x, y, z, range)SERVER

Find a registered door near a set of coordinates. Use it when you know where a door is but not its ID: a doorlock script reacting to a raycast, or a job script locking whatever door is in front of the player.

ParamTypeDescription
x, y, znumberWorld position to search around
rangenumber|nilSearch radius in metres (default 1). The first door found within it is answered, not the nearest: keep it small
local door = exports.whip_core:GetDoorByPosition(x, y, z, 1.0)
if door then exports.whip_core:SetDoorLocked(door.doorId, true) end
Returns: table|nil: the door definition

Doors (Client)

IsDoorLocked(doorId)CLIENT

Check if a door is currently locked, from the client's proximity cache.

local locked = exports.whip_core:IsDoorLocked(17)
if locked then
    print('Door is locked')
end
ParamTypeDescription
doorIdnumberDoor ID
Returns: true / false, or nil for a door the client does not know
A far door is as of your last visit. Lock changes are sent to the players near a door; the client catches up on a door's state as it comes back into range. Gate nothing that matters on a far door's answer — ask the server's IsDoorLocked.
GetDoorByEntity(entity)CLIENT

Find the saved door data for a world entity (by matching model + position).

ParamTypeDescription
entitynumberEntity handle
Returns: table|nil: door data
GetDoorsNearby(range) · GetDoorsNearby(coords, range) · GetDoorsNearby(x, y, z, range)CLIENT

Get all saved doors within a range of the player, or of a point, with the same shapes the server export takes.

ParamTypeDescription
coords / x, y, zvector3 / numberOptional. Left out, the player's position
rangenumberRange in metres (default 25)
Returns: table[]
GetLoadedDoors() CLIENT

Every door the client has streamed in: the ones the player has been near enough to load. Not every door on the server. For the complete set, ask the server's GetAllDoors.

Returns: table[]: array of door data tables
GetDoor(doorId) CLIENT

Get the full data table for a specific door by ID from the client cache.

local door = exports.whip_core:GetDoor(17)
if door then
    print(door.label, door.locked, door.x, door.y, door.z)
end
ParamTypeDescription
doorIdnumberThe door's database ID
Returns: table|nil: full door data or nil

Zone System

Overview

Zones are areas in the game world (boxes, spheres, or polygons) that know when players enter or leave. Players are checked against them every Config.ZonePollInterval (300 ms).

Zone Types

TypeShapeUse case
ZoneBoxRotatable rectangle with heightBuildings, rooms, garages
ZoneSphere3D sphereProximity areas, checkpoints
ZonePolyArbitrary polygon with min/max ZIrregular shapes, parking lots, yards

Quick Example

-- Client, in Whip.register: a safe zone (on the server, declare one with EnsureZone)
local id = exports.whip_core:ZoneBox({
    pos   = vec3(440, -980, 30),
    size  = vec3(20, 20, 10),
    label = 'Police Station',
    group = 'police',
    rules = {
        noPvP     = true,
        noWeapons = true,
        heal      = true,
    },
    notify = true,
    onEnter = function(zone) end,
    onExit  = function(zone) end,
})

Rules Engine

Give a zone a rule and whip enforces it inside, with no code of your own.

RuleTypeEffect
noWeaponsboolRemove weapons on entry, block re-equipping
noPvPboolSafe zone: the player cannot be hurt, and cannot fire or melee while inside
noMeleeboolBlock punching/melee
disableFiringboolBlock firing but allow carrying
speedLimitnumberVehicle speed cap (km/h)
noVehiclesboolEject from vehicle on entry
healboolGradual health regen
healRatenumberHP per tick (default 2)
noWantedLevelboolClear and prevent wanted level
noCollisionboolDisable ped-to-ped collision
noFallDamageboolNo fall damage inside. The player is collision-proof, so crashes and being run over do no damage either.
ejectUnauthorizedboolTeleport unauthorized out

Authorization

Zones can restrict access by job, ACE permission, or character ID. Meeting any one of them lets a player in.

rules = {
    jobWhitelist      = {'police', 'ems'},
    aceWhitelist      = 'whip.vip',
    charWhitelist     = {1, 5},
    ejectUnauthorized = true,
}

Saved zones

Zones made in the Zone Editor or with EnsureZone() are saved and come back at every start. A resource's EnsureZone(key, data) is re-run every start and follows your code when you change it; ask for the zone by its key everywhere (ZoneContains('mrpd', pos), require = { zone = 'mrpd' } on an action). For the server to hear players come and go, give it trackPlayers = true and listen for whip_core:zone:entered / exited; see Zones (Server).

Events

On the client, any resource can hear the local player cross any zone, without creating its own:

AddEventHandler('whip_core:zone:entered', function(zone)
    if zone.group == 'police_station' then
        -- player entered a police zone (zone.id, zone.label are there too)
    end
end)

AddEventHandler('whip_core:zone:exited', function(zone)
    -- player left a zone
end)

In game: the Zone EditorServer owners

/whip → World → Zones opens the Zones page. The Zone Editor provides a free-cam mode where you can fly around, create zones visually (press 1/2/3 for box/sphere/poly), scan rooms (H), edit vertices (4/5), adjust size with scroll, and save to DB.

Room Scanner (Paint Mode)Server owners

Make an outline zone by flying through a room: whip traces its walls as you go, so there are no points to click.

  1. Enter the Zone Editor (/whip → World → Zones → Open the editor)
  2. Fly inside a room
  3. Press H to start scanning: rays fire automatically as you move
  4. Fly through the room: the polygon builds in real time
  5. Press H again to stop and preview
  6. Scroll to adjust height, G to confirm

Doorways and windows are smoothed over, so the outline follows the walls rather than escaping through openings.

Vertex EditorServer owners

Edit individual polygon vertices after creation: no need to delete and redo.

KeyModeEffect
4Position modeMove vertex XY position (yellow markers)
5Height modeAdjust vertex Z height only (blue markers)
EGrabSelect nearest vertex
GConfirmSave vertex position
ScrollHeightAdjust ceiling (Ctrl+Scroll for floor)
EscCancelRevert vertex to original position

Per-vertex Z heights: Each vertex can have its own ceiling and floor height. This allows a single zone to cover a two-story mansion where the garage has a lower ceiling than the main building: the walls slope between different heights.

Zones (Server)

Two kinds of zone live on the server: server zones a resource registers at runtime (ZoneRegister, gone when it stops) and saved zones in the database (EnsureZone and the zone editor, synced to every client). Every lookup takes a saved zone's key as well as its id: a saved zone's id is 'dbzone_<n>', which no resource can know.

Server enter and exit events. Give a zone trackPlayers = true (either kind) and the server sweeps it every Config.ZoneTrackInterval ms (default 1000), firing local server events: AddEventHandler('whip_core:zone:entered', function(e) ... end) with { zoneId, key?, source }, and whip_core:zone:exited with the same plus dropped = true (the player left the server inside it) or removed = true (the zone went with them in it). The client fires events of the same names for its own player; those are the player's word, these are the server's. A player still in the character creator, or logging out, is not in any zone; a player in another routing bucket (an instance) is, wherever they stand.
The server sees a client zone as most of its players see it. A zone made on the client (ZoneBox, ZoneSphere, …) is reported to the server so ZoneContains knows it, by every player who has it. ZoneUpdatePosition, ZoneUpdateSize and re-registering the same id are reported too (at most twice a second per zone), and the server takes the shape most of those players hold, so a zone your resource moves on everyone's screen follows on the server once most of them have moved it, and one modified client reporting a different shape is outvoted. A zone only one player has is whatever that player reports, so a zone the server must be able to trust belongs in ZoneRegister or EnsureZone. A client zone id must be letters, digits, _ and -, 60 at most, or the server never hears of it (the client says so in F8).
ZoneRegister(id, data)SERVER

Register a zone on the server for server-side point-in-zone checks. No tick thread — purely on-demand queries, unless you ask for trackPlayers. The id is yours once registered (the registration rule): another resource's is refused, and your zones go when your resource stops. The shape is checked — a sphere needs pos and radius, a box pos and size, a poly 3 or more points — and refused with what was wrong rather than stored as a zone nothing is ever inside.

ParamTypeDescription
idstringZone ID
datatableZone data (type, pos, size, heading, radius, points, minZ, maxZ, group, label, trackPlayers, tag — your run tag: ReleaseTag removes it after the rest of the run)
Whip.register(function()
    local ok, err = exports.whip_core:ZoneRegister('vault', {
        type = 'box', pos = vector3(255.0, 225.0, 101.9), size = vector3(10.0, 8.0, 4.0), heading = 70.0,
        trackPlayers = true,   -- fire whip_core:zone:entered / :exited on the server
    })
    if not ok then print(err) end
end)
Returns: true, or false, reason
ZoneContains(id, point, trusted)SERVER

Check if a vec3 point is inside a zone. A saved zone (EnsureZone, the editor) or a ZoneRegister one is the server's own; a zone made on the client answers as its players report it. For anti-cheat, pass trusted = true: then only the server's own zones answer, and a client-made one is false.

ParamTypeDescription
idstringZone id, or a saved zone's key
pointvector3Point to test
trustedboolean?true: answer only from a zone the server holds
local here = GetEntityCoords(GetPlayerPed(source))
if not exports.whip_core:ZoneContains('mrpd', here, true) then
    return false, 'You need to be at the station'
end
Returns: boolean
GetPlayersInZone(id)SERVER

Get all player source IDs currently inside a zone. Iterates all players and tests each position — to react as they come and go, use trackPlayers and the events above instead of calling this in a loop. Players in the character creator or logging out are left out; routing buckets are not looked at.

for _, src in ipairs(exports.whip_core:GetPlayersInZone('mrpd')) do
    exports.whip_core:NotifyPlayer(src, 'Lockdown in progress')
end
ParamTypeDescription
idstringZone id, or a saved zone's key
Returns: number[] — array of player source IDs
GetVehiclesInZone(id)SERVER

The vehicles currently inside a zone. vehicleId is nil for a car whip does not track (an ambient NPC car); entity is always there.

for _, v in ipairs(exports.whip_core:GetVehiclesInZone('impound_lot')) do
    if v.vehicleId then exports.whip_core:StoreVehicle(v.vehicleId, 'impound') end
end
ParamTypeDescription
idstringZone id, or a saved zone's key
Returns: { vehicleId, entity }[]
EnsureZone(key, data)SERVER

A saved zone, declared by a key you choose. Made the first time; brought up to date when your declaration changes. The same declaration again writes nothing, so an admin's edits in the zone editor stand until you change yours (a different type makes a new zone under the same key). A key another running resource declared is refused. Call it from Whip.register every start.

Whip.register(function()
    local zone, why = exports.whip_core:EnsureZone('mrpd', {
        type = 'box', pos = vector3(441.0, -982.0, 30.7), size = vector3(60, 50, 20), heading = 0,
        label = 'Mission Row PD', trackPlayers = true,
    })
    if not zone then print('mrpd zone: ' .. why) end
end)
-- then everywhere: ZoneContains('mrpd', pos), and on the client require = { zone = 'mrpd' }
ParamTypeDescription
keystringYours: letters, digits, _ - . :, at most 60
datatabletype ('box' | 'sphere' | 'poly'), pos, size + heading (box), radius (sphere), points (poly, 3 or more), minZ, maxZ, label, group, priority, rules, notify, trackVehicles, trackPlayers
Returns: zone, or false, reason
DeleteZone(keyOrId)SERVER

Delete a saved zone by key or id, for every player. Refused for a zone another running resource declares (it would be made again the next time that resource starts), and for a server zone: ZoneRemove removes your own.

ParamTypeDescription
keyOrIdstringThe zone's key, or its 'dbzone_<n>' id
Returns: true, or false, reason
GetAllZones()SERVER

Every zone the server knows about, as a list. To find one by id use GetZoneDef(id); a list is not keyed, so GetAllZones()[id] is always nil.

Returns: table: { zoneDef, zoneDef, … }
GetZoneDef(id)SERVER

One zone's definition, server-side.

ParamTypeDescription
idstringZone id, or a saved zone's key
Returns: table|nil
ZoneRemove(id)SERVER

Remove one of your server-side zones. The mirror of ZoneRemove on the client: server and client keep separate registries, so removing one does not remove the other.

ParamTypeDescription
idstringZone ID
Returns: true, or false, reason: not registered, or registered by another resource

Zones (Client)

ZoneBox(data)CLIENT

Create a box zone. Give it an id (letters, digits, _ and -, 60 at most): the same id again replaces it, and the server only learns of a zone with an id like that.

ParamTypeDescription
datatable{ id, pos, size, heading, onEnter, onExit, inside, condition, priority, group, label, debug, rules, notify, weather, trackVehicles, onVehicleEnter, onVehicleExit }
Whip.register(function()
    exports.whip_core:ZoneBox({
        id = 'myres_yard', pos = vector3(215.8, -810.1, 30.7), size = vector3(20.0, 15.0, 6.0), heading = 70.0,
        label = 'Scrap Yard', notify = true,
        rules = { noWeapons = true },
        onEnter = function() print('entered the yard') end,
    })
end)
Returns: string zone ID, or false, why when that id is another resource's
ZoneSphere(data)CLIENT

Create a sphere zone.

ParamTypeDescription
datatable{ id, pos, radius, … }: the same fields as ZoneBox, with radius for size
Returns: string zone ID, or false, why
ZonePoly(data)CLIENT

Create a polygon zone.

ParamTypeDescription
datatable{ id, points (vec2[]), minZ, maxZ, … }: the same fields as ZoneBox, with points for pos/size
Returns: string zone ID, or false, why
ZoneRemove(id)CLIENT

Delete one of your zones by ID. Fires onExit if the player was inside. Another resource's zone is refused.

ParamTypeDescription
idstringZone ID
Returns: true, or false, why
ZoneRemoveGroup(group)CLIENT

Delete all of your zones in a group. Another resource's zones in a group of the same name stay.

ParamTypeDescription
groupstringGroup name
Returns: true, count, or false, why
The setters change your own zones. ZoneUpdatePosition, ZoneUpdateSize, every ZoneSet… and ZoneToggleRule take a zone's id or, for a saved zone, its key ('mrpd'), and change only a zone your resource made: whip_core's saved zones and another resource's are refused. Each answers true, or false, why ('no zone "x"', 'zone "x" belongs to …').
ZoneContains(id, point)CLIENT

Check if a point is inside a zone. Instant math check, no polling.

ParamTypeDescription
idstringZone id, or a saved zone's key (EnsureZone)
pointvector3Point to test
Returns: boolean
ZoneIsInside(id)CLIENT

Is the local player currently inside this zone? Based on last polling tick.

ParamTypeDescription
idstringZone id, or a saved zone's key (EnsureZone)
Returns: boolean
ZoneGetInside()CLIENT

Get all zone IDs the local player is currently inside.

Returns: string[]
ZoneGetNearby(pos, radius)CLIENT

Find all zones within a radius of a point, sorted by distance.

ParamTypeDescription
posvector3Center point
radiusnumberSearch radius (default 50m)
Returns: table[]: { id, type, label, pos, dist }
ZoneSetRules(id, rules)CLIENT

Replace the rules table on a zone. See Zone guide for all available rules.

ParamTypeDescription
idstringZone ID
rulestableRules table (noWeapons, noPvP, speedLimit, etc.)
-- Lockdown: the yard turns into a no-weapons, no-PvP zone
exports.whip_core:ZoneSetRules('myres_yard', { noWeapons = true, noPvP = true })
ZoneToggleRule(id, ruleKey)CLIENT

Toggle a single rule on/off.

ParamTypeDescription
idstringZone ID
ruleKeystringRule name (e.g. 'noWeapons')
ZoneUpdatePosition(id, pos)CLIENT

Move a zone to a new position. Re-indexes the spatial grid.

ParamTypeDescription
idstringZone ID
posvector3New center
ZoneUpdateSize(id, size)CLIENT

Resize a zone in place and re-index the spatial grid. The shape stays what it was: pass what that shape expects: a radius for a sphere, a vector3 of dimensions for a box.

ParamTypeDescription
idstringZone ID
sizenumber | vector3Radius for a sphere; dimensions for a box
Returns: true, or false, why: a poly (resized by its points), or a size its shape does not take. The zone is left as it was.
GetZoneDef(id)CLIENT

The full definition of one zone, as the client currently holds it: shape, size, rules, label, priority. Also inside (is the player in it right now), debug, and hasCondition: whether a gate function is attached by ZoneSetCondition. The condition function itself is not returned: it belongs to whoever set it, and the poll loop owns when it runs.

ParamTypeDescription
idstringZone ID
Returns: table|nil
ZoneGetCount()CLIENT

How many zones this client is currently tracking. Useful when checking that a resource cleaned up after itself.

Returns: number
ZoneSetCondition(id, fn)CLIENT

Attach a predicate that decides whether the zone counts as active right now. Returning false makes the zone behave as though the player is not in it: rules off, no enter/exit events.

ParamTypeDescription
idstringZone ID
fnfunction() → boolean
The same as condition in the zone's table: a function crosses to whip_core as a callable reference either way. This form swaps it on a zone that already exists, without making the zone again.
ZoneSetLabel(id, label)CLIENT

Change the display name shown when the player enters the zone.

ParamTypeDescription
idstringZone ID
labelstringNew label
ZoneSetPriority(id, priority)CLIENT

Set which zone wins where two overlap. The rules of every zone you stand in hold together (a no-PvP, no-weapons or no-vehicles from any of them applies), so priority decides only what can disagree: the speed limit (the highest-priority zone that sets one; two at the same priority, the lower limit), the weather (its layer), and the order of the enter and exit callbacks (enters highest first, exits lowest first). A car park's 20 km/h inside a district's 60 needs the higher priority.

ParamTypeDescription
idstringZone ID
prioritynumberHigher wins
ZoneSetNotify(id, enabled)CLIENT

Turn the on-screen enter/exit notification for this zone on or off. The enter and exit events still fire either way: this only controls whether the player is told.

ParamTypeDescription
idstringZone ID
enabledboolean
ZoneSetTrackVehicles(id, enabled)CLIENT

Test the player's vehicle position against the zone instead of the ped's. Matters at speed: a ped's position inside a fast car can skip clean over a thin zone between frames.

ParamTypeDescription
idstringZone ID
enabledboolean
ZoneSetDebug(id, enabled)CLIENT

Draw this zone's outline in the world so you can see where it actually is. Development only: it draws every frame.

ParamTypeDescription
idstringZone ID
enabledboolean

Time & Weather

Overview

The server keeps one clock and one weather for everyone, and every player's game follows it, ticking smoothly between updates. One player can be shown a different time or weather through layers (below): night in a club, fog in a zone, a storm during a mission.

Read the time with local h, m = exports.whip_core:GetTime(). The time, the weather, a frozen clock, a blackout and the time scale are all saved, so a restart picks up where it left off. A new server starts from Config.StartTime.

Config

Config.TimeScale    = 1.0     -- 1.0 = normal GTA speed (48min real = 24h game)
Config.StartTime    = { hour = 12, minute = 0 }
Config.StartWeather = 'CLEAR'

Config.WeatherTypes = {
    'CLEAR', 'EXTRASUNNY', 'CLOUDS', 'OVERCAST', 'RAIN',
    'CLEARING', 'THUNDER', 'SMOG', 'FOGGY', 'XMAS',
    'SNOWLIGHT', 'BLIZZARD', 'HALLOWEEN', 'NEUTRAL',
}

One player's sky: layers

To give one player a different time or weather (night inside a club, fog in a zone, a storm during a mission), push a layer onto them. Layers stack: each field comes from the highest-priority layer that sets it, and when yours comes off, whatever was under it shows again. Yours come off by themselves when your resource stops.

-- Server: 1am and clear skies inside the club, clock held still
exports.whip_core:SetPlayerWeatherLayer(source, 'nightclub', {
    hour = 1, minute = 0, weather = 'CLEAR', frozen = true, priority = 50,
})

-- Server: they leave; the world's sky (or the next layer down) comes back
exports.whip_core:ClearPlayerWeatherLayer(source, 'nightclub')

A client resource sets its own with SetWeatherLayer, and a zone with a weather field does it on enter and exit. The full rules are in Per-Player Weather: Layers.

In game: /whip → World → Time & WeatherServer owners

Open /whip → World → Time & Weather. Controls: set time (hour/minute), quick presets (Dawn/Noon/Sunset/Midnight), weather grid, freeze toggle, blackout toggle, and the time scale (a number from 0 to 10, then Set Scale). All changes apply instantly to the entire server.

Time & Weather

Server-authoritative time and weather control, with per-player layers. See the Time & Weather guide for architecture details.

GetTime()SERVER

Get current server time. Computed from the anchor at the moment you call it, so it is exact rather than as-of-the-last-tick.

Returns: number hour, number minute
local h, m = exports.whip_core:GetTime()
print(('Server time: %02d:%02d'):format(h, m))
GetWeather()SERVER

Get current server weather type.

Returns: string: weather type (uppercase)
SetTime(hour, minute)SERVER

Set the server time. Re-anchors the clock, broadcasts immediately to all clients, writes the whip_world row, and fires whip_core:time:changed { hour, minute }. Out-of-range values wrap, each on its own (25:61 is 01:01).

ParamTypeDescription
hournumber0–23
minutenumber?0–59, default 0
Returns: true, or false, reason for an hour or minute that is not a number
exports.whip_core:SetTime(22, 30) -- 10:30 PM
SetWeather(weather)SERVER

Set the server weather (any case). Validates against Config.WeatherTypes. Broadcasts immediately. Persists. Fires whip_core:weather:changed { weather }.

ParamTypeDescription
weatherstringWeather type: CLEAR, EXTRASUNNY, CLOUDS, OVERCAST, RAIN, CLEARING, THUNDER, SMOG, FOGGY, XMAS, SNOWLIGHT, BLIZZARD, HALLOWEEN, NEUTRAL
local ok, err = exports.whip_core:SetWeather('thunder')   -- any case
if not ok then print(err) end
Returns: true, or false, reason: 'Invalid weather type', or not a string
SetFrozen(frozen)SERVER

Freeze or unfreeze time progression. When frozen, the clock stops globally. Fires whip_core:time:freezeChanged { frozen }.

ParamTypeDescription
frozenbooleantrue = freeze, false = unfreeze
Returns: true
SetBlackout(blackout)SERVER

Toggle blackout mode (all artificial lights off).

ParamTypeDescription
blackoutbooleantrue = blackout on
Returns: true
IsBlackout()SERVER

Is the city blacked out right now?

Returns: boolean
SetTimeScale(scale)SERVER

Set time progression speed. 1.0 = normal GTA speed (48 min real = 24h game). 2.0 = twice as fast. 0.5 = half speed. Clamped to 0–10.

ParamTypeDescription
scalenumber0.0–10.0
Returns: true, or false, reason for a scale that is not a number
GetTimeScale()SERVER

Get the current time scale multiplier.

Returns: number
IsTimeFrozen()SERVER

Check if time is currently frozen.

Returns: boolean

Per-Player Weather: Layers

The server broadcasts one world time and one world weather. On top of that, any single client can stack named layers that change what that player personally sees (rain inside a zone, a frozen 6am behind the character screen, a storm during a mission) without touching anybody else.

Why layers rather than one override. The obvious design is a single "override" slot, and it cannot express the ordinary case. The character screen wants 6am and cloudy; a swamp zone wants fog; the player walks into the swamp. With one slot, whoever writes last wins and whoever clears first clears everything, so stepping out of the swamp would also cancel the character screen. Layers are named, so each source clears only its own and whatever was underneath comes back.

Resolution is per field. A layer sets only what it cares about. A zone declaring weather = 'FOGGY' says nothing about the time, so time keeps resolving from below it. Each of hour, minute, weather, frozen and blackout is decided independently: the highest-priority layer that mentions that field wins; if none do, the server's value is used. Ties break by name, so the same set of layers always resolves the same way.

FieldTypeMeaning
prioritynumberHigher wins. Default 0.
weatherstringAny name from Config.WeatherTypes
hour / minutenumberWhere the clock starts. It still runs unless frozen.
frozenbooleanHold the clock. false is meaningful: it un-freezes a lower layer.
blackoutbooleanKill the city lights for this player

On the client: no round trip

A layer only ever affects the machine it is set on, so there is nothing here to protect and no reason to ask the server. Set it where the trigger is.

-- Fog while inside a zone, cleared when they leave
exports.whip_core:SetWeatherLayer('zone:swamp', { weather = 'FOGGY', priority = 10 })
exports.whip_core:ClearWeatherLayer('zone:swamp')

-- A menu that wants its own light, held still
exports.whip_core:SetWeatherLayer('charselect', {
    weather = 'CLOUDS', hour = 6, minute = 0, frozen = true, priority = 1000,
})
Zones do this for you. Give a zone a weather field and it pushes and pops the layer on enter and exit automatically: a string for just the sky, or a table for the full shape: 
exports.whip_core:ZoneSphere({
    id = 'swamp', pos = vector3(0.0, 0.0, 0.0), radius = 120.0,
    weather = 'FOGGY',                                  -- or { weather = 'FOGGY', hour = 3 }
})
The layer is named after the zone and its priority defaults to just above the zone's own, so where zones overlap, the higher-priority zone's weather wins (as its speed limit does).

From the server

For things the server decides: an admin tool, a scripted scene, a job.

exports.whip_core:SetPlayerWeatherLayer(source, 'mission:heist', {
    weather = 'THUNDER', priority = 50,
})
exports.whip_core:ClearPlayerWeatherLayer(source, 'mission:heist')

When that storm ends, the swamp fog underneath it comes back, which is the whole point.

frozen = false means something. It is not the same as leaving the field out. Omitted, the field resolves from the layer below; set to false, this layer actively un-freezes a clock a lower layer froze. The same is true of blackout. Build layer tables with plain assignments: opts.frozen and x or nil reads false as absent and silently turns "not frozen" into "no opinion".
SetWeatherLayer(name, opts)CLIENT

Add or replace a named layer on this client. Passing nil for opts removes it. The layer is yours, as a server layer is: another resource cannot replace or clear it, and it comes off when your resource stops. The options are checked like the server's: numbers must be numbers, and weather must be one of Config.WeatherTypes.

ParamTypeDescription
namestringUnique per source, e.g. 'zone:swamp'
optstable|nil{ priority?, hour?, minute?, weather?, frozen?, blackout? }
Returns: true, or false, why ('Invalid weather type', 'layer "x" belongs to …')
ClearWeatherLayer(name)CLIENT

Remove one of your layers. Everything else this player is carrying stays.

Returns: true, or false, why (no such layer, or it is another resource's)
GetWeatherLayers()CLIENT

Every active layer in priority order, plus which one currently owns each field. For working out why a stack is not resolving the way you expected.

Returns: table: { layers = { {name, priority} }, owners = { weather = 'zone:swamp', hour = 'server', ... } }
SetPlayerWeatherLayer(source, name, opts)SERVER

Push a layer onto one player from the server. Same shape as the client export. The layer is yours: it comes off every player when your resource stops, and another running resource cannot replace or clear it. What it carries is checked (a weather that does not exist or an hour that is not a number is refused), and only priority, hour, minute, weather, frozen and blackout reach the player.

ParamTypeDescription
sourcenumberPlayer server ID
namestringUnique per source (at most 64 characters). On the player's side it is 'server:' .. name, so it never collides with a layer a client resource set under the same name.
optstable|nilnil clears
Returns: true, or false, reason
ClearPlayerWeatherLayer(source, name)SERVER

Remove one of your layers from one player. Returns true, or false, reason.

GetPlayerWeatherLayers(source)SERVER

What the SERVER pushed to this player. Not the whole picture: the client also holds layers it set for itself, such as the zone it is standing in. Ask the client export for the truth.

Returns: table: { [name] = opts }

Time & Weather (Client)

Client-side time/weather reads: what this player sees, every layer included.

GetCurrentTime()CLIENT

Get the current time as the local player sees it (respects overrides).

Returns: number hour, number minute
GetCurrentWeather()CLIENT

Get the current weather as the local player sees it (respects overrides).

Returns: string
IsTimeFrozen()CLIENT

Is the clock frozen for this player? Layers count: a layer with frozen = true freezes it here while the server's clock runs on.

Returns: boolean
IsTimeOverridden()CLIENT

Is any time/weather layer active for this player: a zone's weather, a resource's SetWeatherLayer, a server's SetPlayerWeatherLayer? GetWeatherLayers says which.

Returns: boolean

NPCs

The NPC Creator: NPCs the server makes and looks after. whip keeps each one doing what you set (its behaviour, its conditions, who it fights), so it never wanders off on its own. Yours go when your resource stops, and with the rest of a run by ReleaseTag.

SpawnNpc(def, opts)SERVER

Make an NPC. It exists at once; the first nearby player's game takes it over within about half a second and applies its brain.

local npcId, netId = exports.whip_core:SpawnNpc({
    model = 's_m_y_dealer_01',
    coords = vector4(x, y, z, heading),
    behaviour = 'guard',
    weapon = 'WEAPON_PISTOL',
}, { tag = 'run:42', hostileTo = { people = { source } } })
FieldTypeDescription
modelstringA ped model name
coordsvector3|vector4|tableWhere; a vector4's w (or heading) faces it
behaviour'stand'|'guard'?stand (default) stays put; guard wanders near its spot. After a fight, either walks back to its spot
conditionstable?{ invincible, canMove, reacts, flees }, each true or false (defaults: false, true, false, false). flees (run away instead of fighting) needs reacts = true: an NPC that reacts to nothing never runs
weaponstring|table?A weapon name (GTA's, or an add-on weapon a resource streams), or { name, ammo }
armournumber?0–100
looktable?A look from the character editor (a character's appearance: face, hair, make-up, tattoos, clothes), checked by the same rules as a character's save, 10,000 bytes of JSON at most. Its ped is the look's freemode model, whatever model says, and every player near it sees the whole look
interiorboolean?It stands inside an MLO: each owning game keeps it frozen until it has the interior, so it never falls through a house that has not loaded
opts.tagstring?Your run tag (see ReleaseTag)
opts.hostileTotable?{ people = { serverId | { charId = n } } }: it fights the nearest of them who is online and not down, and picks again as they come and go. { except = { ... } }: everyone but those (whoever is not on a job's crew), only with opts.range: it never goes for the whole server
opts.fightBackboolean?Fights whoever attacks it (default true), until they go down or a minute after their last hit
opts.corpseMsnumber?How long a body stays (default 60000; 0 = until you remove it)
opts.rangenumber?A guard: 1–500 metres. It fights its hostileTo only within this distance of its spot, chases someone who shot it up to three times as far, and walks back when nobody is left in reach. Leave it out to fight them wherever they are
opts.groupstring?A name (128 characters): hurt one, and every NPC of yours in the same group fights the attacker too (one shot dead included)
Returns: npcId, netId: or false, reason
DespawnNpc(npcId)SERVER

Remove one of your NPCs. Its owner's game deletes the ped (a server delete out from under that game can be sent back).

Returns: true: or false, reason
SetNpcState(npcId, patch)SERVER

Change what one of your NPCs does: { behaviour, hostileTo = audience | false, fightBack, conditions, range = metres | false, post, interior, pace, follow, flee, anim, attack }. hostileTo = false calms it and forgets who attacked it; range = false lets it fight them wherever they are again. All of it is the NPC's brain, so whichever player's game runs it next carries on.

patchTypeDescription
attacktable | false?A thing it attacks while it has nobody to fight: { net = a car's netId } or { at = coords } (a prop, which each game has its own copy of). It shoots at it with its weapon, or walks up to it with none; a car burnt out is left. false: none
postcoords?A new spot: it walks there (or runs: pace) and stands or guards there from then on. With interior = true the spot is inside an MLO, and the NPC waits for it as one spawned there does (only while it is at its post)
gateAtcoords?Where that MLO is looked for, when not the post itself: the spot a group gathers round (a ring spot just outside the MLO's bounds would never find it). SpawnNpc's def.gateAt is the same
pacestring?'walk' (default) or 'run': going to its post, and following
followserverId | falseIt walks after that player (an escort). While they are gone or down it waits where it is; false stops it (set post to where it is, or it walks back)
fleeserverId | falseIt runs from that player and fights nobody meanwhile
animtable | false{ dict, clip } or { scenario }: played over and over where it stands, instead of standing still
-- The alarm went off: the guard turns on whoever tripped it
exports.whip_core:SetNpcState(npcId, { hostileTo = { people = { source } } })

-- The hostage follows their rescuer out, at a run
exports.whip_core:SetNpcState(hostageId, { follow = source, pace = 'run' })
Returns: true: or false, reason
GetNpc(npcId) · ListNpcs({ tag }) · GetNpcBy(kind, value)SERVER

GetNpc: a copy, { npcId, owner, tag, model, netId, alive, health, armour, behaviour, conditions, targets, focus, range, group, killer, killedAt, weapon, coords, post, pace, follow, flee, interior }, or nil (coords where it is now, post where it belongs; interior: its post is inside an MLO). killer is the server's own reading (a car's driver for a run-over), so check a kill against it. ListNpcs: your NPCs, or those under one of your tags. GetNpcBy('netId' | 'entity', value): the npcId, or nil.

Events: whip_core:npc:spawned, :despawned { reason }, :damaged { amount, attacker }, :killed { killer, weapon, coords }. Any server resource can fire an event: before paying out on one, ask GetNpc.
-- A bounty on your own NPCs, paid to whoever the server saw kill one
local paid = {}
AddEventHandler('whip_core:npc:killed', function(e)
    local npc = exports.whip_core:GetNpc(e.npcId)   -- the server's reading, not the event's
    if not npc or npc.owner ~= GetCurrentResourceName() or paid[npc.npcId] then return end
    if not npc.alive and npc.killer then
        paid[npc.npcId] = true
        exports.whip_core:PayPlayer(npc.killer, 500, { reason = 'Bounty' })
    end
end)

Interactions (E-key)

Overview

The 3D Interaction system shows contextual E-key prompts in the game world: circle indicators when far, "[E] Action" boxes when close. Used for ground item pickup, container access, door interaction, and custom interactions.

How It Works

  • Visible range: the circle appears within Config.InteractVisibleRange (5 m)
  • Active range: the E prompt works within Config.InteractActiveRange (2 m)
  • Which one: of the prompts in reach, the one nearest the centre of your view, inside Config.InteractFocusCone (40°)
  • Hidden: while a screen or bar has the input (inventory, shop, throw mode), and while the player is dead or in a vehicle, unless the action's require says alive = false or vehicle = 'in'

Add an Interaction

-- Client, in Whip.register: a press-E prompt at a spot
-- (see AddAction for the F1 wheel and car parts)
Whip.register(function()
    exports.whip_core:AddAction({
        id          = 'stash',
        at          = { coords = vector3(200.0, -800.0, 30.0) },
        label       = 'Open Stash',
        reach       = 3.0,
        group       = 'my_resource',
        canInteract = function(ctx) return not someCondition end,
        onSelect    = function(ctx)
            -- Player pressed E. Its own thread: waiting here is fine.
            print('Interaction triggered!')
        end,
    })
end)

-- Change it (label, position, switched off...)
exports.whip_core:UpdateAction('stash', { label = 'Locked Stash' })

-- Remove it, or every one in a group. (When your resource stops they go by themselves.)
exports.whip_core:RemoveAction('stash')
exports.whip_core:RemoveActionGroup('my_resource')

Full reference: AddAction.

Built-in Interactions

Ground items, containers, and doors auto-register interactions: you don't need to create them manually for framework systems.

Interactions: AddAction (Client)

One declaration for everything a player can do in the world: a prompt at a spot, a prompt riding on an entity, a choice on a car part, or an entry on the F1 wheel. at says where it lives; every other field reads the same wherever that is. It is yours by id, adding the same id again replaces it, and it goes when your resource stops.

AddAction(def)CLIENT

Put an action in the world. Adding the same id again replaces it in place, and it goes when your resource stops: there is nothing to clean up.

Whip.register(function()
    exports.whip_core:AddAction({
        id       = 'bench',
        at       = { coords = vector3(12.1, -1105.3, 29.8), heading = 90.0 },
        label    = 'Weapon Bench',
        icon     = 'store',
        require  = { job = 'gunsmith', item = 'toolkit' },
        onSelect = function(ctx)
            TriggerServerEvent('mygunsmith:openBench')
        end,
    })
end)
FieldTypeDescription
idstring?Yours: another resource's 'bench' is a different action. The same id again replaces it. Left out, one is made from the rest, the same every time
attableRequired. Where it lives; see at
labelstring | function(ctx)What it says. A function is asked every time it is drawn, so it must not wait. The F1 wheel needs one
iconstring?A glyph name; any other text is drawn as it is. On the F1 wheel the icon fills the slab and the centre disc. With no icon, or text longer than 3 letters, the wheel draws the label's first letter
imagestring | function(ctx)?World prompts only: a picture above the label, a path under whip_core's html/: a vehicle's is 'img/vehicles/<model>.webp' (found in the media pack that holds it, where vehicle and furniture pictures live), or a full https://cfx-nui-<resource>/… URL
descriptionstring | function(ctx)?F1 wheel only: what it does, shown beside the name in the pill under the wheel while the player aims at it: 'Start or stop the engine'. A function is asked when the wheel opens, so it must not wait
requiretable?Who may use it; see require
canInteractfunction(ctx)?Your own rule on top of require: return true to offer it. Asked often, so it must not wait
onSelectfunction(ctx)Required: here, or on the options (an option takes the one above it, then the action's). An option with none anywhere does nothing when pressed, and F8 says so. Runs in its own thread, so it may wait: a progress bar, a server callback
optionstable?Several choices on one action; see options
reachnumber?How close you must be to use it, in metres. Default: Config.InteractActiveRange (2 m) for a prompt. Set it to the distance your server check allows, or players see an option the server then refuses as too far
seeFromnumber?World prompts: how far away it appears. Default Config.InteractVisibleRange. Prompts are found through a grid sized by that config value, so a bigger seeFrom is clamped (and F8 says so). Raise the config if you truly need further
scalenumber?World prompts: bigger or smaller than every other prompt: 1.5 is half as big again, 0.75 a quarter smaller. From 0.25 to 4. Every prompt in the game is Config.Interact3D; this is for one family of them
sizeRangenumber?World prompts: the distance its size is designed at. whip draws every prompt the same size on screen at the moment it becomes usable, which is its reach, so a prompt you change the reach of later grows or shrinks with it. Give the first reach here and it keeps its size. Default: its reach
focusMode'aim' | 'near'World prompts: which one E acts on when several are in reach. 'aim' (the default): the one you are looking at, right for loose things side by side. 'near': the closest, in a much wider cone, right for a door or a counter you walk up to
onBlurfunction?World prompts: called when it stops being the one E acts on: you looked away, walked off, or another took over. For a prompt that opens out into a menu and should fold back up
stylestring | table?World prompts: how it looks and moves: a style's name ('subtle') or a table of its own ({ tint = '#ffc850', badgeScale = 1.2 }). See Styles. Change it later with SetActionStyle
holdMsnumber?World prompts: hold E (A on a pad) this many milliseconds to use it, instead of a press. Letting go early, looking away or scrolling to another option cancels it and nothing happens. For the things a player should not do by accident: 1500 to plant a charge. An option can have its own (0 is a press). The hold happens on the player's game: your server still checks the press as any other
pressboolean | vector3 | table?World prompts and car parts: used with the hand. onSelect runs at once as always, and the player's hand goes out from where they stand towards the point and straight back: only how it looks, it never moves them or takes control. true: towards the prompt's own point; a point; or { coords | offset (in the entity's frame), normal (the way the surface faces) }. An option can have its own (false for an option that plays its own animation). Not read on the F1 wheel. No press clips installed, too far or seated: just the press of E. See PlayPress
firstboolean?With at = { vehiclePart }: at the top of the part's stack, above its own options (Open Door, Lock), so E does it, while its canInteract says yes. For what the player walked to the car to do: whip_fuel's Insert Nozzle with a pump's nozzle in hand. An option can have its own. Left out, a resource's options go after the part's own
onGonefunction(ctx)?With at = { entity }: called when the entity has gone and the action has been removed with it: ctx.id, ctx.owner. Add it again from here if the thing comes back. (By netId there is nothing to do: it waits for the entity)
onFound, onLostfunction(ctx)?With at = { model }: told as each prop of the model comes within 50 m of the player and as it goes (past 60 m, or gone from this game), on foot or in a car, once a prop: ctx = { id, owner, entity, model, prop, coords }. Every prop in that range, not only the one whose prompt is up (a prompt is offered on the nearest of each model, and none from a car). For what you put on or beside such props yourself: whip_fuel's nozzles in the holsters of every pump in sight. Each runs in its own thread. In onLost, read ctx.coords (where it was found): the entity may be gone
groupstring?A name for RemoveActionGroup
enabledboolean?false hides it without removing it
Returns: id, false, or false, reason: no at, an at that names nothing (an unknown car part, an entity that is gone), no onSelect, a wheel entry with no label, or a require word that is not one. An action that could not be put in the world is not kept: an id means it is there. Either way there is a third answer, warnings: a list of what was wrong but not refused (below), or nil (the false before it, on success, is so it gets through the export). AddPoint answers the same way.
A misspelt field is warned about, not refused. A field AddAction does not have (lable, or another framework's canUse), a value of the wrong kind (scale = 'big') or a number outside its range is said in F8 with what it most likely meant: lable is not a field — use 'label', and is left out, or held to its range. The action still goes in. A field only one place reads is said too: scale on the F1 wheel does nothing. The same list comes back as the third answer: local id, why, warnings = exports.whip_core:AddAction({ … }). Only require is strict: an unknown word there refuses the action, because it would otherwise require nothing. One foreign word is taken as it is: ox_target's and qb-target's distance is read as reach (and said once in F8).
A function you hand over is not type() == 'function' on the other side. It crosses the export as a reference: calling it works, testing it does not. whip calls your label, canInteract and onSelect; never write code that checks whether they are functions.

The examples below leave out the Whip.register(function() … end) around each AddAction to stay short. Your code keeps it, so the action comes back when whip_core restarts.

at: where it lives

atWhat it is
{ coords = vector3, heading? }A prompt at a point. With heading it stands like a sign facing that way (and is not drawn from behind); without, it turns to face you. follow = function() return x, y, z, heading end moves it with something
{ entity = handle, offset? = vector3, bone? }A prompt riding on an entity: a prop you spawned, a local NPC. It follows it, and is removed (not hidden) a few seconds after the entity is gone. Give the action an onGone = function(ctx) … end to be told when (and add it again from there); without one the console says so. For anything networked, use netId below
{ netId = n, offset? = vector3, bone? }The same, by network id, for a networked NPC or car. While the entity is not streamed in to this player the prompt is simply off their screen; when it streams back in, whatever handle it has now, the prompt is back on it. Nothing to add again. ctx.entity is its handle on this game. The id can come from the server (NetworkGetNetworkIdFromEntity), and need not be streamed in yet when the action is added
{ model = 'prop_vend_soda_01', offset? = vector3, heading?, faces?, perModel? }A prompt on every prop of that model near the player (vending machines, benches, payphones), found the way whip finds its own cash machines and petrol pumps. model may be a list. offset is in the prop's own space: x across it, y out of its face, z up. Without heading the circle turns to face the player; with one it stands like a sign at that turn from the prop's own facing (find it by eye: try 0, 90, 180). faces = 2 for a prop used from both sides. perModel = { ['prop_x'] = { offset = vector3, heading = 90.0 } } places it on one model differently (a pump whose panel is somewhere else); what an entry leaves out is the action's own offset or heading. ctx.entity is the prop pressed, and every option's ctx has ctx.model, ctx.face (1, or 2 on a two-sided prop) and ctx.prop (the prop's id). onFound / onLost above hear every one in sight.
{ vehiclePart = 'hood' }A choice on a car part's prompt: 'hood', 'trunk', 'door_dside_f', 'door_pside_f', 'door_dside_r', 'door_pside_r', and 'bike', 'bicycle', 'boat', the one prompt each of those has (Get On / Board). Engine work goes on 'hood', which only shows while the bonnet is open. ctx.entity is the vehicle
{ radial = true }An entry on the F1 wheel: a slab with its icon and label. Aimed at, the pill under the wheel shows the label and description. Players aim with the mouse or either stick, then click or press A. Entries are sorted by label
{ aimBox = 'vehicle' | 'object' | 'ped' | 'world' }A prompt where the player looks on whatever car, prop or person (or a list of those kinds) they aim at: exactly where the look meets its bounding box: flat on that side like a sign, wrapped round the corner when it runs past one, or just over the top. Where the box is far bigger than the body (a helicopter's rotor span, a plane's wings) it is on the body itself, where the look meets it. It goes where the look goes, and is offered only while the look meets one within reach (a wall in front hides what is behind it). ctx.entity is the thing, ctx.coords the point on its box: GetOffsetFromEntityGivenWorldCoords(ctx.entity, ctx.coords) gives it in the thing's own space (whip_rope ties a rope there). 'world' is the map itself (its ground, walls and rock: anything that is not a car, a prop or a person), where the look meets it: flat on a wall, or just over the ground. There ctx.entity is nil, ctx.world is true and ctx.normal is the way the surface faces (a car or prop still in front of the map wins). Add it while it means something (a rope in hand) and remove it after: while it exists a ray is cast every frame

require: who may use it

Every key you give must pass. Checked on the player's client to decide what to show; if the thing matters, your server event checks again. The client only decides what is offered.

KeyExamplePasses when
alivealive = falseBy default nobody downed is offered anything; false offers it to the downed too (a prompt and the wheel both keep it on offer while downed)
vehiclevehicle = 'out''in': in a vehicle. 'out': on foot. A world prompt is on foot unless it says 'in'; the wheel is offered either way
jobjob = 'police' or { 'police', 'ems' }They have a role at one of these jobs (a key or a jobId)
onDutyonDuty = true…and are on duty there. With no job: on duty anywhere
jobPermissionjobPermission = 'canManage'…and their role there has this permission. With no job: a role at any job that has it
itemitem = 'toolkit', { item = 'lockpick', count = 2 }, { 'toolkit', 'gloves' }They carry all of them
heldheld = 'jerry_can' or { 'jerry_can', 'weapon_pistol' }The item in their hand is one of these (SetHeldItem, said by the resource that draws it: whip_gunny does for every weapon, the jerry can among them)
zonezone = 'mrpd' or a listThey are standing in one of these zones
charIdcharId = 12 or a listThey are one of these characters
aceace = 'whip.devtools'They hold this ACE (asked of the server once, then remembered)
A require is free; a canInteract is not. whip asks canInteract on every prompt pass, at everything in reach, and each ask crosses into your resource: memory made every time, even for a no. Near a car that is about 95 asks a second for each option on it. So say what you can with require (whip checks it first, and skips your canInteract when it fails), and for a state only your resource knows (a nozzle in the hand, a rope end held), add the action while it holds and remove it after: whip_fuel's car offers (whip_fuel/client/car.lua) and whip_rope's tie prompt do.
Only the listed keys are accepted. Any other key (a door's jobs or items, say) refuses the whole action when it is added, with the word it wanted, rather than quietly requiring nothing. A vehiclePart action is always used on foot and alive, so it refuses alive = false and vehicle = 'in'.

ctx: what your functions get

label, canInteract and onSelect are all handed one table. The verbs (ctx.flash, ctx.status, ctx.refuse and the input three) are in onSelect's only, since label and canInteract are asked every frame.

FieldDescription
ctx.id, ctx.ownerYour action's id, and your resource
ctx.optionWhich option this is (see options)
ctx.underonSelect, an option in a menu: the id of the menu option it was chosen in ('repair' for Repair › Engine); nil at the top
ctx.model, ctx.face, ctx.propat = { model } only: the prop's model name, which of its faces (1, or 2 on a two-sided prop), and its id (the same prop's every time)
ctx.entity, ctx.coordsWhat and where: the entity aimed at, the car of a part, the entity a prompt rides on; where the prompt was
ctx.playerA prompt on a person (aimBox = 'ped', entity, netId) that is a real player: { serverId, playerIdx, activeJob, isDead }; nil for an NPC or anything else. Their name is GetPlayerFullName(ctx.player.serverId); their statebags Player(ctx.player.serverId).state.isPolice
ctx.flash(r, g, b)onSelect only. Tint the prompt for a moment (world prompts)
ctx.status(text, ms)onSelect only. Say something on the prompt (world prompts; a notification elsewhere)
ctx.refuse(why)onSelect only. Amber flash and the reason (world prompts; an error notification elsewhere)
ctx.beginInput(opts), ctx.cancelInput(), ctx.inputText()onSelect only. Type a number into the prompt: see typing a number
ctx.typedWhat has been typed so far with a blinking caret, or false, for a label to show. A value, not a function
-- Look at a person: "Frisk", for on-duty police, on a living player (not an NPC)
exports.whip_core:AddAction({
    id          = 'frisk',
    at          = { aimBox = 'ped' },
    label       = 'Frisk',
    reach       = 2.0,
    require     = { job = 'police', onDuty = true },
    canInteract = function(ctx) return ctx.player ~= nil and not ctx.player.isDead end,
    onSelect    = function(ctx) TriggerServerEvent('police:frisk', ctx.player.serverId) end,
})

An aimBox prompt casts a ray every frame while it exists. For an action only some players use (police, here), add it when they go on duty and remove it when they go off (RemoveAction('frisk')), rather than for everyone all the time.

options: several choices on one action

Each option takes its own id, label, icon, image, description, require, canInteract and onSelect. For label, icon, image, description and onSelect an option falls back to the action's when it leaves one out. require and canInteract are added, not replaced: an option is offered only when the action's rules AND its own pass, so an option can narrow who sees it, never widen it. (An option with require = { job = 'ems' } under an action with require = { job = 'police' } is seen by nobody.) Downed is the one exception, settled once per option: the option's own alive if it names one, else the action's. So alive = false on the action covers every option (including one whose require asks for an item), and one option can be for the downed on its own with alive = false. On a world prompt the options are one stack the player scrolls; on the wheel, one entry each.

exports.whip_core:AddAction({
    id      = 'counter',
    at      = { coords = vector3(25.7, -1346.7, 29.5) },
    icon    = 'store',
    options = {
        { id = 'buy',   label = 'Buy',   onSelect = function() TriggerServerEvent('shop:buy') end },
        { id = 'stock', label = 'Restock', require = { job = 'shopkeep', onDuty = true },
          onSelect = function() TriggerServerEvent('shop:restock') end },
    },
})

Menus: an option with options of its own (world prompts)

On a world prompt (coords, entity, netId, model, aimBox) an option may carry options of its own. Its label gets a ›; choosing it puts its options on the same prompt, with a Back first. Pressing one of them, or looking away, folds the prompt back to the top. Any number of levels down. An option down there must also pass every option it is under (their require and canInteract are added), and takes from them whatever it leaves out (icon, onSelect…), then from the action. Its onSelect gets ctx.under, the menu it was chosen in. Ids need only differ within one menu. On a car part or the wheel there are no menus: an option's options there are warned about and left out.

options = {
    { id = 'repair', label = 'Repair', options = {
        { id = 'engine', label = 'Engine', onSelect = function(ctx) TriggerServerEvent('mech:fix', 'engine') end },
        { id = 'body',   label = 'Body',   onSelect = function(ctx) TriggerServerEvent('mech:fix', 'body') end },
    } },
    { id = 'wash', label = 'Wash', onSelect = function() TriggerServerEvent('mech:wash') end },
}
UpdateAction(id, patch)CLIENT

Change some of one of your actions' fields. patch is laid over what it has; an at in it replaces the old one whole.

exports.whip_core:UpdateAction('bench', { label = 'Bench (closed)', enabled = false })
Returns: true, false, warnings, or false, reason, warnings, and a refused change leaves the action exactly as it was. The second answer is false rather than nothing on success, so the third (warnings, as AddAction's) reaches you through the export
SetActionStyle(id, style)CLIENT

Change how one of your actions' world prompts looks, now. It changes in place: the prompt does not fade out and back in, and a stack of options keeps its place, so a prompt can turn red as its timer runs out while you look at it. style is a style's name, a table, or nil for the default (see Styles). UpdateAction(id, { style = … }) with nothing else in the patch does the same.

exports.whip_core:SetActionStyle('vault', { tint = '#ff5a5a', flash = 'fade' })
Returns: true, false, warnings, or false, reason (not an action of yours). The third answer is warnings, as AddAction's: a misspelt field, or a style on something that is not a world prompt (the false before it is so it gets through the export)
RemoveAction(id)CLIENT

Take one of your actions out. Only your own: another resource's id is refused. You do not need this when your resource stops.

Returns: true, or false, reason
RemoveActionGroup(group)CLIENT

Take out every one of your actions with this group. Another resource's group of the same name is untouched.

Returns: true, count, or false, reason
GetAction(id)CLIENT

One of your actions as plain data, and whether each option would be offered to this player right now, and if not, why. The first thing to reach for when "my action never shows".

-- "My bench never shows": ask why
local a = exports.whip_core:GetAction('bench')
for _, opt in ipairs(a and a.options or {}) do
    print(opt.id, opt.offered, opt.why)
end
Returns: table|nil: { id, owner, key, group, reach, seeFrom, enabled, at, label, icon, mounted, engineIds, options = { { id, label, offered, why } } }. mounted is where it lives ('prompt', 'aimbox' for at = { aimBox }, 'props' for at = { model }, 'radial', 'part'), or false if it could not be put there (the F8 console says why)
PlayPress(target, opts)CLIENT

The player's hand goes out towards a point, from where they stand, and comes straight back as it gets there: only how it looks. It answers at once (the press plays in its own thread), so do the thing itself before or right after the call, never waiting on it; it is safe inside any callback. It never walks, turns or moves the player and never takes control; every press is a standing one. With opts.normal (the way the surface faces) the hand comes back where it meets that surface, the prompt's own; it does not test for anything else in the way, so pass a normal for anything on a wall, a door or a panel. For a prompt, AddAction's press does this for you.

ringTheBell()
exports.whip_core:PlayPress(vector3(x, y, z), { normal = vector3(0, -1, 0) })
ParamTypeDescription
targetvector3 | tableA point, or { entity, offset?, bone? } (offset in the entity's frame)
opts.normalvector3?The way the surface faces (either way round): a press pushing into it is preferred, and the hand comes back where it meets it
opts.onContactfunction?Run exactly once for a press that went out: as the hand gets there, or, if the press is cut short on the way (a ragdoll, a car, an emote, its animation slow to load), as it ends. Never when the answer is false

Server owners: Config.InteractPress (enabled is also Hand press in /whip → Settings → Config →World & gameplay): enabled, maxDistance (2.5 m) and followHand (the hand keeps reaching while the player moves). Picking things up off the ground is not a press: it plays GTA's own grab whatever these say.

Returns: true (a press is going out), or false, why: 'off' (no press: switched off or not installed, too far, seated, falling, swimming, aiming, already against the surface, or no animation reaches that way), 'busy' (one is going out), 'dead'

Something in their hand: held props

A flashlight, a clipboard, a sign, a pump's nozzle: put it in the player's hand from your server with HoldProps, never with your own CreateObject and AttachEntityToEntity on the client. whip_core makes the prop on the server and the player's own game ties it to the hand, so everyone sees it where the hand is. It shares the hand with whip's own (an emote's cup, a progress bar's tool, an item being handed over): the hand holds one set, and a new one replaces the old. Yours are kept under '<resource>:<tag>', so nobody else can drop them, and they go when your resource stops.
