When yours leave the hand without you asking, whip_core:heldProps:lost says why (Server Events). whip_fuel's nozzle is the worked example.

HoldProps(source, props, tag)SERVER

Put props in a player's hand, for everyone, replacing whatever the hand held. At most one new set a second for a player: a faster ask waits, and only the newest is made.

exports.whip_core:HoldProps(source, { { model = 'prop_cs_police_torch', offset = { 0.1, 0.0, 0.0 } } }, 'torch')
ParamTypeDescription
sourcenumberThe player
propstable[]One or two: { model, bone?, offset? = { x, y, z }, rot? = { x, y, z } }. bone defaults to the left hand (18905), as whip's own
tagstring?Your name for the set (default 'held'), kept as '<resource>:<tag>': what DropHeldProps names

Your offset and rotation are a start. An admin holding your prop can set where it sits by eye (/w → Edit Held Prop), and from then on that place is used for the first prop of every set with your tag, in place of yours; the bone stays yours. Keep the tag the same for the same prop, so the place they set stays with it.

Returns: true, or false, why
DropHeldProps(source, tag)SERVER

Take your props of tag out of the player's hand; with no tag, whatever of yours they hold. Never anybody else's: an emote that replaced yours stays.

Returns: true when anything went, or false, why when they held none of yours
GetHeldPropsTag(source)SERVER

What the player's hands hold, or are about to: a resource's '<resource>:<tag>', whip's own 'emote', 'bar', 'give' or 'take', or nil.

Returns: string|nil
GetOwnHeldProp(model, tag) · DropOwnHeldProp(model, tag) · SetOwnHeldPropPose(model, tag, pose)CLIENT

Your own held prop (your tag, its model), in this player's hand on their own game. GetOwnHeldProp answers its entity, to read how it is turned. DropOwnHeldProp lets go of it here at once, rather than a round trip later; still tell your server, whose DropHeldProps forgets the set. SetOwnHeldPropPose sits it another way in the hand for a while (a different grip): pose = { bone?, offset = { x, y, z }, rot = { x, y, z } }, or nil for where the server put it. Only while this game holds it.

Returns: GetOwnHeldProp: entity|nil; the other two: boolean (whether it was done)
AimDot(on)CLIENT

whip draws its aim dot for any weapon in the hand by itself (Config.AimDot). This is for something you aim that is not a weapon in the hand: true while it is aimed, false after, and the dot shows in the middle of the screen meanwhile. Taken down if your resource stops while aiming.

Returns: nothing

Typing a number into a prompt

A world prompt can become a numeric field: digits go into it instead of into the game, and E submits. Start it from onSelect with ctx.beginInput; show what is typed from your label with ctx.typed.

exports.whip_core:AddAction({
    id       = 'deposit',
    at       = { coords = vector3(150.2, -1040.1, 29.4) },
    icon     = 'deposit',
    label    = function(ctx)
        return ctx.typed and ('Deposit  $' .. ctx.typed) or 'Deposit'
    end,
    onSelect = function(ctx)
        ctx.beginInput({
            max      = 6,
            onSubmit = function(text) TriggerServerEvent('bank:deposit', tonumber(text)) end,
            onCancel = function() end,
        })
    end,
})
optsTypeDescription
maxnumber?Most digits. Default 9
onSubmitfunction(text)On E. text is a string
onCancelfunction?If they back out, or another input replaces this one

Styles: how a prompt looks and moves

A style is a set of looks a world prompt wears: its size, colour, how see-through it is in each state, and how fast it moves. Give an action one by name, or as a table of its own. Every field is optional; what a style leaves out comes from its base, and in the end from 'default', which is Config.Interact3D.

-- by name: one of the server's styles (Config.Interact3D.styles)
exports.whip_core:AddAction({ id = 'bin', at = { coords = spot }, label = 'Search', style = 'subtle', onSelect = search })

-- your own: a bigger amber circle that starts from 'subtle'
exports.whip_core:AddAction({
    id = 'vault', at = { coords = door }, label = 'Crack the vault', icon = 'lockpick',
    style = { base = 'subtle', badgeScale = 1.3, tint = '#ffc850', fadeMs = 250 },
    onSelect = crack,
})
FieldTypeDescription
basestring?Start from this named style
badgeScalenumber?The circle's size: 1.2 is a fifth bigger. 0.25 to 4. On top of the action's scale, which sizes circle and label together
labelScalenumber?The label's size, the same way
opacitytable?{ seen = 0.35, inReach = 0.85, focused = 1.0 }: how visible it is in sight but too far to use, close enough to use, and as the one E acts on. 0 is invisible, 1 solid. seen = 0 hides it until you are close enough
tintcolour?The circle's colour: '#ffc850', or { 255, 200, 80 }. The art is white, so white is no change; the glyph inside stays dark and readable
labelTintcolour?The label's colour, the same way
fadeMsnumber?How long fading in, out and between states takes, in milliseconds. Default Config.Interact3D.fadeMs (100)
crossfadeMsnumber?How long the ring takes to turn into the key when it becomes the one E acts on
slideMsnumber?How long a stack of options takes to slide when you scroll
flash'blink' | 'fade'An answer flash (ctx.flash, a door's green): 'blink' blinks twice (the default), 'fade' shows once and fades. It fades back to the style's own tint
flashMsnumber?How long that flash lasts. Default Config.Interact3D.flashMs
gap, stackGap, stackAlpha, previewScalenumber?Circle to label gap, the gap between stacked options, how visible an unselected option is, and the picture's size: Config.Interact3D's, for this style only
cullBehindboolean?false: a prompt that stands like a sign is drawn from behind as well
easingstring?How every movement eases: 'smooth' glides to a stop (the default), 'linear' keeps one speed, 'out' starts fast and settles, 'inOut' starts and ends slow, 'back' goes a little past and settles back. fadeEasing, crossfadeEasing and slideEasing set one movement each
appearstring?How it arrives: 'fade' (the default), 'pop' grows in, 'slide' rises into place, 'none' is there at once. appearMs is how long it takes (220)
focusstring?When it becomes the one E acts on: 'none' (the default), 'pop' a quick bump, 'pulse' breathes while it stays focused
idlestring?While it is not: 'none' (the default), 'pulse' breathes, 'bob' floats up and down
pressstring?When it is used: 'none' (the default) or 'pop'
labelWeightnumber?How heavy the label's letters are, 400 (regular) to 800 (extra bold). Default 700
labelOutline, labelOutlineColournumber?, colour?The dark edge round the label's letters that keeps them readable on any background: its width (0 to 8; default 3) and colour (default black)
labelCasestring?'upper' sets the label in capitals, a little spaced; 'none' (the default) as written
labelShadowboolean?false takes away the soft shadow under the label
themestring?The prompt's look: 'keycap' (a rounded square, a key to press), 'classic' (the round white disc), 'glass' (dark and see-through, the key in white), 'rim' (a black disc in a white rim, like the HUD's black skin), 'dot' (a dot far off, a ring in reach, the key when it is the one). Left out, a prompt wears the player's own shape: square by default (Config.Interact3D.theme), and each player can pick Square or Circle in the pause menu, Server Settings → Map & HUD → Prompt shape. Name a theme only when a prompt should look that way whatever the player picked
darkboolean?Black and white swapped, on the square and the circle: a black key with a white outline and a white symbol, and black words with a white outline. Left out, the player's own choice: off by default (Config.Interact3D.dark), and each player can switch it in the pause menu, Server Settings → Map & HUD → Dark prompts. The other themes keep their own colours

Named styles live in Config.Interact3D.styles; whip ships subtle (smaller, and nothing until you are close enough to use it) and lively (grows in, pops when it is focused and when it is used). A server owner adds their own there, and a field set under styles.default changes every prompt that does not say otherwise. Families of whip's own prompts wear one through Config.Interact3D.groupStyles, by group: doors, vehicles, ground_items, garages, containers, properties, conversation, atm, and actions for every AddAction and AddPoint prompt (whip_fuel's pumps among them). A prompt's own style wins over its group's.

A misspelt style is warned about, like any field. style = 'subtel' says there is no style 'subtel' — use 'subtle' in F8 and the prompt wears the default; { tnt = '#fff' } says to use tint. Styles are for world prompts: on the F1 wheel or a car part they do nothing, and F8 says so.

Glyphs

The names a prompt draws as a picture: lock unlock lockpick door hood_closed hood_open trunk_closed trunk_open trunk_lid garage car store turbo furnish house pickup bank deposit withdraw back fuel nozzle cash talk phone bag emote id power headlights seat devtools place give eat respawn objective target pin star timer, and mfr_<brand> for a car maker's badge. Anything else is drawn as the text itself ('$'), smaller the longer it is. 'E', the default, means "the interact key" and is drawn as the key the player's Interact binding is on (F if they moved it) and as A on a pad.

Points from the server: AddPoint

A point your server code adds while it runs: a Talk prompt on an NPC, a "hand in the package" spot, a job board. It is drawn and pressed like any other prompt, but it belongs to your resource (gone when it stops, removed by ReleaseTag with the rest of a run), it is shown to everyone or only the players you name, and pressing E runs your onUse on the server, after whip has checked the distance, the audience and the requirements. Not saved: add it again when your resource starts. A client-side prompt for one player is AddAction.

AddPoint(def)SERVER

Add a prompt from the server, for everyone or only the players you name in audience; pressing it runs onUse on the server.

local pointId = exports.whip_core:AddPoint({
    at       = { netId = npcNetId, offset = vector3(0.0, 0.0, 0.3) },
    label    = 'Talk',
    options  = { { id = 'work', label = 'Got work?' }, { id = 'bye', label = 'Leave' } },
    audience = { people = { source } },
    tag      = 'run:42',
    onUse    = function(source, use)
        if use.option == 'work' then StartJob(source) end
    end,
})
FieldTypeDescription
attableOne place:
{ coords = vector3, heading? } a spot (a heading makes it stand like a sign)
{ netId, offset?, bone? } rides that entity, shown while each player's game has it
{ vehicle = id | { plate = 'ABC123' }, offset?, bone? } rides a whip car wherever it is out (nothing while it is in a garage)
{ ground = groundItemId, offset? } over a ground pile (gone once it is picked up)
{ container = containerId, offset? } over a container
On a car, a pile or a container it sits a little above them unless offset says where: their own prompts are on them
label, iconstring?Its text and glyph
optionstable?Up to 6 { id, label?, icon?, require?, options? }. None: the point is the one choice (use.option is 'default'). A menu: an option with options of its own opens them on the same prompt, with a Back (at most 3 deep, 6 to a level, 40 in all). Only an option with none of its own is pressed; use.path names it from the top ('tools/hack/firewall'), and the server checks the whole path, every option's require on it. What a menu requires, the options in it (and its Back) need too, so a menu for the seated or the downed works in that state. Looking away folds the menu back to the top
requiretable?AddAction's words (job, item, zone, alive = false, ...). An unknown word is refused; a zone must be a saved one. Checked again on the server
audiencetable|'everyone'?{ people = { serverId | { charId = n } } }: only they see it and may use it. Default 'everyone'
reach, seeFrom, focusMode, enabled?As AddAction's
stylestring | table?How it looks on every player's game, as AddAction's (see Styles). false clears it
holdMsnumber?Hold E this long to use it, as AddAction's. In a menu only the options that are pressed are held: Back and a menu's own entry stay a press. onUse is still the only check: a hold is the player's game asking. false clears it
talkboolean?A Talk on an NPC (it opens a conversation with the NPC it rides). It never just vanishes: while the NPC is talking to someone else it reads Config.Conversations.speakingText ("Someone is speaking with this person.") to everyone else, and while you have it switched off (enabled = false) it reads busyText ("They're busy right now."). Pressing it then only says so again. It goes back to itself when the NPC is free. Its icon is talk (speech bubbles) unless you give one
quietForaudience?With talk: who sees nothing (not "busy") while it is switched off, such as the players already on the job it starts. false clears it
tagstring?Your run tag (see ReleaseTag)
onUsefunction(source, use)Runs on the server. use = { pointId, option, path, useId, coords, netId } (path is the option's ids from the top; for a point with no menu it is the option's id). Return false, 'why' to refuse; the player is told why. Keep it quick: start a thread for anything slow
Returns: pointId, false, or false, reason, and either way a third answer, warnings (the second answer is false, not nothing, on success, so the third gets through the export): a field a point does not have (AddAction's onSelect, a misspelt lable) or a reach / seeFrom held to its range, also said in the server console with what it most likely meant; nil when there were none. A wrong value is refused. UpdatePoint(pointId, patch) changes the fields you pass (false clears one; the tag stays). RemovePoint(pointId) takes it out. ListPoints({ tag }) lists yours.

Conversations: StartConversation

An NPC talks and the player answers, in the dialog capsule: what the NPC says and up to four answers show beside it. The scroll wheel picks an answer and E says it (the 3D interaction keys, pad included; no screen opens). A conversation opens only from a press: start it in your point's onUse with fromUse = use.useId. The server checks every answer (only those on screen, only from that player, only near the speaker) before your onChoose hears it. It ends when you end it, an answer that ends is chosen, the player walks away, opens a screen, goes down or logs out, or the NPC dies, goes or turns on them; onEnd(source, why) says which.

Others nearby see it too, as /me bubbles (not the player talking: they have the capsule): what the NPC says above the NPC, then the answer chosen above the player, then the NPC's reply. Config.Conversations.watcherBubbles = false turns that off. While the NPC is talking to someone, a point on it made with talk = true tells everyone else so (see AddPoint).

StartConversation(source, spec)SERVER

Open a conversation between an NPC and the player who pressed your point. Start it from the point's onUse.

local npcId, netId = exports.whip_core:SpawnNpc({ model = 's_m_y_dealer_01', coords = spot })
exports.whip_core:AddPoint({
    at = { netId = netId }, label = 'Talk',
    onUse = function(source, use)
        exports.whip_core:StartConversation(source, {
            fromUse = use.useId, npcId = npcId, speaker = 'Fence',
            line    = 'Got the goods?',
            options = { { id = 'yes', label = 'Here.' }, { id = 'bye', label = 'Leave', ends = true } },
            next    = { yes = { line = 'Let me see.', options = { { id = 'deal', label = 'Deal?' } } } },
            onChoose = function(source, answer, convId)
                if answer == 'deal' then PayFor(source); exports.whip_core:EndConversation(convId) end
            end,
        })
    end,
})
FieldTypeDescription
fromUsenumberuse.useId from your point's onUse, within 10 s. A point on an NPC opens a conversation with that NPC only
npcId / netIdnumberWho speaks: an NPC from SpawnNpc (it must be alive), or any networked entity
speaker, linestringThe name, and what they say (up to 440 characters; a long line is set smaller to fit)
optionstable1 to 4 { id, label, ends?, input?, cost? }. ends = true ends it once chosen (a Leave answer). input = { min, max, prefix }: a typed amount: choosing it turns the answer into a field (digits, E gives it, Backspace on an empty field goes back to the answers), and onChoose gets the whole number, checked against min/max (a haggle). cost = { amount, currency?, method?, reason? }: choosing it costs that, taken by whip before onChoose hears of it (as ChargePlayer takes it: method auto/cash/bank, or currency = an item key for that many of an item). One they cannot pay is refused with the reason and the same answers stay up; what follows a costed answer is not sent ahead before it is paid
nexttable?{ [answerId] = { line, options } }: the reply to an answer, sent ahead so the player sees it at once instead of after a round trip. An answer without one dims the capsule until you UpdateConversation (15 s, then it ends)
layout'grid'|'stack'?Answers in a 2x2 grid (default) or a column
onChoosefunction(source, answerId, convId, amount)?An answer, already checked (and paid, for a costed one). amount: the number typed, for an answer with input (typing needs a keyboard: on a pad, A on the empty field steps back)
canChoosefunction(source, answerId, convId)?Asked before an answer is taken or paid: answer false, 'why' to refuse it: what it needs may have changed since it was offered (they gave the keycard away). UpdateConversation takes one too (false takes it off)
onEndfunction(source, why)?'ended', 'chose', 'left', 'blocked', 'downed', 'logout', 'killed', 'gone', 'hostile', 'no answer', 'replaced', 'released' or 'stopped'
tagstring?Your run tag (see ReleaseTag)
Returns: convId, or false, reason. UpdateConversation(convId, { line, options, next, speaker }) says something else. EndConversation(convId) ends one of yours. GetConversation(convId) reads one. One conversation per player: a new one replaces theirs.

UI Library (Client)

Notification toasts, progress bars, input dialogs, alerts and confirms, skill checks, on-screen text and the typed-line composer; at the end, how your own screen, hotkeys and held-off controls fit with whip's (Screens, input and controls). The exports are the client's, bar the server-run bar, timed action and skill check, which are marked SERVER. Blocking components yield the calling thread until the player interacts.

The rules every blocking component shares:
  • One at a time. A call while another is up returns false, 'busy' without showing anything.
  • Why, as a second value when there is no answer: 'busy', 'cancelled', 'timeout', or 'failed' (SkillCheck). Callers reading one value are unaffected.
  • It closes the inventory first, and will not open over another resource's screen (one declared with SetUIOpen). It answers 'busy'. Your own screen does not block your own dialogs (take the focus back with SetNuiFocus(true, true) when one returns, because it lets go when it closes). A dialog (not a progress bar) also answers 'busy' while one of whip's focus-holding screens is up: the chat composer, the radial wheel, the /whip panel, the character screen, the appearance creator or the furnisher: it could not give their focus back when it closed.
  • It is yours. When your resource stops, whip cancels a bar or dialog you opened and hides text you showed.
  • Positional or one table. Every component takes its arguments either way: Confirm('Sell?', 'Sure?') or Confirm({ title = 'Sell?', message = 'Sure?' }).
  • While one is up, IsAnyUIOpen() is true, so prompts and the radial stay out of the way.
Notify(text, type, duration)CLIENT

Show a notification toast. Non-blocking, stackable (multiple can show at once).

ParamTypeDescription
textstringMessage to display
typestring'success', 'error', 'info', 'warning', default: 'info'
durationnumberMilliseconds to show, default: 3000
-- Simple notification
exports.whip_core:Notify('Item picked up!', 'success')

-- Error with custom duration
exports.whip_core:Notify('Inventory full', 'error', 5000)
LoadModel(model, timeoutMs) · LoadAnimDict(dict, timeoutMs) · LoadTextureDict(dict, timeoutMs) · LoadAnimSet(set, timeoutMs) · LoadPtfxAsset(asset, timeoutMs)CLIENT

Load something the game streams, and wait for it, never longer than timeoutMs (default 5000). LoadModel takes a name or a hash and answers the hash, or nil (a model the game does not have answers at once); the others answer true or false. LoadAnimSet is a walk style's clip set, LoadPtfxAsset a named particle asset. They wait, so call them from a thread (a command, an event handler, a CreateThread) and from a satellite through Whip.call('LoadModel', ...), which answers false instead of leaving your thread waiting if whip_core restarts. You release a model with SetModelAsNoLongerNeeded when you are done with it.

local hash = exports.whip_core:LoadModel('prop_beer_bottle')
if not hash then return end
local obj = CreateObject(hash, x, y, z, true, true, false)
SetModelAsNoLongerNeeded(hash)

if exports.whip_core:LoadAnimDict('mp_player_intdrink') then
    TaskPlayAnim(PlayerPedId(), 'mp_player_intdrink', 'loop_bottle', 8.0, -8.0, -1, 49, 0, false, false, false)
end
Progress(label, duration, opts) · Progress(opts)CLIENT

Show a progress bar. Blocks the calling thread. Can play an animation and put a prop in the player's hand for the length of the bar, and holds off the controls you choose.

ParamTypeDescription
labelstringText above the bar
durationnumberMilliseconds to fill, default: 3000
opts.canCancelboolean?Let the player press X / Escape to stop it. Default false here and in the server Progress, but true in a use with a progress bar
opts.animtable?{ dict, clip, flag } played for the length of the bar. flag default 49: upper body only, so they can still walk if disable.move allows. Or { scenario = 'WORLD_HUMAN_VEHICLE_MECHANIC' } for a GTA scenario: a whole performed task with its own props (the turbo fit and the revive use one)
opts.proptable?{ model, bone, offset, rot } held for the length of the bar. bone default 18905 (left hand); offset/rot are {x, y, z}
opts.disabletable?What is held off: { move, combat, car }. Default: walking and fighting off, driving allowed. { move = false } lets them move freely; { move = 'walk' } lets them walk but no faster (no jumping either), and trying to run cancels the bar
opts.cancelOnDeathboolean?Default true: dying, or being knocked down (ragdolled), ends the bar as 'cancelled', shown as interrupted, red, with why (see InterruptProgress). A long fall ragdolls too, and is said as falling, not as knocked down. false: a bar for the downed, which neither ends
opts.cancelOnExitboolean?Default false. For work done from a seat, like fitting nitrous: getting out of the vehicle the bar began in (pressing to get out, or no longer in it) ends it as 'cancelled'. Not in a vehicle, it ends at once. The server Progress also needs them in one to start ('not in a vehicle') and refuses a finish from outside it ('left the vehicle')
opts.notWhiletable?Work that cannot be done swimming, under water or falling: any of { 'swimming', 'underwater', 'falling' }. In one of them the bar does not start ('refused'); one that begins while it runs ends it as 'cancelled'. Either way the capsule says why: 'You cannot do that while swimming', '… while underwater', '… while falling'. 'swimming' covers under water too (with its own words); 'underwater' alone lets them work on the surface. Under water counts a car sunk with them in it; falling counts a skydive. GetBodyState asks the same question
opts.iconstring?An icon for the hint capsule's disc, which fills as the bar does: the names the 3D prompts use ('eat', 'fuel', 'place'…, in html/js/glyphs.js). Default: an hourglass
opts.itemstring | table?The item the bar is done with: its key ('jerry_can'), or a slot's data { item, metadata } as GetItemAt gives it, for an item whose picture changes with its state. The disc shows the item's picture, in its bubble as the hotbar does, instead of filling; the bar under the words still fills. An item with no picture shows icon. A use with a progress bar passes its own item

Or everything in one table: Progress({ label, duration, canCancel, anim, prop, disable, cancelOnDeath, cancelOnExit, notWhile, icon, item }).

Returns: true if it completed, or false, why, words: why is 'cancelled', 'busy' (another bar or dialog was up), 'timeout' or 'refused' (it never started: notWhile); words is what the capsule said when something stopped or refused it
-- Simple progress bar
local completed = exports.whip_core:Progress('Repairing...', 5000)
if completed then
    exports.whip_core:Notify('Repair done!', 'success')
end

-- Cancelable, with an animation and a prop, and the player may walk
local ok, why = exports.whip_core:Progress({
    label     = 'Drinking...',
    duration  = 5000,
    canCancel = true,
    anim      = { dict = 'mp_player_intdrink', clip = 'loop_bottle' },
    prop      = { model = 'prop_amb_beer_bottle' },
    disable   = { move = false },
})
if not ok and why == 'busy' then
    exports.whip_core:Notify('Finish what you are doing first', 'error')
end
A progress bar is the player's word, not proof. It runs on their machine, so a modified client can skip it and tell your server "done" straight away. If finishing the bar hands out anything (an item, a stat, a revive), run it from the server instead: the server Progress(source, opts) below, or for an item, a declared timed use.
IsProgressActive() · CancelProgress()CLIENT

IsProgressActive: is a progress bar running right now (anyone's)? CancelProgress stops the bar your resource started: its caller gets false, 'cancelled'. It will not cancel another resource's bar, and answers false when there is nothing of yours to cancel.

Returns: boolean: running / cancelled
-- The pump went away mid-bar: stop it
if exports.whip_core:IsProgressActive() then
    exports.whip_core:CancelProgress()
end
InterruptProgress(why) · ShowInterrupted(why, what?)CLIENT

For something the player did not choose stopping their bar or mode: the hint capsule turns red where it stands with why as its title and what stopped under it, for a moment, then goes. A cancel the player chose (X, C) only takes it down, as before. whip's own bars and modes already do this when the player goes down, is knocked down (ragdolled) or falls, gets out with cancelOnExit, goes into a state the bar's notWhile names, runs in a walk-only bar, or walks away from a pump; give mode's time running out too.

InterruptProgress ends the bar your resource started this way; its caller gets false, 'cancelled', why. ShowInterrupted is for a mode of your own that is not a bar (an aim, a placing): call it, then take your mode's text down: HideText does not cut the failure short. Not shown while a bar is up.

ParamTypeDescription
whystringWhat stopped it, in plain words: 'You were knocked down'
whatstring?ShowInterrupted only: what it stopped, under the why: 'Placing the sign'. An interrupted bar shows its own label there
Returns: boolean: interrupted (false: no bar of yours is up) / shown
-- your bar: the engine caught fire under them
exports.whip_core:InterruptProgress('The engine caught fire')

-- your own mode: knocked over while aiming the sign (a long fall ragdolls too: said as falling, as whip's own are)
if IsPedRagdoll(PlayerPedId()) then
    local state, words = exports.whip_core:GetBodyState()
    exports.whip_core:ShowInterrupted(state == 'falling' and words or 'You were knocked down', 'Placing the sign')
    stopSignMode()   -- which takes its HideText down
end
Progress(source, opts)SERVER

Show a progress bar on a player's screen and wait for it, true only if the bar really ran its length. The server keeps its own clock (a one-shot token; an answer sooner than 90% of duration is refused as 'too fast' and logged), so a modified client cannot skip it. Blocks your handler for the length of the bar. Takes the same options as the client Progress, as one table; duration is required.

One option only the server has: near: { coords = vector3, range = 3.0 } or { vehicle = vehicleId, range = 5.0 }. The player must be that close when the bar starts and when it finishes, or the answer is 'too far'. A SecureEvent's own near is checked once, when the event arrives; without this, a player could start an 8-second job and walk away before it ended.

And tag, your run tag: ReleaseTag(tag) ends the bar at once ('cancelled') and takes it off their screen, so a job that is called off does not leave someone stuck under its bar. A tag already released is refused ('run ended'). SkillCheck takes the same tag.

notWhile works here as on the client, but it is the player's game that checks it: the server cannot see whether someone is swimming. A bar it never started answers 'refused', so none of its time counts.

Returns: true, or false, why: 'cancelled', 'refused' (with notWhile), 'busy', 'timeout', 'too fast', 'too far' (with near), 'dead' (they are down, or died before it finished, unless you passed cancelOnDeath = false), 'not in a vehicle' / 'left the vehicle' (with cancelOnExit), 'player left', 'run ended', or a refusal (a missing duration, a bad near)
-- Inside a SecureEvent: a prompt asked to pick the lock. Whip.call, so a whip_core
-- restart mid-bar answers false instead of never (see the box below)
local done = Whip.call('Progress', source, {
    label    = 'Picking the lock...',
    duration = 8000,
    anim     = { dict = 'mini@safe_cracking', clip = 'idle_base' },
    near     = { coords = doorCoords, range = 3.0 },   -- still at the door when it ends
})
if not done then return end
-- the bar really ran: open the door
Using an item? Don't call this yourself: give RegisterUseHandler a table (a declared timed use) and whip also checks the item is still there, takes it, and gives it back if your effect fails.
It waits for the whole bar, so call it from a SecureEvent or a use handler, not a SecureCallback: the client gives up on a callback after 10 seconds.
Without dependency 'whip_core', if whip_core restarts mid-bar, exports.whip_core:Progress never answers: the wait lived in whip_core, and your handler stays stuck with whatever it held (a "busy" flag, say). That is why the example calls it as Whip.call('Progress', source, opts) (the satellite helper): a restart answers false, 'whip_core stopped' instead. The rule for any export that waits (Progress, SkillCheck, a bank ChargePlayer, Callback, anything that reads the database): use Whip.call whenever you hold a flag, a lock or a half-done step across the call. With the dependency your resource stops with whip_core and starts fresh, so nothing is left stuck; the habit still costs nothing, and keeps the resource safe if it ever runs without the dependency.
StartTimedAction(source, name, durationMs, match) · FinishTimedAction(source, name, match)SERVER

The server half of a progress bar. StartTimedAction starts the server's own clock and remembers match; FinishTimedAction answers with those values only if the action was started, at least 90% of durationMs ago, and no more than 15 seconds past it. One-shot; refusals go to the Monitor. Names are scoped to your resource. Same idea as the server-side SkillCheck.

ParamTypeDescription
sourcenumberPlayer server ID
namestringAny name for the action, e.g. 'drink'. Only needs to be unique inside your resource
durationMsnumberStartTimedAction only. The bar's length: the same number you pass to Progress on the client
matchtable|nilOn the start: plain values to remember: the use handler's addr is the usual one. On the finish: leave it out to get the start's values back; pass a table and it must equal them
Returns: StartTimedAction → true, or false, reason (no loaded player, no name, a duration not above 0). FinishTimedAction → a table, the values the start was given ({} if none), or false, reason
You usually want one call, not this pair. For an item, give RegisterUseHandler a table (a declared timed use). For anything else the server starts, call the server Progress(source, opts), which shows the bar and waits. This pair is only for a bar your client must run itself, with the server checking the finish afterwards.
-- The shape: start when the action begins, finish when the client says it finished
exports.whip_core:StartTimedAction(source, 'search', 6000, { bin = binId })
-- ... later, in the SecureEvent the client fires when its bar completes:
local started = exports.whip_core:FinishTimedAction(source, 'search')
if not started then return end   -- skipped the bar, or finished something it never started
-- started.bin is the binId the start remembered — the client never had to name it

Which text input do I use?

whip has three ways to let a player type, and each is right for its place:

You wantUseHow it behaves
A form: several fields, a dropdown, a checkbox, a number with limitsInput(title, fields)A dialog in the middle of the screen with the mouse. Waits for the answer, so call it from a command or your own thread
One line of free text (a chat message, a note, a name) typed without leaving the game viewOpenComposer(opts) (below)The player capsule becomes a text field; keyboard only, no mouse. Does not wait: your onSubmit is called with the text
A short code or number typed at a prompt in the world: a keypad, a safe dialctx.beginInput(opts) in an action's onSelect (Interactions)Digits typed straight into the 3D E-prompt; nothing opens on screen. Does not wait: your onSubmit is called with the text
Input(title, fields) · Input({ title, fields })CLIENT

Show a modal dialog with custom form fields. Gives the player keyboard + mouse focus. Returns values as an indexed table, or false, why when there is no answer.

ParamTypeDescription
titlestringTitle shown at top of the dialog
fieldstableArray of field definitions (see below)
Returns: table: { [1] = firstValue, [2] = secondValue, ... }, or false, why: 'cancelled', 'busy' or 'timeout'.
It waits for the player, so call it from a command or your own CreateThread, never straight from a prompt or vehicle-part callback, where waiting freezes every prompt on screen.

Field Types

TypeFieldsReturns
textlabel, placeholder, defaultstring
numberlabel, placeholder, default, min, maxnumber
selectlabel, options = { {value, label}, ... }, defaultstring (value)
checkboxlabel, placeholder (checkbox label), default (bool)boolean
textarealabel, placeholder, default, rows (1–12, default 3)string

required = true on a field keeps Submit from sending it empty, and a number's min and max are checked when Submit is pressed. A field that fails says why under itself and the dialog stays open. An empty number that is not required comes back as 0.

local result = exports.whip_core:Input('Create Report', {
    { label = 'Title',    type = 'text',     placeholder = 'Enter title...' },
    { label = 'Priority', type = 'select',   options = {
        { value = 'low',  label = 'Low' },
        { value = 'high', label = 'High' },
    }},
    { label = 'Details',  type = 'textarea', placeholder = 'Describe...' },
    { label = 'Urgent',   type = 'checkbox', placeholder = 'Mark as urgent' },
})

if result then
    local title    = result[1]  -- string
    local priority = result[2]  -- 'low' or 'high'
    local details  = result[3]  -- string
    local urgent   = result[4]  -- true or false
    TriggerServerEvent('reports:create', title, priority, details, urgent)
end
SkillCheck(difficulty) · SkillCheck({ difficulty }) · SkillCheck({ difficulty, game })CLIENT

Run a skill check: the ring. Part of a ring lights up and the player pushes the dot in the middle onto it, then holds it there until that part fills (a fifth of a second, slow then quick, Config.SkillCheckHoldMs), with a rising click for each part and a "ta-da" at the end. Then again somewhere else: 6, 12 or 16 parts by difficulty, each a little narrower than the one before. Touching the ring outside the lit part is a miss and fails the check, and so does running out of time: the outer line is the clock, set per difficulty (below) so a skilled player just makes it. It plays with a mouse (just move it, no button, no cursor; Config.SkillCheckMouseSpeed sets how fast) or a controller (the right stick); not the keyboard.

ParamTypeDescription
difficultystring|nil'easy', 'medium' or 'hard': a name from Config.SkillCheckDifficulty in config.lua, where a server can change the three or add its own. Default 'medium'

The difficulties

NameParts to fillThe ring is cut intoLit part, part by partClock
easy64 piecesthree quarters, narrowing evenly to a quarter3.9 s (0.65 s a part)
medium128 piecesa half, narrowing evenly to an eighth7.2 s (0.6 s a part)
hard1616 piecesa quarter, narrowing evenly to a sixteenth9.2 s (0.575 s a part)

Harder means more parts, smaller parts and less time for each (msPerPart in Config.SkillCheckDifficulty). A skilled player needs about half a second a part, so hard is only just possible.

Another resource's game instead of the ring: SkillCheck({ difficulty = 'hard', game = 'phone.reroute' }) (skill check games; 'unavailable' when no running resource has it). A game's own client canStart is asked first: the phone's need a phone, and a player with none is told You need a phone!, nothing opens, and the answer is 'not started' (not a fail).

Returns: true if every round was filled, or false, why: 'failed' (touched the ring off the lit part), 'cancelled', 'busy' or 'timeout'; with a game also 'not started' and 'unavailable'; or a sentence naming a difficulty that is not in the config
A skill check on the client is the player's word. If passing hands something out, run it from the server with SkillCheck(source, difficulty) (server export), which checks the answer and how fast it came.
local passed = exports.whip_core:SkillCheck('hard')

if passed then
    exports.whip_core:Notify('Lock picked!', 'success')
else
    exports.whip_core:Notify('Failed!', 'error')
end
SkillCheck(source, difficulty, opts)SERVER

The same ring, run from the server on a player's screen, with an answer the server can act on: a one-shot token, a minimum time (an answer faster than the rounds can be filled is a failure) and a timeout. Blocks until the player answers or it times out. Call it from a handler.

ParamTypeDescription
sourcenumberThe player
difficultystring|nil'easy', 'medium' or 'hard', as the client export (default 'medium')
optstable|nil{ timeoutMs?, minMs? }: the timeout defaults to the check's own clock plus 2 s. Run medium and hard from a SecureEvent, not a SecureCallback: a client Callback gives up after 10 s, and those two can run 9–11 s. minMs (the fastest believable answer; by default the rounds times the fill time) must be shorter than the timeout, or the call is refused with the reason. When the server stops waiting, the check is taken off the player's screen. tag (your run tag): ReleaseTag(tag) ends it at once, 'cancelled', ring off their screen. game: another resource's game instead of the ring (below), at one of its levels, timed by that game's own minMs and timeoutMs unless you give yours. quiet = true: a player the game cannot start for is not told why
Returns: true, or false, why: 'failed', 'busy', 'cancelled', 'timeout', 'too fast', 'dead' (they are down: not shown one, or passed it lying dead), 'run ended' (its tag was already released), 'Player not loaded', 'not started' (a game they lack something for, such as a phone: they were told, nothing was shown, and it is not a fail) or 'unavailable' (their game does not have that game); or a sentence naming a bad argument (a difficulty that is not in the config or the game's levels, a minMs that does not fit inside the timeout, a game nobody adds)
What it cannot stop: a cheater who waits the honest amount of time and then says "passed". It makes cheating cost the same time as playing. If an outcome must be uncheatable, do not gate it on a minigame.
-- Whip.call: a whip_core restart mid-check answers false instead of never (see Progress)
local passed, why = Whip.call('SkillCheck', source, 'medium')
if not passed then return false, (why == 'busy') and 'Finish what you are doing first' or 'You slipped' end
-- safe to hand over the reward here
Whip.skillCheckGame(id, def) · ListSkillCheckGames()BOTH SIDES

A skill check game of your own, played wherever whip runs a skill check: the server SkillCheck with { game = id }, the client one with { difficulty, game }, and the Director's Skill Check card, whose Game field lists every game on the server. whip_phone adds seven, played on the phone opened to a tablet (phone.bruteforce, phone.coderecall, phone.fragmentmatch, phone.override, phone.reroute, phone.safecrack, phone.stabilise; their levels are in whip_phone's Config.SkillGames). The token, the minimum time, the timeout, the run's tag and the answer are whip_core's, as for the ring. One call from the satellite helper, in a file both sides load (each side reads its own fields), or one on each side with the same id:

FieldSideDescription
labelserverIts name in the Director's list (40 characters)
descserverA line about it (optional)
levelsserver{ easy = { minMs, timeoutMs }, ... }: its levels, each with the fastest honest pass (minMs) and how long the server waits (timeoutMs, up to 120 s: its clock, its opening and the round trip)
canStart(source)serverOptional: what a player needs to play it at all. true, or false, words: they are told the words, nothing starts, and the check answers 'not started', which is not a fail (the phone's: 'You need a phone!')
canStart()clientOptional: the same rule for a client script's SkillCheck({ difficulty, game }), which never reaches the server's. No source, and it must not wait: read what the game already knows (the phone's: GetItemCount('phone'))
run(difficulty, token)clientPlay it, in a thread of its own (it may wait), and answer passed, why ('failed', 'cancelled', 'timeout', 'busy'). It holds whip's one blocking slot meanwhile, so no bar or dialog opens over it
cancel(token)clientOptional: the check was called off (the server gave up, the player went down, its run ended): make run return

The id is '<yours>.<name>'. It is sent again whenever whip_core restarts, and goes when your resource stops; a check of it under way then ends, 'cancelled'. ListSkillCheckGames() (server) answers { id, label, desc, levels, needs, owner } for each (levels: its level names, a list; the timings stay its own); Whip.removeSkillCheckGame(id) takes yours away. The Director card's How hard lists the ring's difficulties and every game's levels, and its Check says when the one picked is not the game's.

Whip.skillCheckGame('mygame.wires', {
    label = 'Cut the Wires',
    levels = { easy = { minMs = 2000, timeoutMs = 30000 }, hard = { minMs = 3000, timeoutMs = 40000 } },
    canStart = function(source) return HasCutters(source) or false, 'You need wire cutters' end,
    run = function(difficulty) return PlayWires(difficulty) end,   -- your screen: passed, why
})
RegisterAskChannel(name, deliver) / AnswerAsk(source, token, yes)SERVER

For a resource with its own screen to ask on (whip_phone registers 'phone'): whip_core's server-asked Yes / No questions marked for your channel (the Director's job invite) are offered to you first. deliver(source, token, kind, payload) answers true when you showed the question (payload: title, message, yes, no); anything else, or an error, and whip_core asks on screen as usual. Answer with AnswerAsk: only you may answer what you took, for that player and the character still playing. When whip_core gives up on it (its timeout, the run's end, the player leaving), the local whip_core:ask:cancelled ({ token }) fires on the player's game: take your screen down then. Yours until your resource stops; questions you were still showing are then asked on screen, the same question, so they can still be answered.

ParamTypeDescription
namestringThe channel's name, letters, digits, _ or -; another running resource's name is refused
deliverfunction(source, token, kind, payload) → true when shown; never waits
tokennumberThe question's number, as deliver was given it
yesbooleantrue Accept, false Decline
exports.whip_core:RegisterAskChannel('phone', function(source, token, kind, payload)
    if not playerHasPhone(source) then return false end      -- whip_core asks on screen instead
    TriggerClientEvent('my_phone:invite', source, token, payload)
    return true
end)
-- later, the player pressed Accept on your screen
exports.whip_core:AnswerAsk(source, token, true)
Returns: true, or false, why: a bad name, a name another resource holds; for AnswerAsk: 'That question is gone', 'That question was not asked through you', 'That question was for another character'
Alert(title, message, btnText) · Alert({ title, message, button })CLIENT

Show an alert dialog with a single OK button. Blocks until the player dismisses it.

ParamTypeDescription
titlestringDialog title
messagestringBody text
btnTextstring|nilButton text, default: 'OK' (button in the table form)
Returns: true once the player pressed the button, or false, why: 'cancelled' (Escape), 'busy' or 'timeout'
exports.whip_core:Alert('Zone Warning', 'You are entering a restricted area.')

-- Or one table
exports.whip_core:Alert({ title = 'Zone Warning', message = 'Restricted area.', button = 'Understood' })
Confirm(title, message, confirmText, cancelText) · Confirm({ title, message, yes, no })CLIENT

Show a confirm dialog with two buttons. Blocks until the player responds.

ParamTypeDescription
titlestringDialog title
messagestringBody text
confirmTextstring|nilConfirm button, default: 'Confirm' (yes in the table form)
cancelTextstring|nilCancel button, default: 'Cancel' (no in the table form)
Returns: true if confirmed, or false, why: 'cancelled' (they said no, or pressed Escape), 'busy' or 'timeout'
local yes = exports.whip_core:Confirm('Delete Vehicle', 'This cannot be undone. Are you sure?')
if yes then
    TriggerServerEvent('garage:deleteVehicle', vehicleId)
end

-- Or one table, with your own button words
local sell = exports.whip_core:Confirm({
    title = 'Sell car', message = 'Sell it for $4,000?', yes = 'Sell', no = 'Keep it',
})
ShowText(text, position, progress)CLIENT

Show persistent instruction text on screen, optionally with a progress bar. Non-blocking. Stays until you call HideText() or replace it with another ShowText(). There is one slot: showing takes it from whoever had it (the newest message is the one the player needs), and whip takes your text down when your resource stops.

It draws as the hint capsule: a twin of the player's HUD capsule. Its round disc shows what is being done, and beside it your controls. Write them as parts split by |: '[E] Place Burger | [Scroll] Rotate | [C] Cancel'. The first part is the title, the rest sit in a row under it; a short [Key] draws as a keycap and {pad:a} as a controller button.

ParamTypeDescription
textstringText to display (e.g. '[E] Open Door')
positionstring|table|nil'bottom' (default) or 'top', or every option in one table: { position, progress, icon, tone }
progressnumber|nil0–100 to fill the disc and draw a bar under the title; omit for no bar
iconstring|nilIn the table: an icon for the disc, by the names the 3D prompts use ('place', 'give', 'eat', 'talk', 'pickup', 'fuel', 'garage'…, all in html/js/glyphs.js). Without one the disc shows the first part's key
tone'warn'|nilIn the table: 'warn' turns the disc's ring amber: it cannot be done here (aiming at nowhere to put it)
-- Show prompt when near a door
exports.whip_core:ShowText('[E] Open Door', 'bottom')

-- With an icon in the disc, and the other controls under the title
exports.whip_core:ShowText('[E] Plant seed  |  [C] Cancel', { icon = 'place' })

-- With a bar — re-call it to update, no separate export needed
exports.whip_core:ShowText('Cracking the safe…', 'bottom', 42)

-- Later, hide it
exports.whip_core:HideText()
progress is not the same as Progress(). This draws a bar you control and update yourself, and never blocks. Progress() runs a timed bar and blocks until it finishes or the player cancels. Use this one when your script already knows the percentage.
HideText()CLIENT

Hide the persistent instruction text shown by ShowText(), only if it is yours. Text another resource put up since is left alone, so your cleanup cannot wipe their message.

Returns: boolean: false when the text on screen is another resource's
ShowObjective(id, text, opts?) · HideObjective(id)CLIENT

An objective card at the top right of this player's screen: the card a Director job shows, with your words and your mark. For something your client runs, such as a filming tool's pretend objective or a mission played on one client. Anything the server runs belongs to the server and goes through the Director. Again with the same id changes the card where it is (a new text lights its ring for a moment). Several cards stack with the newest on top. Yours by id, and gone when your resource stops.

ParameterTypeDescription
idstringYour name for the card, 64 letters at most
textstringWhat to do: 'Get to the docks'. At most 200 characters; colour codes are removed
opts.iconstring|nilThe mark in the disc, by a glyph's name: 'target', 'pin', 'star', 'car', 'cash', 'talk'... (the prompts' glyphs). Without one, or with a name whip does not have, the flag
opts.namestring|nilThe small line under it (a Director job puts its name there)
opts.countdownnumber|nilSeconds on a clock under it, counted down on the screen; opts.countdownTotal is the whole length, for the disc
opts.filmboolean|niltrue: the card stays up on a clean screen (the Camera Creator's play mode, a recording), as part of the picture. Otherwise it hides with the rest of whip
exports.whip_core:ShowObjective('escape', 'Lose the cops', { icon = 'star' })
-- later
exports.whip_core:HideObjective('escape')
Returns: ShowObjective: true, or false, why (an empty text, a bad id or clock). HideObjective: true, also when there was no card
IsRadialOpen()CLIENT

Is the F1 wheel on screen right now? Options on the wheel are added with AddAction and at = { radial = true } (a label is required; an icon and a description are worth giving).

Players open it with F1, or by holding D-pad down on a pad. It opens with nothing aimed at, and the centre shows how to choose. They aim with the mouse (by its direction from the centre) or either stick, then click or press A. Right-click, B or Escape closes it, and the arrow keys or D-pad left and right step round.

-- "Check Pulse" on the wheel, only while on duty as EMS
Whip.register(function()
    exports.whip_core:AddAction({
        id       = 'pulse',
        at       = { radial = true },
        label    = 'Check Pulse',
        icon     = '+',        -- no glyph for it, so a short text
        description = 'Check the person in front of you',
        require  = { job = 'ems', onDuty = true },
        onSelect = function(ctx)
            -- runs when picked
        end,
    })
end)
Returns: boolean

The composer: one line of typed text

The player capsule at the bottom left normally shows stats. The composer turns it into a text field, and the capsule takes the keyboard. whip_chat is the first caller, but nothing about it is chat-specific; any resource that wants one typed line gets the same field.

It takes the keyboard, never the mouse, so the camera stays put while the player types. Suggestion rows are picked with Tab and the arrow keys.
-- The shape a key binding wants: open on the press, take the keyboard on the release
RegisterCommand('+myinput', function()
    exports.whip_core:OpenComposer({
        placeholder = 'Say something',
        maxLength   = 256,
        deferFocus  = true,
        onSubmit    = function(text, mode) print(text) end,
        onCancel    = function() print('never mind') end,
    })
end, false)

RegisterCommand('-myinput', function()
    exports.whip_core:FocusComposer()
end, false)

RegisterKeyMapping('+myinput', 'Type something', 'keyboard', 'T')
You do not need to close it when your resource stops. The composer remembers which resource opened it, and whip closes it the moment that resource stops, handing the keyboard back.
OpenComposer(opts)CLIENT

Turn the player capsule into a text field. One at a time: returns false if a composer is already open, rather than cancelling somebody's half-typed line.

ParamTypeDescription
opts.onSubmitfunctionRequired. function(text, mode). mode is the active mode's name, or nil
opts.placeholderstring?Ghost text while the field is empty
opts.prefillstring?Text to start with, caret at the end
opts.maxLengthnumber?Default 256
opts.modestable?{ name, displayName?, color? } entries, cycled with Tab. The active one rides the bubble and comes back in onSubmit
opts.suggestionstable?{ name, help?, params? } entries, filtered live as the player types
opts.onCancelfunction?Escape, an empty line, or CloseComposer
opts.onScrollfunction?function(delta): PageUp (-1) / PageDown (1), for a log living in another NUI frame
opts.deferFocusboolean?Open WITHOUT taking the keyboard: see below
opts.padboolean?For a controller: the line is typed on whip's pad keyboard (OpenKeyboard's), in the keyboard's own window above the keys, and the capsule stays as it is. Done submits as Enter does, through the same onSubmit; B is onCancel. No modes or suggestions there: a plain line, or a typed-out / command. whip_chat's Chat on the F1 wheel uses it
opts.titlestring?With pad: what the keyboard says over the keys ('Chat')
deferFocus exists for key bindings, and you want it. FiveM calls +command on key down and -command on key up. Take the keyboard on the DOWN and the key that opened the box gets typed into it: press T and find a "t" already sitting there. Open on the press, call FocusComposer on the release.
Returns: boolean: false if one was already open, or onSubmit was missing
FocusComposer()CLIENT

Take the keyboard, for a composer opened with deferFocus. Safe to skip: an un-focused composer arms itself after a quarter of a second rather than sitting there inert.

Returns: boolean
CloseComposer()CLIENT

Close without submitting. Your onCancel runs, the keyboard is released, and the capsule goes back to showing stats. Only closes a composer your resource opened: another resource's half-typed line is left alone.

Returns: boolean: false when none is open, or it is another resource's
IsComposerOpen()CLIENT

Is a composer open right now: any composer, not necessarily yours.

Returns: boolean
Stuck with the keyboard captured? /resetcomposer in the F8 console (developer mode) hands the controls back, whatever took them.

Screens, input and controls

Whether the player is busy, whether a hotkey may act, how your own screen joins whip's, and holding controls off. These are what keep two resources' screens, keys and HUDs from fighting.

IsAnyUIOpen()CLIENT

Is the player busy in any UI: a whip screen (the inventory, a container, vehicle storage, a panel, a shop, another player's inventory, the character creator), a satellite's screen declared with SetUIOpen, or one of the UI Library's blocking components: a progress bar or a dialog (Input, Confirm, Alert, SkillCheck)?

This is the one you usually want. IsInventoryOpen() answers only about the plain inventory, so a check built on it will happily let the player sprint, open a menu or fire a weapon while they are standing in a shop or a car boot. If your question is "may the player start something else right now", ask this: prompts and the radial both do.
Returns: boolean
IsAnyScreenOpen()CLIENT

IsAnyUIOpen minus a bare progress bar: is something up that takes the player's eyes off the world: a screen or a dialog? Ask this to decide whether to hide an overlay of your own. whip's status HUD, the radar and whip_chat follow it: a progress bar is watched with the world, so they stay for it; a dialog or a screen hides them. The whip_core:ui:stateChanged event follows this question, not IsAnyUIOpen, so ask once and then listen. No polling across resources.

local hidden = exports.whip_core:IsAnyScreenOpen()          -- once, to start
AddEventHandler('whip_core:ui:stateChanged', function(e) hidden = e.open end)
Returns: boolean
IsGameInputFree()CLIENT

May a hotkey act on the world right now? false while any screen, bar or dialog is up (IsAnyUIOpen), while another screen holds the mouse or keyboard (the F1 wheel, chat, the /whip panel, character select, and any resource's own screen: anything holding the NUI focus means the game does not have the controls), and while a mode owns the keys: placing an item, give mode, throwing, placing an emote. Ask it at the top of every RegisterKeyMapping command that does something in the world. whip's E prompts ask it too, and close while it is false.

A key mapping fires under a screen. Disabling a control does not stop a RegisterKeyMapping command, and a screen that keeps game input live (SetNuiFocusKeepInput, the furnisher, whip_autos) passes every key through. Without this check, typing "l" in the furnisher's search box locked your car and its R key reloaded your gun. One call per key press is fine; do not poll it.
RegisterCommand('+my_horn', function()
    if not exports.whip_core:IsGameInputFree() then return end
    -- ...the key's work
end, false)
RegisterCommand('-my_horn', function() end, false)
RegisterKeyMapping('+my_horn', 'Horn', 'keyboard', 'h')
Returns: boolean
SetUIOpen(open, key, opts)CLIENT

Declare that your resource's own NUI is open or closed, and whip treats your screen exactly like one of its own. IsAnyUIOpen is the single switch every client module reads: whip's HUD hides on it, whip_chat hides, interaction prompts stop, and nothing else opens on top. This is how a satellite's screen joins it. The claim is keyed from GetInvokingResource, so a resource cannot claim to be another one.

ParamTypeDescription
openbooleantrue when you show your NUI, false when you hide it
keystring?Which of your screens. Leave it out if you only have one. A resource with two screens names each (SetUIOpen(true, 'shop')) so closing one leaves the other held
opts.keepHudboolean?true: a small screen that leaves the HUD up. The status HUD, the minimap and the vehicle dial stay on screen while it is open; chat, the prompts and the hotkeys still make way, as for any screen. The phone opens with it. If your screen sits where the HUD is, say where with SetUIArea and the HUD moves out of its way
Returns: boolean accepted: false only when there was no calling resource to attribute the claim to

While your screen is held, another resource's Input/Confirm/Alert/SkillCheck/Progress will not open on top of it (it answers false, 'busy'). Your own dialogs still open over your own screen, but a dialog lets go of the NUI focus when it closes, so take it back when the dialog returns if your screen is still up: local yes = exports.whip_core:Confirm('Buy it?') SetNuiFocus(true, true). The same goes for OpenComposer.

Call it on open, and clear it on close: both halves matter. Open your NUI without calling this and whip has no idea you are on screen: the HUD and chat stay drawn over your UI, interaction prompts keep firing behind it, and whip's own inventory can still open on top of yours. Close your NUI without calling SetUIOpen(false) and the opposite happens: HUD, chat and prompts stay suppressed with nothing visibly to blame. The one path you do not have to handle is your resource stopping or crashing: whip drops the claim itself, so a dead satellite cannot strand the player.
-- Opening your screen
SetNuiFocus(true, true)
SendNUIMessage({ action = 'show' })
exports.whip_core:SetUIOpen(true)

-- Closing it — every close path, including the NUI's own close button
SetNuiFocus(false, false)
SendNUIMessage({ action = 'hide' })
exports.whip_core:SetUIOpen(false)
SetUIArea(area, key)CLIENT

Say where your resource's UI is drawn on screen, and whip's HUD makes room for it. The vehicle dial (and a controller's buttons standing on it) slides out of the area by the shorter of two ways, up to stand above it or left to stand beside it, and fades while neither keeps it on screen. The phone uses it: its notifications peeking up from the bottom-right corner push the dial up, and the phone itself pushes it left. An area is not a screen: it hides nothing and takes no keys (that is SetUIOpen).

ParamTypeDescription
areatable | nil{ left, top, right, bottom } as fractions of the screen (0 to 1, from the top-left corner), where your UI will sit once it is still. nil or false when it has gone
keystring?Which of your UIs. Leave it out if you only have one
Returns: boolean, or false, reason for an area that is not four fractions with right > left and bottom > top

Send it when it changes, not every frame, and as your UI starts to move: the HUD eases into its new place in about half a second, in step with it. It is held under your resource and let go when that stops. whip_core forgets areas when it restarts, so send yours again from Whip.register.

-- a panel along the bottom-right edge, 22% of the screen wide and 18% tall
exports.whip_core:SetUIArea({ left = 0.76, top = 0.80, right = 0.98, bottom = 1.0 }, 'panel')
-- gone
exports.whip_core:SetUIArea(nil, 'panel')
HoldCleanScreen(id) / ReleaseCleanScreen(id)CLIENT

Nothing on screen but the game's picture, for filming: GTA's HUD and map, every layer of whip's own page, and the prompts, /me bubbles and bay marks in the world all go. It's what the Camera Creator's play mode uses. Chat is its own resource, so it stays (F6 hides it). Other resources hear it come and go on whip_core:ui:cleanScreen (Client Events).

ParamTypeDescription
idstring?Your name for this hold, released by the same name. The screen stays clean while anything holds it
Returns: boolean: false only when there was no calling resource

Hidden, not closed: a screen opened meanwhile still works but can't be seen, so let go as soon as the shot is done. Holds are kept per resource, so one resource can't release another's, and your resource stopping releases its own.

exports.whip_core:HoldCleanScreen('take')      -- rolling
exports.whip_core:ReleaseCleanScreen('take')   -- cut
BlockControls(id, spec) / UnblockControls(id)CLIENT

Hold controls off until you let go: no walking, shooting, driving or radio while your screen, tool or action is up. whip runs one loop for every resource's blocks. whip_core keeps the pause keys and action mode on it, so that loop is always running, and your block adds its controls to it instead of a loop of your own. What it blocks is every block together, worked out when a block changes, not every frame. Keyed per resource like whip's other registries, and swept when your resource stops, so a crash cannot leave the player unable to move. BlockControls again with the same id replaces that block; UnblockControls on an id you do not hold answers true.

ParamTypeDescription
idstring | numberWhich of your blocks: a name you choose, like 'shop'
spec.groupsstring[]?Named sets of controls: move (walk, sprint, jump, duck, cover), combat (attack, aim, weapon select, melee), driving (steer, accelerate, brake, handbrake, get out), vehicleCombat (attacking and aiming from a vehicle), look (mouse / right stick), radio (stations, tracks, radio wheel), weaponWheel (the wheel and weapon scrolling), and the switch driveBy (shooting from a vehicle, turned off once rather than every frame)
spec.controlsinteger[]?Any other GTA control ids, as well as the groups. Name 200 (Esc) when Esc is your way out: while you hold it, Esc is yours and whip's pause menu does not open on it
spec.all / spec.exceptboolean? / integer[]?all = true holds off every control, bar the except ids: a screen that only lets the player look around or walk. An exception never gives back a control another block holds
spec.walkboolean?walk = true keeps the player to a walk at most: no jog and no sprint, while they can still move and do everything else. Sprint is held off and the move speed is capped every frame in the same loop. On its own it is enough: { walk = true }
spec.jogboolean?jog = true keeps the player to a jog at most: they walk and jog as usual, but never sprint (a controller's double click jogs instead). whip_rope uses it while you hold a rope end. With walk as well, or another block's walk, the walk wins
spec.modeboolean?mode = true says this block is a mode of your own: placing, aiming a tool, a minigame. While you hold it, whip's world keys stand down as they do for its own placing: the E prompts close, and the hotbar and wheels do nothing (IsGameInputFree answers false), so E confirms your mode and does not also open the boot it is aimed at. That goes for the E that ends your mode too: the prompts never take a press made while they were stood down. The HUD stays up (SetUIOpen would hide it). On its own it is enough: { mode = true }
spec.hotbarboolean?With mode = true: the hotbar's number keys still use their slots while the rest stand down. Listen for whip_core:hotbar:slotUsed ({ slot }, on the player's game, just before the item is used) to put your mode away for the item, as whip's camera does
Returns: boolean ok, string? why: an unknown group (the reason lists the real ones), a bad control id, except without all, or nothing named. A block holds from the frame you make it.
You can still read a blocked control. A block stops the game acting on a button, not you hearing it: read it with the disabled readers: IsDisabledControlPressed, IsDisabledControlJustPressed, GetDisabledControlNormal. That is how a shop's own camera turns with the mouse it has blocked.
GTA has no "block until I say stop". A blocked control has to be blocked again every frame, which is why whip runs the one loop for everyone: write BlockControls instead of your own Wait(0) loop of DisableControlAction calls, and the cost is shared rather than repeated per resource.
-- Your screen opens
exports.whip_core:BlockControls('shop', {
    groups   = { 'move', 'combat', 'radio', 'driveBy' },
    controls = { 75 },   -- and leaving the vehicle
})

-- It closes
exports.whip_core:UnblockControls('shop')
HoldPlayerPed(id, flags) / ReleasePlayerPed(id)CLIENT

Hold the player's own ped invincible, frozen, hidden or without collision until you let go. whip has one owner for those four: the ped gets every resource's holds together, so your letting go never shows an admin who is invisible or thaws a player who is down, as setting them yourself would. Kept on the new ped a death or a model change hands back, and swept when your resource stops. HoldPlayerPed again with the same id changes what it holds; ReleasePlayerPed on an id you do not hold answers true.

ParamTypeDescription
idstring | numberWhich of your holds: a name you choose, like 'hang'
flagstableAny of invincible, frozen, hidden (other players do not see the ped either), noCollision, each true
Returns: boolean ok, string? why
-- whip_rope: the player hangs off a rope, drawn by a stand-in
exports.whip_core:HoldPlayerPed('hang', { hidden = true, noCollision = true, invincible = true })

-- They let go
exports.whip_core:ReleasePlayerPed('hang')
PermitNativeWeapon(weapon, on)CLIENT

whip takes away every GTA weapon on the player that no resource permits (Config.WeaponGuard): a dead NPC's gun, the shotgun in a police car. If your resource gives the player a native weapon, permit it first, and let go after you take it back. weapon is a hash or a name. Permits are kept per resource and go when it stops.

exports.whip_core:PermitNativeWeapon('WEAPON_PETROLCAN', true)
GiveWeaponToPed(PlayerPedId(), `WEAPON_PETROLCAN`, 100, false, true)
Returns: boolean: false for a weapon that is not a hash or a name

Controller support

A player on a gamepad gets most of whip without you writing anything for it. FiveM's pad key bindings never fire, so whip reads the pad from the game itself. Here is what you get free, and the three things you add for the rest: an action on a button, a pad on your own screen, and a mode's confirm and cancel.

What you get free

  • Prompts (AddAction): A uses the one in view, and D-pad up and down step its options.
  • The F1 wheel: an action with at = { radial = true } is on it. Holding D-pad down opens it.
  • Bars and dialogs: Progress, Input, Confirm, SkillCheck and whip's panels read the pad themselves.
  • Typing: OpenKeyboard is whip's on-screen keyboard.
  • Hints: in ShowText, {pad:a} draws the A button's picture. The others are b, x, y, lb, rb, lt, rt, ls, rs, l3, r3, dpad, dpad_up … dpad_right, view and menu. Your own page can use the same pictures: https://cfx-nui-whip_core/html/img/pad/a.svg.
LB is whip's combo key. LB + A talks and LB + X is the radio, and players can put other actions on LB + a button. Everything above, and everything below, leaves those presses to whip.

An action on a button

Your action goes on whip's buttons beside whip's own. It shows on the pause menu's Controller screen, players move it there, and whip reads the button for you. The phone, talk, the radio and nitrous are all done this way.

RegisterPadAction(id, def) / RemovePadAction(id)CLIENT

Put one of your actions on whip's controller buttons. It goes on the button it asks for while that button has nothing on it (in whip's default, or in a player's own layout that never set that button), and players can move it. One owner per id: registering again replaces it, and it goes when your resource stops.

ParamTypeDescription
idstringIts name: a letter, then letters, digits and _, up to 32. A player's layout saves it by this name
def.labelstringWhat the Controller screen calls it, up to 32 letters
def.commandstring?A key command to run, such as '+my_action'. A + command's - half runs when the button comes up. Give this or onPress
def.onPress / def.onReleasefunction?Run when the button goes down, and (optional) when it comes up. They must not wait
def.slotstring?The button it asks for: dpad_up, dpad_down, dpad_left, dpad_right, l3, veh_a (A in a vehicle), foot_b (B on foot), lb_a, lb_b, lb_x, lb_y, lb_dpad_up … lb_dpad_right. Left out, it starts on no button and players place it
def.wherestring?'car' or 'foot': where it does anything, so the Controller screen says so. A 'car' action also shows in the vehicle's controls over the dial when a driver gets in, while it is ready, so keep it not ready (SetPadActionReady) on a vehicle that has nothing for it
def.menusboolean?true: it works while a screen or menu is open too (talk). Otherwise it waits for IsGameInputFree
def.readyboolean?false: not yet (see SetPadActionReady). Default true
-- client: a button for your own key command, on LB + Y unless a player moved it
Whip.register(function()
    local ok, why = exports.whip_core:RegisterPadAction('mycafe_menu', {
        label = 'Cafe menu', command = 'mycafe_menu', slot = 'lb_y',
    })
    if not ok then print('no pad button: ' .. why) end
end)

If the button it asks for already has another action on it in whip's default, it starts on no button, and F8 says so once, naming what has the button. It is still registered (ok is true), and players can put it on a button themselves. The server's Config.Controller.Layout names whip's own there (D-pad up the phone, LB + A talk, LB + B Gunny's check ammo, LB + X the radio, A in a vehicle nitrous, B on foot Gunny's reload), so the buttons left for you are LB + Y and LB + the D-pad. When two resources ask for one free button, the action whose id comes first in the alphabet has it, so every server settles the same way.

Returns: boolean ok, string? why: a bad field (the reason names it), one of whip's own ids, or an id another running resource holds
SetPadActionReady(id, ready)CLIENT

Can your pad action do anything right now? While it is not ready, its button is GTA's again: the press reaches the game, and GTA's own action on that button is not held off. It keeps its button. Nitrous is ready only while the player drives a car with a bottle, so a motorbike without one keeps A for ducking. Gunny's reload on B on foot is ready only while a gun is drawn, so with none (or a melee weapon) B is GTA's punch.

exports.whip_core:SetPadActionReady('nitrous', true)    -- in a car with a bottle
Returns: boolean ok, string? why: false for an id that is not one of yours
GetPadActionButton(id)CLIENT

Which button an action is on now, in this player's layout, so your own hint can show the right one. Any action: yours, another resource's, or whip's own ('radial', 'inventory', 'engine', 'sprint'). Ask when you show the hint, not once at start: players move actions on the Controller screen.

local slot, pictures = Whip.call('GetPadActionButton', 'mycafe_menu')
if type(slot) == 'string' then
    exports.whip_core:ShowText(pictures .. ' Cafe menu')   -- '{pad:lb}{pad:y} Cafe menu'
end
Returns: string? slot ('lb_y'), string? the button's pictures for ShowText ('{pad:lb}{pad:y}'), string? its name ('LB+Y'); nil when the action is on no button, or there is no such action

A pad on your own screen

The browser cannot read a gamepad inside FiveM. Whip.padScreen (from @whip_core/lib/satellite.lua) reads it for your NUI screen while it is open, sends each press to your page, owns your NUI focus (no mouse cursor while a pad drives; moving the mouse brings it back), and holds the pad's world actions off.

Whip.padScreen(def?)CLIENT

Make one at file scope, then screen:open() when your screen opens and screen:close() on every way it closes. open answers whether a pad is in the player's hands, for your page's button hints. Your page gets { action = 'pad', cmd, down, rep } per press (rep counts a held D-pad's repeats) and { action = 'padDevice', pad } when the player swaps between pad and mouse.

FieldTypeDescription
buttonsstring[]?Which to read. Default up, down, left, right, a, b, x, y; there are also lb (sent when LB comes up without a combo), rb and menu
stickboolean?false: the left stick does not step like the D-pad. Default true
releasestable?{ a = true }: those buttons send down = false when let go (a hold on your page)
keepInputstring?'always': the game keeps its input with the mouse too (a camera that orbits). Default 'pad': only while a pad drives
blocktable | false?Held off while a pad drives, as BlockControls takes it. Default: walking, looking, fighting, the radio and weapon wheels, jump, getting in, cover, reload and Start / Esc. false: nothing (you block yourself)
onButton / onDevicefunction?(cmd, down, rep) and (pad), instead of the two messages
onFramefunction?Every frame a pad drives: a stick of your own (the gunny bench turns its weapon with the right stick)
local screen = Whip.padScreen()

local function openMenu()
    SendNUIMessage({ action = 'open', pad = screen:open() })
    exports.whip_core:SetUIOpen(true)
end

local function closeMenu()
    screen:close()
    SendNUIMessage({ action = 'close' })
    exports.whip_core:SetUIOpen(false)
end

// your page
window.addEventListener('message', (e) => {
    if (e.data.action === 'pad') padPress(e.data.cmd);           // up down left right a b x y
    if (e.data.action === 'padDevice') showPadHints(e.data.pad);
});
Returns: the screen: :open() (answers pad), :close(), :typing(on) (a text field on your page has the keyboard: the pad is left alone and the game gets no input), :pause(on) (another screen of yours has the pad: left alone, your focus untouched; not needed for OpenKeyboard, which the screen leaves the pad to by itself), :isPad()
OpenKeyboard(opts?)CLIENT

Whip's on-screen keyboard, for a pad player who has to type: a search box, a price, a name. It comes up over any page (yours or whip's) and waits for what was typed, so call it from a thread. A types the lit key, X deletes, Y is a space, LB is Caps, LT turns to the symbols page, RB is Done and B leaves it; the right stick moves it round the screen, and it opens where the player left it. While it is up the pad is the keyboard's alone: your Whip.padScreen leaves it alone by itself, and a reader of your own waits between the whip_core:keyboard:opened and whip_core:keyboard:closed events. A keyboard player types into your box as usual, so open it only on a pad (IsControllerActive).

Words. Over the keys it offers up to three ways to finish the word being typed, in the player's language (Config.Keyboard): RT takes the first, or D-pad up reaches them. It learns the words each player sends, on their PC, and offers those first; holding A on a letter with accents (in a language that has them) opens them. Players can turn the words off in the pause menu (Server Settings → Controller). For text that is not words (a plate, a code), pass predict = false.

ParamTypeDescription
opts.titlestringWhat is being typed, shown over the keys ('Search', 'Price')
opts.valuestringThe text it starts with (what is in your box now)
opts.placeholderstringGhost text in the empty field, saying what goes there
opts.numericbooleantrue: a number pad (digits, minus and point)
opts.maxLengthintegerAt most this many characters
opts.predictbooleanfalse: no word suggestions over the keys, and nothing typed is learned (a plate, a serial, a code). On otherwise; never on the number pad
-- a satellite's search box, on A, from a thread: the text goes back to its own page
local text = Whip.call('OpenKeyboard', { title = 'Search', value = current, maxLength = 40 })
if text then SendNUIMessage({ action = 'searchText', text = text }) end
Returns: string what was typed, or nil when the player left it (B, Cancel), or asked for another keyboard before this one answered

A mode's confirm and cancel

A mode of your own (placing, aiming a tool, a minigame) confirms and cancels the way whip's do: on a keyboard the Interact key (E, unless the player moved it in GTA's Key Bindings: the prompts follow it too) and C; A and B on a pad, never LB + A or LB + B.

IsAcceptPressed() / IsAcceptHeld() / IsCancelPressed() · AcceptHint() / CancelHint()CLIENT

Read the first three every frame of your mode; they answer for whichever device is in the player's hands. The other two name the key for a hint: '[E]' (the Interact key's name, '[F]' when the player moved it there) / '[C]', or the button's picture ('{pad:a}' / '{pad:b}') for ShowText. Hold a BlockControls block for as long as the mode runs, with mode = true so whip's E prompts and hotkeys stand down (or a prompt in focus takes the same E), and naming what those keys also do in GTA, so they do not act as well: on a keyboard C is GTA's look behind (26); on a pad B is also reload and melee (45, 140). A's sprint is already held off by whip's pad reader. Read the blocked keys with these readers: they read through the block.

exports.whip_core:BlockControls('placing', { controls = { 26, 45, 140 }, mode = true })
exports.whip_core:ShowText(exports.whip_core:AcceptHint() .. ' Place   ' .. exports.whip_core:CancelHint() .. ' Cancel')
while placing do
    if exports.whip_core:IsAcceptPressed() then place() end
    if exports.whip_core:IsCancelPressed() then placing = false end
    Wait(0)
end
exports.whip_core:HideText()
exports.whip_core:UnblockControls('placing')   -- (and whip lets go of it if your resource stops)
Returns: boolean for the three readers, string for the hints
IsKeyPressed(key, button) / IsKeyHeld(key, button) · KeyHint(keyText, button)CLIENT

Any other key of your mode, by the same rules: key on a keyboard, button on a pad, whichever device is in the player's hands and never both (a pad's buttons are keys on a keyboard too: A is Enter, X is Space, LB is E and Q), and on a pad never with LB held. Either may be nil when that device has no such key. Both are GTA control numbers; a pad's are the frontend ones (201 A, 202 B, 203 X, 204 Y, 206 RB, 199 Start, the D-pad 187–190), never LB (205), which is whip's.
