KeyHint names it for ShowText: keyText is the key's name on a keyboard, button a picture's name (the list under "What you get free") or a list of them drawn side by side.

if exports.whip_core:IsKeyPressed(22, 203) then flip() end           -- Space, or X on a pad
local hint = exports.whip_core:KeyHint('Space', 'x') .. ' Flip   '
          .. exports.whip_core:KeyHint('Scroll', { 'lt', 'rt' }) .. ' Turn'
Returns: boolean for the readers; string for KeyHint ('[Space]' or '{pad:x}', '' when that device has none)

Reading the pad yourself

IsControllerActive()CLIENT

Is the player using a gamepad right now? Use it to choose which button picture to show, not to change what a control does. Ask it once, then listen for whip_core:pad:deviceChanged ({ pad }), which fires when the player swaps, at the moment whip's own hints swap: no need to ask on a timer.

local onPad = false
Whip.register(function() onPad = Whip.call('IsControllerActive') == true end)
AddEventHandler('whip_core:pad:deviceChanged', function(e) onPad = e.pad == true end)
Returns: boolean
PadComboTakes(control) / PadComboUsed()CLIENT

Only for a resource that reads the pad with its own loop (Whip.padScreen already asks these). A press made while LB is held may be whip's combo rather than yours, the same rule whip's own panels keep.

ParamTypeDescription
controlnumberA frontend control just pressed: 201 A, 202 B, 203 X, 204 Y, 206 RB, the D-pad 187–190
-- on a press: skip it when it is whip's combo (no release follows it either)
if IsDisabledControlJustPressed(0, id) and not exports.whip_core:PadComboTakes(id) then press(id) end
-- your screen's own LB: on LB's release, and only if no combo was used during the hold
if IsDisabledControlJustReleased(0, 205) and not exports.whip_core:PadComboUsed() then pageBack() end
Returns: boolean: PadComboTakes: true while LB is held and the button is A or X, or one whose LB slot holds something that works in menus; false when LB is not held. PadComboUsed: true when a combo button went down during the current LB hold (or the last one, until LB goes down again). Ask them on a press, not every frame

Camera System

Overview

Scripted cameras for cutscenes, intros, showrooms and cinematics. One camera at a time, and it is the resource's that started it: when that resource stops, whip hands the view back. Three ways to use it:

  • A sequence, made in the Camera Creator: a timeline of shots, and how the camera moves between them. Play it by name, or paste it as code: PlayCameraSequence.
  • An orbit round anything, left up until you stop it, which the player can turn and zoom: OrbitCamera.
  • One fixed shot (PlayCamera), or a simple path through points (PlayCameraPath, which plays as a sequence).

Players get one more: the driving camera, a chase camera they can switch on for driving.

Everything moves on smooth springs that look the same at any frame rate, turns never go the long way round, and an orbit frames a bike and a bus alike. While a sequence plays, the room the camera is in is kept right for the game, so a shot inside an MLO draws its interior.

The Camera CreatorServer owners

An experimental feature: an unfinished prototype, off by default. Turn it on in /whip → Settings → Config → Experimental features, and it is a row at the end of the /w dev menu. You fly a camera and build a timeline along the bottom of the screen, like the Rockstar Editor; you stay standing where you were.

  • Flying: hold the right mouse button, then WASD, Space and Ctrl to rise and drop, Shift for speed, the wheel to zoom. Let go and the pointer is back for the timeline. On a controller the sticks fly at all times.
  • Keys: press G (or + Key here) to put a key at the playhead, where the camera is now. Added at the end, the playhead moves on two seconds, ready for the next. Drag a key along the timeline to change when it happens; click it to pick it and see its picture.
  • The kind of shot a new key gets is chosen on the card (left), with what it is of: you, your vehicle, or the picked thing (look at a car, a person or a prop and press Pick).
    • Fixed: a place in the world.
    • Orbit: round the subject, sized to it (Fill 1 is "it just fills the screen"), and it can spin slowly.
    • Chase: behind it on a spring, leaning into slides and widening with speed.
    • Mounted: fixed to it, a bonnet or a bumper camera.
    • Track: stands in one place and keeps the subject in frame.
  • Between keys (on the picked key, "Then"): Cut jumps; Glide moves smoothly to the next key, and keys that glide one into the next are one move: the camera flows through the keys between without stopping, still at each key at its time, and the first key's Pace says how the whole glide starts and ends (Steady: already moving). Spring is quick then settles, Orbit swings round the subject instead of cutting across (choose the way round). Between two shots that look at the same subject, the camera keeps it in frame all the way.
  • Weight (on a key the camera stops at: the last one, or one whose Then is Cut): Carries on past this key makes the camera heavy. It arrives at the speed it was going instead of slowing for the key, and drifts on past it the same way, still turning and zooming as it was, slowing to a stop as if its push had let go. Resistance says how soon: low drifts far, high stops soon (it drifts its speed ÷ the resistance: 10 m/s at 2 goes 5 metres). A » on the timeline marks it.
  • Layers on a key: Shake (a camera in hands), a Lens kick (a punch of zoom that fades), and a Filter from that key on.
  • The sequence (on the card): its length, Plays round (keep its fixed places round your vehicle, so it plays round any car anywhere; in the editor they follow the car, and stay where they were if it is gone), Loop, Cinema bars, and Even speed, which spaces the keys so the camera keeps one speed. The playhead goes anywhere along the timeline, past the last key too, and a key is added where it stands.
  • Scrub by dragging along the timeline; Space plays it. While you look through the timeline, grabbing the camera (right mouse) flies on from that picture. F puts the camera at the picked key's picture to fly on from it; E sets the picked key to where the camera is now.
  • Keys on the keyboard: ← → pick the key before or after, Delete deletes it, Ctrl+D duplicates, Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Y undo and redo, V looks through or flies, Esc puts the key down, then leaves. The controls along the bottom show every key, or the controller's buttons when you pick one up.
  • Who has the controls: the editor starts with them, so nothing reaches your character, and a car you are driving stops and holds where it is. Controls → Game in the dock (or Tab; LB + R3 on a controller) gives them to your character with the editor still up: drive the car to where the shot wants it, or look through the timeline and drive while a chase or bonnet camera follows you. The camera and the editor's keys hold still meanwhile; Tab or Esc gives the controls back to the camera.
  • A clean picture: Hide points (P) stops drawing the camera points and the path in the world. Hide HUD (H) leaves nothing on screen but the picture; the camera still flies and Space still plays, and H, Esc or a click brings the editor back. Exit leaves (your draft is kept).
  • On a controller: A adds a key, X sets the picked key here, Y deletes it, D-pad left and right pick keys, up and down zoom, RB plays, ⧉ looks through or flies (hold it to hide the HUD; A, B, X, Y or ☰ brings it back), R3 changes the kind of new keys, ☰ saves, B leaves.

Your work is kept. Leaving keeps the draft for next time, on this PC too, so a restart does not lose it. Save keeps it on the server by name (a permanent admin's), where every admin can Open it and any script can play it: PlayCameraSequence('intro'). Copy code copies it as a Lua call to paste into a script instead.

Making a cinematicServer owners

The Camera Creator is a cinematic kit: place cameras, then go and play while they film you, and record the screen (OBS or any recorder) for the video. No script needed.

  1. Place your cameras in the Camera Creator: a bonnet camera (Mounted), a chase, one by the roadside (Track), an orbit for the reveal. Each key is a camera.
  2. Play in game (the button, or F9). The editor goes away and you are your character again: walk, drive, emote. A capsule at the top says the keys, then fades so it is not in your video.
  3. Roll the shots:
    • F5 plays the timeline from the start, live, while you keep playing; F5 again cuts back to the normal camera. When the timeline ends it goes back by itself (set Loop to keep it going).
    • Page Down / Page Up switch to the next or previous camera and hold it, like a director cutting between cameras; Num 1–Num 9 go straight to one. An orbit keeps spinning, a chase keeps following, a bonnet camera rides along. Switching on the card says whether it cuts or glides.
    • F9 goes back to the editor, the camera where you left it.

A clean picture. While a shot rolls nothing is on screen but the game: whip's HUD, GTA's HUD and map, the prompts and bubbles in the world all go. With Clean screen the whole time on (the card; it is on to start with) the screen stays clean while you play between shots too. Chat is its own resource: F6 hides it. Another resource can put its own UI away too: it hears whip_core:ui:cleanScreen (Client Events).

Round your car, wherever it is. Set Plays round to your vehicle and the fixed and roadside cameras are kept round the car as it is when the shot rolls, and a camera you switch to is placed round where the car is at that moment. A camera 20 m ahead of the car is always 20 m ahead, ready to drive past.

The keys can be moved in GTA's Settings → Key Bindings → FiveM (they appear once you have played in game the first time), and do nothing unless the Camera Creator is on.

Playing a sequence

-- One saved in the Camera Creator, by name (from a thread: the first time, it is asked of the server)
exports.whip_core:PlayCameraSequence('intro')

-- Round a car you hand it ('target' is the Creator's "picked thing")
exports.whip_core:PlayCameraSequence('car_reveal', { subjects = { target = veh }, async = true })

-- Or written out (what Copy code gives you)
exports.whip_core:PlayCameraSequence({
    letterbox = true,
    keys = {
        { t = 0, move = 'glide', ease = 'smooth',
          shot = { kind = 'fixed', pos = { x = -75.2, y = -819.4, z = 326.1 }, rot = { x = -12, y = 0, z = 140 }, fov = 50 } },
        { t = 4000, move = 'orbit', around = 'left',
          shot = { kind = 'orbit', subject = 'vehicle', yaw = 30, pitch = 8, fit = 1.2, fov = 40, turn = 6 } },
        { t = 9000, shot = { kind = 'orbit', subject = 'vehicle', yaw = 160, pitch = 4, fit = 0.9, fov = 36 },
          shake = { amount = 0.3, freq = 6 } },
    },
})

A sequence is checked before anything goes up, and a mistake answers false, why naming the key and the field. Its subjects: 'player' and 'vehicle' need nothing; any other name is one you pass in subjects, as an entity or a place { x, y, z, h }. A subject that goes away mid-sequence (a car deleted) holds the last picture. Every field is under PlayCameraSequence.

Orbiting anything

-- A showroom: the player turns it with the mouse (or the right stick) and zooms with the wheel
exports.whip_core:OrbitCamera(veh, { yaw = 35, pitch = 12, fit = 1.3, fov = 40, turn = 6 })
-- ...when they are done
exports.whip_core:StopCamera()

The driving cameraServer owners

The same chase shot, for driving: each player can switch it on for themselves in the pause menu (Server Settings → Vehicles → Smooth driving camera). It is off until they do, unless you make it the default. In a car, on a motorbike or a quad, it replaces GTA's camera:

  • It follows on a spring that keeps up at any speed, leans towards where the car is going in a slide, looks ahead along the road, pulls in when a wall is behind, and widens a little with speed.
  • The mouse or the right stick looks round the car; a second after letting go it drifts back behind. C (or clicking the right stick) looks behind while held.
  • It shakes a little at speed, and gives a knock in a crash or on landing a jump.
  • GTA's view button still sets how far back it sits, sized to the vehicle. First person stays GTA's own.

It steps aside on its own while the player aims or shoots from the car, for GTA's cinematic camera, on death, and for any other script's camera: a sequence, an orbit, the Camera Creator, noclip, another resource's camera. It comes back a moment after they end, so nothing you write needs to know about it. Switch it off for everyone, change the default, or set the shake in Config.DrivingCamera (/whip → Settings → Config → Vehicles).

Single Camera

Use PlayCamera(opts) to create a single camera at a fixed position.

exports.whip_core:PlayCamera({
    pos    = vector3(-1042.0, -2745.0, 22.0),
    rot    = vector3(-10.0, 0.0, 180.0),
    fov    = 50.0,
    filter = 'cinema',
})
FieldTypeDefaultDescription
posvector3gameplay camCamera world position
rotvector30,0,0Rotation (pitch, roll, yaw)
fovnumber60Field of view
filterstring'none'Timecycle filter name
canLookbooleanfalseAllow mouse look rotation
canMovebooleanfalseAllow WASD camera movement
exitKeybooleantrueESC key exits camera
transitionInnumber0Ease from the gameplay camera into this one (ms)
transitionOutnumber0Ease back to the gameplay camera when it stops (ms)
asyncbooleanfalseReturn straight away instead of waiting: see below
It waits, unless you pass async = true. With exitKey on (the default), canLook or canMove, the camera's controls run in your thread: PlayCamera does not return until the camera ends. That is what a cutscene script wants. If you show a camera and carry on (open a menu, start a timer), pass async = true and it returns at once.

Camera Paths

Use PlayCameraPath(opts) for a simple path through points. Two modes: interpolate (a smooth curve through all of them, at one speed along it, with easing over the whole path) and cycle (jump to each point, hold for cycleDuration). A path plays as a sequence, so anything more (orbits, a subject, per-key moves) is a sequence.

exports.whip_core:PlayCameraPath({
    points = {
        { pos = vector3(-1042.0, -2745.0, 22.0), rot = vector3(-10.0, 0.0, 180.0), fov = 40 },
        { pos = vector3(-1038.0, -2748.0, 22.0), rot = vector3(-5.0, 0.0, 90.0), fov = 50 },
    },
    mode     = 'interpolate',
    duration = 8000,
    easing   = 'smooth',
    loop     = true,
})
FieldTypeDefaultDescription
pointsarrayrequiredArray of { pos, rot, fov?, filter? } keyframes (min 2)
modestring'interpolate''interpolate' (smooth spline) or 'cycle' (jump between)
durationnumber10000Total path duration in ms (interpolate mode)
easingstring'smooth''linear', 'smooth', 'ease-in', 'ease-out'
loopbooleanfalseLoop the path
cycleDurationnumber3000Hold time per point in cycle mode (ms)
transitionInnumber0Ease from the gameplay camera into the path (ms)
transitionOutnumber0Ease back to the gameplay camera when it stops (ms)
asyncbooleanfalseReturn straight away instead of waiting for the path to end

A path waits for its whole length unless async = true, and a loop path never ends by itself, so a looping path without async holds your thread until something calls StopCamera.

Available Filters

'none', 'scanline_cam', 'CAMERA_secuirity', 'CAMERA_secuirity_FUZZ', 'heliGunCam', 'NG_filmic04', 'NG_filmic08', 'cinema', 'underwater', 'Forest', 'Tunnel', 'phone_cam1', 'phone_cam2'

Stopping

exports.whip_core:StopCamera()
if exports.whip_core:IsCameraActive() then
    -- camera is still playing
end

StopCamera stops the camera your resource started (another resource's is left alone) and eases out over its transitionOut. You do not need it in onResourceStop: when the resource that started a camera stops, whip hands the view back.

Camera (Client)

Scripted camera system for cutscenes and cinematics. See Camera guide for config tables and filter list.

PlayCamera(opts)CLIENT

Play a single static camera. Supports optional mouse look and WASD movement. See guide for full config table.

ParamTypeDescription
optstable{ pos, rot, fov, filter, canLook, canMove, exitKey, transitionIn, transitionOut, async }
Waits until the camera ends (with exitKey on, the default, or canLook/canMove) unless async = true.
Returns: true, or false, 'busy' while another resource's camera is up (the same rule as dialogs: it is not taken from them; your own camera you may replace), or false, why for a pos/rot that is not a vector3
exports.whip_core:PlayCamera({
    pos    = vector3(-1042.0, -2745.0, 22.0),
    rot    = vector3(-10.0, 0.0, 180.0),
    fov    = 50.0,
    filter = 'cinema',
})
PlayCameraPath(opts)CLIENT

Play a multi-point camera path. Uses Catmull-Rom spline interpolation ('interpolate' mode) or point-cycling ('cycle' mode). See guide for full config table.

ParamTypeDescription
optstable{ points, mode, duration, easing, loop, cycleDuration, transitionIn, transitionOut, async }
Waits for the whole path, forever for a loop, unless async = true.
Returns: true, or false, why, checked before any camera goes up: fewer than two points, a point without a pos or rot, a duration or cycleDuration of 0, or 'busy' while another resource's camera is up. If anything fails mid-path, the player is handed back to gameplay.
exports.whip_core:PlayCameraPath({
    points = {
        { pos = vector3(100, 200, 30), rot = vector3(0, 0, 180), fov = 40 },
        { pos = vector3(105, 195, 30), rot = vector3(-10, 0, 90), fov = 50 },
    },
    mode     = 'interpolate',
    duration = 8000,
    easing   = 'smooth',
    loop     = true,
    async    = true,   -- a loop never ends by itself: without async this call never returns
})
-- ...later
exports.whip_core:StopCamera()
PlayCameraSequence(sequence, opts)CLIENT

Play a timeline of shots: the Camera Creator's. sequence is the name it was saved under (fetched from the server the first time: call from a thread), or the table itself (Copy code gives you one).

optsTypeDescription
subjectstable{ [name] = entity | { x, y, z, h } }: what the sequence's subject names stand for. 'player' and 'vehicle' (the car the player is in, or was last in) need nothing
asyncbooleanReturn at once; otherwise it waits for the sequence to end
loop, letterboxbooleanOverride the sequence's own
speednumber1 as made, 0.5 half speed (0.05 to 20)
startAtnumberMilliseconds into it to start
holdbooleanStay on the last moment until stopped instead of ending
controlbooleanThe player turns and zooms its orbits (mouse and wheel, or the right stick and triggers)
exitKeybooleanEsc (B) ends it. Off by default
transitionIn, transitionOutnumberMilliseconds to ease from and back to the game's camera

A sequence is { keys, length?, anchor?, loop?, letterbox?, ease? }, times in milliseconds. anchor names a subject its fixed places are kept round (as it stood when the sequence started). ease bends the whole timeline's time ('linear', 'smooth', 'in', 'out', 'strong'), so keys no longer happen at their times; the Camera Creator does not use it (each glide has its own pace), and it straightens a sequence it opens.

A key is { t, shot, move?, ease?, rate?, around?, coast?, shake?, filter?, punch?, label? }. move is how the camera goes on to the next key: 'cut', 'glide' (default; ease its pace, default 'smooth'), 'spring' (rate 3 gentle to 8 brisk) or 'orbit' (between two orbits of one subject; around 'short', 'left' or 'right'). coast (0.2 to 50) gives a key the camera stops at some weight: it arrives at its speed and drifts on past it, the number its resistance. shake = { amount, freq } in degrees and turns a second; punch = { fov, decay } a lens kick from that key; filter a timecycle name from that key on.

A shot has a kind, a fov (default 50) and, all but fixed, a subject name:

kindFields
fixedpos = { x, y, z }, rot = { x = pitch, y = roll, z = yaw } (round the anchor when there is one)
orbityaw (0 behind the subject, 180 in front), pitch (degrees above), fit (1 = it fills the screen) or dist (metres), aim = { x, y, z } the point looked at as a share of its box (−1 to 1; +y its front, +z its top), look = { pitch, yaw } to turn off that point, turn (degrees a second), clear (metres kept off the ground, default 0.35), roll
chasedist, height, ahead (look-ahead), slip (0 follow its nose, 1 follow where it goes), stiff, turnRate, fovAdd and distAdd (at speed), collision (pull in at walls, default on)
mountedoffset = { x, y, z } in its own metres (right, forward, up), rot relative to it: it tilts and rolls with it
trackpos, and the aim and look of an orbit: stands still and keeps the subject in frame
Returns: true, or false, why before any camera goes up: what is wrong with the sequence (the key and the field), a subject or anchor not there, a name with no saved sequence, or 'busy' while another resource's camera is up
OrbitCamera(target, opts)CLIENT

An orbit round an entity (a car, a ped, a prop) or a place { x, y, z, h }, left up until StopCamera. The player turns it and zooms it unless control = false. It returns at once.

optsDescription
yaw, pitch, fit / dist, aim, look, fov, turn, clearThe orbit's numbers, as an orbit shot's (default yaw 35, pitch 12, fit 1.3, fov 40)
controlThe player turns and zooms it (default on)
exitKey, letterboxEsc (B) ends it; cinema bars
transitionIn, transitionOutMilliseconds of ease from and back to the game's camera (default 500 each)
Returns: true, or false, why
GetCameraSequence(name)SERVER

A sequence saved in the Camera Creator, by name: a copy, ready to send to a player's game for PlayCameraSequence. nil when there is none.

Returns: table|nil
StopCamera()CLIENT

Stop the camera your resource started and restore the player's normal view, easing over its transitionOut. Another resource's camera is left alone. Not needed on your resource stopping: whip releases it.

Returns: boolean: false when no camera is playing, or it is another resource's
IsCameraActive()CLIENT

Check if a scripted camera is currently playing.

Returns: boolean

Theming & Skins

Overview

Every visual decision whip's UI repeats — colors, fonts, radii, shadows, spacing — is a CSS custom property declared once in whip_core/html/css/base.css. A skin is a separate resource containing just an fxmanifest.lua and a theme.css that overrides those tokens. It never touches whip_core, so it survives every framework update. The full walkthrough (token catalog, own fonts, partial themes, what is locked) is whip_core/docs/nui-theming.md.

Two ways to activate

Standing theme: Config.Theme = 'your_theme_resource' in whip_core's config: the server's permanent look. Runtime skin: a start/stoppable resource that applies itself via the export below: start reskins every connected client live, stop reverts automatically.

SetActiveTheme(resource)SERVER

Set (or clear, with nil) the server-wide theme override on top of Config.Theme. The override belongs to the resource that set it (the registration rule): only it can change or clear it, a second skin is refused with the first one's name, and when the owning resource stops the override unwinds to Config.Theme by itself — a skin resource writes zero revert code. Applies to connected clients live (the NUI hot-swaps a stylesheet link, no restart) and rides the login sync for late joiners. Fail-soft on every client: a misnamed resource logs to F8 and falls back to the base look, never a blank UI.

ParamTypeDescription
resourcestring|nilResource whose theme.css to apply, usually your own name. nil clears back to Config.Theme (only for the resource that set it).
Returns: bool ok, string|nil err: false, 'the active theme belongs to X — stop it first' when another resource's skin is active
-- A complete start/stop skin's server.lua, in full:
-- (fxmanifest.lua: shared_script '@whip_core/lib/satellite.lua')
Whip.register(function()
    exports.whip_core:SetActiveTheme('my_skin')
end)

GetActiveTheme() reads it back: the theme resource in force and the resource that set it, or Config.Theme and no owner when nothing overrides it.

Inside Whip.register, not at file scope. The override lives in whip_core's state and dies with it on a core restart; Whip.register runs again exactly then, so the one-liner above survives restarts. A file-scope call works until the first restart whip_core, and then your skin silently vanishes.
GetActiveTheme()SERVER

Which theme is in force, and who set it.

local theme, owner = exports.whip_core:GetActiveTheme()
print(('theme %s, set by %s'):format(tostring(theme), owner or 'config.lua'))
Returns: string|nil theme, string|nil owner: the resource whose theme.css is applied and the resource that set it; with no override, Config.Theme (nil for the stock look) and no owner
Going deeper: the NUI documentation set. Three markdown deep-dives live in whip_core/docs/, one per layer: nui-theming.md: the full theming contract (token catalog, bringing your own fonts, partial themes, and what is locked); nui-architecture.md: how the NUI modules are structured and how they talk to the client scripts; and nui-inventory.md: the custom inventory renderer interface, for replacing the inventory's presentation wholesale rather than retinting it. When a question outgrows this section, it is answered there.

Browser features (Chromium 103 or 144)

FiveM's in-game browser is moving from Chromium 103 to Chromium 144. whip's pages load a detector that asks the browser what it can do, feature by feature, so a page can use the new way where the answer is yes and the old way where it is no. Your page can ask the same questions, and so can your Lua.

In your page

Load whip's detector before your own scripts. It sets window.WhipCaps, and puts a caps-… class on <html> for every feature the browser has (caps-anchor, caps-game-view, …).

<script src="https://cfx-nui-whip_core/html/js/caps.js"></script>
FlagWhat the browser has when it is true
chromeIts Chrome version, a number (0 when it does not say).
hasThe :has() selector.
colorMix / relativeColorcolor-mix() / relative colours such as rgb(from var(--x) r g b / 50%): shades worked out from one colour.
textBalancetext-wrap: balance and pretty: even lines, no word left on its own.
startingStyle@starting-style and transition-behavior: allow-discrete: fade in from display: none, and out before it, in CSS alone.
heightAutointerpolate-size: allow-keywords: transitions to and from height: auto.
anchorCSS anchor positioning: a menu or a card placed against the thing it belongs to, and kept on screen.
fieldSizingfield-sizing: content: inputs and text boxes that grow with what is typed.
viewTransitionsdocument.startViewTransition: one change of screen, cross-faded.
schedulerYieldscheduler.yield(): let the browser draw between chunks of a long job.
webgpunavigator.gpu is there (not a promise that the player's GPU can be used).
zoomScreenPxInside a CSS zoom, getBoundingClientRect answers in screen pixels. False on Chromium 103, which answered such boxes unzoomed. Measured, not looked up.
gameViewFiveM's new game view: CfxGameViewRenderer, and gl.CFX_BIND_GAME_VIEW on a WebGL2 texture, so a page can draw or read the game's picture. (<object type="application/x-cfx-game-view"> shows the game on both builds.)

In CSS, @supports is safe for a feature Chromium 103 does not have at all: text-wrap, anchor positioning, field-sizing, interpolate-size, @starting-style. A property 103 does not know is simply skipped there, too. For :has() use the caps-has class (see the warning below), and zoomScreenPx and gameView can only be asked through their classes. Never put var() inside an @supports test: a value holding var() passes in every Chrome, whatever it says.

/* Chromium 103 skips it: the title wraps as it always has */
.card-title { text-wrap: balance; }

/* Only where the browser places menus itself */
@supports (anchor-name: --a) {
    .slot.menu-open { anchor-name: --slot; }   /* only the slot whose menu is up */
    .menu { position-anchor: --slot; position-area: bottom right; position-try-fallbacks: flip-block, flip-inline; }
}

/* :has() through the class, never @supports */
.caps-has .panel:has(.slot.selected) { border-color: var(--ui-accent); }

/* A question @supports cannot ask */
.caps-game-view .camera-preview { display: block; }

In your page's script, read the flags and use the helpers, which fall back by themselves:

if (WhipCaps.anchor) {
    menu.classList.add('anchored');       // the browser places it
} else {
    placeMenuByHand(menu, x, y);         // your old placement
}

// Cross-faded on Chromium 144, an instant change on 103
await WhipCaps.transition(() => showPage('settings'));

// A long list built in chunks, so the screen never stalls
for (const chunk of chunks) {
    renderRows(chunk);
    await WhipCaps.yieldToBrowser();
}
Trust the flags, not CSS.supports alone. FiveM's Chromium 103 ran with every experimental web feature switched on, so a half-built feature parses there: CSS.supports('selector(:has(a))') and @supports selector(:has(a)) are true on it. And anything holding var() passes in every Chrome, because it is only checked when the style is worked out. A flag is true only where the browser has the feature, asked with plain values, and its Chrome version shipped it finished.

In your Lua

GetNuiCaps()CLIENT

What the game's browser can do, as whip_core's page reported it once it loaded: the flags in the table above. A copy, yours to keep.

local caps = exports.whip_core:GetNuiCaps()
if caps and caps.gameView then
    print('this FiveM can hand a page the game picture')
end

-- Or wait for it, if your resource starts before the page has reported
AddEventHandler('whip_core:nui:capsDetected', function(caps)
    print(('the browser is Chrome %d'):format(caps.chrome))
end)
Returns: table|false caps, string|nil err: false, 'not_detected_yet' before whip_core's page has reported (the event above fires when it does). From a satellite, Whip.call('GetNuiCaps').
In game: /nuicaps prints every answer in F8. /nuicaps gameview shows FiveM's new game view live in a box for a few seconds: the live game there means it works, solid blue means it did not bind.

Reading and pressing whip's screens from code

For tests and tools: what whip_core's screens show, and pressing them by their words the way a mouse would, so each screen's own handlers run. Developer mode only: with it off, both answer false, 'developer mode is off'. whip_core's own page, and any other resource's page that loads whip_core's page tools in its <head> (the phone, Whiplash and the dealership do), which also keeps that page's errors with the rest (GetErrorLog below):

<script src="https://cfx-nui-whip_core/html/js/page-tools.js"></script>

A satellite needs nothing else: @whip_core/lib/satellite.lua passes the asks to its page. A keyboard-only menu that takes no mouse can still be pressed if its rows say data-probe-press and answer a click, as /w's do.

ReadScreen(opts?)CLIENT

The words on screen in reading order, a line per block, and every control that can be pressed: buttons, fields, lists, tabs, switches and rows with a pointer cursor. Each control has an id for PressScreen, its words, its kind, near (the heading above it), row (for a control of few words such as "Change", the words of its row), its state and where it is.

local screen = exports.whip_core:ReadScreen({ under = 'People' })   -- the Jobs page's People part
for _, c in ipairs(screen.controls) do print(c.id, c.kind, c.label) end
optsTypeWhat it does
textbooleanfalse leaves the words out
controlsbooleanfalse leaves the controls out
understringOnly the controls under a heading with these words
pagesbooleanfalse leaves out the other resources' pages
Returns: { view, focus, text, controls, pages }|false, why. pages: what each other resource's page shows, by resource name, only the ones showing something.
PressScreen(target, opts?)CLIENT

Presses one control at its middle. target is an id from the last ReadScreen, or its words: an exact match first, then one that starts with them, then one that contains them. near narrows it to a heading or a row, kind to a kind, index picks the nth. With several matches and no index it presses nothing and answers { ambiguous = { ... } }, each with its id. Ids change when the screen does: read again after a press.

exports.whip_core:PressScreen({ label = 'Change', near = 'Who can open it' })   -- a container's row
exports.whip_core:PressScreen('Search containers', { text = 'fridge' })     -- types into the field
exports.whip_core:PressScreen('Weather', { choose = 'Rain' })          -- picks from a list
exports.whip_core:PressScreen({ label = 'Messages', page = 'whip_phone' })   -- on another resource's page
optsTypeWhat it does
buttonstring'left' (the default), 'right' or 'double'
textstringType this into the field instead of clicking it
enterbooleanWith text: press Enter after
choosestringPick the list's choice with these words
Returns: { pressed, kind, chose, typed, covered }|{ ambiguous }|false, why. covered names whatever lay on top of the control when it was pressed.

Screenshots

whip's own screenshots, in place of screenshot-basic. That one copied the whole game picture every frame whether anybody wanted a shot or not, and halved the frame rate on GTA V Enhanced. These read the picture once, when asked, and cost nothing in between. A shot is the game alone, as FiveM hands it over: whip's interface is laid over the game afterwards, so it is not in it. Anything the game draws itself is (DUI screens in the world, 3D prompts, /me bubbles). Ask for ui and whip's page is drawn over the picture as it looks at that moment: whip_core's screens and HUD, not other resources' (the phone, Whiplash, the dealership), and a WebGL map that draws only when it changes may come out empty.

TakeScreenshot(opts?)CLIENT

This player's game picture, now. Waits until it is made (up to 15 s).

local png, why = exports.whip_core:TakeScreenshot({ format = 'png' })
optsTypeWhat it does
formatstring'jpg' (the default), 'png' or 'webp'
qualitynumber0 to 1, for jpg and webp (0.92)
width, heightnumberThe picture's size, the screen's by default; give one and the other keeps the screen's shape
uibooleantrue: with whip's interface drawn over the game, as on screen (under a second longer)
frames, everynumberA burst: frames (2 to 24) read every ms (33 to 1000) into one picture, a grid with each frame's number and time, for movement a still cannot show. 640 wide a frame unless asked; no ui
uploadtable{ url, field }: post it to that address (a helper on this PC) as a file in a form instead, and get its answer back
Returns: dataUrl|false, why (with upload, the answer's text)
RequestScreenshot(source, opts?)SERVER

A player's game picture, from their own game: options as TakeScreenshot's, without upload. Waits until it arrives (up to 30 s). Only an answer to an ask made here is taken. A player's game can still send a picture it made up, so this is for tools, not for catching cheats.

local jpg, why = exports.whip_core:RequestScreenshot(source, { quality = 0.8, ui = true })
Returns: dataUrl|false, why

Errors, frame rate and reviving, for tools

For tests and tools: what went wrong, how smoothly the game runs, and putting a player back on their feet.

GetErrorLog(opts?)SERVERCLIENT

The last 200 things that went wrong on this side: errors in the threads, event handlers, NUI callbacks, commands and statebag handlers of whip_core and of every satellite that loads @whip_core/lib/satellite.lua (unless its fxmanifest says whip_error_tap 'no': the satellite helper), in their SecureEvent and SecureCallback handlers, whip_core's own caught errors (its [whip_core…] lines that say ERROR, threw or errored), red (^1) warnings, and in a player's game the errors of whip_core's page and of satellite pages that load the page tools. A player's errors otherwise reach only their F8 console, which nothing else can read. Each is still printed as before. One that repeats is counted, not kept twice. Not kept: an export's error (its caller gets it, as before), and a plain print a catch site words some other way.

local before = exports.whip_core:GetErrorLog().last
-- ... do the thing being tested ...
local after = exports.whip_core:GetErrorLog({ since = before })
for _, e in ipairs(after.entries) do print(e.resource, e.kind, e.count, e.text) end
Returns: { entries = { { seq, at, side, resource, kind, text, count } }, last, side }. kind is 'error', 'warning' or 'page'.
MeasureFrames(opts?)CLIENT

How smoothly this game runs over the next seconds (1 to 30, 5), as numbers rather than /whipcost's printed table. Waits that long. For a before and after, measure standing still in the same place.

local f = exports.whip_core:MeasureFrames({ seconds = 5 })   -- f.fps, f.fpsWorst1, f.over50 ...
Returns: { seconds, frames, fps, fpsWorst1, medianMs, worstMs, over33, over50 }: frames a second on average and over the worst 1% of frames, the median and longest frame in ms, and how many frames took over 33 ms and over 50 ms.
RevivePlayer(source, reason?)SERVER

Brings a downed player back where they lie, as /w Restore does: the server's record first, then their game stands the ped up and ends the death screen. Full health, no armour. reason goes in the stats change log after revive: (your resource's name if left out).

exports.whip_core:RevivePlayer(source, 'medic')
Returns: true, or false, 'Player not loaded' | 'not down'

Screens in the world (DUI)

A DUI is a page from your resource drawn by a browser of its own into a texture, so the game can draw it in the world: over a head, on a wall, flat on the ground. whip draws its prompts, the /me bubbles, NPC conversations, the garage bay outline, sign-post listings and the Director's marks this way. The page is a file in the resource, loaded from it; nothing comes from the internet.

Each DUI is a whole browser, and it keeps rendering and holding its texture whether or not anything draws it. So whip keeps four rules, and a resource that makes its own DUI should keep them too:

  1. One browser per system, not one per thing. Lay the page out as an atlas of cells and draw each thing from its cell. Thirty garage bays are thirty quads from one texture: the browser count never grows with what is on screen.
  2. A change is another cell or a message, never a new browser. Send a message only when what a cell shows has changed, never every frame.
  3. Made on first use, given back when idle. Make the browser the first time something is drawn from it, and destroy it a while after the last time.
  4. A still page. Animate only while something it shows is happening. A page with an endless animation draws a new frame all the time.

whip's own DUIs keep these rules: each is made the first time it is needed, and given back a while after it was last drawn.

Your own DUI

One browser for every sign your resource shows: made the first time a sign is drawn, sent a sign's words only when they change (held until the page is up), and destroyed a minute after the last sign was drawn.

local PAGE = ('nui://%s/html/signs.html'):format(GetCurrentResourceName())
local TXD, TEX = 'mysigns', 'signs'
local IDLE_MS = 60000

local dui, up, waiting, painted, lastUsed = nil, false, {}, {}, 0

local function release()
    if not dui then return end
    DestroyDui(dui)
    dui, up, waiting, painted = nil, false, {}, {}
end

-- Given back IDLE_MS after the last draw: a timer, not a loop.
local function checkIdle()
    if not dui then return end
    local left = lastUsed + IDLE_MS - GetGameTimer()
    if left > 0 then SetTimeout(left, checkIdle) else release() end
end

-- Every draw calls this: made the first time, and counted as used.
local function ensure()
    lastUsed = GetGameTimer()
    if dui then return end
    dui = CreateDui(PAGE, 1024, 1024)
    CreateRuntimeTextureFromDuiHandle(CreateRuntimeTxd(TXD), TEX, GetDuiHandle(dui))
    local mine = dui
    CreateThread(function()
        while dui == mine and not IsDuiAvailable(mine) do Wait(50) end
        if dui ~= mine then return end
        up = true
        for _, msg in ipairs(waiting) do SendDuiMessage(dui, json.encode(msg)) end
        waiting = {}
    end)
    SetTimeout(IDLE_MS, checkIdle)
end

-- A sign's words, sent only when they change (and held until the page is up).
local function paint(cell, text)
    ensure()
    if painted[cell] == text then return end
    painted[cell] = text
    local msg = { cell = cell, text = text }
    if up then SendDuiMessage(dui, json.encode(msg)) else waiting[#waiting + 1] = msg end
end

-- Each frame a sign is near: its cell of the 4 x 4 atlas, over that spot.
local function drawSign(cell, x, y, z)
    ensure()
    if not up then return end
    local col, row = cell % 4, cell // 4
    SetDrawOrigin(x, y, z, 0)
    DrawSpriteUv(TXD, TEX, 0.0, 0.0, 0.1, 0.1, col / 4, row / 4, (col + 1) / 4, (row + 1) / 4, 0.0, 255, 255, 255, 255)
    ClearDrawOrigin()
end

The page reads each message as a JSON string, and paints only the cell it names:

window.addEventListener('message', (e) => {
    const d = typeof e.data === 'string' ? JSON.parse(e.data) : e.data;
    if (d && d.cell !== undefined) document.querySelectorAll('.cell')[d.cell].textContent = d.text;
});
Keep an atlas inside the game's limit. CreateDui throws for a page wider than the game allows: 8192 pixels on GTA V Enhanced. Pack the cells into more rows rather than one long strip.

Activity Log

whip keeps two timelines: one per character and one per item instance. The admin tools read both, which is how "where did this rifle come from" is answerable at all. A satellite can write to them.

In game: /whip → Economy → Item LogServer owners

Two tabs. Everything is every item event on the server, newest first, updating while you are at the top of it (it pauses when you scroll down to read). Rows that name no item, such as logins and dev tool use, stay on the person's timeline in the Player Manager. On the left, narrow it: one search box for a person, an item or an item's id; what happened: came in (gained, bought), went out (lost, destroyed), traded, dropped & picked up, used, moves; when: the last hour, today, this week, or all Config.ActivityLogDays days the log keeps; and how many at least, which catches a big pile of cash appearing at once. In every row a person opens their page in the Player Manager, an item opens its whole life (how it came to be, where it was last seen, everything since), and a place teleports you there.

Economy is one item at a time: cash first. The item is the page's title; pressing it shows every item as a picture, with a search and four choices: Moved today, Moved this week, Moved this month (busiest first, each tile saying how many times it moved) and All. Today is shown by the hour, the last 7 or 30 days by the day:

  • In the game now: how many there are, counted from pockets, stashes, car boots and gloveboxes and the ground (as last saved, a second behind at most). Not counted: what is inside other items (a wallet's cash, a gun's magazine) and a resource's own storage.
  • Came in, went out, the difference: came in is gained (admin gives, scripts, the ATM, starting cash) plus bought in shops; went out is lost (spent, eaten, paid in) plus destroyed.
  • A graph per hour or day: came in above the line, went out below; point at a bar for its numbers ("how many burgers a day").
  • How many there were: worked back from today's count through the log, so an estimate: where the log saw more come in than there is now, the line stops at none and says so.
  • Where it came from and where it went, by reason (ATM withdrawal, admin: …, bought at 24/7 Store, paid at Burger Shot), who holds the most now and who gained the most (a click on either shows their activity with it).

A satellite's reason on AddItem, AddPlayerCash and the rest is what these reasons read.

LogActivity(source, event, detail, slotData)SERVER

Write a row to a player's timeline. To tie the row to one particular item as well, give the item's address: { kind = 'player', id = source, sub = 'player', slot = 4 }, the addr a use handler or FindItem hands you, or any store's (a gun in a stash). That also gives the item its uid the first time anything touches it.

-- On the player's timeline only
exports.whip_core:LogActivity(source, 'whiplash_entered', 'Bay 3')

-- On the player's timeline AND the rifle in pocket slot 4's own history
exports.whip_core:LogActivity(source, 'serial_filed', 'workbench',
    { kind = 'player', id = source, sub = 'player', slot = 4 })

-- Inside a use handler: the item that was used
exports.whip_core:LogActivity(source, 'lockpick_used', 'garage door', addr)
Give the address, not the table GetItemAt gives you. Everything that crosses an export is a copy, so a uid given to a copy would belong to nothing. A copy still works if the item already has a uid, but the address always works. A { container, slot } table is refused with a reason.
ParamTypeDescription
sourcenumberWhose timeline
eventstringShort event name. Required
detailstring?Free text shown alongside it
slotDatatable?The item's address, with a slot. Adds the row to that item's own timeline too
Returns: true, or false, reason (no event name, a wrong address, an empty slot)
FlushActivityLog()SERVER

Write every log row still owed, now. A row is saved with the change it describes (in the same transaction, once the player's action ends), so this is for tests and for operations work, not something a normal feature needs. Returns false if the database refused the rows (they are kept and tried again).

Returns: boolean

Debug & internal exports

Exports that exist for whip's own tools and tests. A resource should not build on them: they may change without notice.

GetGarageHelperStatus()CLIENT

Internal: a test hook. What the garage position helper is doing right now, for a test or a tool: a feature whose only other evidence is a rectangle painted on a road.

FieldTypeDescription
enabledbooleanConfig.GaragePositionHelper.enabled
duiActivebooleanWhether the one browser this feature uses is up
drawingnumberHow many bay outlines are visible right now
drivingbooleanWhether the player is in a driver's seat
qualifiesbooleanWhether the driven vehicle passes the requireStorable test
Returns: table

Timing your loops (WhipCost)

What a loop of yours really costs on a player's PC. A profiler capture shows where the time goes, but recording adds its own cost, so its numbers run high. /whipcost times every section marked with WhipCost, whip_core's and every satellite's, for a while, then prints one table in the F8 console, the dearest first. Read the us a frame column: its share of every frame. KB a second is the memory a section makes a second, which Lua's garbage collector then has to clear.

A second table follows: memory made, by resource. It covers all of each whip resource, timed or not, for every resource that loads lib/satellite.lua or lib/cost.lua. This is the memory you see climb in resmon and then drop back when the collector clears it. While /whipcost runs, each resource's collector is paused so the counts are exact. A resource that makes more than 32 MB in the run has its collector let go again, and its figure stops there (the table says so). When it ends, the collectors catch up, which may cause a small hitch.

WhipCost.start() / WhipCost.stop(name, started)CLIENTSERVER

Marks a section to time. Load client_script '@whip_core/lib/cost.lua' in your fxmanifest.lua, and server_script '@whip_core/lib/cost.lua' to time server code too (the server console's whipcost prints those: time only, by the server's CPU clock). Off (always, unless /whipcost is running), start() answers nil and stop() returns at once, so a marked loop costs two calls and a check. Never put a Wait() between the two: a run that waited a frame is left out of the table, not counted.

ParamTypeDescription
namestringThe section's line in the table, as 'area: what'
startednumber|nilWhat start() returned
-- client.lua: the café's marker loop, timed by /whipcost
CreateThread(function()
    while true do
        local cost = WhipCost.start()
        drawCafeMarkers()
        WhipCost.stop('mycafe: markers', cost)
        Wait(0)
    end
end)

Then in game, with developer mode on: /whipcost (20 seconds), or /whipcost 60 (5 to 120). Play as usual while it runs. The clock moves in whole milliseconds, so a section that ran fewer than 100 times is marked "rough". After the sections it lists the memory each resource made, then every event, export call and timeout whip_core was asked to run, how often: one a frame from another resource costs both sides every frame. Last come whip_core's own loops, by the line each waits on, with the memory one pass makes.

Returns: start(): number|nil; stop(): nothing

Your page in /w

A resource can add a page of its own to the /w menu: a row at the end of Panels that, picked, swaps the list for your rows, in the same panel. The way back is the page's first row, and Backspace (B on a pad) does the same. Like every /w tool, it shows only to a developer with developer mode on. Your page says what its rows are and what picking one does; whip_core draws them, moves the selection, and asks for the rows again after every pick.

A page can have levels of its own (a list to pick from, one actor's controls): answer a view with back (the name of the level above) and the way back calls your onBack instead of leaving the page. /w opens on the page it was shut on with Escape.

The menu reads only what a row says. Anything a row does on the server is checked there as usual: ask exports.whip_core:HasDevTools(source).

RegisterDevPage(id, def)CLIENT

Adds your page to /w, or replaces the one you added under this id. Call it in Whip.register: whip_core forgets every page when it restarts. The page goes when your resource stops.

FieldTypeDescription
idstringLetters, digits, _ and -. Yours only: another resource's page with the same id is another page
labelstringThe row in /w and the page's title
descstring|nilThe line under the list while your row is picked
rowsfunctionAnswers the rows on screen now: a list of rows, or { title, back, select, rows } for a level of your own (title replaces the label, back names the level above, select is the row id picked when the level first shows). Asked when the page opens, after every pick, and on RefreshDevPage
onSelectfunction(rowId)Enter (or a click) on a row. It must not wait: start a thread for anything that does, then call RefreshDevPage
onBackfunction|nilThe way back on a level that answered back: go up one
onOpen / onClosefunction|nilThe page came on screen, or left it (the way back, Escape, developer mode off)
Row fieldTypeDescription
idstring|numberWhat onSelect is handed. Every row but a note needs one
labelstringThe row's words
kindstring|nil'run' (default): does something once. 'toggle': a switch, lit by active. 'open': a chevron, into a level of yours. 'note': a line to read, never picked
activeboolean|nilA toggle's switch
descstring|nilThe line under the list while the row is picked
closeboolean|nilPicking the row shuts the menu after onSelect, the way Escape does (/w opens on your page again): for an action that should happen with the screen clear
iconstring|nilA glyph drawn before the label, by its name (the prompts' glyphs:'target', 'car', 'pin'...): an icon list, an objective's mark. A name whip does not have draws nothing
sepstringA group header instead of a row: { sep = 'Playback' }
-- client.lua: the café's page in /w, with a level for its menu
local open, level = false, 'top'

Whip.register(function()
    exports.whip_core:RegisterDevPage('cafe', {
        label = 'Café',
        desc  = 'Open or shut the café, restock it, and its menu.',
        rows = function()
            if level == 'menu' then
                return { title = 'Menu', back = 'Café', rows = {
                    { id = 'coffee', label = 'Coffee', desc = 'Puts a coffee in your pockets.' },
                    { id = 'muffin', label = 'Muffin', desc = 'Puts a muffin in your pockets.' },
                } }
            end
            return { select = 'menu', rows = {
                { label = open and 'The café is open' or 'The café is shut', kind = 'note' },
                { id = 'open', label = 'Open', kind = 'toggle', active = open },
                { id = 'restock', label = 'Restock', desc = 'Fills every shelf.' },
                { id = 'menu', label = 'Menu', kind = 'open' },
            } }
        end,
        onSelect = function(rowId)
            if rowId == 'open' then open = not open
            elseif rowId == 'menu' then level = 'menu'
            else TriggerServerEvent('mycafe:devAction', rowId) end   -- the server checks HasDevTools
        end,
        onBack = function() level = 'top' end,
    })
end)
Returns: true, or false, why (a bad id, no label, no rows or onSelect)
RefreshDevPage(id)CLIENT

Your rows changed without a pick (a list arrived from the server, something finished): whip_core asks rows again if your page is on screen, keeping the same row picked. Cheap to call when it is not.

RegisterNetEvent('mycafe:stockList', function(list)
    stock = list
    exports.whip_core:RefreshDevPage('cafe')
end)
Returns: true, or false, why (no page of yours has that id)
RemoveDevPage(id)CLIENT

Takes your page out of /w. Only needed while your resource keeps running: it goes by itself when your resource stops.

Returns: true, or false, why (no page of yours has that id)
RegisterDebugTool(id, def)CLIENT

A switch of your own among /w's debug tools, which show while its Debug row is on (whip's own are Player Stats Debug, Vehicle Stats Debug and Ground Items Debug; yours come after them, by label). onToggle(on) runs when it is switched, and with false when Debug or developer mode goes off; answer false to stay off. Turning it on asks the server again, as any dev tool does. Registering again under the same id replaces it. Call it inside Whip.register: whip_core keeps it in memory. It goes when your resource stops, and a whip_core restart stops yours first.

Whip.register(function()
    exports.whip_core:RegisterDebugTool('mine', {
        label    = 'My Debug',
        desc     = 'What my overlay shows.',
        onToggle = function(on) ShowMyOverlay(on) end,
    })
end)
FieldTypeDescription
labelstringIts row in /w (40 characters at most)
descstring?The line under the list while its row is picked
onTogglefunctiononToggle(on); answer false to stay off
Returns: true, or false, why
RemoveDebugTool(id)CLIENT

Takes your debug tool out of /w (it goes by itself when your resource stops). One that is on is not switched off: that is yours to do.

Returns: true, or false, why (no debug tool of yours has that id)
Whip.objectViewerOption(id, def)CLIENT

Add an option of your own to the Object Viewer's options, or change one: a line in the list G opens on what the viewer has picked out. It shows for the kinds you name, under a heading of your own in your colour. Picked, the list closes and your select runs on that developer's game, in a thread of its own, handed the thing. whip_autos' Open Whiplash is one. From @whip_core/lib/satellite.lua; call it at file scope.

FieldTypeDescription
labelstringThe option's line (48 letters at most)
kindsstring[]What it is for: vehicle, player, npc, object
whipboolean?true: only whip's own (a saved car, a player). false: only the game's (a street car, an NPC walking by). Left out: both
groupstring?The heading it goes under (24 letters); your resource's name when left out
tintstring?The heading's colour: blue, teal, green, amber, red, violet or slate (the default)
hintstring?What it does, in the line under the list while it is pointed at (160 letters)
selectfunctionselect(target). target is { kind, entity, netId, whip, vehicleId, serverId, model, name, coords = { x, y, z, heading } }

The id is '<your namespace>.<name>'. It shows to a developer with developer mode on, and to a Dungeon Master in Dungeon Mode (whose clicks open these options too), so anything your option asks of your server is checked there: exports.whip_core:HasDevTools(source), or the permission it needs.

-- client.lua
Whip.objectViewerOption('mycafe.refuel', {
    label = 'Fill the tank', group = 'My cafe', tint = 'amber', kinds = { 'vehicle' }, whip = true,
    hint = 'Fuel to full, for the cafe\'s delivery van.',
    select = function(target)
        TriggerServerEvent('mycafe:server:refuel', target.vehicleId)   -- yours; the server checks HasDevTools
    end,
})
Returns: true, or false when it is not an option (printed). whip_core's own answer is printed when it refuses one. Whip.removeObjectViewerOption(id) takes one away; it goes by itself when your resource stops.

Weapon System

whip_gunny is whip's weapon system: guns, magazines, ammunition, melee weapons, throwables and the jerry can. It ships with WHIP and needs nothing set up: its items are in /whip → Economy → Items, ready to sell in shops or hand out. It is also the worked example of a resource built the way whip expects, and Learning from gunny says which parts to read. A resource that uses gunny adds dependency 'whip_gunny'.

How it works

Weapons are inventory items with state. A gun carries a serial number and the magazine in it; a magazine carries its own serial and a round count; a revolver or a pump shotgun carries its rounds itself. None of that state lives in gunny: it is whip_core's item metadata, saved with the inventory. gunny owns the rules, whip_core owns the data.

gun item ─ metadata ─┬─ serial          "AB12CD34EF56"
                     ├─ attachments     { muzzle = 'gunny_suppressor' }
                     ├─ attachmentMeta  { muzzle = { ... } }   each fitted attachment's own metadata, given back with it
                     └─ magazine ─┬─ item    'gunny_mag_rifle'
                                  ├─ serial  'GH78IJ90KL12'
                                  ├─ ammo    24
                                  └─ ...     the rest of the magazine's own metadata (its uid)
  • Drawing. Equip on a gun in the inventory tells the player's game to draw it, and the game asks the server, which records where the gun was drawn from and its serial. Its shots, throws and holster go by that record, never by a slot the client names. The moment the gun leaves its slot (dragged, stashed, handed over), the server puts it away.
  • Shooting. The game counts the rounds each frame fires and tells the server, which takes them from the metadata. The game's own count is only believed when it is lower: firing only lowers a count.
  • Reloading. R swaps in the fullest magazine carried, or loads loose rounds into a gun with no magazine (below). Firing stops the moment R is pressed and comes back when the reload is done (aiming stays), so every round fired came from the magazine that was in. A shotgun loaded a shell at a time can still fire to stop partway. From the press until the reload is done the gun cannot be put away or swapped for another (Finish reloading first), and R does nothing while a gun is being put away, so no magazine changes without its reload being played.
  • Loading magazines. Load Bullets on a magazine runs a bar on the server's clock, 300 ms a round, with the magazine and rounds in the player's hands for everyone nearby. Not in the water and not while falling: the bar will not start there, and stops if either begins, saying why (notWhile). Unload puts the rounds back in the pockets.
  • The magazine slot. Open on a gun shows its magazine, or its rounds, as one slot to drag into and out of (below).
  • The weapon bench. Attachments go on and come off there (below).

Magazines, or none

TypeDescriptionReload
Magazine-fedUses separate magazine items (pistol mags, rifle mags). Multiple compatible mags per weapon.R swaps in the fullest magazine carried
No magazine (magless)The rounds are in the gun: revolvers, the tube-fed and break-action shotguns, the launchers.R loads loose rounds carried, all at once. The pump shotgun, pump shotgun Mk II, sawed-off and combat shotgun load a shell at a time, stopped by firing or running (loopedReload).

Calibers

Ammunition is by caliber. Each caliber is an ammo item ('9mm' is 'ammo_9mm', a stack of loose rounds). A magazine takes one caliber's rounds, and a gun lists the magazines it takes. A weapon's or magazine's card shows its caliber as Ammo Type, under its serial.

The weapon bench

Attachments go on and come off at the weapon bench: E at it (A on a controller) with a gun in hand. An attachment is an item: fitting one takes it from the pockets, and taking it off gives it back. Each weapon lists what it takes, slot by slot (scope, muzzle, barrel, grip, flashlight), each a GTA component on that gun (items/attachments.lua). The bench's place, model and name are Config.WeaponBench in gunny's config.lua; enabled = false takes it away.

-- whip_gunny/config.lua
Config.WeaponBench = {
    enabled = true,
    coords  = vector4(-1069.5194, -1666.3589, 3.3856, 302.7092),   -- x, y, z and heading
    model   = `gr_prop_gr_bench_04b`,
    label   = 'Weapon Bench',
}

Controls

KeyControllerAction
RBReload (a magazine swap, or loose rounds into a gun with none). On foot only: in a vehicle the seat reloads by itself (below)
GLB + BCheck the ammo, or, with sticky bombs out, set them all off (drawn or not). On a controller it is a whip button action, so players can move it in the pause menu's Controller screen.
E at the benchAUse the weapon bench

R and G are key mappings (Reload Weapon, Check Ammo / Detonate Sticky Bombs), so players can rebind them in GTA's settings. On a controller, B on foot reloads while a gun is drawn, and players can move it on the Controller screen.

In a vehicle

Shooting from a seat is GTA's drive-by. Shots and ammo count the same as on foot.

WhatHow
ReloadAutomatic, and the only way: firing the last round reloads, and so does pulling the trigger on an empty gun. R (B on a controller) does nothing in a seat, silently, so a gun the seat cannot fire is not swapped by hand. A reload in a seat takes at least the weapon's reloadTime.
G / LB + BCheck ammo, as on foot
RB (controller)Double tap to start aiming; aiming stays on. Double tap again to stop: that double tap fires nothing. While aiming, hold RB to fire: it fires once held for a tenth of a second, and a tap fires nothing, so a stray tap never shoots. On an empty gun the same hold reloads. Not aiming, RB is the handbrake as usual and never fires. LB never aims, because LB + A is talk.

The magazine slot

Open on a gun shows one slot: the magazine in it, or, for a gun with no magazine, its rounds as a stack. Drag a magazine in or out, or rounds in and out of a revolver or a shotgun. With the gun drawn, a change plays a short reload on the gun in the hand. It is a whip_core panel item, so whip_core does the move: server/magpanel.lua is the whole declaration, and the panel guide's worked example walks through it.

The jerry can

jerry_can is GTA's petrol can, and its ammunition is the fuel in it (metadata fuel, 0-100%). Pour it on the ground and light the trail. Pouring it into a car and filling it at a pump are whip_fuel's, through the item's fuelCapacity. A new can is empty.

Throwables

Grenades, sticky bombs, proximity mines, pipe bombs, molotovs, BZ gas, tear gas, hand flares, snowballs, acid packages and newspapers. Each is a stack, and the hand holds the whole stack: GTA throws, cooks and sets them off, and each one thrown is taken from the stack. G (LB + B) sets off every sticky bomb the player has out. The acid package and the newspaper need a recent game build.

Adding weapons

Each item is one entry in one of gunny's item files, and each file's header lists every field and its default: items/weapons.lua, items/magazines.lua, items/calibers.lua and items/attachments.lua. Restart gunny (restart whip_gunny in the server console) and the item exists, with its menu, card and settings. An entry missing what it needs (a gun with no magazines, a caliber not in items/calibers.lua) is left out as gunny starts, and the server console says which and why, on a line starting [GUNNY] WARNING. To add guns without editing gunny's files, so an update never touches them, use a weapon pack.

-- items/weapons.lua: a gun
['gunny_yourgun'] = {
    weight = 2.5,
    description = 'Shown on the item card.',
    hash = `WEAPON_YOURGUN`,
    label = 'Your Gun',
    prop = 'w_pi_yourgun',                 -- its model lying on the ground
    caliber = '9mm',                       -- a key of items/calibers.lua
    compatibleMags = { 'gunny_mag_yourgun' },
    reloadTime = 1000,
    defaultClipComponent = `COMPONENT_YOURGUN_CLIP_01`,
},

-- items/magazines.lua: its magazine
['gunny_mag_yourgun'] = {
    weight = 0.15,
    label = 'Your Gun Magazine',
    prop = 'w_pi_yourgun_mag1',
    caliber = '9mm',
    capacity = 12,
},

A gun with no magazine has magless = true and internalCapacity (the rounds it holds) instead of compatibleMags; loopedReload = true loads it a shell at a time, which needs looped reload animations in its weapon meta. A melee weapon needs only weight, description, hash, label, prop and melee = true. An item's icon is html/img/items/<key>.webp (or .png).

Where the names come from. hash is GTA's name for the weapon, in backticks: whip_core lists every one in shared/gta_weapons.lua (WEAPON_PISTOL_MK2, Pistol Mk II), and shared/gta_weapon_models.lua gives each its model, which is what prop takes (w_pi_pistolmk2). defaultClipComponent is the GTA magazine shown on the gun, COMPONENT_<GUN>_CLIP_01 for most (gunny's own guns in items/weapons.lua show each one), and nothing checks it as gunny starts. What a gun must have: hash, a caliber from items/calibers.lua, and compatibleMags naming magazines in items/magazines.lua (or magless = true with internalCapacity). The rest have defaults, and each file's header says them.

A magazine's size, and a gun's reload time and rounds, can also be changed per item in /whip → Economy → Items, without touching the files. A value set there wins over the file, and its Reset goes back to the file's. A magazine already holding more than a new, smaller size keeps its rounds until they are fired or unloaded. A gun with no magazine holding more than its new size gives the extra rounds back to the pockets the next time it is drawn, never going below the item file's own size.

Debugging

With developer mode on, /w → Debug → Gunny Debug shows the drawn weapon's rounds as the game, gunny and the server each count them, the shot reports sent and answered, and the magazines carried. While anyone has it on, the server prints gunny's debug lines too. /gunnydebugreset zeroes the counters, and /gunnydebugserver says what is drawn: everyone's at the server console, your own in game. Lines starting [GUNNY] WARNING always print: a write that failed, or a change that was undone (and, when even the undo failed, what was lost).

A gun that will not reload

What the player is told says why. Most often the magazine carried is empty, or is not one the gun takes: a gun's magazines are its compatibleMags in items/weapons.lua, and a magazine's card shows its Ammo Type.

The player seesWhy, and what to do
No magazines for this weapon on youNone of the magazines this gun takes is in their pockets (another gun's does not count): carry one
All your magazines for this weapon are emptyFill one: Load Bullets on the magazine, with its caliber's rounds in the pockets
No ammunition for this weapon on youA gun with no magazine (a revolver, most shotguns) loads loose rounds: carry its caliber's
Already fully loadedNothing to do
No room for the old magazineThe old one had nowhere to go, not even the ground, so the reload was undone: make room
Finish reloading firstPutting the gun away or drawing another during a reload: it waits for the reload
Nothing at allR does nothing in a vehicle (the seat reloads by itself: the last round fired, or the trigger on an empty gun), with a melee weapon (R is its light attack), with a screen or a bar up, or while the gun is being put away

And from Load Bullets on a magazine: Magazine is full; No 9mm ammunition available (no rounds of its caliber carried); You cannot do that while swimming, … underwater or … falling; Loading cancelled (stopped before a round went in: rounds already in stay).

From your resource

A gun is an ordinary item, so whip_core's inventory tools work on it: AddItem gives one with a fresh serial, empty, and RemoveItem takes one when any will do. GiveWeapon is for the options (a magazine in it, loaded, a serial you choose), and answers the serial it gave. Which gun a player holds is whip_core's GetHeldItem(source) on the server, with its serial and rounds in the metadata. A resource calling gunny adds dependency 'whip_gunny' to its fxmanifest.

-- Server: a "shots fired" call, at most one a minute per shooter
local lastAlert = {}
AddEventHandler('whip_gunny:weapon:fired', function(e)
    local now = GetGameTimer()
    if e.coords and now - (lastAlert[e.source] or 0) > 60000 then
        lastAlert[e.source] = now
        AlertPolice(e.coords, e.item)   -- your own
    end
end)

-- Client: which weapon is drawn?
local w = exports.whip_gunny:GetDrawnWeapon()
if w and w.kind == 'gun' then --[[ ... ]] end

Give a gun, and take that one back

An armory, a rental, a mission's kit: note the serials you hand out, and take back those, not whatever carbine they carry. FindItemByMeta finds an item by its serial, and StoreTake takes it out of that slot. A gun taken while it is drawn is put away first, and the magazine in it goes with it. A spare magazine they have put into a gun is inside that gun, not in the pockets, so its serial finds nothing until it comes out.

-- Server (dependency 'whip_gunny'): an armory's issue and return
local issued = {}   -- [source] = the serials handed out

local function issue(source)
    local ok, where, gunSerial = exports.whip_gunny:GiveWeapon(source, 'gunny_carbinerifle', { loaded = true }, 'armory issue')
    if not ok then return false, where end
    local _, _, magSerial = exports.whip_gunny:GiveMagazine(source, 'gunny_mag_carbinerifle', 999, 'armory issue')   -- past its size: full
    issued[source] = { gunSerial, magSerial }
    return true
end

-- Exactly what was issued, wherever it is in their pockets; a carbine of their own stays
local function takeBack(source)
    for _, serial in ipairs(issued[source] or {}) do
        local at = exports.whip_core:FindItemByMeta('serial', serial)
        if at and at.kind == 'player' and at.id == source then
            exports.whip_core:StoreTake(at, 1, { reason = 'returned to the armory' })
        end
    end
    issued[source] = nil
end

Every shot fired

whip_gunny:weapon:fired comes each time the server takes rounds off a gun, not once a bullet: automatic fire is counted a frame at a time, so shots can be more than 1, and a shot the server missed is taken a few seconds later from the game's own count. coords is where the shooter stands as the server takes them, and nil once they have gone. It stays on the server (it is not a network event), so it costs little, but a handler of yours runs as often as anyone fires: keep it short.

-- Server: a shell casing for every round
AddEventHandler('whip_gunny:weapon:fired', function(e)
    if not e.coords then return end   -- they left before the server took the shot
    for _ = 1, e.shots do
        DropCasing(e.coords, e.item, e.serial)   -- your own
    end
end)

The rounds on your HUD

There is no event for each shot on the player's game, and a HUD needs none: read GetDrawnWeapon a few times a second while a gun is out, started by whip_gunny:weapon:drawn and ended by :holstered. Its count is live: shots, reloads and the magazine slot change it.

-- Client: the drawn gun's rounds on your HUD, read while a gun is out
local following = 0   -- each draw and holster bumps it, which ends the loop before

AddEventHandler('whip_gunny:weapon:drawn', function(w)
    following = following + 1
    local mine = following
    if w.kind ~= 'gun' then return end
    CreateThread(function()
        while following == mine do
            local gun = exports.whip_gunny:GetDrawnWeapon()
            if not gun then break end
            ShowAmmo(gun.ammo, gun.capacity)   -- your own; capacity is nil with no magazine in
            Wait(150)
        end
    end)
end)

AddEventHandler('whip_gunny:weapon:holstered', function()
    following = following + 1
    HideAmmo()   -- your own
end)

No weapons here

A no-weapons zone, handcuffs, jail: block the player's hands with whip_core's BlockHands, with only = 'weapons' for weapons alone. For a place, block them on the player's game as they walk in (the client's card does it for a hospital zone); for one player, from the server (the server's card: jail, an arrest). While it lasts, gunny refuses a draw and shows the block's label, and a gun already out is put away, with nothing said. UnblockHands with the same id ends it.

-- Server: weapons away while they are in your jail
exports.whip_core:BlockHands(source, 'myjail', { only = 'weapons', label = 'No weapons in here' })

-- ... and back when they are let out
exports.whip_core:UnblockHands(source, 'myjail')

A zone's own Weapons away rule (/whip → World → Zones) works on GTA's weapons, not through gunny: for gunny's guns, use BlockHands.

Weapon packs

Add guns from a resource of your own, without editing gunny: it streams the weapons (their metas and models, in its own fxmanifest), ships their icons as html/img/items/<item>.webp in its files, and registers each item in the shape of gunny's items/weapons.lua and items/magazines.lua, magazines first, in a file both sides load. Gunny takes them in as its own: their menus, magazine slot, Items page settings and bench attachments. A pack's gun may take gunny's own magazines and calibers. When the pack stops they leave gunny (players keep the items, which work again when it is back).

Each export answers true, or false and why. A name gunny or whip_core already uses (one of gunny's items or rounds, another pack's, or another resource's item) is refused. When whip_core refuses an item gunny had taken in before it was up, the console says so and gunny leaves it out, along with a pack gun whose only magazine it was. An attachment kind (medium, holographic) that no item in items/attachments.lua has is said in the console, as it can never be fitted.

-- fxmanifest.lua: the guns themselves, streamed as gunny streams its own
fx_version 'cerulean'
game 'gta5'

shared_script '@whip_gunny/lib/pack.lua'
shared_script 'gunny.lua'

-- components before the weapons that list them
data_file 'WEAPONCOMPONENTSINFO_FILE' 'data/mypack_weaponcomponents.meta'
data_file 'WEAPON_METADATA_FILE' 'data/mypack_weaponarchetypes.meta'     -- which models and textures
data_file 'WEAPON_ANIMATIONS_FILE' 'data/mypack_weaponanimations.meta'
data_file 'WEAPONINFO_FILE' 'data/mypack_weapons.meta'                   -- the guns: damage, range, clip

files {
    'data/*.meta',
    'html/img/items/*.webp',
}
-- the models and their textures (w_ar_mypack_m4.ydr and .ytd) go in the stream folder, which needs no line here

-- gunny.lua: run when gunny is up, and again each time it starts
Gunny.register(function()
    exports.whip_gunny:RegisterMagazine('mypack_mag_m4', {
        weight = 0.2, label = 'M4 Magazine', prop = 'w_ar_mypack_m4_mag', caliber = '5.56x45', capacity = 30,
    })
    exports.whip_gunny:RegisterWeapon('mypack_m4', {
        weight = 3.2, label = 'M4', description = 'A carbine.', hash = `WEAPON_MYPACK_M4`,
        prop = 'w_ar_mypack_m4', caliber = '5.56x45', compatibleMags = { 'mypack_mag_m4' }, reloadTime = 2200,
        attachments = { scope = { medium = `COMPONENT_MYPACK_M4_SCOPE` } },
    })
end)

The weapon files are GTA's own kinds, the ones an add-on weapon comes with: gunny's own fxmanifest.lua streams its add-on guns the same way, and is a full example (clip sets, sounds and patches to Rockstar's weapons too). Gunny.register runs whatever order the resources start in, so the pack needs no dependency. A pack's gun needs what one in items/weapons.lua needs (Adding weapons, above); attachments and defaultClipComponent can be left out. To try one, give it loaded from a test command of yours: exports.whip_gunny:GiveWeapon(source, 'mypack_m4', { loaded = true }). While you build the pack, print what each RegisterWeapon and RegisterMagazine answers: a refused entry says why.

To list the guns in whip's weapon lists too (the Director, the Object Viewer), call Whip.weapons from @whip_core/lib/satellite.lua in the pack.

Learning from gunny

gunny is the worked example of a resource built on whip. If you are writing your own, these are the parts to read: each is a pattern whip expects, and gunny uses it everywhere. The code is in the whip_gunny folder, and Where to look maps it, by file and by what you want to do.

New to whip? Your First Resource builds a small one from an empty folder: the fxmanifest, an item, a message from the game. gunny is far bigger than a resource needs to be, so read it for the patterns, not the size.

Every client message is declared

Everything a game may send gunny's server is a SecureEvent or SecureCallback. The rate limit, and the type and range of each parameter, are stated once, and whip_core checks them before the handler runs. Nothing on gunny's server listens to a raw net event. In your own resource it is the plain call, inside Whip.register:

-- server.lua: your resource
Whip.register(function()
    exports.whip_core:SecureEvent('myguns:server:shotFired', {
        whileDead = true,                   -- a round fired as the player dies is still spent
        rateLimit = 15, burst = 30,         -- about 66 shots a second at most
        params = { {'shotsFired', 'int', 1, 10, 1} },
    }, function(source, player, shotsFired)
        -- ...
    end)
end)

'int' is chosen here on purpose. A count of money or items should be 'amount', which refuses anything outside its range. A shot count should not be refused: the rounds were fired, and refusing the message would hand them back. So 'int' holds it to 1-10 instead (9999 counts as 10, a negative as 1, something that is not a number as 1), one message can never empty a magazine, and a burst of more than ten in one frame is caught up a few seconds later from the game's own count.

gunny itself writes the same call through two small helpers in server/main.lua, RegisterGunnyEvent and RegisterGunnyCallback. They exist for one reason your resource does not have: a weapon pack changes which items gunny's 'slot' params accept, so gunny keeps a list of every declaration to make again. Both take the full name, as SecureEvent does:

-- whip_gunny/server/shooting.lua: the same declaration, through gunny's helper
RegisterGunnyEvent('whip_gunny:server:shotFired', {
    whileDead = true,
    rateLimit = 15, burst = 30,
    params = { {'shotsFired', 'int', 1, 10, 1} },
}, function(source, player, shotsFired)
    -- the server's own record of the drawn gun, never a slot the client names
    local slotData, equipped = GunnyDrawnWeapon(source)
    -- ...
end)

Events are whip_gunny:server:<what> from a client and whip_gunny:client:<what> to one, and callbacks whip_gunny:<name>. For an id that must be exact, the 'id' type refuses instead of holding it in range.

Declare inside Whip.register

whip_core keeps items, callbacks, panels and hooks in memory. Whatever you declare inside Whip.register (from @whip_core/lib/satellite.lua) is declared once whip_core is ready, whichever of the two starts first. gunny's items, its callbacks and events, its magazine slots and its hooks are all declared there.
