With dependency 'whip_core', a whip_core restart stops gunny first and starts it again after, so gunny starts fresh and has nothing to let go of (the satellite helper). gunny also keeps a list of its declarations to make again when a weapon pack changes its item lists; most resources need no such list.

-- fxmanifest.lua
shared_scripts { '@whip_core/lib/satellite.lua' }   -- Whip.register, Whip.call
dependency 'whip_core'                                   -- stopped and started again with whip_core

-- server/items.lua: the items, their magazine slots and right-click actions, declared once whip_core is up
Whip.register(registerWithWhip)

Name the item the player clicked with a 'slot' param

A client naming one of its own items sends its slot, and the handler declares a 'slot' param. whip_core checks the pocket is the player's, the slot is in range and holds the right kind of item, and hands over a copy: { addr, item, amount, metadata }. addr is what every whip_core slot call takes. An item that moved after the player pressed is refused with words they can read ("That item is not there any more").

-- server/magazines.lua: UnloadBullets asks through here
RegisterGunnyCallback('whip_gunny:unloadBulletsFromMag', { params = {
    { 'mag',   'slot', { item = GunnyMagazineItems } },   -- one of the player's own magazines
    { 'count', 'int',  1, 9999, 9999 },      -- 'int' on purpose: left out, it means all of them
} }, function(source, player, mag, count)
    local ok, left, unloaded = GunnyUnloadMagazine(source, mag.addr, count)
    if not ok then return false, left end
    return true, { left = left, unloaded = unloaded }
end)

The game learns the slot from the server first. A right-click option on an item (RegisterContextAction) is handed the item's address, addr, and can tell the game addr.slot and addr.sub (the pocket); the game names them back as { sub, slot } when it asks. When the right-click itself does the work, there is no trip at all: Load Bullets and Unload run on the server in their action, with the addr they were given.

-- server/items.lua: the right-click is handed the item's address, and the player's game is told its slot
exports.whip_core:RegisterContextAction('whip_gunny:equip_weapon', function(source, player, slotData, addr)
    TriggerClientEvent('whip_gunny:client:useWeapon', source, addr.slot, addr.sub)
end)

-- client/weapons.lua: the game names that slot back when it asks, and the 'slot' param checks it
local ok, drawn = Whip.call('Callback', 'whip_gunny:equipWeapon', { sub = pocket or 'player', slot = slot })

Names are server-wide and first come, first served: start every action, event and callback with your resource's name, as gunny's do. An action's name is at most 32 characters.

Declare a panel, do not handle one

The magazine slot (server/magpanel.lua) says how the slot reads the gun's metadata and writes it back, and what may go in (onValidate). whip_core performs the move, and onChange runs once it has landed. One declaration covers both kinds of gun: a magazine for one, a count of rounds for the other. The panel guide's worked example is this file.

gunny needs read and write because a gun keeps its magazine in its own shape. A panel that only holds items (bait on a rod) needs neither: allowedItems says what may go in, and whip_core keeps the contents in the item's metadata.slots. Either way the item must not stack (stack = false in RegisterItem), and needs an action that opens it: its defaultAction, or action in the declaration.

Take before you give, and check every answer

A reload takes the new magazine out of the pockets before it gives the old one back, and unloading lowers the magazine's count before it gives the rounds. A step that fails gives back what was taken (GunnyGiveBack), and says so in the console when even that fails. Every whip_core answer is checked; a call that can wait (AddItem, a bar) goes through Whip.call, which answers instead of throwing if whip_core stops meanwhile, and so does everything the undo after it calls. GunnyStillThere (server/main.lua) reads the slot again after the wait, so the undo lands on the thing it took from and not on whatever sits in that slot now.

-- server/magazines.lua: unloading
meta.ammo = currentAmmo - toUnload                            -- take: the magazine lowered first
if not exports.whip_core:SetItemMetadata(magAddr, meta) then
    return false, 'Could not unload: the magazine was not changed'
end
local added = Whip.call('AddItem', source, caliber.ammoItem, toUnload,   -- then give
    nil, { reason = 'unloaded from a magazine', noDrop = true })
if not added then
    -- no room: the rounds go back into the magazine, if it is still the one lowered
end

A bar the server times

Anything handed out at the end of a bar is timed by the server, not the player's game: loading a magazine runs the server Progress through Whip.call, and loads only once it answers true. A finish sooner than the bar could fill is refused ('too fast'), so a modified game cannot skip it. It waits for the whole bar, so it runs in a thread of its own, from a SecureEvent or a right-click action, never a SecureCallback (the game gives up on one after 10 seconds). After the wait, read the item again: it may have moved.

-- server/magazines.lua: the load, in its own thread (a SecureCallback cannot wait past the game's 10 s)
local done, why = Whip.call('Progress', source, {
    label     = ('Loading %d rounds into magazine'):format(plan.toLoad),
    duration  = plan.toLoad * MS_PER_ROUND,
    canCancel = true,
    anim      = MAG_LOAD_BAR.anim,
    disable   = MAG_LOAD_BAR.disable,    -- walking only, no driving
    notWhile  = MAG_LOAD_BAR.notWhile,   -- not swimming, not falling
})
if not done then return false, why end   -- 'cancelled', 'refused', 'too fast', 'whip_core stopped'...
-- the bar really ran its length: read the magazine again (it may have moved), then load it

Using an item at the end of a bar is simpler still: give RegisterUseHandler a table (a use with a progress bar), and whip runs the bar, checks the item is still there, takes it and calls your onComplete. consume = false keeps it: a fishing rod, a tool.

Go by the server's own record

A drawn gun's shots, throws and holster go by where the server saw it drawn, and its serial, never by a slot the client names (GunnyDrawnWeapon, server/weapons.lua). Every new gun and magazine is given its serial as it is made (RegisterItemDefaultMeta, server/items.lua), which is how gunny knows it is still the same one. An item of yours that must be found again (a rod, a key) needs an id of its own in its metadata the same way: whip's uid is only given the first time the item is logged. A count the client sends is only taken when it is lower than the server's, and a count sent for a magazine that has since been swapped is ignored (GunnyCountChanged).

Calling whip_core: straight, or through Whip.call

On the server, gunny calls an export straight when it answers at once (GetItemAt, SetItemMetadata, StoreTake) inside a handler whip_core runs, as whip_core is up then. It goes through Whip.call for a call that can wait (AddItem, Progress), for everything after such a wait (an undo), and outside whip_core's handlers (a console command). On the client, exports are called straight inside Whip.register, in the one per-frame tick (started by a draw, it ends when nothing is drawn, and gunny puts the gun away the moment whip_core stops), and behind Whip.isReady() for a call that answers at once. Everything else goes through Whip.call, which answers false, why instead of throwing when whip_core is down. Its answer is checked wherever a refusal changes what happens next. Both rules are written at the top of server/main.lua and client/main.lua.

-- Inside a SecureEvent whip_core runs: answers at once, so called straight
local slotData = exports.whip_core:GetItemAt(addr)

-- Can wait (pockets full: it goes to the ground), so through Whip.call, and the answer checked
local where, why = Whip.call('AddItem', source, 'ammo_9mm', 12, nil, { reason = 'unloaded from a magazine' })
if not where then return false, why end

Where to look

Read it in this order: server/main.lua (how gunny declares what a client may ask, and the calling rule), server/items.lua (its items registered with whip_core), server/weapons.lua (the drawn-gun record), server/magpanel.lua (a declared panel), then client/main.lua (the client's rule and the tick). Every file starts with a few lines saying what it does.

FileWhat is in it
config.luaThe settings: the weapon bench
items/*.luaEvery caliber, weapon, magazine and attachment, each file headed by its fields
shared/catalog.luaThe lookups into the items, and what every item must have, on both sides
shared/packs.lua, lib/pack.luaWeapon packs: RegisterWeapon, RegisterMagazine, and the pack's helper Gunny.register
shared/whip_weapons.luagunny's own guns in whip_core's weapon lists (the Director, the Object Viewer)
server/main.luaDeclaring callbacks and events, the drawn-weapon record, the shared helpers, the calling rule
server/items.luaEvery item registered with whip_core; GiveWeapon and GiveMagazine
server/weapons.luaDrawing and putting away; the count version
server/magpanel.luaA gun's magazine slot, a declared panel
server/magazines.luaLoading and unloading magazines
server/reload.luaReloading: a magazine swap, loose rounds, a shell at a time
server/shooting.lua, server/throwables.luaShots and the ammo sync; each throw taken from the stack
server/attachments.luaThe weapon bench
server/debug.luaGunny Debug's server half
client/main.luaAsking the server, the drawn weapon, the one per-frame tick, the calling rule; IsWeaponDrawn, GetDrawnWeapon
client/ammo.luaThe one place the ped's ammunition is written

Gunny Exports (whip_gunny)

Resource: exports.whip_gunny: requires dependency 'whip_gunny' in your fxmanifest.lua. See Weapon System guide for an overview.
GiveWeapon(source, weaponName, overrides, reason) SERVER

Give a player a weapon with fresh metadata and a new serial, set up as you say. Rounds are held to what the gun or the magazine holds.

ParamTypeDescription
sourcenumberThe player's server id
weaponNamestringThe weapon item ('gunny_pistol')
overridestable|nilserial; attachments ({ [slot] = attachment item }); a gun with magazines: magazine (a magazine item it takes) with ammo rounds in it; a gun without: ammo; either: loaded = true fills it (with its first magazine when none is named); the jerry can: fuel, 0-100; a throwable: amount
reasonstring|nilWhy they got it, for the activity log ('shop purchase'), as AddItem takes
-- Loaded, ready to use
exports.whip_gunny:GiveWeapon(source, 'gunny_pistol', { loaded = true })

-- A serial you chose, with an extended magazine holding 10
exports.whip_gunny:GiveWeapon(source, 'gunny_pistol', {
    serial = 'LSPD00000042',
    magazine = 'gunny_mag_pistol_extended', ammo = 10,
})
Returns: true, where, serial: where is 'inventory', or 'ground' at their feet when it did not fit, as AddItem does; serial finds it again with FindItemByMeta('serial', serial) (give and take back), and is nil for a throwable, a stack with none. Or false, reason: an unknown weapon or magazine, a magazine the gun does not take, an attachment it does not take in that slot, or AddItem's own refusal (a player not loaded)
GiveMagazine(source, magName, ammo, reason) SERVER

Give a player a magazine with rounds in it, held to what it holds.

ParamTypeDescription
sourcenumberThe player's server id
magNamestringThe magazine item ('gunny_mag_pistol')
ammonumber|nilRounds in it: none is empty, and any number past its size fills it (its size can be changed on the Items page)
reasonstring|nilWhy they got it, for the activity log
exports.whip_gunny:GiveMagazine(source, 'gunny_mag_pistol', 999)   -- full, whatever its size
Returns: true, where, serial ('inventory' or 'ground', and the magazine's own serial), as GiveWeapon; or false, reason: an unknown magazine, or AddItem's own refusal
RegisterWeapon(item, def) / RegisterMagazine(item, def) SERVERCLIENT

A weapon pack's gun or magazine, on both sides, inside Gunny.register (@whip_gunny/lib/pack.lua). def is an entry of gunny's items/weapons.lua or items/magazines.lua, checked as gunny's own are; a weapon may add attachments ({ [slot] = { [kind] = component } }). Register its magazines first. The same pack registering again replaces its own.

Returns: true, or false, reason: a field the item needs, an unknown caliber or magazine, a name of gunny's own or another pack's

Gunny events

One table each, by whip's naming rule. Listen with AddEventHandler.

EventSidePayload
whip_gunny:weapon:drawnServer{ source, item, kind, serial, slot, pocket }: kind is 'gun', 'melee', 'throwable' or 'fuelCan'
whip_gunny:weapon:holsteredServer{ source, item, serial, slot, pocket, reason }, once however it went: reason is 'holstered', 'moved' (it left its slot), 'replaced', 'logout' or 'dropped'
whip_gunny:weapon:firedServer{ source, item, serial, shots, ammo, coords }, each time the server takes rounds off a drawn gun: a frame of fire, or a shot it missed, caught up a few seconds later. shots is how many (more than 1 in automatic fire), ammo what is left, coords where the shooter is then, or nil once they have gone (every shot fired)
whip_gunny:weapon:drawnClientThe GetDrawnWeapon() table
whip_gunny:weapon:holsteredClient{ item, slot, pocket }

A police alert, evidence carrying the serial, a Director card on a draw: listen to these rather than watching the ped. A gun's serial is found with whip_core's FindItemByMeta('serial', serial). On the player's game there is no event for each shot: a HUD reads GetDrawnWeapon while a gun is out (the rounds on your HUD).

Gunny Client (whip_gunny)

IsWeaponDrawn() CLIENT

Is one of gunny's weapons in the player's hands? To follow it rather than ask, listen for whip_gunny:weapon:drawn / :holstered.

if exports.whip_gunny:IsWeaponDrawn() then return end   -- not with a gun out
Returns: boolean
GetDrawnWeapon() CLIENT

The weapon in the player's hands, as a copy: { item, label, kind, slot, pocket, serial, ammo, capacity, magazine, attachments }, or nil. kind is 'gun', 'melee', 'throwable' or 'fuelCan'. ammo is by kind: a gun's rounds, a throwable's stack, the jerry can's petrol as GTA counts it (0 to 4500, not the item's 0-100%), and 0 for a melee weapon. capacity is the most a gun holds: its magazine's size, or the rounds a gun with no magazine takes; nil with no magazine in, and for anything else. magazine is the magazine's item name ('gunny_mag_pistol'), or nil. Read it as often as you need: the count is kept live as shots, reloads and the magazine slot change it (a HUD).

local w = exports.whip_gunny:GetDrawnWeapon()
if w and w.kind == 'gun' and w.ammo == 0 then
    exports.whip_core:Notify(('Your %s is empty'):format(w.label), 'info')
end
Returns: table|nil
DrawWeapon(slot, pocket) CLIENT

Draw the weapon in a pocket slot, with its animation; another drawn one is put away first. Waits: call it from a thread. To put a weapon away, call whip_core's FreeHands(), which empties the hands of whatever is in them. During a reload (from the press, while the server answers, not only while the animation plays) it answers false, and the gun stays out until the reload ends (a death, or hands blocked by BlockHands, still put it away at once).

ParamTypeDescription
slotnumberThe slot
pocketstring|nil'player' (none) or 'accessory'
local ok, why = exports.whip_gunny:DrawWeapon(3)
Returns: true (drawn, or it already was), or false, reason: the hands blocked, a reload under way, the server refused
There is no client export for opening a weapon's magazine panel, and there does not need to be. gunny declares the magazine and chamber as panel items, so the whip_gunny:open_weapon context action on the weapon opens them and whip_core does the rest: the reading, the validation, the persistence and the client sync. Right-clicking a weapon and choosing Open is the whole interface. See whip_gunny/server/magpanel.lua for the declaration.
LoadBullets(slot, pocket) CLIENT

Load the magazine in a pocket slot with as many rounds as fit and the player carries, behind the server's bar, 300 ms a round; the player is told how it went. Waits until the load ends: call it from a thread. One at a time, so a script that loads every magazine calls it for each in turn.

ParamTypeDescription
slotnumberThe magazine's slot
pocketstring|nil'player' (none) or 'accessory'
for _, slot in ipairs(myMagazineSlots) do   -- your own list
    local ok, why = exports.whip_gunny:LoadBullets(slot)
    if not ok and why ~= 'Magazine is full' then break end   -- out of rounds, or stopped
end
Returns: true, rounds loaded (a load stopped part way keeps what went in), or false, reason: 'Busy' (another bar is up), 'Magazine is full', no rounds carried, 'Loading cancelled'
UnloadBullets(slot, pocket, count) CLIENT

Empty the magazine in a pocket slot into the player's pockets as rounds, or count of them. The player is told how it went. Waits for the server: call it from a thread.

ParamTypeDescription
slotnumberThe magazine's slot
pocketstring|nil'player' (none) or 'accessory'
countnumber|nilHow many (none: all)
local ok, unloaded = exports.whip_gunny:UnloadBullets(4)
Returns: true, rounds unloaded, or false, reason: it is empty, no room for the rounds
ApplyWeaponAttachments(ped, hash, item, attachments) CLIENT

Fit a gun's attachments on any ped holding it (an NPC, a display): attachments as the gun's metadata has them, { [slot] = attachment item }, turned into the GTA components that gun takes. The ped must hold the weapon first.

GiveWeaponToPed(npc, `WEAPON_PISTOL`, 12, false, true)
exports.whip_gunny:ApplyWeaponAttachments(npc, `WEAPON_PISTOL`, 'gunny_pistol', { muzzle = 'gunny_suppressor' })
Returns: nothing

Rope System

whip_rope is a physics rope. Players carry it as an item (rope), tie it to cars, props and the map where they look, tow with it and hang off it. It ships with WHIP and needs nothing set up. Other resources make ropes of their own from a script: whip_fuel's pump hose is one (Rope Exports). Learning from rope says which parts of its code to read.

Using a rope

ToHow
Put one outUse the Rope item. One end is in your hand.
Tie the end you holdLook at a car, a prop or the map (a wall, a rock, the ground) within reach and press the prompt's key. You then hold the other end, if it was lying loose.
Put it down, let it go, coil it upThe wheel (F1, or the wheel's button on a controller). Coiling takes 3 seconds and puts the rope in your pockets.
Pick up or untie an endThe prompt on the end.
Hang onThe prompt on the rope. Jump lets go. A shot knocks a hanging player off, unhurt.

Holding an end you walk or jog, but never sprint (a setting). You pull by hand, gently: walk a metre past the rope's easy stretch and it leaves your hands. If the other end is tied to a car driving away, you fall and are dragged behind it for a few seconds.

How it pulls

A slack rope pulls nothing. Taut, it stretches easily up to 15% past its length, then harder: a car that cannot hold it is pulled back, and a strong one drags it with effort. Both ends feel the same pull, so a light car moves more than a heavy truck. A towed car nobody drives rolls freely.

How it works

The server keeps each rope's two ends (held, put down, tied to a car, a prop or a spot on the map, or loose) and who hangs off it. Every player's game near the rope works out the rest, and all of them see the same rope. A towed car follows the car pulling it at once, at any ping.

SettingsServer owners

/whip → Settings → Rope has the rules (who may handle a rope, keys to tie, tying to the map, reach), the length and node count, ropes per player, what a rope bumps into, and hanging and holding. How it pulls, moves and looks is in whip_rope's config.lua, each setting explained there. A rope keeps the length and node count it was made with: a change counts for ropes put out after it.

A player who leaves with ropes out gets them back as items at their next login. What is owed is kept on disk, so a restart loses none. With Config.Rules.AnyoneCanHandle on (the default), anyone can pick up, untie or coil up anyone's rope, and coiling gives the item to whoever coils it.

Ropes in the Director

whip_rope adds a Ropes group to the Director's cards, and two goals. A run's ropes are found by name (rope unless a scenario makes more than one), and they go when the run ends, a Test's too.

CardWhat it does
Make a RopeA rope with each end tied to a placed car (its front, back or middle), prop or spot, in the player's hand, or lying loose. Its length, and whether players may pick it up and hang off it
Move a Rope EndTies one end somewhere else, hands it to the player, or drops it
Change Rope RulesWhether players may pick it up and hang off it, from now on
Remove a RopeTakes it away; anyone hanging off it drops
Goal: Tie a RopeOn once a rope is tied to a placed car, prop or spot, or between two. Any rope counts, a player's own too, unless it asks for a rope the run made
Goal: Hang on a RopeOn once a run player hangs off a rope, for as long as it asks
When a Rope Is Pulled Too FarOn once a rope the run made is pulled past a stretch (35% past its length unless you set one), and it can snap

A rope ties to cars, props and spots, never to an NPC: Check says so. A prop that moves is tied to itself; one standing still, and a spot, are tied to the map where they stand.

Debugging

CommandWhat it does
/ropedebugThe overlay, for you alone: each rope's ends, its stretch and pull, and the rays it casts a second
/ropestatusWhat your game has, printed in F8
/ropesEvery rope out, printed in the server console
/clearropesTakes every rope in. Each owner gets theirs back (now, or at their next login). A resource's rope is removed and its resource told (whip_rope:ropeRemoved)

All four need developer mode on (/w); the server's two also run from the server console.

Learning from rope

Most of whip_rope is rope physics (client/physics.lua, client/collision.lua, client/contact.lua), which teaches nothing about whip. The parts worth reading are smaller: how the server checks what a game asks and puts it right, how it checks what a game tells it, how nothing a player owns is lost, and how a prompt follows where the player looks. For the patterns gunny shows (declaring inside Whip.register, calling whip_core straight or through Whip.call), see Learning from gunny.

The game acts first, the server corrects it

Picking up or tying an end changes the rope on the player's own game at once, so it feels instant at any ping, and then asks the server. The server checks it in a SecureEvent and tells every game, this one too. A refusal sends that game the rope as the server has it (Ropes.correct), and whip shows the player the reason. A request refused before the handler runs (the rate limit, a bad value) is put right the same way, through the schema's onReject. Every end change on a game goes through Rope.ApplyEnd, which skips an end that has not changed, so the server's echo of the player's own change does nothing.

-- client/interaction.lua: the end in the hand here at once, then the ask
Rope.ApplyEnd(rope, which, { type = 'held', heldBy = Rope.MyServerId() })
TriggerServerEvent('whip_rope:take', rope.serverRopeId, which)

-- server/main.lua: a refusal sends their game the rope as the server has it
local function refuse(source, ropeId, why)
    Ropes.correct(source, ropeId)
    return false, why                                 -- whip shows `why` to the player
end

local function onTake(source, _, ropeId, which)
    local rope = Ropes.all[ropeId]
    if not rope then return refuse(source, ropeId, 'That rope is gone') end
    if rope[which].type == 'held' then return refuse(source, ropeId, 'Someone is holding that end') end
    -- ... the other checks: theirs to handle, hands free, near enough
    rope[which] = { type = 'held', heldBy = source }
    Ropes.sendEnds(rope, which == 'origin', which == 'tail')   -- every game, this one too
end

-- server/main.lua, in its Whip.register block (written out): refused before the handler runs, put right too.
-- `raw` is what the game sent, not checked yet: made a number before it is used.
local function correctOnReject(src, _, raw)
    Ropes.correct(src, tonumber(type(raw) == 'table' and raw[1]))
end
exports.whip_core:SecureEvent('whip_rope:take', {
    rateLimit = 150, burst = 6,
    onReject = correctOnReject,
    params = { { 'ropeId', 'id', 1, 2147483647 }, { 'which', 'enum', { 'origin', 'tail' } } },
}, onTake)

-- client/sync.lua (trimmed): the rope as the server has it, put back on this game
RegisterNetEvent('whip_rope:correction', function(data)
    local rope = Rope.System.ropes[data.serverRopeId]
    if not rope then return end
    Rope.ApplyEnd(rope, 'origin', data.origin)
    Rope.ApplyEnd(rope, 'tail', data.tail)
end)

What a game tells the server is a claim

A game reporting something the server cannot see is checked against what the server can. The node positions the rope's owner sends for the other games are passed on only near the rope's ends (believable, server/main.lua). A shot at someone hanging is believed only from an armed player in range (onShot), a stretched rope only when its ends really are far apart (onStretched), and a blown-up prop only with an explosion by it, which the server does see (OneSync routes every explosion through it as explosionEvent).

-- server/api.lua: a game says a map prop its rope is tied to was blown up. The server cannot see map props, but it
-- sees every explosion (explosionEvent), so it believes the game only with one by the prop just now.
local function onEndBroken(source, _, ropeId, which)
    local rope = Ropes.all[ropeId]
    local w = rope and rope.opts and rope.opts.watch
    if not w or not w.broken or not WHICH[which] then return end
    local e = rope[which]
    local at = e.type == 'object' and Ropes.endPos(e)
    if not at or not blastNear(at) then return end    -- no explosion there: not believed
    if not Ropes.near(source, rope) then return end
    TriggerEvent('whip_rope:ropeEndBroken', rope.id, which, rope.byResource)
end

Nothing a player owns is lost

A rope still out when its owner leaves, or when whip_rope stops, is owed back to their character and kept in whip_rope's resource KVP, so it survives a restart. It is paid as that character loads. The debt comes off the books before the give, so two loads cannot both be paid, and goes back on if the give fails.

-- server/item.lua: paid as the character loads (and to everyone in when whip_rope starts)
local function payOwed(source, charId)
    local owed = Ropes.takeOwed(charId)               -- off the books first: two loads can't both be paid
    if owed <= 0 then return end
    if Ropes.giveItem(source, owed, 'ropes you had out') then
        Whip.call('NotifyPlayer', source, owed == 1 and 'The rope you had out is back in your pockets'
            or ('The %d ropes you had out are back in your pockets'):format(owed), 'info')
    else
        Ropes.owe(charId, owed)                       -- the give failed: owed again
    end
end

A bar the server times, and a look after it

Coiling a rope up runs the server Progress through Whip.call, from a SecureEvent handler, which may wait (a SecureCallback may not: the game gives up on one after 10 seconds). The bar takes seconds, so once it answers the handler looks again: the rope may be gone, or in someone else's hands. Pockets that will not take the item make it owed instead. coilEnded tells the player's game the bar is over, so its hint capsule comes back; that game also gives up waiting by itself after a while, in case the answer never comes.

-- server/main.lua (trimmed): coiling up, a SecureEvent handler, so it may wait (the game gives up on a SecureCallback
-- after 10 s). `player` is the SecureEvent's own: the asking player's record, with its charId.
local function onCoil(source, player, ropeId)
    local rope = Ropes.all[ropeId]
    -- ... the checks: it is there, one of its ends in their hands, theirs to coil, nobody else coiling it
    rope.coiling = source
    local done = Whip.call('Progress', source, {
        label = 'Coiling up the rope', duration = Config.Item.CoilDuration or 3000,
        icon = 'pickup', canCancel = true,
    })
    if Ropes.all[ropeId] == rope then rope.coiling = nil end
    coilEnded(source)                                 -- their game: the bar is over, its hint comes back
    if done ~= true then return false end             -- cancelled, or they left

    -- The bar took seconds: is the rope still there, and still in their hands?
    if Ropes.all[ropeId] ~= rope or Ropes.heldBy(source, true) ~= rope then return false end
    Ropes.remove(ropeId)
    if not Ropes.giveItem(source, 1, 'rope coiled up') then
        Ropes.owe(player and player.charId, 1)        -- pockets that would not take it: owed, never lost
    end
end

A prompt where the player looks

The tie prompt is a whip_core action with aimBox (at: where it lives): it sits where the player's look meets the car, prop or map within reach, and ctx.coords is that point. whip_rope adds it only while an end is in the player's hand and removes it after, because an aimBox action casts a ray every frame while it exists. An action added like this is in whip_core's memory, not yours, and whip_rope keeps a flag saying it is up. whip_core restarting stops whip_rope first (dependency 'whip_core') and starts it again after, so the flag starts false with it and the next look puts the prompt up again. A resource without the dependency keeps running through the restart: it resets the flag in Whip.onCoreLost, or the prompt never comes back.

-- client/ui.lua (trimmed): the tie prompt, on whatever the player looks at
local TIE = {
    id = 'tie', group = 'whip_rope',
    at = { aimBox = { 'vehicle', 'object', 'world' } },   -- a car, a prop, or the map itself
    label = 'Tie the rope here',
    icon = 'place',
    reach = Config.Rules.Reach,
    require = { vehicle = 'out' },
    canInteract = function(ctx) return Rope.CanTieTo(ctx and ctx.entity, ctx and ctx.world) end,
    onSelect = function(ctx) Rope.TieHeldEnd(ctx.entity, ctx.coords, ctx.world, ctx.normal) end,
}
local tieUp = false

-- Five times a second: up only while an end is in the hand
local wantTie = Rope.MyHeld() ~= nil
if wantTie ~= tieUp then
    if wantTie then
        tieUp = Whip.call('AddAction', TIE) == true
    else
        Whip.call('RemoveAction', 'tie')
        tieUp = false
    end
end

Rope Exports (whip_rope)

Resource: exports.whip_rope. A resource that cannot work without ropes adds dependency 'whip_rope'; one that can checks GetResourceState('whip_rope') == 'started' before a call, as whip_fuel does. See Rope System for an overview.

A rope your resource makes is built and simulated as every rope is, and behaves as its spec says. Only your resource can move it with SetRopeEnd or take it away, it stays when the player it was for leaves, and it goes when your resource stops. It is never an item (nobody can coil it up) and never counts against a player's ropes. Its length is fixed for as long as it lasts: for another length, RemoveRope it and CreateRope again (whip_fuel's hose does this each time it is drawn).

Locked or not. With locked = true, nobody but your resource moves it: no prompts, and holding its end is not holding a rope. Without it, players handle it like any rope (pick its ends up, untie them, tie them, put them down, hang off it) and your resource is not told: read GetRope for where its ends are now. That can be the point: put an unlocked rope's end in a player's hand, and whip_rope's own tie prompt lets them hook it to any car, with no code of yours.

A worked example of all of it is whip_fuel's pump hose: whip_fuel/server/hose.lua makes, moves and takes back its ropes, listens to the notices and copes with whip_rope restarting.

A rope's ends

Each end is a table. CreateRope and SetRopeEnd take them, and GetRope answers them in the same shape.

EndFields
{ type = 'held' }heldBy: a player's server id. The rope ends at their right hand (or at heldAt's prop, below)
{ type = 'fixed' }pos: a spot in the world; tied = true: tied to the map there (players see Untie), not put down
{ type = 'vehicle' }netId: a networked car; offset: where on it, in the car's own space (default its middle), or edge = 'front' / 'back': at its nose or tail, which every game works out from the car's model
{ type = 'object' }netId: a networked prop, or 0 for a map prop, which then needs model (a hash: `prop_gas_pump_1a`, not a name in quotes) and worldPos (where it stands) and may give point (the spot it is tied at, default worldPos); offset: where on it; still = true: a map prop that stays put, never pulled loose; mass: what it weighs in kg (a prop's weight cannot be read, so it is guessed from its size, and a heavy one is thrown about like a light one without it)
{ type = 'free' }Loose: it lies where it falls. GetRope also gives at, where it was let go, when the server knows

An end can come loose by itself, with no notice. When the car or prop it is tied to goes (put in a garage, deleted, despawned), on any rope, locked ones too. On a rope that is not locked, also when the player holding it dies or leaves, or when a player unties it. Check GetRope before you rely on where an end is.

CreateRope(spec) SERVER

Make a rope between two things, built on every game near it.

spec fieldTypeDescription
origin, tailtableIts two ends. At least one must be somewhere the server can find: held, fixed, or tied to a car or prop
lengthnumber?Metres, 0.5 to 100 (default: the item rope's length setting). Fixed for the rope's life
linknumber?Metres between its nodes (default: the item rope's). At most 64 nodes: past that the links are made longer
playernumber?The player it is for: their game always has the rope, wherever they are
kindstring?A tag of your own, up to 32 characters, handed back by GetRope
lockedboolean?true: nobody can grab, tie, put down, coil or hang off it. Only your resource moves it (SetRopeEnd). Left out, players handle it like any rope, all but coiling it, and you are not told (locked or not)
take, hangboolean?On a rope that is not locked: take = false, nobody picks its ends up or unties them; hang = false, nobody hangs off it. Changed later with SetRopeRules
looktable?{ model, modelNoShadow, thickness }: its own rope pieces, modelled as whip_rope_seg is (whip_rope/docs/whip_rope_seg.txt). The models are hashes (backticks); a name in quotes is dropped, and the rope is drawn in whip_rope's own pieces
collidetable?{ spacing, vehicles, props }: every spacing'th node is checked against the world (default 2), and whether cars and props count (default: the Rope settings). The map always counts
heldAttable?{ model, offset }: a held end sits at offset on the prop of that model in the hand (a pump's nozzle), not at the hand. This model may be a name ('prop_cs_fuel_nozle') or a hash
watchtable?{ stretch, holdMs, broken }: whip_rope:ropeStretched when it is pulled stretch past its length (0.35: 35%) for holdMs (default 250), and again every 3 seconds while it stays that stretched; broken = true: whip_rope:ropeEndBroken when a map prop it is tied to is blown up
maxStretchnumber?A hard length, 0 to 2 (0.2: 20% past it): past it the two ends are pulled together by one pull, each moved by what it weighs, so a car feels the prop it drags. The pull is at most a very strong hose's, so something caught on the way jolts the car and the rope stretches past its length for a moment, never more than twice maxStretch (whip_rope's Config.Coupling.HardCeiling), where it holds whatever pulls. A car driving away from something that does not move is never held back by it. Left out, the rope is elastic with no hard end. With a watch.stretch above it, the notice comes only when neither end can follow (one fixed in place, the other driving away): whip_fuel's hose (maxStretch 0.3, watch.stretch 0.35) is told only when a car drives off with the nozzle still in it
-- A 6 m tow line from a truck's back to the car behind it, that players cannot take off
local id, why = exports.whip_rope:CreateRope({
    origin = { type = 'vehicle', netId = NetworkGetNetworkIdFromEntity(truck), offset = vector3(0.0, -3.2, 0.6) },
    tail   = { type = 'vehicle', netId = NetworkGetNetworkIdFromEntity(car),   offset = vector3(0.0, 2.1, 0.3) },
    length = 6.0,
    locked = true,
    kind   = 'towline',
})
if not id then print('no tow line: ' .. why) return end
Returns: number: the rope's id, or false, reason: what is wrong with an end ('tail: a vehicle end names netId'), or 'neither end is anywhere yet'
SetRopeEnd(id, which, end) SERVER

Move one end of a rope your resource made. Every game is told.

ParamTypeDescription
idnumberThe rope's id, as CreateRope gave it
whichstring'origin' or 'tail'
endtableWhere it goes: an end
-- Into the player's hand, then down at their feet
exports.whip_rope:SetRopeEnd(id, 'tail', { type = 'held', heldBy = source })
exports.whip_rope:SetRopeEnd(id, 'tail', { type = 'fixed', pos = GetEntityCoords(GetPlayerPed(source)) })
Returns: true, or false, reason: 'not your rope' (another resource's, or gone), a bad which, or what is wrong with the end
A locked rope's held end is yours to move. whip_rope never lets it go for you: not when the player holding it dies, logs out to the character screen, or leaves the server. Move it from all three: whip_core:player:died, whip_core:player:logout (a player switching characters does not leave) and playerDropped, as whip_rope's own server/main.lua does with its last handlers.
SetRopeRules(id, rules) SERVER

Change what players may do with a rope your resource made, and how far it may be pulled before it says so, from now on. A field left out stays as it was. Every game is told.

ParamTypeDescription
idnumberThe rope's id
rulestable{ take?, hang?, stretch? }: take and hang as CreateRope takes them; stretch, its watch.stretch (0.35: 35%), or false to stop it
-- The winch is set: nobody unhooks it now
exports.whip_rope:SetRopeRules(id, { take = false })
Returns: true, or false, reason: 'not your rope', or a rule it cannot read
RemoveRope(id) SERVER

Take away a rope your resource made, on every game.

exports.whip_rope:RemoveRope(id)
Returns: true, or false when it is another resource's or already gone
GetRope(id) SERVER

Any rope's tag, ends and length, a player's or a resource's.

local rope = exports.whip_rope:GetRope(id)
if rope and rope.tail.type == 'held' then
    print(('player %d holds the end of a %.1f m rope'):format(rope.tail.heldBy, rope.length))
end
Returns: { kind, origin, tail, length } (its ends as the server keeps them), or nil
GetRopeEndEntity(id, which) CLIENT

The car or prop a rope's end is tied to on this game. An end moved with SetRopeEnd has reached this game once this answers the new one.

ParamTypeDescription
idnumberThe rope's id
whichstring'origin' or 'tail'
-- Client: the car the tail is tied to, once this game has it
local car = exports.whip_rope:GetRopeEndEntity(id, 'tail')
if car then SetVehicleIndicatorLights(car, 0, true) end
Returns: the entity, or nil: not tied to one, not streamed in here yet, or no such rope on this game

The notices

Every resource hears every rope's notices: check that resource is yours.

EventSideArgsWhen
whip_rope:ropeStretchedServerid, resourcePulled past its watch.stretch for watch.holdMs, and again every 3 seconds while it stays that stretched: act once. The game running one of its ends says so, and the server believes it only when the ends really are far apart and that player is near
whip_rope:ropeEndBrokenServerid, which, resourceA map prop that end is tied to was blown up (watch.broken): believed only with an explosion the server saw by it
whip_rope:ropeRemovedServerid, resource, whywhip_rope took the rope away itself (an admin's /clearropes): forget the id. Not sent for your own RemoveRope, nor when your resource stops
whip_rope:pulledFromHandClientid, which, resourceLocked ropes only, on the game of the player holding that end: the car or prop at the other end dragged them along and they let go, or died. The end stays theirs until you move it, and SetRopeEnd is the server's: send your server a SecureEvent (below). An unlocked rope's end is simply let go, with no notice
-- Made with watch = { stretch = 0.35 }: pulled 35% past its length, it snaps
AddEventHandler('whip_rope:ropeStretched', function(id, resource)
    if resource ~= GetCurrentResourceName() then return end   -- every resource hears every rope's
    exports.whip_rope:RemoveRope(id)
end)

A locked line pulled from a player's hand, dropped at their feet by your server (whip_fuel does the same with its nozzle, in whip_fuel/client/pumps.lua):

-- client: the line pulled from this player's hand; the server moves its end
AddEventHandler('whip_rope:pulledFromHand', function(id, which, resource)
    if resource ~= GetCurrentResourceName() then return end
    TriggerServerEvent('mytow:dropLine', id)
end)

-- server: one of your SecureEvents (inside Whip.register)
exports.whip_core:SecureEvent('mytow:dropLine', { params = { { 'id', 'id', 1, 2147483647 } } }, function(source, player, id)
    local rope = exports.whip_rope:GetRope(id)
    if not rope or rope.tail.type ~= 'held' or rope.tail.heldBy ~= source then return end   -- theirs to drop
    exports.whip_rope:SetRopeEnd(id, 'tail', { type = 'fixed', pos = GetEntityCoords(GetPlayerPed(source)) })
end)
When whip_rope restarts, your ropes go with it. No notice is sent, and rope ids start again from 1. Forget yours when it stops, and make them again when it starts (whip_fuel's hoses do this). 
AddEventHandler('onResourceStop', function(res)
    if res == 'whip_rope' then myRopes = {} end                -- gone, ids and all
end)
AddEventHandler('onResourceStart', function(res)
    if res == 'whip_rope' then CreateThread(makeMyRopes) end   -- made again
end)

Learning from whip_autos

whip_autos is Whiplash: a car customisation shop players drive into (paint, parts, wheels, stance, engine swaps, paid for with in-game money), and bolt-on power (a turbo sold in stages, a nitrous bottle, every car's top speed and shift times, a gearbox computer). It ships with WHIP. Running it as a server owner, its settings and what to check when something goes wrong: whip_autos/README.md. This section is for a developer: it shows how a shop that takes money for work on a car is built on whip, file by file.

Much of it teaches nothing about whip: the shop's camera (client/camera.lua, client/boxfit.lua), the 3D page (html/js/view.js, kit.js), the gearbox computer (client/power/gearbox.lua) and the stance maths in client/tuning.lua. Skip those. fxmanifest.lua lists every file and what it does, and states the calling rule the code keeps: the one in Calling whip_core. With dependency 'whip_core', a whip_core restart stops whip_autos first and starts it again after (the satellite helper), so nothing in it cleans up after whip_core.

The server prices the basket again

The shop's page shows prices, but they are labels: it sends the server what was picked (slots and indices, and the tuning choices) and the total it showed, never a price. The purchase is a SecureEvent whose near keeps it to the shop floor, and whose onReject answers the page even when the request is refused before the handler runs, so the page's pay button never hangs. The handler works every line out again from the server's own Config and the car's stored look: a part the car already has is dropped (ShopFitted, shared/shop.lua), and a total above the one the page showed is refused, not charged.

-- server/main.lua (trimmed): the page sends what was picked and the total it showed, never a price
exports.whip_core:SecureEvent('whip_autos:server:purchase', {
    rateLimit = 3000, burst = 2,
    near      = SHOP_NEAR,   -- its `at` is a function: a /whiplash visit's floor is wherever its car is
    -- A refusal before the handler runs (the cooldown, the distance, a bad value) still answers the page.
    onReject = function(src, why)
        TriggerClientEvent('whip_autos:client:purchaseResult', src, false, tostring(why))
    end,
    params = {
        { 'vehicleId', 'id' },
        { 'method', 'enum', { 'cash', 'bank' } },
        -- At most 40 lines. `slot` and `wheelType` are checked in onPurchase; the tuning fields by server/tuning.lua.
        { 'basket', 'list', {
            { 'slot',      'any' },
            { 'index',     'id', -1, 255 },
            { 'wheelType', 'any' },
            { 'engine',    'any' },
            { 'stance',    'any' },
            { 'setup',     'any' },
            { 'drive',     'any' },
        }, 40 },
        { 'shown', 'int', 0, 1000000000, -1 },
    },
}, onPurchase)

Paid and fitted in one write

ChargePlayer is called straight inside the SecureEvent, so the payment is held and lands in the same transaction as the next whip write, the car's new look (SetVehicleAppearance). A crash in between keeps neither. A fit that fails gives the money back with the receipt (RefundPlayer).

-- server/main.lua, onPurchase (trimmed): each line priced again from the server's own Config and the car's stored look
for _, line in ipairs(basket) do
    -- ... the slot and index checked first, each in its own range
    if ShopFitted(def.properties, line, turboIndex) then
        -- already on the car: dropped, and the rest still goes through
    else
        local price = priceOf(line.slot, line.index, def.properties)
        total = total + price
        lines[#lines + 1] = { slot = line.slot, index = line.index, price = price }
    end
end

-- Never more than the page showed: a price raised in /whip mid-visit is refused, not charged.
if shown >= 0 and total > shown then
    return fail('The prices changed while you were here. Leave and come back to see them.')
end

-- Paid before fitted, and the payment lands with the fitting's write: all of it or none.
local receipt
if total > 0 then
    local payErr
    receipt, payErr = exports.whip_core:ChargePlayer(source, total, { method = method, reason = 'Whiplash customisation' })
    if not receipt then return fail(payErr or 'Payment failed') end
end
local ok = TuningServer.write(vehicleId, tuningChanges, propsFromBasket(lines))   -- one SetVehicleAppearance
if not ok then
    if receipt then exports.whip_core:RefundPlayer(receipt) end
    return fail('Something went wrong fitting that')
end

A claim that every exit gives back

A player trying parts on changes the real car, and everyone near sees it, so the server keeps a session per car: one player per car, one car per player. Every way a visit can end puts the stored look back: the page closing, leaving the driver's seat (whip_core's whip_core:vehicle:exited), leaving the server, and whip_autos stopping. On the player's game, every exit runs one function (teardownLocal, client/session.lua) that lets go of the camera, the controls (BlockControls) and the page, and HoldVehicleAppearance stops whip reporting the unpaid preview as the car's look.

-- server/main.lua (trimmed): a session is the claim, and every way it ends puts the car back
local function endSession(vehicleId)
    if not sessions[vehicleId] then return end
    sessions[vehicleId] = nil
    restore(vehicleId)   -- Whip.call('RestoreVehicleAppearance', vehicleId)
end

AddEventHandler('playerDropped', function()
    local src = source
    for vehicleId, s in pairs(sessions) do
        if s.source == src then endSession(vehicleId) end
    end
end)
AddEventHandler('whip_core:vehicle:exited', leftTheWheel)   -- out of the driver's seat
-- ... and 'whip_autos:server:release' (the page closed), and onResourceStop for every car at once

-- client/session.lua: while it is held, whip does not report the unpaid preview as the car's look, and if this
-- resource stops before letting go, whip puts the stored look back itself
Whip.call('HoldVehicleAppearance', vId, true)

Data on a car that every game applies

An engine swap, a stance, a handling setup and a drivetrain are not GTA mods, so GTA does not sync them. The server writes each as the car's vehicle data, in the purchase's one write (server/tuning.lua), and every game applies it with WatchVehicleData: onGained, onChanged and onLost for what every car in view shows (its sound, its stance, its drivetrain), and driverOnly with onStart and onStop for what only the driver's game sets (a handling layer). A layer for every car driven, data or not, goes by whip_core's seat events instead (client/power/handling.lua).

-- client/tuning.lua (trimmed), inside Whip.register: the engine sound on every car in view that has a swap
exports.whip_core:WatchVehicleData(TUNING_ENGINE_KEY, {
    id = 'engineSound',
    onGained = function(entity, value)
        _engines[entity] = value
        local s = soundFor(entity)
        if s then setEngineSound(entity, s) end
        applyRevs(entity)   -- the rev dial follows the donor engine
    end,
    onChanged = function(entity, value) _engines[entity] = value; setEngineSound(entity, soundFor(entity)) end,
    onLost = function(entity) _engines[entity] = nil; restoreEngineSound(entity) end,
})

-- ... and its power, on the car this player drives only: a handling layer
exports.whip_core:WatchVehicleData(TUNING_ENGINE_KEY, {
    id = 'enginePower',
    driverOnly = true,
    onStart = function(entity, value)
        local set = TuningEngineSet(value, GetVehicleHandlingFloat(entity, 'CHandlingData', 'fMass'))
        if set then exports.whip_core:SetVehicleHandlingLayer({ entity = entity }, 'engine', { set = set }) end
    end,
    onStop = function() exports.whip_core:ClearVehicleHandlingLayer('engine') end,
})

Two kinds of vehicle stat

The turbo's boost is a live stat (RegisterVehicleStat, server/power/turbo.lua): the driver's game simulates it and reports it, whip_core caps how fast it may rise, and the driver's own gauge reads the simulation, returned from whileHeld (client/power/turbo.lua; see Watching vehicle stats). The nitrous bottle is a consume stat: the game bills what it burns, and whip_core caps it and takes the bottle off when it is empty. Fitting a bottle is a declared timed use: whip_core runs the bar and takes the item, and the car is the one the server sees the player in.

-- server/power/nitrous.lua (trimmed): the bottle burns down on the driver's game, billed and capped by whip_core
exports.whip_core:RegisterVehicleStat('nitro', {
    default = 0, min = 0, max = PowerNitrous.BOTTLE, persist = true,
    consume = { maxRate = PowerNitrous.burnPerSec, driverOnly = true, clearAtMin = true, interval = 0.5 },
})

-- Using the item fits it. A table, so whip_core runs the bar, takes the bottle, and gives it back on `false, why`.
exports.whip_core:RegisterUseHandler('nitro', {
    label = 'Installing nitrous...', duration = PowerNitrous.installMs, cancelOnExit = true,
    canUse = function(source)
        local vehicleId, why = carForBottle(source)   -- the car the SERVER sees them in, never the game's word
        if not vehicleId then return false, why end
        return true
    end,
    onComplete = function(source)
        local vehicleId, why = carForBottle(source)   -- asked again: the bar took seconds
        if not vehicleId then return false, why end
        local fitted = exports.whip_core:SetVehicleStat(vehicleId, 'nitro', PowerNitrous.BOTTLE, 'whip_autos:nitrous')
        if not fitted then return false, 'Could not fit the bottle' end
    end,
})

Who may change a car

Whether a player may work on someone else's car is a setting (Config.WhoCanModify): anyone, only the owner for performance and tuning, or only the owner at all (anyone else may still repair it). It is decided in one function both sides load, and the server asks it twice: at the claim, which then tells the game which shelves to leave out (Performance and Tuning, or every shelf, leaving Repair), and again when the player pays. The page hiding a shelf is for the player; the server is the rule.

-- shared/shop.lua: the rule in one place (Config.WhoCanModify, on the settings page)
function ShopMayChange(charId, ownerCharId)
    local rule = Config.WhoCanModify
    if rule ~= 'ownerTuning' and rule ~= 'owner' then return 'all' end
    if ownerCharId == nil or ownerCharId == charId then return 'all' end   -- nobody's car is open to its driver
    if rule == 'owner' then return 'repair' end   -- the services only
    return 'looks'
end

-- server/main.lua, onPurchase: asked again when they pay (the car may have changed hands since the claim)
local may = ShopMayChange(player.charId, def.owner and def.owner.charId)
local looksOnly, repairOnly = may == 'looks', may == 'repair'
-- ... and in its loop over the lines, a line only the owner may buy is dropped:
local dropped = (repairOnly and not SERVICES[slot]) or (looksOnly and ShopIsPerformance(tonumber(slot) or slot))

A settings page, and what is worked out from it

shared/settings.lua puts what an owner changes on a page in /whip (Whip.configPage): the prices, the power, the shifting, how far the sliders go. What an admin saves is written into Config, so the rest of the code keeps reading Config. A file that works something out from Config when it loads builds it again with Whip.onConfigChanged; shared/shop.lua refills its lookups in place, so every file holding one sees the change.

-- shared/shop.lua: a lookup worked out from Config, built again IN PLACE when an admin changes the list in /whip,
-- so every file holding the table sees the new contents
local function refill(t, list, put)
    for k in pairs(t) do t[k] = nil end
    for i, x in ipairs(list) do put(t, i, x) end
end
local function buildServices() refill(SHOP_SERVICES, Config.Services, function(t, _, x) t[x.id] = true end) end
buildServices()
Whip.onConfigChanged('Services', buildServices)

A page of its own

The shop's page is whip_autos' own NUI page, not whip_core's. nui_callback_strict_mode in the manifest lets only that page call its callbacks (the purchase spends money), and every callback answers. Whip.padScreen gives it a controller and the cursor; SetUIOpen stands whip's HUD down while it is up.

-- client/ui.lua: every NUI callback answers, even when it does nothing (an unanswered one leaves the page's fetch
-- hanging). nui_callback_strict_mode 'true' in fxmanifest.lua lets only this resource's page call them.
local function cb(name, fn)
    RegisterNUICallback(name, function(data, done)
        local ok, err = pcall(fn, data or {})
        if not ok then print(('[whip_autos] nui callback "%s" errored: %s'):format(name, tostring(err))) end
        done({})
    end)
end

Director cards

whip_autos adds Whiplash to the Director (cards of your own, tasks and buttons). server/director.lua has two cards made with Whip.card: Goal: Customise Vehicle (a checklist the player's purchases tick off, shared/goals.lua) and Force Open Whiplash. shared/director.lua is a car task (Whip.task). client/look.lua puts a Whiplash button in the world builder (Whip.directorButton) to pick how a placed car comes out, and server/look.lua puts that look on the car when the scenario makes it (whip_core:run:thingMade).

Where to look

To see how toRead

Director: scenarios, access, shipped packs

Scenarios are managed in /whip → Director (the /w menu's Director row opens it too) and built in game, in the world. Every revision is kept, so the one switched on never changes under its players.

Where you build

Open Editor (a scenario's page in /whip), or New scenario, takes you into the world builder on it: place its people and things, set each one up with Configure, and open Blueprint for its cards in a window over the world. Map opens a window of the same kind with the scenario's things on whip's map, each its own picture, where they are now (saved or not), the camera as the arrow; click a mark for its card, with Go to (the camera in front of it) and Configure. The window's Fullscreen is the full editor: the cards over the whole screen, with the Cards, World, Variables and Settings tabs, Save, Test and Check. Its ‹ (or Esc) goes back into the world, the camera where you left it. Exit in the world builder leaves the Director. Changes not saved stay with the scenario while you are away: open it again and they are there (opening another one asks what to do with them).

Who may

LevelPermissionMay
Builderdirector.buildSee every scenario; make, edit, test, switch on and off; restore an old revision; stop a run
Director admindirector.adminEverything a builder may, and delete scenarios, accept shipped packs, export packs, and give or take Director access
Dungeon Modedirector.liveChange the live world: make NPCs, cars and props for everyone, and use the Object Viewer's options on anything, for as long as the server runs. Nothing that lasts past a restart. Neither of the other two includes it, nor does it include them
Full adminwhip.devtoolsAll three, always (and the /director dev commands)

Access is given per account in /whip → Director → Access (pick a character; every character on that account has it). A builder who is not a full admin opens /whip and sees the Director alone (Access is a Director admin's); someone with Dungeon Mode alone (a Dungeon Master) sees its Dungeon Mode page alone.

How a scenario starts

Switching a scenario on makes it available; a run begins the way its Scenario Enabled card's It starts says. When it's switched on (the choice for a new scenario) starts the run at once, with nobody in it: Scenario Enabled's cards play straight away and what they make (an NPC to talk to, the cars, the props) is out for everyone. The first player to talk to its NPC (a Dialog Line), press its prompt (Wait for Press, an Interaction Menu) or come near (Player Arrives) joins the run, and that card plays for them. The job itself starts at Scenario Started By Player (before it nothing counts), or as they join when there is no such card. When the run is over, however it ended, it starts again a couple of seconds later, fresh, for the next player; one that ended before anyone joined (a Succeed with nobody there) waits until the scenario is switched off and on. Start a run or a script's StartScenarioRun puts that player into the waiting run. The other choices (talk to an NPC set to Always present, press something, come near, an item, a timer, a script, by hand) start a run for the player who does it, and Scenario Enabled's cards play then. Test starts one for you at once whatever it says, and anyone with Director access can always press Start a run (on its page in /whip). Started any other way, a player is never in two runs of the same scenario at once, and Runs at once and Players this close join apply. While a test runs, the test map's Free camera (press H for the mouse first) flies a camera round it to watch, your character staying hidden where it stands; pressed again, or on the way back to the editor, the camera is back on you. G hides the test map (its trail and keys too) for a clean screen, and shows it again; the test and every key go on as before, and H brings it back with the mouse. A /w noclip still on when the world builder opens is turned off.

It startsHow
Talk to an NPCTalk on a standing NPC. While its runs are full, others see "They're busy right now."
Press somethingAn E prompt (its words yours) on a placed thing: a standing prop or a spot (a laptop, a keypad, a job board)
A player comes nearA player who walks within the distance of a placed thing. Once a visit: still standing there when their run ends, they must leave and come back. One who could not have a run (its runs are full) gets one as soon as a place frees
Use an itemUsing an item from the inventory (a job note, a burner phone). Kept, unless Used up. Only an item that does nothing else when used: Check refuses one that does, and two scenarios cannot start with the same item
On a timerEvery so many minutes (the first that long after it is switched on): one run for every player near a placed thing. Nobody near: no run until the next time
From a scriptAnother resource asks: exports.whip_core:StartScenarioRun(key, source) (a phone app, a job menu)
By hand (an admin starts it)Only Start a run: admin-run events

The Director in /whip

Director is a group of its own along /whip's header; its pages are the tabs under it.

PageWhat it shows
OverviewEvery scenario at once, over 7, 14, 30 or 90 days, or only some: Showing picks one scenario, the ones a lore character is in, or the ones a player made. What was paid out (the biggest number), runs, how many succeed, how many players, how many are going now; a run a day; the most run scenarios, who plays most, why runs fail, and the newest runs (click one for what its players did in it). Tests are left out of the numbers
ScenariosEvery scenario, how often it runs and succeeds. One scenario's page: its description (the Blueprint's), who made it and when, its things on the map, Active (a switch: on is its newest revision; while it is on, newer edits go live when you switch it off and on), and Previous Versions (every revision, with Restore). New scenario makes one (empty, from an example, or from another resource's template) and takes you into the world on it; Duplicate copies one; Open Editor opens it; Start a run starts one for you; Delete (a Director admin's) is beside its maker
Lore charactersThe people your stories keep coming back to, each on a page of their own: their picture large (Edit picture frames it, as phones show it), and tabs for their Details (name, bank name, ped, notes), Audio (their voice lines) and Interactions (the scenarios that use them, their phone's texts and calls, what they have paid players). Retire takes one out of use (a Director admin's); Bring back returns them
ShippedScenarios resources bring (below): waiting, accepted, refused, and anything this server is missing to run one
Live runsGoing now, with Stop, and scenarios switched on from a file (/director load), with Switch off
AccessBuilders, Director admins and Dungeon Masters, each with their face and name (Director admins only)
Dungeon ModeDungeon Mode's: Start Dungeon Mode, and everything you made that is up now (what it is, its name and model, where, when), each with Remove, the effects you turned on (each with Turn off), and Clear everything I made (effects too). A full admin sees everyone else's too, with who made each, and Clear everyone's

Dungeon Mode: the live world as the scenario

The world builder with no scenario: the world as it is now is what you build in. Whoever has it is a Dungeon Master. /whip → Director → Dungeon Mode → Start Dungeon Mode opens it where you stand; so does the Dungeon Mode row under Panels in the /w menu (a full admin's: /w is only theirs).

You doWhat happens
Pick from Props, NPCs, Vehicles or More (its Weapons), and put it downIt is made in the world for real, for everyone, where you put it: an NPC standing there, an unlocked car, a prop, or a Fixed Weapon (a gun as a prop). It joins your Placed tab as soon as your game has it
Click one of yoursIt is selected: drag its arrows, its centre dot or (after R) its rings to move it. Where you let go is where it stays: an NPC stands there from then on, a prop is shown there for everyone. The bubble's Options opens its options (an NPC's own: attack or follow a player, calm down, a weapon, on guard, invincible, stay put; a Fixed Weapon's Fire and Fire a burst, real shots from its barrel the way it points, everyone hears them); Remove takes it out of the world
Click a playerTheir options, with Spawn a car for them and Send NPCs after them: what is made is yours, as anything you put down
Click anything else in the worldA prop (the map's own, another resource's, or one made here), a ground item, a whip or street car, an NPC or a player: the Object Viewer's options open for it, over the builder. Their Move puts the builder's arrows on it; click anywhere else when you are done and its options come back. A click on the world away from the options puts them away. A click on a car's window is on the car, and a ground item or a prop with no collision is found by its shape
Point at somethingWhat a click there would pick is outlined in white (a ped or a car gets white corners round it instead). What is selected, or has its options open, is blue
A car of yours: Key settingsIts options' Dungeon car group: where its key is (no key, a player's pocket, the ignition, the glovebox, the boot, or on the ground beside it), Locked, and Only its key opens it (no lockpicking, no hotwiring), as the Director's Key settings for a run's car. A car is made unlocked with no key; one made with Spawn a car for them has its key in their pocket. Its key goes when the car goes (one left on the ground goes at the next restart too). A place with no room for the key (a full boot, a key in the ignition already) is refused before anything changes, and whoever sits in the car is told when its ignition key goes
Done or ExitThe builder closes. There is never anything to save: everything was made as you went

How long it lasts. What you make stays until the server restarts, or until you remove it (here, on the Dungeon Mode page, or with its Remove option). It is yours by account, so it stays when you log off; someone else's is theirs to remove (a full admin may remove anyone's). One account may have 150 things up at once, and everyone together 600; and 20 effects on, everyone together 80. An effect is yours as a thing is: only you (or a full admin) turn it off. An NPC whose body is cleared, or a car that is destroyed and taken away, is gone from your list too.

What only a full admin may do. Anything that would last past a restart: making a car someone's (Make vehicle permanently owned by player), putting a saved car away, deleting it, changing its owner or its stats, repairing a player's own saved car (its repair is kept in its record; any other car is anyone's to fix), a player's stats, their movement style, their character editor, kick and ban, the inventory, trunk and glovebox, getting into a player's locked car (Become driver or passenger: getting out would unlock it), and changing a ground item (moving it, changing what it is or how many, removing it: it is saved as it lies). A Dungeon Master sees these greyed, marked Admins only, and the server refuses them too (getting in is done in your own game, which reads the lock again as you press). Restore health and Restore armour are saved with the character but stay open to a Dungeon Master.

The map's own props are each game's own, so a change to one is made for everyone in two parts: the map's one is hidden on every game where it stands, and (for Make it a Dungeon prop and Change model) a prop made here goes up exactly where it stood. Both last until a restart. A hidden one is listed on the Dungeon Mode page with Put back; the prop that took its place has Put the map's one back.

Everything is logged on the activity log (as dungeon_mode): each thing made, moved and removed, and each option used, on the Dungeon Master's timeline (Player Manager), and on the player's own when it was done to a player.

The editor's grid

DoTo
Right-drag (or middle-drag) · wheelMove round the grid · zoom about the pointer. Zoomed far out, cards show their titles alone, larger, and comment boxes their names
Right-click the grid · a card · a pinAdd a card there · its menu · break its wires
Left-drag on empty groundA box: every card it touches is selected (Shift or Ctrl adds to the selection). A click clears it
Drag from a pinA wire: drop it on a pin to connect, on empty ground to add a card there, wired. An outcome can have several wires: every card they lead to starts at the same moment, the first-drawn wire first (as Do in Order does)
Double-click a wireA Reroute dot on it, to bend it round other cards (drag the dot by its middle; a wire dropped on it connects). Deleting a dot joins its wire up again; a dot that leads nowhere is a Check warning, as the outcome it hangs off would be
CA comment box round the selected cards (or an empty one), its name asked for. Drag its title to move it with the cards in it, its corner to resize it; double-click the title to rename it; right-click it to select what is in it or delete it (the cards stay)
Ctrl C · X · V · DCopy · cut · paste where the pointer is · duplicate. Pasted into another scenario, the fields that named the first one's placed things and variables are emptied (the line at the bottom says how many): pick them again there
Ctrl Z · Y · S · AUndo · redo · save · select every card
F · Delete · EscFit the selection (or everything) in view · delete what is selected · clear the selection (with none, back into the world)

Watching it run. With a scenario open, its live runs show on the grid: each card a run enters lights for a moment, and the wire it came along pulses (the cards of the revision that is on; a card the draft has since removed lights nothing). After a test, back in the editor, the test is played back the same way, in the order it ran, and what ran stays lit.

Talking: answers with rules, selling, haggling, flags

A Dialog Line's answers can each have rules (the gear beside the answer in the Card tab: blue while a rule is set). An answer whose rules say no is simply not offered; its cost and its odds show on it: Bribe him [$500, 60%].

RuleChoices
Offered only ifAlways · they have an item (how many) · they carry cash (at least $) · a player flag is set · is not set · a run variable is a value
CostsNothing · an item (how many) · money (cash, else the bank). Taken when chosen; one they cannot pay is refused with the reason and they choose again. An item cost is only offered to someone who carries it
OfferedEvery time · once a run · once ever (that character, for good)
WorksEmpty: always. 1–99 %: a chance, rolled on the server; a miss goes out of the card's Answer N failed outcome (the pin appears once a chance is set)
CardWhat it does
Sell to NPCThe NPC offers to buy an item the player carries at a price each (a field, or a variable: a price a Haggle agreed), up to At most. Yes takes the items (never one a run handed out) and pays them; a payment that fails gives them back. Outcomes: Sold (how many and the money can go in variables), Had none (at once, nothing said), Said no, No answer
HaggleAgrees a price in the capsule (it moves no money: wire Deal to Sell to NPC, Pay or Take Item with the price variable). Each round the player takes the offer, names their own (typed), or walks. They buy: it opens at the opening price and goes up to the ceiling, which the player does not know; a price within it is agreed; a little over (by its patience) and it meets them halfway; much over is an insult: its offer drops to the floor, and a second insult (the first, with short patience) makes it Angry. They sell: the same, the other way. Outcomes: Deal (at least as good as its opening), Bad deal, Walked away, Angry, No answer
Set Player Flag · If Player FlagRemember something about the player for good (Player flags): on, off, a value, or add a number; and branch on one (is set, is not set, is, at least, less than)
Claim Car · Give Car · Put in Car · Change PlateThe run's car made the player's own, saved like any other (ClaimVehicle: a new plate or the one given, what is in it kept, left where it stands or in their garage): the end of a boosting job; a new car of their own (in their garage, or standing at a placed thing); an item put in the run's car's trunk or glovebox (theirs to keep; a test takes it back); another plate on the run's car. A test only says what Claim Car and Give Car would have done
Show Objective · Clear ObjectiveWhat to do next, on the job's card at the top right of the screen until it is cleared, for everyone in the run or this player, with an icon of your choice. Its Subtext is the line under it: The scenario's name (the default), None, or My own words (typed in Subtext words; left empty, there is none). A Countdown's clock sits beside it either way
Show Prop · Hide PropThe scenario's props from the World tab (+ Prop: a list of props checked against the game, or any model), or groups of them, put where they were placed, or taken away, with "their groups too", every run prop of the same groups at once. A standing prop needs no card: it is there whenever the scenario is on. Every prop has Physics on unless you switch it to static (its page): it falls, rolls and gets knocked about, as one networked object that the nearest player's game moves while everyone else's follows. It is held still until something that moves is within 100 m of it (a player, a scripted car, an NPC, traffic: with nothing there, the ground under it may not be loaded yet), and again once nothing is. A standing one stays where it was knocked to until the scenario is switched off and on again (or the server restarts). A static prop is made by each player's own game (ShowPropSet), never networked, and so is one inside an interior, not solid, a Fixed Weapon, or with tasks (its page says which)
Fire WeaponA Fixed Weapon fires: a prop that is a firearm (the world builder's More, Weapons: GTA's, and whip_gunny's own guns marked "(gunny)" while it runs), placed and turned where you want it (selected, a red line shows where it fires), on its own or attached to a car, an NPC or a prop (its page: Attached to). Its shots, the gap between them, at where it points or at a placed thing (it turns to face it first). One player's game fires it, so there is one rocket, not one per player; the shots are real, and hurt whoever is in the way, in a Test too
Interaction MenuA prompt with a menu for the run's players, On a placed thing: riding the run's NPC or car, just above its ground pile or container, else at the spot (before the run has made the NPC, car, pile or container, at the spot it was placed, and the run log says so). Up to eight choices, each At the top or Under another: a choice with choices under it opens them on the same prompt with a Back (three deep, six to a level); every other choice is an outcome, its pin named by its text. Wire a choice back into the card to keep the menu up after it

Sell to NPC and Haggle speak as a Dialog Line does: an answer wired straight to one for the same NPC carries the conversation into it, and one of their outcomes wired to another speaking card carries it on; any other outcome closes it, and the NPC says a parting line over its head. A test changes nothing that lasts: costs and sales are only said, and flags it sets live on the test run alone.

Goals: one card, one thing to do

A Goal card (the Goals group, gold) is Show Objective, Show Blip, the wait and Clear Objective in one, so a scenario reads like a mission list. While it waits, every player in the run sees its objective on the job's card at the top right of the screen (with the job's name) and its mark on their map; give it a Time limit and a clock counts down under the objective, going out of Out of time. When it ends, whichever way, it takes down what it showed (an objective a later card put up stays).

CardDone whenAlso
Goal: Go ToA player in the run (or all of them) is within the distance of a placed thing: ArrivedMarked with a GPS route
Goal: Deliver the CarA player in the run drives the run's car to the drop-off: DeliveredCar lost: it is gone or blown up
Goal: Kill Them AllEvery NPC made for a placed thing (a whole group, a second wave too) is down: All downEach one marked red; the objective says how many are left
Goal: CollectThe run's players have picked up that many of an item between them, counted from when it starts: Collected"Collect Package (2/5)"; an optional area to look in, marked
Goal: Bring Item ToA player in the run is at a placed thing or an NPC (where it is now) carrying the item: BroughtTaken off them there, unless set not to
Goal: Steal the CarA player in the run is in the run's car's driver's seat (or any seat): In the carThe car marked, the mark following it; Car lost
Goal: SearchA player in the run opens the run's container: OpenedCreate Container first
Goal: Speak ToA player in the run talks to the NPC to the end of its Dialog Lines: SpokeThe NPC marked, with a GPS route; NPC lost: dead or gone. Wire its Dialog Line beside it
Goal: SurviveThey hold out for its length (the clock on screen): SurvivedFailed: all of them down at once, or all of them out of its area for three seconds

Everyday cards

What a run hands out. In a live run, items are real: Give Item, Drop Item, Put in Car, a heist's loot and a run car's keys are the player's to keep, and go anywhere any item goes. A test marks everything it hands out as a test's, and takes it back when it ends, from its players and the ground (a test's items). So a live run can tell its own package from anyone else's (Item Picked Up, Take Item, Collect, Bring Item To), an item one of its cards looks for carries a plain tag naming the run. Nothing else reads it, and it stays on the item.

CardWhat it does
Give ItemStraight into the player's pockets (at their feet if it does not fit), or everyone's in the run. Theirs to keep; a test takes it back when it ends
Player Has Item? · Player Has Money?Branches: Yes or No. An item (at least how many) for this player, anyone in the run, or everyone; money as cash on them, in their bank, or either
Charge PlayerTakes money (cash, bank, or cash if they carry enough): Paid or Could not pay. A test takes nothing, says what it would take, and goes the way their money would have
Player has diedAn event: the first time one of the scenario's players dies (or all of them at once), checked against whip's own record
Random ChanceYes some of the time (the chance, rolled on the server), otherwise No
CountdownA clock on the job's card at the top right (under the objective, or "Time left" when there is none) that goes out of Time's up. A pulse into Stop calls it off (Stopped); into Start again starts it over
RemoveTakes away what the run made for a placed thing, there and then: its NPCs, its car (never one that is the player's now), its prop, its item on the ground or its container
Car Destroyed · Car DamagedWait until the run's car is blown up or gone · takes more damage than a share you set, from when the card starts ("deliver it without a scratch"). The server reads a car's health only once a player's game has sent it, so a few readings in a row count
Send SignalTells other resources something happened in this run: a name ("alarm") and, if you like, a value or a variable's. Scripts hear whip_core:run:signalled; a police script can send its officers. A test sends nothing
Wait for Script EventWaits until another resource sends an event (its name for it, typed here: police.backupArrived), only one about a player in this run, sent for this run, or any; with a time limit if you give one (Not in time). What follows acts for the player it was about (about none of them: for whoever this branch was for). In your test, /director send police.backupArrived sends it into your own test, about you
NPC /meWhat the NPC does or says ("hands over a package") above its head for everyone nearby (no answers: Dialog Line has those). Up to four lines, picked one at random or each in turn (the next one each time the card is reached); a chance it shows; and for a group, above each of them still up (each its own pick and roll) or one of them. A standing NPC can say one too. Seen from (a slider, 5 to 250 m; left alone, a /me's own range) is how far away players see it. It keeps its size, as the NPC does, so a camera zoomed in on them from far off sees it as big as they are
