can hear but not talkThat player's game has no microphone: FiveM's box unanswered, or refused.They open F8 and click Allow in the box. Refused earlier: they allow it in FiveM's settings and reconnect.

Your own voice server

Instead of the built-in one: a voice server on another machine, players connecting to a domain name, LiveKit Cloud, or rented hosting that cannot open the voice ports. With whip_voice_url in server.cfg, whip_voice connects players there and the built-in voice server stays off (no add_unsafe_child_process_permission line needed). Players' games then connect to it directly, so it needs a secure address: wss:// with a valid certificate.

Any LiveKit server (LiveKit Cloud, or one you run yourself): these lines, with plain set, never setr (it would send the secret to every player). The voice bot is then yours to run too (whip_voice\service\voicebot, with whip_voicebot_url and whip_voicebot_token).

set whip_voice_url    "wss://your-project.livekit.cloud"
set whip_voice_key    "API..."
set whip_voice_secret "..."
set whip_voice_api    "https://your-project.livekit.cloud"   # where this FiveM server reaches its API

On a Windows server of your own, the setup wizard does it all: LiveKit, an HTTPS front door (Caddy) with a free certificate for your server's address, and the voice bot, as Windows services, and the lines in server.cfg. It needs a Windows server you can log into as an administrator, and no domain name. One double-click, with nothing to answer, in about 10 minutes:

The setup wizard

  1. On the server machine, open resources\whip_voice\service and double-click Setup voice server.bat. When Windows asks whether to let it make changes, say Yes.
  2. The voice address. It works out your server's public address and makes that the voice address: wss:// and the address. Players' games connect to it directly.
  3. Your host's firewall. The wizard opens Windows' own firewall itself. Some hosts have a firewall of their own in their website's control panel (OVH, Hetzner, AWS, Azure, Google Cloud). If yours does, allow these inbound there: TCP 80 and 443 (the secure address, and getting and renewing its certificate), TCP 7881 and UDP 7882 to 7893 (voice). The wizard does not wait for you: if a port is still shut, the check at the end says so, and the certificate comes as soon as it is open.
  4. Caddy and LiveKit. It installs both as Windows services that start with Windows, or adds your voice address to the Caddy the machine already has. A LiveKit of this version already installed is not downloaded again. Caddy gets the certificate for your server's address from Let's Encrypt: it lasts about 6 days, and Caddy renews it by itself every few days, for as long as ports 80 and 443 stay open.
  5. The voice bot. It plays recorded lines into phone calls as the Director's lore characters (Lore phone calls): its own copy of Node.js in C:\LiveKit\voicebot and a Windows service, "whip_voice voice bot", that only this machine can reach. Then the wizard waits for the certificate and checks every piece.
  6. server.cfg. The wizard writes whip_voice's lines into your server's server.cfg (the one in the folder above resources) and keeps the old file beside it as a backup. They go before the line that starts whip_voice (ensure whip_voice, or the ensure of a folder it is in, such as ensure [whip]), older whip_voice_ lines are replaced, and setr sv_mumble true is turned off: whip_voice does not use it, and on, any player's game can listen to any Mumble channel. With no server.cfg above resources, it prints the lines (and puts them on your clipboard) for you to paste after ensure whip_core. Always plain set, never setr: the secret and the token must stay on the server.
  7. Restart the FiveM server. The first time each player joins, FiveM asks them to allow the microphone: its box takes the mouse only with the F8 console open.

The lines it writes, with your server's address in the first:

set whip_voice_url      "wss://203.0.113.10"
set whip_voice_key      "whip..."
set whip_voice_secret   "..."
set whip_voicebot_token "..."

Run the setup again whenever you like: it keeps every key and token, leaves alone what is already installed and the same, and only restarts a service when something about it changed (a restart drops voice for a few seconds). Two FiveM servers on one machine (Legacy and Enhanced) share one voice server: run the setup from each one's whip_voice\service, and the second run keeps the same keys and writes the same lines into its own server.cfg.

A domain name instead

Players can connect to a name such as voice.myserver.com instead of your server's address. You need a domain you own (about $10 a year). Its certificate lasts about 3 months rather than 6 days, and the voice address stays the same if the server ever moves to a new address.

  1. In whip_voice\service, click the folder's address bar, type cmd and press Enter, then run "Setup voice server.bat" -Domain voice.myserver.com with your own domain.
  2. The wizard shows the DNS record to add where you bought the domain (Type A, Name voice, Value your server's address, which it works out), then waits until the internet can see it, usually a few minutes, and carries on by itself.
    • GoDaddy: My Products > your domain > DNS > Add New Record.
    • Namecheap: Domain List > Manage > Advanced DNS > Add New Record (A Record, Host voice).
    • Cloudflare: DNS > Records > Add record, then click the orange cloud so it turns grey ("DNS only"). Cloudflare's proxy cannot carry voice.
  3. The rest is the same, and server.cfg gets the new voice address. Restart the FiveM server.

Once a domain is set up, running the setup again keeps it. To go back to your server's address, run "Setup voice server.bat" -UseIp the same way.

Checking the wizard's voice server

  • Check voice server.bat, next to the setup, changes nothing. It checks the machine: the LiveKit, Caddy and voice bot services, their ports and Windows firewall rules, the voice address (a domain's DNS record too), the certificate and when it runs out, and whether server.cfg's lines match the voice server's keys and the bot's token.
  • /voicecheck, in game with developer mode on (or voicecheck in txAdmin's Live Console), checks from the game's side: the voice system, the keys, the voice address, every player's game (connected, over UDP or TCP, with a microphone, and whether it can read the secret), and the voice bot.

Both say OK, or what is wrong and how to fix it, top to bottom: an early problem often causes the later ones.

What its problems mean

It saysWhat it meansWhat to do
the voice address is …, but the internet sees this server as …The server's address changed: a new server, or the host gave it a new address.Run the setup again: it moves the voice address and updates server.cfg. Then restart the FiveM server.
https://… does not answer properlyUsually no certificate yet: ports 80 and 443 are closed in the host's firewall (or, for a domain, its DNS record is not ready).Open TCP 80 and 443 in the host's control panel (or fix the record), then check again.
the certificate runs out in … hour(s) and Caddy has not renewed itCaddy cannot renew it, usually because ports 80 and 443 are closed in the host's firewall. Once it runs out, players' games cannot connect to voice.Open TCP 80 and 443. Caddy's log, C:\Caddy\logs\caddy.log, says why.
this Caddy is …; certificates for an IP address are known to work from …The Caddy already on the machine is older.If the check finds no certificate, update Caddy (caddyserver.com) and run the setup again.
(a domain) does not exist on the internet yet, or points at another addressThe DNS record is missing, wrong, or still on its way.Add or fix the A record, wait a few minutes, check again.
(a domain) goes through Cloudflare's proxyThe record has the orange cloud.In Cloudflare, click it so it is grey ("DNS only").
TCP 80 or 443 is held by another programAnother web server (IIS, Apache, nginx) has the ports Caddy needs.Stop it. Or keep it: run the setup with -SkipCaddy and point that web server's HTTPS for the voice address at 127.0.0.1:7880, with WebSockets on.
all players connect over TCPUDP 7882-7893 is not getting through.Allow UDP 7882-7893 inbound in the host's firewall.
some players connect over TCPTheir own network blocks UDP.Nothing on your side. Voice works for them, but can stutter.
players can read whip_voice_secretserver.cfg sets it with setr (or sets), which sends it to every player.Run the setup with -NewKeys (it writes new lines, with plain set, into server.cfg), then restart.
the key does not match, or the voice server refused our keyserver.cfg and the voice server have different keys.Run the setup again: it writes the right lines into server.cfg. Then restart.
name is the voice system, so whip_voice is offAnother voice resource started first, and only one can run.Take its ensure out of server.cfg and restart the server.
can hear but not talkThat player's game has no microphone: FiveM's box unanswered, or refused.They open F8 and click Allow in the box. Refused earlier: they allow it in FiveM's settings and reconnect.
the voice bot is not installed, or is running but server.cfg has no whip_voicebot_token lineAn older setup ran, or this server.cfg never got the line.Run the setup again from this server's whip_voice\service: it writes the whip_voicebot_token line into its server.cfg.
the voice bot refused whip_voicebot_tokenserver.cfg and the bot have different tokens.Run the setup again: it writes the bot's line into server.cfg.
the LiveKit, caddy or voice bot service is stoppedA service did not start.Services (Win+R, services.msc) > "LiveKit voice server (whip_voice)", "Caddy web server (HTTPS for whip_voice)" or "whip_voice voice bot" > Start. If it will not start, run the setup again.

Later

  • Run the setup again whenever you like: it keeps your keys and skips what is already done. Run it when the server's address changes: the voice address moves with it, and server.cfg is updated.
  • New keys, if the secret was ever seen, pasted or shared: run "Setup voice server.bat" -NewKeys (as for a domain, above), then restart the FiveM server. It writes the new lines into server.cfg and makes the voice bot a new token too. A second server on the machine: run the setup from its whip_voice\service too, without -NewKeys.
  • Recordings from another site than Fivemanage: open C:\LiveKit\voicebot\config.json as administrator, add the site's start to audioLinks (like "https://cdn.example.com/"), and restart the "whip_voice voice bot" service. Only sites you trust: the bot downloads whatever a Phone Call card links to there.
  • Uninstall: Setup voice server.bat -Uninstall removes the LiveKit and voice bot services and the firewall rules. C:\LiveKit and Caddy are left for you to delete.
  • Never share C:\LiveKit\config.yaml, C:\LiveKit\voicebot\config.json, or the whip_voice_secret and whip_voicebot_token lines: with them, anyone can use your voice server.

Lore phone calls

For server owners and scenario builders. A lore character (one of the Director's named NPCs) phones a player, and a recorded line plays into the call as them talking. It needs whip_voice and its voice bot (Setting up whip_voice).

1. Record the line

Any recorder works: a phone's voice memos, or Audacity on a PC. Save it as mp3, ogg or wav, up to 2 minutes and 15 MB. A minute of mp3 is about 1 MB.

2. Put it where the voice bot can reach it

WhereHowName it as
Fivemanagefivemanage.com > Dashboard > Storage > Upload. Tick Retention Exempt (Fivemanage can delete files after a set time), then Upload All. Open the file and copy its link. Anyone with the link can listen to it.The link: https://r2.fivemanage.com/abc123/irwin-intro.mp3
A resource of yoursPut the file in it, like my_story/audio/irwin_intro.ogg, and ensure the resource. Don't list it in files {}: the voice bot reads it on the server, and players never download it. This is how a story ships with its voice lines.@my_story/audio/irwin_intro.ogg

3. Hear it

You need a lore character (/whip > Director > Lore characters) and a phone with a SIM on you. With dev tools on (/w), type:

/lorecall https://r2.fivemanage.com/abc123/irwin-intro.mp3
/lorecall @my_story/audio/irwin_intro.ogg mags      -- from a named lore character (its key)

Your phone rings from the lore character's number. Answer it: the line plays, they hang up, and chat says how it went (Heard it all: the voice bot works.).

4. In a scenario

Add a Phone Call card (the green Lore group) and fill in From (the lore character; empty is the scenario's own), Recording (the link or the @ name) and To (the players). It goes on by how the call went, so the story can react:

OutcomeWhen
Heard it allThey answered and heard it to the end.
Hung up earlyThey hung up while it played.
Declined · MissedThey declined it, or it rang out.
Busy · No phoneAlready on a call, or no phone with a SIM on them.
Didn't workIt could not ring at all; the run says why (below).

For several players, each gets their own call, and the card goes on by the best of their outcomes. In the Director's Test the card runs for real, but rings only you, the one testing. Each player sets how loud calls are for them in the phone's Settings > Sounds > Call volume (the same as Phone call volume in Server Settings).

The caller's picture. To give a lore character a face on the phone, pick them in /whip > Director > Lore characters and press Edit picture under their picture (Add picture when they have none). Paste a Fivemanage picture link into the box, drag the picture to choose what shows, zoom with the slider, and press Save. It shows on the call screen and in Contacts, Messages and Recents for anyone who has the character saved. Players set their own picture the same way, in the phone's Settings > My card. The links accepted are Picture links accepted in /whip → Settings → Config → Server (Fivemanage by default).

When it doesn't play

It saysWhat to do
only links starting with https://r2.fivemanage.com/ are acceptedUse a Fivemanage file link, or put the file in a resource and use its @ name. Another site: add its start to Config.VoiceBot.audioLinks in whip_voice's config.lua (with your own voice server, its config.json).
the recording is over 120 seconds · over 15 MBShorten it, or save it as mp3.
there is no irwin_intro.ogg · the resource my_story is not startedCheck the path inside the resource, and that the resource is ensured.
You need a phone with a SIM on youThe call rings the phone you carry.
needs whip_voice and its voice botwhip_voice is not started, or its voice bot is not set up (/voicecheck checks the bot).

Lore characters speak

For server owners and scenario builders. A lore character says lines out loud in the world, from its NPC: heard exactly like a player's voice, by the players near it, from its head, through walls and cars, its mouth moving. It greets players who walk up, says goodbye when they leave, and reacts when they bump it or point a gun at it. It needs whip_voice and its voice bot, like Lore phone calls.

1. Give it lines

Upload each recording to Fivemanage as for a phone call (above), then open /whip > Director > Lore characters, pick the character and open their Audio tab. Press + Variant on a line, paste the recording's link, and add a subtitle if you like (it shows above its head as each player starts hearing the line, so it never comes before the voice; a player too far to hear it sees it at once). Add as many variants as you want: it takes them in turn, so it never says the same thing twice running. Play plays one at you, as it will sound. Then Save.

LineWhen it says it
HelloA player walks up to it (Hello when this close, 4 m). Once, until they have walked off and Greet again after (3 minutes) has passed.
GoodbyeA player it met walks away (Goodbye when this far, 10 m).
React positive · React negativeWhen a scenario's Lore Says card or a script asks: something went its way, or did not.
Bumped into · Hit by a car · Gun aimed at it · Gunfire nearby · Its car stolenA player does it to it. The same reaction again only after Same reaction again after (6 s); a reaction cuts in on whatever it was saying.

A line it has no variant for is simply not said. Its NPC must be in the world: a scenario NPC that is that lore character (the NPC's Lore character picker), standing or spawned by a card.

2. In a scenario

Add a Lore Says card (the green Lore group): Who (empty is the scenario's own), Line, and Wait until it has been said. It goes on by done or failed (its NPC is not in the world, it has no such line, or no voice bot; the run's log says why).

For a line only one scenario needs, add a Play Custom Voice Line card instead: Who, the Recording link (pasted in as a voice line's variant is, the same links accepted; Play it at you hears it as it sounds from their NPC), an optional Subtitle, If it is already talking (say it after, the default; cut in; or skip it), and Wait until it has been said. It is said the same way, heard by the players near the NPC, and goes on by Said, Could not or Took too long.

Both cards have a Bonus range slider (0 to 250 m), for a line said where players may not be close: from a car ahead of them, across a yard. For that line the character is heard at full volume that many metres further out than usual, fading away over the usual distance past it, and its subtitle is seen as far, growing with the distance so it stays readable. A line whose range just grew waits a second, so the players now in reach hear it from the start. The next line is back to the usual unless it has a bonus of its own.

3. The settings

In /whip → Settings → Config → Emotes, /me and talk: Lore characters speak (on/off) and Voice line links accepted (Fivemanage by default). The voice range (15 m) and the Hello, Goodbye and reaction timings above are Config.LoreVoice in config.lua.

4. From your own resource

LoreSay(key, line, opts)SERVER

A lore character says one of its voice lines from its NPC in the world, as the Lore Says card does. opts = { near = source, npcId, wait, busy }: near picks its NPC nearest that player (else npcId, else the first); wait = true answers once it has been said; busy ('skip', 'queue', 'cut') overrides the line's own If talking. It WAITS while the recording is fetched: call it from a thread or a handler.

local ok, why = exports.whip_core:LoreSay('irwin', 'positive', { near = source })
Returns: true (or true, 'queued'), or false, why: no such character, no NPC of it in the world, no such line, no voice bot. With wait, also when whip_voice stopped or the NPC went before it was said
CheckPicture(url, frame)SERVER

A profile picture as whip takes one, for a resource that keeps its own (whip_phone: a player's contact card): the link must be on the accepted sites (Picture links accepted), and its framing ({ x, y, z }: where its middle is, 0 to 100 across and down, and the zoom, 1 to 3, as Edit picture makes) is cleaned; the plain framing (the middle, no zoom) is none. An empty link is no picture.

Returns: true, frame (frame nil for none, and for an empty link), or false, why

Voice for other resources

Your resource can use voice (a phone's calls, an intercom, a dispatch channel, a bugged room) without knowing which voice system runs. Never call one by name: Whip.voice, in @whip_core/lib/satellite.lua, calls whichever is running. Everything here is server side, except asking which voice system runs.

A line is a set of players who hear each other wherever they are, through a sound you choose. It carries what they say with their normal talk key (a 'voice' line), or with the radio key (a 'radio' line). The people around them still hear them as usual. A line is yours: it closes when your resource stops.

Whip.voice(name, …) · Whip.voiceSystem()SERVER CLIENT

Whip.voice calls one of the running voice system's exports (below) and answers what it answers, or false, 'no voice system is running'. Whip.voiceSystem() answers which voice system runs (GetVoiceSystem's answer), or false.

-- An intercom between the gate and the guard's desk (server.lua)
local lineId, why = Whip.voice('OpenLine', {
    members = { visitor, guard },
    recipe  = { { 'band', low = 300, high = 3400 }, { 'gain', db = -2 } },
    onEnd   = function(id, reason) print('intercom closed: ' .. reason) end,
})
if not lineId then return false, why end
Returns: the export's answer, or false, reason
OpenLine(spec)SERVER

Open a line: Whip.voice('OpenLine', spec). Its members are players with a character loaded; one not in voice yet is linked once they are.

FieldTypeWhat it is
membersnumber[]Server ids, at most 32. More later with AddLineMember.
trackstring?'voice' (default: the talk key) or 'radio' (the radio key).
recipetable|string?How it sounds at the far end: a list of sound blocks, or the name of one from RegisterSound. None: the plain voice.
speakerRangenumber?1-30 m (default 8): how far a member's device on speaker carries.
pickupboolean?On speaker, the people near the device are heard on the line too, where the voice system has the pickup feature (whip_voice does).
qualitytable?{ clear = metres, range = metres }: worse with distance, gone past range.
sameWorldboolean?Only members in the same routing bucket hear each other.
minMembersnumber?Fewer members than this (default 2) and the line closes by itself.
onEndfunction?(lineId, why): the line closed by itself ('empty'). Not called when you close it.
onLeavefunction?(lineId, src, why): a member went ('left', 'logout', 'removed').
-- A call between two players, sounding like a phone. With minMembers 2 it closes by itself
-- when either leaves or logs out; onEnd says so.
local lineId, why = Whip.voice('OpenLine', {
    members = { caller, callee }, pickup = true, minMembers = 2,
    recipe  = { { 'band', low = 300, high = 3400 }, { 'compress', threshold = -24, ratio = 4 } },
    onEnd   = function(id, reason) print(('call %s over: %s'):format(id, reason)) end,
})
Returns: the line's id (yours to keep), or false, reason
The other line callsSERVER

All through Whip.voice, and only on your own lines.

CallWhat it does
CloseLine(lineId)Everyone on it lets go at once. A line already closed answers true.
AddLineMember(lineId, src) · RemoveLineMember(lineId, src)Put a player on it, or take one off.
SetLineSpeaker(lineId, src, on)That member's device plays the line out loud to the people near it.
SetLineMuted(lineId, src, on)The line stops hearing that member. The people near them still do.
SetLineRecipe(lineId, recipe)A new sound for the line.
GetLine(lineId){ id, track, members = { [src] = { speaker, muted } }, pickup, sameWorld, speakerRange, minMembers }
RegisterSound(name, recipe)Keep a recipe under a name (letters, digits, -, _), then open lines with recipe = name. Answers its full name, '<your_resource>:<name>'.
IsVoiceReady(src)Is that player connected to voice?
Whip.voice('SetLineSpeaker', lineId, callee, true)   -- the callee's phone on speaker
Whip.voice('SetLineMuted', lineId, caller, true)     -- the far side stops hearing the caller
Whip.voice('CloseLine', lineId)                         -- hang up
Returns: true (GetLine: the table; RegisterSound: the name), or false, reason

Sound recipes

A recipe is a list of blocks, in order, each with its settings: { { 'band', low = 300, high = 3400 }, { 'drive', k = 1.5 } }. It is data, never code, and it is checked before it plays: a setting left out takes its default, a number out of range is brought into it, and a block that does not exist is refused. At most 24 blocks, 4 of them ones that make sound of their own (noise, breakup, radio, hum, chorus, vibrato, tremolo, ringmod, reverb). whip_voice plays every block.

BlockSettings (default)What it does
gaindb (0)Louder or quieter.
lowpass · highpasshz (3000 · 300), q (0.7)Cut the highs above, or the lows below, hz.
bandpass · notchhz (1200 · 1000), q (0.7)Only a band around hz, or that band taken out.
bandlow (300), high (3400), qKeep low to high: a telephone.
peak · lowshelf · highshelfhz, db (0), qBoost or cut a band, the lows, or the highs.
drivek (2.5), oversampleSoft clipping: grit, harder the bigger k.
crushsteps (32)A digital edge.
compressthreshold (-24), ratio (4), knee, attack, releaseLoud and quiet squeezed together, like a phone line.
noisekind (white, pink, brown), level (0.02), hz, qA hiss under the voice, only while they talk.
humhz (50), level (0.02)A mains hum under the voice, only while they talk.
breakupstatic (0.06)Drops out more the weaker the line (its quality), with static in the gaps.
beepsup, down, down2 (Hz), levelA beep as they start and stop talking.
panto (-1 left to 1 right)Towards one ear.
echo · reverbtime, feedback, mix · size, mixRepeats, or a room around the device.
chorus · vibrato · tremolorate, depth (mix)A wavering copy, a wavering pitch, a pulsing loudness.
ringmodhz (50), mix (1)A robot.
radiostatic (0.06), distortion (1)whip_voice's walkie-talkie, breaking up with distance.
GetVoiceSystem()SERVER CLIENT

Which voice system runs, or false when none does. Offer only what it can do: its features say so. On the client, the local event whip_core:voice:systemChanged ({ resource, label, features }, all nil when none runs) says when it changes.

Featurewhip_voiceWhat it means
linestrueThe line calls above work.
speakertrueSetLineSpeaker plays a line out loud near a device.
pickuptrueOn speaker, the people near the device are heard on the line.
qualitytrueA line's quality breaks up with distance.
sounds'full''full', every sound block played, or 'basic', a phone or radio filter at most.
local v = Whip.voiceSystem()
if v and not v.features.pickup then
    -- on speaker, only the people near hear the other side: say so in your UI
end
Returns: { resource, label, features }, or false
RegisterVoiceSystem(info)SERVER

For writing a voice resource of your own: make it the voice system. One at a time: refused, naming the other, while another runs; let go when your resource stops. A voice system answers the line calls above with the same arguments, registers the radio and megaphone items, turns whip_core:voice:rangeChanged (the Z key) into metres, and lights the HUD with SetVoiceTalking(talking, mode?).

Whip.register(function()
    local ok, why = exports.whip_core:RegisterVoiceSystem({
        label = 'my_voice',
        features = { lines = true, speaker = true, pickup = false, quality = false, sounds = 'basic' },
    })
    if not ok then print('voice stays off: ' .. why) return end
    -- ... the rest of your registrations
end)
Returns: true, or false, reason

Running whip

For server owners. This part of the docs needs no code: running the server, whip's settings, the admin tools, and building the world in game. (Settings pages, after Configuration, is for whoever writes a resource.) The parts of the developer guides written for you carry a Server owners tag.

What happens behind each Quick Start step, and what to do when one goes wrong. The whip setup block in the server console is the first place to look: it checks OneSync, the game build, the database, the picture packs, the satellites, voice, and any resource that fights whip, and each line marked FIX gives the line that fixes it. Type whipsetup in the server console to see it again.

The database

whip needs MariaDB 10.2.3 or newer, or MySQL 8.0.16 or newer, because older versions ignore the rules that stop a bank balance going below zero. whip_core reads the version as it starts, and the setup report says when it is too old.

When the server starts, whip_core first waits for oxmysql to reach the database. While it can't, the console says every 30 seconds what to check (the connection string, and that MySQL or MariaDB is running), and players who join are told the server is still starting. With no mysql_connection_string at all, whip_core stops and prints the line to add.

On the first start, whip_core creates every table it uses. whip_phone, which keeps tables of its own, does the same. After an update, whip_core changes its tables to match on the next start, so there is never an SQL file to run. If a table can't be created or read, whip_core stops starting and says why in the console rather than running half built, and players are told the server did not start until it is fixed.

WHIPFX's oxmysql

WHIP's txAdmin recipe installs WHIPFX's build of oxmysql (github.com/WHIPFX/oxmysql): oxmysql 2.14.3 with one fix. With it, a query made while no database connection is available (the database is down or restarting) answers its caller with an error at once. Stock oxmysql works with WHIP too, but without the fix such a query can wait for ever; whip_core gives up on one after 65 seconds. The setup report says which of the two your server runs. To get the fix on a server running stock oxmysql, replace its oxmysql folder with the latest release from github.com/WHIPFX/oxmysql/releases (or make the edits in whip_core/dev/oxmysql-p001.diff by hand).

A player's first download

Most of what a player downloads the first time they join is whip's pictures and videos: about 510 MB, in 5 media packs of up to 145 MB each. A pack is downloaded again only when it changes.

An Enhanced server stops downloading any one file after about two minutes, which cuts off a player slower than about 1.2 MB/s partway through a pack. The sv_resourceFileDownloadTimeout 600000 line in the Quick Start raises that to ten minutes. Legacy has no such limit.

Legacy and Enhanced

FiveM runs on both versions of GTA V: Legacy (the FXServer server) and Enhanced (the cfx-server server). One whip runs on both, and almost everything works the same. A script can't reliably tell which one it is on, so an Enhanced server says so with setr whip_platform enhanced. The setup report warns when this server looks like the other platform. To see what your own game was told, turn developer mode on in /w and type whipplatform in F8. Developers: Writing for both platforms.

Configuration

whip_core's settings start in its config.lua, read by whip_core's server and client alike. /whip → Settings → Config has the ones an owner changes (features on or off, money, sizes and times players feel, the first scenes players see, the HUD's look), checks what you type, and applies it. The rest on this page (timings, reaches, fine tuning) are config.lua's alone, each explained beside it there. Most take effect at once, for every player; the few marked Next restart wait for whip_core's next start. Another resource cannot read whip_core's Config (its own Config is a different table); where it needs a value, whip has an export for it, such as GetPockets().

Changing a setting in game

Only a permanent admin sees Config: whip.devtools given in server.cfg, not dev tools given in the Player Manager. Pick a group on the left, change what you need, and press Apply.

  • Checked as you type. A box with a mistake says why under it and is left out of Apply until it is fixed. The server checks every value again, and one Apply is all or nothing: if it refuses a value, nothing is saved, and the bar at the bottom names the setting and why.
  • Each row shows its default (the value in config.lua), Reset to go back when it differs, and who changed it last and when.
  • Positions have Use where I stand: stand where you want it, press it, then Apply. Camera shots (the landing page) are one card of place, turn and zoom. Place camera hides the panel and flies a free camera from the shot as noclip flies (WASD, the mouse, the wheel zooms; on a controller the sticks, the triggers and the D-pad). Enter fills all three in and brings the panel back for Apply, Esc leaves them as they were. Use my camera takes the camera you are looking through now. A character place's hero shot is made in the world instead: Edit in world stands the character there to move like furniture, Pose picks an emote for them, and Use this view takes the camera you have flown to.
  • Fixed rows are shown but cannot change here, with the reason on the row: the lists the database is first filled from, such as Garages and Shops. Each has a button to the section where the real ones are edited.

What is saved wins over config.lua. config.lua stays the default: edit it, and every setting nobody changed in the panel follows it, while one changed in the panel keeps the panel's value until you press Reset. Saved values live in the database (whip_settings; every change, old and new, is also in whip_settings_log) and are copied to settings.json beside config.lua, which players' games read as they load. Values only the server needs go to server_settings.json, which players never download. Do not edit either file: at every start, whip rewrites them from the database wherever they differ.

Resources built on whip can add their own pages beside Config, under the same Settings group: see Settings pages.

Items are changed on the Items page, not here: config.lua's items with every other item, each with its own settings (/whip → Economy → Items).

Characters & money

Cash handed over in the world is not followed. false allows it

Joining: the landing page, character screen and creator: each is a table of camera shots and timings, explained beside it in config.lua

SettingDefaultDescription
LandingtableThe first screen after the loading screen: one camera shot with the whip logo and "Press any button to continue". enabled = false goes straight to the character screen. Also its camera, prompt text, look (sky and clock), fades and streamMs. Shown when joining and after a whip_core restart; /logout goes straight to the character screen
CharSelecttableThe character screen. slots is one hero shot per character place, as many as MaxCharacters (up to 30): its camera, where the character stands (pos), a pose (scenario, anim or an emote name), its own look, and the scene's props. A place with no shot of its own (false, or past the end) shows one that exists; shot 1 must exist. Made in game: Config → Joining → Edit in world. Then quietBucket (no traffic or people), preloadShots, and spawnPicker: after Play the camera looks up, the 3D map comes down over it and the player picks where to arrive, then the map drops into their arrival (false: Play fades to black, as before; a dead or brand new character always gets the fade). Its fades are Config.CharSelectFades
SpawnPointstableThe spawn picker's places, beside where the character last was and the properties they own or have a key to: { id, label, pos } per place, pos a vector4. Server only. Made in game: Config → Joining → Spawn points (shown while Choose where to arrive is on), Here
CreatortableWhere a new character stands while they are made (spawn), its look, and the fades and holds either side of it. Saving sends them to DefaultSpawn. maxOutfits (20, up to 100): the most outfits one character keeps in the character editor's Outfits tab, where the clothes and accessories on now are saved by name and put back on with one press (never the face, hair or tattoos). Saving, renaming and deleting an outfit is kept at once; putting one on is kept by the editor's Save
ArrivalScenestableWhat plays as the picture comes back after picking a character: one of GTA's own character-switch scenes, with the game's own camera move, where the player is (onFoot, one at random; a scene whose walk would go through a wall is passed over; inside a building, a game interior, a property or under a roof, only the lines marked indoors). Someone who left sitting in a car that is still within vehicleRange (400 m) comes back in it, in their seat or the first free one, and wakes up there (inVehicle; on a bicycle, boat or aircraft, no scene). Left on a motorbike: it is stood back up and they arrive beside it (onBike). Left on foot with a car of theirs within nearCarRange (25 m): they arrive at it (nearCar). A line may start part way in (from, 0-1) and end early (to), be lined up with a real vehicle, which keeps its own physics while a door opens as a hand reaches its handle (vehicleClip), and end with them in the seat (getsIn). When it ends the camera stays on the last shot, free to look around, and eases back behind them as they move (the game's own catch-up camera; in a car it cuts back). enabled = false: the picture just fades up. All of it is also in /whip → Settings → Config → Joining: each list shows its scenes with where each starts and ends, Add scenes picks from every switch scene in the game (client/arrival_list.lua), and Watch plays one where you stand (in the seat you sit in, or by the car you stand next to for a scene made with one). A scene can carry its prop (prop: a cigar, a phone, a bottle); a line with none takes the game's own.

Game feel and controls

The minimap is whip's own 3D map, in GTA's radar's place: top-down on foot, tilted in a vehicle and zooming out with speed, turning with the camera, with the blips (turned and flashing as the game has them), the waypoint and the GPS line on it. Each player tunes it in the pause menu's Server Settings → Minimap, beside a live preview of it: on foot or not, its frame rate (120, 60, 45, 30 or 15), its border, north always up or turning with the camera, the player in its centre or a little below, the markers' size and whether they turn with the map, how much of the map it shows on foot, in a vehicle when slow and at top speed, the speeds the zoom runs between, its tilt on foot and in a vehicle, and a tilt that changes with speed. GTA's radar is shown only while /radardebug is open

'black': black discs in a white rim that drains, no capsule behind them (it shows for a notification or chat), a white frame round the minimap (each player picks it in Server Settings → Minimap → Border: the full frame, an outline like an empty gauge's, or none) and the waypoint route in blue. The gauges sit under the frame in five places, the first under its left edge; a gauge that is turned off leaves its place and the ones after it close up. 'classic': discs that fill white, inside the capsule. The minimap sits in the frame's box in either look; /radardebug's frame row moves it. The vehicle dial is not part of it

Each is one of whip's actions ('radial', 'engine', 'inventory', 'sprint'), another resource's (any a resource registers), or false: free, so a resource's action that asks for that button goes there. whip's default names whip's own resources' actions on their buttons: dpad_up = 'phone', veh_a = 'nitrous', lb_a = 'talk', lb_b = 'gunny_check_ammo', lb_x = 'radio'. A named action keeps its button: another resource's that asks for it gets none (F8 says so), and while the named one's resource is not running another may use it. Each action goes on one button. Players change their own in the pause menu (Controller), saved on their PC, and "Reset to whip's default" gives them Layout again. RadialHoldMs (holding the radial's button opens it), SprintDoubleClickMs (two presses sprint), SprintOnA. With more than one, the keyboard has a key to switch, and each player picks theirs in the pause menu (Server Settings → Controller → Keyboard language); until they do, they get the language GTA is set to, if it is listed. InteractRenderer'world'How prompts are drawn. 'world': shapes in the 3D world, with no lag, and hidden behind walls. 'nui': a browser overlay, a frame or two behind the camera. Door prompts are made for 'world': under 'nui' they still show, but flat to the screen, from both sides of the door, with the word lock or unlock in the circle
Interact3DtableThe 'world' prompts' look: badgePx and labelPx (size on screen at InteractActiveRange), fades, the stacked options of a multi-choice prompt, the picture above a label, and depthBias, how far a prompt is pulled toward you so the thing it labels does not cover it. badgePx is every prompt's size; for one family of prompts, use that prompt's own scale. theme: the prompts' shape, 'keycap' (square, the default) or 'classic' (round): what players get until they pick their own in the pause menu (Server Settings → Map & HUD → Prompt shape). dark: black and white swapped (a black key with a white outline and symbol, black words outlined white), off by default; each player can switch it in the same place (Dark prompts). styles: named looks a prompt can wear (subtle and lively ship), and groupStyles: which one each family of whip's own prompts wears (empty by default; for example ground_items = 'subtle'), see Styles
DoorHandleAlong / DoorHandleHeight0.85 / 1.05Where a door's circle sits: how far toward the free edge (a fraction of the door's width) and how high from the bottom of the model, in metres. A garage door (wider than 1.7 m) has no handle spot: its padlock slides across the door with the player at DoorHandleHeight, lies on the door as it swings up, and says "Open Garage" or "Close Garage" (every other door's says nothing)
DoorPromptOffsets{}For door models that rule places wrongly (double gates, shutters): [GetHashKey('model')] = { x = …, y = …, z = … }, one entry per model. x runs along the door from its origin, y is half the panel's thickness, z is height from the origin (not from the bottom, as DoorHandleHeight is)
GroundItemCellSize and ZoneCellSize (both 50) are spatial-grid cell sizes. Both sides read the one shared config.lua, so they cannot disagree unless something overrides one side; ZoneCellSize is read by the client's zone grid only. GroundItemCellSize also cuts the grid door and ground updates travel on: keep it well above 25 m.

Vehicles

SettingDefaultDescription
VehicleTrunkSlots / VehicleTrunkMaxWeight40 / 200.0Boot capacity
VehicleGloveboxSlots / VehicleGloveboxMaxWeight10 / 20.0Glovebox capacity
MotorbikeGloveboxSlots1A motorbike's glovebox slots, unless the bike or its model has its own. A bicycle has no glovebox, and needs no key to ride
VehicleKeySlots / VehicleKeyMaxWeight1 / 1.0Ignition slot: one key
VehicleLockRange8.0Distance to lock or unlock with the L key
UnlockOnExittrueGetting out of a locked car unlocks it (GTA lets anyone open a locked door from inside). false: it stays locked behind them
LockpickGame'ring'The skill check whip's own lockpicks and ignition hack play: 'ring', or a game another resource adds (RegisterSkillCheckGame). If that resource is not running, the ring is played and the console says so
Seats{ NoAutoShuffle = true }Passengers stay in their seat: no slide into an empty driver's seat, the passenger door gives the passenger seat, and GTA's shuffle button does nothing. false is GTA's own way. See Vehicles & Keys, Seats
VehicleTrunkRange2.5Distance from the rear of the vehicle to open the boot
GarageSpotRadius3.5How close to a bay's middle a car must be to be in that bay (and stored there). Whether a bay is occupied goes by its outline instead (GaragePositionHelper's length × width): a vehicle whose body overlaps it, so a car in the bay beside it never counts
Fuelwhip_fuelFuel, petrol pumps, jerry cans and the pump's hose are the whip_fuel resource's, set in its own config.lua and in /whip → Settings → Fuel. Without it whip has no fuel at all: cars just drive. With it: a tank on every car that driving burns (an empty one's engine will not run, though the car still rolls), every side of every pump a nozzle of its own (take it, put it in the car's filler, choose how much at the pump and pay; the LTD pump's screen shows how it is going), a jerry can poured at a car's doors or filled at a pump, and with whip_rope running a hose a car can tear the pump off its island with
VehicleStatsengineThe gauges every car carries, defined like Stats: range, saving, decay and where the gauge sits around the rev dial. engine is whip's and cannot be replaced; a resource adds its own with RegisterVehicleStat (whip_fuel's fuel)
VehicleDamage{ remember = true, engineFloor = 100 }Cars keep their engine and body damage, doors torn off and burst tyres through the garage and a restart (dents are not kept). remember = false: every car comes back like new. engineFloor: the lowest engine health a car comes back at, so a wreck never spawns on fire. See Damage a car keeps
VehicleHudtableThe rev dial at the bottom right while in a vehicle (not on bicycles or trains). In a helicopter or plane it shows flight instruments instead of revs: an attitude indicator, airspeed and altitude tapes, and the landing gear light; on a boat it reads engine power, 0 to 100%, with F / N / R and the anchor light. The vehicle stats (fuel first) orbit the dial up its left side (over its top in an aircraft), and the four segments under it light with the status light above each one. attitude ('ball', a 3D gyro horizon, or 'flat'), flipBank (true if the horizon tips the wrong way when banking), speedUnit ('mph' or 'kmh'), rpmMax (the top of the dial, in thousands, 2 to 20), redline (where its red zone starts, as a share of the dial), rpmElectric (the top for an electric motor: 20), idleRpm (where the needle rests at idle, in thousands, the same for every engine: 0.8 is 800 rpm; an electric motor's rests at 0), idleMeasured (true: each engine rests at its own idle instead, measured from the game's engine recordings, data/rpm_by_model.lua; most come out between 1,000 and 1,400), rpmByClass (the top for a kind of engine, by name: openwheel = 15), rpmByModel (for one model's engine: sultan = 8.5, beating everything else) and dashSkins (true: each car's dial wears that car's own GTA dashboard look, its face colour, fonts, number and needle colours, from data/dash_skins.lua, 555 vehicles; false: every car gets the dial as designed; a car with no dashboard art of its own in GTA, and every aircraft, keeps the dial as designed either way). The dial goes by the vehicle's engine, not its body: a car with an engine swapped in (whip_autos, through SetVehicleRevRange) revs like the engine's model and kind. While you drive, GTA only says how far between idle and flat out an engine is, so the top of the dial and where the needle rests at idle are these settings, and the rev limiter is the top of the dial. A player can switch the whole vehicle HUD off and on for themselves with /vehiclehud (or /vehiclehud off / on), for performance tests; it comes back on at reconnect
VehicleStatsTickInterval1Seconds between the server's checks for vehicle stats that declare a decay; each still changes only once per its own decayInterval. No built-in stat decays, so on a stock server it does nothing. Changing it needs a restart
VehiclePositionSaveInterval / VehiclePositionEpsilon30 / 2.0Seconds between saving where cars are, and metres a car must have moved to be saved. Garaging, despawning and stopping whip_core save it at once anyway; this bounds what a crash loses
VehicleStorageKeepRange5.5How far a player can stray from a car and still move things in its boot or glovebox. Below VehicleTrunkRange + 3.0 it has no effect
DrivingCamera{ Enabled = true, Default = false, Shake = 1.0 }The driving camera each player can switch on in Server Settings → Vehicles. Enabled = false: nobody can, and the row is hidden. Default: whether a player who never chose has it on. Shake: 0 never shakes, 1 as made, up to 3
BikeAutoHelmetfalseGTA's helmet put on a character getting onto a motorbike. false: they ride in what they wear on their head; true: GTA's helmet
ExperimentalDriveSyncfalseA Director car playing a recorded drive. false: one player's game drives it and everyone else sees it as the network sends it. true: every other game plays the drive itself, on a copy only it has, so it is smooth and in the same place on every screen (the Director has the details). Also in /whip → Settings → Config →Vehicles
InteractPresstableThe hand press for doors, the boot, the bonnet, ATMs, pumps and any prompt marked press (PlayPress): enabled (true; false: no presses, the thing just happens on E), maxDistance (2.5 m: further, no press) and followHand (true: the hand keeps reaching while the player moves). Picking things up off the ground still plays GTA's grab. enabled is also Hand press in /whip → Settings → Config →World & gameplay
LogVehicleStoragefalseLogs every boot, glovebox and ignition open on both sides (one line per keypress), for finding why one did not open. Off by default
VehiclePartPromptstableThe circles on a car's boot, bonnet and doors: for each, enabled, where it sits (drop, rise, clearance), range, activeRange and scale. The boot and bonnet circles stay where the shut panel puts them, open or not. An open door also gets a circle on its inside that closes it; the doors' inset is how far in from the handle (the door's thickness). bike, bicycle and boat are the one circle each of those has (get on or board, refuel, store), at the handlebar on your side or the boat's windscreen: only enabled, range, activeRange and scale, as they sit where the vehicle's own parts say (/vehpoints shows where)
VehiclePartPromptScan15.0How far away a car gets its part prompts set up, so they are ready before they should show
VehiclePartOpenAngle70.0Degrees a door swings when fully open: how much further its circles reach, and where they sit on a car without door-handle points
VehiclePartHingeTopFrac / VehiclePartHinges0.52 / {}How whip guesses which way a boot opens (a lid that hangs, a tailgate that stands), and the per-model fix when it guesses wrong
VehicleFillers{}Which side of a car its fuel goes in, by model: left, right or rear. Without a row it goes above a rear wheel at door-handle height, on a side picked once per model (a truck's side tank, where it has one). /vehpoints beside the car shows where
VehicleMakeLogos{}Maker badges on a garage's car list come from the game's own make names. This maps the ones whose logo file is spelled differently, e.g. ['emperor'] = 'emporer'; a make with no logo prints its name to the console once
GarageSpotPromptHeight1.22How high, in metres, a parking bay's prompt floats above the ground

Furnisher and props: the editor a home's owner places furniture with

FurnishPlaceRange8.0A picked prop appears on whatever you are looking at, this close; further away, 3 m in front of you

Enabled (true; false: they stay silent), Links (where a recording may come from, as LorePictureLinks; the voice bot fetches them, players never download them), Range (15 m), GreetRange (4 m: closer, its Hello line), ByeRange (10 m: further, after a hello, its Goodbye line), GreetAgainMinutes (3), ReactAgainSeconds (6) and Gestures (true: it moves its hands as it talks)
PropertySignPosts2 boardsThe For Sale boards a property can stand by: each a prop (model, streamed by whip_core), its label in the property tools, its blank panel where the listing is printed (its middle in metres from the prop's base, w and h), the listing's colours (ink, accent) and back = true for a board printed on both sides. Code-side: a new board needs its panel measured. config.lua only, not in the panel

Each names a glyph the furnisher draws (html/js/furnisher-data.js)
PropSeeds{}Your own props, on top of the 15,000 or so whip ships with (every prop in the game: 1,361 hand-picked, the rest from server/prop_catalog_seed_world.lua): ['prop_model'] = 'category', or { category = …, name = … }. Each is added once, so one you later take out with /prop remove stays out. In game, /prop add <category> adds the prop you look at. /propcheck (developer mode) spawns every prop the furnisher offers once, out of sight, and hides each one that does not spawn; it carries on where it stopped, and a prop that crashed the game is hidden next time

Settings pages for your resource

Your resource's settings can sit in /whip beside Config, so whoever runs the server never opens your config file. Declare them and whip does the rest: the page, the checks, saving, sending each change to every player, and calling you back. The page is a section of its own under Settings, named by your label, and only permanent admins see it, as with Config.

Saved values follow the resource's folder name. whip keeps them under the name the server runs your resource by, so a server owner who renames the folder (mycafe to mycafe-v2) starts from your defaults again, with the old values still saved under the old name. Say so in your install notes: keep the folder name across updates.

Declare the page on both sides, in a shared script, inside Whip.register: the server checks and saves, and each player's game needs your defaults and its own callbacks. The examples after the first leave out where the code sits.

RegisterSettings(def)SERVER CLIENT

Declare your resource's settings page. Values saved before are checked again now: one that no longer passes (you lowered a max) is forgotten with a line in the console, and your default stands.

FieldTypeDescription
labelstringThe page's name in the Settings group, up to 40 characters
settingstableThe settings, in order: one entry each (below)
groupstable|nilIn place of settings, for a long page: { { label = 'Prices', settings = { … } }, … }, each a group on the left

Each entry:

FieldTypeDescription
keystringThe name you read it by: letters, digits, _ and ., starting with a letter or _, up to 64. Unique on the page. A dot makes it a path: a callback on 'prices' also hears 'prices.coffee'
typestring'int', 'number', 'bool', 'string', 'enum', 'vec3', 'vec4', 'list', 'records', 'map' or 'record': one card of fields on the page, each field a setting of its own ('turbo.gain' for the field gain of the card turbo), its default that field of the card's default table
defaultanyIts value until an admin changes it. It must pass the entry's own checks, or that setting is left off the page (the console says which); the page is refused only when none pass
shownWhentable|nil{ path = 'key', equals = value }: the row (a card: all of it) shows only while that setting of yours is that value, so a distance sits under the switch it belongs to
label / helpstringThe row's name, and the line under it
min / max / stepnumber|nilint and number: the range, and how far the box's arrows move it
unitstring|nilint and number: shown beside the box. '$' goes in front, anything else ('m', 'ms') after
optionstableenum: the choices, { { value = 'slow', label = 'Slow' }, … }
maxLen / pattern / patternWhynumber / stringstring: the most characters; a Lua pattern the text must match (start it with ^ and end it with $ to hold the whole text to it); and the words shown when it does not
nullable / emptyLabelboolean / stringAn empty box is a value (nil), and what the row calls it ('none' unless you say)
offWhenEmptybooleanint, number and string: an empty box is false, "off" (a cap that can be switched off)
applystring|nil'live' (default): in force at once, on every side. 'restart': saved now, in force when your resource (or whip_core) next starts; read it as you start, as OnSettingChanged is not called for it. 'readonly': shown, never changed
whystring|nilFor a 'restart' or 'readonly' row: the reason, shown on the row
sidesstring|nil'both' (default), or 'server': kept on the server and never sent to players' games, for a key or a password. Permanent admins still see it on the page
crossfunction|nilfunction(get), run on the server when this setting is part of a save: get(key) gives any of your settings as it will be once saved. Return true, or false, 'why' to refuse the save. For a rule between two settings, give both entries the check
here / limitsboolean / tablevec3 and vec4: a Use where I stand button, and { x = { min, max }, … } for the axes that have a range
itemtablelist: what every entry is, as an entry with no key: { type = 'int', min = 1, max = 9 }. An int, number, string or enum (the panel edits a list as one line, with commas between); for a list of positions, use records with a vec3 field
fieldstablerecords, a map of rows or a record: the fields, each an entry with its key
widget / markerstring / tablewidget = 'mapPoints', for records with a vec3 field and a string field: the rows are icons on the map instead of a table. Edit on the map opens it big, where an icon is dragged to move it, clicked to rename or remove it, and added where the admin stands. marker = { sprite = 361, colour = 1, name = 'Gas Station' }: the icon (a GTA blip and blip colour) and a new row's name
eachtablemap: what every row's value is, when it is one value: { type = 'string', maxLen = 20 }
minItems / maxItems / uniquenumber / stringHow many entries or rows (a map takes maxItems only), and for records a field no two rows may share. The panel offers no Add or Remove past them, so equal ones keep a table's rows as they are
keyKind / keyPattern / keyWhystring|nilmap: keyKind = 'hash' takes a model name and keeps its hash, as GetEntityModel answers. keyKind = 'number' keeps a key typed in digits as a whole number (a mod slot, a wheel type) and any other as a name. Names are checked against keyPattern
Declare before you read. Before RegisterSettings, a setting nobody has changed has no default to give, and GetSetting answers nil. Put the declaration first in your Whip.register function: on the server, a page declared before whip_core has finished starting is refused. A page declared only on the server works there, but a player's game then has no defaults either.
The page belongs to your resource: it goes when your resource stops, and what was saved for it stays, ready for when it starts again.
Returns: boolean, string|nil: ok, and why not, naming the entry
-- shared.lua (in fxmanifest.lua: shared_script 'shared.lua', after whip's helper)
Whip.register(function()
    local ok, why = exports.whip_core:RegisterSettings({
        label = 'My Cafe',
        settings = {
            { key = 'price', type = 'int', min = 1, max = 500, unit = '$', default = 5,
              label = 'Coffee price', help = 'What one coffee costs at the counter.' },
            { key = 'open', type = 'bool', default = true,
              label = 'Counter open', help = 'Off: the counter sells nothing.' },
            { key = 'size', type = 'enum', default = 'regular', label = 'Cup size',
              options = {
                  { value = 'small', label = 'Small' },
                  { value = 'regular', label = 'Regular' },
              } },
        },
    })
    if not ok then print('settings page refused: ' .. why) end
end)
GetSetting(key)SERVER CLIENT

One of your settings as it stands: what an admin saved, else your default. Read it where you use it, not once at start, and a change to a 'live' setting counts from the next read. On a player's game, a sides = 'server' setting answers its default.

ParamTypeDescription
keystringThe entry's key
-- server.lua, in the purchase handler
if not exports.whip_core:GetSetting('open') then
    return false, 'The counter is closed'
end
local price = exports.whip_core:GetSetting('price')
Returns: any: the value (a table comes as your own copy), or nil for a key your page does not have
GetSettings()SERVER CLIENT

Every setting on your page at once, defaults included.

local s = exports.whip_core:GetSettings()
print(('coffee $%d, %s cup, counter open: %s'):format(s.price, s.size, tostring(s.open)))
Returns: table: { [key] = value }
OnSettingChanged(key, fn)SERVER CLIENT

Calls fn after one of your 'live' settings changes, on this side: on the server when an admin applies it, on each player's game when the change arrives. For what you set up once and must redo, such as a blip or a loop's timing; a value you read when you use it needs no callback. One function per key: calling again replaces it, so it belongs inside Whip.register.

ParamTypeDescription
keystringThe entry's key
fnfunctionfunction(value, old, key). It must not wait: start a thread for anything slow
-- client.lua: the counter's blip (made at start) hides while the counter is closed
Whip.register(function()
    exports.whip_core:OnSettingChanged('open', function(open)
        SetBlipAlpha(counterBlip, open and 255 or 0)
    end)
end)
Returns: boolean, string|nil

Your config.lua as the page

A resource that already reads a Config table does not need GetSetting at all. Whip.configPage, from whip's helper (@whip_core/lib/satellite.lua), puts chosen Config values on your page: each key is a path in Config, and its default is what config.lua says. What an admin saves is written into Config on both sides, as the page is declared and whenever a change arrives, so your code keeps reading Config.X. config.lua stays the default, as it does for whip_core's own settings, with one difference in timing: saved values arrive when whip_core is ready, after your files have loaded. Code that reads Config at file scope sees config.lua's values first; whatever it works out there, rebuild with Whip.onConfigChanged, which also runs as the page is declared. whip_autos is the worked example: its shared/settings.lua puts what an owner changes on a page (the prices, the power, the shifting, how far the tuning sliders go), the values of one table together as a card, and leaves the rest to config.lua; each file that works something out from Config at load rebuilds it with Whip.onConfigChanged.

Whip.configPage(def)SERVER CLIENT

Call it once, at file scope (not inside Whip.register), in a shared script loaded after config.lua: it declares the page every time whip_core is ready. A resource has one page, so use this or RegisterSettings, not both. The entries are RegisterSettings' with no default. A table setting is changed in place, so a file that kept Config.Shop in a local sees the new values.

  • A value is kept as its check gives it back: text trimmed, a keyKind = 'hash' map keyed by hashes. Config holds that form from the declaration on.
  • A sides = 'server' setting is written into the server's Config only.
  • Only data goes on a page. An entry whose value holds a function, or a row field its fields do not declare that is a table or a position, is left off with a line in the console saying which.
  • A value in config.lua its own row would refuse (outside min/max, the wrong kind) leaves just that row off the page, with a line in the console saying which and why. The rest of the page stands, and your code keeps reading config.lua's value, so clamp what you read.
FieldTypeDescription
labelstringThe page's name in the Settings group
settings / groupstableAs RegisterSettings; each key a path such as 'Tuning.EngineSwapPrice'
configtable|nilThe table the keys are in. Default Config
-- settings.lua (in fxmanifest.lua: shared_script 'settings.lua', after config.lua)
Whip.configPage({
    label = 'My Cafe',
    groups = {
        { label = 'Prices', settings = {
            { key = 'Prices.coffee', type = 'int', min = 1, max = 500, unit = '$', label = 'Coffee' },
            { key = 'Prices.bagel', type = 'int', min = 1, max = 500, unit = '$', label = 'Bagel' },
        } },
        { label = 'Counter', settings = {
            { key = 'Counter.coords', type = 'vec3', here = true, label = 'Where it stands' },
            { key = 'Counter.open', type = 'bool', label = 'Open' },
        } },
    },
})
Returns: boolean: false when def is not a page (printed). whip_core's refusal, if any, is printed with why when it is declared
Whip.onConfigChanged(path, fn)SERVER CLIENT

For what you worked out from Config at load: a price list, a thread that only starts when an option is on. fn runs after a value on your page changes on this side: an admin's change, or a saved value written over config.lua's as the page is declared. It hears its own path, anything under it ('Counter' hears 'Counter.open') and a change to a table it is inside. Call it at file scope, not inside Whip.register (there it would be added again at every whip_core restart): it lives in your resource and outlasts whip_core restarts. Do not use OnSettingChanged on a configPage key at all: one callback per key, so one of the two would be lost.

ParamTypeDescription
pathstringA path in Config
fnfunctionfunction(value, old, key): key is the path that changed and value its new value, so a hook on 'Counter.coords' that hears 'Counter' change is handed the whole Counter table. Read Config itself when in doubt. It must not wait: start a thread for anything slow
-- client.lua: the counter's blip moves with it
Whip.onConfigChanged('Counter.coords', function()
    local c = Config.Counter.coords
    SetBlipCoords(counterBlip, c.x, c.y, c.z)
end)

Each player's own settings

The pages above are the server's config, set by an admin for everyone. A choice each player makes for their own screen (how loud, which unit, shown or hidden) goes on the pause menu's Server Settings page instead, as a row of yours. Your resource keeps the value where it already does (its own KVP, on the player's PC); the page reads it with your get and changes it with your set. The row goes when your resource stops, and comes back by itself when whip_core restarts.

Whip.playerSetting(def)CLIENT

Puts a row of yours on the Server Settings page. From whip's helper (@whip_core/lib/satellite.lua); call it at file scope, it registers inside Whip.register itself. A refusal is printed in your console with the reason.

FieldTypeDescription
keystringYours, and unique: letters, digits, dots, dashes or underscores, up to 64. Start it with your resource's name ('mycafe.sounds')
labelstringThe row's name
typestring'toggle' (true / false), 'choice' (one of options), or 'slider' (a number)
getfunctionfunction() returns the value now
setfunctionfunction(value) keeps the player's new value. Save it there: the page keeps nothing of yours
defaultanyWhat "Reset this page to server defaults" puts back: a plain value its type takes (true, an option's value, a number in range). Required: a row without one is refused
groupstring?The page's tab: 'Controller', 'Vehicles', 'Map & HUD', 'Chat & voice', or a new one of yours. Default 'Other'
helpstring?One line under the row
optionstable?A choice's options, each { value, label }: two at least
min, max, step, unitnumber?, string?A slider's range, its step (default 1) and what it shows after the number
-- client.lua: each player chooses whether the café's sounds play (kept on their PC)
local sounds = GetResourceKvpInt('sounds') ~= 2   -- 2 is off; never set reads 0, so on

Whip.playerSetting({
    key     = 'mycafe.sounds',
    group   = 'Map & HUD',
    label   = 'Café sounds',
    help    = 'The till and the coffee machine.',
    type    = 'toggle',
    default = true,
    get     = function() return sounds end,
    set     = function(on)
        sounds = on
        SetResourceKvpInt('sounds', on and 1 or 2)
    end,
})
Returns: boolean: false (printed) when def has no key, get or set, or this is the server
RegisterPlayerSetting(def)CLIENT

The export under Whip.playerSetting, for a resource that does not load whip's helper. The same def; put it in Whip.register, or the row is gone after a whip_core restart. A key another running resource holds, one of whip_core's own, or a row with no default value, is refused.

Whip.register(function()
    local ok, why = exports.whip_core:RegisterPlayerSetting(soundsRow)
    if not ok then print('sounds row refused: ' .. why) end
end)
Returns: true, or false, reason
GetPlayerSetting(key)CLIENT

A row's value in force on this player's PC: their choice, else the default. Reads whip_core's own rows too, such as the dial's speed unit.

ParamTypeDescription
keystringThe row's key
local unit = exports.whip_core:GetPlayerSetting('dial.speedUnit')   -- 'mph' or 'kmh'
Returns: any, or nil for a key that is not on the page
SetPlayerSetting(key, value)CLIENT

Change a row's value on this player's PC, as the page does: for a screen of yours that shows the same setting, so the two are one. A resource's row is changed through its own set; a value out of range is brought into it. whip_phone's Settings > Sounds > Call volume is the voice system's voice.callVolume this way.

ParamTypeDescription
keystringThe row's key
valueanyA value its type takes
-- client.lua: the phone's call volume slider, changing the voice system's own setting
local ok, why = exports.whip_core:SetPlayerSetting('voice.callVolume', 75)
local now = exports.whip_core:GetPlayerSetting('voice.callVolume')   -- 75
Returns: true, or false, reason (no such setting, or a value its type does not take)

Dev Tools (/w & /whip)

Whip's admin tooling has two doors. /w is the quick menu: instant toggles that draw over the world. /whip is the Admin Panel: one themed window holding every manager as a section. Its sections are grouped: Players, Vehicles, Economy, World, Director, System and Settings. A group word opens the section you last had in that group. On a controller, LB / RB step through the tabs, on into the next group at the end of one. Push the cursor to the very top of the screen and the panel fades so you can watch the game behind it; move back down and it returns. The last entry of /w opens the panel too.

Developer mode

Holding whip.devtools is not enough on its own. A developer turns developer mode on first: /w opens to one switch, Enable developer mode?, and only once it is on does the menu show the tools. Until then the account is treated exactly as one without dev tools, everywhere: /whip, the dev commands, admin-only doors, prompts and zones, and every satellite that asks whip_core (exports.whip_core:HasDevTools(source)).

While it is on, the player wears the Developer Access Enabled mark in their HUD, so anyone watching their stream can see it. Each switch is printed in the server console and written to the activity log (dev_mode_on / dev_mode_off, with where they stood). Switching it off, by hand or because the server took dev tools back, turns everything off with it: God Mode, Invisible, Noclip, every overlay, the open editors and /whip. The mark comes off too. It is off at every join and after a whip_core restart. Swapping character keeps it, and the next character wears the mark.

A satellite that asks IsPlayerAceAllowed(src, 'whip.devtools') itself skips developer mode. Ask HasDevTools instead.

A tool acting for a developer who is away from the game turns it on or off with exports.whip_core:SetDeveloperMode(source, on) (server). It works as the switch does: on only for an account with dev tools, and logged with the resource that asked. After a whip_core restart, a tool can use it to turn developer mode back on for the developer it acts for.

Dev commands

Typed in chat or F8, with developer mode on (the server console ones in the console).

CommandWhat it does
/whipcost [seconds]Times every part of whip, and every satellite's WhipCost sections, for a while (20 s unless told; 5 to 120) with no profiler running, then prints one table, the dearest first. What your resource costs in game (Measuring your resource)
/nativecostPrices each call the controls loop makes, so a fix goes to the dear one
/paddebugDraws a controller's whole chain live: which controls are down, which button each is on, which whip has claimed and for what
/mousedebugMeasures this player's mouse speed (their GTA sensitivity), for the skill check's dot
/nuicapsPrints what this game's browser can do (GetNuiCaps) in F8
/whipplatformWhich platform this game read when whip started and reads now (Legacy or Enhanced): a wrong one means server.cfg needs setr
/vehpointsOn the vehicle you look at: where each prompt would sit on a bike, boat or aircraft, and why
/radardebugThe minimap tuner: moves its parts live and prints the numbers
/propcheck (restart)Spawns every catalog prop in turn and lists the ones that fail; run again to stop, it carries on next time
/propprobeThe interior probe: what the interior natives say about where you stand
/npcdebugEach NPC's state over its head
whipsetup (server console)Prints the whip setup report again: missing resources, settings and fixes
whipcost [seconds] (server console)The server's half of /whipcost: every section timed with WhipCost on the server, one table, the dearest first
whiperrors [resource] (server console, and F8 with developer mode)The last errors on that side, grouped by the resource they came from, each with its count and latest lines: whip's fault or a resource's, at a glance
whipsupport (server console)One block to copy and send a seller: the server's version, the setup report and the recent errors by resource

The debug panel

Every /w debug tool draws into one pane. Each tool is a section; with two on, the pane holds both. Notifications and a job's objective cards move down under it while it is up.

/w: quick tools

Navigate with Arrow Keys (group labels are skipped; a list taller than the screen scrolls with the picked row, and fades at an edge with more past it), toggle with Enter, close with Escape. The first row is the developer mode switch. A tool either stays on until you switch it off (its row is lit while it runs) or acts once (Restore Health & Armour, Kill Me, Repair Vehicle); Admin Panel opens /whip.

EntryDescription
Developer modeThe switch above. With it off, it is the only row.
NoclipFly freely: invisible, no collision, invincible. WASD + Space/Ctrl + Shift for speed.
InvisibleNobody else sees you; you see yourself at half opacity.
God ModeNo damage, and health kept full whatever else tries to take it.
Restore Health & ArmourOnce: your health and armour full. If you are down, it revives you first (as /whip_revive does), then fills both.
Reveal PlayersEvery player with a character as a blue blip on the minimap and the pause map, named there, and over the head of anyone within 250 m a tag in the /me bubble's capsule: their character's name, charId and account name (the Steam name when Steam is running). The tag is drawn by the game, so it always faces you and nothing hides it; it shrinks with distance to half size. The server sends the list once a second, so players far away are on the map too.
Kill MeOnce: you go down at once, where you stand or sit, as any death does: the death screen, the respawn, and in a car you stay slumped in the seat. Noclip and God Mode go off first. Restore Health & Armour brings you back.
Repair VehicleOnce: the car you are in repaired, whether you are driving it or not (the game that owns the car does the repair).
CoordsShow X/Y/Z/Heading on screen. Press G to copy vector4() to clipboard.
ResourcesEvery resource, those with errors first. Pick one for what it registered with whip on the server and on this game (a count for each registry), its latest errors on each side, and the registrations whip refused it, with a row that runs /whipcost. For a buyer telling whip's fault from a resource's, and a seller checking their own.
Object ViewerNames the props, peds and vehicles within 20 m: walk around and identify object models. Each is a tag pinned to it, drawn by the game: it faces you, nothing in the world hides it, and it shrinks with distance down to a size that stays readable. A ped's tag sits on its head, so a passenger and their car are each picked on their own. The one you look at opens into a card: its picture when whip has one (a car, an NPC, a prop; the kind's icon otherwise), its hash, position and heading, and its Source: a player, whip's saved, street or temporary car, the resource whose NPC it is, a script, or which kind of GTA spawn. On GTA V Enhanced, where the game names only some models, the name comes from whip's own list (every model it has a picture of), or a car's own name. G (D-pad left on a controller) opens its options down the right of the screen, Copy details (its name, hash and a vector4) the first of them.
Edit Held PropWith a resource's prop in your hand, such as a pump's nozzle: the hand position editor opens on it, posed standing and then walking and jogging on the spot (H) in the walk you have now. Drag the arrows to move it and press R to turn it; hold the right mouse button to look round. Confirm & Exit saves it, and it sits there in everyone's hand from then on, those holding it now included. Saving is a permanent admin's. The quick menu hides itself.
DebugShows the debug tools under it: the three below, then any resource's own (RegisterDebugTool), such as whip_gunny's Gunny Debug. Off turns them all off.
Player Stats DebugA section of the debug panel: your stats live: health, armour, hunger, thirst, the ped's own reading beside a vital (amber when they disagree), decay rates, effects and the change log. And a card of stats over every other player within 40 m, drawn by the game at their root so walls never hide it.
Vehicle Stats DebugA section of the debug panel: everything the car you are in is carrying and what is moving it: per-stat bars, rates, change sources, attached data. And a card over every other whip car within 40 m (its plate, id and the stats it carries); the car you get into moves to the panel until you get out.
Ground Items DebugA section of the debug panel for the ground items in your cell of the ground grid and the eight around it: how many piles and items, the most common, who dropped the most, the oldest and newest. Each pile gets a beam into the sky and a named mark on the minimap and pause map. Look at a pile and the panel says what it is, who dropped it, how long it has lain there and where. The ground grid's squares round you are laid on the ground, 11 by 11: blue for an empty square, amber for one with piles, with a card over yours and the nearest with piles saying how many and what.
Admin PanelOpens /whip (below). The quick menu hides itself.
Dungeon ModeOpens Dungeon Mode where you stand: the world builder on the live world. The quick menu hides itself.
A resource's pageUnder Dungeon Mode, a row for each page another resource added. Picked, the list becomes that page; its first row, or Backspace, goes back. Escape shuts the menu, and /w opens on the page again. See Your page in /w.
ExperimentalLast, a row for each experimental feature turned on (and applied) in /whip → Settings → Config → Experimental features: the Camera Creator, and the Systems Creator (the same as /systems). They are unfinished prototypes; with every one off there is no such group.

/director on its own opens the Director in /whip for a Director builder.

The Object Viewer's options

With the Object Viewer on, look at something and press G (D-pad left on a controller): a list of what can be done to it opens down the right of the screen, laid out as the Director's card list is. Search it, jump to a group with its chip, point at an option to read what it does in the line under the list. An option runs at once, flips a switch (on its line), or opens a page of its own (›); Escape or B goes back, then closes. The card stays on the thing while its options are open. What it is decides the list: whip's own (a saved car, a player) or the game's (a street car, an NPC walking by). The thing G would open is outlined in white in the world, and the one whose options are open in blue (a ped or a car gets corners round it instead of an outline).

It isOptions
AnythingCopy details: its name, hash and a vector4, to the clipboard. Another script's object that only your game has (not networked, not the map's) has only this.
A prop of the map'sUnder Map prop: Make it a Dungeon prop (hidden for everyone, and a Dungeon prop of yours put exactly where it stood, to move, change or remove), Change model (another prop where it stands, for everyone: it becomes a Dungeon prop of yours) and Remove for everyone (hidden on every game). All until a restart, or Put back on the Dungeon Mode page.
A networked object (another resource's, or GTA's)Move, Turn invisible and Freeze in place (switches), Swap for a Dungeon prop (another prop in its place, turned as it is, and this one goes), Remove (the resource that made it may make it again).
