A Dungeon prop (one made in Dungeon Mode: its maker's, or any, for a full admin)Under Dungeon prop: Move (everyone sees it where you leave it), Change model (its place and turn kept: search the props whip has pictures of, or use any prop by its name), Solid (a switch: off, players and cars pass through it), Put the map's one back (when it took a map prop's place) and Remove. In Dungeon Mode also Duplicate (a copy in hand, made where you put it down), and a Fixed Weapon's Fire.
A ground itemIts name says what it is; the line under it how many, and who dropped it. Under Ground item: Move (it lies exactly where you leave it), Change item (any item, and how many: one for an item that does not stack; a gun gets a new serial), Set how many (for one that stacks) and Remove. A ground item is saved as it lies, so these are a full admin's. What a change takes away and brings in is on the item log.
Any prop or ground item: effectsUnder Effects: the switches Smoke, Sparks, Flames (for show: they burn nobody), Steam and Glow (a warm light), on for everyone until switched off, the thing goes, or the server restarts (80 at most, everyone's together); and Explode, a real explosion where it stands that hurts whoever is near.
A Dungeon car (one made in Dungeon Mode: its maker's, or any, for a full admin)Under Dungeon car: Key settings, where its key is (no key, a player's pocket, the ignition, the glovebox, the boot, the ground beside it), Locked and Only its key opens it, saved together. The key it had before is taken back first (from a pocket while they are online), and its key goes when the car goes.
A whip car (saved)Return to garage (whoever is in it); Change owner (anyone online, or a character found by name); Open in WHIP Admin Menu (its page in Vehicles); Delete from whip database (asks first: the car, its record, trunk and glovebox, for good); Fix (and its saved damage and dirt); Set stat (each stat with its range); Explode; Become driver (the driver's seat must be empty); Become passenger; Eject all players (and NPCs); Turn invisible, Set invincibility and Freeze in place (switches, kept by whichever game owns the car as owners change, until switched off or the car goes); Move (below); Inspect trunk storage and Inspect glovebox storage (past the lock, from anywhere). And other resources' options: whip_autos adds Open Whiplash.
Any other car (a street car, a temporary one)Remove, Fix, Explode, Make vehicle permanently owned by player (pick someone online: a saved car of theirs is made from it where it stands, paint and parts kept, its plate kept when no other car has it), Move.
A playerRestore health, Restore armour, Revive, Kill (an ordinary death), Set on fire; Freeze in place and Disable combat abilities (switches: no aiming, shooting, punching or drive-bys; they are told, and both end when they leave or swap character); Force escort (brought to your side and held, out of a car first); Move; Change model (the Director's NPC list, with Back to their own look; a relog or a respawn brings their own look back too); Force open character editor; Force change movement style (kept as if they had picked it); Force emote (the emote menu: each one picked, they play; Stop ends it); Adjust stats; Inspect inventory; Open in WHIP Admin Menu (their page in Player Manager); Kick from server (a reason) and Ban from server (a reason, and 1 hour to 30 days or permanent).
An NPCRemove, Kill, Set on fire (a fire started here, on an NPC or a player, goes out after 8 seconds), Move. whip's own NPCs (shopkeepers, the Director's and lore characters) have none: their own systems look after them. One made in Dungeon Mode has them all (Remove is its maker's, or a full admin's), and its card says who made it.
A Dungeon NPC (one made in Dungeon Mode: its maker's, or any, for a full admin)Under Dungeon NPC: Attack a player and Follow a player (pick someone online), Calm down (no more fighting or following), Give a weapon (any GTA weapon, one of whip_gunny's own while it runs, or none: they are made again with it where they stand), and the switches On guard, Invincible and Stay put.
A player, made for themUnder Make for them: Spawn a car for them (any car this game has: a temporary one beside them, unlocked, their key in their pocket) and Send NPCs after them (1 to 6, with pistols, SMGs, shotguns, rifles or fists, from 25 to 40 metres away). What is made belongs to whoever made it, as anything made in Dungeon Mode: until a restart or until it is removed.

Who. A full admin, with the Object Viewer; and a Dungeon Master, from Dungeon Mode's world builder (a click on the thing), who has every option except the ones that last past a restart: those are greyed for them, marked Admins only. Every option used is logged on the user's timeline, and on the player's when it was used on one.

Move puts the furnisher's arrows and rings on the one thing, from where you stand with the game's own camera: drag an arrow along it, the centre dot over the ground, or press R for the rings (a car or a prop tilts and turns; a ped turns). Shift snaps, the right mouse button looks round, and WASD still walks. On a controller: LS moves it the way the camera faces, LT / RT down and up, the D-pad's left and right turn it, RS looks. Done, Escape or B goes back to its options. A player is moved by the server, about ten times a second while dragged.

Another resource adds its own options with Whip.objectViewerOption.

/whip: the Admin Panel

Type /whip (or use the /w entry). It can also be bound to a key: it registers an unbound keybind called "Whip: Open Admin Panel" in GTA's Settings → Key Bindings → FiveM. One window, one Escape ladder: Escape closes an open dialog first, then backs out of a section's drill-down (a selected row, an active edit), then closes the panel.

SectionGroupDescription
Player ManagerPlayersEvery player who has joined, online or not: characters, identifiers, current stats (their HUD's gauges, each one set by typing a value), vehicles, jobs, ban history, admin notes and an activity timeline, and a picture of an online player's game. Teleport to them or bring them, open their inventory, kick, ban and unban, and give or take dev tools until the next restart. See Player Manager.
PhonesPlayersEvery phone number whip keeps and whether it is locked, filtered All / Online / Locked, with one search for a number, a name or a character id. A number's page says whose it is, whether its SIM works, since when, and what it holds (contacts, messages, calls), with the owner's other numbers; Change the number in place, Give me its SIM card, or Delete it. With none picked, Give a character a number. Open phone records reads everything one number did, read only: its conversations, calls and contacts as the owner's phone shows them, the full call log (who, which way, how it ended, how long it rang and talked), its activity by hour and day, and everyone it deals with and who really owns their number. Pick a person anywhere and every part turns to them; Open their phone moves the records to their number.
VehiclesVehiclesEvery car whip knows about, searchable by plate, model, owner or id. A car's page shows its Info (its owner with their picture, then the vehicle, plate, id, category, garage, status Garaged or Out, who is in it, its place on the map and its picture) and its actions as cards. WHIP Actions: open its trunk or glovebox (no lock or distance check), return it to its garage, move it to a garage you pick, teleport yourself or a player to it, bring it to you or to a player, change its owner, give yourself or a player a key. World Actions: eject everyone in it, teleport players into its free seats, lock or unlock it, change a stat, freeze it where it is, take the key out of its ignition (into your pockets), repair it (body, engine, tyres and dirt, kept on its record too). Fun Actions: explode it, burst its tyres, force every door open or shut, fling it into the air, destroy its engine. On GTA V Enhanced the server repairs it, bursts its tyres and destroys its engine itself, so those work on a car nobody is near. Destructive Actions: delete it and everything in it from whip's database. An action that needs the car in the world is dimmed, saying why, while it is in its garage. Live updates to all viewers. With no car picked, Set up a new vehicle opens the wizard: Vehicle (pick a model by class, or type an add-on's name), Owner (by name or character id), Extras (its plate and fuel, and its model's trunk and glovebox or sizes of its own, all optional), Where (a garage, or out beside you), then Create; its page opens. A property's private garage takes only a car its owner or a keyholder owns.
Vehicle AdjustmentsVehiclesTrunk and glovebox for a whole category of vehicles (every motorbike, every SUV) and for one model over its category: their sizes, or off. On the left, the categories, each opening to its vehicles as pictures; a category picked edits all of them, a vehicle picked shows its picture large over its own. The trunk and the glovebox each have Enable override?: off, it is what the category (or config.lua) gives; on, its own slots and weight from the sliders (click a number to type one), and whether it has one at all (Has a trunk). Under them, the trunk and glovebox as the inventory would show them opened, following the sliders as they move. A model not in the vehicle list that has settings of its own still shows, under its own heading, to see and give back. A car's own size (given when it was made) wins, then its model's, then its category's, then config.lua.
GaragesVehiclesCreate, edit and delete garages, move vehicles between garages, teleport to a garage.
ItemsEconomyEvery item, from every resource, with its picture: search, filter by resource, give yourself some. An item's page shows what it is, its settings side by side (name, description and weight for every item, stacking, cooldown and kind for config.lua's, plus any of its own, such as a magazine's size), and its pictures, which an admin can change and add to by link. With none picked, what has been changed. See In game: /whip → Economy → Items.
ShopsEconomyCreate, edit and delete shops, edit catalogs and prices, and link a stocked shop to its container. Stock itself is managed at the shop, with its Manage Stock option.
ContainersEconomyCreate, edit and delete containers, fill the position from where you stand, open any container's inventory.
JobsEconomyCreate, edit and delete jobs and roles, hire and fire, manage permissions. Live updates.
BanksEconomyEverything that can hold a bank account (players, businesses, lore characters, and accounts nobody holds), each with its money, what it is worth and its full log. Open an account to change or close it; New account makes one.
Item LogEconomyOne item's whole life by its uid: made, moved, given, thrown, placed, picked up, used, destroyed. Open it from an item on a player's timeline, or paste a uid. See Activity Log.
ZonesWorldBrowse all persistent zones, edit rules and whitelists, toggle debug rendering, teleport, copy spawn code. "Open the editor" hands the screen to the in-world Zone Editor (fly-cam; 1/2/3 for box/sphere/poly, H room-scan, 4/5 vertex editing), the panel suspends and returns with fresh data when you exit.
DoorsWorldEvery saved door, in folders: lock state, autolock, requirements. "Open the editor" suspends the panel for the in-world Door Editor (look at a door, G to save, E twice to link doubles).
Ground ItemsWorldList all world items, search and filter, teleport, toggle blips and markers, delete.
PropertiesWorldEvery home, what is wrong with each, and the fixes an admin makes by hand; a second tab lists the interiors whip knows, their units and the packs they came from. Live while open. See Properties & Homes.
Time & WeatherWorldSet time, quick presets, weather grid, freeze/blackout toggles, time scale.
DirectorDirectorScenarios (who made each, who played it, its runs and revisions, with Restore), shipped packs, live runs with Stop, and who may build. Edit opens the full-screen editor. See Director.
Lore charactersDirectorThe story's named people: name, bank name, ped or a look made in the character editor, notes, picture, their voice lines, and what they are part of (scenarios, their phone's texts and calls, what they have paid players). New lore character makes one.
MonitorSystemEvery SecureEvent and SecureCallback call, live: what went wrong, who sent what and the busiest events, filtered to Problems or narrowed by event, player or search (players' stat reports are hidden until you ask). All events lists each event's calls and refusals; Watched keys lists the Sentinel's keys and what it caught. History is always recorded server-side: reopening shows what happened while it was closed; the nav badge counts Sentinel detections that arrived while you were in another section.
UI LibrarySystemRun every UI component live (notifications, progress, input, skill check, alert, confirm, on-screen text, radial, 3D interaction). The panel hides while each demo plays, then reports the result.
ConfigSettingsEvery setting in whip_core's config.lua, changed and applied in game. Permanent admins only. See Changing a setting in game.
A resource's pageSettingsThe settings a resource built on whip declared, under its own name, working as Config does. See Settings pages.
Handoffs are deliberate. Flows that need the game screen (the zone/door editors, UI Library demos, Lua-side confirms) suspend the panel (it hides, keys go to the game, it comes back where you left it). Flows that open the inventory (Player Manager's "Open Inventory", a container's "Open", vehicle storage) close the panel: the inventory is its own world.

Vehicle and furniture pictures are made outside the game and come in the packs: a car's is img/vehicles/<model>.webp in whip_media_previews, a prop's is img/props/<model>.webp in whip_media_props. Players receive a new picture when you restart its pack; whip_core reads which ones exist at its own start.

Where whip's pictures are. whip's pictures, videos and map files are split into media packs of at most 256 MB each, by category, so a player downloads each once, and again only when that one changes: whip_media_clothing_male the male body's clothing pictures, whip_media_clothing_female the female body's (the character editor's names for them, and the list of which clothing has a picture, are whip_core's own, so they still work when the pictures are not running), whip_media_props the furniture pictures, whip_media_previews the vehicles, NPCs, tattoos and emote previews, whip_media_map the map, its blip icons and the minimap's tiles. They start in any order, before or after whip_core; whip's setup report says when one is missing. A category that outgrows its pack carries on in a new one (whip_media_props_2); after moving files between packs, adding one or renaming one, run node whip_core/dev/assets_index.mjs, which writes the index whip reads (and warns when one passes 256 MB).

ACE Permission

Both /w and /whip are gated behind the whip.devtools ACE permission. Without it the commands do nothing, and every mutation behind every section is independently ACE-checked server-side, which is the real wall. One exception: a player given a whip permission that opens a section (Director access, say) opens /whip with only that section.

## server.cfg — grant dev tools to an admin
add_ace identifier.license:xxxx whip.devtools allow

To give someone the tools for a while from in game, see Dev tools until the restart.

Viewer Pattern

Sections with live data (Vehicles, Ground Items, Jobs, Shops, Monitor, …) use a viewer tracking pattern. Entering a section registers you as a viewer server-side and the server broadcasts live updates while you look (other admins' edits, gameplay mutations); switching sections or closing the panel unregisters you. Only the active section holds a viewer session: multiple admins can watch the same section and see changes in real time.

Player Manager

Every player who has joined, online or not: the 1,000 most recently seen accounts. Open it with /whip → Players → Player Manager; it needs the whip.devtools ACE, and every action is checked against it again on the server.

FeatureDescription
Player LookupSearch and filter all users by name, license, or character name. Shows online status, character names, ban status.
Player DetailFull profile: identifiers, characters, vehicles, jobs, position, current vehicle. Its Actions are a card each, saying what they do to this player: Teleport To, Bring Here, Open Inventory, Unban (while a ban holds) and Give Dev Tools, with Kick and the two bans apart on the right.
Current StatsWhile the player is online: every stat they have (health, armour, hunger, thirst, oxygen, and any a resource registers), whether it is on their HUD or not, each drawn as their HUD draws its gauge. Type a value and press Apply (or Enter) to set it; it is held to the stat's range, and each change is a line in the server console. Health is in the game's units: the HUD shows it empty at 100 and full at 200. The developer mark follows developer mode, so it is shown, not set.
VehiclesEvery vehicle the account's characters own, newest first, a card each: its picture, its name and plate, its state (garaged, in the world, out but not spawned, or impounded), its garage and its fuel. With more than one character, the card says whose it is. Click a card to open that vehicle on the Vehicles page.
Two game clientsAn account in on two game clients at once (they share a license) is a row for each, with its server id and the character it plays. Config.PlayerManagerSessionWarn (off by default) adds a warning: "2 SESSIONS" on the rows, and on the page an "ALSO IN" pill that opens the other one.
Their gameAn online player's page shows a picture of their game beside their name, taken when you open it: what they see, their HUD and whip's other screens with the game (not other resources' screens, such as the phone). Beside it, where they are on the map, from when you opened the page or from the newest picture. Capture Player's Game takes a new one. Your menu keeps each picture for 5 minutes, so their page opened again in that time shows it without asking their game; after that it is gone. Each picture taken is a line in the server console.
TeleportTeleport to a player or bring them to you (online only).
Open InventoryOpen a character's inventory, online or not: an offline one is loaded from the database. An account with several characters asks which first.
KickKick with a reason. Auto-adds an admin note recording the kick.
Temp BanBan for a set duration (days, hours, minutes). Player sees reason + expiry on connect attempt.
Perma BanPermanent ban. Player sees reason on connect attempt.
UnbanDeactivate an active ban. Shows ban details before confirming.
Admin NotesAdd/delete notes on a player's profile. Kick actions auto-create notes.
ActivityThe Activity Log of every character on the account, newest first, 30 rows at a time (Older for more). Click an item in it to follow that item in the Item Log.
Give Dev ToolsGive the player whip.devtools until the next restart, or take it back (below).

Bans

Bans are enforced on connect: banned players cannot join the server. The ban check uses all identifiers (license, steam, discord, fivem). If ANY identifier matches an active ban, the player is blocked.

Nobody bans someone who outranks them. An admin from server.cfg cannot be banned from the panel: take them out of server.cfg first. Someone given dev tools from the panel can be banned only by an admin from server.cfg.

A temporary ban ends by itself. When a banned player tries to connect, they see:

You are banned from this server.

Reason: [reason text]
Expires: 2026-03-18 22:30:00 PDT

Ban ID: #1

Permanent bans show "This ban is permanent" instead of an expiry date. The timezone is auto-detected from the server.

Finding a player

  • All: every user who has ever connected
  • Online: currently connected players only
  • Banned: users with active bans

The search bar filters by player name, license identifier, and character names (case-insensitive).

Dev tools until the restart

Give Dev Tools on a player's page adds their license to the group.whip_devtools ACE group. FiveM does not save a group added while the server runs, so the next restart takes it away, and so does stopping whip_core. Only a permanent admin can give it, each grant writes an admin note, and a temporary admin cannot hand out rights that are saved (Director access, for one). server.cfg must give the group the tools, and let whip_core add and remove players:

## Dev tools given from the Player Manager, until the next restart
add_ace group.whip_devtools whip.devtools allow
add_ace group.whip_devtools command.w allow
add_ace resource.whip_core command.add_principal allow
add_ace resource.whip_core command.remove_principal allow

The group gets /w and /whip, not the server console. The lines take effect after a full server restart.

Banks

Everyone and everything that can hold a bank account, and all their money. Open it with /whip → Economy → Banks; it needs the whip.devtools ACE, and every action is checked against it again on the server.

Who is listed

Every player with a character, every business (a job) and every lore character, whether they have an account or not. An account nobody holds gets a row of its own. Search by name, license or account number; Most Money sorts the list by what is banked. With nobody picked, the page shows the whole bank: what is in it, the cash on characters, the last 24 hours and how many accounts are frozen.

A dashboard

PartWhat it shows
Total moneyTheir bank accounts and their cash. A player with several characters has a button for each, and All characters adds them up.
Net worth (assumed)An estimate, with every part listed below it (see how it is worked out).
TransactionsHow many there have ever been, and what came in and went out in the last 30 days, day by day. Moves between their own accounts count as neither.
AccountsTheir open accounts, the accounts of other people they can use, and their closed accounts. Press one to open it.
Full logEvery bank transaction, newest first, narrowed to money in, money out or one account. A name in a row opens that person's or business's own page. Cash shows the same for their cash, from the activity log.

How net worth is worked out

PartValued at
Bank accountsTheir balance. Only accounts they own, not other people's they can use.
CashIts face value, wherever it is.
VehiclesWhat the resources selling cars ask (SetVehiclePrices), averaged across them. A car no resource sells (a helicopter, a police car) counts as $0.
PropertiesTheir listed price. A property with no price counts as $0.
ItemsThe average price across every shop selling it, each shop counted once, for what is in their pockets, their cars' boots and gloveboxes and their stashes, including inside other items (a bag's contents, a gun's magazine). Free items and prices in another currency do not count towards the average. An item no shop sells counts as $0 and is named.
BusinessesWhat each business they own is worth: its accounts, and its shelves at the same average.

A deleted character counts as long as it still has an open account, because that money is still in the game. It is marked on the page.

Changing an account

ActionWhat it does
New AccountOpens one for that character or business, with an optional starting amount (and a reason, which goes on its statement). It does not pay Config.StartingBalance, and Config.MaxExtraAccounts limits players, not admins. A lore character has one account, named after its bank name.
Name, Type, New ownerA character's main account stays personal and stays theirs: make another one their main first. The old owner keeps manager access until you take it away. A business's account follows the business's owner, set on the Jobs page.
Freeze, Make Their Main AccountWhile frozen, no money moves in or out, including from this page. The main account is the one wages land in.
Add Money, Take Money, Move MoneyA reason is required. It goes on the statement as Admin: reason, with your character as who did it. Adding money makes it; taking it destroys it; moving it needs the other account's number.
Who can use itGive, change or take away access. The rule that one player's characters pass no money to each other (Config.BlockOwnCharacterTransfers) applies. Staff reach a business's account through their rank, so it is set on the Jobs page.
Delete AccountAsks where any money goes (another account, or out of the game), then closes the account for good. It is closed rather than erased because the statements of other accounts name it, so it stays listed under Closed accounts with its log. A living character's main account cannot be deleted: at their next login a new one would be made, paying the starting balance again.

Everything done here goes on the activity log as bank_admin, on your timeline and the account owner's.

Building in Game

Most of the world is built from /whip with no code: stand where it goes, open the section, save. Each tool's full guide is with its system, marked Server owners.

ToOpenGuide
Add a garage/whip → Vehicles → Garages → + New Garage: the wizard, its bays set out in the worldSetting a garage up
Change a garage: its name, bays, map marker or icon/whip → Vehicles → Garages → a garage → Change (on that part, or Change everything): the wizard, filled inChanging a garage
Add, move or take away a garage's bays/whip → Vehicles → Garages → a garage → Change on Bays (a property's: Properties → its Garage)The bay tool
Set up a home/whip → World → Properties → New property, standing inside itSetting one up
Set up a whole building of homesRegister here, or Stamp mode to fly floor to floorA whole building
Check homes still match their interiorsVerify now, Verify… or Quick checkChecking them
Find the home you are standing in/whip → World → Properties → What property am I in?Properties
Furnish a home as its owner would, or look in its storage/whip → World → Properties → a home → Furniture → Manage furniture; Storage → Inspect storageProperties
Draw a zone: a safe zone, a no-PvP area, a room/whip → World → Zones → Open the editor: 1/2/3 for box, sphere or outline; H scans a roomThe Zone Editor
Lock a door, and say who opens it/whip → World → Doors → Open the editor: look at a door and press G; E on two doors links a doubleThe Door Editor
Open a shop/whip → Economy → ShopsShops in game
Place a stash or storage box/whip → Economy → Containers; Use My Position fills in where you standContainers
Set the time and weather/whip → World → Time & WeatherTime & Weather in game
Build a mission or a scene/whip → Director (or /w → Director)Director
Shipping what you built. A map or MLO resource can carry its own doors (EnsureDoors) and homes (a whip_properties.lua pack), so another server gets them with no admin steps.

How whip is built

whip_core is the base. Every other whip resource, yours included, depends on it for players, items, money and the screens, and reaches it only through exports: add dependency 'whip_core' to your fxmanifest.lua, then call exports.whip_core:ExportName(...). A satellite's own exports work the same way, for example exports.whip_gunny:ExportName(...).

Each resource has the same layers:

LayerWritten inWhat it does
DatabaseMariaDB or MySQLKeeps characters, items, cars and bank accounts between restarts
ServerLua 5.4, with oxmysqlDecides everything. Every change happens here, is checked, and is held in memory before it is saved
ClientLua 5.4, with FiveM nativesRuns on each player's game: the ped, keys, cars, and passing messages to the screens
NUIHTML, CSS and JSThe screens drawn over the game: inventory, bank, character creator, admin tools
DUIHTML, CSS and JS, drawn into the worldThe screens inside the game world: the 3D prompts, /me bubbles, NPC conversations, garage bay outlines, the Director's marks. Each system gets one browser, made the first time it is needed (Screens in the world)

whip needs OneSync (Quick Start). Cars are made by the server, so they stay in the world when their driver leaves.

Server Events

Listen to these with AddEventHandler in your server scripts.

Any server resource can fire them. A whip_core event is an ordinary FiveM event, so another resource could send one with made-up data. Before a handler pays out, gives an item or punishes someone because of one, check who sent it: if GetInvokingResource() ~= 'whip_core' then return end. A handler that only logs or updates a screen needs no check.

How whip names its events

whip_core:<what>:<what happened>, with one table. whip_core:item:added, whip_core:vehicle:entered, whip_core:player:died, and the handler gets one table, function(e) … e.source … e.item … end, so a field can be added to an event later without breaking anyone reading the others. Names containing client: or server: are whip's own network messages between the two sides, not events for you (see the note under Client Events).

Every payload, typed, is in whip_core/types/events.lua.
EventPayload (one table)When
whip_core:onReady{ reason, resources? }whip_core is ready for registrations. reason is 'coreStarted' (whip_core has just started or restarted and remembers nothing: register everything) or 'resourceStarted' with resources, the resources that just started while it was up. Fires on the client too. Most resources should use Whip.register rather than listen to this directly: it does the filtering for you.
whip_core:player:loaded{ source, charId, name, newCharacter, player }Character fully loaded. player is the data sheet; name their full name; newCharacter true on a new character's first load. The client's event carries the same table.
whip_core:player:logout{ source, charId, player, why }The character is leaving: why is 'logout' (back to character select) or 'disconnect'.
whip_core:player:died{ source, charId, killer, reported }The server accepted a player's death. killer is the killer's server id when the server saw a player do it (a car's driver counts), else nil; reported is the victim's own game's description of the killing blow, for display only.
whip_core:player:revived{ source, charId, how, reason }A dead player is alive again: how is 'revived' or 'respawned', reason 'revive', 'respawn', 'revive:admin' or 'revive:self'.
whip_core:character:created{ source, charId }New character created.
whip_core:character:deleted{ source, charId }Character deleted.
whip_core:item:added{ source, item, amount, count, reason, by }A player now carries more of an item than before, by any route: an export, a pickup, a purchase, a give from another player, a drag out of a stash, cash. amount is how many arrived, count what they carry now; reason and by are set when an export made the change (by = 'by my_resource').
whip_core:item:removed{ source, item, amount, count, reason, by }A player now carries less of an item: used, dropped, sold, given away, put in a stash, taken by an export.
whip_core:inventory:changed{ source }Something in a player's pockets changed: ANY change, a move from one of their own slots to another included, which item:added/item:removed never hear (the counts are the same). Once per change. For a resource holding on to "the item in slot 4": look again here, and you know the moment it moves, drops or leaves. whip_gunny puts a drawn gun away with it. (A quiet SetItemMetadata does not fire it: that rewrites a value in place and moves nothing.)
whip_core:heldProps:lost{ source, tag, reason, by? }Props your resource put in a player's hands (HoldProps, tag '<resource>:<tag>') left them without you asking: reason 'replaced' (something else was put in the hand: an emote's cup, an item handed over; by is its tag) or 'world' (the player was moved to another routing bucket). Whose hands hold what now: GetHeldPropsTag(source), the tag ('<resource>:<tag>', or whip's own 'emote', 'bar', 'give', 'take') or nil. whip_fuel drops the nozzle on the ground for 'replaced' and puts it back on its pump for 'world'
whip_core:item:used{ source, item, slot, addr }Item used (hotbar or Use). slot is the slot's data, addr its address.
whip_core:item:given{ source, target, item, amount }Player gave an item to another player.
whip_core:bank:balanceChanged{ type, accountId, amount, actorCharId, newBalance, message, … }Any deposit, withdrawal or transfer. A 'transfer' has fromAccountId, toAccountId, fromBalance and toBalance in place of accountId and newBalance.
whip_core:bank:accountChanged{ accountId, what }An account changed with no money moving: what is 'label', 'type', 'owner', 'frozen', 'main', 'closed' or 'access' ('access' only from the Banks page, not a job's rank changes). whip_phone's Bank app looks again
whip_core:vehicle:lockChanged{ vehicleId, plate, locked, source }A car was locked or unlocked: by the key fob, a lockpick, SetVehicleLocked or the admin tool. Only when the state actually changed. source is nil when no player did it
whip_core:vehicle:lockpicked{ vehicleId, plate, source }Vehicle lockpicked successfully (fires alongside vehicle:lockChanged)
whip_core:vehicle:entered{ vehicleId, plate, source, seat, previousSeat? }A player got into any seat of a framework vehicle, or moved to another seat. seat is -1 for the driver; previousSeat is the seat they moved from inside this car (nil for getting in). The server checks the seat for itself before announcing it. Taking the driver's seat also puts a key from their accessory strip into the car's empty ignition, if it fits
whip_core:vehicle:exited{ vehicleId, plate, source, seat, left }A player left the seat the server had them in, including logging out or disconnecting while in the car: then left is 'logout' or 'dropped' (nil when they got out). A car somebody gets out of is unlocked; one they leave by leaving the game stays as it was. A key their strip put into the ignition goes back to them when they get out.
whip_core:vehicle:registered{ vehicleId, plate, model, session, source }New vehicle registered in framework (first time only)
whip_core:door:lockChanged{ doorId, locked, source, cause }A door was locked or unlocked, only when its state really changed. cause is 'press', 'lockpick', 'autolock', 'code' or 'released' (a HoldDoor ended); source is the player, when one did it.
whip_core:door:denied{ doorId, source, reason }A player's press on a door was refused. reason is what they were told (it is theirs: do not show it to others).
whip_core:run:started{ run, startedBy }A Director run started (never a builder's Test). run is a DirectorRunView; see Director: for other resources.
whip_core:run:ended{ run, outcome, reason, vars, payout, faultCard, stopping }A Director run ended: succeeded, failed, calledOff, aborted or faulted.
whip_core:run:playerLeft{ run, source, charId, why, by, runEnds }A player left a Director run (logged out, disconnected, or a script took them out: by), before its end.
whip_core:run:playerJoined{ run, source, charId, by }A script put a player into a Director run (AddPlayerToScenarioRun).
whip_core:run:signalled{ run, name, data, source }A Director run's Send Signal card ("alarm").
whip_core:scenario:switchedOn / :switchedOff{ scenario, name, rev, replaced | why, by }A Director scenario was switched on or off.
whip_core:container:opened{ containerId, source, charId }The server opened a stash on a player's screen: by E or OpenStore (the admin Containers page is silent). Their game may still decline it.
whip_core:shop:purchased{ shopId, charId, source, items, total, paymentMethod, mode }Player completed a shop purchase.
whip_core:shop:opened{ shopId, source, charId }Player opened a shop.
whip_core:shop:closed{ shopId, source, charId }Player closed a shop.
whip_core:shop:created{ shopId, shop }Shop created (via export or dev tool).
whip_core:shop:updated{ shopId, shop }Shop updated.
whip_core:shop:deleted{ shopId }Shop deleted.
whip_core:shop:priceChanged{ containerId, item, slot?, price, forSale }A stocked shop's item was priced or taken off sale. slot is there when it was set from a shelf slot.
whip_core:time:changed{ hour, minute }Server time changed (via export or dev tool).
whip_core:weather:changed{ weather }Server weather changed.
whip_core:zone:entered{ zoneId, key?, source }A player walked into a zone registered or ensured with trackPlayers = true (the server's own sweep, about once a second)
whip_core:zone:exited{ zoneId, key?, source, dropped?, removed? }…and out of it. dropped: they left the server inside it. removed: the zone went with them in it
whip_core:time:freezeChanged{ frozen }Time frozen or unfrozen.
whip_core:property:ownerChanged{ propertyId, ownerCharId, previousOwnerCharId, by }A property was given to someone (ownerCharId) or made unowned (nil). Every key was taken back with it. by is the charId who did it, when a player or admin did
whip_core:property:keyGranted{ propertyId, charId, by }Someone was given a key to a property
whip_core:property:keyRevoked{ propertyId, charId }A key was taken back
whip_core:job:created / updated / deleted{ jobId, key, … }A job was made, changed (name, icon, ownerCharId, oldOwnerCharId) or deleted.
whip_core:job:hired{ jobId, key, charId, source, roleId, role, by }Someone was hired. source only while they are online.
whip_core:job:fired{ jobId, key, charId, source }Someone was fired (a deleted job fires job:deleted instead, not one per employee)
whip_core:job:roleChanged{ jobId, key, charId, source, roleId, role, oldRoleId }Someone's role changed
whip_core:job:clockedOn / clockedOff{ jobId, key, charId, source }Someone went on or off duty: by any route, logout included. Only on a real change

Also on the server: the vehicle lifecycle (whip_core:vehicle:created, :spawned, :despawned, :released, :deleted, :ownerChanged, :dataChanged) in Vehicle events, and these:

EventPayload (one table)When
whip_core:vehicle:claimed{ vehicleId, from, ownerCharId }ClaimVehicle made a car nobody owned someone's: vehicleId is the new owned car, from the one it was
whip_core:vehicle:plateChanged{ vehicleId, from, to }A car's plate changed (SetVehiclePlate)
whip_core:npc:spawned · :despawned · :damaged · :killed{ npcId, tag, owner, … }An NPC from SpawnNpc (see NPCs). Ask GetNpc before paying out on one
whip_core:flag:changed{ source, charId, name, value, was }A character's flag was set, or cleared (value nil)
whip_core:permission:changed{ userId, permission, granted }An account was given, or lost, a permission
A move tells you THAT their pockets changed, not which slot went where. whip_core:inventory:changed (above) fires once for any change to a player's pockets, a drag from one of their own slots to another included, with only { source }: look again with GetInventory or FindItem. There is deliberately no event carrying each move's detail (this slot, from here to there): moves are extremely frequent, and that would be a broadcast on a hot path. For the detail, observe them where they happen:

• onValidate and onChange on a panel: for moves in and out of a panel you opened, or a specific item's panel.
• whip_core:item:added / item:removed: for what a player carries. They fire whenever the amount of an item on a player changes, whatever changed it, but not for a rearrangement inside their own pockets (nothing arrived or left). Items inside a bag they carry are not counted.
• GetOpenStores(source): to ask what a player is currently in, rather than being told when they move.
item:added / item:removed fire from the one place every change to a player's inventory passes through: cash, pickups, drops, gives between players, shops, item use, stash drags and the store calls alike. They are about the player's pockets only: an item put in a stash fires nothing. Logging in is not a change: what a character arrives with is the starting point.
Duty is an event and a state bag. whip_core:job:clockedOn / clockedOff say when it changes. Player(source).state.whipJob holds the key of the job they are on duty at (the most recent clock-on), or false. Read it whenever you need it, which a resource that starts late can do where it missed the events. On the client, the local whip_core:job:clockedOn / clockedOff fire for the local player.
-- Example: log all item usage
AddEventHandler('whip_core:item:used', function(e)
    print(('Player %d used %s'):format(e.source, e.item))
end)

Client Events

Listen to these with AddEventHandler in your client scripts.

The same naming rule as the server's (above): one table.

EventPayload (one table)When
whip_core:onReady{ reason, resources? }whip_core's client is ready for registrations: see the server table. Prefer Whip.register.
whip_core:player:loaded{ source, charId, name, newCharacter, player }The character is in the world and the picture is back: the end of the load, not the start. The safe "player is ready" hook. The same table as the server's event (player is the data sheet).
whip_core:player:spawned{}The player has just been put into the world. Fires after every load, and a second time for a new character, once the appearance creator closes.
whip_core:player:died{ reconnected, respawnRefused }The local player died (reconnected = they loaded in already dead; respawnRefused = the server refused a respawn too soon after the death, so the same death is back after a revived).
whip_core:player:revived{ how }Alive again: how is 'revived' (where they lay) or 'respawned' (at a hospital).
whip_core:appearance:modelChanged{}The player's ped was rebuilt with a new model (the load, /charedit). The new ped starts with the game's default walk, clipset and face: a resource that set one puts it back here.
whip_core:run:joined / :updated{ runId, scenario, name, objective, countdown }This player is in a Director run / its band (objective, clock) changed. Never a Test. GetMyRuns() answers the same.
whip_core:run:left / :ended{ runId, scenario, name, why } / { runId, scenario, name, outcome, payout }This player left a Director run / it ended for them.
whip_core:player:logout{ charId }The local player is logging out to character select.
whip_core:job:clockedOn / clockedOff{ jobId, key }The local player went on or off duty at a job.
whip_core:job:listChanged{ jobs }The local player's job list changed: hired, fired, promoted, a job renamed. jobs is what GetPlayerJobs answers.
whip_core:ui:stateChanged{ open }Some screen or dialog opened (true) or everything closed (false): the IsAnyScreenOpen question, so a progress bar alone does not fire it.
whip_core:ui:cleanScreen{ on }The screen went clean for a recording (the Camera Creator playing in game): whip's own HUD, prompts and GTA's HUD are hidden. Put your resource's UI away while on is true, and back when it is false.
whip_core:hands:blocked{ label, only }A resource blocked the player's hands (BlockHands, this game's or the server's): only is 'weapons' for a weapons-only block, nil for everything. Put away what you hold that it covers. A block of everything also runs the 'freeHands' moment.
whip_core:hands:unblocked{}The last block on the player's hands went.
whip_core:pad:deviceChanged{ pad }The player went from keyboard to pad or back (settled over 400 ms), the moment whip's own button hints swap: swap yours here. It also fires once as whip_core starts. Controller support
whip_core:keyboard:opened / :closed{ id, owner } / { id }Whip's on-screen keyboard (OpenKeyboard) came up / went. The pad is the keyboard's between them: a reader of your own leaves it alone (Whip.padScreen does by itself).
whip_core:nui:capsDetected{ chrome, has, colorMix, …, gameView }whip_core's page has said what the game's browser can do, or it changed. The same table as GetNuiCaps.
whip_core:zone:entered{ zoneId, key?, label, group }Local player entered a zone. key is the name a saved zone was made with (EnsureZone), the same field the server's event carries, so match on it. (id, the same as zoneId, is still sent.)
whip_core:zone:exited{ zoneId, key?, label, group }Local player left a zone.
whip_core:weather:layerChanged{ name, layer }A local time/weather layer was set (layer is its settings) or removed (layer is nil).
whip_core:vehicle:entered{ vehicleId, entity, plate, seat }Local player got into any vehicle, or moved to another seat in it. seat is -1 for the driver, so "driver only" is data.seat == -1: the same test as on the server
whip_core:vehicle:exited{ vehicleId, entity, plate, seat }Local player got out of any vehicle
whip_core:property:entered{ propertyId, name }Local player walked into a property's space (GetCurrentProperty now answers it)
whip_core:property:exited{ propertyId, name }Local player walked out of it
whip_core:property:furnished{ propertyId, interiorId, count }A property's furniture is up on this client (count pieces, on interior interiorId)
whip_core:property:unfurnished{ propertyId, interiorId }It was taken away again (walked off, its interior unloaded or redrawn, the furnisher opened)
whip_core:property:furnishStateChanged{ propertyId, interiorId, state }Its GetInteriorFurnishState answer changed: 'pending', 'done', 'none' or 'idle'. interiorId is the copy whip last found ready, nil before that
whip_core:permission:changed{ permission, granted }This player's account was given, or lost, a permission. whip shows nothing: handle it to tell them
whip_core:ask:cancelled{ token }whip_core gave up on a question it asked this player (its timeout, a run's end, a logout). For a resource that showed it on its own screen (RegisterAskChannel): take that screen down
whip_core:devtools:modeChanged{ on }This player's developer mode went on or off (their /w switch, or the server taking dev tools away). It starts off at every join; HasDevTools() says where it is now. For what a client shows only to developers; anything the server does for them, the server checks again

whip's own network messages

Names containing client: are messages whip_core's server sends its own client scripts. They are listed because resources have leaned on them, but they are not events for you: a network message only reaches a resource that has RegisterNetEvent'd it, its arguments are whatever whip needs that week, and several fire at the start of something rather than the end. Prefer the local events above.

MessageArgumentsWhen
whip_core:client:playerLoadedserializedDataThe character's data has arrived and loading is starting. Use whip_core:player:loaded, which fires when it has finished. serializedData.isNewCharacter is true on a brand-new character's first load
whip_core:client:playerLogoutnoneReturned to character select. Use whip_core:player:logout
whip_core:client:updateCashcashTotalCash balance changed
whip_core:client:inventoryUpdate{ inventory, weights }Any inventory change
whip_core:client:vehicleLockStatevehicleId, lockedVehicle lock toggled (the players near the car)
whip_core:client:vehicleKeysSynckeysTablePlayer's key cache updated
whip_core:client:notifymessage, kind, durationEvery toast the server sends. From your server code use NotifyPlayer(source, text, kind), or, inside a SecureEvent, return false, text, which also records the refusal
whip_core:client:groundItemCreateddataGround item spawned nearby
whip_core:client:groundItemDeletedidGround item removed
whip_core:client:containerCreateddefNew container created
whip_core:client:containerDeletedcontainerIdContainer removed
whip_core:client:jobsSyncjobsTableFull job data synced on character load
whip_core:client:jobClockStatejobId, stateJob clock state changed (true=on, false=off)
Player ready: Use whip_core:player:loaded as the safe "player is ready" hook: it fires once the character is really in the world, with PlayerData and inventory populated.

Data Structures

Inventory Format

-- Returned by GetInventory(source)
{
    player = {
        [1] = { item = 'food',        amount = 3, metadata = nil },
        [3] = { item = 'vehicle_key', amount = 1, metadata = {
            vehicleId = 42, plate = 'ABC123', model = 'adder'
        }},
    },
    accessory = {
        [4] = { item = 'id_card', amount = 1, metadata = nil },   -- slots 4 and 5 take anything
    },
}

Vehicle

Every vehicle read on the server answers the same snapshot, a copy: GetVehicle, GetVehicleBy and the rest.

-- Returned by GetVehicle(vehicleId)
{
    vehicleId   = 42,
    plate       = 'ABC123',
    model       = 'adder',
    displayName = 'Adder',     -- from the vehicle catalog; nil for a model it does not have
    class       = 7,           -- the same
    vehType     = 'automobile',
    session     = false,       -- true: nobody owns it (street traffic, or a temp car)
    temp        = false,       -- true: a SpawnTempVehicle car (a rental, a job van)
    secure      = false,       -- true: cannot be lockpicked or hot-wired
    owner       = { charId = 1, name = 'Sam Reed', online = true },
    state       = 'out',       -- 'out' | 'garaged' | 'impounded'
    garage      = nil,         -- the garage's key while it is garaged
    coords      = vector3(-200.5, -1300.2, 31.0),
    heading     = 180.0,
    spawned     = true,
    entity      = 4610,        -- nil while it is not in the world
    netId       = 88,
    locked      = false,
    stats       = { fuel = 85.0, ... },
    data        = { ... },       -- your resources' keys; always a table
    properties  = { ... },       -- GTA vehicle properties
    storage     = { trunk = { slots = 20, maxWeight = 100, used = 12 }, glovebox = { ... } },   -- only when already loaded
    occupants   = { ... },       -- only with { occupants = true }
}

Bank Transaction (from event)

-- whip_core:bank:balanceChanged payload
{
    type          = 'deposit',  -- 'deposit' | 'withdraw' | 'transfer'
    accountId     = 1,
    amount        = 5000,
    actorCharId   = 1,
    newBalance    = 15000,
    message       = 'Paycheck',
    ownerCharId   = 1,          -- a deposit: whose account it is
    accountType   = 'personal', -- 'personal' | 'savings' | 'shared' | 'business'
    label         = 'Main',     -- the account's name
}
-- a transfer has fromAccountId / toAccountId, fromBalance / toBalance, and the same three for each side:
-- fromOwnerCharId, fromAccountType, fromLabel, toOwnerCharId, toAccountType, toLabel

Examples

Every registration below is inside Whip.register: secure events, callbacks, stats, items, jobs, actions. Registered at the top of a file instead, they vanish the first time whip_core restarts. Whip.register comes from shared_script '@whip_core/lib/satellite.lua' in your fxmanifest (the satellite helper). Event handlers (AddEventHandler) are FiveM's own and stay outside it.

Some examples use items whip does not ship, such as repair_kit and cocaine. Define an item first, with RegisterItem or in Config.Items; until then AddItem refuses it and a require = { item = ... } is never met.

SecureEvent: Before & After

-- BEFORE: raw RegisterNetEvent, validating by hand
local lastTrade = {}

RegisterNetEvent('trading:server:trade', function(targetId, itemKey, amount)
    local source = source
    local player = exports.whip_core:GetPlayer(source)
    if not player then return end

    -- Rate limit: yours to write, and yours to remember to clean up on disconnect
    local now = GetGameTimer()
    if lastTrade[source] and now - lastTrade[source] < 1000 then return end
    lastTrade[source] = now

    -- Every parameter arrives from the client and is whatever they felt like sending
    targetId = tonumber(targetId)
    amount   = tonumber(amount)
    if not targetId or targetId ~= math.floor(targetId) then return end
    if targetId < 1 or targetId > 256 then return end
    if not amount or amount ~= math.floor(amount) then return end
    if amount < 1 or amount > 999 then return end
    if type(itemKey) ~= 'string' or #itemKey > 60 then return end
    if itemKey:match('[^%w_]') then return end

    -- ...and none of this appears in the Monitor, so when it silently
    -- refuses something you find out from a player, not from a tool.
    doTrade(source, player, targetId, itemKey, amount)
end)

-- AFTER: SecureEvent — more protection, half the code
Whip.register(function()
    exports.whip_core:SecureEvent('trading:server:trade', {
        rateLimit = 1000,
        params = {
            {'targetId', 'id'},                       -- names a player: refused if bad, never clamped
            {'itemKey', 'key', 60},
            {'amount', 'amount', 999},         -- a whole number 1-999, refused if bad
        },
        -- And one check the hand-written version never had: they must be standing together
        near = {
            at = function(source, player, targetId) return GetEntityCoords(GetPlayerPed(targetId)) end,
            range = 3.0,
        },
    }, function(source, player, targetId, itemKey, amount)
        -- Everything already validated. Just write your logic.
        doTrade(source, player, targetId, itemKey, amount)
    end)
end)

Mechanic Job: Engine prompt + Inventory

-- client.lua — a choice on the bonnet's prompt, which shows while the bonnet is open
Whip.register(function()
    exports.whip_core:AddAction({
        id          = 'repair',
        at          = { vehiclePart = 'hood' },
        label       = 'Repair Engine',
        require     = { item = 'repair_kit' },   -- only offered to someone carrying one
        canInteract = function(ctx)
            return GetVehicleEngineHealth(ctx.entity) < 900.0
        end,
        onSelect    = function(ctx)
            TriggerServerEvent('mechanic:repair', VehToNet(ctx.entity))
        end,
    })
end)

-- The server said yes. Repair natives run on the game that controls the car, so take control first
RegisterNetEvent('mechanic:client:repair', function(netId)
    local veh = NetToVeh(netId)
    if exports.whip_core:TakeVehicleControl({ entity = veh }) then
        SetVehicleEngineHealth(veh, 1000.0)
    end
end)

-- server.lua — using SecureEvent for automatic protection
Whip.register(function()
    exports.whip_core:SecureEvent('mechanic:repair', {
        rateLimit = 2000,
        params = {
            {'netId', 'id'},                  -- names a car: refused if bad, never clamped
        },
        -- Beside that car, or not at all: the client naming a car proves nothing
        near = {
            at = function(source, player, netId)
                local veh = NetworkGetEntityFromNetworkId(netId)
                if DoesEntityExist(veh) then return GetEntityCoords(veh) end
            end,
            range = 6.0,
        },
    }, function(source, player, netId)
        local ok = exports.whip_core:RemoveItem(source, 'repair_kit', 1, 'repair')
        if not ok then
            return false, 'No repair kit!'   -- shown to the player, logged as rejected
        end
        -- Engine health is a client native: the mechanic's own game does the repair
        TriggerClientEvent('mechanic:client:repair', source, netId)
        exports.whip_core:NotifyPlayer(source, 'Vehicle repaired!', 'success')
    end)
end)

Drug Spot: Interaction + Ground Items

-- client.lua
Whip.register(function()
    exports.whip_core:AddAction({
        id       = 'package',
        at       = { coords = vector3(1050.0, -3200.0, 5.9) },
        label    = 'Pick Up Package',
        icon     = 'pickup',
        onSelect = function(ctx)
            TriggerServerEvent('drugs:pickup')
        end,
    })
end)

-- server.lua
Whip.register(function()
    exports.whip_core:SecureEvent('drugs:pickup', {
        rateLimit = 60000,                                         -- one package a minute
        near = { at = vector3(1050.0, -3200.0, 5.9), range = 3.0 },   -- at the spot, not from anywhere
    }, function(source, player)
        local where, err = exports.whip_core:AddItem(source, 'cocaine', 5, nil, 'drug spot')   -- 'inventory' | 'ground'
        if not where then return false, err end
        exports.whip_core:NotifyPlayer(source, 'Picked up package', 'success')
    end)
end)

Dealership: Sell a Car

-- server.lua
function SellVehicle(buyerSource, vehicleId, price)
    -- ChargePlayer takes cash or bank as you ask, and hands back a receipt for a refund
    local receipt, err = exports.whip_core:ChargePlayer(buyerSource, price, { method = 'cash', reason = 'Car sale' })
    if not receipt then return false, err end

    -- The car becomes theirs, and they get a key (TransferVehicle gives one by default)
    local ok, why = exports.whip_core:TransferVehicle(vehicleId, buyerSource)
    if not ok then
        exports.whip_core:RefundPlayer(receipt)   -- money back, the way it was paid
        return false, why
    end

    return true
end
Selling a brand-new car? CreateOwnedVehicle(source, data, { giveKey = true, spawnAt = vector4(...) }) creates it, brings it out and hands over the key in one call, and removes it again if any step fails, so the only thing left for you to undo is the payment. See CreateOwnedVehicle.

Police Plate Runner: Vehicle API

-- client.lua — "Run Plate" on any car's boot prompt (the plate is at the back), for on-duty police
Whip.register(function()
    exports.whip_core:AddAction({
        id      = 'run_plate',
        at      = { vehiclePart = 'trunk' },
        label   = 'Run Plate',
        icon    = 'P',
        require = { job = 'police', onDuty = true },

        -- Every car has a plate: read it off the car, no lookup needed here
        onSelect = function(ctx)
            TriggerServerEvent('police:runPlate', GetVehicleNumberPlateText(ctx.entity))
        end,
    })
end)

-- server.lua — whose car is it? The server checks the officer again: require only decides what is offered
Whip.register(function()
    exports.whip_core:SecureEvent('police:runPlate', {
        rateLimit = 2000,
        params = { {'plate', 'string', 8} },
    }, function(source, player, plate)
        if not exports.whip_core:IsPlayerClockedOn(source, 'police') then
            return false, 'On-duty police only'
        end
        local v = exports.whip_core:GetVehicleBy('plate', plate)
        if not v or v.session then   -- a street car or a rental: nobody owns it
            return false, plate .. ': no record'
        end
        exports.whip_core:NotifyPlayer(source, ('%s (%s) is registered to character #%d'):format(plate, v.model, v.owner.charId))
    end)
end)

Impound System: Write Exports + Event Hooks

-- server.lua — Impound a vehicle: lock it and take the keys
Whip.register(function()
    exports.whip_core:SecureEvent('impound:seize', {
        rateLimit = 2000,
        -- names a car: refused if bad, never clamped. anyOwner + session: police seize anyone's car,
        -- street cars included.
        params = { {'vehicle', 'vehicle', { anyOwner = true, session = true }} },
        -- beside the car being seized, where it is NOW (not GetVehicle(id).coords — its last SAVED spot)
        near = { at = 'vehicle', range = 8.0 },
    }, function(source, player, v)
        -- Only on-duty police may seize a car — the server decides, not the client
        if not exports.whip_core:IsPlayerClockedOn(source, 'police') then
            return false, 'Only on-duty police can impound'
        end

        -- Take the keys off the car's owner, if they are online (source is the officer)
        local owner = v.owner.charId and exports.whip_core:GetPlayerFromCharId(v.owner.charId)
        if owner then exports.whip_core:RemoveVehicleKey(owner.source, v.vehicleId) end

        -- Lock the vehicle
        exports.whip_core:SetVehicleLocked(v.vehicleId, true)

        exports.whip_core:NotifyPlayer(source, 'Vehicle impounded', 'success')
    end)
end)

-- Listen for lockpick events — alert police dispatch
AddEventHandler('whip_core:vehicle:lockpicked', function(data)
    local ped = GetPlayerPed(data.source)
    local coords = GetEntityCoords(ped)
    TriggerClientEvent('dispatch:alert', -1, {
        title = 'Vehicle Break-In',
        plate = data.plate,
        x = coords.x, y = coords.y, z = coords.z,
    })
end)

Gas Station: fuel is a stat

There is no SetVehicleFuel. Fuel is an ordinary vehicle stat (registered by whip_fuel: this needs it running), read and written the same way as nos, boost or anything a satellite registers, so a resource that learns the stat API can already do fuel.

-- server.lua — Fill up a vehicle at a gas station
local PUMPS = { vector3(49.4, 2778.8, 58.0), vector3(263.9, 2606.5, 44.9) }

Whip.register(function()
    exports.whip_core:SecureEvent('gasstation:refuel', {
        rateLimit = 2000,
        -- 'vehicle' resolves the id AND checks this player owns the car,
        -- so the handler never has to look one up or compare an owner.
        params = { {'vehicle', 'vehicle'} },
        near = { at = 'vehicle', range = 5.0 },   -- and they are at (or in) that car
    }, function(source, player, v)
        -- ...and the car is at a pump: the client saying "I'm at the station" proves nothing
        local atPump = false
        for _, pump in ipairs(PUMPS) do
            if #(v.coords - pump) < 12.0 then atPump = true break end
        end
        if not atPump then return false, 'Drive up to a pump first' end

        local fuel = exports.whip_core:GetVehicleStat(v.vehicleId, 'fuel')
        local cost = math.ceil((100 - fuel) * 5) -- $5 per percent

        if cost < 1 then return false, 'The tank is already full' end

        local receipt, err = exports.whip_core:ChargePlayer(source, cost, { method = 'cash', reason = 'Fuel' })
        if not receipt then
            return false, err   -- 'Not enough cash (have $5, need $20)'
        end

        -- The last argument is the SOURCE of the change. It shows up in the
        -- Vehicle Stat Debug tool, so a gauge that moves can be traced to who moved it.
        exports.whip_core:SetVehicleStat(v.vehicleId, 'fuel', 100.0, 'gasstation:refuel')
        exports.whip_core:NotifyPlayer(source, ('Refueled for $%d'):format(cost), 'success')
    end)
end)

Tow Truck: GetNearbyVehicles

-- client.lua — List vehicles near the player for towing: a choice on any car's boot prompt
Whip.register(function()
    exports.whip_core:AddAction({
        id       = 'tow_scan',
        at       = { vehiclePart = 'trunk' },
        label    = 'Scan for Tow',
        onSelect = function(ctx)
            local nearby = exports.whip_core:GetNearbyVehicles(30.0)
            for _, v in ipairs(nearby) do
                print(('[TOW] %s (%s) — %.1fm — ID: %s'):format(
                    v.plate, v.model, v.distance, tostring(v.vehicleId)))

                ('Found %d vehicles nearby'):format(#nearby), 'info')
        end,
    })
end)

React to Player Events

-- server.lua — Welcome message when player loads
AddEventHandler('whip_core:player:loaded', function(e)
    TriggerClientEvent('chat:addMessage', e.source, {
        args = {'Server', 'Welcome back, ' .. e.player.fullName .. '!'}
    })
end)

-- server.lua — Log bank transactions
AddEventHandler('whip_core:bank:balanceChanged', function(tx)
    if tx.type == 'transfer' then   -- a transfer names two accounts
        print(('[BANK] transfer: $%d from account %d to %d'):format(tx.amount, tx.fromAccountId, tx.toAccountId))
    else
        print(('[BANK] %s: $%d on account %d'):format(tx.type, tx.amount, tx.accountId))
    end
end)

-- server.lua — React to vehicle events
AddEventHandler('whip_core:vehicle:entered', function(data)
    if data.seat ~= -1 then return end   -- drivers only
    print(('Player %d is driving %s (%s)'):format(
        data.source, data.plate, tostring(data.vehicleId)))
end)

AddEventHandler('whip_core:vehicle:lockChanged', function(data)
    -- source is nil when a script (not a player) changed the lock
    print(('Vehicle %s %s by %s'):format(
        data.plate, data.locked and 'locked' or 'unlocked',
        data.source and ('player ' .. data.source) or 'a script'))
end)

-- client.lua — React to enter/exit locally
AddEventHandler('whip_core:vehicle:entered', function(data)
    if data.vehicleId then
        print('Entered framework vehicle: ' .. data.vehicleId)
    else
        print('Entered unregistered vehicle: ' .. (data.plate or 'unknown'))
    end
end)

Police Department: Jobs System

-- server.lua — the police job and its events, made whenever whip_core is ready
Whip.register(function()
    local job, why = exports.whip_core:EnsureJob('police', {
        name = 'Police Department',
        icon = 'shield',
    })
    if not job then print('[PD] no police job: ' .. tostring(why)) return end

    -- Arrest (requires on duty, and standing next to them)
    exports.whip_core:SecureEvent('pd:arrest', {
        rateLimit = 3000,
        params = { {'targetId', 'id'} },   -- names a player: refused if bad, never clamped
        near = {
            at = function(source, player, targetId) return GetEntityCoords(GetPlayerPed(targetId)) end,
            range = 3.0,
        },
    }, function(source, player, targetId)
        -- A job is named by its key everywhere — no id to look up first
        if not exports.whip_core:IsPlayerClockedOn(source, 'police') then
            return false, 'Must be on duty!'
        end
        -- Do arrest logic...
        print(('Player %d arrested by %s'):format(targetId, player.fullName))
    end)
end)

-- server.lua — Track on-duty officers. A local event, so AddEventHandler.
AddEventHandler('whip_core:job:clockedOn', function(e)
    if e.key ~= 'police' then return end
    local cops = exports.whip_core:GetClockedOnEmployees('police') or {}
    print(('Officer on duty — %d total active'):format(#cops))
end)

-- Or just ask, whenever you need to know:
--   exports.whip_core:IsPlayerClockedOn(source, 'police')   -- a job by its key or jobId
--   Player(source).state.whipJob                           -- the job KEY, or false (for clients)

-- client.lua — "Arrest" where an on-duty officer looks at another player. require does the duty
-- check: no job id to look up. canInteract leaves NPCs out (ctx.player is nil on them).
Whip.register(function()
    exports.whip_core:AddAction({
        id          = 'pd_arrest',
        at          = { aimBox = 'ped' },
        label       = 'Arrest',
        icon        = 'A',
        reach       = 3.0,
        require     = { job = 'police', onDuty = true },
        canInteract = function(ctx) return ctx.player ~= nil end,
        onSelect    = function(ctx)
            TriggerServerEvent('pd:arrest', ctx.player.serverId)
        end,
    })
end)

Camera: Character Creation Intro

-- client.lua — Cinematic intro during character creation

-- A looping camera that cycles between angles around the player. async: a loop never ends
-- by itself, so without it this call would never return
local ped = PlayerPedId()
local pos = GetEntityCoords(ped)

exports.whip_core:PlayCameraPath({
    points = {
        { pos = pos + vector3(2.0, 2.0, 0.5),  rot = vector3(-5.0, 0.0, 225.0),  fov = 40, filter = 'cinema' },
        { pos = pos + vector3(-2.0, 2.0, 0.5), rot = vector3(-5.0, 0.0, 315.0),  fov = 45, filter = 'cinema' },
        { pos = pos + vector3(0.0, 3.0, 1.0),  rot = vector3(-10.0, 0.0, 180.0), fov = 50, filter = 'cinema' },
    },
    mode          = 'cycle',
    cycleDuration = 4000,
    loop          = true,
    async         = true,
})

-- Later, when character creation is done:
exports.whip_core:StopCamera()

Shop: Business Gun Store with Jobs Integration

-- fxmanifest.lua
fx_version 'cerulean'
game 'gta5'
lua54 'yes'
dependency 'whip_core'
shared_script '@whip_core/lib/satellite.lua'
server_script 'server.lua'

-- server.lua — Sets up a gun shop owned by a business, tracks sales
local gunShop

Whip.register(function()
    -- The job: made once, found again on every start
    local job, why = exports.whip_core:EnsureJob('gun_dealer', {
        name = 'Ammu-Nation',
        icon = 'crosshair',
    })
    if not job then print('[GunShop] no job: ' .. tostring(why)) return end

    -- The shop, linked to the job
    gunShop, why = exports.whip_core:EnsureShop('ammunation_main', {
        name       = 'Ammu-Nation',
        mode       = 'infinite',          -- unlimited stock
        jobId      = job.jobId,            -- revenue goes to business bank
        npcModel   = 's_m_m_ammucountry',
        x = -330.2, y = 6084.3, z = 31.5, heading = 228.0,
        blipSprite = 110,
        blipColor  = 1,
        catalog    = {
            gunny_pistol     = 2500,
            gunny_mag_pistol = 150,
            ammo_9mm         = 10,
            bandage          = 50,
        },
    })
    if not gunShop then print('[GunShop] no shop: ' .. tostring(why)) return end
    print('[GunShop] Ready — shop #' .. gunShop.shopId)
end)

-- Track purchases for a loyalty discount system
local purchaseCounts = {}

AddEventHandler('whip_core:shop:purchased', function(data)
    if not gunShop or data.shopId ~= gunShop.shopId then return end

    -- Count purchases per character
    purchaseCounts[data.charId] = (purchaseCounts[data.charId] or 0) + 1
    local count = purchaseCounts[data.charId]

    -- Every 10th purchase, give a free bandage
    if count % 10 == 0 then
        exports.whip_core:AddItem(data.source, 'bandage', 1)
        exports.whip_core:NotifyPlayer(data.source,
            'Loyalty reward! Free bandage for your ' .. count .. 'th purchase!', 'success')
    end
end)

Shop: Dynamic Pricing Based on Supply

-- server.lua — Prices go up as items sell, reset daily
local basePrices = { food = 50, drink = 30 }
local salesCount = { food = 0, drink = 0 }
local shopKey = 'dynamic_store'

AddEventHandler('whip_core:shop:purchased', function(data)
    local shop = exports.whip_core:GetShopBy('key', shopKey)
    if not shop or data.shopId ~= shop.shopId then return end

    -- Track sales and increase prices by 5% per sale
    local newCatalog = {}
    for _, item in ipairs(data.items) do
        salesCount[item.itemKey] = (salesCount[item.itemKey] or 0) + item.amount
    end

    for itemKey, basePrice in pairs(basePrices) do
        local markup = 1.0 + ((salesCount[itemKey] or 0) * 0.05)
        newCatalog[itemKey] = math.floor(basePrice * markup)
    end

    exports.whip_core:UpdateShop(shop.shopId, { catalog = newCatalog })
end)

Shop: Robbery Alert When Player Opens Shop Armed

-- server.lua — Alert police when an armed player opens a shop
AddEventHandler('whip_core:shop:opened', function(data)   -- { shopId, source, charId }
    -- Armed? The server reads the weapon in their hand itself
    local weapon = GetSelectedPedWeapon(GetPlayerPed(data.source))
    if weapon == 0 or weapon == GetHashKey('WEAPON_UNARMED') then return end

    local shop = exports.whip_core:GetShop(data.shopId)
    if not shop then return end

    -- Alert all on-duty police (each row is { charId, source })
    for _, cop in ipairs(exports.whip_core:GetClockedOnEmployees('police') or {}) do
        exports.whip_core:NotifyPlayer(cop.source,
            'Armed customer at ' .. shop.name .. ' — possible robbery!', 'warning')
    end
end)

Shop: Stocked Player-Owned Store

-- server.lua — Create a player-owned shop backed by a container
Whip.register(function()
    -- The job for the business
    local job, why = exports.whip_core:EnsureJob('player_store', {
        name = 'Player General Store',
    })
    if not job then print('[Store] no job: ' .. tostring(why)) return end

    -- The container that holds the shop's stock — made once, found again every restart.
    -- Staff only: without requirements anyone could walk up and empty it.
    local container
    container, why = exports.whip_core:EnsureContainer('player_store_1:stock', {
        name = 'Store Stock', type = 'stash',
        slots = 50, maxWeight = 500.0,
        x = 100.0, y = 200.0, z = 30.0,
        prop = 'prop_cs_cardbox_01',
        requirements = { jobs = 'player_store' },
    })
    if not container then print('[Store] no stock: ' .. tostring(why)) return end

    -- The stocked shop, linked to the container and the job
    exports.whip_core:EnsureShop('player_store_1', {
        name        = 'General Store',
        mode        = 'stocked',
        jobId       = job.jobId,
        containerId = container.containerId,
        npcModel    = 'a_m_m_business_01',
        x = 102.0, y = 200.0, z = 30.0, heading = 180.0,
    })

    -- Now employees can:
    -- 1. At the shopkeeper's prompt → "Manage Stock" → opens the container
    -- 2. Drag items into the container from their inventory
    -- 3. Right-click items → "Set Price" and "Mark For Sale"
    -- 4. Customers at the shopkeeper's prompt → "Browse" → buy listed items
    -- 5. Revenue goes to the business bank account
end)

Time & Weather: Nightclub Interior Override

-- server.lua — Night and clear skies for whoever is inside the nightclub
-- (On the client, a zone's own weather field does this with no code: see Per-Player Weather.)

-- Player enters the nightclub (from your zone or interaction)
function OnEnterNightclub(source)
    exports.whip_core:SetPlayerWeatherLayer(source, 'nightclub', {
        hour = 1, minute = 0, weather = 'CLEAR', frozen = true, priority = 50,
    })
end

-- Player leaves it: whatever was underneath comes back
function OnExitNightclub(source)
    exports.whip_core:ClearPlayerWeatherLayer(source, 'nightclub')
end

-- Nothing to clean up on disconnect: whip drops a player's layers when they leave.

-- server.lua — Adjust NPC behavior when weather changes
AddEventHandler('whip_core:weather:changed', function(data)
    if data.weather == 'THUNDER' or data.weather == 'RAIN' then
        print('Rain detected — enabling umbrella vendors')
        -- Your logic: spawn umbrella vendors, increase taxi demand, etc.
    end
end)

-- client.lua — Indoor thunder ambience while a layer (a zone's weather, the server's
-- SetPlayerWeatherLayer) gives this player a storm. A server-wide change is the server event above.
AddEventHandler('whip_core:weather:layerChanged', function(e)
    if exports.whip_core:GetCurrentWeather() == 'THUNDER' then
        -- start indoor thunder ambience
    else
        -- stop it
    end
end)

Time & Weather: Scheduled Weather Cycle

-- server.lua — Auto-cycle weather every 30 real minutes
local weatherCycle = { 'CLEAR', 'CLOUDS', 'OVERCAST', 'RAIN', 'CLEARING', 'CLEAR' }
local cycleIndex = 1

CreateThread(function()
    while true do
        Wait(1800000) -- 30 minutes
        cycleIndex = (cycleIndex % #weatherCycle) + 1
        exports.whip_core:SetWeather(weatherCycle[cycleIndex])
        print('Weather cycled to ' .. weatherCycle[cycleIndex])
    end
end)

Weapon Shop: Give Weapon + Ammo (whip_gunny)

-- fxmanifest.lua: dependency 'whip_gunny' as well as whip_core

-- client.lua — "Buy Pistol" at the counter
local COUNTER = vector3(21.6, -1106.5, 29.8)

Whip.register(function()
    exports.whip_core:AddAction({
        id       = 'buy_pistol',
        at       = { coords = COUNTER },
        label    = 'Buy Pistol ($5000)',
        onSelect = function() TriggerServerEvent('gunshop:buyPistol') end,
    })
end)

-- server.lua — the sale, at the counter only, once every few seconds
local COUNTER = vector3(21.6, -1106.5, 29.8)

Whip.register(function()
    exports.whip_core:SecureEvent('gunshop:buyPistol', {
        rateLimit = 3000,
        near = { at = COUNTER, range = 3.0 },
    }, function(source, player)
        -- Take payment: a receipt, or why not ('Not enough cash (have $20, need $5000)')
        local receipt, err = exports.whip_core:ChargePlayer(source, 5000, { method = 'cash', reason = 'Pistol' })
        if not receipt then return false, err end   -- shown to the player

        -- Give the weapon; if that fails, give the money back
        local ok, why = exports.whip_gunny:GiveWeapon(source, 'gunny_pistol', nil, 'Pistol purchase')
        if not ok then
            Whip.call('RefundPlayer', receipt)
            return false, why
        end

        -- A loaded magazine and spare rounds. AddItem can wait (full pockets: it goes on the
        -- ground), so it goes through Whip.call, which answers even if whip_core stops meanwhile
        exports.whip_gunny:GiveMagazine(source, 'gunny_mag_pistol', 12, 'Pistol purchase')
        Whip.call('AddItem', source, 'ammo_9mm', 24, nil, 'Pistol purchase')

        Whip.call('NotifyPlayer', source, 'Pistol purchased!', 'success')
    end)
end)

A sale is a SecureEvent from a prompt, not a chat command: the event is rate limited and only taken at the counter, and whip_core is up while it runs. Once something has waited (GiveWeapon gives through AddItem), the rest goes through Whip.call.
